question: If $(x^{2}+5x+5)^{x+5}=1$ then the number of integers satisfying this equation is
search_text: if $(x^{2}+5x+5)^{x+5}=1$ then the number of integers satisfying this equation is {'a': '2', 'b': '3', 'c': '4', 'd': '5'} 2021 2021-08-19 shift_1 mathematics   12 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: $\because (x^2+5x+5)^{x+5}=1$ for an integer power to equal $1$ , the possibilities are: the exponent is $0$ with a nonzero base, the base is $1$ , or the base is $-1$ with an even exponent. case i $x+5=0$ $\rightarrow \; x=-5$ here the base is $5 \ne 0$ , so $x=-5$ is valid. case ii $x^2+5x+5=1$ $\rightarrow \; x^2+5x+4=0$ $\rightarrow \; (x+1)(x+4)=0$ $\rightarrow \; x=-1,-4$ both are valid. case iii $x^2+5x+5=-1$ and $x+5$ is even. $\rightarrow \; x^2+5x+6=0$ $\rightarrow \; (x+2)(x+3)=0$ $\rightarrow \; x=-2,-3$ for $x=-2$ , the exponent is $3$ , which is odd, so it is not valid. for $x=-3$ , the exponent is $2$ , which is even, so $x=-3$ is valid. thus the integer solutions are $x=-5,-4,-3,-1$ . hence the number of integers satisfying the equation is $4$ . © examsnet.com

question: The sum of the roots of the equation $e^{4 t}-10 e^{3 t}+29 e^{2 t}-22 e^{t}+4=0$ is _______
search_text: the sum of the roots of the equation $e^{4 t}-10 e^{3 t}+29 e^{2 t}-22 e^{t}+4=0$ is _______ {'a': '$\\log_{e}10$', 'b': '$2\\log_{e}2$', 'c': '$\\log_{2}29$', 'd': '$2\\log_{10}2$'} 2021 2021-08-19 shift_1 mathematics   14 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: $e^{4 t}-10 e^{3 t}+29 e^{2 t}-22 e^{t}+4=0$ ...(i) let $e^{t}=x$ and roots of (1) be $t_{1}, t_{2}, t_{3}, t_{4}$ $\therefore x^{4}-10 x^{3}+29 x^{2}-22 x+4=0$ then, roots are $x_{1}, x_{2}, x_{3}, x_{4}$ product of roots $x_{1} \cdot x_{2} \cdot x_{3} \cdot x_{4}=4$ $\rightarrow e^{t_1}\cdot e^{t_2}\cdot e^{t_3} e^{t_4}=4$ $\rightarrow e^{t_{1}+t_{2}+t_{3}+t_{4}}=4$ $t_{1}+t_{2}+t_{3}+t_{4}=\log_{e}\;4=\log_{e}\;2^{2}=2\log_{e}\;2$ sum of roots $=2\log_{e}\;2$ © examsnet.com

search_text: if the slope of one of the lines represented by $a x^{2}+2 h x y+b y^{2}=0$ is the square of the other then, $\left| \frac{a+b}{h}+\frac{8 h^{2}}{a b} \right|=$ {'a': '3', 'b': '2', 'c': '6', 'd': '4'} 2021 2021-08-19 shift_1 mathematics   49 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: let m be the slope of one of the lines given by $a x^{2}+2 h x y+b y^{2}=0$ then, the other line has slope $m^{2}$ . $\therefore m+m'=\frac{-2 h}{b}$ and $m \cdot m^{2}=\frac{a}{b}$ $\because (m+m^{2})^{3}=m^{3}+(m^{2})^{3}+3 m \cdot m^{2}(m+m^{2})$ $\left(-\frac{2 h}{b}\right)^{3}=\frac{a}{b}+\frac{a^{2}}{b^{2}}+3 \cdot \frac{a}{b} \cdot \left(-\frac{2 h}{b}\right)$ $\rightarrow \frac{-8 h^{3}}{b^{3}}=\frac{a}{b}+\frac{a^{2}}{b^{2}}-\frac{6 a h}{b^{2}}$ $\rightarrow \frac{a}{b}+\frac{a^{2}}{b^{2}}-\frac{6 a h}{b^{2}}+\frac{8 h^{3}}{b^{3}}=0$ or $a^{2} b+a b^{2}+8 h=6 a b h$ or $a b(a+b)+8 h^{2}=6 a b h$ or $\frac{a+b}{h}+\frac{8 h^{2}}{a b}=6$ or $\left| \frac{a+b}{h}+\frac{8 h^{2}}{a b} \right|=6$ © examsnet.com

search_text: let $l_{1}$ be a straight line passing through the origin and $l_{2}$ be the straight line $x+y=1$ . if the intercepts made by the circle $x^{2}+y^{2}-x+3y=0$ on $l_{1}$ and $l_{2}$ are equal, then which of the following equations represent $l_{1}$ _______ {'a': '$x+y=0$ & $x+7y=0$', 'b': '$x-y=0$ & $x+7y=0$', 'c': '$x-7y=0$ & $x+y=0$', 'd': '$x-7y=0$ & $x-y=0$'} 2021 2021-08-19 shift_1 mathematics   53 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: let $l_{1}: y=mx$ (equation of line passes through origin) intercept made by $l_{1}$ and $l_{2}$ are equal $\rightarrow l_{1}$ and $l_{2}$ are at the same distance from centre of circle $x^{2}+y^{2}-x+3y=0$ now, centre $\left(\frac{1}{2}, \frac{-3}{2}\right)$ $\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;$ [∵ centre = (-g - f)] distance of $l_{1}$ from $\left(\frac{1}{2},-\frac{3}{2}\right)=\frac{\left| m\cdot\frac{1}{2}+\frac{3}{2} \right|}{\sqrt{m^{2}+1}}$ distance of $l_{2}$ from $\left(\frac{1}{2},-\frac{3}{2}\right)=\frac{\left| \frac{1}{2} - \frac{3}{2} - 1 \right|}{\sqrt{1+1}}$ $\because l_{2}: x+y-1=0$ $\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;$ $[\because y = mx \rightarrow mx - y = 0]$ $\rightarrow \frac{\left| \frac{m+3}{2} \right|}{\sqrt{m^{2}+1}} = \frac{2}{\sqrt{2}}$ squaring both sides, we get $\frac{(m+3)^{2}}{4(m^{2}+1)} = \frac{4}{2}$ $\rightarrow m^{2}+6m+9=8(m^{2}+1)$ $\rightarrow 7m^{2}-6m-1=0$ $\rightarrow m=\frac{6 \pm \sqrt{36+28}}{14} = \frac{6 \pm 8}{14}$ $=1, \frac{-1}{7}$ $\therefore l_{1}$ is $y=x$ and $y=\frac{-1}{7}x$ or $x-y=0$ or $x+7y=0$ © examsnet.com

search_text: $f(x)=\begin{cases} \frac{72^{x}-9^{x}-8^{x}+1}{\sqrt{2}-\sqrt{1+\cos x}}, & x \neq 0 \\ k \log 2 \log 3, & x=0 \end{cases}$ find the value of k for which the function f is continuous. {'a': '$\\sqrt{2}$', 'b': '24', 'c': '$18 \\sqrt{3}$', 'd': '$24 \\sqrt{2}$'} 2021 2021-08-19 shift_1 mathematics   63 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: f is continuous at $x=0$ $\therefore \lim\limits_{x \to 0}\; f(x)=f(0)$ $\rightarrow \lim\limits_{x \to 0} \frac{72^{x}-9^{x}-8^{x}+1}{\sqrt{2}-\sqrt{1+\cos x}} = k \log 2 \log 3$ $\rightarrow k \log 2 \cdot \log 3$ $= \lim\limits_{x \to 0} \frac{(9^{x}-1)(8^{x}-1)(\sqrt{2}+\sqrt{1+\cos x})}{2-(1+\cos x)}$ $= \lim\limits_{x \to 0} \left[ \frac{9^{x}-1}{x} \cdot \frac{8^{x}-1}{x} \cdot \frac{x^{2}}{1-\cos x} \cdot (\sqrt{2}+\sqrt{1+\cos x}) \right]$ $= \log 9 \cdot \log 8 \cdot 2 (\sqrt{2}+\sqrt{2})$ $= 2 \log 3 \cdot 3 \log 2 \cdot 4 \sqrt{2}$ $\rightarrow k \log 3 \cdot \log 2 = 24 \sqrt{2} \log 3 \cdot \log 2$ $\rightarrow k = 24 \sqrt{2}$ © examsnet.com

search_text: $\int \frac{e^{x}(x+3)}{(x+5)^{3}} \, dx =$ {'a': '$\\frac{e^{x}}{(x+5)^{2}} + c$', 'b': '$e^{x} (x+5)^{2} + c$', 'c': '$e^{x} (x+3)^{2} + c$', 'd': '$\\frac{e^{x}}{(x+3)^{2}} + c$'} 2021 2021-08-19 shift_1 mathematics   75 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: $\text{let } i = \int \frac{e^{x}(x+3)}{(x+5)^{3}} \, dx = \int e^{x} \left[ \frac{1}{(x+5)^{2}} - \frac{2}{(x+5)^{3}} \right] \, dx$ $\int \left[ f(x) + f'(x) \right] e^{x} \, dx = e^{x} f(x) + c$ $\rightarrow i = \frac{e^{x}}{(x+5)^{2}} + c$ © examsnet.com

question: If $\int \frac{(x-1)^2}{(x^2+1)^2} \, dx = \tan^{-1}(x) + g(x) + k$ , then $g(x)$ is equal to ______
search_text: if $\int \frac{(x-1)^2}{(x^2+1)^2} \, dx = \tan^{-1}(x) + g(x) + k$ , then $g(x)$ is equal to ______ {'a': '$\\tan^{-1}\\left(\\frac{x}{2}\\right)$', 'b': '$\\frac{1}{x^2+1}$', 'c': '$\\frac{1}{2(x^2+1)}$', 'd': '$\\frac{2}{x^2+1}$'} 2021 2021-08-19 shift_1 mathematics   76 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: $\int \frac{(x-1)^2}{(x^2+1)^2} \, dx = \int \left( \frac{1}{x^2+1} - \frac{2x}{(x^2+1)^2} \right) dx$ $= \tan^{-1}(x) - \int \frac{2x}{(x^2+1)^2} \, dx$ $\text{let } x^2+1 = t$ $\rightarrow 2x \, dx = dt$ $= \tan^{-1}(x) - \int t^{-2} \, dt = \tan^{-1}(x) + \frac{1}{t} + k$ $\rightarrow \int \frac{(x-1)^2}{(x+1)^2} \, dx = \tan^{-1}(x) + \frac{1}{x^2+1} + k$ comparing with $\int \frac{(x-1)^2}{(x^2+1)^2} \, dx = \tan^{-1}(x) + g(x) + k$ we have $g(x) = \frac{1}{x^2+1}$ © examsnet.com

search_text: if $\int \frac{1-(\cot x)^{2021}}{\tan x+(\cot x)^{2022}} dx$ $= \frac{1}{a} \log \left| (\sin x)^{2023}+(\cos x)^{2023} \right| +c$ , then $a=$ {'a': '2020', 'b': '2021', 'c': '2022', 'd': '2023'} 2021 2021-08-19 shift_1 mathematics   77 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: $\frac{1}{a} \log \left| (\sin x)^{2023}+(\cos x)^{2023} \right| +c$ $= \int \frac{1-(\cot x)^{2021}}{\tan x+(\cot x)^{2022}} dx = \int \frac{1-\frac{(\cos x)^{2021}}{(\sin x)^{2021}}}{\frac{\sin x}{\cos x}+\frac{(\cos x)^{2022}}{(\sin x)^{2022}}} dx$ $= \int \frac{(\sin x)^{2021}-(\cos x)^{2021}}{(\sin x)^{2023}+(\cos x)^{2023}} \cdot \cos x \sin x dx$ $= \int \frac{\cos x (\sin x)^{2022}-\sin x (\cos x)^{2022}}{(\sin x)^{2023}+(\cos x)^{2023}} dx$ $\because \int \frac{f'(x)}{f(x)} dx = \log \left| f(x) \right| +c$ $\rightarrow \frac{1}{a} \log \left| (\sin x)^{2023}+(\cos x)^{2023} \right| +c$ $= \frac{1}{2023} \log \left| (\sin x)^{2023}+(\cos x)^{2023} \right| +c$ ⇒ a = 2023 © examsnet.com

question: $\int\limits_{2}^{4} \{|x-2|+|x-3|\} d x =$
search_text: $\int\limits_{2}^{4} \{|x-2|+|x-3|\} d x =$ {'a': '1', 'b': '2', 'c': '3', 'd': '4'} 2021 2021-08-19 shift_1 mathematics   78 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: let $i = \int\limits_{2}^{4} (|x-2|+|x-3|) d x$ $\because x - a = \begin{cases} x - a, & x \ge a \\ -(x - a), & x < a \end{cases}$ $\therefore i = \int\limits_{2}^{4} |x-2| d x + \int\limits_{2}^{3} |x-3| d x + \int\limits_{3}^{4} |x-3| d x$ $= \int\limits_{2}^{4} (x-2) d x - \int\limits_{2}^{3} (x-3) d x + \int\limits_{3}^{4} (x-3) d x$ $= \left( \frac{x^{2}}{2} - 2x \right)_{2}^{4} - \left( \frac{x^{2}}{2} - 3x \right)_{2}^{3} + \left( \frac{x^{2}}{2} - 3x \right)_{3}^{4}$ $= \left[ \left( \frac{16}{2} - 8 \right) - \left( \frac{4}{2} - 4 \right) \right] - \left[ \left( \frac{9}{2} - 9 \right) - \left( \frac{4}{2} - 6 \right) \right] + \left[ \left( \frac{16}{2} - 12 \right) - \left( \frac{9}{2} - 9 \right) \right]$ $= \left| \left[ 0 - (-2) \right] - \left[ \left( \frac{-9}{2} \right) - (-4) \right] + \left[ (-4) - \left( -\frac{9}{2} \right) \right] \right|$ $= \left| 2 + \frac{9}{2} - 4 - 4 + \frac{9}{2} \right| = \left[ 2 + 9 - 8 \right] = 3$ © examsnet.com

question: $\int\limits_{-\frac{1}{2}}^{\frac{1}{2}} \left\{[x]+\log\left(\frac{1+x}{1-x}\right)\right\} dx=$
search_text: $\int\limits_{-\frac{1}{2}}^{\frac{1}{2}} \left\{[x]+\log\left(\frac{1+x}{1-x}\right)\right\} dx=$ {'a': '$2 \\log\\left(\\frac{1}{2}\\right)$', 'b': '0', 'c': '$-\\frac{1}{2}$', 'd': '1'} 2021 2021-08-19 shift_1 mathematics   79 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: $\text{let } i=\int\limits_{-\frac{1}{2}}^{\frac{1}{2}} \left\{[x]+\log\left(\frac{1+x}{1-x}\right) dx\right\}$ $\because \int\limits_{-a}^{a} f(x)\,dx = \begin{cases} 2\int_{0}^{n} f(x)\,dx, & f(-x)=f(x) \\ 0, & f(-x)=-f(x) \end{cases}$ $= \int\limits_{-\frac{1}{2}}^{\frac{1}{2}} [x]\,dx + \int\limits_{-\frac{1}{2}}^{\frac{1}{2}} \log\left(\frac{1+x}{1-x}\right) dx$ let $f(x)=\log\left(\frac{1+x}{1-x}\right)$ $f(-x)=\log\left(\frac{1-x}{1+x}\right) = -f(x)$ $\;\;\;\;$ [odd function] $= \int\limits_{-\frac{1}{2}}^{\frac{1}{2}} [x]\,dx + 0 = \int\limits_{-\frac{1}{2}}^{0} [x]\,dx + \int\limits_{0}^{\frac{1}{2}} [x]\,dx$ $= \int\limits_{-\frac{1}{2}}^{0} (-1)\,dx + \int\limits_{0}^{\frac{1}{2}} 0\,dx$ $= -\left(x\right)_{-\frac{1}{2}}^{0} + 0 = -\left(0+\frac{1}{2}\right) = -\frac{1}{2}$ © examsnet.com

question: A metal ball of mass $2\text{ kg}$ moving with a velocity of $36\text{ km/h}$ has a head on collision with astationary ball of mass $3\text{ kg}$ . After the collision, if both balls move together, the loss in kinetic energy due to collision is ______
search_text: a metal ball of mass $2\text{ kg}$ moving with a velocity of $36\text{ km/h}$ has a head on collision with astationary ball of mass $3\text{ kg}$ . after the collision, if both balls move together, the loss in kinetic energy due to collision is ______ {'a': '40 j', 'b': '60 j', 'c': '100 j', 'd': '140 j'} 2021 2021-08-19 shift_1 physics   87 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: given, mass of ball $1,\ m_1=2\text{ kg}$ mass of ball $2,\ m_2=3\text{ kg}$ $u_1=36\text{ km/h}=36\times\frac{5}{18}\text{ m/s}=10\text{ m/s}$ $u_2=0$ after collision, the two balls will stick together and their combined  velocity be v. now, by using law of conservation of momentum, $m_1 u_1+m_2 u_2=(m_1+m_2)v$ $\rightarrow v=\frac{2\times10+3\times0}{5}=4\text{ ms}^{-1}$ ∴ energy loss = energy before collision $(e_2)-\text{energy after collision}(e_1)$ $=\left(\frac{1}{2}m_1 u_1^2+\frac{1}{2}m_2 u_2^2\right)-\frac{1}{2}(m_1+m_2)v^2$ $=\left(\frac{1}{2}\times2\times10^2+\frac{1}{2}\times3\times0^2\right)-\frac{1}{2}(2+3)4^2$ $=\frac{1}{2}\times2\times100-\frac{1}{2}\times5\times16$ $=100-40=60\text{ j}$ © examsnet.com

question: Two inductors A and B when connected in parallel are equivalent to a single inductor of inductance $1.5\,\mathrm{H}$ , and when connected in series are equivalent to a single inductor of inductance $8\,\mathrm{H}$ . Find the difference in the inductances of A and B.
search_text: two inductors a and b when connected in parallel are equivalent to a single inductor of inductance $1.5\,\mathrm{h}$ , and when connected in series are equivalent to a single inductor of inductance $8\,\mathrm{h}$ . find the difference in the inductances of a and b. {'a': '3h', 'b': '7.5h', 'c': '2h', 'd': '4h'} 2021 2021-08-19 shift_1 physics   115 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: given, series equivalent inductance, $l_{eq}=8\,\mathrm{h}$ parallel equivalent inductance, $l_{\text{eq}_2}=1.5\,\mathrm{h}=\frac{3}{2}\,\mathrm{h}$ let two inductors used here be $l_1$ and $l_2$ , then $l_{\text{eq}_1}($ series $) = l_1 + l_2$ $\therefore l_{\text{eq}_1}=l_1+l_2=8$ ...(i) and $\frac{1}{l_{\text{eq}_1}}$ (parallel) $= \frac{1}{l_1} + \frac{1}{l_2}$ $\rightarrow l_{\text{eq}_2}=\frac{l_1 l_2}{l_2+l_1}$ $\rightarrow \frac{3}{2}=\frac{l_1(8-l_1)}{8}$ $\rightarrow 12=8l_1-l_1^2$ $\rightarrow l_1^2-8l_1+12=0$ $\rightarrow l_1^2-6l_1-2l_1+12=0$ $\rightarrow l_1(l_1-6)-2(l_1-6)=0$ $\therefore l_1=2\,\mathrm{h}$ or $6\,\mathrm{h}$ and $l_2=(8-2)$ or $(8-6)$ $=6\,\mathrm{h}$ or $2\,\mathrm{h}$ ∴ difference between inductances is $(l_1-l_2)$ or $(l_2-l_1)=6-2$ = 4h © examsnet.com

search_text: a resonant frequency of a current is f. if the capacitance is made four times the initial value. then the resonant  frequency will become ______ {'a': '$\\frac{f}{2}$', 'b': '2f', 'c': 'f', 'd': '$\\frac{f}{4}$'} 2021 2021-08-19 shift_1 physics   116 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: given, initial resonance frequency, $f_{i}=f$ initial capacitance and inductance be $c_{1}=c$ and $l_{1}=l$ final capacitance and inductance one $c_{2}=4c$ and $l_{2}=l$ let final frequency be $f'$ . since, $\omega=\frac{1}{\sqrt{lc}}=2\pi f$ where, ω and $f$ and angular frequency and frequency. $\therefore f \propto \frac{1}{\sqrt{lc}}$ $\rightarrow \frac{f}{f'}=\sqrt{\frac{l'c'}{lc}}=\frac{\sqrt{l4c}}{\sqrt{lc}}=\sqrt{4}=2$ $\therefore f'=\frac{f}{2}$ © examsnet.com

(i), we get $r^{3}=\frac{ke^{2}}{m \cdot \frac{n^{2} h^{2}}{4 \pi^{2} m^{2} r^{2}}}$ $r^{3}=\frac{k e^{2} \cdot 4 \pi^{2} m^{2} r^{2}}{m n^{2} h^{2}}$ $\therefore r=\frac{4 \pi^{2} k r^{2} m}{n^{2} h^{2}}$ © examsnet.com

search_text: a transistor is connected in common emitter configuration. the collector supply is $8\ \mathrm{v}$ and the voltage drop across a resistor of $800\ \omega$ in the collector circuit is $0.5\ \mathrm{v}$ . if the current gain factor $\alpha$ is $0.96$ , the base current is _____ {'a': '$2.6 \\times 10^{-5}\\ \\mathrm{a}$', 'b': '$3.6 \\times 10^{-5}\\ \\mathrm{a}$', 'c': '$5.6 \\times 10^{-5}\\ \\mathrm{a}$', 'd': '$6.6 \\times 10^{-5}\\ \\mathrm{a}$'} 2021 2021-08-19 shift_1 physics   120 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: given, collector voltage, $v_{c}=8\ \mathrm{v}$ voltage drop across resistor, $r=800\ \omega$ and $v=0.5\ \mathrm{v}$ current gain, $\alpha=0.96$ let, collector, emitter and base current be $i_{c}, i_{e}$ and $i_{b}$ , respectively. since, $\;\; \alpha=\frac{i_{c}}{i_{e}}$ and $\;\; i_{e}=i_{b}+i_{c}$ $\because \;\; \alpha=\frac{i_{c}}{i_{b}+i_{c}}=\frac{1}{\frac{i_{b}}{i_{c}}+1}$ $\rightarrow \;\; \frac{i_{b}}{i_{c}}=\frac{1}{\alpha}-1$ $=\frac{100}{96}-1=\frac{4}{96}=0.042$ $\rightarrow \;\; i_{b}=0.042 i_{c}=0.042 \times \frac{0.5}{800} \left( \because i_{c}=\frac{v}{r} \right)$ $=\frac{42 \times 10^{-3} \times 5 \times 10^{-1}}{800}$ $=2.625 \times 10^{-5}\ \mathrm{a}$ © examsnet.com

search_text: when $20\,\text{g}$ of $\mathrm{caco}_3$ is treated with $20\,\text{g}$ of $\mathrm{hcl}$ , the mass of $\mathrm{co}_2$ formed would be ______ {'a': '10g', 'b': '8.8g', 'c': '22.2g', 'd': '20g'} 2021 2021-08-19 shift_1 chemistry   132 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: let $\mathrm{caco}_3(s)$ be consumed completely. $\underset{\text{carbonate}}{\underset{\text{calcium}}{\mathrm{caco}_3(s)}}+\underset{\text{acid}}{\underset{\text{hydrochloric}}{2\,\mathrm{hcl}(aq.)}}\rightarrow\underset{\text{chloride}}{\underset{\text{calciurn}}{\mathrm{cacl}_2(aq)}}+\mathrm{h_2o}(l)+\mathrm{co_2}(g)$ $\therefore 20\,\text{g}$ of $\mathrm{caco}_3$ gives $=44\,\text{g}$ of $\mathrm{co}_2$ gas $\therefore 20\,\text{g}$ of $\mathrm{caco}$ , will give $=\frac{44}{100} \times 20\,\text{g}$ of $\mathrm{co}_2$ $=8.8\,\text{g}$ of $\mathrm{co}_2$ now, hcl, be completely consumed. $73\,\text{g}$ of $\mathrm{hcl}$ give $=44\,\text{g}$ of $\mathrm{co}_2$ gas $\therefore 20\,\text{g}$ of $\mathrm{hcl}$ gives $=\frac{44}{73} \times 20\,\text{g}$ of $\mathrm{co}_2=12.05\,\text{g}$ of $\mathrm{co}_2$ hence, $\mathrm{caco}_3$ give least amount of $\mathrm{co}_2$ gas. so, $\mathrm{caco}_3$ is limiting reactant ∴ amount of $\mathrm{co}_2$ , formed will be $8.8\,\text{g}$ . © examsnet.com

question: If a chemical reaction is known to be non-spontaneous at $298\,\text{K}$ but spontaneous at $350\,\text{K}$ . then which among the following conditions is true for the reaction?
search_text: if a chemical reaction is known to be non-spontaneous at $298\,\text{k}$ but spontaneous at $350\,\text{k}$ . then which among the following conditions is true for the reaction? {'a': '$\\delta g = -$ ve, $\\delta h = -$ ve, $\\delta s = +$ ve', 'b': '$\\delta g = +$ ve, $\\delta h = +$ ve, $\\delta s = +\\text{v e}$', 'c': '$\\delta g = -\\text{v e}, \\delta h = +\\text{v e}, \\delta s = +\\text{v e}$', 'd': '$\\delta g = +$ ve, $\\delta h = +$ ve, $\\delta s = -$ ve'} 2021 2021-08-19 shift_1 chemistry   134 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: according to gibb's free energy, $\delta g = \delta h - t \delta s$ reaction is non spontancous i.e. $\delta g > 0$ at $298\,\text{k}$ . as the temperature increases from $298\,\text{k}$ to $350\,\text{k}$ . the reaction becomes spontaneous i.e. $\delta g < 0$ . $\delta g = \delta h - t \delta s$ $\delta g < 0$ when $\delta h$ and $\delta s$ are +ve then, $\delta g$ will be positive till $\delta h > t \delta s$ . when the temperature is increased further $\delta h$ becomes less than $t \delta s$ i.e. $\delta h < t \delta s$ and $\delta g$ becomes $-\text{v e.}$ thus, reaction becomes spontancous. © examsnet.com

question: The real valued function $f(x)=\frac{x}{e^{x}-1}+\frac{x}{2}+1$ defined on $R \setminus \{0\}$ is _______
search_text: the real valued function $f(x)=\frac{x}{e^{x}-1}+\frac{x}{2}+1$ defined on $r \setminus \{0\}$ is _______ {'a': 'an odd function', 'b': 'an even function', 'c': 'both even & odd function', 'd': 'neither even nor odd function'} 2021 2021-08-19 shift_2 mathematics   1 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: $f(x)=\frac{x}{e^{x}-1}+\frac{x}{2}+1$ now, $f(-x)=\frac{-x}{\frac{1}{e^{x}}-1}-\frac{x}{2}+1$ $=\frac{-x e^{x}}{1-e^{x}}-\frac{x}{2}+1$ $=\frac{-2 x e^{x}-x(1-e^{x})}{2(1-e^{x})}+1$ $=\frac{-2 x e^{x}-x+x e^{x}}{2(1-e^{x})}+1$ $=\frac{-x e^{x}-2 x+x}{2(1-e^{x})}+1$ $=\frac{-2 x+x(1-e^{2})}{2(1-e^{x})}+1$ $=\frac{-x}{1-e^{x}}+\frac{x}{2}+1$ $=\frac{x}{e^{x}-1}+\frac{x}{2}+1 =f(x)$ ∴ $f(x)$ is an even function. © examsnet.com

search_text: let $f: r \rightarrow r$ be a function defined by $f(x)=\frac{4^{x}}{4^{x}+2}$ . what is the value of $f\left(\frac{1}{4}\right)+2 f\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)+f\left(\frac{3}{4}\right)=?$ {'a': '4', 'b': '3', 'c': '2', 'd': '1'} 2021 2021-08-19 shift_2 mathematics   3 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: $f(x)=\frac{4^{x}}{4^{x}+2}$ $f(1-x)=\frac{4^{1-x}}{4^{1-x}+2}=\frac{\frac{4}{4^{x}}}{\frac{4}{4^{x}}+2}$ $=\frac{4}{4+2\cdot 4^{x}}$ $f(1-x)=\frac{2}{4^{x}+2}$ ...(i) and $1-f(x)=1-\frac{4^{x}}{4^{x}+2}$ $=\frac{4^{x}+2-4^{x}}{4^{x}+2}=\frac{2}{4^{x}+2}=f(1-x)$ $\rightarrow f(l-x)+f(x)=l$ ...(ii) put $x=\frac{1}{4}$ in eq. (ii), we get $f\left(\frac{3}{4}\right)+f\left(\frac{1}{4}\right)=1$ ...(iii) now, put $x=\frac{1}{2}$ in eq. (ii), we get $f\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)+f\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)=1$ or $2f\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)=1$ ...(iv) adding eqs. (iii) and (iv), we have $f\left(\frac{1}{4}\right)+2 f\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)+f\left(\frac{3}{4}\right)=2$ © examsnet.com

question: $\begin{bmatrix} a^{2} & 15 & 31 \\ 12 & b^{2} & 41 \\ 35 & 61 & c^{2} \end{bmatrix}$ and $\begin{bmatrix} 2a & 3 & 5 \\ 2 & 2b & 8 \\ 1 & 4 & 2c-3 \end{bmatrix}$ are two matrices such that the sum of the principal diagonal elements of both A and B are equal, then the product of the principal diagonalelements of B is _______.
search_text: $\begin{bmatrix} a^{2} & 15 & 31 \\ 12 & b^{2} & 41 \\ 35 & 61 & c^{2} \end{bmatrix}$ and $\begin{bmatrix} 2a & 3 & 5 \\ 2 & 2b & 8 \\ 1 & 4 & 2c-3 \end{bmatrix}$ are two matrices such that the sum of the principal diagonal elements of both a and b are equal, then the product of the principal diagonalelements of b is _______. {'a': '4', 'b': '0', 'c': '-4', 'd': '-12'} 2021 2021-08-19 shift_2 mathematics   7 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: $\begin{bmatrix} a^{2} & 15 & 31 \\ 12 & b^{2} & 41 \\ 35 & 61 & c^{2} \end{bmatrix}$ $\begin{bmatrix} 2a & 3 & 5 \\ 2 & 2b & 8 \\ 1 & 4 & 2c-3 \end{bmatrix}$ given, trace of $a=$ trace of b $\rightarrow a^{2}+b^{2}+c^{2}=2a+2b+2c-3$ $\rightarrow (a^{2}-2a+1)+(b^{2}-2b+1)+(c^{2}-2c+1)=0$ $\rightarrow (a-1)^{2}+(b-1)^{2}+(c-1)^{2}=0$ $\rightarrow a=1, b=1, c=1$ then product of diagonal elements of b $=(2a)(2b)(2c-3)=(2)(2)(2-3)=-4$ © examsnet.com

search_text: let $a, b, c$ be such that $b+c \neq 0$ and $\begin{vmatrix} a & a+1 & a-1 \\ -b & b+1 & b-1 \\ c & c-1 & c+1 \end{vmatrix}+$ $\begin{vmatrix} a+1 & b+1 & c-1 \\ a-1 & b-1 & c+1 \\ (-1)^{n+2}a & (-1)^{n-1}b & (-1)^{n}c \end{vmatrix}=0$ , then the value of n is {'a': 'zero', 'b': 'any even integer', 'c': 'any odd integer', 'd': 'any integer'} 2021 2021-08-19 shift_2 mathematics   8 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: $\begin{vmatrix} a & a+1 & a-1 \\ -b & b+1 & b-1 \\ c & c-1 & c+1 \end{vmatrix}+\begin{vmatrix} a+1 & b+1 & c-1 \\ a-1 & b-1 & c+1 \\ (-1)^{n+2}a & (-1)^{n-1}b & (-1)^{n}c \end{vmatrix}=0$ $\because |a| = |a^{t}|$ $\rightarrow \begin{vmatrix} a & -b & c \\ a+1 & b+1 & c-1 \\ a-a & b-1 & c+1 \end{vmatrix}+(-1)^n\begin{vmatrix} a+1 & b+1 & c-1 \\ a-1 & b-1 & c+1 \\ a & -b & c \end{vmatrix}=0$ $r_{2} \leftrightarrow r_{3}$ and $r_{3} \leftrightarrow r_{1}$ in 2 nd determinant $\rightarrow \begin{vmatrix} a & -b & c \\ a+1 & b+1 & c-1 \\ a-1 & b-1 & c+1 \end{vmatrix}+(-1)^n\begin{vmatrix} a & -b & c \\ a+1 & b+1 & c-1 \\ a-1 & b-1 & c+1 \end{vmatrix}=0$ both determinants are equal and their sum is zero when n is an  odd integer. © examsnet.com

question: If $\left|z-2\right|=\left|z-1\right|$ , where $z$ is a complex number, then locus   z is a straight line
search_text: if $\left|z-2\right|=\left|z-1\right|$ , where $z$ is a complex number, then locus   z is a straight line {'a': 'parallel to $x-$ axis', 'b': 'parallel to $y-$ axis', 'c': 'parallel to $y=x$', 'd': 'parallel to $y=-x$'} 2021 2021-08-19 shift_2 mathematics   9 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: $\because \left|z-2\right|=\left|z-1\right|$ let $z=x+iy$ , then $\rightarrow \left|x+iy-2\right|^{2}=\left|x+iy-1\right|^{2}$ $\rightarrow (x-2^{2}+y^{2}=(x-1)^{2}+y^{2}$ $\rightarrow x^{2}-4x+4=x^{2}-2x+1$ $\rightarrow -2x+4x=4-1$ $\rightarrow x=\frac{3}{2}$ which is parallel to y-axis. © examsnet.com

question: If $\left(\frac{1+i}{1-i}\right)^{m}=1$ , then m can not be equal to ______
search_text: if $\left(\frac{1+i}{1-i}\right)^{m}=1$ , then m can not be equal to ______ {'a': '1934', 'b': '2024', 'c': '2172', 'd': '$10^{100}$'} 2021 2021-08-19 shift_2 mathematics   10 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: $\left(\frac{1+i}{1-i}\right)^{m}=1$ $\rightarrow \left[\frac{(1+i)(1+i)}{(1-1)(1+i)}\right]^{m}=1$ $\rightarrow \left(\frac{1-1+2i}{1+1}\right)^{m}=1$ $\rightarrow i^{m}=1$ ⇒ m is multiple of $4\left[\because i^{4n}=1, \forall n \in n\right]$ option (a) is not a multiple of $.$ $\therefore m \neq 1934$ © examsnet.com

question: If $1+x^{2}=\sqrt{3}x$ , then $\sum\limits_{n=1}^{24}\left(x^{n}-\frac{1}{x^{n}}\right)^{2}$ is equal to
search_text: if $1+x^{2}=\sqrt{3}x$ , then $\sum\limits_{n=1}^{24}\left(x^{n}-\frac{1}{x^{n}}\right)^{2}$ is equal to {'a': '48', 'b': '-48', 'c': '-24', 'd': '24'} 2021 2021-08-19 shift_2 mathematics   11 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: given, $x^{2}-\sqrt{3}x+1=0$ $\rightarrow x=\frac{\sqrt{3}\pm\sqrt{3-4}}{2}$ $x=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\pm\frac{1}{2}i=\cos\frac{\pi}{6}+i\sin\frac{\pi}{6}$ $\rightarrow x^{2n}=\cos\frac{2n\pi}{6}\pm i\sin\frac{2n\pi}{6}$ $\rightarrow x^{2n}=\cos\frac{n\pi}{3}\pm i\sin\frac{n\pi}{3}$ and $x^{-2n}=\cos\frac{n\pi}{3}\pm i\sin\frac{n\pi}{3}$ now, $\left(x^{n}-\frac{1}{x^{n}}\right)^{2}=\left(x^{2n}+\frac{1}{x^{2n}}-2\right)$ $=-2+2\cos\frac{n\pi}{3}$ $\rightarrow\sum_{n=1}^{24}\left(x^{n}-\frac{1}{x^{n}}\right)^{2}=\sum_{n=1}^{24}\left(-2+2\cos\frac{n\pi}{3}\right)$ $=-48+2\left[\cos\frac{\pi}{3}+\cos\frac{2\pi}{3}+\dots+\cos\frac{24\pi}{3}\right]$ $=-48+2\left[\frac{\cos\left(\frac{2\pi}{3}+\frac{23\pi}{6}\right)\cdot\sin\frac{24\pi}{6}}{\sin\frac{\pi}{6}}\right]$ $=-48+2\cdot0=-48$ © examsnet.com

search_text: if $\theta \in [0, 2\pi]$ and $\cos 2\theta = \cos \theta + \sin \theta$ then the sum of all values of $\theta$ satisfying the equation is ______ {'a': '$\\frac{21\\pi}{2}$', 'b': '$\\frac{11\\pi}{4}$', 'c': '$\\frac{24\\pi}{4}$', 'd': '$\\frac{31\\pi}{4}$'} 2021 2021-08-19 shift_2 mathematics   23 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: $\cos 2\theta = \cos \theta + \sin \theta$ $\rightarrow (\cos^2 \theta - \sin^2 \theta) - (\cos \theta + \sin \theta) = 0$ $\rightarrow (\cos \theta + \sin \theta)(\cos \theta - \sin \theta - 1) = 0$ $\rightarrow \cos \theta + \sin \theta = 0$ or $\cos \theta - \sin \theta = 1$ when $\cos \theta + \sin \theta = 0$ , then $\tan \theta = -1$ $\text{then } \theta = n\pi + \frac{3\pi}{4}$ $\rightarrow \theta = \frac{3\pi}{4}, \frac{7\pi}{4} \in [0, 2\pi]$ and when $\cos \theta - \sin \theta = 1$ , then $\sin \theta + (1 - \cos \theta) = 0$ and $2 \sin \frac{\theta}{2} \left( \cos \frac{\theta}{2} + \sin \frac{\theta}{2} \right) = 0$ and $\sin \frac{\theta}{2} = 0, \cos \frac{\theta}{2} + \sin \frac{\theta}{2} = 0$ $\rightarrow \frac{\theta}{2} = n\pi, \tan \frac{\theta}{2} = -1$ $\rightarrow \frac{\theta}{2} = n\pi, \tan \frac{\theta}{2} = -1$ $\rightarrow \theta = 0, 2\pi \in [0, 2\pi]$ $\theta = \frac{6\pi}{4} \in [0, 2\pi]$ sum of all values of θ $= \frac{3\pi}{4} + \frac{7\pi}{4} + 0 + 2\pi + \frac{6\pi}{4} = \frac{24\pi}{4}$ © examsnet.com

search_text: if the acute angle between lines $a x^{2}+2 h x y+b y^{2}=0$ is $\frac{\pi}{4}$ , then $4 h^{2}=$ _______ {'a': '$a^{2}+4ab+b^{2}$', 'b': '$a^{2}+6ab+b^{2}$', 'c': '$(a-2b)(2a+b)$', 'd': '$a^{2}-6ab+b^{2}$'} 2021 2021-08-19 shift_2 mathematics   49 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: angle between pair of lines $a x^{2}+2 b x y+b y^{2}=0$ is given by $\tan \theta = \left| \frac{2 \sqrt{h^{2}-a b}}{a+b} \right|$ $\because \theta = \frac{\pi}{4}$ $\tan \frac{\pi}{4} = \left| \frac{2 \sqrt{h^{2}-a b}}{a+b} \right|$ $\rightarrow \left( \frac{a+b}{2} \right)^{2}=h^{2}-a b$ $\rightarrow a^{2}+b^{2}+2ab=4h^{2}-4ab$ $\rightarrow 4h^{2}=a^{2}+b^{2}+6ab$ © examsnet.com

search_text: the angle between the lines represented by $\cos \theta(\cos \theta+1) x^{2}-(2 \cos \theta+\sin^{2} \theta) x y+$ $(1-\cos \theta) y^{2}=0$ is ______ {'a': '$\\frac{\\pi}{4}$', 'b': '$\\frac{\\pi}{6}$', 'c': '$\\frac{\\pi}{3}$', 'd': '$\\frac{\\pi}{12}$'} 2021 2021-08-19 shift_2 mathematics   50 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: given pair of lines, $\cos \theta(\cos \theta+1) x^{2}-(2 \cos \theta+\sin^{2} \theta) x y +(1-\cos \theta) y^{2}=0$ comparing with $a x^{2}+2 h x y+b y^{2}=0$ $a=\cos \theta(\cos \theta+1)$ $h=-\frac{2 \cos \theta+\sin^{2} \theta}{2}$ $b=1-\cos \theta$ $a+b=\cos^{2} \theta+1$ $h^{2}-ab=\frac{4 \cos^{2} \theta+\sin^{4} \theta+4 \cos \theta \sin^{2} \theta}{4} - \cos \theta (1-\cos^{2} \theta)$ $=\frac{4 \cos^{2} \theta+(1-\cos^{2} \theta)^{2}+4 \cos \theta \sin^{2} \theta-4 \cos \theta \sin^{2} \theta}{4}$ $=\frac{\cos^{4} \theta+2 \cos^{2} \theta+1}{4}=\left(\frac{\cos^{2} \theta+1}{2}\right)^{2}$ if θ be the acute angle between the lines, then $\tan \theta=\frac{2 \sqrt{h^{2}-ab}}{|a+b|}=\frac{2\left(\frac{\cos^{2} \theta+1}{2}\right)}{\cos^{2} \theta+1}=1$ $\rightarrow \theta=\frac{\pi}{4}$ © examsnet.com

search_text: if $y=e^{x^{2}+e^{x^{2}+e^{x^{2}+\dots}}}$ then $\frac{d y}{d x}=$ {'a': '$\\frac{2 x}{1-y}$', 'b': '$\\frac{2 x y}{y-1}$', 'c': '$\\frac{2 x y}{1-y}$', 'd': '$\\frac{2 y}{y-1}$'} 2021 2021-08-19 shift_2 mathematics   67 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: $y=e^{x^{2}+e^{x^{2}+e^{x^{2}+\dots}}}$ $y=e^{x^{2}+y}$ taking log on both sides $\log y = x^{2}+y$ differentiating w.r.t. x $\frac{1}{y} \frac{d y}{d x}=2 x+\frac{d y}{d x}$ $\rightarrow \left(\frac{1}{y}-1\right) \frac{d y}{d x}=2 x$ $\frac{d y}{d x}=\frac{2 x y}{1-y}$ © examsnet.com

search_text: $\frac{d}{dx}\left(\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{\cos x}{1+\sin x}\right)\right)=$ {'a': '$\\frac{1}{2}$', 'b': '$-\\frac{1}{2}$', 'c': '1', 'd': '-1'} 2021 2021-08-19 shift_2 mathematics   68 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: $\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{\cos x}{1+\sin x}\right)=\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{\sin \left(\frac{\pi}{2}-x\right)}{1+\cos \left(\frac{\pi}{2}-x\right)}\right)$ $=\tan^{-1}\left[\frac{2 \sin \left(\frac{\pi}{4}-\frac{x}{2}\right) \cos \left(\frac{\pi}{4}-\frac{x}{2}\right)}{2 \cos ^{2}\left(\frac{\pi}{4}-\frac{x}{2}\right)}\right]$ $=\tan^{-1}\left[\tan \left(\frac{\pi}{4}-\frac{x}{2}\right)\right]$ $\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{\cos x}{1+\sin x}\right)=\frac{\pi}{4}-\frac{x}{2}$ $\therefore \frac{d}{dx}\left(\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{\cos x}{1+\sin x}\right)\right)=\frac{d}{dx}\left(\frac{\pi}{4}-\frac{x}{2}\right)=\frac{-1}{2}$ © examsnet.com

(i) w.r.t. x $\frac{2x}{a^{2}}+\frac{y}{2}\frac{dy}{dx}=0$ $\rightarrow \frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{-4x}{a^{2}y}=m_{1}$ (let) differentiating eq. (i) and (ii) meet each other at right angles $m_{1}m_{2}=-1$ $\rightarrow \frac{16}{3y^{2}}\cdot\frac{-4x}{a^{2}y}=-1$ $\rightarrow 64x=3a^{2}y^{3}$ $\rightarrow a^{2}=\frac{64x}{3y^{3}}$ $\rightarrow a^{2}=\frac{64x}{3\times16x}$ $\;\;\;\;\;\;$ [as $y^{3}=16x$ ] $\rightarrow a^{2}=\frac{4}{3}$ © examsnet.com

question: $\int \frac{1+x+\sqrt{x+x^{2}}}{\sqrt{x}+\sqrt{1+x}} d x =$
search_text: $\int \frac{1+x+\sqrt{x+x^{2}}}{\sqrt{x}+\sqrt{1+x}} d x =$ {'a': '$\\frac{1}{2} ( \\sqrt{1+x} ) + c$', 'b': '$\\sqrt{1+x} + c$', 'c': '$2 (1+x)^{\\frac{3}{2}} + c$', 'd': '$\\frac{2}{3} (1+x)^{\\frac{3}{2}} + c$'} 2021 2021-08-19 shift_2 mathematics   74 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: $\text{let } i = \int \frac{1+x+\sqrt{x+x^{2}}}{\sqrt{x}+\sqrt{1+x}} d x$ $= \int \frac{(1+x)+\sqrt{x} \sqrt{1+x}}{\sqrt{x}+\sqrt{1+x}} d x$ $= \int \frac{\sqrt{1+x} ( \sqrt{1} + x + \sqrt{x} )}{ ( \sqrt{1+x} + \sqrt{x} ) } d x$ $= \int \sqrt{1+x} d x$ $\text{let } 1+x = t^{2}$ $\rightarrow d x = 2 t d t$ $\therefore i = 2 \int t^{2} d t = \frac{2 t^{3}}{3} + c = \frac{2}{3} (1+x)^{\frac{3}{2}} + c$ © examsnet.com

question: $\int (\cos x) \log \cot \frac{x}{2} \, dx =$
search_text: $\int (\cos x) \log \cot \frac{x}{2} \, dx =$ {'a': '$(\\sin x) \\log \\cot \\frac{x}{2} + c$', 'b': '$(\\cos x) \\log \\cot \\frac{x}{2} + c$', 'c': '$(\\sin x) \\log \\cot \\frac{x}{2} + x + c$', 'd': '$(\\sin x) \\log \\cot \\frac{x}{2} - x + c$'} 2021 2021-08-19 shift_2 mathematics   75 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: $\text{let } i = \int \overset{ii}{(\cos x)} \overset{i}{\log \cot \frac{x}{2}} \, dx$ $= \log \cot \frac{x}{2} \cdot \int \cos x \, dx$ $- \int \left[ \frac{d}{dx} \left( \log \cot \frac{x}{2} \right) \int \cos x \, dx \right] dx$ $\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;$ [integrating by parts] $= \log \left(\cot \frac{x}{2}\right) \cdot \sin x - \int \frac{1}{\cot \frac{x}{2}} \cdot -\csc^2 \frac{x}{2} \cdot \frac{1}{2} \cdot \sin x \, dx$ $= (\sin x) \log \cot \frac{x}{2} + \int 1 \, dx$ $= (\sin x) \log \cot \frac{x}{2} + x + c$ © examsnet.com

search_text: $\int \sqrt{e^{4x}+e^{2x}} dx =$ {'a': '$\\frac{1}{2} e^{x}(\\sqrt{e^{2x}+1}) + \\frac{1}{2} \\sinh^{-1}(e^{x}) + c$', 'b': '$\\frac{1}{2} e^{x}(\\sqrt{e^{2x}+1}) + \\sinh^{-1}(e^{x}) + c$', 'c': '$\\frac{1}{2} (\\sqrt{e^{2x}+1}) + \\frac{1}{2} \\sinh^{-1}(e^{x}) + c$', 'd': '$\\sqrt{e^{4x}+e^{2x}} + \\sqrt{e^{2x}+1} + c$'} 2021 2021-08-19 shift_2 mathematics   76 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: $i = \int \sqrt{e^{4x}+e^{2x} d x} = \int e^{x} \sqrt{e^{2x}+1} dx$ pute $e^{x}=t$ $\rightarrow e^{x} dx = dt$ $\therefore i = \int \sqrt{t^{2}+1} dt$ $= \frac{1}{2} t \sqrt{t^{2}+1} + \frac{1}{2.1} \sinh^{-1}(t) + c$ $= \frac{1}{2} e^{x} \sqrt{e^{2x}+1} + \frac{1}{2} \sinh^{-1}(e^{x}) + c$ © examsnet.com

question: If $\int \frac{1}{1+\sin x} \, dx = \tan(f(x)) + c$ , then $f'(0)=$ _______
search_text: if $\int \frac{1}{1+\sin x} \, dx = \tan(f(x)) + c$ , then $f'(0)=$ _______ {'a': '0', 'b': '1', 'c': '$\\frac{1}{2}$', 'd': '$-\\frac{1}{2}$'} 2021 2021-08-19 shift_2 mathematics   77 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: $\int \frac{1}{1+\sin x} \, dx = \tan(f(x)) + c$ $\rightarrow \int \frac{1-\sin x}{\cos^2 x} \, dx = \tan(f(x)) + c$ $\rightarrow \int (\sec^2 x - \sec x \tan x) \, dx = \tan(f(x)) + c$ $\rightarrow \tan x - \sec x + c = \tan(f(x)) + c$ $\rightarrow \tan\left(\frac{\pi}{4} + \frac{x}{2}\right) = \tan(f(x))$ $\rightarrow -\tan\left(\frac{-\pi}{4} - \frac{x}{2}\right) = \tan(f(x))$ $\rightarrow f(x) = -\frac{\pi}{4} + \frac{x}{2}$ $\rightarrow f'(x) = \frac{1}{2}$ at $x=0, f'(0)=\frac{1}{2}$ © examsnet.com

question: The speed of ripples $(v)$ on water surface depends on surface tension $(\sigma)$ , density $(\rho)$ , and wavelength $(\lambda)$ . Then the square of speed $(v)$ is proportional to _____
search_text: the speed of ripples $(v)$ on water surface depends on surface tension $(\sigma)$ , density $(\rho)$ , and wavelength $(\lambda)$ . then the square of speed $(v)$ is proportional to _____ {'a': '$\\frac{\\sigma}{\\rho \\lambda}$', 'b': '$\\frac{\\rho}{\\sigma \\lambda}$', 'c': '$\\frac{\\rho}{\\sigma \\lambda}$', 'd': '$\\sqrt{\\frac{\\rho \\lambda}{\\sigma}}$'} 2021 2021-08-19 shift_2 physics   81 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: given, speed of ripple of water $=v$ surface tension $=\sigma$ density $=\rho$ wavelength $=\lambda$ as we know that, $\sigma=\frac{\text{force}}{\text{length}}$ and dimensional formula of $\sigma=\frac{[\text{mlt}^{-2}]}{[\text{l}]}=[\text{ml}^{0}\text{t}^{-2}]$ and dimensional formula of $\rho, v$ and λ are $[\text{ml}^{-3}\text{t}^{0}], [\text{m}^{0}\text{lt}^{-1}]$ and $[\text{m}^{0}\text{lt}^{0}]$ . let $[\sigma]=[\rho]^{a}[v]^{b}[\lambda]^{c}$ $\rightarrow [\text{ml}^{0}\text{t}^{-2}]=[\text{ml}^{-3}\text{t}^{0}]^{a}[\text{m}^{0}\text{lt}^{-1}]^{b}[\text{m}^{0}\text{lt}^{0}]^{c}$ $=[\text{m}^{a}\text{l}^{-3a+b+c}\text{t}^{-b}]$ $\rightarrow a=1$ $\rightarrow b=2$ $\rightarrow -3a+b+c=0$ $\rightarrow -3+2+c=0$ c = 1 $\therefore [\sigma]=[\rho]^{1}[v]^{2}[\lambda]^{1}$ hence, $\sigma \propto \rho v^{2} \lambda$ $\rightarrow v^{2} \propto \frac{\sigma}{\rho \lambda}$ © examsnet.com

search_text: a quarter horse power motor runs at a speed of 600 rpm. assuming $60\%$ efficiency, the work done by the motor in one rotation is _______ {'a': '7.46 j', 'b': '74.6 j', 'c': '111.9 j', 'd': '11.19 j'} 2021 2021-08-19 shift_2 physics   88 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: given, power of motor, $p=\frac{1}{4} \text{hp}$ $=\frac{1}{4} \times 746 \text{w}$ angular speed of motor $\omega=600 \text{rpm}$ $=600 \times \frac{2\pi}{60}=20\pi \text{rads}^{-1}$ ∴ time for one rev $=\frac{60}{600}=0.1 \text{s}$ efficiency, $n=\frac{60}{100}$ $\because p=\frac{w}{t}$ ∴ w (in 1 rotation) $=p \times t$ $=\frac{746}{4} \times \frac{1}{10}=18.65 \text{j}$ hence, work done by motor $=n \times w=\frac{60}{100} \times 18.65$ = 11.19 j © examsnet.com

search_text: a refrigerator with coefficient of performance $0.25$ releases $250 \text{j}$ of heat to a hot reservoir. the  work done on the working substance is _____ {'a': '$\\frac{100}{3}$ j', 'b': '150 j', 'c': '200 j', 'd': '50 j'} 2021 2021-08-19 shift_2 physics   102 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: given, coefficient of performance (cop) $=0.25$ heat coming out, $q_{c}=250 \text{j}$ since, $\text{cop} = \frac{q_{l}}{\text{work}(w)}$ $\rightarrow \text{cop} = \frac{q_{1}}{q_{h}-q_{1}}$ $\rightarrow \frac{q_{h}-q_{1}}{q_{2}} = \frac{100}{25} = 4$ $\rightarrow \frac{q_{h}}{q_{l}} - 1 = 4$ $\rightarrow \frac{q_{h}}{q_{l}} = 5$ $\rightarrow q_{l} = \frac{250}{5} = 50$ ∴ $w = q_{h} - q_{l}$ $= 250 - 50 = 200 \text{j}$ © examsnet.com

search_text: light of wavelength $300\,\text{nm}$ in medium a enters into medium b through a plane surface. if the frequency of light is $5\times10^{14}\,\text{hz}$ and the ratio of speed in medium a to that is medium b is $\frac{4}{5}$ , the absolute refractive index of medium bis, {'a': '1.6', 'b': '1.5', 'c': '1.3', 'd': '1.45'} 2021 2021-08-19 shift_2 physics   105 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: given, wavelength of light $a,\ \lambda_a=300\,\text{nm}$ $=300\times10^{-9}\,\text{m}$ frequency of light in $a,\ f_a=5\times10^{14}\,\text{hz}$ ratio of speed of light $\frac{v_a}{v_b}=\frac{4}{5}$ let $\mu_a,\ \mu_{\text{air}}$ and $\mu_b$ are refractive indexes of medium a, air and b respectively. ∵ absolute refractive index $=\frac{\mu_a}{\mu_{\text{air}}}$ $=\frac{\text{speed of light in air}(c)}{\text{speed of light in medium}a(v_a)}$ $\rightarrow \mu_a=\frac{3\times10^{8}}{f_a\lambda_a}$ $\rightarrow \mu_a=\frac{3\times10^{8}}{5\times10^{14}\times300\times10^{-9}}=0.2\times10^{1}=2$ now, $\frac{\mu_b}{\mu_a}=\frac{v_a}{v_b}$ $\rightarrow \mu_b=\mu_a\left(\frac{v_a}{v_b}\right)=2\left(\frac{4}{5}\right)=\frac{8}{5}=1.6$ © examsnet.com

search_text: charge on the outer sphere is q  and the inner sphere is grounded. the charge on the inner sphere is $q'$ , for $(r_{2}>r_{1})$ . then _____ {'a': "$q' r_{1}=q r_{2}$", 'b': "$q' q$", 'c': "$q' = \\frac{r_{1}}{r_{2}}q$", 'd': "$q' = -\\left(\\frac{r_{1}}{r_{2}}\\right)q$"} 2021 2021-08-19 shift_2 physics   108 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: given, charge on outer sphere $=q$ inner sphere is grounded. since, charge flows till potential $(v)$ becomes same. and $v=\frac{k q}{r}$ where, r is radius of sphere $(r_{2}>r_{1})$ . $\frac{k q'}{t_{1}}=\frac{-k q}{t_{2}}$ $\rightarrow q'=-q\left(\frac{r_{1}}{r_{2}}\right)$ © examsnet.com

question: Four capacitors with capacitances $C_{1}=1\;\mu\text{F}, C_{2}=1.5\;\mu\text{F}$ , $C_{3}=2.5\;\mu\text{F}$ and $C_{4}=0.5\;\mu\text{F}$ are connected as shown and are connected to a 30 volt source. The potential difference between points a and b is:
search_text: four capacitors with capacitances $c_{1}=1\;\mu\text{f}, c_{2}=1.5\;\mu\text{f}$ , $c_{3}=2.5\;\mu\text{f}$ and $c_{4}=0.5\;\mu\text{f}$ are connected as shown and are connected to a 30 volt source. the potential difference between points a and b is: {'a': '5 v', 'b': '9 v', 'c': '10 v', 'd': '13 v'} 2021 2021-08-19 shift_2 physics   109 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: given, $c_{1}, c_{2}, c_{3}$ and $c_{4}$ are $1\;\mu\text{f}, 1.5\;\mu\text{f}, 2.5\;\mu\text{f}$ and $0.5\;\mu\text{f}$ . supply voltage $=30\;\text{v}$ let $v_{ab}$ is potential across a and b, q is charge in circuit and $q_{1}, q_{2}$ are branch charges. since, series cquivalent capacitance $\frac{1}{c_{3}}=\frac{1}{c_{1}}+\frac{1}{c_{2}}$ $\rightarrow c_{1}=\frac{c_{1}c_{2}}{c_{1}+c_{2}}$ and in parallel connection voltages remain same $\therefore q_{1}=\frac{c_{1}c_{2}}{c_{1}+c_{2}}v$ $\rightarrow q_{1}=\frac{1 \times 1.5}{1+1.5} \times 30$ $=\frac{1.5}{2.5} \times 30 = 18\;\mu\text{c}$ similarly, $q=\frac{2.5 \times 0.5}{2.5+0.5} \times 30 = 12.5\;\mu\text{c}$ $\therefore v_{ab}=v_{a}-v_{b}=(v-v_{b})-(v-v_{a})$ $=\frac{q_{2}}{c_{3}}-\frac{q_{1}}{c_{1}}=\frac{12.5}{2.5}-\frac{18}{1}=-13\;\text{v}$ $\therefore v_{ba}=13\;\text{v}$ © examsnet.com

search_text: in a potentiometer of 10 wires, the balance point is obtained on the $6^{\text{th }}$ wire. to shift the balance point to $8^{\text{th }}$ wire, we should {'a': 'increase resistance in the main circuit', 'b': 'decrease resistance in the main circuit', 'c': 'increase resistance in series with the cell whose emf is to be measured', 'd': 'decrease resistance in series with the cell whose emf is to be measured'} 2021 2021-08-19 shift_2 physics   110 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: let length of each wire be $l$ . ∴ total length $=10 l$ at, 1 st balance point, $l_{1}: l_{2}=6 l: 4 l$ and as in case of potentiometer, $\frac{emf_{1}}{emf_{2}}=\frac{l_{1}}{l_{2}}$ i.e. $\varepsilon \propto l$ if $l$ increases, emf also increases and emf is only increased by increasing resistance $(r)$ in main circuir. © examsnet.com

question: In a co-axial, straight cable, the central conductor and the outer conductor carry equal currents in opposite directions. The magnetic field is zero ______
search_text: in a co-axial, straight cable, the central conductor and the outer conductor carry equal currents in opposite directions. the magnetic field is zero ______ {'a': 'outside the cable', 'b': 'inside the inner conductor', 'c': 'inside the outer conductor', 'd': 'in between the two conductors'} 2021 2021-08-19 shift_2 physics   111 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: according to question, construction of current and conductor is ∵ magnetic field due to straighr conductor, $(b)=\frac{1}{2\pi}\frac{\mu_0 i}{r}$ let $b_{\text{net}}, b_{1}$ and $b_{2}$ are net magnetic field,  magnetic field due to conductor 1 and 2 , respectively. $\therefore b_{\text{net}}=b_{1}-b_{2}=\frac{\mu_0 i}{2\pi}\left(\frac{1}{r_{1}}-\frac{1}{r_{2}}\right)$ $\because r_{2}>r_{1}$ ∴ $b_{\text{net}}$ will only be zero outside conductor or cable. © examsnet.com

question: The magnetic field, of a given length of wire for single tum coil, at its center is  B . then its value for two turns coil for the same wire is ____
search_text: the magnetic field, of a given length of wire for single tum coil, at its center is  b . then its value for two turns coil for the same wire is ____ {'a': '$\\frac{b}{4}$', 'b': '$\\frac{b}{2}$', 'c': '4 b', 'd': '2 b'} 2021 2021-08-19 shift_2 physics   112 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: given, initial magnetic field at centre of single  turn coil $=b$ final number of turn, $n_{2}=2$ let final magnetic field be b' $\because b=\frac{\mu_{0}}{2} \frac{i}{r}$ where, $\mu_{0}$ is permeability, i is current, r is radius, but length $l$ of conductor is same. $\rightarrow l=2\pi r=2 \times 2 \pi r'$ $\rightarrow r=\frac{r}{2}$ now, $b \propto \frac{n}{r}$ $\therefore \frac{b'}{b}=\frac{2}{\frac{r}{2}} \times \frac{r}{1}=4$ ⇒ b' = 4b © examsnet.com

Mutual inductance of the system is ______

(i.e., $m_{12}=m_{21}=m$ ) $\therefore m=(\mu_{0} n_{1} n_{2} a_{2} l)$ $=4 \pi \times 10^{-7} \times 1500 \times 4000 \times 2 \times 10^{-3} \times 60 \times 10^{-2}$ $=9.04 \times 10^{-3}=9.04 \text{mh} \simeq 9 \text{mh}$ © examsnet.com

question: A bulb of resistance $280~\Omega$ is supplied with a $200~\mathrm{V}~\mathrm{AC}$ supply. What is the peak current?
search_text: a bulb of resistance $280~\omega$ is supplied with a $200~\mathrm{v}~\mathrm{ac}$ supply. what is the peak current? {'a': 'nearly $1~\\mathrm{a}$', 'b': 'nearly $2~\\mathrm{a}$', 'c': 'nearly $1.4~\\mathrm{a}$', 'd': 'nearly $2.8~\\mathrm{a}$'} 2021 2021-08-19 shift_2 physics   114 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: given, resistance of bulb, $r=280~\omega$ supply voltage $v_{\mathrm{rms}}=200~\mathrm{v}$ as, $v_{\mathrm{rms}} = \frac{v_a}{\sqrt{2}} =$ root mean square speed $\rightarrow v_{0} = \sqrt{2} v_{\mathrm{rms}}$ where, $v_{0}$ is peak voltage, as,   v= ir $\therefore i_{0} = \frac{v_0}{r} = \frac{\sqrt{2} \times 200}{280} = \frac{5\sqrt{2}}{7} = 1.010~\mathrm{a}$ which is nearly 1 a. © examsnet.com

question: The magnetic field of a plane electromagnetic wave is given by $B=(400\mu\mathrm{T})\sin\left[(4.0\times10^{15}\,\mathrm{s}^{-1})\left(t-\frac{x}{c}\right)\right]$ . Average energy density corresponding to the electric field is _______
search_text: the magnetic field of a plane electromagnetic wave is given by $b=(400\mu\mathrm{t})\sin\left[(4.0\times10^{15}\,\mathrm{s}^{-1})\left(t-\frac{x}{c}\right)\right]$ . average energy density corresponding to the electric field is _______ {'a': '$8\\times10^{-3}\\,\\mathrm{jm}^{-3}$', 'b': '$31.8\\times10^{-3}\\,\\mathrm{jm}^{-3}$', 'c': '$80\\times10^{-3}\\,\\mathrm{jm}^{-3}$', 'd': '$3.18\\times10^{-3}\\,\\mathrm{jm}^{-3}$'} 2021 2021-08-19 shift_2 physics   115 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: given, equation of magnetic field, $b=400\mu\mathrm{t}\sin\left[4\times10^{15}\left(t-\frac{x}{c}\right)\right]$ ∴ average energy, $e_{av}=\frac{1}{2}\varepsilon_{0}e_{0}^{2}=\frac{1}{2}\frac{b_{0}^{2}}{\mu_{0}}$ where, $\varepsilon_{0}$ is free space permittiviry  and $\mu_{0}$ is free space permeability. $\therefore e_{av}=\frac{1}{2}\frac{b_{0}^{2}}{\mu_{0}}=\frac{1}{2}\times\frac{(400\times10^{-6})^{2}}{4\pi\times10^{-7}}=\frac{0.2}{\pi}$ $=63.66\times10^{-3}\,\mathrm{j}/\mathrm{m}^{3}$ © examsnet.com

question: The de Broglie wavelength associated with a proton under the influence of an electric potential of 100 volts is _____
search_text: the de broglie wavelength associated with a proton under the influence of an electric potential of 100 volts is _____ {'a': '1.227å', 'b': '2.86 pm', 'c': '12.27å', 'd': '$1.146 \\times 10^{-21}\\;\\mathrm{m}$'} 2021 2021-08-19 shift_2 physics   116 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: given, electric potential, $v=100\;\mathrm{v}$ since, $\lambda = \frac{h}{p} = \frac{h}{m c} = \frac{h}{\sqrt{2 m e}} = \frac{h}{\sqrt{2 m e v}}$ where, λ  is wavelength, h is planck's constant i.e. $6.63 \times 10^{-34}\;\mathrm{j s}^{-1}$ , m is mass of photon, c is speed and e is charge on proton $\therefore \lambda = \frac{6.63 \times 10^{-34}}{\sqrt{2 \times 1.67 \times 10^{-27} \times 1.6 \times 10^{-19} \times 200}}$ $= 0.203 \times 10^{-11}\;\mathrm{m}$ $= 2.03\;\pm$ it is near to $2.86\;\pm$ . © examsnet.com

search_text: the length of gemmanium rod is $0.925 \text{ cm}$ and its are of cross section is $1 \text{ mm}^{2}$ . if for germanium $n_{i}=$ $2.5 \times 10^{19} \text{ m}^{-3}, \mu_{h}=0.19 \text{ m}^{2} / \text{ v-s},$ $\mu_{e}=0.39 \text{ m}^{2} / \text{ v-s}$ , then the resistance of the rod  is________. {'a': '2.5ω', 'b': '4.0ω', 'c': '5.0ω', 'd': '10.0ω'} 2021 2021-08-19 shift_2 physics   119 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: given, length of germanium, $l=0.925 \text{ cm}$ $=0.925 \times 10^{-2} \text{ m}$ area of cross-section, $a=1 \text{ mm}^{2}$ $=(10^{-3} \text{ m})^{2}$ $=10^{-6} \text{ m}^{2}$ $n_{t}=2.5 \times 10^{19} \text{ m}^{-3}$ $\mu_{n}=0.19 \text{ m}^{2} / \text{ v-s}$ $\mu_{e}=0.39 \text{ m}^{2} / \text{ v-s}$ conductivity, $\sigma = n_{t} e (\mu_{e}+\mu_{n})$ $=2.5 \times 10^{19} \times 1.6 \times 10^{-19} (0.39+0.19)$ $=2.32 \text{ mho} \text{ m}^{-1}$ resistivity, $\rho = \frac{1}{\sigma} = 0.431 \ \omega \text{ -m}$ and resistance, $r = \frac{\rho l}{a}$ $= \frac{0.431 \times 0.925 \times 10^{-2}}{10^{-6}}$ $=0.3986 \times 10^{4}=3.9 \times 10^{3}$ $=4 \times 10^{3} \ \omega = 4 \text{ k} \ \omega$ © examsnet.com

question: If the energies of two light radiations $E_{1}$ and $E_{2}$ are $25\ \mathrm{eV}$ and $100\ \mathrm{eV}$ respectively, then their respective wavelengths $\lambda_{1}$ and $\lambda_{2}$ would be in the ratio $\lambda_{1}:\lambda_{2}=$ ______
search_text: if the energies of two light radiations $e_{1}$ and $e_{2}$ are $25\ \mathrm{ev}$ and $100\ \mathrm{ev}$ respectively, then their respective wavelengths $\lambda_{1}$ and $\lambda_{2}$ would be in the ratio $\lambda_{1}:\lambda_{2}=$ ______ {'a': '2 : 1', 'b': '4 : 1', 'c': '1 : 4', 'd': '1 : 2'} 2021 2021-08-19 shift_2 chemistry   122 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: we know that, energy $=\frac{h c}{\lambda}$ here, $h=$ planck's constant (js) $c=$ speed of light $\left(\frac{m}{s}\right)$ $\lambda=$ wavelength $(m)$ now for energy $e_{1}=25\ \mathrm{ev}$ $e_{1}=\frac{h c}{\lambda_{1}} \rightarrow 25=\frac{h c}{\lambda_{1}}$ ...(i) similarly for energy, $e_{2}=\frac{h c}{\lambda_{2}}$ $100=\frac{h c}{\lambda_{2}}$ ...(ii) by divide $e_{1}$ and $e_{2}$ , we get $\frac{25}{100}=\frac{\lambda_{2}}{\lambda_{1}}$ $\rightarrow \frac{1}{4}=\frac{\lambda_{2}}{\lambda_{1}}$ $\lambda_{1}:\lambda_{2}=4:1$ or $\lambda_{1}=4\lambda_{2}$ © examsnet.com

search_text: the electron configuration of $\mathrm{fe}^{3+}$ is _______ (atomic number of $\mathrm{fe}=26$ ) {'a': '$[\\mathrm{ar}] 3 d^{5} 4 s^{1}$', 'b': '$[\\mathrm{ar}] 3 d^{6} 4 s^{0}$', 'c': '$[\\mathrm{ar}] 3 d^{5} 4 s^{0}$', 'd': '$[\\mathrm{ar}] 3 d^{6} 4 s^{2}$'} 2021 2021-08-19 shift_2 chemistry   123 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: for general electonic configuration of metal, $\mathrm{fe}=1 s^{2}, 2 s^{2} 2 p^{6}, 3 s^{2} 3 p^{6} 3 d^{6}, 4 s^{2}$ now, for fe $=[\mathrm{ar}] 3 d^{6} 4 s^{2}$ $\mathrm{fe}^{2+}=[\mathrm{ar}] 3 d^{6} 4 s^{0}$ [remove $2 e^{-}$ from s-orbital first ] $\rightarrow \mathrm{fe}^{3+}=[\mathrm{ar}] 3 d^{6} 4 s^{0}$ $\mathrm{fe}^{3+}$ is denoted as ferric (iii) ion. © examsnet.com

search_text: the element with outer electronic configuration $(n-1) d^{2} n s^{2}$ , where $n=4$ , would belong to ______ {'a': '$2^{n d}$ period, $2^{n d}$ group', 'b': '$4^{t h}$ period, $4^{\\text{th }}$ group', 'c': '$4^{\\text{th }}$ period, $2^{n d}$ group', 'd': '$2^{n d}$ period, $4^{t h}$ group'} 2021 2021-08-19 shift_2 chemistry   124 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: for electronic configuration $=(n-1) d^{2} n s^{2}$ sum of electrons present in outer most orbital (d and s ) denoted group and period position is represented by principal quantum number. e.g. $(n-1) d^{2} n s^{2}$ group = number of valence electrons in d and s-orbital. sum of electrons in d and s orbital $=2+2=\{4\}$ ∴  number of electrons in d-orbital and valence shell $=4$ ∴ 4th group and 4th period. © examsnet.com

question: Two flasks A and B have equal volumes. A is maintained at $300\text{ K}$ and B at $600\text{ K}$ . Equal masses of $\mathrm{H}_{2}$ and $\mathrm{CO}_{2}$ are taken in flasks A and B respectively. Find the ratio of total K. E of gases in flask A to that of B
search_text: two flasks a and b have equal volumes. a is maintained at $300\text{ k}$ and b at $600\text{ k}$ . equal masses of $\mathrm{h}_{2}$ and $\mathrm{co}_{2}$ are taken in flasks a and b respectively. find the ratio of total k. e of gases in flask a to that of b {'a': '1 : 2', 'b': '11 : 1', 'c': '33 : 2', 'd': '55 : 7'} 2021 2021-08-19 shift_2 chemistry   131 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: formula of kinetic energy $=\frac{3 nrt}{2}$ total kinetic energy expression for a and b flask, $\mathrm{ke}_{a}=\frac{3 n_{a} rt_{a}}{2}$ and $\mathrm{ke}_{b}=\frac{3 n_{h} rt_{b}}{2}$ ...(i) let us consider common mass $=m$ $n_{a}=\frac{m}{2}$ and $n_{b}=\frac{m}{44}$ taking ratio (i) and (ii) we get, $\frac{\mathrm{ke}_{a}}{\mathrm{ke}_{b}}=\frac{n_{a} t_{a}}{n_{b} t_{b}}$ $\frac{\mathrm{ke}_{a}}{\mathrm{ke}_{b}}=\frac{ \frac{m}{\frac{2}{m}} \times 300 }{ \frac{44}{2} \times 600 }$ $[\mathrm{ke}_{a} : \mathrm{ke}_{b} = 11 : 1]$ © examsnet.com

question: For the redox reaction $\mathrm{MnO}_{4}^{-} + \mathrm{C}_{2} \mathrm{O}_{4}^{2-} + \mathrm{H}^{+} \rightarrow \mathrm{Mn}^{2+} + \mathrm{CO}_{2} + \mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}$ , the correct coefficients of the reactants for the balanced reaction are respectively $\mathrm{Mn} 0_{4}^{-}, \mathrm{C}_{2} \mathrm{O}_{4}^{2-}$ and $\mathrm{H}^{+}$ ______
search_text: for the redox reaction $\mathrm{mno}_{4}^{-} + \mathrm{c}_{2} \mathrm{o}_{4}^{2-} + \mathrm{h}^{+} \rightarrow \mathrm{mn}^{2+} + \mathrm{co}_{2} + \mathrm{h}_{2}\mathrm{o}$ , the correct coefficients of the reactants for the balanced reaction are respectively $\mathrm{mn} 0_{4}^{-}, \mathrm{c}_{2} \mathrm{o}_{4}^{2-}$ and $\mathrm{h}^{+}$ ______ {'a': '2,5,16', 'b': '16,3,12', 'c': '15,16,12', 'd': '2,16,5'} 2021 2021-08-19 shift_2 chemistry   133 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: the unbalanced redox reaction is $\mathrm{mno}_{4}^{-} + \mathrm{c}, \mathrm{o}_{4}^{2-} + \mathrm{h}^{+} \rightarrow \mathrm{mn}^{2+} + \mathrm{co}_{2} + \mathrm{h}_{2}\mathrm{o}$ (i) balanced c atoms $\mathrm{mno}_{\overset{+7}{4}} + \mathrm{c}_{2} \mathrm{o}_{4}^{2-} + \mathrm{h}^{+} \rightarrow \mathrm{mn}^{2+} + 2 \mathrm{co}_{2} + \mathrm{h}_{2}\mathrm{o}$ oxidation state of mn decreases from $+7$ to $+2$ . to balance the increase or decrease in oxidation number, multiply mn  containing species with 2 and c containing species with $5.$ $2 \mathrm{mno}_{4}^{-} + 5 \mathrm{c}_{2} \mathrm{o}_{4}^{2-} \rightarrow 2 \mathrm{mn}^{2+} + 10 \mathrm{co}_{2}$ (ii) balance $\text{'o'}$ atoms by adding 8 water molecules to the product side. $2 \mathrm{mno}_{4}^{-} + 5 \mathrm{c}_{2} \mathrm{o}_{4}^{2-} \rightarrow 2 \mathrm{mn}^{2+} + 10 \mathrm{co}_{2} + 8 \mathrm{h}_{2}\mathrm{o}$ (iii) balance 'h' atoms by adding $16 \mathrm{h}^{+}$ ions to the reactant side. $2 \mathrm{mno}_{4}^{-} + 5 \mathrm{c}_{2} \mathrm{o}_{4}^{2-} + 16 \mathrm{h}^{+} \rightarrow 2 \mathrm{mn}^{2+} + 10 \mathrm{co}_{2} + 8 \mathrm{h}_{2}\mathrm{o}$ hence, $\mathrm{mno}_{4}^{-} \rightarrow 2 \mathrm{c}_{2} \mathrm{o}_{4}^{2-} \rightarrow 5, \mathrm{h}^{+}=16$ © examsnet.com

question: When the temperature of 2 moles of an ideal gas is increased by $20^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ at constant pressure. find the work involved in the process.
search_text: when the temperature of 2 moles of an ideal gas is increased by $20^{\circ}\mathrm{c}$ at constant pressure. find the work involved in the process. {'a': '5r', 'b': '40r', 'c': '15r', 'd': '20r'} 2021 2021-08-19 shift_2 chemistry   134 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: temperature of an ideal gas increased by $=20^{\circ}\mathrm{c}$ i.e. $t_{2}$ initial temperature of gas, $t_{1}=0^{\circ}\mathrm{c}$ number of moles, $n=2$ formula of work done, $w=-nr(t_{2}-t_{1})$ $w=-2 r(20-0)$ $w=-40 r$ but work involved in the process, $w=+ve$ $w=40 r$ here, $r=$ rate constant i.e. $8.314\,\mathrm{jk}^{-1}\,\mathrm{mol}^{-1}$ $w=40 \times 8.314=332.56\,\mathrm{jk}^{-1}\,\mathrm{mol}^{-1}$ © examsnet.com

question: Using the data provided, find the value of equilibrium constant for the following reaction at $298\ \text{K}$ and 1 atm pressure. $\mathrm{NO}_{(g)} + \frac{1}{2} \mathrm{O}_{2(g)} \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{NO}_{2}(g)$ $\Delta_{f} H^{0}(\mathrm{NO}_{(g)}) = 90.4\ \text{kJ}\ \text{mol}^{-1}$ $\Delta_{f} H^{0}(\mathrm{NO}_{2(g)}) = 32.48\ \text{kJ}\ \text{mol}^{-1}$ $\Delta S^{0} \text{@} 298\ \text{K} = -70.8\ \mathrm{J\,K^{-1}\,mol^{-1}}$ $\operatorname{antilog}(0.50) = 3162$
search_text: using the data provided, find the value of equilibrium constant for the following reaction at $298\ \text{k}$ and 1 atm pressure. $\mathrm{no}_{(g)} + \frac{1}{2} \mathrm{o}_{2(g)} \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{no}_{2}(g)$ $\delta_{f} h^{0}(\mathrm{no}_{(g)}) = 90.4\ \text{kj}\ \text{mol}^{-1}$ $\delta_{f} h^{0}(\mathrm{no}_{2(g)}) = 32.48\ \text{kj}\ \text{mol}^{-1}$ $\delta s^{0} \text{@} 298\ \text{k} = -70.8\ \mathrm{j\,k^{-1}\,mol^{-1}}$ $\operatorname{antilog}(0.50) = 3162$ {'a': '$3.162 \\times 10^{4}$', 'b': '$3.162 \\times 10^{-4}$', 'c': '$3.162 \\times 10^{6}$', 'd': '$3.162 \\times 10^{7}$'} 2021 2021-08-19 shift_2 chemistry   135 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: $\mathrm{no}(g) + \frac{1}{2} \mathrm{o}_{2}(g) \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{no}_{2}(g)$ given, $\delta_{f} h^{0}(\mathrm{no}_{(g)}) = 90.4\ \text{kj}\ \text{mol}^{-1}$ $\delta h^{\circ} = \sigma \delta h^{\circ}$ product $-\sigma \delta_{f} h^{\circ}(\mathrm{no})$ $= 3248 - 90.4$ $= -57.92\ \text{kj}\ \text{mol}^{-1}$ we know that. standard gibb's free energy, $\delta g^{\circ} = \delta h^{\circ} - t \delta s^{\circ}$ $= -57.92 - 298 \times (-70.8)$ $= -57.92 + 21.098 = -36.82\ \text{kj/mol}$ $= -38.82 \times 10^{3}\ \text{j/mol}$ we also know, $\delta g^{\circ} = -2.303 rt \log k_{eq}$ here, $k_{eq} =$ equilibrium constant $-36.82 \times 10^{3} = -2303 \times 8.314 \times 298 \times \log k_{eq}$ $\log k_{eq} = \frac{36.82}{5.70584}$ $\log k_{eq} = 0.501$ $k_{eq} = \operatorname{antilog} 0.501$ $= 3162 \times 10^{6}$ © examsnet.com

search_text: calculate the poh of $0.10 \; \mathrm{m}  \mathrm{hcl}$ solution. {'a': '13', 'b': '1', 'c': '7', 'd': '14'} 2021 2021-08-19 shift_2 chemistry   136 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: $\mathrm{hcl}$ is the strongest acid, it dissociate into ions, $\underset{mole}{\underset{0.10}{\mathrm{hcl}}} \rightarrow \mathrm{h}\underset{mole}{\underset{0.10}{+}} + \mathrm{cl}\underset{mole}{\underset{0.10}{-}}$ we know that $\mathrm{ph} = -\log [\mathrm{h}^{+}]$ $\mathrm{ph} = -\log [0.10]$ ⇒ ph = 1 using formula of $\mathrm{ph} + \mathrm{poh} = 14$ at $273 \mathrm{k}$ , $1 + \mathrm{poh} = 14$ $\mathrm{poh} = 14 - 1 = 13$ © examsnet.com

search_text: if a, b, c are the angles of a triangle then the system of  equations $-x + y \cos c + z \cos b = 0$ , $x \cos c - y + z \cos a = 0,$ $x \cos b + y \cos a - z = 0$ {'a': 'only zero solution', 'b': 'a non-zero solution for all triangles $\\delta abc$', 'c': 'only zero solution but for certain values of $a, b, c$', 'd': 'a non-zero solution if $\\delta abc$ is an equilateral triangle & not for all triangles'} 2021 2021-08-20 shift_1 mathematics   5 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: $-x + y \cos c + z \cos b = 0$ $x \cos c - y + z \cos a = 0$ $x \cos b + y \cos a - z = 0$ $\delta = \begin{vmatrix} -1 & \cos c & \cos b \\ \cos c & -1 & \cos a \\ \cos b & \cos a & -1 \end{vmatrix}$ $= -1 (1 - \cos^{2} a)$ $+ \cos c (\cos a \cos b + \cos c)$ $+ \cos b (\cos a \cos c + \cos b)$ $= -1 + \cos^{2} a + 2 \cos a \cos b \cos c$ $+ \cos^{2} c + \cos^{2} b$ $= - \sin^{2} a + \cos^{2} b + \cos^{2} c$ $+ 2 \cos a \cos b \cos c$ clearly, $\delta > 0$ ⇒ system of equations has a non-zero solution. © examsnet.com

search_text: if $\tan \beta = \frac{\tan \alpha + \tan \gamma}{1 + \tan \alpha \tan \gamma}$ then $\frac{\sin 2\alpha + \sin 2\gamma}{1 + \sin 2\alpha \sin 2\gamma} =$ {'a': '$\\sin 2\\beta$', 'b': '$\\cos 2\\beta$', 'c': '$\\tan 2\\beta$', 'd': '$\\sec 2\\beta$'} 2021 2021-08-20 shift_1 mathematics   22 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: $\tan \beta = \frac{\tan \alpha + \tan \gamma}{1 + \tan \alpha \tan \gamma}$ $\tan \beta = \frac{\sin \alpha \cos \gamma + \sin \gamma \cos \alpha}{\cos \alpha \cos \gamma + \sin \alpha \sin \gamma}$ $\tan \beta = \frac{\sin(\alpha + \gamma)}{\cos(\alpha - \gamma)}$ $\frac{\sin 2\alpha + \sin 2\gamma}{1 + \sin 2\alpha \sin 2\gamma}$ $= \frac{2 \sin(\alpha+\gamma) \cos(\alpha-\gamma)}{1 + (2 \sin \alpha \cos \gamma)(2 \sin \gamma \cos \alpha)}$ $= \frac{2 \sin(\alpha+\gamma) \cos(\alpha-\gamma)}{1 + [\sin(\alpha+\gamma) + \sin(\alpha-\gamma)] [\sin(\alpha+\gamma) - \sin(\alpha-\gamma)]}$ $= \frac{2 \sin(\alpha+\gamma) \cos(\alpha-\gamma)}{1 + \sin^2(\alpha+\gamma) - \sin^2(\alpha-\gamma)}$ $= \frac{2 \sin(\alpha+\gamma) \cos(\alpha-\gamma)}{\sin^2(\alpha+\gamma) + \cos^2(\alpha-\gamma)}$ $= \frac{2 \tan \beta}{1 + \tan^2 \beta} = \sin 2\beta$ © examsnet.com

search_text: let $c$ be the circle with center $(0,0)$ and radius 3 units. the equation of the locus of the mid points of the chords of the circle $c$ that subtends an angle of $\frac{2\pi}{3}$ at its center is ______. {'a': '$x^2+y^2=\\frac{1}{4}$', 'b': '$x^2+y^2=\\frac{27}{4}$', 'c': '$x^2+y^2=\\frac{9}{4}$', 'd': '$x^2+y^2=\\frac{5}{4}$'} 2021 2021-08-20 shift_1 mathematics   54 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: let $a=(3\cos\theta, 3\sin\theta)$ then, $b=\left(3\cos\left(\theta+\frac{2\pi}{3}\right), 3\sin\left(\theta+\frac{2\pi}{3}\right)\right)$ let $(h, k)$ be the required point $2h=3\cos\theta+3\cos\left(\theta+\frac{2\pi}{3}\right)$ $=3\left[\cos\theta+\cos\theta\left(-\frac{1}{2}\right)-\sin\theta\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)\right]$ $=\frac{3}{2}(\cos\theta-\sqrt{3}\sin\theta)$ $\rightarrow\cos\theta-\sqrt{3}\sin\theta=\frac{4h}{3}$ $\rightarrow\sqrt{3}\cos\theta-3\sin\theta=\frac{4h}{\sqrt{3}}$ ...(i) $2k=3\sin\theta+3\sin\left(\theta+\frac{2\pi}{3}\right)$ $=3(\sin\theta+\sin\theta\left(\frac{-1}{3}\right)+\cos\theta\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)$ $=\frac{3}{2}(\sin\theta+\sqrt{3}\cos\theta)$ $\rightarrow\sqrt{3}\cos\theta+\sin\theta=\frac{4k}{3}$ ...(ii) $4\sin\theta=\frac{4}{3}(k-\sqrt{3}h)$ (from (i) and (ii)) $\sin\theta=\frac{k-\sqrt{3}h}{3}$ $\cos\theta=\frac{3k+\sqrt{3}h}{3\sqrt{3}}=\frac{\sqrt{3}k+h}{3}$ $\rightarrow\left(\frac{k-\sqrt{3}h}{3}\right)^2+\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}k+h}{3}\right)^2=1$ $\rightarrow k^2+3h^2-2\sqrt{3}hk+3k^2+h^2+2\sqrt{3}kh=9$ $\rightarrow4(k^2+h^2)=9 \rightarrow x^2+y^2=\frac{9}{4}$ © examsnet.com

search_text: if $\int \frac{(2x+1)^{6}}{(3x+2)^{8}} \, d x = p\left(\frac{2x+1}{3x+2}\right)^{q}+r$ , then $\frac{p}{q}=$ _______ {'a': '$\\frac{1}{7^{2}}$', 'b': '$\\frac{1}{7}$', 'c': '$7^{2}$', 'd': '7'} 2021 2021-08-20 shift_1 mathematics   77 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: $\int \frac{(2x+1)^{6}}{(3x+2)^{8}} \, d x$ $\int \left(\frac{2x+1}{3x+2}\right)^{6}\left(\frac{1}{3x+2}\right)^{2} \, d x$ $\text{let} \frac{2x+1}{3x+2}=t$ $\rightarrow \frac{(3x+42-(2x+1)3)}{(3x+2^{2})} = \frac{dt}{dx}$ $\rightarrow \left(\frac{1}{3x+2}\right)^{2} \, d x = d t$ $\rightarrow \int t^{6} \, d t = \frac{t^{7}}{7}+c$ $\rightarrow p=\frac{1}{7}, q=7$ $\frac{p}{q} = \frac{1}{49} = \frac{1}{7^{2}}$ © examsnet.com

question: The solution of the differential equation $2x\left(\frac{dy}{dx}\right)-y=4$ represents a family of ______
search_text: the solution of the differential equation $2x\left(\frac{dy}{dx}\right)-y=4$ represents a family of ______ {'a': 'ellipses', 'b': 'parabolas', 'c': 'straight lines', 'd': 'circles'} 2021 2021-08-20 shift_1 mathematics   80 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: $2x\frac{dy}{dx}-y=4$ $\frac{dy}{dx} - \left(\frac{y}{2x}\right) = \frac{4}{2x}$ $if = e^{\int \frac{-1}{2x}\,dx} = e^{\frac{\log x}{-2}} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{x}}$ $\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{x}} y\right) = \int \frac{2}{x\sqrt{x}}\,dx$ $\rightarrow \frac{y}{\sqrt{x}} = 2\left(\frac{x^{-\frac{3}{2}+1}}{-\frac{3}{2}+1}\right) + c$ $\frac{y}{\sqrt{x}} = 2\left(\frac{x^{-\frac{1}{2}}}{-\frac{1}{2}}\right) + c$ $y = c\sqrt{x} - 4$ $\rightarrow (y+4)^2 = c^2 x$ ⇒ represents a parabola. © examsnet.com

search_text: when a force $\vec{f}=17-2x+6x^{2}\,\text{n}$ acts on a body of mass $2\,\text{kg}$ and displaces it from $x=0\,\text{m}$ to $x=8\,\text{m}$ , the work done is ______ {'a': '1096 j', 'b': '270 j', 'c': '35 j', 'd': '135 j'} 2021 2021-08-20 shift_1 physics   86 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: given, force on body, $f=17-2x+6x^{2}$ mass of body, $m=2\,\text{kg}$ initial position, $x_i=0\,\text{m}$ final position, $x_f=8\,\text{m}$ since, work, $\int dw = \int f \cdot dx$ $=\int (17-2x+6x^2)\,dx$ $\rightarrow w = \left[ 17x - \frac{2x^2}{2} + \frac{6x^3}{3} \right]_{0}^{8}$ $= \left[ 17x - x^2 + 2x^3 \right]_{0}^{8}$ $= 17 \times 8 - 8^2 + 2 \times 8^3$ $= 1096\,\text{j}$ © examsnet.com

question: A sphere and a hollow cylinder without slipping, roll down two separate inclined planes $A$ and $B$ respectively. They cover same distance in a given duration. If the angle of inclination of plane $A$ is $30^{\circ}$ , then and the angle of inclination of plane $B$ must be _____ (approximately).
search_text: a sphere and a hollow cylinder without slipping, roll down two separate inclined planes $a$ and $b$ respectively. they cover same distance in a given duration. if the angle of inclination of plane $a$ is $30^{\circ}$ , then and the angle of inclination of plane $b$ must be _____ (approximately). {'a': '60°', 'b': '53°', 'c': '45°', 'd': '37°'} 2021 2021-08-20 shift_1 physics   89 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: moment of inertia of sphere and hollow cylinder are, $i_{\text{sphcre}}=\frac{2}{5}mr^{2}$ and $i_{\text{cylinder}}=mr^{2}$ angle of inclination, $\theta=30^{\circ}$ let, acceleration of body $=a$ friction force $=f$ mass of body $=m$ radius of body $=r$ $m g \sin \theta - f = m a$ ...(i) torque, $\tau = r f = i \alpha$ $\rightarrow f = \frac{i \alpha}{r}$ ...(ii) from eqs. (i) and (ii), we get $m g \sin \theta - \frac{i \alpha}{r} = m a$ angular acceleration, $\alpha = \frac{a}{r}$ $\rightarrow m g \sin \theta - \frac{i a}{r^{2}} = m a$ $\rightarrow m g \sin \theta = a \left( m + \frac{i}{r^{2}} \right)$ $a = \frac{m g \sin \theta}{m + \frac{i}{r^{2}}} = \frac{g \sin \theta}{1 + \frac{i}{m r}}$ ∵ distance covered by body, $s = \frac{1}{2} a t^{2}$ $\because s_{\text{sphere}} = s_{\text{cylinder}}$ $\frac{1}{2} a_{\text{sphere}} \times t^{2} = \frac{1}{2} \times s_{\text{cylinder}} \times t^{2}$ $\rightarrow a_{\text{sphcre}} = a_{\text{cylinder}}$ $\rightarrow \frac{g \sin 30^{\circ}}{1 + \frac{\frac{2}{5} m r^{2}}{m r^{2}}} = \frac{g \sin \theta}{1 + \frac{m r^{2}}{m r^{2}}}$ $\rightarrow \frac{ \frac{1}{2} }{ \frac{7}{5} } = \frac{ \sin \theta }{2} \rightarrow \sin \theta = \frac{5}{7}$ $\rightarrow \theta = \sin^{-1}\left( \frac{5}{7} \right) = 45.6^{\circ} \approx 45^{\circ}$ © examsnet.com

(i), we get $c' = \frac{360 \times 10^{-9}}{3.6 \times 10^{-3}} = 10^{-4}\;\mathrm{f}$ $\text{final potential stored in capacitor} = \frac{q_0}{c'}$ $= \frac{15 \times 10^{-3}}{10^{-4}} = 150\;\mathrm{v}$ hence, voltage difference $= 250 - 150 = 100\;\mathrm{v}$ © examsnet.com

search_text: an alloy of metals $x$ and $y$ weighs $12\,\text{g}$ and contains  atoms $x$ and $y$ in the ratio of $2:5$ . the percentage of metal $x$ in the alloy is 20 by mass. if the atomic mass of $x$ is 40 , what is the atomic mass of metal $y$ . {'a': '64 amu', 'b': '32 amu', 'c': '60 amu', 'd': '50 amu'} 2021 2021-08-20 shift_1 chemistry   132 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: mass of sample of alloy $=12\,\text{g}$ $\%$ of metal $x$ in sample $=20$ ∴ if $x$ is the mass of metal $x$ in sample $\frac{x}{12} \times 100 = 20$ $\rightarrow x = 2.4\,\text{g}$ if $y$ is the mass of metal $y$ in sample, then $y = 12 - 2.4 = 9.6\,\text{g}$ number of atoms of x $=\frac{6.022 \times 10^{23} \times 2.4}{40}$ $=361 \times 10^{22}$ ratio of atoms of $x$ and $y = 2:5$ number of atoms of $y = \frac{361 \times 10^{22} \times 5}{2}$ $=9.025 \times 10^{22}$ atoms $9.025 \times 10^{22}$ atoms of $y$ are present in $9.6\,\text{g}$ . $6.022 \times 10^{23}$ atoms of $y$ are present in $\frac{95}{9.025 \times 10^{22}} \times 6.022 \times 10^{23} = 64\,\text{g}$ atomic mass of $y = 64\,\text{amu}$ . © examsnet.com

search_text: an organic compound of molecular formula $\mathrm{c}_6\mathrm{h}_6\mathrm{br}_2$ has six carbon atoms in a ring system, two non-conjugate double bonds and two bromo groups at 1,4 positions. then the compound is ______ {'a': 'aromatic but non-homo-cyclic', 'b': 'aromatic and hetero-cyclic', 'c': 'homo-cyclic but not aromatic', 'd': 'neither homo-cyclic nor hetero-cyclic'} 2021 2021-08-20 shift_1 chemistry   141 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: for a compound to be aromatic, it must have $(4n+12)\pi$ -electrons, here, two double bonds and $4\pi$ -electrons are present in the compound. therefore, it is anti-aromatic. homocyclic compounds are ring structures that consist only of carbon atoms with in the ring. bromo group is attached to ring system as substituent, so $\mathrm{c}_6\mathrm{h}_6\mathrm{br}_2$ is homocyclic but not aromacic. hence, option, (c) is correct. © examsnet.com

search_text: using kjeldahl's method over $1 \mathrm{g}$ of a soil sample, the ammonia evolved could neutralize $25 \mathrm{ml}$ of $1 \mathrm{m} \mathrm{h}_{2}\mathrm{so}_{4}$ . then, the percentage of nitrogen present in the sample is _______ {'a': '100%', 'b': '60%', 'c': '70%', 'd': '25%'} 2021 2021-08-20 shift_1 chemistry   142 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: $25 \mathrm{ml}$ of $1 \mathrm{m} \mathrm{h}_{2}\mathrm{so}_{4}$ corresponds to $25 \mathrm{mmol}$ . it will neutralise 50 mol of $\mathrm{nh}_{3}$ . weight of $n = \frac{14 \times 50}{1000} \mathrm{g} = 0.70 \mathrm{g}$ thus $1 \mathrm{g}$ of sample of organic compound contains $0.70 \mathrm{g}$ of nitrogen. $\%$ of nitrogen in organic sample is $\frac{0.70}{1} \times 100 = 70 \%$ © examsnet.com

search_text: if $500\ \mathrm{ml}$ of $\mathrm{cacl}_{2}$ solution contains $3.01 \times 10^{22}$ chloride ions, molarity of the solution will be _____ {'a': '0.05 m', 'b': '0.01 m', 'c': '0.1 m', 'd': '0.02 m'} 2021 2021-08-20 shift_1 chemistry   147 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: $\mathrm{cacl}_{2} \rightarrow \mathrm{ca}^{2+}+2 \mathrm{cl}^{-}$ $\mathrm{cl}^{-}=3.01 \times 10^{22}\ \mathrm{ions}$ for $2 \mathrm{cl}^{-}=\frac{3.01 \times 10^{22}}{2}$ $=1.505 \times 10^{22}\ \mathrm{cacl}_{2}$ required mole $=\frac{1.505 \times 10^{22}}{6.02 \times 10^{23}}=\frac{0.25}{10}=0.025\ \mathrm{mol}$ molarity for $0.025$ mole of $\mathrm{cacl}_{2}$ $=\frac{0.025}{500} \times 1000=0.05\ \mathrm{m}$ © examsnet.com

search_text: if hydrogen electrons dipped in two solutions of $\mathrm{ph}=3$ and $\mathrm{ph}=6$ are connected by a salt bridge, the emf of the resulting cell is {'a': '$0.177\\,\\text{v}$', 'b': '$0.3\\,\\text{v}$', 'c': '$0.052\\,\\text{v}$', 'd': '$0.104\\,\\text{v}$'} 2021 2021-08-20 shift_1 chemistry   150 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: $\mathrm{ph}_{1}=3$ $\rightarrow [\mathrm{h}^{+}]_{1}=10^{-3}\,\text{m}$ $\mathrm{ph}_{2}=6$ $\rightarrow [\mathrm{h}^{+}]_{2}=10^{-6}\,\text{m}$ now, $e_{\text{cell}}=e^{\circ}_{\text{cell}}+\frac{0.059}{1}\log\frac{10^{-3}}{10^{-6}}$ $=0+0.059\times 3$ $e_{\text{cell}}=0.177\,\text{v}$ © examsnet.com

question: In an adsorption experiment, a graph between $\log\left(\frac{x}{m}\right)$ versus $\log P$ was found to be linear with a slope of $45^{\circ}$ . The intercept on $\log\left(\frac{x}{m}\right)$ axis was found to be $0.3010$ . The amount of gas adsorbed per gram of charcoal under a pressure of $0.5$ atm is
search_text: in an adsorption experiment, a graph between $\log\left(\frac{x}{m}\right)$ versus $\log p$ was found to be linear with a slope of $45^{\circ}$ . the intercept on $\log\left(\frac{x}{m}\right)$ axis was found to be $0.3010$ . the amount of gas adsorbed per gram of charcoal under a pressure of $0.5$ atm is {'a': '0.5 g', 'b': '1.0 g', 'c': '1.5 g', 'd': '0.75 g'} 2021 2021-08-20 shift_1 chemistry   151 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: $\frac{x}{m}=k p^{\frac{1}{n}} [\text{ adsorption}$ isotherm] $\log\frac{x}{m}=\log k+\frac{1}{n}\log p$ ∴ plot of $\log\frac{x}{m}$ vs $\log p$ is linear with slope $=\frac{1}{n}$ and intercept $=\log k$ hence, $\frac{1}{n}=\tan\theta=\tan 45^{\circ}=1$ i.e. $n=1$ $\log k=0.3010$ or $k=$ antilog $(0.3010)=2$ at $p=0.5\text{ atm}$ , $\frac{x}{m}=k p^{\frac{1}{n}} \rightarrow \frac{x}{m}=2 \times (0.5)^{1}=1.0$ © examsnet.com

search_text: the correct order of acidic strength among the following is _______ {'a': '$\\mathrm{fch}_{2}\\mathrm{co}_{2}\\mathrm{h} > \\mathrm{c}_6\\mathrm{h}_5\\mathrm{co}_{2}\\mathrm{h}$ $>\\mathrm{ch}_{3}\\mathrm{ch}_{2}\\mathrm{chclco}_{2}\\mathrm{h} > \\mathrm{ch}_3\\mathrm{co}_2\\mathrm{h}$', 'b': '$\\mathrm{c}_6\\mathrm{h}_5\\mathrm{co}_2\\mathrm{h} > \\mathrm{ch}_3\\mathrm{co}_2\\mathrm{h}$ $>\\mathrm{ch}_{3}\\mathrm{ch}_{2}\\mathrm{chclco}_{2}\\mathrm{h} > \\mathrm{fch}_{2}\\mathrm{co}_{2}\\mathrm{h}$', 'c': '$\\mathrm{ch}_{3}\\mathrm{ch}_{2}\\mathrm{chclco}_{2}\\mathrm{h} > \\mathrm{fch}_{2}\\mathrm{co}_{2}\\mathrm{h}$ $>\\mathrm{ch}_3\\mathrm{co}_2\\mathrm{h} > \\mathrm{c}_6\\mathrm{h}_5\\mathrm{co}_2\\mathrm{h}$', 'd': '$\\mathrm{fch}_{2}\\mathrm{co}_{2}\\mathrm{h} > \\mathrm{ch}_{3}\\mathrm{ch}_{2}\\mathrm{chclco}_{2}\\mathrm{h}$ $>\\mathrm{c}_6\\mathrm{h}_5\\mathrm{co}_2\\mathrm{h} > \\mathrm{ch}_3\\mathrm{co}_2\\mathrm{h}$'} 2021 2021-08-20 shift_1 chemistry   158 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: carboxylic acids are the most acidic compounds among the organic compounds. due to presence of electron withdrawing group i.e. chlorine and fluorine, $\mathrm{fch}_{2}\mathrm{cooh}$ and $\mathrm{ch}_{3}\mathrm{ch}_{2}\mathrm{chclcooh}$ are more acidic, than $\mathrm{c}_6\mathrm{h}_5\mathrm{cooh}$ and $\mathrm{ch}_3\mathrm{cooh}$ . fluorine is more electron withdrawing group than chlorine. therefore, $\mathrm{fch}_{2}\mathrm{cooh} > \mathrm{ch}_{3}\mathrm{ch}_{2}\mathrm{chclcooh}$ $>\mathrm{c}_6\mathrm{h}_5\mathrm{cooh} > \mathrm{ch}_3\mathrm{cooh}$ © examsnet.com

question: Let $f(x)=(x+2)^{2}-2, x \ge -2.$ Then $f^{-1}(x)=$
search_text: let $f(x)=(x+2)^{2}-2, x \ge -2.$ then $f^{-1}(x)=$ {'a': '$-\\sqrt{2+x}-2$', 'b': '$\\sqrt{2+x}+2$', 'c': '$\\sqrt{2+x}-2$', 'd': '$-\\sqrt{2+x}+2$'} 2021 2021-08-20 shift_2 mathematics   1 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: let $f(x)=y$ , then $x=f^{-1}(y)$ , here $y=(x+2)^{2}-2$ or $y+2=(x+2)^{2}$ $x+2=\sqrt{y+2}$ $\rightarrow x=\sqrt{y+2}-2$ $\therefore f^{-1}(y)=\sqrt{y+2}-2$ $\therefore f^{-1}(x)=\sqrt{x+2}-2$ © examsnet.com

search_text: if $' f'$ is the greatest integers function defined on $r$ as $f(x)= \lfloor x \rfloor$ and ' $g$ ' is the modulus function defined on $r$ as $g(x)= \lvert x \rvert$ , then the value of $(g \circ f)\left(\frac{-5}{3}\right)$ is {'a': '1', 'b': '2', 'c': '3', 'd': '4'} 2021 2021-08-20 shift_2 mathematics   2 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: $f(x)= \lfloor x \rfloor,\ g(x)= \lvert x \rvert$ $\text{now},\ f\left(-\frac{5}{3}\right) = \lfloor -\frac{5}{3} \rfloor$ $= \lfloor -1.667 \rfloor \approx -2$ then, $g\left(f\left(-\frac{5}{3}\right)\right)=g(-2)$ $(g \circ f)\left(-\frac{5}{3}\right)= \lvert -2 \rvert = 2$ $\therefore (g \circ f)\left(-\frac{5}{3}\right)=2$ © examsnet.com

question: If $f: R \rightarrow R$ and $g: R \rightarrow R$ are two functions defined by $f(x)=a x+b (a \neq 0) \forall x \in R$ and $g(x)=c x^{3}+d (c \neq 0) \forall x \in R$ , then $(fog)^{-1}(x)=$
search_text: if $f: r \rightarrow r$ and $g: r \rightarrow r$ are two functions defined by $f(x)=a x+b (a \neq 0) \forall x \in r$ and $g(x)=c x^{3}+d (c \neq 0) \forall x \in r$ , then $(fog)^{-1}(x)=$ {'a': '$\\left(\\frac{x-a d+b}{a c}\\right)^{1/2}$', 'b': '$\\left(\\frac{x+a d-b}{a c}\\right)^{1/3}$', 'c': '$\\left(\\frac{x-a d-b}{a c}\\right)^{1/3}$', 'd': '$\\left(\\frac{x+a d+b}{a c}\\right)^{1/3}$'} 2021 2021-08-20 shift_2 mathematics   3 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: given, $f(x)=a x+b$ and $g(x)=c x^{3}+d$ $f(g(x))=f(c x^{3}+d)$ $=a(c x^{3}+d)+b$ $(f og)(x)=a c x^{3}+a d+b$ ...(i) let $(fog)(x)=y$ , then $x=(fog)^{-1} y$ from eq. (i), we get $y=a c x^{3}+a d+b$ i.e. $a c x^{3}=y-a d-b$ $x^{3}=\frac{y-a-d-b}{a c}$ $x=\left[\frac{y-a d-b}{a c}\right]^{1/3}$ $\therefore (fog)^{-1}(y)=\left[\frac{y-a d-b}{a c}\right]^{1/3}$ or $(fog)^{-1}(x)=\left[\frac{x-a d-b}{a c}\right]^{1/3}$ © examsnet.com
