question: If the function $f(x)=a x^{3}+b x^{2}+26 x-24$ satisfies the conditions of Rolle's theorem in $[2,4]$ and $f'\left(3+\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\right)=0$ , then the value of $a b=$
search_text: if the function $f(x)=a x^{3}+b x^{2}+26 x-24$ satisfies the conditions of rolle's theorem in $[2,4]$ and $f'\left(3+\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\right)=0$ , then the value of $a b=$ {'a': '-9', 'b': '9', 'c': '-3', 'd': '3'} 2021 2021-08-23 shift_2 mathematics   73 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: $f(x)=a x^{3}+b x^{2}+26 x-24 \dots$ (i) on $[2,4]$ $\because f(x)$ satisfies the role's theorem $\rightarrow f(2)=f(4)$ $\rightarrow a(2)^{3}+b(2^{2})+26(2)-24$ $=a(4)^{3}+b(4)^{2}+26(4)-24$ $\rightarrow 8a+4b+28=64a+16b+80$ $\rightarrow 56a+12b+52=0$ $\rightarrow 14a+3b+13=0$ ...(ii) on differentiating eq. (i) w.r.t. $x$ $f'(x)=\frac{d}{dx}(a x^{3}+b x^{2}+26 x-24)$ $f'(x)=3 a x^{2}+2 b x+26$ at, $x=3+\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$ $f'\left(3+\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\right)=3a\left(3+\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\right)^{2}+2b\left(3+\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\right)+26$ $0=3a\left(9+\frac{1}{3}+\frac{6}{\sqrt{3}}\right)+6b+\frac{2b}{\sqrt{3}}+26$ $\rightarrow (28+6\sqrt{3})a+\left(\frac{6\sqrt{3}+2}{\sqrt{3}}\right)b+26=0$ $(28a+6b+26)+(18a+2b)\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$ ...(iii) $=0+0\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$ $28a+6b+26=0$ on comparing rational and irrational part, $18a+2b=0$ and $54a+6b=0$ and $\therefore 28a-54a+26=0$ $6b=-54a$ and $\rightarrow -26a+26=0$ $\rightarrow a=1$ $b=\frac{-54 \times 1}{6} \rightarrow b=-9$ $\therefore ab=-9$ $∴a b =-9$ © examsnet.com

search_text: $\int (1-\cos x) \csc^2 x \, dx =$ {'a': '$\\tan \\frac{x}{2} + c$', 'b': '$-\\tan \\frac{x}{2} + c$', 'c': '$2\\tan \\frac{x}{2} + c$', 'd': '$-2\\tan \\frac{x}{2} + c$'} 2021 2021-08-23 shift_2 mathematics   74 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: let $i=\int (1-\cos x) \csc^2 x \, dx$ $i=\int \csc^2 x \, dx - \int \cos x \cdot \csc^2 x \, dx$ $=-\cot x - \int \cos x \cdot \csc x \, dx$ $=-\cot x + \csc x + c$ $\frac{1-\cos x}{\sin x} + c$ $\left[\because 1-\cos x = 2 \sin^2 \frac{x}{2}\right]$ $\frac{2 \sin^2 \frac{x}{2}}{2 \sin \frac{x}{2} \cos \frac{x}{2}} + c$ $i=\tan \frac{x}{2} + c$ © examsnet.com

search_text: find the value of $k$ if $\int \cos^{k}(x) \sin(x) dx = \frac{-1}{4} \cos^{4}(x) + c$ {'a': '4', 'b': '3', 'c': '2', 'd': '1'} 2021 2021-08-23 shift_2 mathematics   75 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: to find $k$ given, $\int \cos^{k}(x) \sin(x) dx = \frac{-1}{4} \cos^{4}(x) + c$ let $i = \int \cos^{k}(x) \sin(x) dx$ let $\cos x = t$ $\rightarrow -\sin x dx = dt$ $\rightarrow \sin x dx = -dt$ $\therefore i = -\int t^{k} dt$ $i = \frac{-t^{k+1}}{k+1} + c$ $i = \frac{-\cos^{k+1} x}{k+1} + c$ $= \frac{-1}{4} \cos^{4}(x) + c$ $\rightarrow k+1=4 \rightarrow k=3$ © examsnet.com

search_text: if $f'(x)=\tan^{2}(x)+\cot^{2}(x)$ and $f\left(\frac{\pi}{4}\right)=0$ , then $f(x)=$ {'a': '$\\tan(x)-\\cot(x)-x+\\frac{\\pi}{2}$', 'b': '$\\tan(x)-\\cot(x)-2x+\\frac{\\pi}{2}$', 'c': '$\\tan(x)+\\cot(x)-2x+\\frac{\\pi}{2}$', 'd': '$\\sec(x)-\\csc(x)-2x+\\frac{\\pi}{2}$'} 2021 2021-08-23 shift_2 mathematics   76 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: $f'(x)=\tan^{2}x+\cot^{2}x$ $\therefore f(x)=\int(\tan^{2}x+\cot^{2}x)\,dx$ $=\int\left(\frac{\sin^{2}x}{\cos^{2}x}+\frac{\cos^{2}x}{\sin^{2}x}\right)dx$ $=\int\frac{\sin^{4}x+\cos^{4}x}{\sin^{2}x\cdot\cos^{2}x}\,dx$ $=\int\frac{(\sin^{2}x+\cos^{2}x)^{2}-2\sin^{2}x\cdot\cos^{2}x}{\sin^{2}x\cdot\cos^{2}x}\,dx$ $=\int\frac{1}{\sin^{2}x\cdot\cos^{2}x}\,dx-\int2\,dx$ $=\int\frac{\sin^{2}x+\cos^{2}x}{\sin^{2}x\cdot\cos^{2}x}\,dx-2x+c$ $=\int\sec^{2}x\,dx+\int\csc^{2}x\,dx-2x+c$ $f(x)=\tan x-\cot x-2x+c$ $\because f\left(\frac{\pi}{4}\right)=0$ $\tan\frac{\pi}{4}-\cot\frac{\pi}{4}-2\left(\frac{\pi}{4}\right)+c=0$ $1-1-\frac{\pi}{2}+c=0\rightarrow c=\frac{\pi}{2}$ $\therefore f(x)=\tan x-\cot x-2x+\frac{\pi}{2}$ © examsnet.com

search_text: $\int\frac{\sin x-\cos x}{\sqrt{\sin 2 x}} d x=$ {'a': '$-\\log \\left|\\sin x-\\cos x+\\sqrt{\\sin 2 x}\\right|+c$', 'b': '$-\\log \\left|\\sin x+\\cos x-\\sqrt{\\sin 2 x}\\right|+c$', 'c': '$-\\log \\left|\\sin x+\\cos x+\\sqrt{\\sin 2 x}\\right|+c$', 'd': '$-\\log \\left|\\sin x-\\cos x-\\sqrt{\\sin 2 x}\\right|+c$'} 2021 2021-08-23 shift_2 mathematics   77 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: let $i=\int\frac{\sin x-\cos x}{\sqrt{\sin 2 x}} .d x$ $i=\int\frac{\sin x-\cos x}{\sqrt{1+2\sin x .\cos x-1}} d x$ $i=\int\frac{\sin x-\cos x}{\sqrt{(\cos x+\sin x)^2-1}} d x$ let $\sin x+\cos x=t$ $\rightarrow \cos x-\sin x=\frac{dt}{dx}$ $\rightarrow -(\sin x-\cos x) d x = d t$ $\rightarrow (\sin x-\cos x) d x = -d t$ $\therefore i=-\int\frac{dt}{\sqrt{t^2-1}}$ $\left[\because \int\frac{1}{\sqrt{x^2-a^2}} d x = \log \left|x+\sqrt{x^2-a^2}\right|+c \right]$ $=-\log \left|t+\sqrt{t^2-1}\right|$ $=-\log \left|\sin x+\cos x+\sqrt{(\sin x+\cos x)^2}-1\right|+c$ $i=-\log \left|\sin x+\cos x+\sqrt{\sin 2 x}\right|+c$ © examsnet.com

question: Find the particular solution of the following differential equation, given that $y=1$ when $x=0$ . $(1+x^{2}) \; \frac{dy}{dx}=e^{m(\tan^{-1}(x))}-y$
search_text: find the particular solution of the following differential equation, given that $y=1$ when $x=0$ . $(1+x^{2}) \; \frac{dy}{dx}=e^{m(\tan^{-1}(x))}-y$ {'a': '$x \\; e^{\\tan^{-1}(x)} = \\tan^{-1}(x)+1$', 'b': '$x\\; e^{\\tan^{-1}(x)} = \\tan^{-1}(x)-1$', 'c': '$y \\; e^{\\tan^{-1}(x)} = \\tan^{-1}(x)+1$', 'd': '$y\\; e^{\\tan^{-1}(x)} = \\tan^{-1}(x)-1$'} 2021 2021-08-23 shift_2 mathematics   80 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: (c) given, differential equation $(1+x^{2}) \; \frac{dy}{dx} \;\; =e^{m(\tan^{-1} x)}-y, y(0)=1$ $\; \frac{dy}{dx} \;\; =\; \frac{e^{m \tan^{-1} x}}{1+x^{2}}-\; \frac{y}{1+x^{2}}$ $\rightarrow \;\; \; \frac{dy}{dx}+y\left(\; \frac{1}{1+x^{2}}\right)=\; \frac{e^{m \tan^{-1} x}}{1+x^{2}} \;\;\; \cdot\cdot\cdot\cdot\cdot\cdot\cdot (i)$ on comparing with bernoulli's equation $\; \frac{dy}{dx}+p y=q$ $\rightarrow \;\; p=\; \frac{1}{1+x^{2}},$ $q=\; \frac{e^{m \tan^{-1} x}}{1+x^{2}}$ $\therefore \;\; i f=e^{\int p dx}=e^{\int\; \frac{1}{1+x^{2}} dx}=e^{\tan^{-1} x}$ solution $y$ eq. (i), we get $y \cdot i f=\int q \cdot i f dx+c$ $\rightarrow \;\; y \cdot e^{\tan^{-1} x}=\int\; \frac{e^{m \tan^{-1} x}}{1+x^{2}} \cdot e^{\tan^{-1} x} dx+c$ $\; \text{ put } \; \tan^{-1} x=t$ $\rightarrow \;\; \; \frac{1}{1+x^{2}} dx=dt$ $\rightarrow \;\; y \cdot e^{\tan^{-1} x}=\int e^{m t} \cdot e^{t} dt+c$ $\rightarrow \;\; y \cdot e^{\tan^{-1} x} \;\; =\; \frac{e^{(m+1) t}}{m+1}+c$ $\;\; =\; \frac{e^{(m+1) \tan^{-1} x}}{m+1}+c$ $\because \;\; y \;\; =1, \; \text{ when, } \; x=0$ $1 \cdot e^{0} \;\; =\; \frac{e^{(m+1) \cdot 0}}{m+1}+c$ $\rightarrow \;\; \;\; =\; \frac{1}{m+1}+c$ $c \;\; =1-\; \frac{1}{m+1}=\; \frac{m}{m+1}$ $\therefore \;\; y e^{\tan^{-1} x} \;\; =\; \frac{e^{(m+1) \tan^{-1} x}}{m+1}+\; \frac{m}{m+1}$ © examsnet.com

search_text: a small sphere is hung by a string fixed to a wall as shown  in the figure. the sphere is pushed from the wall by a stick.  the forces acting on the sphere are as shown. then,  identify the incorrect expression. {'a': '$p=w\\tan\\theta$', 'b': '$t=p+w=0$', 'c': '$t^{2}=p^{2}+w^{2}$', 'd': '$t=p+w$'} 2021 2021-08-23 shift_2 physics   85 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: as per given diagram, the sphere remains in equilibrium when, net horizontal and vertical forces are equal to zero. i.e., $\sum f_{x}=0 \rightarrow p-t\sin\theta=0$ $\rightarrow p=t\sin\theta$ ...(i) and $\sum f_{y}=0 \rightarrow w-t\cos\theta=0$ $w=t\cos\theta$ ...(ii) by dividing eq. question: A cylinder of mass $12\;\mathrm{kg}$ is sliding on plane with an initial velocity $20\;\mathrm{m}\,\mathrm{s}^{-1}$ . If the coefficient of friction between the surface and the cylinder is $0.5$ , before stopping. the cylinder describes a distance of ______

[i.e. final velocity, $v = 0$ ] using equation of motion, $v^{2} = u^{2} + 2 a s$ by substituting the value, we get $0 = (20)^2 + 2(-5) s$ $\rightarrow s = 40\;\mathrm{m}$ © examsnet.com

question: A body of mass $M$ is dropped from a height $h$ on a sand floor. If the body penetrates $x \text{ cm}$ into the sand, the average resistance offered by the sand to the body is ______
search_text: a body of mass $m$ is dropped from a height $h$ on a sand floor. if the body penetrates $x \text{ cm}$ into the sand, the average resistance offered by the sand to the body is ______ {'a': '$mg \\left( \\frac{h}{x} \\right)$', 'b': '$mg \\left( \\frac{x+h}{x} \\right)$', 'c': '$mg \\left( h + x \\right)$', 'd': '$mg \\left( \\frac{x-h}{x} \\right)$'} 2021 2021-08-23 shift_2 physics   90 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: given, mass of body $=m$ height above the sand floor $=h$ distance penetrated into sand $=x$ let $v$ be the velocity with which body strikes the surface. then, by equation of motion, we get $v^{2}=u^{2}+2 g h \rightarrow v^{2}=2 g h$ ...(i) $[\because$ initial velocity at highest point, $u=0]$ with this velocity $v$ , when body passes through the sand floor it comes to rest after travelling a distance $x$ . let $f$ be the resisting force acting on body. then, net downward force will be $f_{\text{net}}=mg-f$ by work-energy theorem, work done by all forces is equal to change in $\text{ke}$ , which gives $w = \delta k$ $f_{\text{net}} \times x = k_f - k_i$ $(mg-f) x = 0 - \frac{1}{2} m v^{2}$ $[\because \text{ final ke, } k_f = 0]$ $(mg-f) x = -\frac{1}{2} m v^{2}$ ...(ii) substituting the value from eq. (i) in eq. (ii), we get $\rightarrow mg x - f x = -\frac{1}{2} m (2 g h)$ $\rightarrow mg x - f x = -mg h$ $\rightarrow f x = mg x + mg h$ $\rightarrow f = mg \left( \frac{x+h}{x} \right)$ © examsnet.com

question: A disc of mass $4\text{ kg}$ and radius $0.4\text{ m}$ is rotating with angular velocity $30\text{ rads}^{-1}$ . When two point-masses, each $0.25\text{ kg}$ , are attached on the periphery of the disc, at diametrically opposite points, its angular velocity becomes _______
search_text: a disc of mass $4\text{ kg}$ and radius $0.4\text{ m}$ is rotating with angular velocity $30\text{ rads}^{-1}$ . when two point-masses, each $0.25\text{ kg}$ , are attached on the periphery of the disc, at diametrically opposite points, its angular velocity becomes _______ {'a': '$24\\text{ rads}^{-1}$', 'b': '$27\\text{ rads}^{-1}$', 'c': '$21\\text{ rads}^{-1}$', 'd': '$10\\text{ rads}^{-1}$'} 2021 2021-08-23 shift_2 physics   91 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: given, mass of disc, $m=4\text{ kg}$ radius of disc, $r=0.4\text{ m}$ initial angular velocity of disc, $\omega_{1}=30\text{ rad s}^{-1}$ mass of point-masses, $m=0.25\text{ kg}$ now, moment of inertia of disc, $i_{3}=\frac{1}{2}mr^{2}$ moment of inertia of disc and two point mass system, $i_{2}=\frac{1}{2}mr^{2}+2mr^{2}$ let $\omega_{2}$ be the final angular velocity. according to conservation of angular momentum, $i_{1}\omega_{1}=i_{2}\omega_{2}\rightarrow\omega_{2}=\frac{i_{1}\omega_{1}}{i_{2}}$ substituting the values, we get $\omega_{2}=\frac{\frac{1}{2}mr^{2}(30)}{\frac{1}{2}mr^{2}+2mr^{2}}$ $=\frac{\frac{1}{2}\times4\times(0.4)^{2}\times30}{\frac{1}{2}\times4\times(0.4)^{2}+2\times0.25\times(0.4)^{2}}$ $\omega_{2}=24\text{ rad/s}$ hence, the final angular velocity of system is $24\text{ rad/s}$ . © examsnet.com

question: If rotational inertia parameter of a body rolling down a rough inclined plane (of inclination $\theta$ and height $h$ ) without slipping is given by $\beta = \frac{I_{CM}}{MR^{2}}$ , then time taken by the body to reach the bottom of the inclined plane is given by ______
search_text: if rotational inertia parameter of a body rolling down a rough inclined plane (of inclination $\theta$ and height $h$ ) without slipping is given by $\beta = \frac{i_{cm}}{mr^{2}}$ , then time taken by the body to reach the bottom of the inclined plane is given by ______ {'a': '$t = \\frac{1}{\\sin\\theta} \\sqrt{\\frac{(1+\\beta) 2 h}{g}}$', 'b': '$t = \\frac{1}{\\cos\\theta} \\sqrt{\\frac{(1+\\beta) 2 h}{g}}$', 'c': '$t = \\frac{1}{\\sin\\theta} \\sqrt{\\frac{(1-\\beta) 2 h}{g}}$', 'd': '$t = \\frac{1}{\\sin\\theta} \\sqrt{\\frac{(1+\\beta) h}{g}}$'} 2021 2021-08-23 shift_2 physics   92 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: given, mass of body $=m$ radius $=r$ angle of inclination $=\theta$ height of inclined surface $=h$ also, $\beta = \frac{i_{cm}}{mr^{2}}$ using, the acceleration produced in body rolling down the inclined plane $a = \frac{g \sin\theta}{1+\frac{i_{cm}}{mr^{2}}} = \frac{g \sin\theta}{1+\beta}$ by using equation of motion, $s = u t + \frac{1}{2} a t^{2}$ where $u = 0$ (initial velocity) $t =$ time taken to reach at bottom. $s = 0 + \frac{1}{2} \frac{g \sin\theta}{(1+\beta)} t^{2}$ $\rightarrow t^{2} = \frac{2 s (1+\beta)}{g \sin\theta}$ but, from the diagram, $\frac{h}{s} = \sin\theta$ $\rightarrow s = \frac{h}{\sin\theta}$ substituting the value of $s$ , we get $t = \sqrt{\frac{2 h (1+\beta)}{g \sin^{2}\theta}}$ $= \frac{1}{\sin\theta} \sqrt{\frac{2 h (1+\beta)}{g}}$ © examsnet.com

question: A bob of a pendulum of length $0.5\ \mathrm{m}$ has a speed of $6\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ at its lowest point. Find the speed of the bob when the string of the pendulum makes $60^{\circ}$ with the vertical. (take $g=10\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$ )
search_text: a bob of a pendulum of length $0.5\ \mathrm{m}$ has a speed of $6\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ at its lowest point. find the speed of the bob when the string of the pendulum makes $60^{\circ}$ with the vertical. (take $g=10\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$ ) {'a': '$26\\ \\mathrm{m\\,s^{-1}}$', 'b': '$\\sqrt{31}\\ \\mathrm{m\\,s^{-1}}$', 'c': '$13\\ \\mathrm{m\\,s^{-1}}$', 'd': '$1.3\\ \\mathrm{m\\,s^{-1}}$'} 2021 2021-08-23 shift_2 physics   94 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: given, length of pendulum, $l=0.5\ \mathrm{m}$ speed at lowest point, $v_{1}=6\ \mathrm{m/s}$ angle made by string with vertical, $\theta=60^{\circ}$ in $\delta obc,\ \frac{oc}{ob}=\cos\theta=\cos 60^{\circ}$ $\frac{l-h}{l}=\cos 60^{\circ}$ $\rightarrow h =l(1-\cos 60^{\circ})$ $\rightarrow h =0.5\left(1-\frac{1}{2}\right)=0.25\ \mathrm{m}$ using law of conservation of mechanical energy, we get $k_{i}+u_{i}=k_{f}+u_{f}$ $\rightarrow \frac{1}{2} m v_{1}^{2}+0=\frac{1}{2} m v_{2}^{2}+m g h$ [taking initial potential energy at ground is equal to zero.] $\rightarrow \frac{1}{2} m v_{2}^{2} =\frac{1}{2} m v_{1}^{2}-m g h$ $\rightarrow v_{2}^{2} =v_{1}^{2}-2 g h$ substituting the values, we get $v_{2} =\sqrt{(6)^{2}-2\times10\times0.25}$ $=\sqrt{31}\ \mathrm{m/s}$ hence, the final velocity at an angle $60^{\circ}$ is $\sqrt{31}\ \mathrm{m/s}$ . © examsnet.com

question: The radius of earth is about $6400 \text{km}$ and that of mars is $3200 \text{km}$ . And mass of the earth is about 10 times mass of mars. An object weighs $200 \text{N}$ on the surface of earth. Then its weight on the surface of mars will be ______
search_text: the radius of earth is about $6400 \text{km}$ and that of mars is $3200 \text{km}$ . and mass of the earth is about 10 times mass of mars. an object weighs $200 \text{n}$ on the surface of earth. then its weight on the surface of mars will be ______ {'a': '80 n', 'b': '40 n', 'c': '20 n', 'd': '8 n'} 2021 2021-08-23 shift_2 physics   95 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: given, radius of earth and mars are $6400 \text{km}$ and $3200 \text{km}$ , respectively. mass of earth $=10$ (mass of mars) $m_e = 10 m_m$ we know that, acceleration due to gravity at surface of a planet is $g = \frac{gm}{r^2},$ where, $m =$ mass of planet and $r =$ radius of planet. taking the ratio of acceleration due to gravity of mars to earth, $\frac{g_m}{g_e} = \frac{ \frac{gm_m}{r_m^2} }{ \frac{gm_e}{r_e^2} }$ $= \frac{m_m}{m_e} \times \left( \frac{r_e}{r_m} \right)^2$ by substituting the values, we get $\frac{g_m}{g_e} = \frac{1}{10} \times \left( \frac{6400}{3200} \right)^2 = \frac{1}{10} \times 4$ $\rightarrow g_m = \frac{2}{5} g_e$ given, the weight on earth's surface, $w_e = m g_e = 200 \text{n}$ ∴ weight on the mars surface, $w_m = m g_m = \frac{2}{5} (m g_e)$ $= \frac{2}{5} \times 200 \text{n} = 80 \text{n}$ © examsnet.com

search_text: the gravitational field in a region is given by $\mathbf{i} = (5\hat{i}+12\hat{j})\,\mathrm{n\,kg^{-1}}$ . the change in the gravitational potential energy of an object of mass $3\,\mathrm{kg}$ when it is taken from the origin to a point $(8\,\mathrm{m},-2\,\mathrm{m})$ is {'a': '1 j', 'b': '16 j', 'c': '48 j', 'd': '3 j'} 2021 2021-08-23 shift_2 physics   96 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: given, gravitational field intensity, $\mathbf{i} = (5\hat{i}+12\hat{j})\,\mathrm{n\,kg^{-1}}$ mass of object, $m=3\,\mathrm{kg}$ we know that, change in potential energy from to $p(8\,\mathrm{m},-2\,\mathrm{m})$ is given by $\delta u = m \delta v = m \int\limits_{(0,0)}^{(8,-2)} \mathbf{i} \cdot d\mathbf{r}$ $=3 \int\limits_{(0,0)}^{(8,-2)} (5\hat{i}+12\hat{j}) \cdot (dx\,\hat{i}+dy\,\hat{j})$ $=3\left[5x+12y\right]_{(0,0)}^{(8,-2)}$ $\delta u = 3[40-24] = 48\,\mathrm{j}$ © examsnet.com

search_text: a particle of mass ' $m$ ' is under an influence of a force $\mathbf{f} = -k \mathbf{x} + \mathbf{f}_0$ . the particle when disturbed will oscillate ______ {'a': 'about $x=0$ with $\\omega = \\sqrt{\\frac{k}{m}}$', 'b': 'about $x=0$ with $\\omega = \\sqrt{\\frac{m}{k}}$', 'c': 'about $x = \\frac{f_0}{k}$ with $\\omega = \\sqrt{\\frac{k}{m}}$', 'd': 'about $x = \\frac{f_0}{k}$ with $\\omega \\neq \\sqrt{\\frac{k}{m}}$'} 2021 2021-08-23 shift_2 physics   97 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: given that, mass of particle $=m$ restoring force, $\mathbf{f} = (-k \mathbf{x} + \mathbf{f}_0) n$ $= -k \left(x - \frac{\mathbf{f}_0}{k}\right) = -k y$ $\left[\text{take, } x - \frac{\mathbf{f}_0}{k} = y\right]$ which is shm. we know that, at the mean position, $y = 0$ $x - \frac{\mathbf{f}_0}{k} = 0 \rightarrow x = \frac{\mathbf{f}_0}{k}$ $\therefore f = m a \rightarrow m a = -k y$ $m(-\omega^{2} y) = -k y \rightarrow \omega = \sqrt{\frac{k}{m}}$ frequency of shm, $\omega = \sqrt{\frac{k}{m}}$ © examsnet.com

question: One thousand small water drops of equal radii combine to form a big drop. The ratio of final surface energy to total initial surface energy is ______
search_text: one thousand small water drops of equal radii combine to form a big drop. the ratio of final surface energy to total initial surface energy is ______ {'a': '$1000:1$', 'b': '$1:1000$', 'c': '$10:1$', 'd': '$1:10$'} 2021 2021-08-23 shift_2 physics   98 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: let radius of big drop $=r$ radius of small drop $=t$ number of small drops, $n=1000$ in this process, the volume remains same $v_{f}=v_{i}$ $\rightarrow \frac{4}{3} \pi r^{3}=n\left(\frac{4}{3} \pi r^{3}\right)$ $\rightarrow r^{3}=1000 r^{3} \rightarrow r=10r$ ...(i) initial surface area, $a_{1}=n 4 \pi r^{2}$ final surface area, $a_{2}=4 \pi r^{2}$ now, increase in surface area, $\delta a=a_{2}-a_{1}=4 \pi [r^{2}-n r^{2}]$ we know that, surface energy, $se = ta$ [where, $t=$ surface tension of liquid $]$ according to question. $\frac{se_{f}}{se_{i}}=\frac{ta_{2}}{ta_{1}}=\frac{4 \pi r^{2}}{n(4 \pi r^{2})}$ $=\frac{r^{2}}{1000 r^{2}}$ [from eq. (i)] $=\frac{(10 r)^{2}}{1000 r^{2}}=\frac{100 r^{2}}{1000 r^{2}}=\frac{1}{10}$ or $1:10$ © examsnet.com

search_text: if the ratio of amplitudes of two interfering waves is $4:3$ , then the ratio of maximum and minimum intensity is: {'a': '16 : 18', 'b': '18 : 16', 'c': '49 : 1', 'd': '94 : 1'} 2021 2021-08-23 shift_2 physics   105 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: given, the ratio of amplitudes of two interfering waves is $4:3$ i.e., $\frac{a_{1}}{a_{2}}=\frac{4}{3}$ we know that, intensity of wave is proportional to square of amplitude. $\therefore \frac{i_{max}}{i_{min}} = \left(\frac{a_{max}}{a_{min}}\right)^{2}$ , where maximum and minimum amplitudes are $a_{max} = a_{1}+a_{2}$ and $a_{min} = a_{1}-a_{2}$ substituting the values, we get $\frac{i_{max}}{i_{min}} = \left(\frac{a_{1}+a_{2}}{a_{1}-a_{2}}\right)^{2}$ multiplying and dividing by $a_{2}^{2}$ in rhs, we get. $\frac{i_{max}}{i_{min}} = \left( \frac{ \frac{a_{1}}{a_{2}} + 1 }{ \frac{a_{1}}{a_{2}} - 1 } \right)^{2}$ $= \left( \frac{ \frac{4}{3} + 1 }{ \frac{4}{3} - 1 } \right)^{2}$ $= \left( \frac{7}{1} \right)^{2} = \frac{49}{1}$ © examsnet.com

search_text: among the following, which transition in the hydrogen spectrum would have the same wavelength as balmer  transition, $n=4$ to $n=2$ in $\mathrm{he}^+$ spectrum? {'a': '$n=4 \\rightarrow n=2$', 'b': '$n=3 \\rightarrow n=2$', 'c': '$n=4 \\rightarrow n=1$', 'd': '$n=2 \\rightarrow n=1$'} 2021 2021-08-23 shift_2 chemistry   123 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: we know that, $\frac{1}{\lambda}=r_{\mathrm{h}} z^{2}\left[\frac{1}{n_{1}^{2}}-\frac{1}{n_{2}^{2}}\right]$ for he, $(z=2)$ $\frac{1}{\lambda_{\mathrm{he}}} = r_{\mathrm{h}} (2)^{2}\left[\frac{1}{2^{2}}-\frac{1}{4^{2}}\right]$ $=r_{\mathrm{h}} 4\left[\frac{1}{4}-\frac{1}{16}\right]=r_{\mathrm{h}} 4 \times \frac{3}{16}$ $\rightarrow \frac{1}{\lambda_{\mathrm{he}}} = \frac{3}{4} r_{\mathrm{h}}$ for option (d), $n=1$ and $n_{2}=2$ $\frac{1}{\lambda_{\mathrm{h}}} = \frac{r_{\mathrm{h}}}{1} - \left[\frac{1}{1^{2}} - \frac{1}{2^{2}}\right] = \frac{3}{4} r_{\mathrm{h}}$ so, option (d) is correct. © examsnet.com

search_text: arrange $n, s, o \text{ and } f$ in order of decreasing electron gain enthalpy {'a': '$f>s>o>n$', 'b': '$n>o>s>f$', 'c': '$o>s>f>n$', 'd': '$s>o>n>f$'} 2021 2021-08-23 shift_2 chemistry   124 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: electron gain enthalpy increases with decrease in atomic size. on moving from left to right in the periodic table, the atomic size decreases and electron gain enthalpy increase for fluorine. in case of oxygen, due to its small size and compact nature, the incoming electron is not accommodated with ease resulting into low electron gain enthalpy than sulphur. so the correct order of electron gain    enthalpy is $f>s>o>n$ . © examsnet.com

search_text: which pair among the following does not have the same bond order? {'a': '$\\mathrm{cn}^{-} \\text{ and } \\mathrm{no}^{+}$', 'b': '$\\mathrm{cn}^{-} \\text{ and } \\mathrm{co}$', 'c': '$\\mathrm{o}_{2}^{2-} \\text{ and } \\mathrm{b}_{2}$', 'd': '$\\mathrm{o}_{2}^{+} \\text{ and } \\mathrm{no}^{+}$'} 2021 2021-08-23 shift_2 chemistry   127 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: we know that, $\text{bond order} = \frac{\text{number of } e^{-} \text{ s bonding orbital} - \text{number of } e^{-} \text{ s antibonding orbital}}{2}$ for $\mathrm{o}_{2}^{+}$ molecular orbital configuration of $\mathrm{o}_{2}^{+}$ is $\sigma 1s^{2} \sigma^{*} 1s^{2} \sigma 2s^{2} \sigma^{*} 2s^{2} \sigma 2p_{z}^{2} \pi 2p_{x}^{2} \approx \pi 2p_{y}^{2} \pi^{*} 2p_{x}^{1}$ number of electrons in bonding orbital $=10$ number of electrons in antibonding orbital $=5$ bond order of $\mathrm{no}_{2}^{+} = \frac{10-5}{2} = 2.5$ for $\mathrm{no}^{+}$ molecular orbital configuration is $\sigma 1s^{2} \sigma^{*} 1s^{2} \sigma 2s^{2} \sigma^{*} 2s^{2} \pi 2p_{x}^{2} \pi 2p_{y}^{2} \sigma 2p_{z}^{2}$ number of electrons in bonding orbital $=10$ number of electrons in antibonding orbital $=4$ bond order $= \frac{10-4}{2} = 3$ so, $\mathrm{o}_{2}^{+}$ and $\mathrm{no}^{+}$ does not have same bond order. © examsnet.com

question: Pressure of $1\,\mathrm{g}$ ideal gas $X$ at $300\,\mathrm{K}$ is $2\,\mathrm{atm}$ . When $2\,\mathrm{g}$ of another gas $Y$ is introduced in the same vessel at same temperature, the pressure become 1 atm. The correct relationship between molar mass of $X$ and $Y$ is _____
search_text: pressure of $1\,\mathrm{g}$ ideal gas $x$ at $300\,\mathrm{k}$ is $2\,\mathrm{atm}$ . when $2\,\mathrm{g}$ of another gas $y$ is introduced in the same vessel at same temperature, the pressure become 1 atm. the correct relationship between molar mass of $x$ and $y$ is _____ {'a': '$m_{y}=2 m_{x}$', 'b': '$m_{y}=4 m_{x}$', 'c': '$m_{x}=4 m_{y}$', 'd': '$m_{x}=5 m_{y}$'} 2021 2021-08-23 shift_2 chemistry   131 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: given, initially, $p = 2\,\mathrm{atm},\ t = 300\,\mathrm{k}$ , $v = vl,\ m_{x} = 1\,\mathrm{g}$ finally, $p = 2+1 = 3\,\mathrm{atm},\ t = 300\,\mathrm{k}$ , $m_{y} = 2\,\mathrm{g},\ v = vl$ let molar mass of gas $x$ and $y$ be $m_{x}$ and $m_{y}$ respectively. applying ideal gas equation to initial and final conditions. initially, $2 \times v = \frac{1}{m_{x}} rt$ ...(i) finally, $3 \times v = \left( \frac{1}{m_{y}} + \frac{2}{m_{y}} \right) rt$ ...(ii) dividing (i) by (ii), we get $m_{y}=4 m_{x}.$ © examsnet.com

search_text: if the mole fraction of ethanol in a solution of ethanol in water is $0.050$ , then find the molarity of the given  solution. {'a': '$3.5\\text{ m}$', 'b': '$2.8\\text{ m}$', 'c': '$1.7\\text{ m}$', 'd': '$0.95\\text{ m}$'} 2021 2021-08-23 shift_2 chemistry   133 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: moles of ethanol $=0.050$ moles of water $=1-0.050=0.95\text{ mol}$ . mass of ethanol $=0.05 \times 46=2.3\text{ g}$ . mass of $h_2o =0.95 \times 18=17.1\text{ g}$ mass of solution $=2.3+17.1\text{ g}=19.4\text{ g}$ assuming, density of water $=1\text{ g/ml}$ volume of solution $=\frac{\text{mass of solution}}{\text{density}}$ $=\frac{19.4}{1}=19.4\text{ ml}=0.0194\text{ l}$ molarity of solution $=\frac{\text{number of moles of ethanol}}{\text{volume of solution (l)}}$ $=\frac{0.050}{0.0194}=2.57 \cong 2.8\text{ m}$ © examsnet.com

question: When the reaction $A + 2B \rightleftharpoons 2C + D$ was studied, it was observed that the initial concentration of $B$ was $1.5$ times that of $A$ , and the equilibrium concentrations of $A$ and $C$ were equal. Then $K_{c}$ for the given equilibrium equals _______
search_text: when the reaction $a + 2b \rightleftharpoons 2c + d$ was studied, it was observed that the initial concentration of $b$ was $1.5$ times that of $a$ , and the equilibrium concentrations of $a$ and $c$ were equal. then $k_{c}$ for the given equilibrium equals _______ {'a': '4.1', 'b': '0.3', 'c': '2.5', 'd': '1.8'} 2021 2021-08-23 shift_2 chemistry   135 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: $\begin{array}{llllllll} \text{a} & \text{+} & \text{2b} & \rightleftharpoons & \text{2c} & \text{+} & \text{d} & {} \\ \text{at t=0} & a & {} & \frac{3}{2}a & {} & 0 & {} & 0 \\ \text{at eq.} & a-x & {} & \frac{3}{2}(a-x) & {} & 2x & {} & x \end{array}$ given, $[a]=[c]$ $\rightarrow a-x=2x$ $\therefore x=\frac{a}{3}$ now, $k_{c}=\frac{[c]^{2}[d]}{[a][b]^{2}}$ $= \frac{ \left( \frac{2a}{3} \right)^{2} \times \frac{a}{3} }{ \left( a - \frac{a}{3} \right) \left( \frac{3a}{2} - \frac{2a}{3} \right)^{2} }$ $\therefore k_{c}=0.3$ © examsnet.com

(i), (ii) and (iii)] $\rightarrow \cos^2 \theta+9 \sin^2 \theta+6 \sin \theta \cos \theta+4 \cos^2 \theta+\sin^2 \theta+4 \cos \theta \sin \theta$ $=\cos^2 \theta+\sin^2 \theta-2 \sin \theta \cos \theta$ $\rightarrow 4 \cos^2 \theta+9 \sin^2 \theta+12 \sin \theta \cos \theta=0$ $\rightarrow (2 \cos \theta+3 \sin \theta)^2=0$ $\rightarrow 2 \cos \theta+3 \sin \theta=0$ $\rightarrow 3 \sin \theta=-2 \cos \theta$ $\rightarrow \frac{\sin \theta}{\cos \theta}=-\frac{2}{3}$ $\rightarrow \tan \theta=-\frac{2}{3}$ equation of line passing through $a(-5,-4)$ is $y+4=\tan \theta(x+5)$ $\rightarrow y+4=-\frac{2}{3}(x+5)$ $\rightarrow 3 y+12=-2 x-10$ $\rightarrow 2 x+3 y+22=0$ © examsnet.com

search_text: if the lengths of the tangents drawn from the point $(1,2)$ to the circles $x^{2}+y^{2}+x+y-4=$ 0 and $3 x^{2}+3 y^{2}-x-y-\lambda=0$ are in the ratio $3:4$ , then $\lambda=$ ______ {'a': '$\\frac{23}{4}$', 'b': '$\\frac{17}{4}$', 'c': '$-\\frac{28}{3}$', 'd': '$\\frac{19}{4}$'} 2021 2021-08-24 shift_1 mathematics   50 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: $c_{1}: x^{2}+y^{2}+x+y-4=0$ $c_{2}: 3 x^{2}+3 y^{2}-x-y-\lambda=0$ $\rightarrow x^{2}+y^{2}-\frac{x}{3}-\frac{y}{3}-\frac{\lambda}{3}=0$ ∴ length of tangent drawn by an external point is $\sqrt{s_1}$ . ∴ length of tangent drawn from $(1,2)$ to $c_{1}$ and $c_{2}$ are $l_{1}$ and $l_{2}$ respectively. $l_{1}=\sqrt{s_{1}}=\sqrt{1^{2}+2^{2}+1+2-4}$ $=\sqrt{1+4+1+2-4}=\sqrt{4}$ $l_{1}=2$ $\therefore l_{2}=\sqrt{s_{1}^{2}}=\sqrt{1^{2}+2^{2}-\frac{1}{3}-\frac{2}{3}-\frac{\lambda}{3}}$ $=\sqrt{4-\frac{\lambda}{3}}$ given that, $\frac{l_{1}}{l_{2}}=\frac{3}{4}$ $=\frac{2}{\sqrt{4-\frac{\lambda}{3}}}=\frac{3}{4}$ $\rightarrow 3 \sqrt{4-\frac{\lambda}{3}}=8$ $\rightarrow 9\left(4-\frac{\lambda}{3}\right)=64$ $\rightarrow 4-\frac{\lambda}{3}=\frac{64}{9}$ $\rightarrow 4-\frac{64}{9}=\frac{\lambda}{3}$ $\rightarrow \frac{36-64}{9}=\frac{\lambda}{3}$ $\lambda=-\frac{28}{3}$ © examsnet.com

search_text: if three consecutive vertices of a parallelogram are $a(4,3,5), b(0,6,0) c(-8,1,4)$ and $d$ is the fourth vertex, then the angle between $\overline{a c}$ and $\overline{b d}$ is {'a': '$\\cos^{-1}\\left(\\frac{65}{\\sqrt{149}\\,\\sqrt{161}}\\right)$', 'b': '$\\cos^{-1}\\left(\\frac{55}{\\sqrt{149}\\,\\sqrt{161}}\\right)$', 'c': '$\\cos^{-1}\\left(\\frac{73}{\\sqrt{149}\\,\\sqrt{161}}\\right)$', 'd': '$\\cos^{-1}\\left(\\frac{15}{\\sqrt{149}\\,\\sqrt{161}}\\right)$'} 2021 2021-08-24 shift_1 mathematics   59 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: given, $a(4,3,5, b(0,6,0), c(-8,1,4)$ and d are the vertices of a parallelogram let d be the point $(x, y, z)$ . ∴ diagonals of parallelogram bisect each other. ⇒ mid-point of $ac=$ mid point of bd $\left(\frac{4+(-8)}{2}, \frac{3+1}{2}, \frac{5+4}{2}\right)=\left(\frac{x+0}{2}, \frac{y+6}{2}, \frac{z+0}{2}\right)$ $\rightarrow \left(-2,2,\frac{9}{2}\right)=\left(\frac{x}{2}, \frac{y+6}{2}, \frac{z}{2}\right)$ $\rightarrow \frac{x}{2}=-2, \frac{y+6}{2}=2, \frac{z}{2}=\frac{9}{2}$ $x=-4, y=-2, z=9$ ∴ d is $(-4,-2,9)$ . now, $ac=pv$ of $c-pv$ of $a$ $=(-8\hat{i}+\hat{j}+4\hat{k})-(4\hat{i}+3\hat{j}+5\hat{k})$ $=-8\hat{i}+\hat{j}+4\hat{k}-4\hat{i}-3\hat{j}-5\hat{k}$ $=-12\hat{i}-2\hat{j}-\hat{k}$ bd = pv of d - pv of b $=(-4\hat{i}-2\hat{j}+9\hat{k})-(0\hat{i}+6\hat{j}+0\hat{k})$ $=-4\hat{i}-8\hat{j}+9\hat{k}$ let θ be the angle between $ac$ and $bd$ . then, $\cos \theta =\left|\frac{ac \cdot bd}{|ac|\,|bd|}\right|$ $=\left|\frac{(-12\hat{i}-2\hat{j}-\hat{k})\cdot(-4\hat{i}-8\hat{j}+9\hat{k})}{\sqrt{(12)^{2}+(2)^{2}+(1)^{2}}\,\sqrt{(4)^{2}+(8)^{2}+(9)^{2}}}\right|$ $\rightarrow \cos \theta =\left|\frac{48+16-9}{\sqrt{161\sqrt{149}}}\right|$ $\rightarrow \theta =\cos^{-1}\left(\frac{55}{\sqrt{149}\,\sqrt{161}}\right)$ © examsnet.com

question: Solve the differential equation: $\frac{dy}{dx}=e^{x+y}$
search_text: solve the differential equation: $\frac{dy}{dx}=e^{x+y}$ {'a': '$e^{x}+e^{y}=c$', 'b': '$e^{x}-e^{y}=c$', 'c': '$e^{x}+e^{-y}=c$', 'd': '$e^{x}-e^{-y}=c$'} 2021 2021-08-24 shift_1 mathematics   80 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: $\frac{dy}{dx}=e^{x+y}$ $\frac{dy}{dx}=e^{x} \cdot e^{y}$ $\rightarrow \frac{dy}{e^{y}}=e^{x} dx$ $e^{-y} dy=e^{x} dx$ integrating both sides, $\int e^{-y} dy=\int e^{x} dx$ $\rightarrow \frac{e^{-y}}{-1}=e^{x}+c$ $\rightarrow e^{x}+e^{-y}+c=0$ $\rightarrow e^{x}+e^{-y}=-c$ $\rightarrow e^{x}+e^{-y}=c$ when $c=-c$ $\rightarrow v_{av}=\frac{2 v_{1} v_{2}}{v_{1}+v_{2}}$ by substituting the values, we get $v_{av}=\frac{2 \times 18 \times 36}{18+36}$ $=\frac{2 \times 36 \times 18}{54}=\frac{72}{3} \text{m/s}$ © examsnet.com

question: Which of the following pairs of physical quantities possess same dimension?
search_text: which of the following pairs of physical quantities possess same dimension? {'a': 'force and surface tension', 'b': 'frequency and velocity gradient', 'c': 'angular speed and solid angle', 'd': "stefan's constant and plank's constant"} 2021 2021-08-24 shift_1 physics   81 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: we know that, the dimension formula of given physical quantities are [force] $=[\mathrm{mlt}^{-2}]$ [surface tension] $=[\mathrm{ml}^{0} \mathrm{t}^{2}]$ [frequency] $=[m^{0} l^{0} t^{-1}]$ [velocity gradient] $=[m^{0} l^{0} t^{-1}]$ [angular speed] $=[m^{0} l^{0} t^{-1}]$ [solid angle ] $=[m^{0} l^{0} t^{0}]$ [stefan's constant ] $=[\mathrm{ml}^{0} \mathrm{t}^{3} \mathrm{k}^{-4}]$ and [planck's constant ] $=[\mathrm{ml}^{2} \mathrm{t}^{-1}]$ hence, we found that only (frequency and velocity gradient ) pair has same dimensions. © examsnet.com

question: A train travels from city-A to city-B with a constant speed of $18\ \mathrm{m}\cdot\mathrm{s}^{-1}$ and returns back to city-A with a constant speed of $36\ \mathrm{m}\cdot\mathrm{s}^{-1}$ . Find its average speed during the journey.
search_text: a train travels from city-a to city-b with a constant speed of $18\ \mathrm{m}\cdot\mathrm{s}^{-1}$ and returns back to city-a with a constant speed of $36\ \mathrm{m}\cdot\mathrm{s}^{-1}$ . find its average speed during the journey. {'a': '$\\frac{72}{5}\\ \\mathrm{m}\\cdot\\mathrm{s}^{-1}$', 'b': '$\\frac{36}{3}\\ \\mathrm{m}\\cdot\\mathrm{s}^{-1}$', 'c': '$\\frac{72}{3}\\ \\mathrm{m}\\cdot\\mathrm{s}^{-1}$', 'd': '$\\frac{36}{5}\\ \\mathrm{m}\\cdot\\mathrm{s}^{-1}$'} 2021 2021-08-24 shift_1 physics   82 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: given that, specd of train from city- a to city-b. $v_1=18\ \mathrm{m/s}$ specd of train from city-b to city- a $v_2=36\ \mathrm{m/s}$ in this process, the distance travelled by train from a to b and b to a will be equal. now, using the expression of average speed for equal distance, we know $v_{\text{av}}=\frac{2 v_1 v_2}{v_1+v_2}$ by substituting the values, we get $v_{\text{av}}=\frac{2 \times 18 \times 36}{18+36}$ $=\frac{2 \times 36 \times 18}{54}=\frac{72}{3}\ \mathrm{m/s}$ © examsnet.com

question: What is the angle of banking of a railway track of radius of curvature $250\ \text{m}$ , if the maximum velocity of the train is $90\ \text{km p h}$ ? (use $g=10\ \text{m}\cdot\text{s}^{-2})$
search_text: what is the angle of banking of a railway track of radius of curvature $250\ \text{m}$ , if the maximum velocity of the train is $90\ \text{km p h}$ ? (use $g=10\ \text{m}\cdot\text{s}^{-2})$ {'a': '$\\theta = \\text{tan}^{-1}\\left(\\frac{1}{2}\\right)$', 'b': '$\\theta = \\text{tan}^{-1}\\left(\\frac{1}{3}\\right)$', 'c': '$\\theta = \\text{tan}^{-1}\\left(\\frac{1}{4}\\right)$', 'd': '$\\theta = \\text{tan}^{-1}\\left(\\frac{1}{5}\\right)$'} 2021 2021-08-24 shift_1 physics   83 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: given, radius of curvature, $r=250\ \text{m}$ maximum velocity of train, $v=90\ \text{kmh}^{-1}$ $=\frac{90 \times 5}{18}\ \text{m/s}=25\ \text{m/s}$ let $\theta$ be the angle of banking of railway track. then, by using an expression of maximum safe speed. $v_{2}=r g \tan \theta$ $\rightarrow \tan \theta = \frac{v^{2}}{r g}$ by substituting the values, we get $\tan \theta = \frac{(25)^{2}}{250 \times 10} = \frac{625}{2500} = \frac{1}{4}$ ∴ $\theta = \tan^{-1}\left(\frac{1}{4}\right)$ © examsnet.com

question: From the top of a tower $19.6\,\mathrm{m}$ high, a ball is thrown horizontally. If the line joining the point of projection to the point where it hits the ground makes an angle of $45^{\circ}$ with the horizontal, then the initial velocity of the ball is _____
search_text: from the top of a tower $19.6\,\mathrm{m}$ high, a ball is thrown horizontally. if the line joining the point of projection to the point where it hits the ground makes an angle of $45^{\circ}$ with the horizontal, then the initial velocity of the ball is _____ {'a': '$9.8\\,\\mathrm{m}\\cdot\\mathrm{s}^{-1}$', 'b': '$4.9\\,\\mathrm{m}\\cdot\\mathrm{s}^{-1}$', 'c': '$14.7\\,\\mathrm{m}\\cdot\\mathrm{s}^{-1}$', 'd': '$2.8\\,\\mathrm{m}\\cdot\\mathrm{s}^{-1}$'} 2021 2021-08-24 shift_1 physics   84 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: given that, height of tower, $h=19.6\,\mathrm{m}$ angle of line joining from point of projection to the point of ground with horizontal, θ = 45° in $\delta aob,\ \tan\theta=\frac{h}{r}$ $\tan 45^{\circ}=\frac{h}{r}$ $\rightarrow 1=\frac{h}{r}$ $\rightarrow r=h=19.6\,\mathrm{m}$ where, r be the horizontal distance. we know that, time taken to reach from point a to b, $t=\sqrt{\frac{2h}{g}}$ by substituting the values, we get $t=\sqrt{\frac{2\times 19.6}{9.8}}=2\,\mathrm{s}$ now, horizontal distance $=$ horizontal velocity $\times$ time ⇒ r = ut 19.6 = u × 2  [by substituting the values of r and t, we get] ∴ initial velocity, $u=9.8\,\mathrm{m/s}$ © examsnet.com

search_text: when a force $\overset{\rightarrow}{f}$ given by $\overset{\rightarrow}{f}=6\hat{i}-18\hat{j}+10\hat{k}$ acts on a body, it imparts an acceleration of $8 \mathrm{m} \dot{s}^{-2}$ . then find the mass of the body ______ {'a': '$\\frac{\\sqrt{115}}{4} \\ \\mathrm{kg}$', 'b': '$10\\sqrt{2} \\ \\mathrm{kg}$', 'c': '$\\frac{\\sqrt{115}}{2 \\ \\mathrm{kg}}$', 'd': '$\\frac{\\ 115}{2} \\ \\mathrm{kg}$'} 2021 2021-08-24 shift_1 physics   85 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: given that, force vector, $\overset{\rightarrow}{f}=6\hat{i}-18\hat{j}+10\hat{k}$ magnitude of force, $f = |f| = \sqrt{6^{2} + (-18)^{2} + 10^{2}}$ $= \sqrt{460} \mathrm{n}$ acceleration, $a = 8 \mathrm{m/s^2}$ by newton's law of motion, $f = m a$ $\rightarrow m = \frac{f}{a}$ by substituting the values, we get mass of body, $m = \frac{\sqrt{460}}{8} = \frac{\sqrt{115}}{4} \mathrm{kg}$ © examsnet.com

question: A car moving at a speed ' $v$ ' is stopped by a retarding force ' $F$ ' in a distance ' $s$ '. If the retarding force were $3 F$ , the car will be stopped in a distance ______
search_text: a car moving at a speed ' $v$ ' is stopped by a retarding force ' $f$ ' in a distance ' $s$ '. if the retarding force were $3 f$ , the car will be stopped in a distance ______ {'a': '$\\frac{s}{3}$', 'b': '$\\frac{s}{6}$', 'c': '$\\frac{s}{9}$', 'd': '$\\frac{s}{12}$'} 2021 2021-08-24 shift_1 physics   86 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: given that, initial speed of car, $v_i=v$ final speed of car when it stops, $v_f=0$ distance travelled $=s$ retarding force $=f$ by newton's law of motion, $f = m a = m \left( \frac{v_i^2 - v_i^2}{2 s} \right)$ ...(i) $\begin{bmatrix} \text{using relation} \\ a = \frac{v_f^2 - v_i^2}{2 s} \end{bmatrix}$ $= \frac{m (-v^2)}{2 s}$ $f = \frac{-m v^2}{2 s}$ when, retarding force, $f' = 3 f$ let $s'=$ new distance travelled. similarly, from eq. (i) we can write $3 f = \frac{-m v^2}{2 s'}$ ...(ii) substituting value of f from eq. (i) into eq. (ii), we get $3 \left( \frac{-m v^2}{2 s} \right) = \frac{-m v^2}{2 s^2}$ ⇒ $s' = \frac{s}{3}$ hence, the body will stop by travelling distance $\frac{s}{3}$ , when retarding force is $3 f$ . © examsnet.com

search_text: find the angle between the vectors $\vec{a}=2\hat{i}+4\hat{j}+4\hat{k}$ and $\vec{b}=4\hat{i}+2\hat{j}-4\hat{k}$ . {'a': '0°', 'b': '45°', 'c': '60°', 'd': '90°'} 2021 2021-08-24 shift_1 physics   88 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: given, $\vec{a}=2\hat{i}+4\hat{j}+4\hat{k}$ and $\vec{b}=4\hat{i}+2\hat{j}-4\hat{k}$ . let $\theta$ be the angle between $a$ and $b$ . by using dot product, $a \cdot b = ab \cos \theta$ , where, a and b are magnitudes of a and b respectively. now, $a=\sqrt{2^{2}+4^{2}+4^{2}}=6$ $b=\sqrt{4^{2}+2^{2}+(-4)^{2}}=6$ substituting the values, in dot product, we get $(2\hat{i}+4\hat{j}+4\hat{k}) \cdot (4\hat{i}+2\hat{j}-4\hat{k}) = (6)$ (6) $\cos \theta$ $8+8-16=36 \cos \theta$ cosθ = 0 ⇒ θ = 90° © examsnet.com

question: A thin rod of mass ' $m$ ' and length ' $2 l$ ' is made to rotate about an axis passing through its centre and perpendicular to it. Its angular velocity changes from 0 to $\omega$ in time ' $t$ '. What is the torque acting on the rod?
search_text: a thin rod of mass ' $m$ ' and length ' $2 l$ ' is made to rotate about an axis passing through its centre and perpendicular to it. its angular velocity changes from 0 to $\omega$ in time ' $t$ '. what is the torque acting on the rod? {'a': '$\\frac{m l^{2} \\omega}{12 t}$', 'b': '$\\frac{m l^{2} \\omega}{t}$', 'c': '$\\frac{m l^{2} \\omega}{3 t}$', 'd': '$\\frac{4m l^{2} \\omega}{3 t}$'} 2021 2021-08-24 shift_1 physics   90 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: given that, mass of rod $=m$ length of rod, $l=21$ initial and final angular velocities are 0 and $\omega$ respectively, time taken $=t$ we know that, torque acting on body having moment of inertia $(i)$ and angular acceleration $(\alpha)$ is $\tau = l \alpha$ where, $i = \frac{1}{12} ml^{2} = \frac{1}{12} m(2)^{2}$ $= \frac{1}{3} m l^{2}$ and $\alpha = \frac{\omega_{f} - \omega_{i}}{t} = \frac{\omega - 0}{t} = \frac{\omega}{t}$ now, substituting the values, we get $\tau = \frac{1}{3} m l^{2} \frac{\omega}{t}$ © examsnet.com

question: A flywheel having moment of inertia $10 \text{ kg} \cdot \text{m}^{2}$ is rotating at $50 \text{ rad} \cdot \text{s}^{-1}$ . What amount of work needs to be done in order to bring this flywheel to rest in 10 seconds?
search_text: a flywheel having moment of inertia $10 \text{ kg} \cdot \text{m}^{2}$ is rotating at $50 \text{ rad} \cdot \text{s}^{-1}$ . what amount of work needs to be done in order to bring this flywheel to rest in 10 seconds? {'a': '$11400 \\text{ j}$', 'b': '$12500 \\text{ j}$', 'c': '$13000 \\text{ j}$', 'd': '$14500 \\text{ j}$'} 2021 2021-08-24 shift_1 physics   91 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: given that, moment of inertia, $i=10 \text{ kg}\cdot\text{m}^{2}$ initial angular velocity, $\omega_{0}=50 \text{ rad} / \text{s}$ final angular velocity, $\omega=0$ time taken to stop wheel, $t=10 \text{ s}$ we know that, work done by torque = change of rotational ke $w=\delta \text{ke}=k_f - k_i$ $w=\frac{1}{2} i \omega^{2} - \frac{1}{2} i \omega_{a}^{2}$ $w=0-\frac{1}{2} \times 10 \times (50)^{2}$ = -12500 j so, amount of work done to bring the flywheel to rest is $12500 \text{ j}$ . © examsnet.com

question: Two particles ' $P$ ' and ' $Q$ ' describe SHM of same amplitude ' $a$ ' and same frequency ' $f$ ' along the same straight line. The maximum distance between the two particles is $a \sqrt{2}$ . The phase difference between the particle is _____
search_text: two particles ' $p$ ' and ' $q$ ' describe shm of same amplitude ' $a$ ' and same frequency ' $f$ ' along the same straight line. the maximum distance between the two particles is $a \sqrt{2}$ . the phase difference between the particle is _____ {'a': 'zero', 'b': '$\\frac{\\pi}{2}$', 'c': '$\\frac{\\pi}{6}$', 'd': '$\\frac{\\pi}{3}$'} 2021 2021-08-24 shift_1 physics   92 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: given that, two particles p and q describes shm of same amplitude $a$ and frequency $f$ . let equation of motion of two particles are $x_{1}=a \sin \omega t$ and $x_{2}=a \sin (\omega t + \phi)$ where, $\phi$ be the phase difference. ∴ path difference, $x_{2}-x_{1}=a \sin (\omega t + \phi) - a \sin \omega t$ $x_{2}-x_{1}=2 a \sin \left( \frac{\omega t + \phi - \omega t}{2} \right) \cos \left( \frac{\omega t + \phi + \omega t}{2} \right)$ [using identity $\sin a - \sin b = 2 \sin \left( \frac{a-b}{2} \right) \cdot \cos \left( \frac{a+b}{2} \right) ]$ ∴ $x_{2}-x_{1}=2 a \sin \left( \frac{\phi}{2} \right) \cos \left( \omega + \frac{\phi}{2} \right)$ the distance $x_{2}-x_{1}$ will be maximum when $\cos \left( \omega t + \frac{\phi}{2} \right) = 1$ ∴ maximum distance $x_{2}-x_{1} = \sqrt{2} a$ $= 2 a \sin \frac{\phi}{2}$ $\rightarrow \sin \frac{\phi}{2} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$ $\rightarrow \sin \frac{\phi}{2} = \sin 45^{\circ}$ $\rightarrow \frac{\phi}{2} = 45^{\circ}$ phase difference, $\phi = 90^{\circ} = \frac{\pi}{2}$ © examsnet.com

question: A simple harmonic oscillation is represented by $x=A \cos \left(\omega t+\frac{\pi}{4}\right)$ . Its speed is maximum when ' $t$ ' equals _____
search_text: a simple harmonic oscillation is represented by $x=a \cos \left(\omega t+\frac{\pi}{4}\right)$ . its speed is maximum when ' $t$ ' equals _____ {'a': '$\\frac{\\pi}{2\\omega}$', 'b': '$\\frac{\\pi}{4\\omega}$', 'c': '$\\frac{\\pi}{\\omega}$', 'd': '$\\frac{2\\pi}{\\omega}$'} 2021 2021-08-24 shift_1 physics   93 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: given that, equation of a particle executing simple harmonic motion is $x=a \cos \left(\omega t+\frac{\pi}{4}\right)$ now, velocity of particle, $v=\frac{dx}{dt}$ $v=\frac{d}{dt}\left[a \cos \left(\omega t+\frac{\pi}{4}\right)\right]$ $=-a\omega \sin \left(\omega t+\frac{\pi}{4}\right)$ $v$ is maximum when $\sin \left(\omega t+\frac{\pi}{4}\right)=1$ $\sin \left(\omega t+\frac{\pi}{4}\right)=\sin \frac{\pi}{2}$ $\rightarrow \omega t+\frac{\pi}{4}=\frac{\pi}{2}$ $\rightarrow t=\frac{\pi}{4\omega}$ © examsnet.com

question: A communication satellite of $500\ \mathrm{kg}$ revolves around the earth in a circular orbit of radius $4.0 \times 10^{7}\ \mathrm{m}$ in the equatorial plane of the earth from west to east. The magnitude of angular momentum of the satellite is _____
search_text: a communication satellite of $500\ \mathrm{kg}$ revolves around the earth in a circular orbit of radius $4.0 \times 10^{7}\ \mathrm{m}$ in the equatorial plane of the earth from west to east. the magnitude of angular momentum of the satellite is _____ {'a': '$\\approx 0.13 \\times 10^{14}\\ \\mathrm{kg} \\cdot \\mathrm{m}^{2} \\cdot \\mathrm{s}^{-1}$', 'b': '$\\approx 1.30 \\times 10^{14}\\ \\mathrm{kg} \\cdot \\mathrm{m}^{2} \\cdot \\mathrm{s}^{-1}$', 'c': '$\\approx 0.58 \\times 10^{14}\\ \\mathrm{kg} \\cdot \\mathrm{m}^{2} \\cdot \\mathrm{s}^{-1}$', 'd': '$\\approx 2.58 \\times 10^{14}\\ \\mathrm{kg} \\cdot \\mathrm{m}^{2} \\cdot \\mathrm{s}^{-1}$'} 2021 2021-08-24 shift_1 physics   94 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: given that, mass of satellite, $m=500\ \mathrm{kg}$ radius of orbit, $r=4 \times 10^{7}\ \mathrm{m}$ now, the satellite is revolving in equatorial plane so, its time period will be equal to time period of  rotation of earth i.e., $t=24\ \mathrm{h}$ . ∴ angular velocity of satellite, $\omega = \frac{2\pi}{t}$ now, angular momentum, $l = m \omega r^{2} = m \left(\frac{2\pi}{t}\right) r^{2}$ $= 500 \times \left(\frac{2\pi}{24 \times 3600}\right) \times (4 \times 10^{7})^{2}$ $= 0.58 \times 10^{14}\ \mathrm{kg} \cdot \mathrm{m}^{2} \cdot \mathrm{s}^{-1}$ © examsnet.com

question: The rotation of the earth (of radius $R$ ) about its axis speeds up to a value such that a man at latitude angle $45^{\circ}$ feels weightlessness. The duration of a day in such a case is _______
search_text: the rotation of the earth (of radius $r$ ) about its axis speeds up to a value such that a man at latitude angle $45^{\circ}$ feels weightlessness. the duration of a day in such a case is _______ {'a': '$\\pi \\left( \\sqrt{\\frac{r}{g}} \\right)$', 'b': '$\\pi \\left( \\sqrt{\\frac{2r}{g}} \\right)$', 'c': '$\\frac{\\pi}{2} \\left( \\sqrt{\\frac{r}{g}} \\right)$', 'd': '$\\pi \\left( \\sqrt{\\frac{g}{r}} \\right)$'} 2021 2021-08-24 shift_1 physics   95 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: given that, angle of laticude, $\lambda = 45^{\circ}$ we know that, the expression of gravity at latitude angle is $g_{\lambda} = g - \omega^{2} r \cos^{2} \lambda$ the weight of man of mass $m$ at this point $w = m g_{\lambda} = m(g - \omega^{2} r \cos^{2} 45^{\circ})$ according to question, man feels weightlessness ∴ w = 0 $m(g - \omega^{2} r \cos^{2} 45^{\circ}) = 0$ but $m \neq 0$ , then $g - \omega^{2} r \cos^{2} 45^{\circ} = 0$ $\rightarrow \omega = \sqrt{\frac{2q}{r}}$ now, using time period, (duration of day) $= t = \frac{2\pi}{\omega} = 2\pi \sqrt{\frac{r}{2g}} = \pi \sqrt{\frac{2r}{g}}$ © examsnet.com

question: When a $8\ \mathrm{m}$ long wire is stretched by a load of $10\ \mathrm{kg} \cdot \mathrm{wt}$ , it is elongated by $1.5\ \mathrm{mm}$ . The energy stored in the wire in this process is_____ $(g=10\ \mathrm{m} \cdot \mathrm{s}^{-2})$
search_text: when a $8\ \mathrm{m}$ long wire is stretched by a load of $10\ \mathrm{kg} \cdot \mathrm{wt}$ , it is elongated by $1.5\ \mathrm{mm}$ . the energy stored in the wire in this process is_____ $(g=10\ \mathrm{m} \cdot \mathrm{s}^{-2})$ {'a': '7.5j', 'b': '0.05j', 'c': '5j', 'd': '0.075j'} 2021 2021-08-24 shift_1 physics   96 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: given that, weight of load, $w=10\ \mathrm{kg}$ -wt $f=w=10 \times 10\ \mathrm{n}=100\ \mathrm{n}$ elongation in wire, $\delta l=1.5\ \mathrm{mm}=1.5 \times 10^{-1}\ \mathrm{m}$ length of wire, $l=8\ \mathrm{m}$ we know that, elastic potential energy stored in wire, $u=\frac{1}{2} f \delta l=\frac{1}{2} \times 100 \times 1.5 \times 10^{-3}=0.075\ \mathrm{j}$ © examsnet.com

If the mass of the vehicle to be lifted is $1400\,\text{kg}$ , then $F$ must at least be _______ $(g=10\,\text{m}\,\dot{s}^{-2})$
search_text: in a vehicle lifter, the enclosed gas exerts a force ' $f$ ' on a small piston of $8\,\text{cm}$ diameter. the pressure is transmitted to a second piston of diameter $24\,\text{cm}$ . if the mass of the vehicle to be lifted is $1400\,\text{kg}$ , then $f$ must at least be _______ $(g=10\,\text{m}\,\dot{s}^{-2})$ {'a': '1600 n', 'b': '1200 n', 'c': '1800 n', 'd': '700 n'} 2021 2021-08-24 shift_1 physics   97 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: given, force on small piston, $f_1=f$ diameter of small piston, $d_1=8\,\text{cm}$ mass of vehicle placed on large piston (lift), $m=1400\,\text{kg}$ diameter of large piston, $d_2=24\,\text{cm}$ by using pascal's law, equal pressure will be  transmitted from small piston to lift $p=\frac{f_1}{a_1}=\frac{f_2}{a},$ $\rightarrow\frac{f}{\frac{\pi d_4^2}{4}}=\frac{mg}{\frac{\pi d_2^2}{4}}$ $f=m a\left(\frac{d_1}{d_2}\right)^2=1400\times10\times\left(\frac{8}{24}\right)^2$ = 1556 n = 1600 n © examsnet.com

question: A body cools down from $52.5^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ to $47.5^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ in 5 minutes and from $47.5^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ to $42.5^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ in $7.5$ minute. Then the temperature of the surroundings is _______
search_text: a body cools down from $52.5^{\circ}\mathrm{c}$ to $47.5^{\circ}\mathrm{c}$ in 5 minutes and from $47.5^{\circ}\mathrm{c}$ to $42.5^{\circ}\mathrm{c}$ in $7.5$ minute. then the temperature of the surroundings is _______ {'a': '$39^{\\circ}\\mathrm{c}$', 'b': '$25^{\\circ}\\mathrm{c}$', 'c': '$35^{\\circ}\\mathrm{c}$', 'd': '$15^{\\circ}\\mathrm{c}$'} 2021 2021-08-24 shift_1 physics   98 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: given that, for first condition, initial temperature, $t_{1}=52.5^{\circ}\mathrm{c}$ final temperature, $t_{v}=47.5^{\circ}\mathrm{c}$ average temperature, $t_{\mathrm{av}}=\frac{t_{1}+t_{2}}{2}$ $=\frac{525+47.5}{2}=50^{\circ}\mathrm{c}$ for second condition, initial temperature, $t_{1}=47.5^{\circ}\mathrm{c}$ final temperature, $t_{2}=42.5^{\circ}\mathrm{c}$ average temperature, $t_{\mathrm{av}}=\frac{t_{1}+t_{2}}{2}$ $=\frac{47.5+42.5}{2}=45^{\circ}\mathrm{c}$ let $t_{0}$ be the temperature of surroundings. now, using expression of rate of cooling, $r=\frac{\delta t}{\delta}=-k(t_{\mathrm{av}}-t_{0})$ substituting the values in above equation from $1^{\text{st}}$ and 2nd conditions, we get $\frac{t_{1}-t_{2}}{t_{1}}=-k(t_{\mathrm{av}}-t_{0})$ $\frac{52.5-47.5}{5}=-k(50-t_{0})$ ...(i) similarly, $\frac{47,5-42.5}{7.5}=-k(45-t_{0})$ ...(ii) dividing eq. (i) by eq. (ii), we get $\frac{\frac{52.5-47.5}{5}}{\frac{47.5-42.5}{7.5}}=\frac{-k(50-t_{0})}{-k(45-t_{0})}$ $\rightarrow \frac{5}{5} \times \frac{7.5}{5} = \frac{50-t_{0}}{45-t_{0}}$ $\rightarrow \frac{3}{2} = \frac{50-t_{0}}{45-t_{0}}$ $t_{0}=35^{\circ}\mathrm{c}$ hence, the temperature of surroundings is $35^{\circ}\mathrm{c}$ . © examsnet.com

question: Two plates of same area are placed in contact. Their thickness as well as their thermal conductivities are in the ratio $2:3$ . The outer surface of one plate is maintained at $10^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ and that of the other at $0^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ . Temperature at the common surface is ______
search_text: two plates of same area are placed in contact. their thickness as well as their thermal conductivities are in the ratio $2:3$ . the outer surface of one plate is maintained at $10^{\circ}\mathrm{c}$ and that of the other at $0^{\circ}\mathrm{c}$ . temperature at the common surface is ______ {'a': '$0^{\\circ}\\mathrm{c}$', 'b': '$25^{\\circ}\\mathrm{c}$', 'c': '$5^{\\circ}\\mathrm{c}$', 'd': '$6.5^{\\circ}\\mathrm{c}$'} 2021 2021-08-24 shift_1 physics   99 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: given that, two plates are having same surface area (a). let $k_{1},k_{2}$ and $t_{1}, t_{2}$ be their conductivities and thickness respectively, according to question, $\frac{k_{1}}{k_{2}}=\frac{t_{1}}{t_{2}}=\frac{2}{3}$ ...(i) since, the rate of flow of heat through both plates be same, then $\frac{\delta q}{\delta t}=\frac{k_{1} a \delta t_{1}}{t_{1}}=\frac{k_{2} a \delta t_{2}}{t_{2}}$ $\rightarrow \frac{k_{1}}{k_{2}} \times \frac{t_{2}}{t_{1}} \times (t_{1}-t)=(t-t_{2})$ [where t be the temperature of common surface] $\frac{2}{3} \times \frac{3}{2} (10-t)=(t-0)$ t = 5°c © examsnet.com

question: The efficiency of Carnot heat engine ______
search_text: the efficiency of carnot heat engine ______ {'a': 'is independent of the temperature of the source and the sink', 'b': 'is independent of the working substance', 'c': 'can be $100\\%$', 'd': 'is no affected by the thermal capacity of the source or the sink.'} 2021 2021-08-24 shift_1 physics   101 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: we know that, the efficiency of carnot heat engine is $\eta=1-\frac{t_{2}}{t_{1}}$ where, $t_{1}=$ temperature of source (hot reservoir) $t_{2}=$ temperature of sink (cold reservoir) hence, efficiency depends only on the temperature of hot and cold reservoir but independent of the working substance. © examsnet.com

question: In a thermodynamic process the pressure of a fixed mass of a gas is changed in such a manner that the gas released 30 joules of heat and 18 joules of work was done on the gas. If the initial internal energy of the gas was 60 joules, the final internal energy will be:
search_text: in a thermodynamic process the pressure of a fixed mass of a gas is changed in such a manner that the gas released 30 joules of heat and 18 joules of work was done on the gas. if the initial internal energy of the gas was 60 joules, the final internal energy will be: {'a': '32 j', 'b': '48 j', 'c': '72 j', 'd': '96 j'} 2021 2021-08-24 shift_1 physics   102 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: given that, heat released, $\delta q = -30 \mathrm{j}$ work done on the gas, $\delta w = -18 \mathrm{j}$ change in internal energy $=\delta u$ initial internal cnergy, $u_i = 60 \mathrm{j}$ let final internal energy, $u_f = u$ by using first law of thermodynamics, $\delta q = \delta w + \delta u$ substituting the values, we get $-30 = -18 + (u_f - u_i)$ $-30+18=u-60$ $\rightarrow u=48 \mathrm{j}$ hence, the final internal energy of gas is $48 \mathrm{j}$ . © examsnet.com

question: The speed of the sound in Oxygen $\mathrm{O}_2$ at a certain temperature is $460\ \mathrm{m}\cdot\mathrm{s}^{-1}$ . The speed of the sound in Helium He at the same temperature will be ______ (assume both the gasses to be ideal)

(i) by eq. (ii), we get $\frac{v_1}{v_2}=\sqrt{\frac{\gamma_1 rt}{m_1}}\times\sqrt{\frac{m_2}{\gamma_2 rt}}=\sqrt{\frac{\gamma_1}{\gamma_2}\times\frac{m_2}{m_1}}$ substituting the values, we get $\frac{460}{v_2}=\sqrt{\frac{7}{5}\times\frac{4}{32}\times\frac{3}{5}}$ $\rightarrow v_2=1420\ \mathrm{m/s}$ hence, speed of sound in helium gas at the same temperature is $1420\ \mathrm{m/s}$ . © examsnet.com

search_text: the radius of curvature of the face of planoconvex lens is $12\,\text{cm}$ and its refractive index is $1.5$ . then the focal length of the lens is: {'a': '26 cm', 'b': '22 cm', 'c': '24 cm', 'd': '20 cm'} 2021 2021-08-24 shift_1 physics   105 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: (c) given, refractive index of lens, $\mu=1.5$ radius of curved face, $r_{1}=12\,\text{cm}$ radius of plane face, $r_{2}=\infty$ now, using the expression of focal length. $\frac{1}{f}=\mu-1\left[\frac{1}{r_{1}}-\frac{1}{r_{2}}\right]$ substituting the values, we get $\frac{1}{f}=(1.5-1)\left[\frac{1}{12}-\frac{1}{\infty}\right]$ $\frac{1}{f}=0.5\times\frac{1}{12}$ $\rightarrow f=\frac{12}{0.5}\,\text{cm}=24\,\text{cm}$ hence, the focal length of given plano-convex lens is $24\,\text{cm}$ . © examsnet.com

search_text: a circular plate sheet of radius $10\ \mathrm{cm}$ is placed in a uniform electric field of $2\sqrt{3} \times 10^{5}\ \mathrm{n}\cdot\mathrm{c}^{-1}$ , making an angle of $60^{\circ}$ with the field. then find the electric flux through the sheet. {'a': '$1.36 \\times 10^{2}\\ \\mathrm{n}\\cdot\\mathrm{m}^{2}\\cdot\\mathrm{c}^{-1}$', 'b': '$9.42 \\times 10^{3}\\ \\mathrm{n}\\cdot\\mathrm{m}^{2}\\cdot\\mathrm{c}^{-1}$', 'c': '$0.515 \\times 10^{2}\\ \\mathrm{n}\\cdot\\mathrm{m}^{2}\\cdot\\mathrm{c}^{-1}$', 'd': '$0.515 \\times 10^{4}\\ \\mathrm{n}\\cdot\\mathrm{m}^{2}\\cdot\\mathrm{c}^{-1}$'} 2021 2021-08-24 shift_1 physics   106 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: given that, radius of plate, $r=10\ \mathrm{cm}$ $=10 \times 10^{-2}\ \mathrm{m}$ uniform electric field, $e=2\sqrt{3} \times 10^{5}\ \mathrm{nc}^{-1}$ since, the angle between plate and electric field is $60^{\circ}$ . then, angle between normal to the plate and electric field, $\theta = 90^{\circ} - 60^{\circ} = 30^{\circ}$ . by using expression of electric flux, $\phi = ea \cos \theta = 2\sqrt{3} \times 10^{5} \times \pi (10 \times 10^{-2})^{2} \times \cos 30^{\circ}$ $=9.42 \times 10^{3}\ \mathrm{n}\cdot\mathrm{m}^{2}\cdot\mathrm{c}^{-1}$ © examsnet.com

question: Four point-charges are placed at the vertices of a square of side $2.8\ \mathrm{m}$ as shown in the figure. Find the electric potential at the centre of the square.
search_text: four point-charges are placed at the vertices of a square of side $2.8\ \mathrm{m}$ as shown in the figure. find the electric potential at the centre of the square. {'a': '450 v', 'b': '495  v', 'c': '405 v', 'd': '378 v'} 2021 2021-08-24 shift_1 physics   108 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: given that, the point charges are placed on vertices of a square as shown in figure. let $r$ be the distance of $o$ from the each comer. in $\triangle abc,\ ac^{2}=ab^{2}+bc^{2}$ $(2r)^{2}=a^{2}+a^{2}=2a^{2}$ $\rightarrow r=\frac{a}{\sqrt{2}}$ $r=\frac{2.8}{\sqrt{2}}\ \mathrm{m}$ $(\because a=2.8\ \mathrm{m})$ now, using expression of electric potential at a point due to point charge $v=\frac{kq}{r}$ now, total electric potential at o due to all the four charges $q_{1}, q_{2} q_{3}$ and $q_{4}$ $v_{0}=v_{1}+v_{2}+v_{3}+v_{4}$ $v_{0}=\frac{kq_{1}}{r}+\frac{kq_{2}}{r}+\frac{kq_{1}}{r}+\frac{kq_{4}}{r}$ $v_{0}=\frac{k}{r}[q_{1}+q_{2}+q_{3}+q_{4}]$ substituting the values, we get $v_{e}=\frac{9 \times 10^{9} \times \sqrt{2}}{2.8}(20+40-34+16) \times 10^{-9}$ $=190.89\ \mathrm{v}$ © examsnet.com

search_text: number of electrons flowing per second is a conductor carrying a current of $9\,\mathrm{a}$ is _____ {'a': '$3 \\times 10^{19}$', 'b': '$5.6 \\times 10^{19}$', 'c': '$5.6 \\times 10^{20}$', 'd': '$3 \\times 10^{20}$'} 2021 2021-08-24 shift_1 physics   109 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: given that, electric current, $i=9\,\mathrm{a}$ let $n$ be the number of electron passing through a conductor in time $t$ . we know that, $i=\frac{q}{t}$ and $q=n e$ ∴ $i=\frac{n e}{t}$ ⇒ $\frac{n}{t}=\frac{1}{e}$ substituting the values, we get number of electron flowing per second. $\frac{n}{t}=\frac{9}{1.6 \times 10^{-19}}=5.6 \times 10^{19}$ electrons per second © examsnet.com

(i) and (iv), we get $t=\frac{ibl}{2\pi}$ © examsnet.com

search_text: torques $\tau_{1}$ and $\tau_{2}$ are required for a magnetic needle to remain perpendicular to the magnetic fields $b_{1}$ and $b_{2}$ at two different places. the ratio $b_{1}: b_{2}$ is {'a': '$\\tau_{2}: \\tau_{1}$', 'b': '$\\tau_{1}: \\tau_{2}$', 'c': '$\\frac{\\tau_{1} + \\tau_{2}}{\\tau_{1} - \\tau_{2}}$', 'd': '$\\frac{\\tau_{1} - \\tau_{2}}{\\tau_{1} + \\tau_{2}}$'} 2021 2021-08-24 shift_1 physics   112 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: given that torques $\tau_{1}$ and $\tau_{2}$ are required for a magnetic needle to remain perpendicular to the magnetic field $b_{1}$ and $b_{2}$ . we know that, torque acting on a magnet in uniform magnetic field. ∴ $\tau = mb \sin \theta$ where, $\theta = 90^{\circ}$ (given) now, $\frac{\tau_{1}}{\tau_{2}} = \frac{mb_{1} \sin 90^{\circ}}{mb_{2} \sin 90^{\circ}}$ hence, $\frac{b_{1}}{b_{2}} = \frac{\tau_{1}}{\tau_{2}}$ © examsnet.com

search_text: the initial rate of increase of current when a battery of emf $6\ \mathrm{v}$ is connected in series with an inductance of $2\ \mathrm{h}$ and resistance $12\ \omega$ is ______ {'a': '$0.5\\ \\mathrm{a}\\ \\mathrm{s}^{-1}$', 'b': '$1\\ \\mathrm{a}\\ \\mathrm{s}^{-1}$', 'c': '$3\\ \\mathrm{a}\\ \\mathrm{s}^{-1}$', 'd': '$4\\ \\mathrm{a}\\ \\mathrm{s}^{-1}$'} 2021 2021-08-24 shift_1 physics   113 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: given that, emf of batrery, $e=6\ \mathrm{v}$ resistance, $r=12\ \omega$ inductance, $l=2\ \mathrm{h}$ we know that, the instantaneous current in the circuit containing $r$ and $l$ in series with battery of emf $e$ is $i=i_{0}\left(1-e^{\frac{-z}{2}t}\right)$ where, maximum current at steady state $i_{0}=\frac{e}{r}$ ∴ $i=\frac{e}{r}\left(1-e^{\frac{-r}{t}}\right)$ now, the rate of increase of current. $\frac{di}{dt}=\frac{e}{r}\left[0-\frac{-r}{l}e^{\frac{-r}{2}t}\right]=\frac{e}{l}e^{\frac{-r}{l}t}$ at $(t=0)$ initial condition, $\frac{dl}{dt}\big|_{t=0}=\frac{e}{l}e^{0}=\frac{e}{l}=\frac{6}{2}=3\ \mathrm{a}/\mathrm{s}$ © examsnet.com

search_text: $1\\ \text{amu}$ is ______ {'a': '$931\\\\ \\text{kev}$', 'b': '$931\\\\ \\text{ev}$', 'c': '$931\\\\ \\text{mev}$', 'd': '$9.31\\\\ \\text{mev}$'} 2021 2021-08-24 shift_1 physics   118 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: given that atomic mass $=1$ amu $=1.66 \times 10^{-27}\\ \text{kg}$ by using einstein's equation of mass energy relation, $e=mc^{2}$ where, $c=$ speed of light $=3 \times 10^{8}\\ \text{m/s}$ . $e=\left(1.66 \times 10^{-27}\right) \times \left(3 \times 10^{8}\right)^{2}\\ \text{j}$ $=1.494 \times 10^{-11}\\ \text{j}$ we know, $1\\ \text{mev}=1.6 \times 10^{-13}\\ \text{j}$ $1\\ \text{j}=\frac{1}{1.6} \times 10^{13}\\ \text{mev}$ substituting the value, we get $e=1.494 \times 10^{-11} \times \frac{1}{1.6} \times 10^{13}\\ \text{mev}$ $=931\\ \text{mev}$ © examsnet.com

search_text: if $a b c d e f$ is a regular hexagon with $\overrightarrow{ab}=\vec{a}$ and $\overrightarrow{bc}=\vec{b}$ then $\overrightarrow{ce}$ equals {'a': '$\\vec{b}-\\vec{a}$', 'b': '$-\\vec{b}$', 'c': '$\\vec{b}-\\overrightarrow{2b}$', 'd': '$\\vec{a}-\\overrightarrow{2b}$'} 2021 2021-08-24 shift_2 mathematics   28 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: in a regular hexagon $abcdef$ , let $\overrightarrow{ab}=\vec{a}$ and $\overrightarrow{bc}=\vec{b}$ . using vector addition, $\overrightarrow{ac}=\overrightarrow{ab}+\overrightarrow{bc}=\vec{a}+\vec{b}$ . in a regular hexagon, $\overrightarrow{ad}$ is parallel to $\overrightarrow{bc}$ and has twice its length, so $\overrightarrow{ad}=2\vec{b}$ . therefore $\overrightarrow{cd}=\overrightarrow{ad}-\overrightarrow{ac}=2\vec{b}-(\vec{a}+\vec{b})=\vec{b}-\vec{a}$ . also, $\overrightarrow{de}$ is opposite to $\overrightarrow{ab}$ , so $\overrightarrow{de}=-\vec{a}$ . thus $\overrightarrow{ce}=\overrightarrow{cd}+\overrightarrow{de}=(\vec{b}-\vec{a})+(-\vec{a})=\vec{b}-2\vec{a}$ . hence the correct answer is option c, whose intended expression is $\vec{b}-2\vec{a}$ ; the printed option appears to contain a typo if it literally reads $\vec{b}-2\vec{b}$ . © examsnet.com

search_text: if one of the lines given by the equation $2 x^{2}+a x y+3 y^{2}=0$ coincide with one of those given by the equation $2 x^{2}+b x y-3 y^{2}=0$ , while the other two lines are perpendicular to each other, then the values of $a$ and $b$ are {'a': '$a=4 \\ \\& \\ b=1$', 'b': '$a=-5 \\ \\& \\ b=-1$', 'c': '$a=4 \\ \\& \\ b=1$', 'd': '$a=-5 \\ \\& \\ b=-1$'} 2021 2021-08-24 shift_2 mathematics   50 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: given, equation of pair of straight line $2 x^{2}+a x y+3 y^{2}=0$ and $2 x^{2}+b x y-3 y^{2}=0$ let the slope of line $m$ and $m_{1}$ of the equation $2 x^{2}+a x y+3 y^{2}=0$ ∴ $m+m_{1}=\frac{-a}{3}$ and $m m_{1}=\frac{2}{3}$ slope of the other line is $m$ and $m_{2}$ . then, $m+m_{2}=\frac{b}{3}$ and $m m_{2}=-\frac{2}{3}$ given, $m_{1} m_{2}=-1$ ...(i) ∴ $\frac{m m_{1}}{m m_{2}}=-1$ $\rightarrow m_{1}=-m_{2}$ $\rightarrow m_{1}+m_{2}=0$ ...(ii) from eqs.(i) and (ii), we get $m_{1}=1$ and $m,=-1$ $\therefore m=\frac{2}{3}$ $m+m_{1}=-\frac{a}{3}$ $\rightarrow \frac{2}{3}+1=-\frac{a}{3}$ $\rightarrow a=-5$ and $\rightarrow b=-1$ $a=-5$ $b=-1$ ∴ $a=-5 \ \& \ b=1$ and $a=-4 \ \& \ b=-1$ © examsnet.com

(i) and (ii), we get $(3,2)$ ∴ radical centre of circle is $(3,2)$ . length of tanget from $(3,2)$ to s is $\sqrt{s_{t}}$ $=\sqrt{(3)^{2}+(2)^{2}+2(3)+17(2)+4}=\sqrt{57}$ © examsnet.com

search_text: if the lines $2x - y + 3 = 0$ and $4x + ky + 3 = 0$ are conjugate with respect to the ellipse $5x^{2} + 6y^{2} - 15 = 0$ , then ' $k$ ' equals ______ {'a': '1', 'b': '2', 'c': '3', 'd': '6'} 2021 2021-08-24 shift_2 mathematics   58 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: $2x - y + 3 = 0$ and $4x + ky + 3 = 0$ are conjugate with respect to ellipse $5x^{2} + 6y^{2} - 15 = 0$ we know that $a_{1}x + b_{1}y + c_{1} = 0$ and $a_{2}x + b_{2}y + c_{2} = 0$ are conjugate with $\frac{x^{2}}{a^{2}} + \frac{y^{2}}{b} = 1$ then, $a^{2}a_{1}a_{2} + b^{2}b_{1}b_{2} = c_{1}c_{2}$ ∴ here, $a_{1} = 2, b_{1} = -1, c_{1} = 3$ $a_{2} = 4, b_{2} = k_{,}, c_{2} = 3$ $a^{2} = \frac{15}{5}, b^{2} = \frac{15}{6}$ ∴ $\frac{15}{5}(2)(4) - \left(\frac{15}{6}\right)(k) = 9$ $\rightarrow k = 6$ © examsnet.com

question: A line $A B$ in three dimensions makes angles $45^{\circ}$ and $120^{\circ}$ with the positive $x$ -axis and the positive $y$ -axis respectively. If $A B$ makes an acute angle $\theta$ with the positive $z$ -axis, then $\theta$ equals _____
search_text: a line $a b$ in three dimensions makes angles $45^{\circ}$ and $120^{\circ}$ with the positive $x$ -axis and the positive $y$ -axis respectively. if $a b$ makes an acute angle $\theta$ with the positive $z$ -axis, then $\theta$ equals _____ {'a': '30°', 'b': '45°', 'c': '60°', 'd': '75°'} 2021 2021-08-24 shift_2 mathematics   62 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: here, line ab in line dimensions makes an  angle $45^{\circ}$ and $120^{\circ}$ with positive x-axis and y-axis respectively and acuts angle $\theta$ with positive z-axis. ∴ $\cos^{2}45^{\circ}+\cos^{2}120^{\circ}+\cos^{2}\theta=1$ $\rightarrow \left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right)^{2}+\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{2}+\cos^{2}\theta=1$ $\rightarrow\cos^{2}\theta=1-\left(\frac{1}{2}+\frac{1}{4}\right)$ $\cos^{2}\theta=\frac{1}{4}$ $\rightarrow\cos\theta=\frac{1}{2}$ ⇒ θ = 60° © examsnet.com

question: If $\lfloor . \rfloor$ denotes the Greatest integer function, then $f(x)=\lfloor x \rfloor^{2}-\lfloor x^{2} \rfloor$ is discontinuous at ______
search_text: if $\lfloor . \rfloor$ denotes the greatest integer function, then $f(x)=\lfloor x \rfloor^{2}-\lfloor x^{2} \rfloor$ is discontinuous at ______ {'a': 'all integers', 'b': 'all integers except 0 and 1', 'c': 'all integers except 1', 'd': 'all integers except 0'} 2021 2021-08-24 shift_2 mathematics   64 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: we have, $f(x)=\lfloor x \rfloor^{2}-\lfloor x^{2} \rfloor$ $\lim\limits_{x\to 0^{-}}f(x)=\lim\limits_{h\to 0}\lfloor 0-h \rfloor^{2}-\lfloor (0-h)^{2} \rfloor$ $=(-1)^{2}-0=1$ $\lim\limits_{x\to 0^{-}}f(x)=\lim\limits_{h\to 0}(0+h)^{2}-\lfloor (0+h)^{2} \rfloor$ $=0-0=0$ ∵ $f(x)$ is discontinuous of $x=0$ now, $\lim\limits_{x\to 1}f(x)=\lim\limits_{h\to 0}\lfloor 1-h \rfloor^{2}-\lfloor (1-h)^{2} \rfloor$ $=1-1=0$ ∵ $f(x)$ is continuous at $x=1$ . ∴ $f(x)$ is discontinuous at all integer except 1. © examsnet.com

question: The derivative of $\sec^{-1}\left(\frac{1}{2x^{2}-1}\right)$ with respect to $\sqrt{1-x^{2}}$ at $x=\frac{1}{2}$ equals ______
search_text: the derivative of $\sec^{-1}\left(\frac{1}{2x^{2}-1}\right)$ with respect to $\sqrt{1-x^{2}}$ at $x=\frac{1}{2}$ equals ______ {'a': '2', 'b': '$\\frac{1}{2}$', 'c': '$\\frac{1}{4}$', 'd': '4'} 2021 2021-08-24 shift_2 mathematics   68 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: $\text{let } u=\sec^{-1}\left(\frac{1}{2x^{2}-1}\right)$ and $v=\sqrt{1-x^{2}}$ put $x=\cos\theta$ ∴ $u=\sec^{-1}\left(\frac{1}{2\cos^{2}\theta-1}\right)$ and $v=\sqrt{1-\cos^{2}\theta}$ $\rightarrow u=\sec^{-1}(\sec 2\theta)$ and $v=\sin\theta$ $\rightarrow u=2\theta$ and $v=\sin\theta$ $\frac{du}{d\theta}=2$ and $\frac{dv}{d\theta}=\cos\theta$ $\rightarrow \frac{du}{dv} = \frac{ \frac{du}{d\theta} }{ \frac{dv}{d\theta} } = \frac{2}{\cos\theta}$ $\rightarrow \frac{du}{dv} = \frac{2}{x}$ $[\because \cos\theta = x]$ at $x=\frac{1}{2}$ $\rightarrow \left( \frac{du}{dv} \right)_{x=\frac{1}{2}} = \frac{2}{\frac{1}{2}} = 4$ © examsnet.com

search_text: the value of ' $c$ ', of the lagrange's mean value theorem, for $f(x)=\sqrt{x^{2}-x}, x \in[1,4]$ is _____ {'a': '$\\frac{4}{3}$', 'b': '$\\frac{3}{2}$', 'c': '$\\frac{5}{4}$', 'd': '3'} 2021 2021-08-24 shift_2 mathematics   70 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: we have, $f(x)=\sqrt{x^{2}-x}, x \in[1,4]$ $\rightarrow f(1)=\sqrt{1-1}=0$ $f(4)=\sqrt{16-4}=\sqrt{12}=2\sqrt{3}$ $\rightarrow f'(c)=\frac{2c-1}{2\sqrt{c^{2}-r}}$ by lagrange's mean value theorem $f'(c)=\frac{f(b)-f(a)}{b-a}$ $\frac{2c-1}{2\sqrt{c^{2}-c}}=\frac{f(4)-f(1)}{4-1}=\frac{2\sqrt{3}-0}{3}$ $\rightarrow \frac{2c-1}{2\sqrt{c^{2}-c}}=\frac{2}{\sqrt{3}}$ $\sqrt{3}(2c-1)=4\sqrt{c^{2}-c}$ $\rightarrow 3(2c-1)^{2}=16c^{2}-16c$ $\rightarrow 3(4c^{2}-4c+1)=16c^{2}-16c$ $\rightarrow 12c^{2}-12c+3=16c^{2}-16c$ $\rightarrow 4c^{2}-4c-3=0$ $(2c-3)(2c+1)=0$ $\rightarrow c=\frac{3}{2} \in(1,4)$ ∴ $c=\frac{3}{2}$ © examsnet.com

search_text: the point on the curve $x^{2}+y^{2}=a^{2}, y \geq 0$ , at which the tangent is parallel to the $x$ -axis, is _____ {'a': '$(a, 0)$', 'b': '$(-a, 0)$', 'c': '$(0, a)$', 'd': '$(0, -a)$'} 2021 2021-08-24 shift_2 mathematics   73 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: we have, $x^{2}+y^{2}=a^{2}$ $\rightarrow 2x + 2y \frac{dy}{dx} = 0$ $\rightarrow \frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{-x}{y}$ tangent is parallel to $x$ -axis. ∴ $\frac{dy}{dx} = 0$ $\rightarrow \frac{-x}{y} = 0 ; \therefore x = 0$ putting the value of $x$ in $x^{2}+y^{2}=a^{2}$ $\rightarrow 0 + y^{2} = a^{2}$ $\rightarrow y = a, y \geq 0$ ∴ the point on the curve is $(0, a)$ . © examsnet.com

search_text: $\int 3^{x} (f'(x)+f(x) \log 3) dx =$ {'a': "$3^{x} f'(x) + c$", 'b': '$3^{x} \\log 3 + c$', 'c': '$3^{x} f(x) + c$', 'd': '$3^{x} + c$'} 2021 2021-08-24 shift_2 mathematics   74 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: $\text{let } i = \int 3^{x} f'(x)+f(x) \log 3) dx$ $i = \int 3^{x} f'(x) dx + \int 3^{x} f(x) \log 3 dx$ $i = 3^{x} \int f'(x) dx - \int \left( \frac{d(3^{x})}{dx} \int f'(x) dx \right) dx + \int 3^{x} f(x) \log 3 dx$ $i = 3^{x} f(x) - \int (3^{x} f(x) \log 3) dx + \int 3^{x} f(x) \log 3 dx$ $i = 3^{x} f(x) + c$ © examsnet.com

search_text: if $\int \frac{3\cos x-2\sin x}{4\sin x+5\cos x} \, dx$ $= a \log|5\cos x+4\sin x|+bx+c$ , then $a$ and $b$ are _____ {'a': '$a=\\frac{22}{41} \\& b=\\frac{7}{41}$', 'b': '$a=\\frac{-22}{41} \\& b=\\frac{7}{41}$', 'c': '$a=\\frac{-22}{41} \\& b=\\frac{-7}{41}$', 'd': '$a=\\frac{22}{41} \\& b=\\frac{7}{41}$'} 2021 2021-08-24 shift_2 mathematics   76 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: we have, $\int \frac{3\cos x-2\sin x}{4\sin x+5\cos x} \, dx$ $= a(5\cos x+4\sin x)+bx+c$ on differentiating both sides, we get $\frac{3\cos x-2\sin x}{4\sin x+5\cos x}=\frac{a(-5\sin x+4\cos x)}{4\sin x+5\cos x}+b$ $\rightarrow \frac{3\cos x-2\sin x}{4\sin x+5\cos x}$ $=\frac{-5a\sin x+4a\cos x+4b\sin x+5b\cos x}{4\sin x+5\cos x}$ $\rightarrow 3\cos x-2\sin x=(4b-5a)\sin x+(5b+4a)\cos x$ equating the coefficient of $\cos x$ and $\sin x$ , we get $5b+4a=3$ and $5a-4b=2$ solving, we get $a=\frac{22}{41}$ and $b=\frac{7}{41}$ © examsnet.com

search_text: if $i=\int\limits_{0}^{\pi} x\{\sin^{2}(\sin x)+\cos^{2}(\cos x)\}\,dx$ , then $[i]=$ ______. here [.] denotes g. i. f {'a': '3', 'b': '4', 'c': '5', 'd': '6'} 2021 2021-08-24 shift_2 mathematics   79 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: we have, $i=\int\limits_{0}^{\pi} x\{\sin^{2}(\sin x)+\cos^{2}(\cos x)\}\,dx$ $i=\int\limits_{0}^{\pi}(\pi-x)[\sin^{2}(\sin(\pi-x)]+\cos^{2}(\cos(\pi-x))\,dx$ $i=\int\limits_{0}^{\pi}(\pi-x)[\sin^{2}(\sin x)+\cos^{2}(\cos x)]\,dx$ $2i=\pi\int\limits_{0}^{\pi}[\sin^{2}(\sin x)+\cos^{2}(\cos x)]\,dx$ $i=\pi\int\limits_{0}^{\pi}[\sin^{2}(\sin x)+\cos^{2}(\cos x)]\,dx$ $\left[\because\int\limits_{0}^{2} f(x)\,dx=2\int\limits_{0}^{a} f(x)\,dx\right]$ $i=\pi\int\limits_{0}^{\pi/2}\left[\sin^{2}\left(\sin\left(\frac{\pi}{2}-x\right)\right)+\cos^{2}\left(\cos\left(\frac{\pi}{2}-x\right)\right)\right]\,dx$ $i=\pi\int\limits_{0}^{\pi/2} \sin^{2}(\cos x)+\cos^{2}(\sin x)\,dx$ $2l=\pi\int\limits_{0}^{\pi/2} 2\,dx$ $\rightarrow i=\pi\left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right)=\frac{\pi^{2}}{2}$ $[i]=\left[\frac{\pi^{2}}{2}\right]=4\;\;\;\;$ $\left[\begin{array}{ll}\because \pi^2 & \in (9,10) \\ \frac{\pi^2}{2} & \in (4.5,5) \end{array}\right]$ © examsnet.com

search_text: if the equation of motion of a projectile is given by $y=12x-\frac{3}{4}x^{2}$ and its horizontal component of velocity is $3\ \mathrm{m}\ \mathrm{s}^{-1}$ , then find its range. $(g=10\ \mathrm{m}\ \mathrm{s}^{-2})$ {'a': '$12.4\\ \\mathrm{m}$', 'b': '$21.6\\ \\mathrm{m}$', 'c': '$30.6\\ \\mathrm{m}$', 'd': '$36.0\\ \\mathrm{m}$'} 2021 2021-08-24 shift_2 physics   84 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: let $u$ and $\theta$ be the velocity of projection and angle of projection, respechively. given that, horizontal component of velocity. $u_{x}=u \cos \theta=3\ \mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}$ equation of projectile motion is given by $y=12x-\frac{3}{4}x^{2}$ ...(i) we know, general equation of projectile motion, $y=x \tan \theta-\frac{g x^{2}}{2 u^{2} \cos^{2} \theta}$ ...(ii) comparing eqs. (i) and (ii), we get tanθ = 12 $\rightarrow \frac{\sin \theta}{\cos \theta}=12$ $\sin \theta=12 \cos \theta$ multiplying on both side by $(u)$ $u \sin \theta=12(u \cos \theta)=12 \times 3$ i.e. $u \sin \theta=36\ \mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}$ now, using the expression of range. $r=\frac{u^{2} \sin 2\theta}{g}$ $r=\frac{2 u^{2} \sin \theta \cos \theta}{g}$ $r=\frac{2(u \sin \theta)(u \cos \theta)}{g}$ [using identity $\sin 2\theta=2 \sin \theta \cos \theta$ ] substituting the values, we get $r=\frac{2 \times 36 \times 3}{10}$ = 21.6 m © examsnet.com

search_text: a shell of mass ' $m$ ', moving with velocity ' $v$ ' suddenly breaks into two pieces. if one of those parts having mass $\frac{m}{6}$ remains stationary, find the velocity of the other part. {'a': '$\\frac{6v}{5}$', 'b': '$2v$', 'c': '$\\frac{3v}{4}$', 'd': '$\\frac{4v}{3}$'} 2021 2021-08-24 shift_2 physics   89 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: given that, mass of shell $=m$ mass of lst part, $m_{1}=\frac{m}{6}$ then, mass of 2nd part, $m_{2}=m-\frac{m}{6}=\frac{5m}{6}$ velocity of lst part, $v_{1}=0$ velocity of shell $=v$ let velocity of $2\text{nd}$ part $=v_{2}$ by using law of conservation of linear momentum, initial linear momentum = final linear momentum. $m v = m_{1} v_{1} + m_{2} v_{2}$ substituting the values, we get $m v = \frac{m}{6} \times 0 + \frac{5m}{6} \times v_{2}$ $\rightarrow v_{2} = \frac{6}{5} v$ hence, the velocity of $2\text{nd}$ part is $\frac{6}{5} v$ in the same direction as that of shell. © examsnet.com
