question: How many grams of $\mathrm{Mg}$ is required to completely reduce $100\,\text{ml}, 0.1\,\text{M}\,\mathrm{NO}_3^{-}$ solution using the following reaction $\mathrm{NO}_3^{-} + \mathrm{Mg} \longrightarrow \mathrm{Mg}^{2+} + \mathrm{NH}_3$
search_text: how many grams of $\mathrm{mg}$ is required to completely reduce $100\,\text{ml}, 0.1\,\text{m}\,\mathrm{no}_3^{-}$ solution using the following reaction $\mathrm{no}_3^{-} + \mathrm{mg} \longrightarrow \mathrm{mg}^{2+} + \mathrm{nh}_3$ {'a': '$0.96$', 'b': '$0.62$', 'c': '$0.24$', 'd': '$0.75$'} 2022 2022-07-04 shift_2 chemistry   128 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: (a) $\mathrm{mg} + \mathrm{no}_3^{-} \rightarrow \mathrm{mg}^{2+} + \mathrm{nh}_3$ the complete balanced equation of the given . reaction is $4\,\mathrm{mg} + \mathrm{no}_3^{-} + 9\,\mathrm{h}^{\oplus} \rightarrow 4\,\mathrm{mg}^{2+} + \mathrm{nh}_3 + 3\,\mathrm{h}_2\mathrm{o}$ given, conc. of $\mathrm{no}_3^{-} = 0.1\,\text{m}$ volume of $\mathrm{no}_3^{-} = 100\,\text{ml}$ we know that, molarity $= \frac{\text{number of moles}}{\text{volume of solution (in l)}}$ $\text{hence, number of moles} = \text{molarity} \times \text{volume of solution (in l)}$ $\text{so, number of moles} = 0.1 \times 100 \times 10^{-3} = 10\,\text{mmol} = 10^{-2}\,\text{mol}$ from above eq., 1 mole $\mathrm{no}_3^{-}$ reacts with 4 moles $\mathrm{mg}$ . so, $\mathrm{io}^{-2}$ mole $\mathrm{no}_3^{-}$ reacts with $4 \times 10^{-2}$ moles $\mathrm{mg}$ . now, to calculate the mass of $\mathrm{mg}$ required, use the formula, number of moles $= \frac{\text{given mass}}{\text{molar mass}}$ molar mass of $\mathrm{mg} = 24\,\text{g}\,\text{mol}^{-1}$ on substituting the value, $4 \times 10^{-2} = \frac{\text{mass of } \mathrm{mg}}{24}$ we will get, $\text{mass of } \mathrm{mg} = 24 \times 4 \times 10^{-2}$ $\text{mass of } \mathrm{mg} = 0.96\,\text{g}$ © examsnet.com

question: Match the following A. Isothermal process i. $q=\Delta U$ B. Adiabatic process ii. $W=-P \times \Delta V$ C. Isobaric process iii. $W=\Delta U$ D. Isochoric process iv. $W=-nRT \ln\left( \; \frac{V_f}{V_i} \right)$
search_text: match the following a. isothermal process i. $q=\delta u$ b. adiabatic process ii. $w=-p \times \delta v$ c. isobaric process iii. $w=\delta u$ d. isochoric process iv. $w=-nrt \ln\left( \; \frac{v_f}{v_i} \right)$ {'a': '$a-$ (iv), $b-$ (iii), $c-$ (ii), $d-$ (i)', 'b': '$a-$ (iii), $b-$ (iv), $c-$ (i), $d-$ (ii)', 'c': '$a-$ (i), $b-$ (ii), $c-$ (iii), $d-$ (iv)', 'd': '$a-($ ii), $b-($ i) $,  c-(iv)$ (iii)'} 2022 2022-07-04 shift_2 chemistry   131 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: (a) work done in an isothermal process can be calculated by using formula, $w=-n r t \ln\left( \; \frac{v_f}{v_i} \right)$ (b) for an adiabatic process, $q=0$ . so, $\delta u=w$ $\delta u=q+w \rightarrow \delta u=w$ (c) work done for an isobaric process is $w=-p_{\text{ext}} \times \delta v$ (d) for an isochoric process, $\delta v=0$ so, $w=-p \delta v=0$ hence, $q=\delta u$ © examsnet.com

question: Which of the following expression is correct
search_text: which of the following expression is correct {'a': '$\\delta g=-r t \\ln k$', 'b': '$\\delta g=\\;\\frac{1}{r t^{2} \\ln k}$', 'c': '$\\delta g^{0}=-r t \\ln k$', 'd': '$\\delta g^{0}=-\\;\\frac{1}{r t^{2} \\ln k}$'} 2022 2022-07-04 shift_2 chemistry   132 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: (c) using equation, $\delta g=\delta g^{\circ}+r t \ln q$ where, $\delta g \rightarrow$ change in free energy $\delta g^{\circ} \rightarrow$ change in standard free-energy $r \rightarrow$ gas constant $t \rightarrow$ temperature $q \rightarrow$ reaction quotient at equilibrium, $\delta g=0\;\text{ and }\;q=k$ so, $0=\delta g^{\circ}+r t \ln k$ $\rightarrow \delta g^{\circ}=-r t \ln k$ © examsnet.com

search_text: the $\mathrm{ph}$ of $0.01\ \mathrm{n}$ lime water is {'a': '$13.09$', 'b': '$10$', 'c': '$12$', 'd': '$9.8$'} 2022 2022-07-04 shift_2 chemistry   133 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: (c) lime water is $\mathrm{ca}(\mathrm{oh})_2$ . acidity of lime water is 2 . so, normality $=$ acidity $\times$ molarity $\rightarrow\ \text{molarity}\ =\ \frac{0.01}{2}\ \mathrm{m}$ concentration of $[\ \mathrm{oh}^{-}\ ]$ ions, $[\ \mathrm{oh}^{-}\ ] = 2 \times \frac{0.01}{2} = 0.01\ \mathrm{m}$ $\text{now,}\ \mathrm{poh} = -\log [\ \mathrm{oh}^{-}\ ]$ $\mathrm{poh} = -\log 10^{-2}$ $\rightarrow\ \mathrm{poh} = 2 \log 10 = 2$ $\mathrm{ph} + \mathrm{poh} = 14$ $\rightarrow\ \mathrm{ph} = 14 - \mathrm{poh} = 14 - 2$ thus, $\mathrm{ph}=12$ © examsnet.com

question: Among $\mathrm{P}_4, \mathrm{S}_8$ and $\mathrm{N}_2$ , the elements which undergo disproportionation when heated with $\mathrm{NaOH}$ solution
search_text: among $\mathrm{p}_4, \mathrm{s}_8$ and $\mathrm{n}_2$ , the elements which undergo disproportionation when heated with $\mathrm{naoh}$ solution {'a': '$\\mathrm{p}_4, \\mathrm{s}_8$ only', 'b': '${}^2\\mathrm{n}_2, \\mathrm{s}_8$ only', 'c': '$\\mathrm{n}_2, \\mathrm{p}_4$ only', 'd': '$\\mathrm{p}_4, \\mathrm{n}_2, \\mathrm{s}_8$'} 2022 2022-07-04 shift_2 chemistry   136 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: (a) $\mathrm{p}_4$ reacts with $\mathrm{naoh}$ . on heating, it gives $\mathrm{nah}_2\mathrm{po}_2$ and $\mathrm{ph}_3$ . $\mathrm{p}_4 + 3\mathrm{naoh} + 3\mathrm{h}_2\mathrm{o} \xrightarrow{\delta} 3\mathrm{nah}_2\mathrm{po}_2 + \mathrm{ph}_3$ this reaction is a disproportionation reaction as oxidation state of $\mathrm{p}$ changes from 0 to +1 and -3 . which implies that, it undergoes oxidation and reduction simultaneously. $\mathrm{s}_8$ reacts with $\mathrm{naoh}$ on heating to given $\mathrm{na}_2\mathrm{s}$ and $\mathrm{na}_2\mathrm{s}_2\mathrm{o}_3$ . $\mathrm{s}_8 + 12\mathrm{naoh} \rightarrow 4\mathrm{na}_2\mathrm{s} + 2\mathrm{na}_2\mathrm{s}_2\mathrm{o}_3 + 6\mathrm{h}_2\mathrm{o}$ this reaction is a disproportionation reaction as oxidation state of $\mathrm{s}$ changes from 0 to -2 and +2 . which implies that, it undergoes oxidation and reduction simultaneously. but, $\mathrm{n}_2$ is an inert gas. so, it does not react with $\mathrm{naoh}$ . thus, only $\mathrm{p}_4$ and $\mathrm{s}_8$ undergo disproportionation when heated with $\mathrm{naoh}$ solution. © examsnet.com

question: Identify the correct statements about the anomalous behavior of Boron I. Boron trihalides can form dimeric structures. II. Boron shows $+1$ as stable oxidation state III. Maximum covalency of Boron is four. IV. Boron does not form $\mathrm{BF}_{6}^{6-}$ ion.
search_text: identify the correct statements about the anomalous behavior of boron i. boron trihalides can form dimeric structures. ii. boron shows $+1$ as stable oxidation state iii. maximum covalency of boron is four. iv. boron does not form $\mathrm{bf}_{6}^{6-}$ ion. {'a': 'i, ii only', 'b': 'ii, iii only', 'c': 'iii, iv only', 'd': 'i, tv only'} 2022 2022-07-04 shift_2 chemistry   137 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: (i) size of boron atom is very small, so it cannot accomodate 4 large halide atoms and thus, does not form dimer. also, the electron deficiency of boron is removed by $p\pi-p\pi$ back-bonding. hence, the boron trihalides do not form dimers. (ii) in boron family, as we move down the group, two oxidation states are shown by them, i.e. +1 and +3 . however, boron shows only +3 oxidation state because of the absence of inert pair effect. boron does not show +1 oxidation state. (iii) boron shows a maximum covalency of four because of absent of $d$ -orbitals. (iv) boron does not form $\mathrm{bf}_6^{6-}$ ion because of absence of empty $d$ -orbitals. hence, only statements iii and iv are correct. © examsnet.com

search_text: the hybridizations of carbon in graphite, diamond and $\mathrm{c}_{60}$ are respectively {'a': '$2\\ \\mathrm{sp}^{2},\\ \\mathrm{sp}^{3},\\ \\mathrm{sp}$', 'b': '$\\mathrm{sp}^{2} \\cdot \\mathrm{sp}^{3} \\cdot \\mathrm{sp}^{2}$', 'c': '$\\mathrm{sp},\\ \\mathrm{sp}^{2},\\ \\mathrm{sp}^{3}$', 'd': '$\\mathrm{sp} \\cdot \\mathrm{sp}^{3} \\cdot \\mathrm{sp}$'} 2022 2022-07-04 shift_2 chemistry   138 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: (b) in graphite, each carbon atom combines with three other carbon atoms with three sigma bonds. so, hybridisation is $\mathrm{sp}^{2}$ . in diamond, each carbon atom combines with four other carbon atoms with four sigma bonds. so, hybridisation is $\mathrm{sp}^{3}$ . in fullerene, hybridisation of carbon atoms is $\mathrm{sp}^{2}$ . hence, the hybridisation of carbon in graphite, diamond and fullerene, $\mathrm{c}_{60}$ are $\mathrm{sp}^{2}, \mathrm{sp}^{3}$ and $\mathrm{sp}^{2}$ respectively. © examsnet.com

search_text: match list i with list ii list i (defects) list ii (examples) a. frenkel defects 1. $\mathrm{feo}$ b. schottkey defects 2. $\mathrm{nacl}$ c. vacancy defects 3. $\mathrm{agcl}$ d. metal deficiency defects 4. crystals with vacant lattice sites. a b c d 1. 4 3 2 1 2. 3 2 4 1 3. 1 2 3 4 4. 2 3 4 1 {'a': '3', 'b': '2', 'c': '4', 'd': '1'} 2022 2022-07-04 shift_2 chemistry   141 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: a. frenkel defects is a defect in which an atom/ion occupies a normally vacant site other. than its own. this defect is possible if the cations are smaller in size as compared to the anions. size of $\mathrm{ag}^{+}$ is smaller than $\mathrm{cl}^{\ominus}$ so, it shows frenkel defect. b. schottky defects is a type of defect in which both cations and anions remain missing from their lattice sites in equal numbers. this is possible if size of both ions is nearly same. size of $\mathrm{na}^{+}$ is equal to size of $\mathrm{cl}^{\ominus}$ so, it shows schottky defect. c. vacancy defects is a defect in which crystals have vacant sites. d. metal deficiency defects, in this solids have less number of metals, feo shows metal deficiency defect due to variable oxidation state of $\mathrm{fe}$ . hence, the correct match is list i (defects) list ii (examples) a. frenkel defects (iii) $\mathrm{agcl}$ b. schottky defects (ii) $\mathrm{nacl}$ c.vacancy defects (iv) crystals with vacant lattice sites d. metal deficiency defects (i) $\mathrm{feo}$ © examsnet.com

search_text: $x \% \left( \frac{w}{v} \right)$ solution of urea is isotonic with $4 \% \left( \frac{w}{v} \right)$ solution of a non-volatile solute of molar mass $120 \mathrm{g} \mathrm{mol}^{-1}$ . the value of $x$ is {'a': '2', 'b': '4', 'c': '3', 'd': '5'} 2022 2022-07-04 shift_2 chemistry   144 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: (a) $4\% w/v$ solution means $100 \mathrm{ml}$ of solution contains $4 \mathrm{g}$ of non-volatile solute. molar mass of solute $=120 \mathrm{g} \mathrm{mol}^{-1}$ moles, $\dot{n}_s = \frac{4}{120} = \frac{1}{30} \mathrm{mol}$ $x \% \left( \frac{w}{v} \right)$ so mass of urea is $x \mathrm{g}$ . molar mass of urea $=60 \mathrm{g} \mathrm{mol}^{-1}$ using formula, number of moles $= \frac{\text{mass}}{\text{molar mass}}$ moles, $n_v = \frac{x}{60} \mathrm{mol}$ for isotonic solution, $\pi_s = \pi_u$ $c_o = c_s$ $n_v = n_s$ $\frac{x}{60} = \frac{1}{30}$ $x = 2$ $\therefore 2\% (w/v)$ solution of urea is isotonic with $4\%$ $(w/v)$ solution of non-volatile solute. © examsnet.com

search_text: $f(x)=\log \left( \left( \frac{2x^{2}-3}{x} + \sqrt{\frac{4x^{4}-11x^{2}+9}{|x|}} \right) \right)$ is {'a': 'an odd function', 'b': 'an even function', 'c': 'a polynomial function', 'd': 'not a function'} 2022 2022-07-05 shift_1 mathematics   1 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: 👈: video solution $f(x)=\log \left( \left( \frac{2x^{2}-3}{x} \right) + \sqrt{\frac{4x^{4}-11x^{2}+9}{|x|}} \right)$ $f(-x)=\log \left( \frac{2(-x)^{2}-3}{-x} + \sqrt{\frac{4(-x)^{4}-11(-x)^{2}+9}{|-x|}} \right)$ $f(-x)=\log \left[ \frac{2x^{2}-3}{-x} + \sqrt{\frac{4x^{4}-11x^{2}+9}{|x|}} \right]$ we know that, if function $f(x)$ is an odd function. then, $f(x)+f(-x)=0$ $\log \left[ \left( \frac{2x^{2}-3}{x} \right) . + \sqrt{\frac{4x^{4}-11x^{2}+9}{|x|}} \right]$ $+\log \left[ \sqrt{\frac{4x^{4}-11x^{2}+9}{|x|}} - \frac{(2x^{2}-3)}{x} \right]$ $=\log \left[ \frac{4x^{4}-11x^{2}+9}{x^{2}} - \frac{(2x^{2}-3)^{2}}{x^{2}} \right]$ $=\log \left[ \frac{4x^{4}-11x^{2}+9-4x^{4}-9+12x^{2}}{x^{2}} \right]$ $=\log 1=0$ © examsnet.com

search_text: let $f: r \setminus \left\{ -\frac{1}{2} \right\} \rightarrow r$ be defined by $f(x)=\frac{x-2}{2x+1}$ . if $\alpha, \beta$ satisfy the equation $f(f(x)) = -x$ , then $4(\alpha^{2}+\beta^{2})=$ {'a': '17', 'b': '12', 'c': '24', 'd': '34'} 2022 2022-07-05 shift_1 mathematics   2 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: 👈: video solution $f(x)=\frac{x-2}{2x+1}$ $f(f(x)) = -x$ (given) $\rightarrow \frac{f(x)-2}{2f(x)+1} = -x$ $\frac{x-2}{2x+1} - 2$ $\rightarrow \frac{2x-4}{2x+1} + 1$ $\rightarrow \frac{x-2-4x-2}{2x-4+2x+1} = -x$ $\rightarrow \frac{-3x-4}{4x-3} = -x \rightarrow \frac{3x+4}{4x-3} = x$ $\rightarrow 3x+4 = 4x^2 - 3x$ $\rightarrow 4x^2 - 6x - 4 = 0$ $\rightarrow 2x^2 - 3x - 2 = 0$ $\text{ now, } (\alpha+\beta)^2 = \alpha^2 + \beta^2 + 2\alpha\beta$ $\rightarrow \frac{9}{4} = \alpha^2 + \beta^2 - 2 \quad \left[ \because \alpha\beta = -1 \right]$ $\rightarrow \alpha^2 + \beta^2 = \frac{17}{4}$ $\rightarrow 4(\alpha^2 + \beta^2) = 17$ © examsnet.com

search_text: if two vectors $\vec{a}$ and $\vec{b}$ are mutually perpendicular, then the component of $\vec{a} \cdot \vec{b}$ along the direction of $\vec{a} + \vec{b}$ is {'a': '$\\sqrt{|\\vec{a}|^2 + |\\vec{b}|^2}$', 'b': '$\\sqrt{|\\vec{a}|^2 - |\\vec{b}|^2}$', 'c': '$\\frac{|\\vec{a}|^2 - |\\vec{b}|^2}{\\sqrt{|\\vec{a}|^2 + |\\vec{b}|^2}}$', 'd': '$\\frac{|\\vec{a}|^2 + |\\vec{b}|^2}{\\sqrt{|\\vec{a}|^2 - |\\vec{b}|^2}}$'} 2022 2022-07-05 shift_1 physics   85 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: the two vectors $\vec{a}$ and $\vec{b}$ are mutually perpendicular to each other $\;\; \text{a. b} \; = 0.$ $\rightarrow a b \cos \theta = 0$ $\rightarrow \cos \theta = 0 \rightarrow \theta = 90^{\circ}$ $|\vec{a} - \vec{b}| \;$ $\; = \sqrt{a^2 + b^2 - 2ab \cos 90^{\circ}}$ $\; = \sqrt{a^2 + b^2}$ unit vector along $\vec{a} - \vec{b}$ $= \frac{\vec{a} - \vec{b}}{|\vec{a} - \vec{b}|} = \frac{\vec{a} - \vec{b}}{\sqrt{a^2 + b^2}}$ component of $(\vec{a} + \vec{b})$ in direction of $(\vec{a} - \vec{b})$ will be given as, $\; = \frac{(\vec{a} + \vec{b}) \cdot (\vec{a} - \vec{b})}{|\vec{a} - \vec{b}|}$ $\; = \frac{\vec{a} \cdot \vec{a} - \vec{a} \cdot \vec{b} + \vec{b} \cdot \vec{a} - \vec{b} \cdot \vec{b}}{\sqrt{a^2 + b^2}}$ $\; = \frac{a^2 - b^2}{\sqrt{a^2 + b^2}} = \frac{|\vec{a}|^2 - |\vec{b}|^2}{\sqrt{|\vec{a}|^2 + |\vec{b}|^2}}$ © examsnet.com

search_text: an electron in the hydrogen atom excites from $2^{\;\text{nd }\;}$ orbit to $4^{\;\text{th }\;}$ orbit then the change in angular momentum of the electron is (planck's constant $h = 6.64 \times 10^{-34} \mathrm{j} - \mathrm{s}$ ) {'a': '$2.11 \\times 10^{-34} \\mathrm{j} - \\mathrm{s}$', 'b': '$1.05 \\times 10^{-34} \\mathrm{j} - \\mathrm{s}$', 'c': '$0.57 \\times 10^{-34} \\mathrm{j} - \\mathrm{s}$', 'd': '$4.22 \\times 10^{-34} \\mathrm{j} - \\mathrm{s}$'} 2022 2022-07-05 shift_1 physics   117 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: change in angular momentum of the electron in $h$ -atom when it is excited from 2 nd orbit to 4 th orbit is given as $\delta l = l_2 - l_1$ - (a) change in angular momentum of the electron in $h$ -atom when it is excited from 2 nd orbit to 4 th orbit is given as $\delta l = l_2 - l_1$ where, $l_2$ is angular momentum of 4 th excited state $(n=5)$ and $l$ is angular moment of 2 nd excited state $(n=3)$ . $\therefore \delta l \;=\; \frac{n_2 h}{2\pi} - \frac{n_1 h}{2\pi}$ $\;=\; \frac{h}{2\pi} [n_2-n_1] = \frac{6.64 \times 10^{-3}}{2 \times 314} [5-4]$ $\;= 2.11 \times 10^{-34} \mathrm{j} - \ \mathrm{s}$ © examsnet.com

question: Choose the correct statement of the following
search_text: choose the correct statement of the following {'a': 'the nuclear density in general, is independent of mass number a.', 'b': 'the radius of a nucleus is directly proportional to the mass number ,a of the nucleus.', 'c': 'the binding energy of a nucleus is inversely proportional to its mass defect .', 'd': 'energy is absorbed when heavy nuclei undergo transmutation into light nuclei.'} 2022 2022-07-05 shift_1 physics   118 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: we know that, the radius $(r)$ of nucleus is given as $r=r_0 a^{1/3}$ or $r \propto a^{1/3}$ where, $r_0=\text{constant}$ $a=\text{mass number}$ $\therefore$ nuclear density, $\rho=\frac{\text{mass}}{\text{volume}}=\frac{ma}{\frac{4}{3}\pi r^3}$ (here, $m$ is mass of each nucleon) $\rightarrow \;\; \rho=\frac{ma}{\frac{4}{3}\pi (r_0 a^{1/3})^3}=\frac{ma}{\frac{4}{3}\pi r_0^3 a}$ $\rho=\frac{3m}{4\pi r_0^3}$ hence, it is clear from above formula, nuclear density is independent of mass number $a$ . the binding energy, $e=\delta m c^2$ i. e $e \propto \delta m$ where, $\delta m=$ mass defect energy is released when heavy nuclei undergo transmutation into light nuclei. © examsnet.com

search_text: the rate constant of a reaction at $500\ \text{k}$ and $700\ \text{k}$ are $0.02\ \text{s}^{-1}$ and $0.2\ \text{s}^{-1}$ respectively. the activation energy of the reaction (in $\text{kj mol}^{-1}$ ) is $(r=8.3\ \text{jk}^{-1}\ \text{mol}^{-1})$ {'a': '$66.90$', 'b': '$33.45$', 'c': '$22.30$', 'd': '$44.45$'} 2022 2022-07-05 shift_1 chemistry   146 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: given, $k_1 = 0.02\ \text{s}^{-1}$ $k_2 = 0.2\ \text{s}^{-1}$ $e_a = ?$ $r = 8.3$ $t_1 = 500\ \text{k}$ $t_2 = 700\ \text{k}$ $\text{in} \frac{k_2}{k_1} = -\frac{e_a}{r} \left( \frac{1}{t_2} - \frac{1}{t_1} \right)$ $\text{in} \frac{0.2}{0.02} = -\frac{e_a}{8.3} \left[ \frac{1}{700} - \frac{1}{500} \right]$ $\text{in} 10 = \frac{-e_a}{8.3} \left( \frac{500-700}{700 \times 500} \right)$ $2.302 \times 8.3 \times 700 \times 500 = 200 e_a$ $\rightarrow e_a = \frac{2.302 \times 8.3 \times 700 \times 500}{200}$ $= 33436\ \text{j/mol}$ $\approx 33.44\ \text{kj/mol}$ © examsnet.com

search_text: if $a=\begin{bmatrix} x & 0 \\ 1 & 1 \end{bmatrix}$ and $b=\begin{bmatrix} 8 & 0 \\ 7 & 1 \end{bmatrix}$ and $a^{3}=b$ , then $x=$ {'a': '$-2$ or $3$', 'b': '$-2$', 'c': '$2$ or $-3$', 'd': '$2$'} 2022 2022-07-05 shift_2 mathematics   3 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: 👈: video solution given, $a=\begin{bmatrix} x & 0 \\ 1 & 1 \end{bmatrix}$ and $b=\begin{bmatrix} 8 & 0 \\ 7 & 1 \end{bmatrix}$ . $a^2=\begin{bmatrix} x & 0 \\ 1 & 1 \end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix} x & 0 \\ 1 & 1 \end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix} x^2 & 0 \\ x+1 & 1 \end{bmatrix}$ . $a^3=a^2a=\begin{bmatrix} x^2 & 0 \\ x+1 & 1 \end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix} x & 0 \\ 1 & 1 \end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix} x^3 & 0 \\ x^2+x+1 & 1 \end{bmatrix}$ . since $a^3=b$ , $\begin{bmatrix} x^3 & 0 \\ x^2+x+1 & 1 \end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix} 8 & 0 \\ 7 & 1 \end{bmatrix}$ . equating the top-left entries gives $x^3=8$ , so $x=2$ over the reals. equating the bottom-left entries gives $x^2+x+1=7$ , i.e. $x^2+x-6=0$ . thus $(x+3)(x-2)=0$ , so $x=-3$ or $x=2$ . the value $x=-3$ fails $x^3=8$ , so it is rejected. hence the only valid value is $x=2$ . therefore the correct option is $2$ . © examsnet.com

search_text: if the solution of the system of simultaneous equations $\; \frac{1}{x} + \; \frac{2}{y} - \; \frac{3}{z} - 1 = 0$ , $\; \frac{2}{x} - \; \frac{4}{y} + \; \frac{3}{z} - 1 = 0$ and $\; \frac{3}{x} + \; \frac{6}{y} - \; \frac{6}{z} - 4 = 0$ is $x = \alpha, y = \beta, z = \gamma$ then $\alpha^{2} + \gamma^{2} =$ {'a': '$5 \\beta$', 'b': '$\\beta^{2}$', 'c': '$3 \\beta$', 'd': '$\\beta^{2}$'} 2022 2022-07-05 shift_2 mathematics   6 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: 👈: video solution $\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 & -3 \\ 2 & -4 & 3 \\ 3 & 6 & -6 \end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix} \frac{1}{x} \\ \frac{1}{y} \\ \frac{1}{z} \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 1 \\ 4 \end{bmatrix}$ let $a \; = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 & -3 \\ 2 & -4 & 3 \\ 3 & 6 & -6 \end{bmatrix}, x = \begin{bmatrix} \frac{1}{x} \\ \frac{1}{y} \\ \frac{1}{z} \end{bmatrix}.$ $b \; = \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 1 \\ 4 \end{bmatrix}$ $|a| \; = 1(24-18) - 2(-12-9) - 3(12+12)$ $\; = 6 + 42 - 72$ $\; = -24$ $\text{adj} a \; = \begin{bmatrix} 6 & 21 & 24 \\ -6 & 3 & 0 \\ -6 & -9 & -8 \end{bmatrix}^{t}$ $\; = \begin{bmatrix} 6 & -6 & -6 \\ 21 & 3 & -9 \\ 24 & 0 & -8 \end{bmatrix}$ $a^{-1} \; = \; \frac{1}{|a|} \text{adj} a$ $\; = \; \frac{-1}{24} \begin{bmatrix} 6 & -6 & -6 \\ 21 & 3 & -9 \\ 24 & 0 & -8 \end{bmatrix}$ $x = \; a^{-1} b$ $\; = \; \frac{-1}{24} \begin{bmatrix} 6 & -6 & -6 \\ 21 & 3 & -9 \\ 24 & 0 & -8 \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 1 \\ 4 \end{bmatrix}$ $\; = \; \frac{-1}{24} \begin{bmatrix} 6-6-24 \\ 21+3-36 \\ 24-32 \end{bmatrix}$ $\; = \; \frac{-1}{24} \begin{bmatrix} 6-6-24 \\ 21+3-36 \\ 24-32 \end{bmatrix}$ $\; = \; \frac{-1}{24} \begin{bmatrix} -24 \\ -12 \\ -8 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ \frac{1}{2} \\ \frac{1}{3} \end{bmatrix}$ $\therefore \alpha = 1, \beta = 2, \gamma = 3$ $\; \text{now,} \; \alpha^2 + \gamma^2 = 1 + 9$ $= 10 = 5 \beta$ © examsnet.com

search_text: $\sum\limits_{k=1}^{6} \sin \left(\frac{2\pi k}{7}\right) - i \cos \left(\frac{2\pi k}{7}\right) =$ {'a': '$1$', 'b': '$i$', 'c': '$-1$', 'd': '${-1}$'} 2022 2022-07-05 shift_2 mathematics   7 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: 👈: video solution we have, $\sum\limits_{k=1}^{6} \sin \left(\frac{2\pi k}{7}\right) - i \cos \left(\frac{2\pi k}{7}\right)$ $= -i \left[ \sum\limits_{k=1}^{6} \cos \left(\frac{2\pi k}{7}\right) + i \sin \left(\frac{2\pi k}{7}\right) \right] = -i \sum\limits_{k=1}^{6} c^{\frac{i2\pi k}{7}}$ $= -i \left[ e^{i2\pi/7} + e^{i4\pi/7} + \dots + e^{i12\pi/7} \right]$ this forms a gp $= -i \left[ e^{i2\pi/7} \cdot \frac{1-(e^{i2\pi/7})^6}{1-e^{i2\pi/7}} \right]$ $= -i \left[ \frac{e^{i2\pi/7} - e^{i14\pi/7}}{1-e^{i2\pi/7}} \right]$ $= -i \left[ \frac{e^{i2\pi/7} - 1}{1-e^{i2\pi/7}} \right]$ $\left[ \because e^{i14\pi/7}=1 \right]$ $=i$ © examsnet.com

search_text: all the pairs (x.y) that satisfy the inequality $2^{\sqrt{}}$ equation $\sqrt{\sin^{2} x - 2 \sin x + 5}$ $\;\frac{1}{4^{\sin^{2} y}} \leq 1$ also satisfy the {'a': '$2|\\sin x| = \\sin y$', 'b': '$2 \\sin x = \\sin y$', 'c': '$2 \\sin x = 2 \\sin y$', 'd': '$\\sin x = |\\sin y|$'} 2022 2022-07-05 shift_2 mathematics   13 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: 👈: video solution we have, $2^{\sqrt{\sin^{2} x - 2 \sin x + 5}} \times \frac{1}{4^{\sin^{2} y}} \leq 1$ $\; \rightarrow 2^{\sqrt{\sin^{2} x - 2 \sin x + 1 + 4}} \leq 4^{\sin^{2} y}$ $\; \rightarrow 2^{\sqrt{(\sin x - 1)^2 + 4}} \leq 2^{2 \sin^{2} y}$ $\; \rightarrow \sqrt{(\sin x - 1)^2 + 4} \leq 2 \sin^{2} y$ $\; \sqrt{(\sin x - 1)^2 + 4} \in [2, 2\sqrt{2}]$ and $2 \sin^{2} y \in [0, 2]$ $\; \therefore \;\; (\sin x - 1)^2 + 4 = 2 \sin^{2} y = 2$ $\; \rightarrow (\sin x - 1)^2 = 0$ $\; \rightarrow \sin x = 1$ and $2 \sin 2y = 2$ $\; \rightarrow \sin 2y = 1 \rightarrow |\sin y| = 1$ $\; \sin x = |\sin y|$ © examsnet.com

search_text: it is given that the discrete random variable is $x \sim b(n, p)$ and $p(x=2)=p(x=3)$ . then mean of $x$ is {'a': '$2-p$', 'b': '$3-p$', 'c': '$p-2$', 'd': '$p-3$'} 2022 2022-07-05 shift_2 mathematics   39 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: 👈: video solution $p(x=2)=p(x=3)$ $\;{}^{n}c_{2}p^{2}q^{n-2}={}^{n}c_{3}p^{3}q^{n-3}$ $\;{}^{n}c_{2}q={}^{n}c_{3}p$ $\;{}^{n}c_{2}(1-p)={}^{n}c_{3}p$ $\;{}^{n}c_{2}=({}^{n}c_{2}+{}^{n}c_{3})p$ $\;\;\frac{n!}{2!(n-2)!}=\left(\;\frac{n!}{2!(n-2)!}+\;\frac{n!}{3!(n-3)!}\right)p$ $\rightarrow\;\frac{1}{2!(n-2)!}=\;\frac{1}{2!(n-3)!}\left[\;\frac{1}{n-2}+\;\frac{1}{3}\right]p$ $\rightarrow\;\frac{1}{n-2}=\left(\;\frac{3+n-2}{3(n-2)}\right)p$ $\rightarrow 3=(n+)p$ $\rightarrow 3=np+p$ $\rightarrow np=3-p$ $\;\text{mean}\;\;=np$ $\;=3-p$ © examsnet.com

search_text: if $\sqrt{5} y - \sqrt{8} = 0$ is the equation of the directrix of a hyperbola $\frac{x^{2}}{a^{2}} - \frac{y^{2}}{b^{2}} + 1 = 0$ and $\frac{\sqrt{5}}{2}$ is its eccentricity then $a =$ {'a': '$\\sqrt{2}$', 'b': '$\\sqrt{3}$', 'c': '$\\sqrt{5}$', 'd': '$\\sqrt{6}$'} 2022 2022-07-05 shift_2 mathematics   54 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: 👈: video solution equation of directrix of conjugate hyperbola is $y = \pm \frac{b}{e}$ comparing it with the given equation of directrix, we get $\frac{b}{e} = \frac{\sqrt{8}}{\sqrt{5}}$ $\rightarrow b = \frac{\sqrt{8}}{\sqrt{5}} e \rightarrow b = \frac{2 \sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{5}} \times \frac{\sqrt{5}}{2}$ $\rightarrow b = \sqrt{2} \rightarrow a^{2} = b^{2} (e^{2} - 1)$ $\rightarrow a^{2} = 2 \left( \frac{5}{4} - 1 \right) \rightarrow a^{2} = 2 \times \frac{1}{4}$ $\rightarrow a^{2} = \frac{1}{2}$ $\rightarrow a = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$ © examsnet.com

(i) and (ii) represent the same line $\frac{b^2 x_1}{a \cos \theta} = \frac{-a^2 y_1}{b \cot \theta} = \frac{a^2 b^2}{a^2+b^2}$ $\;\frac{b^2 x_1}{a \cos \theta} = \;\frac{a^2 b^2}{a^2+b^2}$ and $\frac{-a^2 y_1}{b \cot \theta} = \frac{a^2 b^2}{a^2+b^2}$ $\sec \theta = \frac{a^3}{(a^2+b^2) x_1}$ and $\tan \theta = \frac{-b^3}{(a^2+b^2) y_1}$ as $\sec^2 \theta - \tan^2 \theta = 1$ $\left(\frac{a^3}{(a^2+b^2) x_1}\right)^2 - \left(\frac{-b^3}{(a^2+b^2) y_1}\right)^2 = 1$ $\rightarrow \frac{a^6}{(a^2+b^2)^2 x_1^2} - \frac{b^6}{(a^2+b^2)^2 y_1^2} = 1$ $\rightarrow \frac{a^6}{x_1^2} - \frac{b^6}{y_1^2} = (a^2+b^2)^2$ the locus of the required point is $\frac{a^6}{x^2} - \frac{b^6}{y^2} = (a^2+b^2)^2$ © examsnet.com

search_text: if $\alpha, 2\alpha, 3\alpha$ are angles made by a ray with $ox, oy, oz$ axes respectively then all the possible values of $\alpha$ are {'a': '$\\;\\frac{\\pi}{6}, \\frac{\\pi}{12}$', 'b': '$\\;\\frac{\\pi}{6} \\cdot \\frac{\\pi}{3}$', 'c': '$\\frac{\\pi}{4}, \\frac{\\pi}{3}$', 'd': '$\\frac{\\pi}{6}, \\frac{\\pi}{4}$'} 2022 2022-07-05 shift_2 mathematics   57 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: 👈: video solution $l=\cos\alpha, m=\cos 2\alpha$ and $n=\cos 3\alpha$ $\;l^2+m^2+n^2=1$ $\;\cos^2\alpha+\cos^2 2\alpha+\cos^2 3\alpha=1$ $\;\cos^2\alpha+(2\cos^2\alpha-1)^2+(4\cos^3\alpha-3\cos\alpha)^2=1$ let $\cos\alpha=y$ $\;y^2+(2y^2-1)^2+(4y^3-3y)^2=1$ $\rightarrow y^2+4y^4+1-4y^2+16y^6+9y^2-24y^4=1$ $\rightarrow 16y^6-20y^4+6y^2=0$ $\rightarrow \;\; 8y^4-10y^2+3=0 \quad [\because y^2 \neq 0]$ $\rightarrow \;\; y^2=\frac{3}{4}$ and $y^2=\frac{1}{2}$ $\;\cos\alpha=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\;\text{ and }\;\cos\alpha=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$ $therefore \;\; \alpha=\frac{\pi}{6}, \frac{\pi}{4}$ © examsnet.com

search_text: $\lim\limits_{n \rightarrow \infty} \sqrt{2} \left[ \frac{(2+\sqrt{2})^{n}+(2-\sqrt{2})^{n}}{(2+\sqrt{2})^{n}-(2-\sqrt{2})^{n}} \right] =$ {'a': '$2+\\sqrt{2}$', 'b': '$2-\\sqrt{2}$', 'c': '$1$', 'd': '$\\sqrt{2}$'} 2022 2022-07-05 shift_2 mathematics   59 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: 👈: video solution we have, $\; \lim\limits_{n \rightarrow \infty} \sqrt{2} \left[ \frac{(2+\sqrt{2})^{n}+(2-\sqrt{2})^{n}}{(2+\sqrt{2})^{n}-(2-\sqrt{2})^{n}} \right]$ $\; = \sqrt{2} \lim\limits_{n \rightarrow \infty} \; \frac{(2+\sqrt{2})^{n} \left[1+ \left(\frac{2-\sqrt{2}}{2+\sqrt{2}}\right)^{n} \right]}{(2+\sqrt{2})^{n} \left[1- \left(\frac{2-\sqrt{2}}{2+\sqrt{2}}\right)^{n} \right]}$ $\; = \sqrt{2} \; \frac{ \lim\limits_{n \rightarrow \infty} \left[1+ \left(\frac{2-\sqrt{2}}{2+\sqrt{2}}\right)^{n} \right] }{ \lim\limits_{n \rightarrow \infty} \left[1- \left(\frac{2-\sqrt{2}}{2+\sqrt{2}}\right)^{n} \right] }$ $= \sqrt{2}$ $\left[ \because \lim\limits_{n \rightarrow \infty} \left(\frac{2-\sqrt{2}}{2+\sqrt{2}}\right)^{n} = 0 \right]$ © examsnet.com

search_text: if $a>0,[\cdot]$ denotes greatest integer function and $\lim\limits_{x \to a^{-}}\left(\frac{|x|^3}{a}-\left[\frac{x}{a}\right]^3\right)=k,$ $\lim\limits_{x \to a^{-}}\left(\frac{|x|^3}{a}-\left[\frac{x}{a}\right]^3\right)=l$ , then {'a': '$2k=l$', 'b': '$k-l=1$', 'c': '$l-k=1$', 'd': '$l=a^{2}, k$ does not exist'} 2022 2022-07-05 shift_2 mathematics   60 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: 👈: video solution we have, $\lim\limits_{x \to a^{-}}\left(\frac{|x|^3}{a}-\left[\frac{x}{a}\right]^3\right)=k$ $\rightarrow \lim\limits_{x \to a^{-}}\frac{|\dot{x}|^3}{a}-\lim\limits_{x \to a^{-}}\left[\frac{x}{a}\right]^3=k \rightarrow \frac{a^3}{a}-0=k$ $k=a^2$ now, $\lim\limits_{x \to a^{+}}\left(\frac{|x|^3}{3}-\left[\frac{x}{a}\right]^3\right)=l$ $\lim\limits_{x \to a^{+}}\frac{|x|^3}{a}-\lim\limits_{x \to a^{+}}\left[\frac{x}{a}\right]^3 =1$ $a^2-1=l$ $k-1=l \rightarrow k-l=1$ $\;$ © examsnet.com

question: If $f(x)=\begin{cases} \frac{1-\sin^3 x}{3\cos^2 x}, & x < \frac{\pi}{2} \\ \alpha, & x=\frac{\pi}{2} \\ \frac{\beta(1-\sin x)}{(\pi-2x)^2}, & x>\frac{\pi}{2} \end{cases}$ is continuous at $x=\frac{\pi}{2}$ , then $\alpha \beta =$
search_text: if $f(x)=\begin{cases} \frac{1-\sin^3 x}{3\cos^2 x}, & x < \frac{\pi}{2} \\ \alpha, & x=\frac{\pi}{2} \\ \frac{\beta(1-\sin x)}{(\pi-2x)^2}, & x>\frac{\pi}{2} \end{cases}$ is continuous at $x=\frac{\pi}{2}$ , then $\alpha \beta =$ {'a': '$1$', 'b': '$-1$', 'c': '2', 'd': '$-2$'} 2022 2022-07-05 shift_2 mathematics   62 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: 👈: video solution $f(x)$ is continuous at $\frac{\pi}{2}$ $\lim\limits_{x \rightarrow \frac{\pi^{-}}{2}} f(x) = \lim\limits_{x \rightarrow \frac{\pi^{-}}{2}} f(x) = f\left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right)$ $= \lim\limits_{x \rightarrow \frac{\pi^{-}}{2}} f(x) = \lim\limits_{x \rightarrow \frac{\pi^{-}}{2}} \left(\frac{1-\sin^3 x}{3\cos^2 x}\right)$ $= \lim\limits_{x \rightarrow \frac{\pi^{-}}{2}} \left(\frac{(1-\sin x)(1+\sin^2 x+\sin x)}{3(1-\sin x)(1+\sin x)}\right)$ $= \lim\limits_{x \rightarrow \frac{\pi^{-}}{2}} \left[\frac{1+\sin^2 x+\sin x}{3(1+\sin x)}\right] = \frac{3}{3(2)}$ $= \frac{1}{2}$ and $\lim\limits_{x \rightarrow \frac{\pi^{+}}{2}} f(x) = \lim\limits_{x \rightarrow \frac{\pi^{+}}{2}} \frac{\beta(1-\sin x)}{(\pi-2x)^2}$ $= \lim\limits_{h \to 0^{+}} \frac{\beta\left(1-\sin\left(\frac{\pi}{2}+h\right)\right)}{\left(\pi-2\left(\frac{\pi}{2}+h\right)\right)^2}, \quad h = x-\frac{\pi}{2}$ $= \lim\limits_{h \to 0^{+}} \beta\left(\frac{1-\cos h}{4h^2}\right)$ $= \lim\limits_{h \to 0^{+}} \frac{\beta\left(2\sin^2\left(\frac{h}{2}\right)\right)}{4\times 4\left(\frac{h}{2}\right)^2} = \frac{\beta}{8}$ $\therefore \frac{1}{2} = \frac{\beta}{8} = \alpha$ $\rightarrow \alpha = \frac{1}{2} \text{ and } \beta = 4$ $\therefore \alpha\beta = 2$ © examsnet.com

question: $f: R \rightarrow R$ is a function such that $|f(x)-y| \leq \;\frac{1}{2}|x-y| \forall x, y \in R$ and $f'(x) \geq \frac{1}{2} \;\; \forall x \in R, f(1)=\frac{1}{2}$
search_text: $f: r \rightarrow r$ is a function such that $|f(x)-y| \leq \;\frac{1}{2}|x-y| \forall x, y \in r$ and $f'(x) \geq \frac{1}{2} \;\; \forall x \in r, f(1)=\frac{1}{2}$ {'a': '1', 'b': '0', 'c': '2', 'd': 'infinite'} 2022 2022-07-05 shift_2 mathematics   63 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: 👈: video solution $|f(x)-y| \leq \;\frac{1}{2}|x-y|, \forall x, y \in r$ $=\lim\limits_{h \rightarrow 0}|f(x+h)-f(x)| \leq \;\frac{1}{2}|x+h-x|$ $=\lim\limits_{h \rightarrow 0}\;\frac{|f(x+h)-f(x)|}{h} \leq \;\frac{1}{2}$ $f'(x) \leq \;\frac{1}{2}$ but $f'(x) \geq \;\frac{1}{2}$ (given) $\rightarrow \;\; f'(x)=\;\frac{1}{2} \rightarrow f(x)=\;\frac{1}{2}x+c$ $\rightarrow \;\; f(1)=\;\frac{1}{2} \times 1+c \rightarrow \;\frac{1}{2}=\;\frac{1}{2}+c$ $\;\; c=0$ $\therefore \;\; f(x)=\;\frac{1}{2}x \;\text{ or }\; y=\;\frac{1}{2}x$ substitute $y=\;\frac{1}{2}x$ in equation $y=x^2-2x-5$ to determine the number of points of intersection $\;\frac{1}{2}x=x^2-2x-5$ $\rightarrow 2x^2-5x-10=0$ $\rightarrow x=\frac{5 \pm \sqrt{25+80}}{4}=\frac{5 \pm \sqrt{105}}{4}$ $\therefore$ there are two point of intersection. © examsnet.com

search_text: if $\; \frac{d^{n} y}{d x^{n}} = y_{n}$ and $y = e^{\sqrt{x}} + e^{-\sqrt{x}}$ , then $4 x y_{2} + 2 y_{1} =$ {'a': '$-y$', 'b': '$y$', 'c': '$2y$', 'd': '$-2 y$'} 2022 2022-07-05 shift_2 mathematics   64 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: 👈: video solution given, $\; \; \frac{d^{n} y}{d x^{n}} = y_{n} \; \text{ and } \; y = e^{\sqrt{x}} + e^{-\sqrt{x}}$ $\rightarrow \; \; y_{1} = e^{\sqrt{x}} \times \frac{1}{2 \sqrt{x}} + e^{-\sqrt{x}} \times \left( \frac{-1}{2 \sqrt{x}} \right)$ $\; = \; \frac{1}{2 \sqrt{x}} \left[ e^{\sqrt{x}} - e^{-\sqrt{x}} \right]$ $\rightarrow \; \; 2 \sqrt{x} y_{1} = e^{\sqrt{x}} - e^{-\sqrt{x}}$ again differentiate, we get, $\; 2 \sqrt{x} y_{2} + 2 y_{1} \times \frac{1}{2 \sqrt{x}}$ $\; = e^{\sqrt{x}} \times \frac{1}{2 \sqrt{x}} - e^{-\sqrt{x}} \left( \frac{-1}{2 \sqrt{x}} \right)$ $\rightarrow \; \frac{4 x y_{2} + 2 y_{1}}{2 \sqrt{x}} = \; \frac{e^{\sqrt{x}} + e^{-\sqrt{x}}}{2 \sqrt{x}}$ $\rightarrow 4 x y_{2} + 2 y_{1} = y$ © examsnet.com

search_text: if the two curves $y = a^{x}$ and $y = b^{x}$ intersect at angle $\alpha$ , then $\tan \alpha =$ {'a': '$\\; \\frac{\\log a-\\log b}{1+\\log a \\log b}$', 'b': '$\\; \\frac{\\log a+\\log b}{1-\\log a \\log b}$', 'c': '$\\; \\frac{\\pi}{4}$', 'd': '$\\; \\frac{\\pi}{2}$'} 2022 2022-07-05 shift_2 mathematics   65 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: 👈: video solution $y = a^x$ and $y = b^x$ only intersect at the point $(0,1)$ $\; y = a^x, \; \frac{dy}{dx} = a^x \log a$ let $m_1 = \frac{dy}{dx}|_{(0,1)} = \log a$ $\; y = b^x, \; \frac{dy}{dx} = b^x \log b$ let $m_2 = \; \frac{dy}{dx}|_{(0,1)} = \log b$ $\; \tan \alpha = \left| \; \frac{m_1-m_2}{1+m_1 m_2} \right| = \left| \; \frac{\log a-\log b}{1+\log a \log b} \right|$ © examsnet.com

search_text: an object of mass $10 \text{kg}$ is released from rest in a liquid. if the object moves a distance of $2 \text{m}$ while sinking in time duration of $1 \text{s}$ , then the mass of the liquid displaced by the submerged object is (acceleration due to gravity $=10 \text{m} \text{s}^{-2}$ ) {'a': '$25 \\text{kg}$', 'b': '$6 \\text{kg}$', 'c': '$3 \\text{kg}$', 'd': '$4 \\text{kg}$'} 2022 2022-07-05 shift_2 physics   96 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: given, mass of object, $m=10 \text{kg}$ distance travelled by object, $s=2 \text{m}$ time, $t=1 \text{s}$ according to given situation, $s\;=u t+\;\frac{1}{2} a t^2$ $\rightarrow \;\; s\;=0+\;\frac{1}{2} a t^2$ $[ \therefore u=0]$ $s\;=\;\frac{1}{2} a t^2$ $\rightarrow \;\; 2\;=\;\frac{1}{2} \times a \times 1^2$ $a\;=4 \text{m s}^{-2}$ net force on the object in liquid, $f_{\;\text{net }\;}=m a=10 \times 4=40 \text{n}$ weight of the object, $w\;=m g$ $\;=10 \times 10=100 \text{n}$ upthrust force on the object, $f'=w-f_{\;\text{net }\;}=100-40=60 \text{n}$ according to archimedes' principle, weight liquid displaced = upthrust force $\rightarrow \;\; m'=\;\frac{f'}{g}=\;\frac{60}{10}=6 \text{kg}$ © examsnet.com

search_text: the amount of heat needed to heat 200 grams of ice at $-10^{\circ}\mathrm{c}$ to convert it into water at $30^{\circ}\mathrm{c}$ is specific heat capacity of ice $=2100\,\mathrm{jkg}^{-1}\,\mathrm{k}^{-1}$ specific heat capacity of water $=4186\,\mathrm{j}\,\mathrm{kg}^{-1}\,\mathrm{k}^{-1}$ latent heat of fusion of ice $=3.35\times10^{5}\,\mathrm{j}\,\mathrm{kg}^{-1}$ {'a': '$96316\\,\\mathrm{j}$', 'b': '$67000\\,\\mathrm{j}$', 'c': '$92116\\,\\mathrm{j}$', 'd': '$71200\\,\\mathrm{t}$'} 2022 2022-07-05 shift_2 physics   97 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: given, $s_{\text{ice}}=2100\,\mathrm{j}\,\mathrm{kg}^{-1}\,\mathrm{k}^{-1}$ $s_{\text{water}}=4186\,\mathrm{j}\,\mathrm{kg}^{-1}\,\mathrm{k}^{-1}$ latent heat of fusion of ice, $l_{\text{kee}}=3.35\times10^5\,\mathrm{jkg}^{-1}$ mass of ice, $m=200\,\mathrm{g}=0.2\,\mathrm{kg}$ temperature of ice, $t_1=-10^{\circ}\mathrm{c}$ final temperature of water, $t_2=30^{\circ}\mathrm{c}$ total required heat, $q=m\,s_{\text{lie}}(0-t_1)+m\,l_{\text{lce}}+m\,s_{\text{water}}(t_2-0)$ $=0.2\times2100[0-(-10)]+0.2\times3.35\times10^5+0.2\times4186(30-0)$ $=0.2\times2100\times10+0.2\times3.35\times10^5+0.2\times4186\times30$ $=9.6316\times10^4\,\mathrm{j}$ $=96316\,\mathrm{j}$ © examsnet.com

(i) by eq. (ii), we get $\; \frac{\; \frac{1}{10}}{t'} = \frac{70-t_0}{60-t_0}$ $\; \rightarrow \; \frac{t'}{10} = \frac{70-t_0}{60-t_0} \rightarrow t' = 10 \left( \frac{70-t_0}{60-t_0} \right)$ $\text{ clearly, } \; \rightarrow \; \frac{70-t_0}{60-t_0} > 1$ $\therefore t' > 10 \text{ minutes.}$ © examsnet.com

question: The rms speed of oxygen and room temperature is about $500 \text{ms}^{-1}$ . The rms speed of hydrogen at the same temperature is about
search_text: the rms speed of oxygen and room temperature is about $500 \text{ms}^{-1}$ . the rms speed of hydrogen at the same temperature is about {'a': '$125 \\text{ms}^{-1}$', 'b': '$2000 \\text{m s}^{-1}$', 'c': '$8000 \\text{m s}^{-1}$', 'd': '$500 \\text{m s}^{-1}$'} 2022 2022-07-05 shift_2 physics   100 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: given $(v_{\text{rms}})_{\text{o}_2} = 500 \text{m/s}$ $(v_{\text{rms}})_{\text{h}_2} = ?$ we know that, $v_{\text{rms}} = \sqrt{\frac{3rt}{m}}$ $\rightarrow v_{\text{rms}} \propto \frac{1}{\sqrt{m}}$ $\rightarrow \frac{(v_{\text{ms}})_{\text{h}_2}}{(v_{\text{rms}})_{\text{o}_2}} = \sqrt{\frac{m_{\text{o}_2}}{m_{\text{h}_2}}}$ $\rightarrow \frac{(v_{\text{ms}})_{\text{h}_2}}{500} = \sqrt{\frac{32}{2}}$ $= \sqrt{16} = 4$ $\rightarrow (v_{\text{ms}})_{\text{h}_2} = 4 \times 500 = 2000 \text{ms}^{-1}$ © examsnet.com

search_text: among the following, the equation representing a progressive wave is (a) $y=2\cos 3x \sin 10t$ (b) $y=2\sqrt{x - v t}$ (c) $y=3\sin(5x-0.5t)+4\cos(5x-0.5t)$ (d) $y=\cos x \sin t+\cos 2x \cdot \sin 2t$ {'a': 'a and d', 'b': 'c', 'c': 'a,c, d', 'd': 'b'} 2022 2022-07-05 shift_2 physics   101 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: a wave which travels continuously in a medium in the same direction without the change in its amplitude is called a progressive wave. equation of progressive wave is given as $y(x,t)=a \sin (\omega t - k x + \varphi)$ we can write the above equation as a linear combination of sine and cosine function as, $y(x,t)=a \sin (k x - \omega t)+b \cos (k x - \omega t)$ hence, among the given options $y=3 \sin (5x-0.5t)+4 \cos (5x-0.5t)$ represents the equation of progressive wave. © examsnet.com

search_text: a beam of light both reflects and refracts at the surface between air and glass. the index of refraction of the glass is 1.4. if the refracted and the reflected rays are perpendicular to each other, then the angle of incidence in the air is {'a': '$\\tan^{-1}(1.4)$', 'b': '$\\sin^{-1}\\left(\\;\\frac{1}{1.4}\\right)$', 'c': '$\\tan^{-1}\\left(\\;\\frac{1}{1.4}\\right)$', 'd': '$\\sin^{-1}\\left(\\;\\frac{1.4}{\\pi}\\right)$'} 2022 2022-07-05 shift_2 physics   102 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: given, refractive index of glass, $\mu=1.4$ when the light beam incident of polarizing angle i.e at $i=i_p$ , then refracted and reflected rays are perpendicular to each other. hence, according to brewster's law $\;\mu=\tan i_p$ $\;\rightarrow \;\; i_p=\tan^{-1}(\mu)=\tan^{-1}(1.4)$ $\;\therefore \;\text{ angle of incidence }\;$ $\;i=i_p=\tan^{-1}(1.4)$ $\;$ © examsnet.com

search_text: a ray of light is incident at $30^{\circ}$ from a medium of refractive index 2 into a medium of refractive index 1 , then the angle of refraction is {'a': '$30^{\\circ}$', 'b': '$*0^{\\circ}$', 'c': '$45^{\\circ}$', 'd': '$90^{\\circ}$'} 2022 2022-07-05 shift_2 physics   103 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: the given situation is shown below according to snell's law, $\;2\mu_1\;=\;\frac{\sin 30^{\circ}}{\sin r}$ $\rightarrow\;\frac{\mu_1}{\mu_2}\;=\;\frac{\frac{1}{2}}{\sin r}$ $\rightarrow\;\frac{1}{2}\;=\;\frac{1}{2\sin r}$ $\rightarrow\sin r\;=1=\sin 90^{\circ}$ $\rightarrow r\;=90^{\circ}$ © examsnet.com

question: A charge $Q$ is to be divided between two objects. The values of the charges on the objects so that the electrostatic force between them will be maximum is
search_text: a charge $q$ is to be divided between two objects. the values of the charges on the objects so that the electrostatic force between them will be maximum is {'a': '$\\frac{q}{2},\\\\;\\frac{q}{2}$', 'b': '$\\frac{q}{3},\\\\;\\frac{2}{3}q$', 'c': '$\\frac{q}{4},\\\\;\\frac{3}{4}q$', 'd': '$\\frac{q}{5},\\\\;\\frac{4}{5}q$'} 2022 2022-07-05 shift_2 physics   104 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: let $q$ be divided into two charges $q$ and $q-q$ i.e $q_1=q$ and $q_2=q-q$ $\therefore$ electrostatic force between $q$ and $q-q$ is given as $f = \frac{1}{4\pi \epsilon_0} \cdot \frac{q(q-q)}{r^2}$ $f$ will be maximum if $\\;\\;\frac{df}{dq}=0$ $\rightarrow \\;\frac{d}{dq} \cdot \left[ \frac{q(q-q)}{r^2} \right] =0$ $\rightarrow q(0-1)+(q-q) \cdot 1=0$ $\rightarrow q-2q=0$ $\rightarrow q=\frac{q}{2}$ $\\;\text{hence,}\\; q_1=q=\frac{q}{2}$ $\\;q_2=q-q=q-\frac{q}{2}=\frac{q}{2}$ © examsnet.com

search_text: in a space having electric field $\vec{e} = a( x \hat{i} + y \hat{j})$ the potential at a point $(10 \, \text{m}, 20 \, \text{m})$ is zero, then the potential at the origin is $[ a = 10 \, \text{vm}^{-2} ]$ {'a': '$500 \\, \\text{v}$', 'b': '$2000 \\, \\text{v}$', 'c': '$2500 \\, \\text{v}$', 'd': '$1500 \\, \\text{v}$'} 2022 2022-07-05 shift_2 physics   105 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: from the given situation, $v_a - v_0 = -\int\int e \, dx\,dy$ $0 - v_0 = -\int\limits_{0}^{10} \int\limits_{0}^{20} (a x \hat{i} + a y \hat{j}) \,dx\,dy$ $\rightarrow \; -v_0 = -\int\limits_{0}^{10} \int\limits_{0}^{20} a x \hat{i} \,dx \hat{i} + a \hat{j} \,dy \hat{j}$ $v_0 = -\int\limits_{0}^{10} \int\limits_{0}^{20} a x \,dx + a y \,dy$ $= \int\limits_{0}^{10} a x \,dx + \int\limits_{0}^{20} a y \,dy$ $= \left[ a \frac{x^2}{2} \right]_{0}^{10} + \left[ \frac{a y^2}{2} \right]_{0}^{20}$ $= a \frac{10^2}{2} + a \frac{20^2}{2} = 50 a + 200 a$ $= 250 a = 250 \times 10 \; [ \because a = 10 \, \text{vm}^{-2} ]$ $= 2500 \, \text{v}$ © examsnet.com

search_text: a metal loop of area $10\ \text{cm}^{2}$ is placed in a region such that its area vector points along $\hat{k}$ . the region contains a uniform magnetic field of magnitude $1.73\ \text{t}$ that points in the direction $\hat{i}+\hat{j}+\hat{k}$ . when the magnetic field is switched off, the field decreases to zero at a steady rate in $10\ \text{s}$ , then the magnitude of emf induced in the loop is {'a': '$0.10\\ \\text{mv}$', 'b': '$0.17\\ \\text{mv}$', 'c': '$1\\ \\text{mv}$', 'd': '$1.7\\ \\text{mv}$'} 2022 2022-07-05 shift_2 physics   112 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: given, area of metal loop, $a=10\ \text{cm}^{2}=10^{-3}\ \text{m}^{2},\ \vec{a}=10^{-3}\ \hat{k}$ magnitude of magnetic field; $b=1.73\ \text{t}$ magnetic field is directed along, $\hat{i}+\hat{j}+\hat{k}$ unit vector along the direction of magnetic field, $\;\ \hat{\vec{n}} = \frac{\hat{i+\hat{j}+\hat{k}}}{\sqrt{1^{2}+1^{2}+1^{2}}} = \frac{\hat{i+\hat{j}+\hat{k}}}{\sqrt{3}}$ $\therefore\ \vec{b}=b\ \hat{\vec{n}}$ $= 1.73\ \frac{\hat{(i+\hat{j}+\hat{k})}}{\sqrt{3}} = \hat{i}+\hat{j}+\hat{k}$ magnetic flux linked with coil, $\begin{aligned} \phi = \vec{b} \cdot \vec{a} \end{aligned}$ $(\hat{i}+\hat{j}+\hat{k}) \cdot (10^{-3} \hat{k}) = 10^{-3}\ \text{wb}$ $\text{ induced emf, } |e| = \frac{\delta \phi}{\delta t} = \frac{\phi - \phi_{2}}{10}$ $= \frac{10^{-3}-0}{10} = \frac{10^{-3}-0}{10} = 10^{-4}\ \text{v}$ $= 0.1 \times 10^{-3}\ \text{v}$ $= 0.1\ \text{mv}$ © examsnet.com

(i)] $\;=k_e$ $\therefore \;\; k_e\;=k_b$ © examsnet.com

question: A particle of mass $2 \times 10^{-27} \mathrm{kg}$ has de-Broglie wavelength of $3.3 \times 10^{-10} \mathrm{m}$ . The kinetic energy of this particle is (Plank's Constant $h = 6.6 \times 10^{-34} \mathrm{J}\cdot\mathrm{s}$ )
search_text: a particle of mass $2 \times 10^{-27} \mathrm{kg}$ has de-broglie wavelength of $3.3 \times 10^{-10} \mathrm{m}$ . the kinetic energy of this particle is (plank's constant $h = 6.6 \times 10^{-34} \mathrm{j}\cdot\mathrm{s}$ ) {'a': '$5 \\times 10^{-20} \\mathrm{j}$', 'b': '$8 \\times 10^{-20} \\mathrm{j}$', 'c': '$1 \\times 10^{-21} \\mathrm{j}$', 'd': '$6 \\times 10^{-22} \\mathrm{j}$'} 2022 2022-07-05 shift_2 physics   116 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: mass of particle, $m = 2 \times 10^{-27} \mathrm{kg}$ de-broglie wavelength, $\lambda = 3.3 \times 10^{-10} \mathrm{m}$ planck's constant $h = 6.6 \times 10^{-34} \mathrm{j}\cdot\mathrm{s}$ we know that, de-broglie wavelength $\; \lambda = \frac{h}{p}$ $\; \rightarrow \;\; \lambda = \frac{h}{\sqrt{2 m k}}$ $( \because p = \sqrt{2 m k})$ where, $k$ is kinetic energy of particle $\; \rightarrow \;\; \lambda^2 = \frac{h^2}{2 m k}$ $\; \rightarrow \;\; k = \frac{h^2}{2 m \lambda^2} = \frac{(6.6 \times 10^{-34})^2}{2 \times 2 \times 10^{-27} \times (3.3 \times 10^{-10})^2}$ $\; = 1 \times 10^{-21} \mathrm{j}$ $\;$ © examsnet.com

question: The frequency of the light emitted when an electron comes down from $n=4$ to $n=2$ level in hydrogen atom is $\;\frac{3}{7}$ times of the following transition of the $\mathrm{Li}$ atom
search_text: the frequency of the light emitted when an electron comes down from $n=4$ to $n=2$ level in hydrogen atom is $\;\frac{3}{7}$ times of the following transition of the $\mathrm{li}$ atom {'a': '4 to 3', 'b': '4 to 1', 'c': '3 to 2', 'd': '5 to 3'} 2022 2022-07-05 shift_2 physics   118 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: we know that, frequency of light radiation emitted during the transition of electron from energy level $n_2$ to $n_1$ in h-atom $v = z^2 r c \left[ \;\frac{1}{n_1^2} - \;\frac{1}{n_2^2} \right] ( \because z=1 \; \text{ for hydrogen } \; )$ where $r$ is rydberg constant and $c$ is speed of light. for the first case $n_1=2$ and $n_2=4$ $\; v_1 = r c \left( \;\frac{1}{2^2} - \;\frac{1}{4^2} \right) = r c \times \;\frac{3}{16}$ $\; v_1 = \;\frac{3 r c}{16}$ ......(i) $\;\frac{3}{7}$ times of transition of li atom $= \;\frac{7}{3} \times \;\frac{3 r c}{16} = \;\frac{7 r c}{16}$ for lithium atom, $z=3$ and for transition for 4 th orbit to 3 rd orbit is given as $v_2 = z^2 r c \left( \;\frac{1}{3^2} - \;\frac{1}{4^2} \right)$ $= (3)^2 r c \left( \;\frac{7}{144} \right) = \;\frac{7}{16} r c$ © examsnet.com

question: Which of the following reactions is not a disproportionation reaction?
search_text: which of the following reactions is not a disproportionation reaction? {'a': '$\\mathrm{caco}_3 \\longrightarrow \\mathrm{cao} + \\mathrm{co}_2$', 'b': '$\\mathrm{p}_4 + 3 \\mathrm{naoh} + 3 \\mathrm{h}_2\\mathrm{o} \\longrightarrow 3 \\mathrm{nah}_2\\mathrm{po}_2 + \\mathrm{ph}_3$', 'c': '$2 \\mathrm{h}_2\\mathrm{o}_2 \\longrightarrow 2 \\mathrm{h}_2\\mathrm{o} + \\mathrm{o}_2$', 'd': '$2 \\mathrm{cu}^{+} \\longrightarrow \\mathrm{cu}^{2+} + \\mathrm{cu}$'} 2022 2022-07-05 shift_2 chemistry   128 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: disproportionation reactions are the reactions in which a compound undergoes oxidation as well as reduction. $\mathrm{caco}_3 \rightarrow \mathrm{cao} + \mathrm{co}_2$ is an example of decomposition reaction. there is no simultaneous oxidation or reduction happening. $\therefore$ it is not an example of disproportionation reaction. rest all examples $\overset{0}{\mathrm{p}}_4 + 3 \mathrm{naoh} + 3 \mathrm{h}_2\mathrm{o} \rightarrow 3 \mathrm{nah}_2\overset{+1}{\mathrm{po}_2} + \overset{-3}{\mathrm{ph}_3}$ $\; 2 \mathrm{h}_2 \overset{-1}{\mathrm{o}_2} \rightarrow 2 \mathrm{h}_2 \overset{-2}{\mathrm{o}} + \overset{0}{\mathrm{o}}_2$ $\; {2\mathrm{cu}^{+}}^{+1} \rightarrow \overset{2+}{\mathrm{cu}} + \overset{0}{\mathrm{cu}}$ the element undergoes oxidation and reduction both. hence, are examples of disproportionation reactions. © examsnet.com

question: For a reaction $2\mathrm{CO}(\mathrm{g}) + \mathrm{O}_2(\mathrm{g}) \rightleftharpoons 2\mathrm{CO}_2(\mathrm{g}), \Delta_{r} G^{0} = -128\,\mathrm{kJ}$ at $300\,\mathrm{K}$ . If $\Delta_{r} S^{\circ}$ of the reaction is $-40\,\mathrm{J}\,\mathrm{K}^{-1}$ , calculate $\Delta_{r} U$ of the reaction.
search_text: for a reaction $2\mathrm{co}(\mathrm{g}) + \mathrm{o}_2(\mathrm{g}) \rightleftharpoons 2\mathrm{co}_2(\mathrm{g}), \delta_{r} g^{0} = -128\,\mathrm{kj}$ at $300\,\mathrm{k}$ . if $\delta_{r} s^{\circ}$ of the reaction is $-40\,\mathrm{j}\,\mathrm{k}^{-1}$ , calculate $\delta_{r} u$ of the reaction. {'a': '$-137.5\\,\\mathrm{kj}$', 'b': '$-128\\,\\mathrm{kj}$', 'c': '$-140\\,\\mathrm{kj}$', 'd': '$126.2\\,\\mathrm{kj}$'} 2022 2022-07-05 shift_2 chemistry   130 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: $2\mathrm{co}(\mathrm{g}) + \mathrm{o},(\mathrm{g}) \rightleftharpoons 2\mathrm{co}_2(\mathrm{g})$ given, $\delta_r g = -128\,\mathrm{kj}$ $\delta_r s^{\circ}\; = -40\,\mathrm{k} \rightarrow \delta_r u = ?$ $\delta g\; = \delta h - t \delta s$ ....(i) $\delta h\; = \delta u + \delta n r t$ .......(ii) from (i) and (ii), $\delta g\; = \delta u + \delta n r t - t \delta s$ $-128000\; = \delta u + (-1) \times 8.314 \times 300 - 300 \times (-40)$ $-128000\; = \delta u - 2494.2 + 12000$ $-128000\; = \delta u - 9505.8$ $\delta u\; = -128000 - 9505.8$ $\; = -137505.8\,\mathrm{j} \cong -137.50\,\mathrm{kj}$ © examsnet.com

question: Which of the following equations are correct? (A) $U = H - PV$ (B) $G = H - TS$ (C) $U = q + W$
search_text: which of the following equations are correct? (a) $u = h - pv$ (b) $g = h - ts$ (c) $u = q + w$ {'a': '$a, b$ and $c$', 'b': '$a$ and $b$ only', 'c': '$a$ and $c$ only', 'd': '$b$ and $c$ only'} 2022 2022-07-05 shift_2 chemistry   131 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: (a) $u = h - p v$ , (b) $g = h - t s$ , (c) $u = q + w$ the enthalpy of system is sum of internal energy and product of pressure and volume. $\delta h\; = \delta u + p \delta v ; \;\; h = u + p v$ $\;u\; = h - p v$ also, $\delta g = \delta h - t \delta s$ or $g = h - t s$ according to first law of thermodynamics, $\delta u = q - w$ $\therefore$ equation (c), $u = q + w$ is incorrect. option (b), only (a) and (b) are correct. © examsnet.com

question: For a reaction $A(g)+\;\frac{1}{2} B(g) \rightleftharpoons C(g)+\;\text{ heat }$ favorable conditions for the reaction to occur in the forward direction are
search_text: for a reaction $a(g)+\;\frac{1}{2} b(g) \rightleftharpoons c(g)+\;\text{ heat }$ favorable conditions for the reaction to occur in the forward direction are {'a': 'low t and low p', 'b': 'low t and high p', 'c': 'high t and low p', 'd': 'high t and high p'} 2022 2022-07-05 shift_2 chemistry   132 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: for the given reaction, $a(g)+\;\frac{1}{2} b(g) \rightleftharpoons c(g)+\;\text{ heat }\;$ low temperature will favour the forward reaction as it is an exothermic reaction. according to le-chatelier's principle, if there is any change in the conditions of equilibrium, then the equilibrium shifts in the direction that can reduce the effect of the change. as given reaction is. exothermic, increase temperature will favour backward/reverse reaction and decrease temperature will favour forward reaction. number of moles of reactant $=1+0.5=1.5$ number of moles of product $=1$ $\therefore$ high pressure will favour forward reaction as the effect of increased pressure can be minimised, if it goes in forward reaction. © examsnet.com

search_text: if we resolve the rational fraction $\;\frac{1}{(1-2 x)^{2}(1-3 x)}$ in to partial fractions of the form $\;\frac{a}{1-3x} + \;\frac{b}{1-2x} + \;\frac{c}{(1-2x)^2}$ , then what is the $\min\{a, b, c\}=$ {'a': '$1$', 'b': '$9$', 'c': '$-2$', 'd': '$-6$'} 2022 2022-07-06 shift_1 mathematics   19 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: 👈: video solution we have, $\;\;\frac{1}{(1-2x)^2 \cdot (1-3x)} = \;\frac{a}{(1-3x)} + \;\frac{b}{1-2x} + \;\frac{c}{(1-2x)^2}$ $\;\rightarrow 1=a(1-2x)^2+b(1-2x)(1-3x)+c(1-3x)$ substitute $x=\;\frac{1}{2}$ , we get $\;1=c \left(1-\;\frac{3}{2}\right) \rightarrow 1=c \left(-\;\frac{1}{2}\right)$ $\;c=-2$ substitute $x=\;\frac{1}{3}$ , we get $1=a \left(1-\;\frac{2}{3}\right)^2 \rightarrow a=9$ substitute $x=0$ , we get $1=a+b+c$ $\rightarrow 1=9+b-2$ $\rightarrow b=-6$ $\text{min}\{a, b \;\text{ and }\; c\}=-6$ © examsnet.com

search_text: if $\int\frac{dx}{x^{2022}(1+x^{2022})^{\frac{1}{2022}}}=-\frac{(1+x^{m})^{\frac{n}{m}}}{n x^{n}}+c$ , then $m-n=$ {'a': '1', 'b': '2', 'c': '3', 'd': '0'} 2022 2022-07-06 shift_1 mathematics   73 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: 👈: video solution given $\int\frac{dx}{x^{2022}(1+x^{2022})^{\frac{1}{2022}}}=-\frac{(1+x^{m})^{\frac{n}{m}}}{n x^{n}}+c$ let $i=\int\frac{dx}{x^{2022}(1+x^{2022})^{\frac{1}{2022}}}$ $\;=\int\frac{dx}{x^{2022}\left[x^{2022}\left(1+\frac{1}{x^{2022}}\right)\right]^{\frac{1}{2022}}}$ $\;=\int\frac{dx}{x^{2023}\left[1+\frac{1}{x^{2022}}\right]^{\frac{1}{2022}}}$ let $\;1+\frac{1}{x^{2022}}=t$ $\rightarrow -2022 \times \frac{1}{x^{2023}}dx=dt$ $\rightarrow \;\; \frac{1}{x^{2023}}dx=-\frac{1}{2022}dt$ $\rightarrow \;\; i=\frac{-1}{2022}\int\frac{1}{t^{\frac{1}{2022}}}dt$ $\;=\frac{-1}{2022}\int t^{-\frac{1}{2022}}dt$ $\;=-\frac{1}{2022}\left(\frac{t^{-\frac{1}{2022}+1}}{1}\right)+c$ $=-\frac{1}{2021}\left[(1+x^{-2022})^{\frac{2021}{2022}}\right]$ $\;=-\frac{1}{2021}\left[\frac{x^{2022}+1}{x^{2022}}\right]^{\frac{2021}{2022}}$ $\;=\frac{-[x^{2022}+1]^{2021}}{x^{2021}}\times 2021$ $\;\therefore n=2021 \text{ and } m=2022$ $\;\therefore m-n=1$ © examsnet.com

search_text: the equation for the trajectory of a projectile is $y = \left(\;\frac{x}{\sqrt{3}} - \;\frac{x^{2}}{60}\right)  \mathrm{m}$ . the velocity of projection of the projectile is (acceleration due to gravity $=10  \mathrm{m}\,\mathrm{s}^{-2}$ ) {'a': '$8  \\mathrm{m}\\,\\mathrm{s}^{-1}$', 'b': '$40  \\mathrm{m}\\,\\mathrm{s}^{-1}$', 'c': '$16  \\mathrm{m}\\,\\mathrm{s}^{-1}$', 'd': '$20  \\mathrm{m}\\,\\mathrm{s}^{-1}$'} 2022 2022-07-06 shift_1 physics   84 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: given equation for trajectory of a projectile, $y = \left(\;\frac{x}{\sqrt{3}} - \;\frac{x^{2}}{60}\right)   \mathrm{m}$ .......(i) to find velocity of projection of projectile comparing with equation $y = x \tan \theta - \;\frac{g}{2 \mu^{2} \cos^{2} \theta} \cdot x^{2}$ ......(ii) we get, $\tan \theta = \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$ $\therefore \; \theta = 30^{\circ}$ $\cos 30^{\circ} = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$ ......(iii) also, $\;\frac{g}{2 \mu^{2} \cos^{2} \theta} = \frac{1}{60}$ $g = 10  \mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}, \cos^{2} \theta = \cos^{2} 30^{\circ} = \left(\;\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)^{2} = \frac{3}{4}$ $\frac{10}{2 u^{2} \times \cos^{2} 30^{\circ}} = \frac{1}{60}$ $\rightarrow u^{2} = \frac{10 \times 60}{2 \times \frac{3}{4}} \rightarrow u^{2} = \frac{1200}{3} = 400$ $\rightarrow u = \sqrt{400} \rightarrow u = 20  \mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}$ © examsnet.com

search_text: f- centers are formed in $\mathrm{nacl}$ crystal if it is heated with $\mathrm{na}$ vapour. the above is due to {'a': 'schottky defect', 'b': 'dislocation defect', 'c': 'metal excess defect', 'd': 'metal deficiency defect'} 2022 2022-07-06 shift_1 chemistry   142 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: when crystals of $\mathrm{nacl}$ are heated with sodium vapour, the sodium ions are deposited on the surface of $\mathrm{nacl}$ crystals and the $\mathrm{cl}^{-}$ ions diffuse to form $\mathrm{nacl}$ . during the process the loss of electron from $\mathrm{na}$ to form $\mathrm{na}^{+}$ ion takes place. the electron given out by na diffuses into the crystal and occupies anionic site which is called f-centre. therefore, the formation of f-centres is metal excess defect. © examsnet.com

The Vapour pressure of water. when $12\,\text{g}$ of urea (molar mass, $60\,\text{g}\,\text{mol}^{-1}$ ) and $36\,\text{g}$ of glucose (molar mass, $180\,\text{g}$ $\text{mol}^{-1}$ ) is dissolved in $100\,\text{g}$ of water at the same temperature (in torr) is
search_text: at $298\,\text{k}$ , the vapour pressure of pure water is 25 torr. the vapour pressure of water. when $12\,\text{g}$ of urea (molar mass, $60\,\text{g}\,\text{mol}^{-1}$ ) and $36\,\text{g}$ of glucose (molar mass, $180\,\text{g}$ $\text{mol}^{-1}$ ) is dissolved in $100\,\text{g}$ of water at the same temperature (in torr) is {'a': '$25.02$', 'b': '$24.12$', 'c': '$23.92$', 'd': '$23.32$'} 2022 2022-07-06 shift_1 chemistry   143 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: given, $p^{\circ}=25$ torr, mass of urea $=12\,\text{g}$ mass of glucose $=36\,\text{g}$ , mass of water $=100\,\text{g}$ moles of urea $=\;\frac{\text{ mass }}{\text{ molecular mass }}\;=\frac{12}{60}=0.2$ moles of glucose $=\;\frac{\text{ mass }}{\text{ molecular mass }}\;=\frac{36}{180}=0.2$ moles of water $=\;\frac{\text{ mass }}{\text{ molecular mass }}\;=\frac{100}{18}=5.55$ mole fraction of urea $=\;\frac{0.2}{0.2+0.2+5.55}\;=\frac{0.2}{5.95}=0.0336$ mole fraction of glucose $=\;\frac{0.2}{0.2+0.2+5.55}\;=\frac{0.2}{5.95}=0.0336$ $\;\frac{p^{\circ}-p}{p^{\circ}}=$ mole fraction of solute $\rightarrow\;\frac{25-p}{25}\;=0.0336+0.0336$ $\rightarrow\;25-p\;=25 \times 0.0672$ $\rightarrow\;p\;=25-16.8$ $\;=23.32\;\text{ torr }\;$ © examsnet.com

search_text: if $a=\begin{bmatrix} \sin\alpha & -\cos\alpha \\ \cos\alpha & \sin\alpha \end{bmatrix}$ and $a+a^{-1}=i$ , then $\alpha=$ {'a': '$0$', 'b': '$\\frac{\\pi}{3}$', 'c': '$\\frac{\\pi}{6}$', 'd': '$\\frac{\\pi}{4}$'} 2022 2022-07-06 shift_2 mathematics   5 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: 👈: video solution given, $a=\begin{bmatrix} \sin\alpha & -\cos\alpha \\ \cos\alpha & \sin\alpha \end{bmatrix}$ $\operatorname{adj} a = \begin{bmatrix} \sin\alpha & \cos\alpha \\ -\cos\alpha & \sin\alpha \end{bmatrix}$ $|a| = \sin^{2}\alpha + \cos^{2}\alpha = 1$ $a^{-1}=\begin{bmatrix} \sin\alpha & \cos\alpha \\ -\cos\alpha & \sin\alpha \end{bmatrix}$ $a+a^{-1} = \begin{bmatrix} \sin\alpha & -\cos\alpha \\ \cos\alpha & \sin\alpha \end{bmatrix} + \begin{bmatrix} \sin\alpha & \cos\alpha \\ -\cos\alpha & \sin\alpha \end{bmatrix}$ $= \begin{bmatrix} 2\sin\alpha & 0 \\ 0 & 2\sin\alpha \end{bmatrix}$ $a+a^{-1}=i,$ if $2\sin\alpha=1$ $\sin\alpha = \frac{1}{2} \rightarrow \alpha = \frac{\pi}{6}$ © examsnet.com

question: If the vertices $A, B$ and $C$ of an isosceles triangle $A B C$ are respectively $z_{1}, z_{2}$ and $z_{3}$ and if $\angle C = 90^{\circ}$ , then
search_text: if the vertices $a, b$ and $c$ of an isosceles triangle $a b c$ are respectively $z_{1}, z_{2}$ and $z_{3}$ and if $\angle c = 90^{\circ}$ , then {'a': '$(z_{1} - z_{2}) = (z_{1} - z_{3})(z_{3} - z_{2})$', 'b': '$(z_{1} - z_{2})^{2} = (z_{1} - z_{3})(z_{3} - z_{2})$', 'c': '$(z_{1} - z_{2})^{2} = 2(z_{1} - z_{3})(z_{3} - z_{2})$', 'd': '$z_{1}^{2} + z_{2}^{2} + z_{3}^{2} = z_{1} z_{2} z_{3} + 2$'} 2022 2022-07-06 shift_2 mathematics   9 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: 👈: video solution $\triangle a b c$ is an isosceles right. angled triangle with $a b$ as hypotenuse. $\frac{z_1 - z_2}{z_3 - z_2} = \sqrt{2} e^{\frac{i\pi}{4}}$ [apply rotation about a point $b$ ] .....(i) $\frac{z_2 - z_1}{z_3 - z_1} = \sqrt{2} e^{-\frac{i\pi}{4}}$ [apply rotation about a point $a$ ].......(ii) $\rightarrow \left(\frac{z_1 - z_2}{z_3 - z_2}\right) \left(\frac{z_2 - z_1}{z_3 - z_1}\right) = 2$ $\rightarrow \frac{(z_1 - z_2)(z_1 - z_2)}{(z_3 - z_2)(z_1 - z_3)} = 2$ $\rightarrow (z_1 - z_2)^2 = 2 (z_1 - z_3)(z_3 - z_2)$ © examsnet.com

search_text: if $\alpha_{1}, \alpha_{2}, \dots, \alpha_{23}$ are the $23^{\;\text{rd}\;}$ roots of unity, then $\alpha_{1}^{47}+\alpha_{2}^{47}+\cdots+\alpha_{23}^{47}=$ {'a': '$23$', 'b': '$-1$', 'c': '$1$', 'd': '$0$'} 2022 2022-07-06 shift_2 mathematics   10 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: 👈: video solution $\because \alpha_1, \alpha_2, \alpha_3, \dots, \alpha_{23}$ are the 23 rd roots of unity. $\therefore \alpha^{23}-1=0 \rightarrow \alpha^{23}=1$ now, $\alpha_1^{47}+\alpha_2^{47^{\circ}}+\dots+\alpha_{23}^{47}$ $\;= \alpha_1 (\alpha_1^{23})^2 + \alpha_2 (\alpha_2^{23})^2 + \dots + \alpha_{23} (\alpha_{23}^{23})^2$ $\;= \alpha_1+\alpha_2+\dots+\alpha_{23}$ sum of roots $=0$ © examsnet.com

question: The sum of squares of roots of the equation $x^{\frac{2}{3}}+x^{\frac{1}{3}}-2=0$ is
search_text: the sum of squares of roots of the equation $x^{\frac{2}{3}}+x^{\frac{1}{3}}-2=0$ is {'a': '82', 'b': '65', 'c': '50', 'd': '37'} 2022 2022-07-06 shift_2 mathematics   11 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: 👈: video solution given, equation is $\;x^{\frac{2}{3}}+x^{\frac{1}{3}}-2\;=0$ $\rightarrow\;\; x^{\frac{2}{3}}+x^{\frac{1}{3}}\;=2$ $\rightarrow\;\; \left(x^{\frac{2}{3}}+x^{\frac{1}{3}}\right)^3\;=2^3$ $\rightarrow\;\; \left(x^2+x+3x\left(x^{\frac{2}{3}}+x^{\frac{1}{3}}\right)\right)\;=8$ $\left[ \therefore (a+b)^3. \right] \;= a^3+b^3+3ab(a+b)$ $\rightarrow\; x^2+x+3x \times 2=8 \rightarrow$ $\;x^2+7x-8=0$ $\rightarrow\; (x+8)(x-1)=0 \rightarrow x=1,-8$ sum of square roots $=(1)^2+(-8)^2$ $\;=1+64=65$ © examsnet.com

search_text: the two pairs of straight lines $12x^{2}+7xy-12y^{2}=0$ and $12x^{2}+7xy-12y^{2}-x+7y-1=0$ constitute a {'a': 'square of area $\\frac{1}{25}$ sq.units', 'b': 'square of area $\\frac{1}{5}$ sq.units', 'c': 'rectangle of area $\\frac{1}{10}$ sq.units', 'd': 'rectangle of area $\\frac{1}{15}$ sq.units'} 2022 2022-07-06 shift_2 mathematics   45 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: 👈: video solution $12x^2+7xy-12y^2=0$ $12x^2+16xy-9xy-12y^2=0$ $4x(3x+4y)-3y(3x+4y)=0$ $(4x-3y)(3x+4y)=0$ $4x-3y=0$ and $3x+4y=0$ slope of the two lines are $\frac{4}{3}$ and $\frac{-3}{4}$ , respectively. the two lines are perpendicular. $12x^2+7xy-12y^2-x+7y-1=0$ $12x^2+x(7y-1)-12y^2+7y-1=0$ $x=-\frac{b+\sqrt{b^2-4ac}}{2a}$ $x=-\frac{(7y-1) \pm \sqrt{(7y-1)^2-4\times 12(-12y^2+7y-1)}}{2\times 12}$ $x=\frac{1-7y \pm \sqrt{49y^2+1-14y-336y+48+576y^2}}{24}$ $\rightarrow 24x=1-7y \pm \sqrt{625y^2-350y+49}$ $\rightarrow 24x=1-7y \pm (25y-7)$ $\rightarrow 24x=1-7y+25y-7$ or $24x=1-7y-25y+7$ $\rightarrow 24x-18y+6=0$ or $24x+32y-8=0$ $m_3=\frac{24}{18}$ and $m_4=\frac{-24}{32}$ $\rightarrow m_3=\frac{4}{3}$ and $m_4=\frac{-3}{4}$ again, $m_3 \times m_4=-1$ , the two lines are perpendicular. the two lines $3x+4y=0$ and $4x-3y=0$ intersect at a point $(0,0)$ . $d_1$ , and $d_2$ are the distance of a point $(0,0)$ to the line $24x-18y+6=0$ and $24x+32y-8=0$ $d_1=\frac{6}{\sqrt{(24)^2+(18)^2}}, d_2=\frac{8}{\sqrt{(24)^2+(32)^2}}$ $d_1=\frac{6}{30}=\frac{1}{5}, d_2=\frac{8}{40}=\frac{1}{5}$ $\therefore$ the given figure is a square of side $\frac{1}{5}$ unit. area of square $=\frac{1}{25}$ sq. units © examsnet.com

search_text: $\lim\limits_{n\to\infty}\sum\limits_{r=1}^{n}\cot^{-1}\left(r^{2}+\frac{3}{4}\right)=$ {'a': '$\\cot^{-1}2$', 'b': '$\\cot^{-1}\\frac{1}{3}$', 'c': '$\\tan^{-1}2$', 'd': '$\\tan^{-1}\\frac{1}{3}$'} 2022 2022-07-06 shift_2 mathematics   59 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: 👈: video solution $\lim\limits_{n\to\infty}\sum\limits_{r=1}^{n}\cot^{-1}\left(r^{2}+\frac{3}{4}\right)$ $=\lim\limits_{n\to\infty}\sum\limits_{r=1}^{n}\tan^{-1}\left[\;\frac{1}{r^{2}+1-\frac{1}{4}}\right]$ $=\lim\limits_{n\to\infty}\sum\limits_{r=1}^{n}\tan^{-1}\left[\;\frac{\left(r+\frac{1}{2}\right)-\left(r-\frac{1}{2}\right)}{1+\left(r+\frac{1}{2}\right)\left(r-\frac{1}{2}\right)}\right]$ $=\lim\limits_{n\to\infty}\sum\limits_{r=1}^{n}\left[\tan^{-1}\left(r+\frac{1}{2}\right)-\tan^{-1}\left(r-\frac{1}{2}\right)\right]$ $\left[ \because \tan^{-1}(a-b)=\tan^{-1}\left[\frac{a-b}{1+a\cdot b}\right] \right]$ $=\lim\limits_{n\to\infty}\left[\left(\tan^{-1}\frac{3}{2}-\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)\right)\right]+\left[\tan^{-1}\frac{5}{2}-\tan^{-1}\frac{3}{2}\right]$ $+\left[\tan^{-1}\frac{7}{2}-\tan^{-1}\frac{5}{2}\right]\cdots$ $+\left[\tan^{-1}\left(n+\frac{1}{2}\right)-\tan^{-1}\left(n-\frac{1}{2}\right)\right]$ $\;=\lim\limits_{n\to\infty}\left[\tan^{-1}\left(n+\frac{1}{2}\right)-\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)\right]$ $\;=\lim\limits_{n\to\infty}\left[\tan^{-1}\left(n+\frac{1}{2}\right)-\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)\right]$ $\;=\tan^{-1}\infty-\tan^{-1}\frac{1}{2}=\frac{\pi}{2}-\tan^{-1}\frac{1}{2}$ $\;=\cot^{-1}\frac{1}{2}=\tan^{-1}2$ © examsnet.com

search_text: let $f(x) = \begin{cases} |x|, & -\infty < x < 2 \\ |2x-4|, & 2 \le x \le 20. \end{cases}$ $x = a$ is a point where $f(x)$ is continuous but not differentiable and $x = b$ is a point where $f(x)$ is not differentiable $(a \neq b)$ . then $a + b =$ {'a': '$1$', 'b': '$2$', 'c': '$-2$', 'd': '$0$'} 2022 2022-07-06 shift_2 mathematics   62 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: 👈: video solution $|x| = \begin{cases} -x, & \text{if } x < 0 \\ x, & \text{if } x \ge 0 \end{cases}$ and $|2x-4| = \begin{cases} 2x-4, & \text{if } x \ge 2 \\ -(2x-4), & \text{if } x < 2. \end{cases}$ $f(x) = \begin{cases} -x, & -\infty < x < 0 \\ x, & 0 \le x < 2 \\ 2x-4, & 2 \le x \le 20 \end{cases}.$ at $x = 0$ lhl $= \lim\limits_{\text{rhl}} f(x) = 0$ rhl = $\lim\limits_{x \to 0^{+}} f(x) = 0$ $f(0) = 0$ $f(x)$ is continuous at $x = 0$ at $x = 2$ lhl $= \lim\limits_{x \to 2^{-}} f(x) = 2$ $\text{rhl} = \lim\limits_{x \to 2^{+}} f(x) = 0$ $f(x)$ is not continuous at $x = 2$ $f'(x) = \begin{cases} -1, & -\infty < x < 0 \\ 1, & 0 \le x < 2 \\ 2, & 2 \le x \le 20 \end{cases}.$ the function is not differentiable at both the points $x = 0$ and $x = 2$ . here, $a = 0$ and $b = 2$ $a + b = 0 + 2$ $\therefore a + b = 2$ © examsnet.com

question: Four charges, each charge $q$ coloumb are placed at points $(-1,0,0),(1,0,0),(0,-1,0)$ and $(0,1,0)$ in the $x y$ - plane. The distances along the axes are measured in meters. The magnitude of the electric field at the point $z=1 m$ on the $z-$ axis is
search_text: four charges, each charge $q$ coloumb are placed at points $(-1,0,0),(1,0,0),(0,-1,0)$ and $(0,1,0)$ in the $x y$ - plane. the distances along the axes are measured in meters. the magnitude of the electric field at the point $z=1 m$ on the $z-$ axis is {'a': '$\\;\\frac{1}{2\\sqrt{2}} \\;\\frac{q}{\\pi\\varepsilon_0} \\mathrm{cm}^{-2}$', 'b': '$\\;\\frac{1}{4} \\;\\frac{q}{\\pi\\varepsilon_0} \\mathrm{cm}^{-2}$', 'c': '$\\;\\frac{q}{\\pi\\varepsilon_0} \\mathrm{cm}^{-2}$', 'd': '$\\;\\frac{q}{2\\pi\\varepsilon_0} \\mathrm{cm}^{-2}$'} 2022 2022-07-06 shift_2 physics   104 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: the given situation is shown below. according to given situation we have to find electric field at point $p(0,0,1)$ . distance of point $p$ from each charges is equal to $\sqrt{1^2+1^2}=\sqrt{2}$ $e_{a p}\;=e_{b p}=e_{c p}=e_{d p}=\;\frac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0} \cdot \;\frac{q}{(\sqrt{2})^2}$ $\;=\;\frac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0} \cdot \;\frac{q}{2}$ $e_{a p}$ and $e_{b p}$ are perpendicular to each other. let $e'$ be the resultant electric field of $e_{a p}$ and $e_{b p}$ , then $e'\;=\sqrt{e_{a p}^2+e_{b p}^2}=\sqrt{2 e_{a p}^2} . \; \; [\because e_{a p}=e_{b p}]$ $\;=e_{a p} \sqrt{2}$ $\;=\;\frac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0} \;\frac{q\sqrt{2}}{2}=\;\frac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0} \;\frac{q}{\sqrt{2}}$ $e'\;=\;\frac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0} \;\frac{q}{\sqrt{2}}$ in the similar way, net electric field due to $e_{c p}$ and $e_{p p}$ $e''=\;\frac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0} \cdot \;\frac{q}{\sqrt{2}}$ again $e'$ and $e''$ are directed in same direction i.e along $+z$ direction, hence net electric field, $e_{\;\text{net }\;}=e'+e''=2 e'$ $[\because e'=e'']$ $=2\;\frac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}\;\frac{q}{\sqrt{2}}=\;\frac{q}{2\sqrt{2} \pi \varepsilon_0} \mathrm{n} / \mathrm{c}$ © examsnet.com

question: A capacitor of capacitance $C_{1}=10\;\mu\text{F}$ to charged using $9\;\text{V}$ battery. It is then removed from the battery and connected to another capacitor $C_{2}=20\;\mu\text{F}$ as shown in the figure. The charge on $C_{2}$ after equilibrium has reached is
search_text: a capacitor of capacitance $c_{1}=10\;\mu\text{f}$ to charged using $9\;\text{v}$ battery. it is then removed from the battery and connected to another capacitor $c_{2}=20\;\mu\text{f}$ as shown in the figure. the charge on $c_{2}$ after equilibrium has reached is {'a': '$6.0\\times10^{-5}\\;\\text{c}$', 'b': '$6.0\\times10^{-6}\\;\\text{c}$', 'c': '$3.0\\times10^{-5}\\;\\text{c}$', 'd': '$3.0\\times10^{-6}\\;\\text{c}$'} 2022 2022-07-06 shift_2 physics   105 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: given, $c_{1}\;=10\;\mu\text{f}$ $\;=10^{-5}\;\text{f}$ $v_{1}\;=9\;\text{v}$ charge on capacitor $c_{1}$ , $q_{1}\;=c_{1}v_{1}$ $\;=9\times10^{-5}\;\text{c}$ $c_{2}\;=20\;\mu\text{f}=2\times10^{-5}\;\text{f}$ when uncharged capacitor $c_{2}$ is connected with charged capacitor $c_{1}$ , then charges will flow from capacitor $c_{1}$ to $c_{2}$ till both gain the same potential i.e common potential. common potential, $v=\frac{\;\text{ total charge }\;}{\;\text{ total capacitance }\;}$ $\;=\frac{q_{1}}{c_{1}+c_{2}}=\frac{9\times10^{-5}}{10^{-5}+2\times10^{-5}}$ $\;=\frac{9\times10^{-5}}{3\times10^{-5}}=3\;\text{v}$ charge on capacitor $c_{2},\;q_{2}=c_{2}v$ $=2\times10^{-5}\times3=6\times10^{-5}\;\text{c}$ © examsnet.com

question: Two parallel plate capacitors $8\,\mu\mathrm{F}$ each are connected in parallel to a $10\,\mathrm{V}$ battery. The plate separation in one of the capacitor is reduced to $40\%$ of its initial value. The increase in the total charge stored on the capacitors is
search_text: two parallel plate capacitors $8\,\mu\mathrm{f}$ each are connected in parallel to a $10\,\mathrm{v}$ battery. the plate separation in one of the capacitor is reduced to $40\%$ of its initial value. the increase in the total charge stored on the capacitors is {'a': '$80\\,\\mu\\mathrm{c}$', 'b': '$120\\,\\mu\\mathrm{c}$', 'c': '$100\\,\\mu\\mathrm{c}$', 'd': '$150\\,\\mu\\mathrm{c}$'} 2022 2022-07-06 shift_2 physics   106 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: given, $c_1\;=c_2=8\,\mu\mathrm{f}=8\times 10^{-6}\,\mathrm{f}$ $v\;=10\,\mathrm{v}$ since, $c_1$ and $c_2$ are connected in parallel. equivalent capacitance, $c_{ev}=c_1+c_2=8\times 10^{-6}+8\times 10^{-6}=1.6\times 10^{-5}\,\mathrm{f}$ total charge, $q_i=c_{eq}\cdot v$ $\;=1.6\times 10^{-5}\times 10$ $\;=1.6\times 10^{-4}\,\mathrm{c}$ we know that, capacitance $c=\;\frac{\varepsilon_0 a}{d}$ $\rightarrow c\propto\frac{1}{d}$ $\rightarrow\;\frac{c'}{c''}=\;\frac{d''}{d'}=\;\frac{d'-40\%\ \text{of}\ d}{d'}=\;\frac{\frac{3}{5}d'}{d'}$ $\rightarrow\;\frac{c^r}{c''}=\;\frac{3}{5}$ $\rightarrow c''=\;\frac{5}{3}c'$ $\;=\;\frac{5}{3}\times 8\times 10^{-6}=\;\frac{40}{3}\times 10^{-6}\,\mathrm{c}$ new capacitance, $c'''=c''+c_2$ $\;=\;\frac{40}{3}\times 10^{-6}+8\times 10^{-6}$ $\;=\;\frac{64}{3}\times 10^{-6}\,\mathrm{f}$ now value of total charge, $q_f=c'''\times v$ $\;=\;\frac{64}{3}\times 10^{-6}\times 10$ $\;=\;\frac{64}{3}\times 10^{-5}\,\mathrm{c}$ increased value of charge, $\delta q\;=q_f-q_1$ $\;=\;\frac{64}{3}\times 10^{-5}-1.6\times 10^{-4}$ $\;=\;\frac{160}{3}\,\mu\mathrm{c}$ © examsnet.com

search_text: a metal wire of $1\ \mathrm{cm}$ length and $1\ \mathrm{mm}$ radius has a resistance of $3 \times 10^{-3}\ \omega$ . if a wire of the same metal of length $3\ \mathrm{cm}$ and radius $0.5\ \mathrm{mm}$ is drawn, the resistance of the wire {'a': '$0.036\\ \\omega$', 'b': '$0.09\\ \\omega$', 'c': '$1.2\\ \\omega$', 'd': '$3.1\\ \\omega$'} 2022 2022-07-06 shift_2 physics   107 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: length of metal wire, $l_1=1\ \mathrm{cm}=10^{-2}\ \mathrm{m}$ $r_1\;=1\ \mathrm{mm}=10^{-3}\ \mathrm{m}$ $r_1\;=3 \times 10^{-3}\ \omega$ resistivity of wire is given as $\rho=r\;\frac{a}{l}$ $\;=3 \times 10^{-3} \times \frac{\pi r_1^2}{l_1}=3 \times 10^{-3} \times \frac{314 \times (10^{-3})^2}{10^{-2}}$ $\;=9.42 \times 10^{-7}\ \omega-\mathrm{m}$ again for second case, $l_2\;=3\ \mathrm{cm}=3 \times 10^{-2}\ \mathrm{m},\ r_2=0.5\ \mathrm{mm}=5 \times 10^{-4}\ \mathrm{m}$ $\therefore r_2\;=\rho\;\frac{l_2}{a_2}=\rho\;\frac{l_2}{\pi r_2^2}$ $\;=9.42 \times 10^{-7} \times \frac{3 \times 10^{-2}}{314 \times (5 \times 10^{-4})^2}$ $\;=0.36 \times 10^{-1}\ \omega$ $\;=0.036\ \omega$ © examsnet.com

search_text: let $a=\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 \\ -2 & 1 \end{bmatrix}$ and $b^{-1}=\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 2 \end{bmatrix}$ . if $(a b^{-1})^{-1}=\begin{bmatrix} a & b \\ c & d \end{bmatrix}$ , then $2b+5c+10d=$ {'a': '$0$', 'b': '$1$', 'c': '$-1$', 'd': '$2$'} 2022 2022-07-07 shift_1 mathematics   5 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: 👈: video solution $ab^{-1}=\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 \\ -2 & 1 \end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 2 \end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 5 \\ -2 & 0 \end{bmatrix}$ now, $|ab^{-1}|=0-(-10)=10$ and $\operatorname{adj}(ab^{-1})=\begin{bmatrix} 0 & -5 \\ 2 & 1 \end{bmatrix}$ $\because (ab^{-1})^{-1}=\frac{1}{|ab^{-1}|}\operatorname{adj}(ab^{-1})$ $\therefore \begin{bmatrix} a & b \\ c & d \end{bmatrix}=\frac{1}{10}\begin{bmatrix} 0 & -5 \\ 2 & 1 \end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix} 0 & -\frac{1}{2} \\ \frac{1}{5} & \frac{1}{10} \end{bmatrix}$ $\rightarrow a=0, b=-\frac{1}{2}, c=\frac{1}{5}, d=\frac{1}{10}$ $\therefore 2b+5c+10d=-1+1+1=1$ © examsnet.com

search_text: let $a = \begin{bmatrix} n & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & n & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & n \end{bmatrix}$ and $b = \begin{bmatrix} 0 & 0 & n \\ 0 & n & 0 \\ n & 0 & 0 \end{bmatrix}$ . then $a^2 + b^2 + ab =$ {'a': '$n ( ni + nb + b )$', 'b': '$n ( 2ni + b )$', 'c': '$n^{2}(2 i + b)$', 'd': '$n ( ni + n a + b )$'} 2022 2022-07-07 shift_1 mathematics   6 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: 👈: video solution $a^2 = \begin{bmatrix} n^2 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & n^2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & n^2 \end{bmatrix}, b^2 = \begin{bmatrix} n^2 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & n^2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & n^2 \end{bmatrix}$ $b = \begin{bmatrix} 0 & 0 & n^2 \\ 0 & n^2 & 0 \\ n^2 & 0 & 0 \end{bmatrix}.$ now, $a^2 + b^2 + ab$ $= 2\begin{bmatrix} n^2 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & n^2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & n^2 \end{bmatrix} + \begin{bmatrix} 0 & 0 & n^2 \\ 0 & n^2 & 0 \\ n^2 & 0 & 0 \end{bmatrix}.$ $= 2n^2\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix} + n\begin{bmatrix} 0 & 0 & n \\ 0 & n & 0 \\ n & 0 & 0 \end{bmatrix}$ $= 2n^2 i + n b = n(2n i + b)$ © examsnet.com

search_text: let $z$ and $w$ be two complex numbers such that $\overline{z}+i\overline{w}=0$ and $\operatorname{arg}(zw)=\pi$ . then $\operatorname{arg}z=$ {'a': '$\\frac{3\\pi}{4}$', 'b': '$\\frac{\\pi}{2}$', 'c': '$\\frac{5\\pi}{4}$', 'd': '$\\frac{\\pi}{4}$'} 2022 2022-07-07 shift_1 mathematics   7 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: 👈: video solution given, $\overline{z}+i\overline{w}=0$ $\rightarrow \overline{z}-i\overline{w}=0$ $\dots[\because \overset{-}{i} = -i]$ $\rightarrow \overline{z}-\overline{i w}=0$ $\dots[\because \overline{z_1 \cdot z_2} = \overset{-}{z_1} \cdot \overset{-}{z_2}]$ $\rightarrow \overline{z-i w}=0 \left[\because \overset{-}{z_1} - \overset{-}{z_2} = \overline{z_1 - z_2}\right]$ $\rightarrow z-i w=0$ $z=i w$ according to question, $\arg(z w)=\pi$ $\rightarrow \arg z + \arg w = \pi$ $\rightarrow \arg z + \arg\left(\frac{z}{i}\right) = \pi$ $\dots[\because z = i w]$ $\rightarrow\; \arg z + \arg z - \arg(i) \; = \pi$ $2\arg(z) - \frac{\pi}{2} = \pi$ $\rightarrow \arg(z) = \frac{3\pi}{4}$ © examsnet.com

search_text: let $z=x+$ iy be a complex number with $x, y \in \mathbb{z}$ . then the area (in square units) of the rectangle whose vertices are the roots of the equation $\overline{z} \cdot z^{3}+z \cdot \overline{z}^{3}=350$ is {'a': '$48$', 'b': '$32$', 'c': '$40$', 'd': '$44$'} 2022 2022-07-07 shift_1 mathematics   9 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: 👈: video solution $\overline{z} z^{3}+z \overline{z}^{3}=350$ $\rightarrow z \overline{z} (z^{2}+\overline{z}^{2}) =350$ let $z=x+i y$ $\rightarrow \overline{z}=x-i y$ $\therefore (x+i y)(x-i y) [(x+i y)^{2}+(x-i y)^{2}] =350$ $\rightarrow (x^{2}+y^{2}) \cdot 2 (x^{2}-y^{2}) =350$ $\rightarrow (x^{2}+y^{2}) (x^{2}-y^{2}) =175=25 \times 7$ $\rightarrow x^{2}+y^{2}=25$ and $x^{2}-y^{2}=7$ on adding eqs. (i) and (ii), $2 x^{2}=32$ $\rightarrow x^{2}=16 \rightarrow x=\pm 4$ and $y^{2}=9 \rightarrow y=\pm 3$ $\therefore$ vertices of the rectangle are $(4,3),(4,-3),(-4,-3)$ and $(-4,3)$ $ab = 6$ and $ad = 8$ required area $=6 \times 8$ $=48\text{sq. units}$ © examsnet.com

search_text: if $1, \omega, \omega^{2}$ are the cube roots of unity, then $(2-\omega)^{2}(2-\omega^{2})^{2}(2-\omega^{10})^{2}(2-\omega^{11})^{2} =$ {'a': '$-7^{-4}$', 'b': '$7^{4}$', 'c': '$7^{8}$', 'd': '$-7^{8}$'} 2022 2022-07-07 shift_1 mathematics   10 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: 👈: video solution $1, \omega, \omega^2$ are the cube roots of units. $\rightarrow 1+\omega+\omega^2=0$ given, $(2-\omega)^2 (2-\omega^2)^2 (2-\omega^{10})^2 (2-\omega^{11})^2$ $= \{(2-\omega)(2-\omega^2)\}^2 \{(2-\omega)(2-\omega^2)\}^2$ $= \{(2-\omega)(2-\omega^2)\}^4$ $= \{4-2(\omega+\omega^2)+\omega^3\}^4$ $\; = (4-2(-1)+1)^4 = 7^4$ © examsnet.com
