question: Let $f(x)=x^{2}+\frac{1}{x^{2}}$ and $g(x)=x-\frac{1}{x}$ for $x \in \mathbb{R}\setminus\{-1,0,+1\}$ then, the local minimum of $\;\frac{f(x)}{g(x)}$ is
search_text: let $f(x)=x^{2}+\frac{1}{x^{2}}$ and $g(x)=x-\frac{1}{x}$ for $x \in \mathbb{r}\setminus\{-1,0,+1\}$ then, the local minimum of $\;\frac{f(x)}{g(x)}$ is {'a': '$-3$', 'b': '$2\\sqrt{2}$', 'c': '$2-2\\sqrt{2}$', 'd': '$3$'} 2022 2022-07-07 shift_1 mathematics   11 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: 👈: video solution $f(x)=x^2+\;\frac{1}{x^2}= \left(x-\;\frac{1}{x}\right) +2, g(x)=x-\;\frac{1}{x}$ let $x-\;\frac{1}{x}=t$ $f(x)=t^2+2, g(x)=t$ $\frac{f(x)}{g(x)}=t+\frac{2}{t}=h(t)$ $h'(t)=1-\frac{2}{t^2}$ on putting $h'(t)=0$ $\rightarrow 1-\frac{2}{t^2}=0$ $\rightarrow t=\pm \sqrt{2}.$ $\rightarrow h'(t)=\frac{4}{t^3}$ $h''(-\sqrt{2})<0$ and $h''(\sqrt{2})>0.$ $\therefore t=\sqrt{2}$ is a point of minima. local minimum value of $h(t)=\sqrt{2}+\frac{2}{\sqrt{2}}=2\sqrt{2}$ $\therefore$ required local minimum value $=2\sqrt{2}$ © examsnet.com

search_text: which of the following quadratic equations whose real roots $x_{1}, x_{2}$ satisfy the conditions $x_{1}^{2}+x_{2}^{2}=5,3(x_{1}^{5}+x_{2}^{5})=11(x_{1}^{3}+x_{2}^{3})$ ? {'a': '$x^{2}+3x+2=0$', 'b': '$x^{2} \\pm 3x + 11 = 0$', 'c': '$x^{2} \\pm 5x + 2 = 0$', 'd': '$x^{2} \\pm 5x + 11 = 0$'} 2022 2022-07-07 shift_1 mathematics   13 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: 👈: video solution $\frac{x_1^5+x_2^5}{x_1^3+x_2^3}=\;\frac{11}{3}$ $\rightarrow \frac{ (x_1^2+x_2^2)(x_1^3+x_2^3) - x_1^2 x_2^2 (x_1+x_2) }{x_1^3+x_2^3}= \frac{11}{3}$ $\ldots \left[ \because a^5+b^5= (a^2+b^2)(a^3+b^3) - a^2 b^2 (a+b) \right]$ $\rightarrow (x_1^2+x_2^2) -\; \frac{x_1^2 x_2^2 (x_1+x_2)}{(x_1+x_2)(x_1^2 - x_1 x_2 + x_2^2)} =\; \frac{11}{3}$ $\rightarrow 5 -\; \frac{x_1^2 x_2^2}{5 - x_1 x_2} =\; \frac{11}{3}$ $\rightarrow$ let $x_1 x_2 = t$ $\rightarrow 5 - \frac{t^2}{5-t} = \frac{11}{3}$ $\rightarrow 3 (25-5t-t^2) = 55-11t$ $\rightarrow 3 t^2 + 4t -20 \; =0$ $\rightarrow t = 2, -\frac{10}{3}$ $\rightarrow x_1 x_2 = 2, -\frac{10}{3}$ when $x_1 x_2 = 2$ $(x_1+x_2)^2 = x_1^2 + 2 x_1 x_2 + x_2^2$ $= 5 + 2 \times 2 = 9$ $\rightarrow x_1+x_2 = \pm 3$ when $x_1 x_2 = -\frac{10}{3}$ $(x_1+x_2)^2 = 5 - \frac{-20}{3} = -\frac{5}{3} < 0$ which is not possible. $\therefore x_1+x_2 = \pm 3$ required quadratic equation $x^2 \pm 3x + 2 = 0$ . © examsnet.com

search_text: in a toy factory, the machines $a, b$ and $c$ are used to manufacture $30\%, 40\%$ and $30\%$ of the output, respectively. the probabilities of toys made by machines $a, b$ , and $c$ to be defective are respectively $2\%, 3\%$ and $1\%$ . a toy is taken from the factory and is found to be defective. the probability that it was manufactured by the machine $b$ is {'a': '$\\frac{4}{5}$', 'b': '$\\frac{2}{9}$', 'c': '$\\frac{3}{4}$', 'd': '$\\frac{4}{7}$'} 2022 2022-07-07 shift_1 mathematics   37 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: 👈: video solution $p(a)=\frac{30}{100}, p(b)=\frac{40}{100}, p(c)=\frac{30}{100}$ $p\left(\frac{e}{a}\right)=\frac{2}{100}, p\left(\frac{e}{b}\right)=\frac{3}{100}, p\left(\frac{e}{c}\right)=\frac{1}{100}$ where $e$ denotes defective toys. ∴ required probability $= p\left(\frac{b}{e}\right)$ $= \frac{ p(b) \cdot p\left(\frac{e}{b}\right) }{ p(a) \cdot p\left(\frac{e}{a}\right) + p(b) \cdot p\left(\frac{e}{b}\right) + p(c) \cdot p\left(\frac{e}{c}\right) }$ $\ldots\text{[by baye's theorem]}$ $= \frac{ \frac{40}{100} \times \frac{3}{100} }{ \frac{30}{100} \times \frac{2}{100} + \frac{40}{100} \times \frac{3}{100} + \frac{30}{100} \times \frac{1}{100} }$ $= \frac{120}{60+120+30} = \frac{120}{210} = \frac{4}{7}$ © examsnet.com

search_text: on the locus of the point $p(x, y)$ equidistant from $(3,0)$ and $(0,4)$ , if $a$ and $b$ are two points that satisfy $4 x = 3 y$ and $x = y$ respectively, then the distance between $a$ and $b$ is {'a': '$\\; \\frac{5}{2}$', 'b': '$5$', 'c': '$\\; \\frac{25}{4}$', 'd': '$25$'} 2022 2022-07-07 shift_1 mathematics   41 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: 👈: video solution $pq = pr$ $\rightarrow \sqrt{(x-3)^2+(y-0)^2} = \sqrt{(x-0)^2+(y-4)^2}$ $\rightarrow x^2 - 6x + 9 + y^2 = x^2 + y^2 - 8y + 16$ $\rightarrow 6x - 8y + 7 = 0$ $\rightarrow y = \frac{6x+7}{8}$ $\text{let } a = \left(\alpha, \frac{6\alpha + 7}{8}\right)$ and $b = \left(\beta, \frac{6\beta + 7}{8}\right)$ according to question, $4\alpha = 3\left(\frac{6\alpha + 7}{8}\right)$ and $\beta = \frac{6\beta + 7}{8}$ $\rightarrow \alpha = \frac{3}{2}$ and $\beta = \frac{7}{2}$ $\therefore a = \left(\frac{3}{2}, 2\right)$ and $b = \left(\frac{7}{2}, \;\frac{7}{2}\right)$ $\therefore ab = \sqrt{ \left(\frac{3}{2} - \frac{7}{2}\right)^2 + \left(2 - \frac{7}{2}\right)^2 } = \frac{5}{2}$ © examsnet.com

search_text: a particle is moving along $x$ -axis with velocity $v = e^{-\beta x}$ . at time $t = 0$ , the particle is {'a': '$e^{-\\beta t}$', 'b': '$\\;\\frac{1}{\\beta} e^{(1 - \\beta t)}$', 'c': '$\\;\\frac{1}{\\beta} \\log [1 - \\beta t]$', 'd': '$\\;\\frac{1}{\\beta} \\log [1 + \\beta t]$'} 2022 2022-07-07 shift_1 physics   84 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: velocity of particle, $v = e^{-\beta x}$ $\rightarrow \frac{dx}{dt} = e^{-\beta x}$ or $\frac{dx}{e^{-\beta x}} = dt$ or $e^{\beta x} dx = dt$ $\rightarrow$ integrating, we get $\int\limits_{0^x e}^{\beta x} dx = \int\limits_{0}^{t} dt$ $\rightarrow \frac{1}{\beta} \left[ e^{\beta x} \right]_{0}^{x} = \left[ t \right]_{0}^{t}$ $\rightarrow \frac{1}{\beta} (e^{\beta x} - e^{0}) = t - 0 \rightarrow \frac{1}{\beta} (e^{\beta x} - 1) = t$ $e^{\beta x} = \beta t + 1$ taking log, we get $\log (e^{\beta x}) = \log (\beta t + 1)$ $\rightarrow \beta x = \log (\beta t + 1)$ $\rightarrow x = \frac{1}{\beta} \cdot \log (\beta t + 1)$ so, displacement function for the particle is $x = \frac{1}{\beta} \cdot \log (\beta t + 1)$ © examsnet.com

(assume the co-efficient of static friction between the masses and the surface is constant). then the correct statement of the following is {'a': '$m_{3}$ begins to slide at a higher inclination angle than $m_{1} \\& m_{2}$', 'b': '$m_{3}$ begins to slide at a lower inclination angle than $m_{1} \\& m_{2}$', 'c': '$m_{1}, m_{2} \\& m_{3}$ begins to slide at the same inclination angle', 'd': '$m_{2}$ begins to slide at a higher inclination angle than $m_{1} \\& m_{3}$'} 2022 2022-07-07 shift_1 physics   85 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: an object started to slide down an inclined plane when angle of incline (also called angle of repose) is just equals to angle of friction. let $\theta=$ angle at which a mass started to slide down an incline. then, force of friction $=$ downward force. $\rightarrow \mu n = m g \sin \theta$ $\rightarrow \mu m g \cos \theta = m g \sin \theta$ $\rightarrow \tan \theta = \mu$ $\rightarrow \theta = \tan^{-1} \mu$ hence, angle does not depend on mass of body. so all three masses slides down at same instant at same inclination angle $(\theta)$ . © examsnet.com

search_text: a bar of mass $m$ resting on a smooth horizontal plane starts moving due to a constant force $f$ . in the process of its rectilinear motion the angle $\theta$ between the direction of this force and the horizontal varies as $\theta = kx$ , where $k$ is a constant and $x$ is the distance traversed by the bar from its initial position. the velocity (v) of the bar as a function of the angle $\theta$ is {'a': '$v = \\sqrt{\\frac{2f \\sin \\theta}{mk}}$', 'b': '$v = \\sqrt{\\frac{2f}{mk \\sin \\theta}}$', 'c': '$v = \\frac{2f \\sin \\theta}{mk}$', 'd': '$v = \\frac{2f}{mk \\sin \\theta}$'} 2022 2022-07-07 shift_1 physics   86 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: componentof force response for horizontal motion is $f \cos \theta$ so, acceleration of bar, $a = \frac{f \cos \theta}{m}$ as acceleration, $a = \frac{dv}{dt}$ , we have $\rightarrow \frac{dv}{dt} = \frac{f \cos \theta}{m}$ we can also express this as, $\rightarrow \frac{dv}{dx} \cdot \frac{dx}{dt} = \frac{f \cos \theta}{m}$ $\rightarrow v dv = \frac{f \cos \theta}{m} dx$ integrating both sides and putting $\theta = kx$ , we get $\int v dv = \int \frac{f \cos kx}{m} dx$ $\rightarrow \frac{v^2}{2} = \frac{f}{m} \int \cos kx \cdot dx$ $\rightarrow \frac{v^2}{2} = \frac{f}{m} \cdot \left(\frac{\sin kx}{k}\right)$ $\rightarrow v^2 = \frac{2f \sin kx}{m k}$ $\rightarrow v = \sqrt{\frac{2f \sin \theta}{m k}}$ © examsnet.com

question: A block of mass $5\text{ kg}$ starts up a $45^{\circ}$ incline plane with initial kinetic energy of $100\text{ J}$ . search_text: a block of mass $5\text{ kg}$ starts up a $45^{\circ}$ incline plane with initial kinetic energy of $100\text{ j}$ . if the coefficient of friction between block and plane is $0.5$ then the distance covered by the block before it stops is (acceleration due to gravity $=10\text{ m s}^{-2}$ ) {'a': '$\\; \\frac{4\\sqrt{2}}{3}\\text{ m}$', 'b': '$\\; \\frac{3}{\\sqrt{2}}\\text{ m}$', 'c': '$2\\sqrt{2}\\text{ m}$', 'd': '$\\; \\frac{6}{5}\\sqrt{2}\\text{ m}$'} 2022 2022-07-07 shift_1 physics   87 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: block stops on incline plane when its initial k.e is used in doing work against friction and partly it is converted into potential energy. as angle of incline is given $45^{\circ}$ so, distance covered on incline $(s)$ is related to height of block (h) as, $\rightarrow \sin 45^{\circ}=\frac{h}{s}$ or $s=\sqrt{2} h$ let block covers a distance $s$ over block and reaches up-to height $h$ . then, $\text{initial k.e of block} = \text{work done against friction} + \text{potential energy gained by block}$ $\rightarrow \frac{1}{2} m u^2 = \mu m g \cos \theta \cdot s + m g h$ $\rightarrow \frac{1}{2} m u^2 = \mu m g \cos \theta \cdot \sqrt{2} \cdot h + m g h$ $\rightarrow h = \frac{\; \frac{1}{2} m u^2}{\sqrt{2} \mu m g \cos \theta + m g}$ here, initial $\text{k.e} = \frac{1}{2} m u^2 = 100\text{ j}$ $m=5\text{ kg},\ \theta=45^{\circ},\ g=10\text{ m/s}^2$ so, $h = \frac{100}{\sqrt{2} \times 0.5 \times 5 \times 10 \times \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} + 5 \times 10}$ $= \frac{100}{50 \times 1.5} = \frac{4}{3}$ hence, distance covered over block, $s=\sqrt{2} h$ $\rightarrow s = \frac{\sqrt{2} \times 4}{3}\text{ m} = \frac{4\sqrt{2}}{3}\text{ m}$ © examsnet.com

search_text: if the earth suddenly shrinks to $\; \frac{1}{64}$ of its original volume, while keeping the same mass, then the duration of the day will be [assume earth is a perfect sphere] {'a': '$24$ hours', 'b': '$1.5$ hours', 'c': '$16$ hours', 'd': '$48$ hours'} 2022 2022-07-07 shift_1 physics   89 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: if earth shrinks to $\frac{1}{64}$ of its original volume; $\frac{4}{3} \pi r^3 = \frac{1}{64} \left( \frac{4}{3} \pi r^3 \right)$ here, $r=$ new radius and $r=$ original radius $\rightarrow r^3 = \frac{r^3}{64}$ or $r = \frac{r}{4}$ as there is no external torque, angular momentum of earth remains constant i.e., $i_1 \omega_1 = i_2 \omega_2$ $\ldots \left[ \because i_{\text{sphere}} = \frac{2}{5} m r^2 \right]$ $\rightarrow \frac{2}{5} m r^2 \cdot \frac{2 \pi}{t_1} = \frac{2}{5} m r^2 \frac{2 \pi}{t_2}$ $\ldots \left[ \therefore \omega = \frac{2 \pi}{t}, t = \text{time of revolution about axis} \right]$ $\rightarrow t_2 = \frac{r^2 t_1}{r^2}$ $\rightarrow t_2 = \frac{ \frac{r^2}{16} \times t_1 }{r^2}$ $\ldots \left[ \therefore r = \frac{r}{4} \right]$ $\rightarrow t_2 = \frac{t_1}{16} = \frac{24}{16} \text{h}$ or $t_2 = 1.5 \text{h}$ © examsnet.com

question: A wheel is rotating freely at some angular speed. A second wheel initially at rest and with thrice the rotational inertia of the first, is suddenly coupled to the first wheel. The fraction of the original rotational kinetic energy lost is
search_text: a wheel is rotating freely at some angular speed. a second wheel initially at rest and with thrice the rotational inertia of the first, is suddenly coupled to the first wheel. the fraction of the original rotational kinetic energy lost is {'a': '$0.50$', 'b': '$0.25$', 'c': '$0.66$', 'd': '$0.75$'} 2022 2022-07-07 shift_1 physics   90 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: let, $i_1=$ inertia of first (rotating)  wheel $\omega_1=$ angular speed of first wheel $i_2=3 i_1=$ inertia of second wheel $\omega_2=0=$ angular speed of second wheel let $\omega=$ angular speed of coupled wheels. according to conservation of angular momentum, total initial angular momentum $=$ total final angular momentum $\rightarrow i_1 \omega_1 + i_2 \times 0 = (i_1+i_2) \omega$ $\rightarrow \omega = \frac{i_1 \omega_1}{i_1+i_2} = \frac{i_1 \omega_1}{i_1+3 i_1} \rightarrow \omega = \frac{\omega_1}{4}$ now, initial rotational energy of system is $k_1 = \frac{1}{2} i_1 \omega_1^2 + \frac{1}{2} i_2 (0)^2$ $\rightarrow k_1 = \frac{1}{2} i_1 \omega_1^2$ final rotational kinetic energy of system is $k_2 = \frac{1}{2} (i_1+i_2) \omega^2$ $= \frac{1}{2} (i_1+3 i_1) \cdot \frac{\omega_1^2}{16}$ or $k_2 = \frac{1}{4} k_1$ $= \frac{1}{2} \times 4 i_1 \times \frac{\omega_1^2}{16}$ $= \frac{1}{4} \left( \frac{1}{2} i_1 \omega_1^2 \right)$ hence, fraction of lost energy $= \frac{\delta k}{k_1} = \frac{k_1 - k_2}{k_1} = \frac{\frac{3}{4} k_1}{k_1}$ $= \frac{3}{4} = 0.75$ © examsnet.com

question: There is a planet which is 8 times massive and 27 times denser than the earth. If $g'$ and $g$ are the accelerations due to gravity on the surfaces of the planet and the earth respectively then

(i)}$ we gẹt, $\rightarrow g=\frac{gm}{r^2}=\frac{gm}{\left(\frac{3}{4\pi}\cdot\frac{m}{d}\right)^{\frac{2}{3}}}$ $\rightarrow g \propto m^{\frac{1}{3}} d^{\frac{2}{3}}$ hence, ratio of acceleration due to gravity on surface of planet and that on surface of earth will be $\frac{g'}{g}=\frac{m^{\frac{1}{3}}}{m^{\frac{1}{3}}}\frac{d^{\frac{2}{3}}}{d^{\frac{2}{3}}}=\left(\frac{m'}{m}\right)^{\frac{1}{3}}\cdot\left(\frac{d'}{d}\right)^{\frac{2}{3}}$ given, $\frac{m'}{m}=8$ and $\frac{d'}{d}=27$ so $\frac{g'}{g}=8^{\frac{1}{3}}\cdot27^{\frac{2}{3}}=2\times9$ or $g'=18 g$ © examsnet.com

search_text: the coefficient of volume expansion of a material is $5 \times 10^{-4} {}^{\circ}\mathrm{c}^{-1}$ . the fractional change in its density for a $40^{\circ} \mathrm{c}$ rise in temperature is nearly {'a': '$0.01$', 'b': '$0.02$', 'c': '$0.03$', 'd': '$0.04$'} 2022 2022-07-07 shift_1 physics   97 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: as density, $\rho \propto \frac{1}{v}$ where, $v=$ volume we have, $\frac{\rho_2}{\rho_1} = \frac{v_1}{v_2} = \frac{v_1}{v_1(1 + r \delta \theta)}$ $r=$ coefficient of cubical expansion $\delta \theta =$ rise of temperature since, $\rho_2 = \rho_1 (1 - r \delta \theta)$ here, $r = 5 \times 10^{-4} {}^{\circ}\mathrm{c}^{-1}$ $\delta \theta = 40^{\circ} \mathrm{c}$ so, in given case $\frac{\rho_2}{\rho_1} = 1 - 5 \times 10^{-4} \times 40$ $= 1 - 2 \times 10^{-2} = 0.08$ hence, fractional change in density $= \frac{\delta \rho}{\rho_1}$ $\rightarrow \frac{\delta \rho}{\rho_1} = \frac{\rho_2 - \rho_1}{\rho_1} = \frac{\rho_2}{\rho_1} - 1$ $\rightarrow$ fractional change is $\frac{\delta \rho}{\rho_1} = 0.08 - 1 = -0.02$ hence, negative sign shows decrease in density. © examsnet.com

search_text: a beam of light is incident from air on the surface of a liquid. the angle of incidence is $\theta$ and the angle of refraction is $\alpha$ . if the critical angle for liquid when surrounded by air is $\theta_{c}$ then $\sin \theta_{c}$ is {'a': '$\\; \\frac{\\sin (\\alpha)}{\\sin (\\theta)}$', 'b': '$\\sin (\\alpha) \\times \\sin (\\theta)$', 'c': '$\\; \\frac{\\sin (\\theta)}{\\sin (\\alpha)}$', 'd': '$\\; \\frac{\\sin (\\alpha)}{\\cos (\\theta)}$'} 2022 2022-07-07 shift_1 physics   102 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: refractive index of liquid with respect to air, $n_{la} = \frac{\sin i}{\sin r}$ here, $i = \theta$ and $r = a$ so, refractive index of liquid with respect to air, $n_{la} = \frac{\sin \theta}{\sin a}$ now, if $\theta =$ angle of critical incidence for liquid then, refractive index of air with respect to liquid is $n_{al} = \frac{1}{n_{la}} = \frac{\sin \theta}{\sin 90^{\circ}}$ © examsnet.com

search_text: in young's double slit experiment. light of wavelength $480\text{ nm}$ is incident on two slits separated by a distance of $4 \times 10^{-4}\text{ m}$ . if a thin plate of thickness $1.4 \times 10^{-6}\text{ m}$ and refractive index $\frac{13}{7}$ is placed between one of the slits and screen. the phase difference introduced at the position of central maxima is {'a': '$5\\pi$', 'b': '$\\frac{7}{3}\\pi$', 'c': '$\\frac{7}{4}\\pi$', 'd': '$4\\pi$'} 2022 2022-07-07 shift_1 physics   103 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: the $\text{ydse}$ setup is shown below additional path difference introduced by medium plate, $\delta l = (\mu - 1) t$ as, a path difference of one wavelength is equals to a phase difference $\delta \phi = \frac{\delta l \times 2\pi}{\lambda}$ so, $\delta\phi = \frac{(\mu-1) t \times 2\pi}{\lambda}$ here, $\mu = \frac{13}{7},\ t = 1.4 \times 10^{-6},\ \lambda = 480 \times 10^{-9}\ \text{m}$ $\therefore \delta\phi = \frac{ \left(\frac{13}{7} - 1\right) \times 1.4 \times 10^{-6} \times 2\pi }{480 \times 10^{-9}}$ $\therefore = \frac{6 \times 1.4 \times 2\pi \times 10^{-6}}{7 \times 480 \times 10^{-9}} = 5\pi \text{ rad}$ © examsnet.com

search_text: two wires $a$ and $b$ of same material having length $l_{a}, l_{b}$ and radii $r_{a}, r_{b}$ and drift velocity $v_{a}, v_{b}$ respectively carries same current. if $l_{a}=l_{b}$ and $r_{a}=2 r_{b}$ then the value of $\left(\;\frac{v_{a}}{v_{b}}\right)$ is is {'a': '$0.25$', 'b': '$0.5$', 'c': '$2.0$', 'd': '$1.0$'} 2022 2022-07-07 shift_1 physics   108 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: current through a wire is given by $i=n e v_d a=n e v_d \pi r^{2}$ here, $n=$ number density of free charge carriers $v_d=$ drift speed of electrons $r=$ radius of wire $e=$ charge on an electron here, for two wires $a$ and $b$ $i_a=i_b$ (given) $n_a=n_b$ (wires have same material) $r_a=2 r_b$ (given) so we have, $i_a=i_b$ $\rightarrow n e v_a \pi r_a^{2}=n e v_b \pi r_b^{2}$ $\rightarrow \frac{v_a}{v_b}= \left(\frac{r_b}{r_a}\right)^2= \left(\frac{r_b}{2 r_b}\right)^2$ $\rightarrow \frac{v_a}{v_b}= \frac{1}{4}=0.25$ © examsnet.com

question: A long solenoid having 100 turns per $\mathrm{cm}$ carries a current of $\; \frac{4}{\pi} \mathrm{A}$ . At the centre of it is placed a coil of 200 turns of cross sectional area $25 \mathrm{cm}^{2}$ having its axis parallel to the field produced by the solenoid. When the direction of the current in the solenoid is reversed with in $0.04 \mathrm{s}$ , the induced emf in the coil is
search_text: a long solenoid having 100 turns per $\mathrm{cm}$ carries a current of $\; \frac{4}{\pi} \mathrm{a}$ . at the centre of it is placed a coil of 200 turns of cross sectional area $25 \mathrm{cm}^{2}$ having its axis parallel to the field produced by the solenoid. when the direction of the current in the solenoid is reversed with in $0.04 \mathrm{s}$ , the induced emf in the coil is {'a': '$0.2 \\mathrm{v}$', 'b': '$0.4 \\mathrm{v}$', 'c': '$0.002 \\mathrm{v}$', 'd': '$0.016 \\mathrm{v}$'} 2022 2022-07-07 shift_1 physics   109 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: due to solenoid a magnetic filled exists around coil placed at centre magnetic field intensity produced by solenoid, $b = \mu_0 n i$ flux linked with coil is $\phi_b = n \cdot b \cdot a,$ where, $n =$ number of turns in coil $a = \text{area of coil}$ as current in solenoid is reversed, change in flux is $\delta \phi_b = 2 n \cdot b \cdot a$ this change in flux produces an emf in coil given by induced emf $e =$ rate of change of flux $\rightarrow e = \frac{2 n b a}{\delta t} = \frac{2 n (\mu_0 n i) a}{\delta t}$ here $n = 200, a = 25 \mathrm{cm}^{2} = 25 \times 10^{-4} \mathrm{m}^{2}$ $i = \frac{4}{\pi} \mathrm{a}, n = 100 \text{ tuns/cm} = 100 \times 100 \text{ turns/m}$ $\mu_0 = 4 \pi \times 10^{-7} \mathrm{t} \cdot \mathrm{ma}^{-1}$ and $\delta t = 0.04 \mathrm{s}$ so induced $\text{emf}$ : $e = \frac{2 \times 200 \times 4 \pi \times 10^{-7} \times 10^{4} \times \frac{4}{\pi} \times 25 \times 10^{-4}}{0.04} = 0.4 \mathrm{v}$ induced $\text{emf}$ in coil is $0.4 \mathrm{v}$ © examsnet.com

search_text: a particle of charge $1.0 \times 10^{-16} \, \mathrm{c}$ moves through a uniform magnetic field $\vec{b} = b_0 (\hat{i} + 4 \hat{j}) \, \mathrm{t}$ . the particle velocity at some instant is $\vec{v} = (2 \hat{i} + 4 \hat{j}) \, \mathrm{m} \, \mathrm{s}^{-1}$ and the magnetic force acting on it is $3 \times 10^{-16} \hat{k} \, \mathrm{n}$ . the magnitude of $b_{\circ}$ is {'a': '$1.0 \\, \\mathrm{t}$', 'b': '$2.5 \\, \\mathrm{t}$', 'c': '$0.5 \\, \\mathrm{t}$', 'd': '$0.75 \\, \\mathrm{t}$'} 2022 2022-07-07 shift_1 physics   110 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: force on a charged particle moving in region of a magnetic field is given  by : $f = q(v \times b)$ $\dots (i)$ here, $q = 1.0 \times 10^{-16} \, \mathrm{c}$ $v = (2\hat{i} + 4\hat{j}) \, \mathrm{m/s}, \quad b = b_0 (\hat{i} + 4\hat{j}) \, \mathrm{t}$ $f = 3 \times 10^{-16} \hat{k} \, \mathrm{n}$ subtracting in $\text{eq (i)}$ , we get : $3 \times 10^{-16} \hat{k} = 1 \times 10^{-16}$ $\begin{vmatrix} \hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k} \\ 2 & 4 & 0 \\ b_0 & 4b_0 & 0 \end{vmatrix}$ $\rightarrow 3\hat{k} = \hat{i}(0) - \hat{j}(0) + \hat{k}(8b_0 - 4b_0)$ $\rightarrow 3\hat{k} = 4b_0 \hat{k}$ or $b_0 = \frac{3}{4} = 0.75 \, \mathrm{t}$ © examsnet.com

search_text: a $100 \, \mu \mathrm{f}$ capacitor is connected to a $100 \, \mathrm{v}, 50 \, \mathrm{hz} \, \mathrm{ac}$ supply. the rms value of the current is {'a': '$3.14 \\, \\mathrm{a}$', 'b': '$4.75 \\, \\mathrm{a}$', 'c': '$2.33 \\, \\mathrm{a}$', 'd': '$5.5 \\, \\mathrm{a}$'} 2022 2022-07-07 shift_1 physics   113 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: given, $v_{\text{rms}} = 100 \, \mathrm{v}, f = 50 \, \mathrm{hz}$ $c_1 = 100 \, \mu \mathrm{f} = 100 \times 10^{-6} \, \mathrm{f}$ now, reactance of capacitor, $x_c = \frac{1}{c \omega} = \frac{1}{c \times 2 \pi f}$ $\rightarrow x_c = \frac{1}{100 \times 10^{-6} \times 2 \pi \times 50} = \frac{100}{\pi} \, \omega$ $\text{r. m. s}$ value of current in circuit will be $i_{\text{rms}} = \frac{v_{\text{rms}}}{x_c}$ $= \frac{100}{\frac{100}{\pi}} = \pi \, \mathrm{a} = 3.14 \, \mathrm{a}$ © examsnet.com

question: The equation that represents magnetic field of a plane electromagnetic wave which is propagating along $x$ -direction with wavelength $10\ \text{mm}$ and maximum electric field $60\ \text{V}\ \text{m}^{-1}$ in $y$ -direction is (c - speed of light)
search_text: the equation that represents magnetic field of a plane electromagnetic wave which is propagating along $x$ -direction with wavelength $10\ \text{mm}$ and maximum electric field $60\ \text{v}\ \text{m}^{-1}$ in $y$ -direction is (c - speed of light) {'a': '$(6 \\times 10^{-7}) \\sin \\left[0.2\\pi (ct - x)\\right] \\hat{k}$ tesla', 'b': '$(2 \\times 10^{-7}) \\sin \\left[200\\pi (c t - x)\\right] \\hat{k}$ tesla', 'c': '$(2 \\times 10^{-7}) \\sin \\left[200\\pi (c t - x)\\right] \\hat{i}$ tesla', 'd': '$(6 \\times 10^{-7}) \\sin \\left[0.2\\pi (ct - x)\\right] \\hat{i}$ tesla'} 2022 2022-07-07 shift_1 physics   115 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: equation of magnetic field of an electromagnetic wave is given by : $b = b_0 \sin(\omega t - kx) \hat{k}$ $= b_0 \sin\left(2\pi f t - \frac{2\pi}{\lambda} \cdot x \right) \hat{k}$ $\ldots \left[\because \omega = 2\pi f \text{ and } k = \frac{2\pi}{\lambda}\right]$ $b_0 \sin \frac{2\pi}{\lambda}[f\lambda t - x] \hat{k}$ $b = b_0 \sin \frac{2\pi}{\lambda}[ct - x] \hat{k}$ $\ldots (i)$ also direction of b vector is perpendicular to e and also tp direction of propagation and $b_0 = \frac{e_0}{c}$ here, $e_0 = 60\ \text{v m}^{-1}$ $\therefore b_0 = \frac{60}{3 \times 10^8} = 20 \times 10^{-7}$ also $k = \frac{2\pi}{\lambda}$ here $k = 200\pi = \frac{2\pi}{\lambda}$ $\rightarrow \lambda = \frac{1}{100}\ \text{m} = \frac{100}{100}\ \text{cm} = 10\ \text{mm} = 10^{-2}\ \text{m}$ putting the values is eq. (i), we get $b = 2 \times 10^{-7} \sin \left[\frac{2\pi}{10^{-2}} (ct - x)\right] \hat{k}$ $= 2 \times 10^{-7} \sin 200\pi (t - x) \hat{k}$ © examsnet.com

question: The average number of photons emitted per second by a laser of power $6.6 \times 10^{-3} \text{W}$ producing a light of wavelength $600 \text{nm}$ is (Planck's constant, $h = 6.6 \times 10^{-34} \text{J} \text{s}$ )
search_text: the average number of photons emitted per second by a laser of power $6.6 \times 10^{-3} \text{w}$ producing a light of wavelength $600 \text{nm}$ is (planck's constant, $h = 6.6 \times 10^{-34} \text{j} \text{s}$ ) {'a': '$2 \\times 10^{16}$', 'b': '$3 \\times 10^{16}$', 'c': '$4 \\times 10^{16}$', 'd': '$3 \\times 10^{16}$'} 2022 2022-07-07 shift_1 physics   116 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: photons emitted per second $n = \frac{\text{power}}{\text{energy of 1 photon}}$ $= \frac{p}{hc} = \frac{p\lambda}{hc}$ note $\therefore hc = 1240 \text{ev-nm}$ $1 \text{ev} = 1.6 \times 10^{-19} \text{j}$ as given that , $\lambda = 600 \text{nm}$ so, $\frac{hc}{\lambda} = \frac{1240 \text{ev-nm}}{600 \text{nm}}$ $= 2.067 \text{ev}$ $= 2.067 \times 1.6 \times 10^{-19} \text{j} = 33 \times 10^{-19}$ so, number of photons per second $n = \frac{p}{\frac{hc}{\lambda}} = \frac{6.6 \times 10^{-3}}{33 \times 10^{-19}}$ $= 2 \times 10^{16}$ photons per second © examsnet.com

search_text: $1.8\ \text{g}$ of glucose (molar mass $180\ \text{g}\ \text{mol}^{-1}$ ) is dissolved in $0.1\ \text{kg}$ of water. the freezing point of the solution $($ in $^{\circ}\ \text{c}$ ) is $(k_f\;\text{ for water }\;=1.86\ \text{k}\ \text{kg}\ \text{mol}^{-1})$ {'a': '$+0.186$', 'b': '$-0.372$', 'c': '$-0.186$', 'd': '$+0.372$'} 2022 2022-07-07 shift_1 chemistry   144 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: depression in freezing point is given as $\delta t = i k_f \times m$ where, $i=$ van't hoff factor $k_f=$ molal freezing point depression constant $m = \text{molality}$ molar mass of glucose $(\mathrm{c}_6 \mathrm{h}_{12} \mathrm{o}_6)$ $=12 \times 6+12 \times 1+6 \times 16=180\ \text{g/mol}$ molality of glucose $= \frac{\;\text{ mass of solute }\;}{\;\text{ molar mass of solute }\;} \times \frac{1}{\;\text{ mass of solvent (kg) }\;}$ $= \frac{1.8}{180} \times \frac{1}{0.1} = 0.1\ \text{m}$ $\therefore \delta t = 1 \times 1.86\ \text{k kg / mol} \times 0.1\ \text{m}$ $=0.186^{\circ}\ \text{c}$ $\therefore$ $\text{freezing point of solution = freezing point of water - depression in freezing point}$ $=0^{\circ}\ \text{c} - 0.186^{\circ}\ \text{c} = \therefore 186^{\circ}\ \text{c}$ © examsnet.com

search_text: let $f: r \rightarrow r$ be defined by $f(x)=2x+3$ . if $\alpha$ . $\beta$ are the roots of the equation $f(x^{2})-2f\left(\;\frac{x}{2}\right)-1=0$ then $\alpha^{2}+\beta^{2}=$ {'a': '$13$', 'b': '$25$', 'c': '$5$', 'd': '$18$'} 2022 2022-07-07 shift_2 mathematics   1 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: 👈: video solution $f(x)=2x+3$ $f(x^{2})-2f\left(\frac{x}{2}\right)-1=0$ $\rightarrow 2x^{2}+3-2(x+3)-1=0$ $\rightarrow 2x^{2}-2x-4=0$ $\rightarrow x^{2}-x-2=0$ $\rightarrow x=2$ or $x=-1$ $\therefore \alpha^{2}+\beta^{2}=4+1=5$ © examsnet.com

question: If a matrix $A$ satisfies the equation $A^{3}-6 A^{2}+11 A-6 I=0$ , then $A^{-1}$ can be
search_text: if a matrix $a$ satisfies the equation $a^{3}-6 a^{2}+11 a-6 i=0$ , then $a^{-1}$ can be {'a': '$\\;\\frac{1}{4} i$', 'b': '$4 i$', 'c': '$3 i$', 'd': '$\\;\\frac{1}{3} i$'} 2022 2022-07-07 shift_2 mathematics   4 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: 👈: video solution $a^{3}-6 a^{2}+11 a-6 i=0$ $a^{3}-a^{2}-5 a^{2}+5 a+6 a-6 i=0$ $\rightarrow a^{2}[a-i]-5 a[a-i]+6[a-i]=0$ $\rightarrow [a-i] [a^{2}-5 a+6] =0$ $\rightarrow (a-i)(a-2 i)(a-3 i)=0$ $\therefore a-3 i$ can be a zero matrix. $\rightarrow a=3 i$ $\rightarrow a a^{-1}=3 a^{-1}$ $\rightarrow i=3 a^{-1}$ $\rightarrow a^{-1}=\frac{1}{3} i$ © examsnet.com

question: The rank of the matrix $A = \begin{bmatrix} 2 & 1 & 2 \\ 1 & 0 & 1 \\ 4 & 1 & 4 \end{bmatrix}$ is
search_text: the rank of the matrix $a = \begin{bmatrix} 2 & 1 & 2 \\ 1 & 0 & 1 \\ 4 & 1 & 4 \end{bmatrix}$ is {'a': '$0$', 'b': '$1$', 'c': '$2$', 'd': '$3$'} 2022 2022-07-07 shift_2 mathematics   5 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: 👈: video solution convert matrix into row echelon form. $\; \begin{bmatrix} 2 & 1 & 2 \\ 1 & 0 & 1 \\ 4 & 1 & 4 \end{bmatrix} \xrightarrow[ ]{r_1 \rightarrow r_1 - r_2} \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 & 1 \\ 4 & 1 & 4 \end{bmatrix}$ $\; \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 & 1 \\ 4 & 1 & 4 \end{bmatrix} \; \xrightarrow[r_3 \rightarrow r_3 - 4 r_1]{r_2 - r_1} \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & -3 & 0 \end{bmatrix}$ $\; \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & -3 & 0 \end{bmatrix}_{r_3 \rightarrow \left(-\frac{1}{3}\right) r_3}^{\xrightarrow[ ]{r_2 \rightarrow (-1) r_2}} \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 3 & 0 \end{bmatrix}$ $\; \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 3 & 0 \end{bmatrix} \xrightarrow[r_3 \rightarrow r_3 - r_2]{} \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \end{bmatrix}$ number of non-zero rows is 2 . $\therefore$ rank of matrix is 2 . © examsnet.com

question: $\; \frac{(1+i)x-2i}{3+i} + \; \frac{(2-3i)y}{3-i} = i \Rightarrow x+y=$

search_text: $f(x)=\begin{cases}4 & -\infty < x < -\sqrt{5}\\ x^2-1 & -\sqrt{5} \le x \le \sqrt{5}\\ 4 & \sqrt{5} \le x < \infty \end{cases}$ if $k$ is the number of points where $f(x)$ is not differentiable then $k-2=$ {'a': '$2$', 'b': '$1$', 'c': '$0$', 'd': '$3$'} 2022 2022-07-07 shift_2 mathematics   62 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: 👈: video solution points to check, $x=-\sqrt{5}, x=\sqrt{5}$ $f(x)=\begin{cases}4 & -\infty < x < -\sqrt{5}\\ x^2-1 & -\sqrt{5} \le x \le \sqrt{5}\\ 4 & \sqrt{5} \le x < \infty \end{cases}.$ at $x=-\sqrt{5},$ $\text{lhl} = \text{rhl} = f(-\sqrt{5}) = 4$ $\text{lhd} = 0, \text{rhd} = 2(-\sqrt{5}) = -2\sqrt{5}$ $\text{lhd} \neq \text{rhd}$ $\rightarrow \text{not differentiable at } x=-\sqrt{5}$ $\text{at } x=\sqrt{5}$ $\text{lhd} = 2\sqrt{5}, \text{rhd} = 0$ $\rightarrow$ not differentiable at $x=\sqrt{5}$ $\therefore k=2, k-2=0$ © examsnet.com

search_text: $\int \sqrt{x+\sqrt{x^{2}+2}} \, dx =$ {'a': '$\\frac{3}{2}(x+\\sqrt{x+2})^{3/2} - 2(x+\\sqrt{x^{2}+2})^{1/4} + c$', 'b': '$\\frac{1}{3}(x+\\sqrt{x^{2}+2})^{3/2} - 2(x+\\sqrt{x^{2}+2})^{1/4} + c$', 'c': '$(x+\\sqrt{x^{2}+2})^{-3/2} - 2(x+\\sqrt{x^{2}+2})^{-1/2} + c$', 'd': '$\\frac{(x+\\sqrt{x^{2}+2})^{2}-6}{3 \\sqrt{x+\\sqrt{x^{2}+2}}} + c$'} 2022 2022-07-07 shift_2 mathematics   72 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: 👈: video solution $(\sqrt{x^2+2}+x)(\sqrt{x^2+2}-x)=2$ $i=\int \sqrt{x+\sqrt{x^2+2}} \, dx$ on putting $\sqrt{x^2+2}+x=t$ $\rightarrow \sqrt{x^2+2}-x=\frac{2}{t}$ $\therefore \sqrt{x^2+2}=\frac{t+\frac{2}{t}}{2}$ $\text{also } \left(\frac{x}{\sqrt{x^2+2}}+1\right) dx = dt$ $\rightarrow dx = \frac{t+\frac{2}{t}}{2t} \, dt$ $\therefore i=\int \sqrt{t} \cdot \left(\frac{t+\frac{2}{t}}{2t}\right) \, dt = \int \left(\frac{\sqrt{t}}{2}+t^{-3/2}\right) \, dt$ $\therefore = \frac{t^{3/2}}{3} - \frac{t^{1/2}}{\frac{1}{2}} + c$ $= \frac{t^2-6}{3 t^{1/2}} + c$ $\rightarrow \frac{(\sqrt{x^2+2}+x)^2-6}{3 \sqrt{\sqrt{x^2+2}+x}} + c$ © examsnet.com

search_text: two wooden blocks of mass $m_{1}$ and $m_{2}$ rest on a frictionless table. a bullet of mass $m$ is fired at $m_{1}$ with speed $v$ which embedded in it and the two together finally collide with $m_{2}$ . find the velocity of $m_{2}$ after collision. [ignore any energy loss and treat the problem to be one dimensional] {'a': '$\\; \\frac{2 m v}{m_{1} + m_{2} + m}$', 'b': '$\\; \\frac{m v}{m_{1} + m_{2} + m}$', 'c': '$\\; \\frac{(m_{1} + m_{2} + m) v}{m_{1} + m_{2} + m}$', 'd': '$\\; \\frac{m_{1} + m_{2}}{m_{1} + m_{2} + m} v$'} 2022 2022-07-07 shift_2 physics   87 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: for an elastic collision of 2 masses $m_1$ and $m_2$ with initial velocities $u_1$ and $u_2$ , final velocities of masses after collision are $v_1 = \left(\frac{m_1 - m_2}{m_1 + m_2}\right) u_1 + \frac{2 m_2 u_2}{(m_1+m_2)}$ and $v_2 = \left(\frac{m_2 - m_1}{m_1 + m_2}\right) u_2 + \frac{2 m_1 u_2}{m_1 + m_2}$ these are obtained as standard results by applying conservation of energy and momentum equations. now, in given case at first bullet is embedded in mass $m_1$ . let speed of bullet + block system be $v_1$ after collision. then by conservation of momentum we have. $m v = (m + m_1) v_1$ or $v_1 = \frac{m v}{m + m_1}$ note here we are not using standard result as first collision is perfectly inelastic. now, bullet $+m_1$ strikes $m_2$ and it is given in problem that this collision is elastic. now, by formula we have, $v_2 = \left(\frac{(m + m_1) - m_2}{m + m_1 + m_2}\right) v_1 + 0$ and $v_3 = \left(\frac{m_2 - (m + m_1)}{m_2 + m + m_1} \times 0\right) + \left(\frac{2 (m + m_1) v_1}{m + m_1 + m_2}\right)$ $\rightarrow v_3 = \frac{2 (m + m_1)}{m + m_1 + m_2} \cdot \frac{m v}{(m + m_1)}$ $= \frac{2 m v}{m + m_1 + m_2}$ note you can remember these standard and useful results for finding final velocities in case of elastic collisions. © examsnet.com

search_text: a wheel undergoes a constant acceleration starting form rest at $t=0$ . the angular velocity of the wheel is $3.14\;\frac{\text{rad}}{\text{sec}}$ when $t=2\text{ s}$ . the accelerator is abruptly ceased at $t=20\text{ s}$ . the number of revolutions, wheel makes in the interval $t=0$ to $t=40\text{ s}$ is {'a': '$100$', 'b': '$175$', 'c': '$225$', 'd': '$150$'} 2022 2022-07-07 shift_2 physics   90 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: given, $\omega=314\;\frac{\text{rad}}{\text{s}}$ at $t=2\text{ s}$ let $\alpha=$ constant angular acceleration then using $\omega_1=\omega_0+\alpha t$ we have, $\omega_1=\alpha t$ $\cdots [\because \omega_0=0]$ $\therefore 314=\alpha(2)$ $\rightarrow \alpha=\frac{314}{2}\;\frac{\text{rad}}{\text{s}^2}$ now, angle covered in 20 seconds is given by, $\theta_1=\omega_0 t+\frac{1}{2}\alpha t^2$ $\rightarrow\theta_1=\frac{1}{2}\alpha t^2$ so, $\theta_1=\frac{1}{2}\times\frac{314}{2}\times(20)^2=3.14\text{ rad}$ at $t=20\text{ s},\text{ angular speed of wheel,}$ $\rightarrow\omega_2=\omega_0+\alpha t$ $\rightarrow\omega_2=0+\frac{314}{2}\times 20$ as, acceleration does not operates after $t=20\text{ s}$ . so, wheel now rotates freely (with constant angular speed) upto $40\text{ s}$ . angular displacement in radians covered in another 20s of freewheeling is $\theta_2\;=\omega_1\times t$ $=314\times 20=628\text{ rad}$ total angle covered by wheel, $\theta=(314+628)\text{ rad}$ $=942\text{ rad}$ $\therefore$ number of revolutions of wheel $n=\frac{\theta}{2\pi}=\frac{942}{2\pi}$ $=\frac{314\times 3}{2\times 314}=150$ © examsnet.com

(c) lithium chloride exists as licl. $2 \mathrm{h}_{2}\mathrm{o}$ {'a': 'a, b only', 'b': 'a, c only', 'c': 'b. c only', 'd': 'a, b, c'} 2022 2022-07-07 shift_2 chemistry   136 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: alkali metals are strong reducing agents because after the removal of the only valence electron $(n s^{1})$ they can gain the electronic configuration of noble gases $(n-1) p^{6}$ , that is more stable electronic configuration. $\mathrm{ko}_{2}$ is paramagnetic oxide due to the presence of 1 unpaired electrons. the number of electrons present is 17 where the sixteen electrons are from two oxygen atoms and one from the negative charge $(\mathrm{o}_{2}^{-})$ . its molecular orbital configuration can be written as $\sigma 1s^{2} \sigma^{\times} 1s^{2} \sigma 2s^{2} \sigma^{\times} 2s^{2} \sigma 2p_{z}^{2} \pi 2p_{x}^{2} = \pi 2p_{y}^{2} \pi \times 2p_{x}^{2}$ $= \pi^{\times} 2p_{y}^{1} \sigma \times 2p_{z}^{0}.$ so, statement (b) is wrong. the hydration enthalpies of alkali metal ions decrease with increase in ionic sizes. $\mathrm{li}^{+} > \mathrm{na}^{+} > \mathrm{k}^{+} > \mathrm{rb}^{+}$ $\mathrm{li}^{+}$ has maximum degree of hydration and for this reason, lithium salts are mostly hydrated, e.g. $\mathrm{licl} \cdot 2 \mathrm{h}_{2}\mathrm{o}$ . © examsnet.com

search_text: the decreasing order of acidic nature of the following compounds is {'a': 'iii $>$ ii $>$ i', 'b': 'ii $>$ iii $>$ i', 'c': 'ii $>$ i $>$ iii', 'd': 'i $>$ iii $>$ ii'} 2022 2022-07-07 shift_2 chemistry   140 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: terminal alkynes contain $\text{s p} \ \mathrm{c} - \mathrm{h}$ group that is acidic in nature. acidity also depends on the stability of the conjugate base formed. $- \mathrm{no}_2$ is electron withdrawing group and therefore decreases the electron density on the carbanion and thus stabilises the conjugate base. $- \mathrm{nh}_2$ is electron donating group and therefore increases the electron density on the carbanion and thus destabilises the conjugate base. therefore, the acidity order is $\mathrm{ii} > \mathrm{i} > \mathrm{iii}.$ © examsnet.com

question: The density of $\mathrm{Na}$ is $0.613\ \mathrm{g}\ \mathrm{cm}^{-3}$ . If the edge length of unit cell of $\mathrm{Na}$ is $5\ \mathrm{A}^{0}$ , the effective number of atoms of $\mathrm{Na}$ per unit cell is (Atomic weight of $\mathrm{Na}=23\ \mathrm{u}$ )
search_text: the density of $\mathrm{na}$ is $0.613\ \mathrm{g}\ \mathrm{cm}^{-3}$ . if the edge length of unit cell of $\mathrm{na}$ is $5\ \mathrm{a}^{0}$ , the effective number of atoms of $\mathrm{na}$ per unit cell is (atomic weight of $\mathrm{na}=23\ \mathrm{u}$ ) {'a': '8', 'b': '1', 'c': '2', 'd': '4'} 2022 2022-07-07 shift_2 chemistry   141 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: we know that, $d=\frac{z \times m}{a^{3} \times n_{a}}$ where, $d$ is density, $z$ is the number of atoms, $m$ is the atomic mass, $a$ is edge length and $n_{a}$ is avogadro's number. $z=\frac{d \times a^{3} \times n_{a}}{m}$ $=\frac{0.613\ \mathrm{g}\ \mathrm{cm}^{-3} \times (5 \times 10^{-8}\ \mathrm{cm})^{3} \times 6.023 \times 10^{23}}{23\ \mathrm{g}}=2$ © examsnet.com

question: Ag crystallizes in fcc lattice. What is the total number of tetrahedral voids present in $540\,\mathrm{g}$ of Ag metal? $(N_A=$ Avagadro number; Ag atomic weight $=108\,\mathrm{g}\,\mathrm{mol}^{-1})$
search_text: ag crystallizes in fcc lattice. what is the total number of tetrahedral voids present in $540\,\mathrm{g}$ of ag metal? $(n_a=$ avagadro number; ag atomic weight $=108\,\mathrm{g}\,\mathrm{mol}^{-1})$ {'a': '$10 n_a$', 'b': '$20 n_a$', 'c': '$40 n_a$', 'd': '$60 n_a$'} 2022 2022-07-07 shift_2 chemistry   142 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: ag crystallises in an fcc lattice, so each unit cell contains 4 ag atoms and 8 tetrahedral voids. number of moles of ag in $540\,\mathrm{g}$ $=\dfrac{540\,\mathrm{g}}{108\,\mathrm{g}\,\mathrm{mol}^{-1}}=5\,\mathrm{mol}$ . number of ag atoms $=5n_a$ . number of unit cells $=\dfrac{5n_a}{4}=1.25n_a$ . each unit cell contains 8 tetrahedral voids. total number of tetrahedral voids $=8\times1.25n_a=10n_a$ . alternatively, in an fcc lattice the number of tetrahedral voids is twice the number of atoms: total tetrahedral voids $=2\times5n_a=10n_a$ . hence the correct option is $10n_a$ . © examsnet.com

search_text: $3.1 \text{g}$ of a compound. ' $x$ ' (molar mass $=62 \text{g} \text{mol}^{-1}$ ) is dissolved in $19.5 \text{g}$ of other compound, $y$ (molar mass $=78 \text{g} \text{mol}^{-1}$ ). the ratio of mole fractions of $x$ and $y$ in the solution is {'a': '$1:5$', 'b': '$5:1$', 'c': '$4:1$', 'd': '$1:4$'} 2022 2022-07-07 shift_2 chemistry   143 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: the number of moles of $x = \frac{w_x}{m_x} = \frac{3.1 \text{g}}{62 \text{g} \text{mol}^{-1}} = 0.05 \text{mol}$ the number of moles of $y = \frac{w_y}{m_y} = \frac{19.5 \text{g}}{78 \text{g} \text{mol}^{-1}} = 0.25 \text{mol}$ mole fraction of $x = \frac{\text{moles of x}}{\text{total moles}} = \frac{0.05}{0.75} = 0.066$ mole fraction of $y = \frac{\text{moles of y}}{\text{total moles}} = \frac{0.25}{0.75} = 0.33$ the ratio of mole fraction of $x$ and $y = \frac{0.066}{0.33} = \frac{1}{5}$ © examsnet.com

search_text: the standard gibbs energy $(\delta g^{0})$ for the following reaction is $\mathrm{a}(s)+\mathrm{b}^{2+}(aq) \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{a}^{2+}(aq)+\mathrm{b}(s),\; k_{c}=10^{12}$ at $25^{\circ}\mathrm{c} (k_{c}= \text{ equilibrium constant })$ {'a': '$-150\\ \\mathrm{kj}$', 'b': '$-96.80\\ \\mathrm{kj}$', 'c': '$-68.47\\ \\mathrm{kj}$', 'd': '$-100\\ \\mathrm{kj}$'} 2022 2022-07-07 shift_2 chemistry   145 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: the standard gibb's free energy change $(\delta g^{\circ})$ at standard conditions is given by the formula $\delta g^{\circ}=-r t \ln lok_{eq}$ where, $r$ is gas constant $=8.314\ \mathrm{j\ mol^{-1}\ k^{-1}}$ , $t=(25+273)\ \mathrm{k}=298\ \mathrm{k}$ and $k_{eq}$ is the equilibrium constant $\delta g^{\circ}\;=-8.314 \times 298 \times 2.303 \log 10^{12}$ $=-68,470.18\ \mathrm{j}=-68.47\ \mathrm{kj}$ © examsnet.com

question: What is the concentration (in mol $L^{-1}$ ) of the product after $20\ \text{s}$ in the following reaction. Given that $A \rightarrow 3B$ , rate $= k[A]^{\circ}$ Time(s) Concentration of the reactant $(\text{mol}\ \text{L}^{-1})$ $0$ $0.1$ $15$ $0.05$ $20$ $0.1-x$
search_text: what is the concentration (in mol $l^{-1}$ ) of the product after $20\ \text{s}$ in the following reaction. given that $a \rightarrow 3b$ , rate $= k[a]^{\circ}$ time(s) concentration of the reactant $(\text{mol}\ \text{l}^{-1})$ $0$ $0.1$ $15$ $0.05$ $20$ $0.1-x$ {'a': '$6.6 \\times 10^{-2}$', 'b': '$1.32 \\times 10^{-1}$', 'c': '$1.98 \\times 10^{-1}$', 'd': '$2.2 \\times 10^{-2}$'} 2022 2022-07-07 shift_2 chemistry   146 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: for the zero order reaction, $a \rightarrow 3b$ the half-life is given by the formula $t_{\frac{1}{2}} = \frac{a_0}{2k}$ where, $a_0$ is the initial concentration and $k$ is the rate constant. after $15\ \text{s}$ the concentration of $a\ (0.1\ \text{mol}\ \text{l}^{-1})$ is reduced to its half value $(0.05\ \text{mol}\ \text{l}^{-1})$ , so, $t_{\frac{1}{2}} = 15\ \text{s}$ $k = \frac{01}{2\times 15} = 0.0033\ \text{mol}\ \text{l}^{-1}\ \text{s}^{-1}$ for zero order reaction after time ' $t$ ' the concentration of reactant $a$ is given by formula $[a] = [a_0] - kt$ after $t = 20\ \text{s}$ $[a] = 0.1\ \text{mol}\ \text{l}^{-1} - 0.0033\ \text{mol}\ \text{l}^{-1}\ \text{s}^{-1} \times 20\ \text{s}$ $= 0.033\ \text{mol}\ \text{l}^{-1}$ this implies that $(0.1 - 0.033) = 0.067$ moles of reactant $a$ are converted to product $b$ . since, 1 mole of $a$ gives 3 moles of $b$ , so $0.067$ moles of reactant $a$ will give $(0.066 \times 3) = 0.198$ moles of $b$ , i.e. $1.98 \times 10^{-1}$ moles. © examsnet.com

question: Freundlich adsorption isotherm fails at which of the following condition?
search_text: freundlich adsorption isotherm fails at which of the following condition? {'a': 'high temperature', 'b': 'low temperature', 'c': 'high pressure', 'd': 'low pressure'} 2022 2022-07-07 shift_2 chemistry   147 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: the freundlich adsorption isotherm is the mathematical representation for the variation of the extent of adsorption $\left(\frac{x}{m}\right)$ with pressure $(p)$ at a given temperature. $\frac{x}{m}=k \cdot p^{1/n}(n>l)$ where ' $x$ ' is the mass of the gas adsorbed on mass ' $m$ ' of the adsorbent at pressure ' $p$ '. ' $k$ ' and ' $n$ ' are constants that depend on the nature of the adsorbent and the gas at a particular temperature. experimentally, it was determined that the extent of gas adsorption varies with pressure raised to the power $\frac{1}{n}$ until saturation pressure $p_s$ is reached. at high pressure, $\frac{x}{m}$ becomes independent of pressure. hence, freundlich equation becomes $\frac{x}{m}=k \cdot p^0 \rightarrow \frac{x}{m}=k$ thus, the freundlich adsorption isotherm fails at higher pressure. © examsnet.com

search_text: arrange the following oxides in correct order of their acidic character. ${\mathrm{n}_{2}\mathrm{o}_{3}}_i, \;\; {\mathrm{p}_{2}\mathrm{o}_{3}}_{ii}, {\mathrm{n}_{2}\mathrm{o}_{5}}_{iii}, \;\; {\mathrm{as}_{2}\mathrm{o}_{3}}_{iv}$ {'a': 'i $>$ iii $>$ ii $>$ iv', 'b': 'iii $>$ i $>$ ii $>$ iv', 'c': 'iv $>$ ii $>$ i $>$ iii', 'd': 'iii $>$ i $>$ iv $>$ ii'} 2022 2022-07-07 shift_2 chemistry   149 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: acidic character of oxides in group 15 to 18 . elements decreases down the group. as we move down the group, the atomic size increases and electronegativity decreases. the oxide in the . higher oxidation state of the elements is more acidic than that of lower oxidation state. in $\mathrm{n}_{2}\mathrm{o}_{3}(i), \mathrm{p}_{2}\mathrm{o}_{3}$ (ii) and $\mathrm{as}_{2}\mathrm{o}_{3}$ (iv), n, $\mathrm{p}$ and as are in $+3$ oxidation state respectively whereas in $\mathrm{n}_{2}\mathrm{o}_{5}$ (iii) the $\mathrm{n}$ is in $+5$ oxidation state. so, the acidity order is $\mathrm{n}_{2}\mathrm{o}_{5} > \mathrm{n}_{2}\mathrm{o}_{3} > \mathrm{p}_{2}\mathrm{o}_{3} > \mathrm{as}_{2}\mathrm{o}_{3} \; \text{, i.e. iii } \; > \; \text{ i } \; > \; \text{ ii } \; > \; \text{ iv } \;$ © examsnet.com

question: Which of the following represents correct order of oxidizing power of halogens with water
search_text: which of the following represents correct order of oxidizing power of halogens with water {'a': '$\\mathrm{i}_2 > \\mathrm{br}_2 > \\mathrm{cl}_2 > \\mathrm{f}_2$', 'b': '$\\mathrm{cl}_2 > \\mathrm{f}_2 > \\mathrm{br}_2 > \\mathrm{i}_2$', 'c': '$\\mathrm{f}_2 > \\mathrm{cl}_2 > \\mathrm{i}_2 > \\mathrm{br}_2$', 'd': '$\\mathrm{f}_2 > \\mathrm{cl}_2 > \\mathrm{br}_2 > \\mathrm{i}_2$'} 2022 2022-07-07 shift_2 chemistry   150 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: whenever one of the halogens is involved in oxidising a species in solution, the halogen is reduced to a halide ion associated with water molecules. the following reactions illustrate this process $\mathrm{f}_2(g) + 2e^{-} \rightarrow 2\mathrm{f}^{-}(aq)$ $\rightarrow \mathrm{cl}_2(g) + 2e^{-} \rightarrow 2\mathrm{cl}^{-}(aq)$ $\mathrm{br}_2(l) + 2e^{-} \rightarrow 2\mathrm{br}^{-}(aq)$ $\mathrm{i}_2(g) + 2e^{-} \rightarrow 2\mathrm{i}^{-}(aq)$ smaller the size of ion, higher is the energy released when the ion is hydrated. since, the size of ions increases in the order $\mathrm{f}^{-} < \mathrm{cl}^{-} < \mathrm{br}^{-} < \mathrm{i}^{-}$ . the order of hydration energy is $\mathrm{f}^{-}(aq) > \mathrm{cl}^{-}(aq) > \mathrm{br}^{-}(aq) > \mathrm{i}^{-}(aq)$ because of very high hydration enthalpy of the fluoride ion, $\mathrm{f}_2$ gets very easily reduced followed by $\mathrm{cl}_2$ , then $\mathrm{br}_2$ and $\mathrm{i}_2$ . therefore, the correct order of oxidising power of halogens is $\mathrm{f}_2 > \mathrm{cl}_2 > \mathrm{br}_2 > \mathrm{i}_2$ . © examsnet.com

search_text: which of the following elements are not regarded as transition elements? {'a': '$\\mathrm{zn}, \\mathrm{cd}, \\mathrm{hg}$', 'b': '$\\mathrm{cu}, \\mathrm{zn}, \\mathrm{hg}$', 'c': '$\\mathrm{ag}, \\mathrm{zn}, \\mathrm{hg}$', 'd': '$\\mathrm{ag}, \\mathrm{cd}, \\mathrm{hg}$'} 2022 2022-07-07 shift_2 chemistry   151 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: transition elements are characterised by partially filled $(n-1) d$ subshells. $\mathrm{zn}, \mathrm{cd}, \mathrm{hg}, \mathrm{cu}$ and $\mathrm{ag}$ all have completely filled $(n-1) d$ subshell. but $\mathrm{zn}, \mathrm{cd}$ , and $\mathrm{hg}$ are not considered as transition metals as in their most common oxidation state, i.e. $+2$ , they have $d^{10}$ configuration. whereas $\mathrm{cu}$ and $\mathrm{ag}$ when exists in $+2$ oxidation state have $d^9$ configuration. electronic configuration of $\mathrm{zn}$ is $[ \mathrm{ar}] 3 d^{10} 4 s^2$ electronic configuration of $\mathrm{cd}$ is $[ \mathrm{ar}] 3 d^{10} 4 s^2$ electronic configuration of $\mathrm{hg}$ is $[ \mathrm{ar}] 3 d^{10} 4 s_1^2$ electronic configuration of $\mathrm{cu}$ is $[ \mathrm{ar}] 3 d^{10} 4 s^1$ electronic configuration of $\mathrm{ag}$ is [ar] $d^{10} 4 s^1$ © examsnet.com

search_text: the hybridization of metals involved in the following complexes, respectively are $[\mathrm{mn}(\mathrm{cn})_6]^{3-}, [\mathrm{cof}_6]^{3-}$ {'a': '$sp^{3}d^{2}, sp^{3}d^{2}$', 'b': '$sp^{3}d^{2}, d^{2}sp^{3}$', 'c': '$d^{2}sp^{3}, d^{2}sp^{3}$', 'd': '$d^{2} s p^{3}, s p^{3} d^{2}$'} 2022 2022-07-07 shift_2 chemistry   152 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: in $[\mathrm{mn}(\mathrm{cn})_6]^{3-}$ ,mn is in +3 oxidation state $\mathrm{mn}^{3+} (3d^4)$ = $\mathrm{mn}^{3+}\text{ ion in } [\mathrm{mn}(\mathrm{cn})_6]^{3-}$ = as $\mathrm{cn}^{-}$ is a strong field ligand, it causes pairing of two $3d$ electrons, thereby making two $d$ -orbitals vacant, namely $d_{x^2-y^2}$ and $d_{z^2}$ . these two $d$ -orbitals and one $4s$ and three $4p$ -orbitals hybridize and give $d^{2} s p^{3}$ -hybridization. in $[\mathrm{co}(\mathrm{f})_6]^{3-}$ , co is in $+3$ oxidation state. $\mathrm{co} = 3d^{7} 4s^{0}$ $\mathrm{co}^{3+} = 3d^{7} 4s^{0}$ as $\mathrm{f}^{-}$ is a weak field ligand, so it cannot cause the pairing of unpaired $3d$ -electrons. thus, one $4s$ , three $4p$ -orbitals and two $4d$ -orbitals hybridise and give $sp^{3} d^{2}$ -hybridisation. © examsnet.com

search_text: if $x^{2}+px+1$ is a factor of $a x^{3}+bx+c$ , then {'a': '$a^{2}+c^{2}=ab+3$', 'b': '$a^{2}-c^{2}=ab$', 'c': '$a^{2}-c^{2}=-ab$', 'd': '$2a^{2}+c^{2}=ab$'} 2022 2022-07-08 shift_1 mathematics   11 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: 👈: video solution given, $x^{2}+px+1$ is a factor of $ax^{3}+bx+c$ then, $ax^{3}+bx+x(x^{2}+px+1)(mx+n)$ $=ax^{3}+bx+c=mx^{3}+nx^{2}+mpx^{2}+npx+n+mx$ comparing both the expression, we get $m=a, mp+n=0, np+m=b, n=c$ ⇒ $p=\frac{-n}{m} \text{ or } p=\frac{-c}{a}$ $c\left(\frac{-c}{a}\right)+a=b\rightarrow -c^{2}+a^{2}=ab$ ∴ $a^{2}-c^{2}=ab$ © examsnet.com

search_text: suppose a triangle of area 27 sq. units is formed by $18 x^{2}-9 x y+y^{2}=0$ and $y=c$ . then the centroid of the triangle is {'a': '$(3,12)$', 'b': '$(12,3)$', 'c': '$(-12,3)$', 'd': '$(-3,12)$'} 2022 2022-07-08 shift_1 mathematics   46 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: 👈: video solution the given pair of lines $18x^2 - 9xy+y^2 =0$ is homogeneous. ⇒ the two lines passes through the origin, i.e $o (0,0)$ . the other two points of the triangle can be determined by substituting y=c in equation of pair of lines $18x^2-9xc +c^2=0$ ⇒ $18x^2-6xc-3xc+c^2=0$ ⇒ $6x(3x-c)-c(3x-c)=0$ $(6x-c)(3x-c)=0\rightarrow x=\frac{c}{6}, x=\frac{c}{3}$ the two points are $\left(\frac{c}{6}, c\right)$ and $\left(\frac{c}{3}, c\right)$ area $=27$ $\frac{1}{2} \begin{vmatrix} 0 & 0 & 1 \\ \frac{c}{3} & c & 1 \\ \frac{c}{6} & c & 1 \end{vmatrix} = 27 \rightarrow \frac{1}{2} \left[ \frac{c^2}{3} - \frac{c^2}{6} \right] = 27$ ⇒ $\frac{1}{2} \times \frac{c^2}{6} = 27 \rightarrow c^2 = 27 \times 2 \times 6$ $c=18$ the three points of the triangle are $(0,0),(3,18),(6,18)$ . centroid of triangle $= \left( \frac{0+3+6}{3} , \frac{0+18+18}{3} \right)$ $=(3, 12)$ © examsnet.com

search_text: the straight line $x \cos \alpha + y \sin \alpha = p$ cuts the circle $x^{2}+y^{2}-a^{2}=0$ at $a$ and $b$ . then the equation of circle having $ab$ as diameter is {'a': '$x^{2}+y^{2}-a^{2}+p(x \\cos \\alpha + y \\sin \\alpha - p)=0$', 'b': '$x^{2}+y^{2}-a^{2}-p(x \\cos \\alpha + y \\sin \\alpha + p)=0$', 'c': '$x^{2}+y^{2}-a^{2}+2p(x \\cos \\alpha + y \\sin \\alpha - p)=0$', 'd': '$x^{2}+y^{2}-a^{2}-2p(x \\cos \\alpha + y \\sin \\alpha - p)=0$'} 2022 2022-07-08 shift_1 mathematics   51 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: 👈: video solution equation of circle having diameter $ab$ ⇒ $(x^{2}+y^{2}-a^{2})+\lambda (x \cos \alpha + y \sin \alpha - p)=0$ ⇒ $x^{2}+y^{2}+x\lambda \cos \alpha + y\lambda \sin \alpha -a^{2}-\lambda p=0$ coordinate of centre $=\left(\frac{-\lambda \cos \alpha}{2}, \frac{-\lambda \sin \alpha}{2}\right)$ $ab$ is the diameter of required circle so its centre lies on the line $x \cos \alpha + y \sin \alpha = p$ $-\frac{\lambda}{2}\cos^{2}\alpha - \frac{\lambda}{2}\sin^{2}\alpha = p$ ⇒ $-\frac{\lambda}{2}=p$ ⇒ $\lambda = -2p$ ∴ the required equation is $x^{2}+y^{2}-a^{2}-2p(x \cos \alpha + y \sin \alpha - p)=0$ © examsnet.com

search_text: if $\lim\limits_{n\rightarrow\infty}x_n$ exists and is finite, $x_1=2,\; x_{n+1}=\frac{a+bx_n}{b+cx_n}\;\forall n\in\mathbb{n}$ and $c>b>a>0$ then $\lim\limits_{n\rightarrow\infty}x_n=$ {'a': '$\\sqrt{\\frac{ab}{c}}$', 'b': '$\\sqrt{\\frac{a}{c}}$', 'c': '$\\sqrt{\\frac{c}{b}}$', 'd': '$\\sqrt{\\frac{a}{b}}$'} 2022 2022-07-08 shift_1 mathematics   59 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: 👈: video solution $x_{n+1} = \frac{a+bx_n}{b+cx_n}$ $\lim\limits_{x\rightarrow\infty}x_{n+1}= \frac{a+b\lim\limits_{x\rightarrow\infty}x_n}{b+c\lim\limits_{x\rightarrow\infty}x_n}$ ∴ $\lim\limits_{x\rightarrow\infty}x_{n+1} = \lim\limits_{x\rightarrow\infty}x_n = y$ (let) $y=\frac{a+by}{b+cy}$ ⇒ $by+cy^2=a+by\rightarrow cy^2=a$ ⇒ $y^2=\frac{a}{c}\rightarrow y=\sqrt{\frac{a}{c}}$ ∴ $\lim\limits_{x\rightarrow\infty}x_n = \sqrt{\frac{a}{c}}$ © examsnet.com

search_text: the integral value of $n$ for which $\lim\limits_{x \rightarrow0}\; \frac{(\cos x-1)(\cos x-e^{x})}{x^{n}}$ is a finite non zero real number is {'a': '$4$', 'b': '$3$', 'c': '$2$', 'd': '$1$'} 2022 2022-07-08 shift_1 mathematics   60 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: 👈: video solution $\lim\limits_{x \rightarrow0} \frac{(\cos x-1)(\cos x-e^{x})}{x^{n}}$ $\lim\limits_{x \rightarrow0}\left(\frac{\cos x-1}{x^2}\right) \times \lim\limits_{x \rightarrow0}\frac{\cos x-e^{x}}{n^{n-2}}$ $= \lim\limits_{x \rightarrow0} \frac{-2 \sin^2 \frac{x}{2}}{4 \times \left(\frac{x}{2}\right)^2} \times \lim\limits_{x \rightarrow0} \frac{\cos x - e^{x}}{x^{n-2}}$ $= -\frac{1}{2} \times \lim\limits_{x \rightarrow0} \frac{\cos x - e^{x}}{x^{n-2}} [\text{0/0 form}]$ apply l'hospital rule $-\frac{1}{2} \lim\limits_{x \rightarrow0} \frac{-\sin x - e^{x}}{(n-2) x^{n-3}}$ $= -\frac{1}{2} \lim\limits_{x \rightarrow0} \frac{-\sin x - e^{x}}{(n-2)} \times \lim\limits_{x \rightarrow0} \frac{1}{x^{n-3}}$ $= \frac{1}{2}(n-2) \lim\limits_{x \rightarrow0} \frac{1}{x^{n-3}}$ the above limit is finite if $n-3=0$ . ∴ $n=3$ © examsnet.com

search_text: if $f(x)=\begin{cases} \tan^{-1} x, & \text{ when } |x| \le 1 \\ \frac{1}{2}(|x|-1), & \text{ when } |x| > 1 \end{cases}$ , then the domain of $\frac{d}{dx} f(x)$ is {'a': '$\\{r-\\{-1,1\\}\\}$', 'b': '$r-(-1,1)$', 'c': '$r-[-1,1]$', 'd': '$r-\\{-1\\}$'} 2022 2022-07-08 shift_1 mathematics   63 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: 👈: video solution $f(x) = \begin{cases} \tan^{-1}x, & \text{ when }|x|<1 \\ \frac{1}{2}(|x|-1), & \text{ when }|x|>1 \end{cases}$ $= \begin{cases} \frac{1}{2}(x-1), & \text{ when } x>1 \\ \tan^{-1}, & \text{ when } -1 < x<1 \\ \frac{1}{2}(-x-1), & \text{ when } x<-1 \end{cases}$ $f'(x) = \begin{cases} \frac{1}{2}, & \text{ when } x>1 \\ \frac{1}{1+x^2}, & \text{ when } -1 < x<1 \\ \frac{-1}{2}, & \text{ when } x<-1 \end{cases}$ $\lim\limits_{x\to -1^{-}} f'(x) = \frac{-1}{2}$ $\lim\limits_{x\to -1^{+}} f'(x) = \lim\limits_{x\to -1^{+}} \frac{1}{1+x^2} = \frac{1}{2}$ ∴ $f(x)$ is not differentiable at $-1$ $\lim\limits_{x\to -1^{+}} f'(x) = \frac{1}{2}$ $\lim\limits_{x\to -1^{-}} f'(x) = \lim\limits_{x\to -1^{-}} \frac{1}{1+x^2} = \frac{1}{2}$ $f(x)$ is differentiable at $x=1$ ∴ $f'(-1)$ does not exist. ∴ the domain of the function is $r-(-1)$ . © examsnet.com

search_text: if $x=a\cos^{3}\theta, y=a\sin^{3}\theta$ , then $\frac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}}$ at $\theta=\frac{\pi}{4}$ is {'a': '$\\frac{4\\sqrt{2}}{3a}$', 'b': '$\\frac{2}{3a}$', 'c': '$\\frac{2\\sqrt{2}}{3a}$', 'd': '$\\frac{7\\sqrt{2}}{3a}$'} 2022 2022-07-08 shift_1 mathematics   64 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: 👈: video solution given, $x=a\cos^{3}\theta$ $\frac{dx}{d\theta}=3a\cos^{2}\theta(-\sin\theta)$ and $y=a\sin^{3}\theta$ similarly, $\frac{dy}{d\theta}=3a\sin^{2}\theta\cos\theta$ $\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{\frac{dy}{d\theta}}{\frac{dx}{d\theta}}=\frac{3a\sin^{2}\theta\cos\theta}{-3a\cos^{2}\theta\sin\theta}=-\tan\theta$ again differenciating w.rt.x, $\frac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}}=-\sec^{2}\theta\times\frac{d\theta}{dx}$ $=-\sec^{2}\theta\times\frac{1}{-3a\cos^{2}\theta\sin\theta}$ $=\frac{\csc\theta\sec^{4}\theta}{3a}$ $\left.\frac{d^{2}y}{dx^{2}}\right|_{\theta=\frac{\pi}{4}}=\frac{\sqrt{2}\times4}{3a}=\frac{4\sqrt{2}}{3a}$ © examsnet.com

search_text: at $x=0, f(x)={\cos x-1}+\frac{x^{2}}{2}-\frac{x^{2}}{3}$ {'a': 'has a minimum value', 'b': 'has a maximum value', 'c': 'has no extremum value', 'd': 'is not defined'} 2022 2022-07-08 shift_1 mathematics   68 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: 👈: video solution $f(x) = \cos x - 1 + \frac{x^2}{2} - \frac{x^3}{3}$ $f'(x) = -\sin x + \frac{2x}{2} - \frac{3x^2}{3} = -\sin x + x - x^2$ $f'(x) = 0, \text{ when } x = 0$ $f''(x) = -\cos x + 1 - 2x$ $f''(0) = -\cos 0 + 1 - 2 \times 0$ $= -1 + 1 - 0 = 0$ ∵ $0$ has no extremum value. © examsnet.com

search_text: the minimum value of $\left(1+\frac{1}{\sin^{n}\alpha}\right)\left(1+\frac{1}{\cos^{n}\alpha}\right)$ is is {'a': '$1$', 'b': '$2$', 'c': '$(1+2^{n})^{2}$', 'd': '$(1+2^{n/2})^{2}$'} 2022 2022-07-08 shift_1 mathematics   69 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: 👈: video solution let $y = \left(1+\frac{1}{\sin^{n}\alpha}\right)\left(1+\frac{1}{\cos^{n}\alpha}\right)$ $y = 1 + \frac{1}{\sin^{n}\alpha} + \frac{1}{\cos^{n}\alpha} + \frac{1}{\sin^{n}\alpha \cos^{n}\alpha}$ $y = 1 + \sin^{-n}\alpha + \cos^{-n}\alpha + \sin^{-n}\alpha \cos^{-n}\alpha$ $\frac{dy}{d\alpha} = \frac{-n}{\sin^{n+1}\alpha} \cos \alpha + \frac{n}{\cos^{n+1}\alpha} \sin \alpha + \frac{1}{\sin^{n}\alpha} \left[ \frac{n}{\sin^{n+1}\alpha} \sin \alpha \right]$ $+ \frac{1}{\cos^{n}\alpha} \left[ \frac{-n}{\sin^{n+1}\alpha} \cos \alpha \right]$ $= \frac{-n \cos \alpha}{\sin^{n+1}\alpha} \left(1+\frac{1}{\cos^{n}\alpha}\right) + \frac{n \sin \alpha}{\cos^{n+1}\alpha} \left(1+\frac{1}{\sin^{n}\alpha}\right)$ $\frac{dy}{dx} = 0, \text{ where } \alpha = \frac{\pi}{4}$ $y$ at $\alpha = \frac{\pi}{4} = (1+\sqrt{2^n})^2 (1+\sqrt{2})^2$ $= (1+\sqrt{2^n})^2 = (1+2^{n/2})^2$ © examsnet.com

search_text: $0 < x < 1, \int \frac{dx}{\sqrt{x^{2} - x^{5}}} = \frac{1}{3} \log |f(x)| + c$ , then $f\left(\frac{1}{2}\right) =$ {'a': '$\\; \\frac{\\sqrt{8} - \\sqrt{7}}{\\sqrt{8} + \\sqrt{7}}$', 'b': '$\\; \\frac{\\sqrt{8} + \\sqrt{7}}{\\sqrt{8} - \\sqrt{7}}$', 'c': '$2(\\sqrt{8} - \\sqrt{7})$', 'd': '$2(\\sqrt{8} - \\sqrt{7})^{2}$'} 2022 2022-07-08 shift_1 mathematics   71 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: 👈: video solution let $i = \int \frac{dx}{\sqrt{x^{2} - x^{5}}}$ $i = \int \frac{1}{x \sqrt{1 - x^{3}}} dx$ let $x^{3} = \sin^{2} t$ $3 x^{2} dx = 2 \sin t \cos t dt$ $\rightarrow i = \frac{1}{3} \int \frac{3 x^{2} dx}{x^{3} \sqrt{1 - x^{3}}}$ $= \frac{2}{3} \int \frac{1}{\sin^{2} t \cos t} \sin t \cos t dt$ $= \frac{2}{3} \int \csc t dt$ $= \frac{2}{3} \log |\csc t - \cot t| + c$ $= \frac{2}{3} \log \left| \frac{1 - \cos t}{\sin t} \right| + c$ $= \frac{2}{3} \log \left| \frac{1 - \sqrt{1 - \sin^{2} t}}{\sqrt{\sin^{2} t}} \right| + c$ $= \frac{1}{3} \log \left( \left| \frac{1 - \sqrt{1 - x^{3}}}{\sqrt{x^{3}}} \right|^{2} \right) + c$ here, $f(x) = \left| \frac{1 - \sqrt{1 - x^{3}}}{\sqrt{x^{3}}} \right|^{2}$ $f\left(\frac{1}{2}\right) = \left| \frac{1 - \sqrt{1 - \left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{3}}}{\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{3/2}} \right|^{2}$ $= \left( \frac{1 - \frac{\sqrt{7}}{\sqrt{8}}}{\frac{1}{\sqrt{8}}} \right)^{2} = (\sqrt{8} - \sqrt{7})^{2}$ from option (a) $\colon \left( \frac{\sqrt{8} - \sqrt{7}}{\sqrt{8} + \sqrt{7}} \right) \times \left( \frac{\sqrt{8} - \sqrt{7}}{\sqrt{8} - \sqrt{7}} \right)$ $= (\sqrt{8} - \sqrt{7})^{2}$ © examsnet.com

search_text: $\int (1+x) \log (1+x^{2}) \, dx = \left( x + \;\frac{x^{2}}{2} + \;\frac{1}{2} \right) \log (1+x^{2}) + g(x) + c$ , then $g(x)=$ {'a': '$-2x - \\;\\frac{x^{2}}{2} + 2 \\tan^{-1} x$', 'b': '$2 \\tan^{-1} x + \\;\\frac{x^{2}}{2} + \\;\\frac{x^{3}}{3}$', 'c': '$2 \\tan^{-1} x - \\;\\frac{x^{2}}{2} + 3x$', 'd': '$2 \\tan^{-1} x + 3x + \\;\\frac{x^{3}}{2}$'} 2022 2022-07-08 shift_1 mathematics   73 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: 👈: video solution let $i = \int (1+x) \log (1+x^{2}) \, dx$ using by parts $\log (1+x^{2}) \left[ \frac{x^{2}}{2} + x \right] - \int \frac{2x}{1+x^{2}} \times \left( \frac{x^{2}}{2} + x \right) \, dx$ $= \left( \frac{x^{2}}{2} + x \right) \log (1+x^{2}) - \int \frac{x^{2} (x+2)}{1+x^{2}} \, dx$ $= \left( \frac{x^{2}}{2} + x \right) \log (1+x^{2}) - \int \frac{x^{3} + 2x^{2}}{1+x^{2}} \, dx$ $= \left( \frac{x^{2}}{2} + x \right) \log (1+x^{2}) - \int (x+2) - \frac{x+2}{1+x^{2}} \, dx$ $= \left( \frac{x^{2}}{2} + x \right) \log (1+x^{2}) - \left( \frac{x^{2}}{2} + 2x \right) + \frac{1}{2} \int \frac{2x}{1+x^{2}} \, dx$ $+ 2 \int \frac{1}{1+x^{2}} \, dx$ $= \left( \frac{x^{2}}{2} + x \right) \log (1+x^{2}) - \frac{x^{2}}{2} - 2x +$ $\frac{1}{2} \log (1+x^{2})$ $+ 2 \tan^{-1} x$ $= \left( \frac{x^{2}}{2} + x + \frac{1}{2} \right) \log (1+x^{2}) - \frac{x^{2}}{2} - 2x + 2 \tan^{-1} x + c$ $\text{compare i with } \left( x + \frac{x^{2}}{2} + \frac{1}{2} \right)$ $\log (1+x^{2}) + g(x) + c, \text{ we get }$ $g(x) = -2x - \frac{x^{2}}{2} + 2 \tan^{-1} x$ © examsnet.com

search_text: $\int\limits_{0}^{2\pi} \cos m x \cos n x dx + \int\limits_{-\pi}^{\pi} \sin m x \cos n x dx =$ {'a': '0 . if $m=n$ and $m, n \\in z$', 'b': '$\\pi$ if $m=n, m, n \\in z$', 'c': '$\\pi$ if $m \\neq n, m, n \\in z$', 'd': '$2 \\pi \\forall m, n \\in r$'} 2022 2022-07-08 shift_1 mathematics   75 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: 👈: video solution when, $m=n, m \in z$ let $i = \int\limits_{0}^{2\pi} \cos^{2}(m x) \, dx + \frac{1}{2} \int\limits_{-\pi}^{\pi} 2 \sin(m x) \cos(m x) \, dx$ $\int\limits_{0}^{2\pi} \cos^2 m x dx + \frac{1}{2} \int\limits_{-\pi}^{\pi} \sin 2 m x dx$ using the formula. $\int\limits_{0}^{2a} f(x) = \begin{cases} 2\int\limits_{0}^{a} f(x) dx & \text{if } f(2a-x)=f(x) \\ 0 & \text{if } f(2a-x)=-f(x) \end{cases}$ and $\int\limits_{-a}^{a} f(x) = \begin{cases} 2\int\limits_{0}^{a} f(x) dx & \text{if } f(-x)=f(x) \\ 0 & \text{if } f(-x)=-f(x) \end{cases}$ $i = 2 \int\limits_{0}^{\pi} \cos^2 m x dx + 0$ $= \int_{0}^{\pi} (1 + \cos 2 m x) \, dx$ $= \left[ x + \frac{\sin 2 m x}{2 m} \right]_0^{\pi} = \pi$ © examsnet.com

search_text: a $1 \text{ kg}$ box placed at the origin starts sliding along $x$ -axis under the action of a force $\overset{\rightarrow}{f} = f \hat{i}$ . its acceleration as a function of $x$ is given by $a(x) = \beta \cdot x$ where $\beta = 5 \text{ s}^{-2}$ . the work done by $\overset{\rightarrow}{f}$ in moving the box from $x = 2 \text{ cm}$ to $x = 5 \text{ cm}$ in joule is {'a': '$52.5 \\times 10^{-4}$', 'b': '$105.5 \\times 10^{-4}$', 'c': '$17.0 \\times 10^{-4}$', 'd': '$34.0 \\times 10^{-4}$'} 2022 2022-07-08 shift_1 physics   88 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: given, force on block, $\text{bo} f = f \hat{i}$ acceleration of block, $a = \beta \cdot x = 5 x$ now, let instantaneous velocity of block is $v$ , then $\frac{d v}{d t} = a$ $\rightarrow \rightarrow \frac{d v}{d x} \frac{d x}{d t} = a$ $\rightarrow v \frac{d v}{d x} = a$ $\text{ or } v d v = a d x$ now, integrating between limits $x_1 = 2 \times 10^{-2} \text{ m}$ to $x_2 = 5 \times 10^{-2} \text{ m}$ $\rightarrow \int_{v_1}^{v_2} v \cdot d v = \int\limits_{x_1}^{x_2} 5 x \cdot d x$ $\rightarrow \left[ \frac{v^2}{2} \right]_{v_1}^{v_2} = \frac{5}{2} \left[ x^2 \right]_{x_1}^{x_2}$ $\rightarrow \frac{1}{2} (v_2^2 - v_1^2) = \frac{5}{2} (x_2^2 - x_1^2)$ here, $x_1 = 2 \text{ cm}$ and $x_2 = 5 \text{ cm}$ so $\rightarrow \frac{1}{2} (v_2^2 - v_1^2) = \frac{5}{2} (5^2 - 2^2) \times (10^{-2})^2$ multiplying with mass of body $m = 1 \text{ kg}$ , we get $\frac{1}{2} m (v_2^2 - v_1^2) = \frac{5}{2} \times m \times 21 \times 10^{-2}$ $\rightarrow$ change in kinetic energy $= \frac{5}{2} \times 1 \times 21 \times (10^{-2})^2 = 525 \times 10^{-4}$ as change in $ke = \text{work done}$ $\therefore \text{work done} = 52.5 \times 10^{-4} \text{ j}$ © examsnet.com

search_text: a body is located at $(1.1, 0.1)\,\text{m}$ and experiences a force of $2\,\text{n}$ in the direction $\hat{i} + \hat{j}$ . the torque acting on the body in $n - m$ is {'a': '$(-\\sqrt{2} \\hat{i} + \\sqrt{2} \\hat{j})$', 'b': '$(-\\hat{i} + \\hat{j})$', 'c': '$(\\hat{i} - \\hat{j})$', 'd': '$(\\sqrt{2} \\hat{i} + \\sqrt{2} \\hat{j})$'} 2022 2022-07-08 shift_1 physics   89 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: torque on a particle, $\tau = \vec{r} \times \vec{f}$ $\vec{r} =$ position vector of particle $\vec{f} =$ force vector as particle is located at $(1,1,1)$ m; position vector of particle, $\vec{r} = x \hat{i} + y \hat{j} + z \hat{k} = (\hat{i} + \hat{j} + \hat{k})\,\text{m}$ and direction of force is along vector $(\hat{i} + \hat{j})$ hence, unit vector in direction of force, $\hat{n} = \frac{\hat{i} + \hat{j}}{\sqrt{2}}$ force in vector form, $\vec{f} = \text{magnitude} \times \text{direction}$ $= 2 \hat{n}$ $= 2 \frac{\hat{i} + \hat{j}}{\sqrt{2}} = \sqrt{2} (\hat{i} + \hat{j}) \,\text{n}$ so torque, $\tau = \vec{r} \times \vec{f}$ $= \begin{vmatrix} \hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k} \\ 1 & 1 & 1 \\ \sqrt{2} & \sqrt{2} & 0 \end{vmatrix}$ $= \hat{i}(1 \times 0 - \sqrt{2} \times 1) - \hat{j}(1 \times 0 - \sqrt{2} \times 1)$ $+ \hat{k}(1 \times \sqrt{2} - \sqrt{2} \times 1)$ $= -\sqrt{2} \hat{i} + \sqrt{2} \hat{j} + 0 \hat{k}$ $\text{torque} = (-\sqrt{2} \hat{i} + \sqrt{2} \hat{j})\,\text{n-m}$ © examsnet.com

search_text: the moment of inertia of a thin uniform rectangular plate of mass ' $m$ ', having length ' $a$ ' and width ' $b$ ' about an axis perpendicular to the plane of the plate and passing through one of its vertices is {'a': '$\\frac{2}{3} mab$', 'b': '$\\frac{1}{3} mab$', 'c': '$\\frac{2}{3} m (a^{2}+b^{2})$', 'd': '$\\frac{1}{3} m (a^{2}+b^{2})$'} 2022 2022-07-08 shift_1 physics   90 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: for a rectangular lamina moment of inertia about its centroidal axis given by $i_{cm}=\frac{v_c}{12}(a^2+b^2)$ now, moment of inertia of lamina about an axis passing through one of vertices is obtained by using parallel axis theorem. now, moment of inertia about any vertex, $i_{\text{corner}}=i_{cm}+m \cdot d^2$ $d=$ distance between axes $i_{\text{corner}}=\frac{m}{12}(a^2+b^2)+m d^2$ now from diagram, $d^2=\left(\frac{a}{2}\right)^2+\left(\frac{b}{2}\right)^2$ $i_{\text{corner}}=\frac{m}{12}(a^2+b^2)+m \left(\frac{a^2+b^2}{4}\right)$ $=m \left(\frac{a^2+a l^2+b^2+3b^2}{12}\right)$ $=m \left(\frac{4(a^2+b^2)}{12}\right)$ $=m \left(\frac{a^2+b^2}{3}\right)=\frac{1}{3}m(a^2+b^2)$ © examsnet.com

search_text: a block of $10\text{ kg}$ mass is connected to the top of a frictionless inclined plane of inclination $45^{\circ}$ by a spring of negligible mass, unstretched length $0.8\text{ m}$ and spring constant $100\sqrt{2}\text{ nm}^{-1}$ . then the distance of the block from the top along the incline in the equilibrium position is (acceleration due to gravity $=10\,\text{m}\,\text{s}^{-2}$ ) {'a': '$0.9\\text{ m}$', 'b': '$1.1\\text{ m}$', 'c': '$1.3\\text{ m}$', 'd': '$1.5\\text{ m}$'} 2022 2022-07-08 shift_1 physics   91 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: the given situation is given below : block stops when net force on block is zero. $\rightarrow$ component of weight along incline $=$ spring force $\rightarrow m g \sin\theta=k x$ substituting $m=10\text{ kg},\theta=45^{\circ}$ $k=100\sqrt{2}\text{ nm}^{-1}$ , we get $10\times10\times\sin45^{\circ}=100\sqrt{2}\times x$ $\rightarrow x=0.5\text{ m}$ as, unstretched length of spring is $0.8\text{ m}$ , total length of spring (or distance of block from top) in equilibrium, $l=0.5+0.8=1.3\text{ m}$ © examsnet.com

The sphere is made to execute SHM by stretching through a distance and released, then the time period of such oscillation is (K= spring constant
search_text: a solid sphere of mass $m$ and radius $r$ is attached to a spring of negligible mass kept on a horizontal plane such that it can roll without slipping. the sphere is made to execute shm by stretching through a distance and released, then the time period of such oscillation is (k= spring constant {'a': '$2\\pi \\sqrt{\\;\\frac{3m}{2k}}$', 'b': '$2\\pi \\sqrt{\\;\\frac{5k}{7m}}$', 'c': '$2\\pi \\sqrt{\\;\\frac{7m}{5k}}$', 'd': '$2\\pi \\sqrt{\\;\\frac{3k}{2m}}$'} 2022 2022-07-08 shift_1 physics   92 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: let at some extension $x$ centre of sphere has a speed $v$ and angular speed of rotation of sphere be $\omega$ . then total energy of system, $e=$ rotational energy + translational energy + spring energy $\rightarrow e=\frac{1}{2}i\omega^2+\frac{1}{2}mv^2+\frac{1}{2}kx^2$ $\text{ for sphere, } i=\frac{2}{5}mr^2$ also no ship condition is, $v=r\omega$ so, total energy, $e=\frac{1}{2}mv^2+\frac{1}{2}\cdot\frac{2}{5}mr^2\left(\frac{v}{r}\right)^2+\frac{1}{2}kx^2$ as total energy remains constant, $\frac{de}{dt}=0$ $\rightarrow \frac{d}{dx} \left\{ \frac{1}{2}mv^2+\frac{1}{5}mv^2+\frac{1}{2}kx^2 \right\} =0$ $\rightarrow \frac{d}{dt} \left( \frac{7}{10}mv^2+\frac{1}{2}kx^2 \right) =0$ $\rightarrow \frac{7}{10}m \cdot 2v \frac{dv}{dt} + \frac{1}{2}k \cdot 2x \frac{dx}{dt} =0$ $\rightarrow \frac{7}{5}m v a + \frac{kx}{2} v =0 \rightarrow a = -\frac{5}{7} \frac{k}{m} \cdot x$ as, acceleration $\propto$ - displacement so, motion is $\text{shm}$ . hence, $\omega^2 = \frac{5}{7} \frac{k}{m}$ time period of oscillation, $\rightarrow t = \frac{2\pi}{\omega} = 2\pi \sqrt{ \frac{7}{5} \frac{m}{k} }$ © examsnet.com

question: The escape speed of an object on the surface of the earth is $V$ . If the object is thrown out with speed $4 V$ from the surface of the earth. the speed of the object far away from the earth is
search_text: the escape speed of an object on the surface of the earth is $v$ . if the object is thrown out with speed $4 v$ from the surface of the earth. the speed of the object far away from the earth is {'a': '$3 v$', 'b': '$\\sqrt{15} v$', 'c': '$2.5 v$', 'd': '$\\sqrt{8} v$'} 2022 2022-07-08 shift_1 physics   93 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: given, $v=$ escape speed so, $v_{\text{escape}}=v=\sqrt{\frac{g m}{r} \times 2}$ $...(i)$ $m=$ mass of earth, $r=$ radius of earth now, when an object is projected with speed $4 v$ from surface of earth, let its speed at infinity is $v^{'}$ then by energy conservation, $\text{initial energy}=\text{final energy}$ $\rightarrow -\frac{g m m}{r}+\frac{1}{2}m(4v)^2=0+\frac{1}{2}m(v^{'})^2$ $\rightarrow \frac{-g m m}{r}+16\left(\frac{1}{2} m v^2\right)=\frac{1}{2} m v^2$ $...(ii)$ substituting value of $v$ from eq. (i) in eq. (ii), we get $\frac{-g m m}{r}+16\left(\frac{1}{2} m \frac{g m \times 2}{r}\right)=\frac{1}{2} m (v^{'})^2$ $\rightarrow \frac{15 g m m}{r}=\frac{1}{2} m (v^{'})^2$ $\rightarrow v'^{2}=15 \times \frac{2 g m}{r}$ $\rightarrow v'^{2}=15 \times v^2$ $\ldots \left[\therefore v^2=\frac{2 g m}{r}\right]$ $\rightarrow v'=\sqrt{15} \cdot v$ © examsnet.com

question: The work done in stretching a spring of natural length $25\ \text{cm}$ and spring constant $50\ \text{Nm}^{-1}$ from $50\ \text{cm}$ to $60\ \text{cm}$ is
search_text: the work done in stretching a spring of natural length $25\ \text{cm}$ and spring constant $50\ \text{nm}^{-1}$ from $50\ \text{cm}$ to $60\ \text{cm}$ is {'a': '$1.5\\ \\text{j}$', 'b': '$2\\ \\text{j}$', 'c': '$3.5\\ \\text{j}$', 'd': '$5\\ \\text{j}$'} 2022 2022-07-08 shift_1 physics   94 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: when a spring is stretched from some initial extension $x_i$ to some final extension $x_f$ , then work done in stretching $=$ change in potential energy of spring. work done, $w=\delta u$ $=\;\frac{1}{2} k (x_f^2-x_i^2)$ here, $k=50\ \text{n}/\text{m},\ x_f=60\ \text{cm}=60\times 10^{-2}\ \text{m}$ $x_i=50\ \text{cm}=50\times 10^{-2}\ \text{m}$ so, work done $w=\frac{1}{2}\times 50\left[(60\times 10^{-2})^2-(50\times 10^{-2})^2\right]$ $\rightarrow w=\frac{1}{2}\times 50\times 10^{-4}(3600-2500)$ $=1.5\ \text{j}$ © examsnet.com

question: The surface tension and vapour pressure of a liquid at $25^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ are $8 \times 10^{-2} \ \mathrm{Nm}^{-1}$ and $2.5 \times 10^{3} \ \mathrm{Pa}$ respectively. The radius of the smallest spherical water droplet which can form without evaporating at $25^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ is
search_text: the surface tension and vapour pressure of a liquid at $25^{\circ} \mathrm{c}$ are $8 \times 10^{-2} \ \mathrm{nm}^{-1}$ and $2.5 \times 10^{3} \ \mathrm{pa}$ respectively. the radius of the smallest spherical water droplet which can form without evaporating at $25^{\circ} \mathrm{c}$ is {'a': '$64 \\mu\\mathrm{m}$', 'b': '$30 \\mu\\mathrm{m}$', 'c': '$60 \\mu\\mathrm{m}$', 'd': '$3 \\mu\\mathrm{m}$'} 2022 2022-07-08 shift_1 physics   95 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: for evaporation water pressure (excess pressure due to surface tension) is greater than vapor pressure. $\rightarrow$ excess pressure in drop $\geq$ vapor pressure $\rightarrow \frac{2 t}{r} \geq p$ where, $t=$ surface tension $p=$ vapor pressure $r=$ radius of drop $\rightarrow r=\frac{2 t}{p}$ here, surface tension, $t=8 \times 10^{-2} \ \text{n/m}$ vapor pressure, $p=25 \times 10^{3} \ \mathrm{pa}$ hence, radius of drop $r=\frac{2 \times 8 \times 10^{-2}}{25 \times 10^{3}}$ $\rightarrow r=\frac{16}{25} \times 10^{-4} \ \mathrm{m}$ $\rightarrow r=64 \times 10^{-6} \ \mathrm{m}=64 \mu\mathrm{m}$ © examsnet.com

question: A body of volume $V$ floats on water with $\;\frac{1}{3}$ of its volume above the surface. The volume of the object above the surface when floating on a liquid of specific gravity $1.5$ is
search_text: a body of volume $v$ floats on water with $\;\frac{1}{3}$ of its volume above the surface. the volume of the object above the surface when floating on a liquid of specific gravity $1.5$ is {'a': '$\\;\\frac{3 v}{8}$', 'b': '$\\;\\frac{4 v}{9}$', 'c': '$\\;\\frac{5 v}{9}$', 'd': '$\\;\\frac{2 v}{3}$'} 2022 2022-07-08 shift_1 physics   96 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: in water, by archimedes principle, weight $=$ upthrust weight of fluid displaced $=$ volume inside water $\rightarrow m g = \frac{2}{3} v \cdot \rho_w \cdot g \times p_w \times g$ $\dots(i)$ let $x$ part of volume be above surface in liquid of density $\rho$ then, $m g = (1-x) v \cdot \rho \cdot g$ $\dots(ii)$ $\rightarrow (1-x) v \rho g = \frac{2}{3} v \rho_w g$ $\rightarrow 1-x = \frac{2}{3} \cdot \frac{\rho_w}{\rho} = \frac{2}{3} \times \left( \frac{1}{\text{ specific gravity }} \right)$ as, specific gravity $= \frac{\rho_{\text{fluid }}}{\rho_{\text{water }}}$ here, specific gravity $=1.5$ hence, $x = \frac{2}{3 \times 1.5} = \frac{4}{9}$ $v - \frac{4}{9} v = \frac{5}{9} v$ part of volume of object lies above the surface of liquid. © examsnet.com

question: The change in density of mercury, when it is heated from $10^{\circ}\,\mathrm{C}$ to $60^{\circ}\,\mathrm{C}$ is (The coefficient of volume expansion of mercury is $18.2 \times 10^{-5} \, \mathrm{K}^{-1}$ )
search_text: the change in density of mercury, when it is heated from $10^{\circ}\,\mathrm{c}$ to $60^{\circ}\,\mathrm{c}$ is (the coefficient of volume expansion of mercury is $18.2 \times 10^{-5} \, \mathrm{k}^{-1}$ ) {'a': '$1.82\\%$', 'b': '$0.91\\%$', 'c': '$9.1\\%$', 'd': '$0.45\\%$'} 2022 2022-07-08 shift_1 physics   97 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: as density $\propto \frac{1}{\text{volume}}$ or $\rho \propto \frac{1}{v}$ $\rightarrow \frac{\rho'}{\rho} = \frac{v'}{v'} = \frac{v}{v + r v \delta \theta} \rightarrow \rho' = \rho \left( \frac{1}{1 + r \delta \theta} \right)$ $\rightarrow \rho' \approx \rho (1 + r \delta \theta)^{-1} \rightarrow \rho' = \rho (1 - r \delta \theta)$ $\text{here, } r = 18.2 \times 10^{-5} \, \mathrm{k}^{-1} \text{.}$ $\text{and } \delta \theta = 60 - 10 = 50 \, \mathrm{k}$ $\rightarrow \frac{\rho'}{\rho} = 1 - (18.2 \times 10^{-5} \times 50)$ $= 0.9909$ so, percentage change in density, $\rightarrow \left( \frac{\rho'}{\rho} - 1 \right) \times 100 = \frac{\rho' - \rho}{\rho} \times 100$ $\rightarrow \frac{\delta \rho}{\rho} \times 100$ $= (0.9909 - 1) \times 100$ $= 0.0091 \times 100 = 0.91\%$ © examsnet.com
