search_text: temperature of a cold reservoir of a carnot engine is $127^{\circ}  \mathrm{c}$ . if the efficiency of the carnot engine is $20\%$ , then the temperature of the hot reservoir is {'a': '$500^{\\circ}  \\mathrm{c}$', 'b': '$227^{\\circ}  \\mathrm{c}$', 'c': '$273^{\\circ}  \\mathrm{c}$', 'd': '$400^{\\circ}  \\mathrm{c}$'} 2022 2022-07-08 shift_1 physics   98 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: efficiency of a carnot engine is given by, $\eta=1-\frac{t_2}{t_1}$ $t_2=\text{ temperature of sink }$ $t_1=\text{ temperature of source }$ here, $t_2=127^{\circ}  \mathrm{c}=127+273=400  \mathrm{k}$ and so $\frac{20}{100}=1-\frac{400}{t_1}$ $\rightarrow \frac{400}{t_1}=\frac{80}{100}$ $\rightarrow t_1=\frac{400 \times 100}{80}=500  \mathrm{k}$ or $\text{''}t_1=500-273=227^{\circ}  \mathrm{c}$ © examsnet.com

search_text: two boxes are at the same temperature. the first box contains gas with molecular mass $m_{1}$ and $r m s$ speed $v_{1}$ . the second box contains gas with molecular mass $m_{2}$ and average speed $v_{2}$ . if $v_{1}=1.5 v_{2}$ , then $\;\frac{m_{1}}{m_{2}}$ is {'a': '$1.25$', 'b': '$0.74$', 'c': '$0.52$', 'd': '$0.26$'} 2022 2022-07-08 shift_1 physics   100 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: $\text{r . m. s}$ speed is given by $v_{\text{rms}}=v_1=\sqrt{\;\frac{3rt}{m}}$ average speed is given by, $v_{\text{avg}}=v_2=\sqrt{\;\frac{8}{\pi}\cdot\frac{rt}{m}}$ $\;\text{given,}\;\;v_1=1.5 v_2$ $\rightarrow (v_1)^2=(1.5)^2\cdot v_2^2$ $\rightarrow \frac{3rt}{m_1}=\frac{9}{4}\cdot\frac{8}{\pi}\cdot\frac{rt}{m_2}$ $\rightarrow \frac{m_1}{m_2}=\frac{3\times4\times\pi}{9\times8}=\frac{\pi}{6}$ $\rightarrow \frac{m_1}{m_2}=0.52$ © examsnet.com

If the horizontal component of earth's magnetic field $=3.2 \times 10^{-5}\ \text{T}$ , then the pole strength of magnet is
search_text: a bar magnet of length $16\ \text{cm}$ is placed in the magnetic meridian with the $\text{n}$ - pole pointing towards geographical north. two neutral points separated by $12\ \text{cm}$ are obtained on the equatorial line of the magnet. if the horizontal component of earth's magnetic field $=3.2 \times 10^{-5}\ \text{t}$ , then the pole strength of magnet is {'a': '$0.25\\ \\text{am}$', 'b': '$0.5\\ \\text{am}$', 'c': '$1\\ \\text{am}$', 'd': '$2\\ \\text{am}$'} 2022 2022-07-08 shift_1 physics   107 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: the given situation is shown below. note earth's field goes from south to north: at neutral point horizontal component of earth, is opposed by field of magnet so, at neutral point, $b_h=b_{\text{magnet}}$ ⇒ $b_h = \frac{\mu_0}{4\pi} \cdot \frac{m}{r^3}$ where, $m=$ magnetic dipole moment of magnet and $r=$ distance of neutral point from centre of magnet here, $b_h = 3.2\times 10^{-5}\text{t}$ $r-6\ \text{cm}=6\times 10^{-2}\ \text{m}$ hence, $3.2 \times 10^{-5} = 10^{-7} \times \frac{m}{(6 \times 10^{-2})^3}$ ⇒ $m=\frac{3.2 \times 10^{-5} \times 216 \times 10^{-6}}{10^{-7}}$ $=6. \times 10^{-2}\ \text{a-m}^2$ if length of magnet is taken $2l$ , then $m=m \cdot 2l$ , (∵ m= pole strength) here, $2l=16\ \text{cm}=16\times 10^{-2}\ \text{m}$ ⇒ $6.9 \times 10^{-2} = m \times 16 \times 10^{-2}$ ⇒ $m = \frac{6.9}{16} = 0.43\ \text{a-m} \simeq 0.5\ \text{a-m}$ © examsnet.com

question: Two long wires carrying current is $8 A$ and $6 A$ along $x$ axes and $y$ axes respectively. The magnetic field at the point $(2\hat{i}+4\hat{j})$ is (Take $\mu_{0}=4\pi \times 10^{-7}$ SI unit)
search_text: two long wires carrying current is $8 a$ and $6 a$ along $x$ axes and $y$ axes respectively. the magnetic field at the point $(2\hat{i}+4\hat{j})$ is (take $\mu_{0}=4\pi \times 10^{-7}$ si unit) {'a': '$1 \\times 10^{-6} \\,\\text{t}$', 'b': '$2 \\times 10^{-6} \\,\\text{t}$', 'c': '$1 \\times 10^{-7} \\,\\text{t}$', 'd': '$2 \\times 10^{-7} \\,\\text{t}$'} 2022 2022-07-08 shift_1 physics   110 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: the situation given can be shown as magnetic field at some point $p$ with position vector $r$ due to a straight long current carrying wire is given by $b=\frac{\mu_0 i}{2\pi d}$ where, $d=$ perpendicular distance of point from wire. here, $r=2\hat{i}+4\hat{j}\,\text{m}$ ⇒ for wire on x - axis, $d=d_x=4\,\text{m}$ and for wire on y-axis $d=d_y=2\,\text{m}$ as magnetic fields due to wires along $x$ and along $y$ -axis are in opposite direction ( $rh$ rule) so, $b_{\text{net}} = b+b_x$ $=\frac{\mu_0 i_2}{2\pi d_y}(\hat{k}) + \frac{\mu_0 i_1}{2\pi d_x}(-\hat{k})$ $= \frac{\mu_0}{2\pi} \left(\frac{i_2}{d_y} - \frac{i_1}{d_x}\right) \hat{k}$ $= \frac{4\pi \times 10^{-7}}{2\pi} \left(\frac{6}{2} - \frac{8}{4}\right) \hat{k}$ $= 2 \times 10^{-7} \hat{k} \,\text{t}$ ∴ $\left|b_{\text{net}}\right| = 2 \times 10^{-7} \,\text{t}$ © examsnet.com

search_text: if $\alpha, \beta$ are the roots of the equation $2 x^{2}+6 x+k=0$ , then the maximum value of $\left[\;\frac{\alpha}{\beta}+\;\frac{\beta}{\alpha}\right]$ when $k < 0$ is {'a': '$0$', 'b': '$1$', 'c': '$-1$', 'd': '$-2$'} 2022 2022-07-08 shift_2 mathematics   14 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: given, $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are the roots of $2x^2 +6x +k=0$ $\rightarrow \alpha + \beta = \frac{-6}{2} = -3$ and $\alpha\beta = \frac{k}{2}$ now, $\frac{\alpha}{\beta} + \frac{\beta}{\alpha} = \frac{\alpha^2 + \beta^2}{\alpha\beta}$ $= \frac{(\alpha+\beta)^2 - 2\alpha\beta}{\alpha\beta}$ $\rightarrow \frac{\alpha}{\beta} + \frac{\beta}{\alpha} = \frac{2(9-k)}{k} = \frac{18}{k} - 2$ ∵ $k<0 \quad \left(\frac{18}{k} - 2\right) < 0, \forall k < 0$ thus, $\left[ \frac{\alpha}{\beta} + \frac{\beta}{\alpha} \right]_{\max} = \left[ \frac{18}{k} - 2 \right] = \left[ \frac{18}{k} \right] - 2 = -2$ where, $\left[ \frac{18}{k} \right] = 0$ for $k < -18$ © examsnet.com

search_text: a student is to answer 10 out of 13 questions in an examination such that he must choose at least 4 from the first five questions. the number of choices available to him is {'a': '196', 'b': '140', 'c': '168', 'd': '176'} 2022 2022-07-08 shift_2 mathematics   16 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: total number of questions $=13$ now of questions to be selected $=10$ restriction - at least 4 from first 5 questions are to be selected. case i: if exactly 4 out of first 5 questions are selected. number of ways of selecting 4 questions from 5 questions $=\binom{5}{4}=5$ remaining $10-4=6$ questions are selected from last $13-5=8$ questions in $\binom{8}{6}$ ways ∴ number of ways $=5 \times \binom{8}{6}=140$ case ii: if exactly 5 out of first 5 questions are selected. number of ways of selecting 5 out of 5 questions $=\binom{5}{5}=1$ remaining $10-5=5$ questions are selected from last $13-5=8$ questions in $\binom{8}{5}$ ways. ∴ number of ways $=1 \times \binom{8}{5}=56$ ∴ total number of ways $=140+56=196$ © examsnet.com

search_text: $\frac{x^{2}+1}{x^{4}+4} = \frac{a x+b}{x^{2}-2 x+2} + \frac{c x+d}{x^{2}+2 x+2} \rightarrow 3 a+2 b+3 c =$ {'a': '$-d$', 'b': '$d$', 'c': '$2d$', 'd': '$-2d$'} 2022 2022-07-08 shift_2 mathematics   19 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: $\frac{x^2+1}{x^4+4} = \frac{ax+b}{x^4-2x+2} + \frac{cx+d}{x^2+2x+2}$ $\rightarrow \frac{x^2+1}{x^4+4}$ $= \frac{(ax+b)(x^2+2x+2)+(cx+d)(x^2-2x+2)}{(x^2+2)-2x^2}$ $\rightarrow x^2+1 = (a+c)x^2 + (2a+b-2c+d)x^2$ $+ (2a+2b+2c-2d)x + (2b+2d)$ on comparing both sides: $a+c=0 \rightarrow a=-c, 2b+2d=1$ and $2a+b-2c+d=1$ $\rightarrow 2(a-c)+b+d=1$ $\rightarrow 4a + \frac{1}{2} = 1$ $\rightarrow 4a = 1 - \frac{1}{2} = \frac{1}{2}$ $\rightarrow a = \frac{1}{8}$ and $c = -\frac{1}{8}$ now, $2a+2b+2c-2d=0$ $\rightarrow 2(a+c) + 2(b-d) = 0$ $\rightarrow b = d$ and $2b+2d=1$ $\rightarrow 4b=1 \rightarrow b=d = \frac{1}{4}$ now, $3a+2b+3c=2b$ $\because 3a+3c=0$ $=2d$ © examsnet.com

search_text: if $1-\cot 23^{\circ} = \;\frac{x}{1-\cot 22^{\circ}}$ , then $x =$ {'a': '$1$', 'b': '$2$', 'c': '$\\;\\frac{1}{2}$', 'd': '$3$'} 2022 2022-07-08 shift_2 mathematics   20 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: given, $1-\cot 23^{\circ} = \frac{x}{1-\cot 22^{\circ}}$ $\rightarrow x = (1-\cot 23^{\circ})(1-\cot 22^{\circ})$ $\rightarrow x = \frac{\sin 23^{\circ} - \cos 23^{\circ}}{\sin 23^{\circ}} \times \frac{\sin 22^{\circ} - \cos 22^{\circ}}{\sin 22^{\circ}}$ $\rightarrow (\sin 23^{\circ} \cdot \sin 22^{\circ} + \cos 23^{\circ} \cdot \cos 22^{\circ})$ $\rightarrow x = \frac{ -(\sin 23^{\circ} \cos 22^{\circ} + \cos 23^{\circ} \sin 22^{\circ}) }{ \sin 23^{\circ} \cdot \sin 22^{\circ} }$ $\rightarrow x + \frac{ -(\sin 23^{\circ} - 22^{\circ}) - \sin (23^{\circ} + 22^{\circ}) }{ \sin 23^{\circ} \cdot \sin 22^{\circ} }$ $\rightarrow x = \frac{2(\cos 1^{\circ} - \sin 45^{\circ})}{2\sin 23^{\circ} \sin 22^{\circ}} = \frac{2\left(\cos 1^{\circ} - \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right)}{\cos 1^{\circ} - \cos 45^{\circ}}$ $\rightarrow \frac{2\left(\cos 1^{\circ} - \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right)}{\cos 1^{\circ} - \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}} = 2$ © examsnet.com

search_text: let $\tan 30^{\circ}$ and $\tan 15^{\circ}$ be the roots of the quadratic equation $x^{2}+ax+b=0$ , then $1+a-b=$ {'a': '$0$', 'b': '$1$', 'c': '$a b$', 'd': '$a^{2} b^{2}$'} 2022 2022-07-08 shift_2 mathematics   22 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: $\tan 15^{\circ}=\tan (45^{\circ}-30^{\circ})$ $=\;\frac{1-\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}}{1+\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}}=\;\frac{\sqrt{3}-1}{\sqrt{3}+1}$ given, $\tan 30^{\circ}$ and $\tan 15^{\circ}$ are the roots of the equation $x^{2}+ax+b=0$ $\;\because \;\text{sum of roots}\;=\tan 30^{\circ}+\tan 15^{\circ}=-a$ $\;\rightarrow \;\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}+\;\frac{\sqrt{3}-1}{\sqrt{3}+1}=-a$ $\;\rightarrow \;\frac{\sqrt{3}+1+3-\sqrt{3}}{\sqrt{3}(\sqrt{3}+1)}=-a \rightarrow a=\;\frac{-4}{\sqrt{3}(\sqrt{3}+1)}$ now, product of roots $=\tan 30^{\circ} \cdot \tan 15^{\circ}=b$ $\rightarrow \;\; b=\;\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}} \times \;\frac{\sqrt{3}-1}{\sqrt{3}+1} \;\text{.}\;$ now, we have to find $1+a-b$ . $\;\; \text{then,}\; 1+a-b=1-\;\frac{4}{\sqrt{3}(\sqrt{3}+1)}-\;\frac{\sqrt{3}-1}{\sqrt{3}(\sqrt{3}+1)}$ $\;=\;\frac{\sqrt{3}(\sqrt{3}+1)-4-\sqrt{3}+1}{\sqrt{3}(\sqrt{3}+1)}=\;\frac{3+\sqrt{3}-3-\sqrt{3}}{\sqrt{3}(\sqrt{3}+1)}=0$ © examsnet.com

search_text: statement 1: the eccentricity of the hyperbola $9x^{2}-16y^{2}-72x+96y-144=0$ is $\frac{5}{4}$ statement 2: the eccentricity of the hyperbola $\;\frac{x^{2}}{a^{2}}-\;\frac{y^{2}}{b^{2}}=1$ is $\sqrt{1+\;\frac{b^{2}}{a^{2}}}$ {'a': 'statement 1 is true, statement 2 is true; statement 2 is correct explanation for statement $1.$', 'b': 'both statements are true and statement 2 is not the correct explanation of statement 1 .', 'c': 'statement 1 is false; statement 2 is true.', 'd': 'statement 1 is true; statement 2 is false.'} 2022 2022-07-08 shift_2 mathematics   55 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: 👈: video solution $9x^{2}-16y^{2}-72x+96y-144=0$ $\rightarrow 9(x^{2}-8x)-16(y^{2}-6y)-144=0$ $\rightarrow 9(x^{2}-8x+16)-16(y^{2}-6y+9)-144$ $-144+144=0$ $\rightarrow 9(x-4)^{2}-16(y-3)^{2}=144$ $\rightarrow \frac{(x-4)^{2}}{4^{2}}-\frac{(y-3)^{2}}{3^{2}}=1$ here, $a=4, b=3$ $e=\sqrt{1+\frac{b^{2}}{a^{2}}}=\sqrt{1+\frac{9}{16}}=\frac{5}{4}$ $\therefore$ statement i and statement ii are true and statement ii is a correct explanation for statement i. © examsnet.com

search_text: if the coordinates of the vertices of a triangle $\text{abc}$ are $a(7,6,4), b(5,4,6)$ . $c(3,2,0)$ and the bisector of $\angle bac$ meets the side $bc$ at $d$ , then the coordinates of $d$ are {'a': '$\\left(\\;\\frac{13}{3},\\;\\frac{10}{3},4\\right)$', 'b': '$\\left(\\;\\frac{11}{3},\\;\\frac{8}{3},2\\right)$', 'c': '$(9,8,6)$', 'd': '$(7,5,3)$'} 2022 2022-07-08 shift_2 mathematics   56 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: 👈: video solution $\rightarrow \frac{ab}{ac} = \frac{bd}{cd}$ now, $ab = \sqrt{4+4+4}=2\sqrt{3}$ $ac = \sqrt{16+16+16}=4\sqrt{3}$ $\rightarrow \frac{bd}{cd} = \frac{2\sqrt{3}}{4\sqrt{3}} = \frac{1}{2}$ $\rightarrow d$ divides $bc$ in the ratio $1:2$ internally. $\rightarrow d \equiv \left(\frac{3+10}{3}, \frac{8+2}{3}, \frac{12+0}{3}\right)$ $\equiv \left(\frac{13}{3}, \frac{10}{3}, 4\right)$ © examsnet.com

search_text: $(\sqrt{x+\sqrt{12x-36}}+\sqrt{x-\sqrt{12x-36}}) dx=$ {'a': '$2\\sqrt{3}x+c,\\qquad\\forall x$', 'b': '$\\;\\frac{4(x-3)^{3/2}}{2}+c,\\forall x$', 'c': '$\\begin{cases}\\frac{4}{3}(x-3)^{3/2}+c, & \\text{if } x>6 \\\\ 2\\sqrt{3}x+c, & \\text{if } 3\\le x\\le6.\\end{cases}$', 'd': '$\\begin{cases}\\frac{4}{3}(x-3)^{3/2}+c, & \\text{if } 3\\le x\\le6 \\\\ 2\\sqrt{3}x+c, & \\text{if } x>6.\\end{cases}$'} 2022 2022-07-08 shift_2 mathematics   71 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: 👈: video solution $i=\int (\sqrt{x+\sqrt{12x-36}}+\sqrt{x-\sqrt{12x-36}}) dx$ put $t^2=12x-36$ $\rightarrow x=\frac{t^2+36}{12}$ and $2t\,dt=12\,dx \rightarrow t\,dt=6\,dx$ $i=\int \left(\sqrt{\frac{t^2+36}{12}+t}+\sqrt{\frac{t^2+36}{12}-t}\right)\left(\frac{t}{6}\right)dt$ $i=\frac{1}{6}\int \frac{(t+6)+(t-6)}{\sqrt{12}}t\,dt$ $[\text{when } t^2>36]$ $=\frac{1}{6\sqrt{12}}\int (2t)t\,dt=\frac{1}{3\sqrt{12}}\int t^2\,dt$ $=\frac{1}{3\sqrt{12}}\left(\frac{t^3}{3}\right)+c=\frac{1}{9\sqrt{12}}(12x-36)^{\frac{3}{2}}+c$ $=\frac{(12)^{3/2}}{9(12)^{1/2}}(x-3)^{3/2}+c=\frac{12}{9}(x-3)^{3/2}+c$ $=\frac{4}{3}(x-3)^{3/2}+c,\text{ if }x>6$ now, $i=\frac{1}{6\sqrt{12}}\int (t+6-(t-6))t\,dt\quad[3\le x\le6]$ $=\frac{1}{6\sqrt{12}}\int 12t\,dt=\frac{\sqrt{12}}{6}\int t\,dt$ $=\frac{\sqrt{12}}{6}\left(\frac{t^2}{2}\right)+c'=\frac{1}{\sqrt{12}}(12x-36)+c'$ $=\sqrt{12}x+\left(\frac{-36}{\sqrt{12}}+c'\right)$ $\therefore i=2\sqrt{3}x+c,$ if $3\le x\le6$ © examsnet.com

search_text: $\int\;\frac{x\,dx}{\;\sqrt[15]{(1+x^2)^{12}(2+x^2)^{18}}} = \alpha\left(\frac{1+x^2}{2+x^2}\right)^{\frac{1}{n}} + c \rightarrow \frac{n}{\alpha} =$ {'a': '6', 'b': '4', 'c': '2', 'd': '8'} 2022 2022-07-08 shift_2 mathematics   72 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: 👈: video solution $i = \int\frac{x\,dx}{\sqrt[15]{(1+x^2)^{12}(2+x^2)^{18}}}$ $= \int\frac{x\,dx}{(1+x^2)^{\frac{12}{15}}(2+x^2)^{\frac{18}{15}}}$ $= \int\frac{x\,dx}{(1+x^2)^{\frac{4}{5}}(2+x^2)^{\frac{6}{5}}}$ $= \int\frac{x\,dx}{(1+x^2)^2 \left(\frac{2+x^2}{1+x^2}\right)^{\frac{6}{5}}}$ put $u = \frac{2+x^2}{1+x^2}$ $\rightarrow du = \frac{(1+x^2)(2x) - (2+x^2)(2x)}{(1+x^2)^2}\,dx$ $\rightarrow du = \frac{2x(1+x^2-2-x^2)\,dx}{(1+x^2)^2}$ $\rightarrow du = \frac{-2x\,dx}{(1+x^2)^2}$ $\rightarrow \frac{x\,dx}{(1+x^2)^2} = -\frac{du}{2}$ then, $i = -\frac{1}{2} \int \frac{dx}{u^{\frac{6}{5}}}$ $= -\frac{1}{2} \left[ \frac{u^{-\frac{6}{5}+1}}{-\frac{6}{5}+1} \right] + c$ $= \frac{5}{2} \times u^{-\frac{1}{5}} + c$ $= \frac{5}{2} \left(\frac{1+x^2}{2+x^2}\right)^{-\frac{1}{5}} + c$ thus, $\alpha = \frac{5}{2}$ and $n = 5$ then, $\frac{n}{\alpha} = \frac{5}{\frac{5}{2}} = 2$ © examsnet.com

search_text: $\int\limits_{0}^{\infty}(x^{12}+x^{-12}) \;\frac{\log x}{x} dx=$ {'a': '0', 'b': '$1$', 'c': '$\\log 2$', 'd': '$e^{2}$'} 2022 2022-07-08 shift_2 mathematics   74 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: 👈: video solution $i = \int\limits_{0}^{\infty} (x^{12} + x^{-12}) \frac{\log x}{x^2} dx$ put $t = \frac{1}{x} \rightarrow dt = -\frac{1}{x^2} dx$ $\rightarrow -x dt = \frac{1}{x} dx \rightarrow -\frac{dt}{t} = \frac{1}{x} dx$ $\therefore i = \int\limits_{0}^{\infty} (t^{-12} + t^{12}) (-\log t) \frac{-dt}{t}$ $= \int\limits_{0}^{\infty} (t^{-12} + t^{12}) \frac{\log t}{t} dt$ $= -\int\limits_{0}^{\infty} (t^{-12} + t^{12}) \frac{\log t}{t} dt$ $i = -\int\limits_{0}^{\infty} (x^{-12} + x^{12}) \frac{\log x}{x} dx$ $2i = 0 \rightarrow i = 0$ © examsnet.com

search_text: two wires $a$ and $b$ of lengths in the ratio $1:2$ and masses in the ratio $2:1$ are stretched by same tension. the ratio of the fundamental frequencies of wires $a$ and $b$ is {'a': '$2\\sqrt{2}:1$', 'b': '$1:\\sqrt{2}$', 'c': '$1:1$', 'd': '$\\sqrt{2}:1$'} 2022 2022-07-08 shift_2 physics   101 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: fundamental frequency in a stretched wire is given as, $f=\frac{1}{2l}\sqrt{\frac{t}{\mu}},$ where, $t=\;\text{tension}\;$ $l=\;\text{length}\;$ $\mu=\;\text{mass per unit length}\;$ ratio of fundamental frequencies of wire $a$ and $b$ , $\;\frac{f_a}{f_b}\;=\;\frac{1}{2l_a}\sqrt{\;\frac{t_a}{\mu_a}\;}\times\;\frac{2l_b}{t}\sqrt{\;\frac{\mu_b}{t_b}\;}$ $\;=\;\frac{l_b}{l_a}\cdot\sqrt{\;\frac{t_a}{t_b}\;}\sqrt{\;\frac{\mu_b}{\mu_a}\;}$ here $\;\frac{l_b}{l_a}=\;\frac{2}{1}$ $\;\frac{\mu_a}{\mu_b}=\;\frac{\frac{m_a}{l_a}}{\frac{m_b}{l_b}}=\;\frac{m_a}{m_b}:\;\frac{l_b}{l_a}=\;\frac{2}{1}\times\;\frac{2}{1}\ \dots\ \left[\because\frac{m_a}{m_b}=2/1\text{ and }\frac{l_b}{l_a}=2/1\right]$ or $\frac{\mu_a}{\mu_b} = \frac{2}{1} \times \frac{2}{1} = \frac{4}{1}$ $\frac{\mu_b}{\mu_a} = \frac{1}{4}$ so, $\frac{f_a}{f_b} \cdot \frac{2}{1} \cdot \sqrt{1} \cdot \sqrt{\frac{1}{4}} = 1:1$ © examsnet.com

search_text: a radioactive element $a$ converts into another stable element $b$ . half life of $a$ is $1.5$ hrs. after time $t$ the ratio of atoms of $a$ and $b$ is found to be $1: 8$ , then $t$ in hours is {'a': '$6$', 'b': '$8$', 'c': 'between $3$ to $4.5$', 'd': 'between $4.5$ to $6$'} 2022 2022-07-08 shift_2 physics   118 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: number of atoms of $a$ and $b$ are as shown for $a \rightarrow$ $n_0 \xrightarrow{t}\;\frac{n_0}{2} \xrightarrow{t}\;\frac{n_0}{4} \xrightarrow{t}\;\frac{n_0}{8} \xrightarrow{t}\;\frac{n_0}{16} \dots$ for $b \rightarrow$ $o \xrightarrow{t}\;\frac{n_0}{2} \xrightarrow{t}\;\frac{3}{4} n_0 \xrightarrow{t}\;\frac{7}{8} n_0 \xrightarrow{t}\;\frac{15}{16} n_0 \dots$ ratio of atoms of $a$ and $b$ after one half-life, time period $=\frac{\frac{n_0}{2}}{\frac{n_0}{2}}=1$ after 2 half-life, time period $=\frac{\frac{n_0}{4}}{\frac{3 n_0}{4}}=\frac{1}{3}$ after 3 half-life, time period $=\frac{\frac{n_0}{8}}{\frac{7 n_0}{8}}=\frac{1}{7}$ after 4 half-life, time period $=\frac{\frac{n_0}{16}}{\frac{15 n_0}{16}}=\frac{1}{15}$ as $\frac{1}{7} < \frac{1}{8} < \frac{1}{15}$ ratio of $a: b$ becomes $\frac{1}{8}$ sometime between 3 half-lifes to 4 half -lifes . so, ratio becomes $1: 8$ after $3 \times 1.5$ hrs but earlier than $4 \times 1.5$ hours. © examsnet.com

search_text: if $\cot x \cot y = a$ and $x + y = \frac{\pi}{6}$ , then the quadratic equation satisfying $\cot x$ and $\cot y$ is {'a': '$t^2 + (1 - a) \\sqrt{3} t + a = 0$', 'b': '$\\sqrt{3} t^2 + (1 - a) t + a \\sqrt{3} = 0$', 'c': '$\\sqrt{3} t^2 + (a - 1) t + a \\sqrt{3} = 0$', 'd': '$2 t^2 + (a - 1) \\sqrt{3} t + a = 0$'} 2023 2023-05-15 shift_2 mathematics   19 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: let $u=\cot x$ and $v=\cot y$ . given $uv=a$ . using $\cot(x+y)=\frac{\cot x \cot y-1}{\cot x+\cot y}$ , we get $\cot\frac{\pi}{6}=\frac{a-1}{u+v}.$ since $\cot\frac{\pi}{6}=\sqrt{3}$ , $\sqrt{3}=\frac{a-1}{u+v},$ so $u+v=\frac{a-1}{\sqrt{3}}.$ the quadratic with roots $u$ and $v$ is $t^2-(u+v)t+uv=0.$ substitute the sum and product: $t^2-\frac{a-1}{\sqrt{3}}t+a=0.$ multiplying by $\sqrt{3}$ gives $\sqrt{3}t^2-(a-1)t+a\sqrt{3}=0,$ i.e. $\sqrt{3}t^2+(1-a)t+a\sqrt{3}=0.$ thus the correct option is the one with option b. © examsnet.com

subject: Chemistry
question: Which of the following amine cannot be prepared by the Gabriel phthalimide synthesis method?
search_text: which of the following amine cannot be prepared by the gabriel phthalimide synthesis method? {'a': 'ethylamine', 'b': 'benzylamine', 'c': 'phenylamine', 'd': 'propylamine'} 2023 2023-05-19 shift_1 chemistry   160 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: correct answer: phenylamine (option c) gabriel phthalimide synthesis prepares only primary amines that can be formed through an $\text{s}_\text{n}2$ reaction on an alkyl/benzylic halide. step 1: phthalimide is treated with alcoholic $\text{koh}$ to form potassium phthalimide: $\text{c}_6\text{h}_4(\text{co})_2\text{nh} + \text{koh} \rightarrow \text{c}_6\text{h}_4(\text{co})_2\text{n}^-\text{k}^+ + \text{h}_2\text{o}$ step 2: the phthalimide anion attacks an alkyl halide $r-x$ by an $\text{s}_\text{n}2$ pathway to give $n$ -alkylphthalimide. step 3: alkaline hydrolysis (or hydrazinolysis) of the $n$ -alkylphthalimide liberates the primary amine $r\text{nh}_2$ . ethylamine ( $\text{c}_2\text{h}_5\text{nh}_2$ ) comes from ethyl halide, propylamine ( $\text{c}_3\text{h}_7\text{nh}_2$ ) from propyl halide, and benzylamine ( $\text{c}_6\text{h}_5\text{ch}_2\text{nh}_2$ ) from benzyl halide. all three of these halides are $\text{sp}^3$ (or benzylic) halides that readily undergo $\text{s}_\text{n}2$ substitution, so their amines can be prepared this way. phenylamine (aniline) would require chlorobenzene to react with the phthalimide anion. in chlorobenzene the $\text{c}-\text{cl}$ bond has partial double-bond character due to resonance, and the planar aryl carbon is shielded from backside attack, so nucleophilic substitution by $\text{s}_\text{n}2$ does not occur. therefore the phthalimide anion cannot be attached to a benzene ring, and phenylamine cannot be prepared by gabriel phthalimide synthesis. phenylamine is instead prepared by reduction of nitrobenzene, e.g. $\text{c}_6\text{h}_5\text{no}_2 \xrightarrow{\text{sn/hcl}} \text{c}_6\text{h}_5\text{nh}_2$ . hence the amine that cannot be prepared by the gabriel phthalimide synthesis is phenylamine, option c. © examsnet.com

question: If a function $f: \mathbb{R} \longrightarrow \mathbb{R}$ is defined by $f(x)=x^3-x$ , then $f$ is [AP EAPCET 18 May 2024 Shift 1]
search_text: if a function $f: \mathbb{r} \longrightarrow \mathbb{r}$ is defined by $f(x)=x^3-x$ , then $f$ is [ap eapcet 18 may 2024 shift 1] {'a': 'one - one and onto', 'b': 'one - one but not onto', 'c': 'onto but not one - one', 'd': 'neither one - one nor onto'} 2024 2024-05-18 shift_1 mathematics   1 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: for one-one: $f(-1)=(-1)^3-(-1)=0$ , $f(0)=0$ , and $f(1)=0$ . since $f(-1)=f(0)=f(1)$ , different inputs give the same output, so $f$ is not one-one. for onto: $f(x)=x^3-x$ is a polynomial, hence continuous on $\mathbb{r}$ . as $x\to \infty$ , $f(x)=x^3-x\to \infty$ . as $x\to -\infty$ , $f(x)=x^3-x\to -\infty$ . since $f$ is continuous and takes arbitrarily large positive and negative values, its range is all of $\mathbb{r}$ . therefore, $f$ is onto. hence $f$ is onto but not one-one, so the correct option is onto but not one - one . © examsnet.com

question: If $f(x)=\sqrt{x}-1$ and $g\{f(x)\}=x+2\sqrt{x}+1$ then $g(x)=$ [AP EAPCET 18 May 2024 Shift 1]
search_text: if $f(x)=\sqrt{x}-1$ and $g\{f(x)\}=x+2\sqrt{x}+1$ then $g(x)=$ [ap eapcet 18 may 2024 shift 1] {'a': '$(x+2)^2$', 'b': '$(x-2)^2$', 'c': '$(\\sqrt{x}+2)^2$', 'd': '$(\\sqrt{x}-2)^2$'} 2024 2024-05-18 shift_1 mathematics   2 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: given $f(x)=\sqrt{x}-1$ and $g(f(x))=x+2\sqrt{x}+1$ . we must express $g(f(x))$ entirely in terms of $f(x)$ . first, simplify the given expression using the perfect square identity: $x+2\sqrt{x}+1=(\sqrt{x}+1)^2$ now relate $\sqrt{x}$ to $f(x)$ : since $f(x)=\sqrt{x}-1$ , we have $\sqrt{x}=f(x)+1$ . substituting this into the expression gives: $g(f(x))=((f(x)+1)+1)^2=(f(x)+2)^2$ since this holds for every $x$ in the domain, replacing $f(x)$ by a general variable $x$ yields: $g(x)=(x+2)^2$ check: $g(f(x))=(\sqrt{x}-1+2)^2=(\sqrt{x}+1)^2=x+2\sqrt{x}+1$ , which matches the given condition. therefore, the correct answer is $(x+2)^2$ . © examsnet.com

question: For all positive integers ' $n$ ' if $3 (5^{2 n+1}) +2^{3 n+1}$ is divisible by $k$ , then the number of prime numbers less than or equal to $k$ is [AP EAPCET 18 May 2024 Shift 1]
search_text: for all positive integers ' $n$ ' if $3 (5^{2 n+1}) +2^{3 n+1}$ is divisible by $k$ , then the number of prime numbers less than or equal to $k$ is [ap eapcet 18 may 2024 shift 1] {'a': '17', 'b': '6', 'c': '7', 'd': '8'} 2024 2024-05-18 shift_1 mathematics   3 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: the given expression is $f(n) = 3 \cdot 5^{2n+1} + 2^{3n+1}$ . since $f(n)$ is divisible by $k$ for every positive integer $n$ , $k$ must divide both $f(1)$ and $f(2)$ . compute $f(1) = 3 \cdot 5^{3} + 2^{4} = 375 + 16 = 391$ . compute $f(2) = 3 \cdot 5^{5} + 2^{7} = 9375 + 128 = 9503$ . so $k = \text{hcf}(391, 9503)$ . applying the euclidean algorithm: $9503 = 24 \times 391 + 119$ , $391 = 3 \times 119 + 34$ , $119 = 3 \times 34 + 17$ , $34 = 2 \times 17 + 0$ . hence $\text{hcf}(391, 9503) = 17$ , so $k = 17$ . verification: working modulo $17$ , we have $5^{2} = 25 \equiv 8$ and $2^{3} = 8$ . therefore $f(n) = 3 \cdot 5 \cdot 25^{n} + 2 \cdot 8^{n} \equiv 15 \cdot 8^{n} + 2 \cdot 8^{n} = 17 \cdot 8^{n} \equiv 0 \pmod{17}$ . so $17$ divides $f(n)$ for all positive integers $n$ , confirming $k = 17$ . the prime numbers less than or equal to $17$ are $2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13, 17$ . counting them gives $7$ primes. therefore, the number of prime numbers less than or equal to $k$ is $7$ . © examsnet.com

question: If $α, β, γ$ are the roots of $\begin{vmatrix} 1-x & -2 & 1 \\ -2 & 4-x & -2 \\ 1 & -2 & 1-x \end{vmatrix}=0$ , then $αβ+βγ+γα=$ [AP EAPCET 18 May 2024 Shift 1]
search_text: if $α, β, γ$ are the roots of $\begin{vmatrix} 1-x & -2 & 1 \\ -2 & 4-x & -2 \\ 1 & -2 & 1-x \end{vmatrix}=0$ , then $αβ+βγ+γα=$ [ap eapcet 18 may 2024 shift 1] {'a': '$6$', 'b': '$8$', 'c': '$0$', 'd': '$-1$'} 2024 2024-05-18 shift_1 mathematics   4 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: let $d=\begin{vmatrix}1-x&-2&1\\-2&4-x&-2\\1&-2&1-x\end{vmatrix}.$ apply $r_1\to r_1+r_2+r_3$ : $d=\begin{vmatrix}-x&-x&-x\\-2&4-x&-2\\1&-2&1-x\end{vmatrix}.$ taking $-x$ common from $r_1$ : $d=-x\begin{vmatrix}1&1&1\\-2&4-x&-2\\1&-2&1-x\end{vmatrix}.$ apply $c_2\to c_2-c_1$ and $c_3\to c_3-c_1$ : $d=-x\begin{vmatrix}1&0&0\\-2&6-x&0\\1&-3&-x\end{vmatrix}.$ expanding along $r_1$ : $d=-x(6-x)(-x)=x^2(6-x).$ thus, $x^2(6-x)=0$ , so the roots are $\alpha=0$ , $\beta=0$ , and $\gamma=6$ . therefore, $\alpha\beta+\beta\gamma+\gamma\alpha=0\cdot0+0\cdot6+6\cdot0=0.$ hence, the correct option is $0$ . © examsnet.com

search_text: if the determinant of a 3rd order matrix $a$ is $k$ , then the sum of the determinants of the matrices $a^4$ and $(a-a^4)$ is [ap eapcet 18 may 2024 shift 1] {'a': '$2k$', 'b': '$0$', 'c': '$k^2$', 'd': '$k$'} 2024 2024-05-18 shift_1 mathematics   5 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: the intended expression is the determinant of the sum of the matrices $a^4$ and $(a-a^4)$ , because the $a^4$ terms cancel when the matrices are added. add the matrices: $a^4+(a-a^4)=a^4+a-a^4=a$ . now take the determinant: $|a^4+(a-a^4)|=|a|$ . given $|a|=k$ , the required value is $k$ . thus the correct option is $k$ . note: if the phrase is read literally as $|a^4|+|a-a^4|$ , it is not determined by $|a|=k$ alone; the standard intended exam interpretation is the determinant of the matrix sum. © examsnet.com

question: While solving a system of linear equations $AX = B$ using Cramer's rule with the usual notation if $\Delta = \begin{vmatrix} 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 2 & -1 & 2 \\ -1 & 1 & 5 \end{vmatrix} ; \Delta_1 = \begin{vmatrix} 5 & 1 & 1 \\ 4 & -1 & 2 \\ 11 & 1 & 5 \end{vmatrix}$ and $X = \begin{bmatrix} \alpha \\ 2 \\ \beta \end{bmatrix}$ , then $\alpha^2+\beta^2=$ [AP EAPCET 18 May 2024 Shift 1]
search_text: while solving a system of linear equations $ax = b$ using cramer's rule with the usual notation if $\delta = \begin{vmatrix} 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 2 & -1 & 2 \\ -1 & 1 & 5 \end{vmatrix} ; \delta_1 = \begin{vmatrix} 5 & 1 & 1 \\ 4 & -1 & 2 \\ 11 & 1 & 5 \end{vmatrix}$ and $x = \begin{bmatrix} \alpha \\ 2 \\ \beta \end{bmatrix}$ , then $\alpha^2+\beta^2=$ [ap eapcet 18 may 2024 shift 1] {'a': '9', 'b': '13', 'c': '5', 'd': '25'} 2024 2024-05-18 shift_1 mathematics   6 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: we have, $\; \delta = \begin{vmatrix} 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 2 & -1 & 2 \\ -1 & 1 & 5 \end{vmatrix}$ $\; = 1(-5-2)-1(10+2)+1(2-1)$ $\; = -7-12+1$ $\; = -18 \neq 0$ $\; \delta_1 = \begin{vmatrix} 5 & 1 & 1 \\ 4 & -1 & 2 \\ 11 & 1 & 5 \end{vmatrix}$ $\; = 5(-5-2)-1(20-22)+1(4+11)$ $\; = -35+2+15$ $\; = -18$ $\; \delta_3 = \begin{vmatrix} 1 & 1 & 5 \\ 2 & -1 & 4 \\ -1 & 1 & 11 \end{vmatrix}$ $\; = 1(-11-4)-1(22+4)+5(2-1)$ $\; = -15-26+5 = -36$ $\; \therefore \;\; \alpha = \frac{\delta_1}{\delta} = \frac{-18}{-18} = 1$ $\; \therefore \;\; \beta = \frac{\delta_3}{\delta} = \frac{-36}{-18} = 2$ hence, $\alpha^2+\beta^2=1^2+2^2=5$ . © examsnet.com

question: If real parts of $\sqrt{-5-12i}, \sqrt{5+12i}$ are positive values, the real part of $\sqrt{-8-6i}$ is a negative value and $a+i b = \frac{\sqrt{-5-12i} + \sqrt{5+12i}}{\sqrt{-8-6i}}$ then $2a+b=$ [AP EAPCET 18 May 2024 Shift 1]
search_text: if real parts of $\sqrt{-5-12i}, \sqrt{5+12i}$ are positive values, the real part of $\sqrt{-8-6i}$ is a negative value and $a+i b = \frac{\sqrt{-5-12i} + \sqrt{5+12i}}{\sqrt{-8-6i}}$ then $2a+b=$ [ap eapcet 18 may 2024 shift 1] {'a': '$3$', 'b': '$2$', 'c': '$-3$', 'd': '$-2$'} 2024 2024-05-18 shift_1 mathematics   7 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: to find $a+i b = \frac{\sqrt{-5-12i} + \sqrt{5+12i}}{\sqrt{-8-6i}}$ and calculate $2a+b$ : calculate $\sqrt{-5-12i}$ and $\sqrt{5+12i}$ : since the real parts of $\sqrt{-5-12i}$ and $\sqrt{5+12i}$ are positive: $\sqrt{-5-12i} = \sqrt{\frac{13-5}{2}} + i \sqrt{\frac{13+5}{2}} = 2-3i$ $\sqrt{5+12i} = \sqrt{\frac{13+5}{2}} + i \sqrt{\frac{13-5}{2}} = 3+2i$ calculate $\sqrt{-8-6i}$ : given that the real part is negative: $\sqrt{-8-6i} = -\sqrt{\frac{10-8}{2}} + i \sqrt{\frac{10+8}{2}} = -1+3i$ find $a+i b:$ using the calculations from the previous steps: $a+i b = \frac{(2-3i)+(3+2i)}{-1+3i} = \frac{5-i}{-1+3i}$ multiply the numerator and the denominator by the conjugate of the denominator: $= \frac{(5-i)(-1-3i)}{(-1+3i)(-1-3i)}$ simplify: $\; = \;\frac{-5+i-15i-3}{1+9} = \frac{-8-14i}{10}$ $\; = -\frac{4}{5} - \frac{7i}{5}$ thus, $a = -\frac{4}{5}$ and $b = -\frac{7}{5}$ . calculate $2a+b$ : $2a+b = 2\left(-\frac{4}{5}\right) + \left(-\frac{7}{5}\right) = -\frac{8}{5} - \frac{7}{5} = -3$ hence, the result is -3 . © examsnet.com

question: The set of all real values of $c$ for which the equation $z \overline{z}+(4-3i) \overline{z}+(4+3i) z+c=0$ represents a circle is [AP EAPCET 18 May 2024 Shift 1]
search_text: the set of all real values of $c$ for which the equation $z \overline{z}+(4-3i) \overline{z}+(4+3i) z+c=0$ represents a circle is [ap eapcet 18 may 2024 shift 1] {'a': '$[25, \\infty)$', 'b': '$[-5,5]$', 'c': '$(-\\infty,-5] \\cup [5, \\infty)$', 'd': '$(-\\infty, 25]$'} 2024 2024-05-18 shift_1 mathematics   8 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: the given equation $z \overline{z}+(4-3i) z+(4+3i) \overline{z}+c=0$ is analyzed to determine the real values of $c$ that form a circle. key steps identifying the circle's center: $z \overline{z}$ is the modulus squared of $z$ , and the terms $(4-3i) z$ and $(4+3i) \overline{z}$ suggest the transformation involves the complex number $4-3i$ . thus, the center of the circle is at $4-3i$ . finding the radius: to find the radius, use the formula that incorporates the modulus of the center: $\sqrt{(4)^2+(-3)^2-c}=\sqrt{25-c}$ the radius needs to be non-negative for the equation to represent a circle: $\sqrt{25-c} \geq 0$ which simplifies to: $25-c \geq 0 \;\; \rightarrow \;\; c \leq 25$ conclusion the real values of $c$ for which the equation represents a circle are in the interval: $(-\infty, 25]$ © examsnet.com

search_text: if the sum of two roots $\alpha, \beta$ of the equation $x^4-x^3-8 x^2+2 x+12=0$ is zero and $\gamma, \delta (\gamma > \delta)$ are its other roots, then $3\gamma+2\delta=$ [ap eapcet 18 may 2024 shift 1] {'a': '0', 'b': '1', 'c': '3', 'd': '5'} 2024 2024-05-18 shift_1 mathematics   12 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: we are given the polynomial equation $x^4-x^3-8 x^2+2 x+12=0$ with roots $\alpha, \beta, \gamma$ , and $\delta$ . it is known that the sum of two of the roots, $\alpha$ and $\beta$ , is zero, i.e., $\alpha+\beta=0$ . from vieta's formulas, the sum of all roots is: $s_1=\alpha+\beta+\gamma+\delta=1$ given $\alpha+\beta=0$ , we find: $\gamma+\delta=1$ similarly, from vieta's formulas, the sum of the products of the roots taken two at a time is: $s_2=\alpha\beta+\alpha\gamma+\alpha\delta+\beta\gamma+\beta\delta+\gamma\delta=-8$ using $\alpha+\beta=0$ , simplify to: $\alpha\beta+\gamma\delta=-8$ from the sum of the products of the roots taken three at a time, we have: $s_3=\alpha\beta\gamma+\alpha\beta\delta+\alpha\gamma\delta+\beta\gamma\delta=-2$ substitute $(\alpha+\beta)\gamma\delta+\alpha\beta(\gamma+\delta)=-2$ and rearrange: $\alpha\beta=-2$ from vieta's formulas, the product of the roots is given by: $s_4=\alpha\beta\gamma\delta=12$ use $\alpha\beta=-2$ to find: $\gamma\delta=-6 \; \; \ldots (v)$ next, solve the system of equations obtained from (ii) and (v): $\gamma+\delta=1$ $\gamma\delta=-6$ these are the equations for a quadratic: $t^2-(\gamma+\delta)t+\gamma\delta=0 \rightarrow t^2-t-6=0$ solving, we find the roots to be: $t = \frac{1 \pm \sqrt{1+24}}{2} = \frac{1 \pm 5}{2}$ thus, $t=3$ or $t=-2$ . since $\gamma > \delta$ , we assign $\gamma = 3$ and $\delta = -2$ . finally, compute: $3\gamma+2\delta=3 \times 3+2 \times (-2)=9-4=5$ © examsnet.com

question: $\lim\limits_{n\to\infty} n^4 \left[ \frac{1}{n^5} + \frac{1}{(n^2+1)^{\frac{5}{2}}} + \frac{1}{(n^2+4)^{\frac{5}{2}}} + \frac{1}{(n^2+9)^{\frac{5}{2}}} + \dots + \frac{1}{4\sqrt{2}n^5} \right] =$ [AP EAPCET 18 May 2024 Shift 1]
search_text: $\lim\limits_{n\to\infty} n^4 \left[ \frac{1}{n^5} + \frac{1}{(n^2+1)^{\frac{5}{2}}} + \frac{1}{(n^2+4)^{\frac{5}{2}}} + \frac{1}{(n^2+9)^{\frac{5}{2}}} + \dots + \frac{1}{4\sqrt{2}n^5} \right] =$ [ap eapcet 18 may 2024 shift 1] {'a': '$\\frac{3}{4\\sqrt{2}}$', 'b': '$\\frac{3\\sqrt{2}}{4}$', 'c': '$\\frac{5}{6\\sqrt{2}}$', 'd': '$\\frac{5\\sqrt{2}}{6}$'} 2024 2024-05-18 shift_1 mathematics   74 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: $\;\lim\limits_{n\to\infty} x^4 \left[ \begin{array}{c} \frac{1}{x^5} + \frac{1}{(x^2+1)^{\frac{5}{2}}} + \frac{1}{(x^2+4)^{\frac{5}{2}}} \\ + \frac{1}{(x^2+9)^{\frac{5}{2}}} + \dots + \frac{1}{4\sqrt{2}x^5} \end{array} \right]$ $\;\lim\limits_{n\to\infty} \sum\limits_{r=1}^{n} \frac{x^4}{(x^2+r^2)^{\frac{5}{2}}} \left[ \because \lim\limits_{n\to\infty} \frac{x^4}{x^5}=0 \right]$ $\;\lim\limits_{n\to\infty} \sum\limits_{r=1}^{n} \frac{1}{n} \left[ \frac{1}{\left(1+\left(\frac{r}{n}\right)^2\right)^{\frac{5}{2}}} \right]$ $=\int\limits_{0}^{1} \frac{1}{(1+x^2)^{\frac{5}{2}}} dx$ $\;\;\;\text{ let } x = \tan \theta$ $dx = \sec^2 \theta d\theta$ $\;x \to 0, \theta \to 0 \;\text{ and }\;$ $\;x \to 1, \theta \to \frac{\pi}{4}$ $=\int\limits_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{4}} \frac{1}{(1+\tan^2 \theta)^{\frac{5}{2}}} \times \sec^2 \theta d\theta$ $=\int\limits_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{4}} \frac{1}{\sec^3 \theta} d\theta$ $=\int\limits_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{4}} \cos^3 \theta d\theta$ $=\frac{1}{4} \int\limits_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{4}} (\cos 3\theta + 3\cos \theta) d\theta$ $=\frac{1}{4} \left[ \frac{\sin 3\theta}{3} + 3 \sin \theta \right]_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{4}}$ $=\frac{1}{4} \left[ \frac{1}{3} \sin \left(\pi - \frac{\pi}{4}\right) + 3 \sin \frac{\pi}{4} \right]$ $=\frac{1}{4} \left[ \frac{1}{3} \times \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} + \frac{3}{\sqrt{2}} \right]$ $=\frac{1+9}{4 \times 3 \sqrt{2}} \rightarrow \frac{10}{4 \times 3 \sqrt{2}} = \frac{5}{6 \sqrt{2}}$ © examsnet.com

search_text: $\int\limits_{\log 4}^{\log 5} \frac{e^{2x}+e^x}{e^{2x}-5e^x+6} dx =$ [ap eapcet 18 may 2024 shift 1] {'a': '$\\log \\left( \\frac{64}{9} \\right)$', 'b': '$\\log \\left( \\frac{256}{81} \\right)$', 'c': '$\\log \\left( \\frac{32}{3} \\right)$', 'd': '$\\log \\left( \\frac{128}{27} \\right)$'} 2024 2024-05-18 shift_1 mathematics   75 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: $\text{ let } i = \int\limits_{\log 4}^{\log 5} \frac{e^{2x}+e^x}{e^{2x}-5e^x+6} dx$ $= \int\limits_{\log 4}^{\log 5} \frac{(e^x)^2 + e^x}{(e^x-3)(e^x-2)} dx$ $= \int\limits_{\log 4}^{\log 5} \frac{e^x(e^x+1)}{(e^x-3)(e^x-2)} dx$ let $e^x = t$ $\rightarrow e^x dx = dt$ when $x \rightarrow \log 4, t \rightarrow 4$ $x \rightarrow \log 5, t \rightarrow 5$ $i = \int\limits_{4}^{5} \frac{t+1}{(t-3)(t-2)} dt$ $= \int\limits_{4}^{5} \frac{4}{t-3} - \frac{3}{t-2}$ [ ∵ by partial fraction] $= \left[ 4 \log |t-3| - 3 \log |t-2| \right]_4^5$ $= \left[ \log \left\| \frac{(t-3)^4}{(t-2)^3} \right\|. \right]_4^5$ $= \log \frac{2^4}{3^3} - \log \frac{1}{2^3} = \log \frac{2^4}{3^3} \times 2^3$ $= \log \left( \frac{2^7}{3^3} \right) = \log \left( \frac{128}{27} \right)$ © examsnet.com

search_text: $\int\limits_{1}^{2} \;\frac{x^4-1}{x^6-1} dx=$ [ap eapcet 18 may 2024 shift 1] {'a': '$\\;\\frac{1}{\\sqrt{3}} \\mathrm{tan}^{-1} \\left( \\frac{\\sqrt{3}}{2} \\right)$', 'b': '$\\;\\;\\frac{121}{6}$', 'c': '$\\;\\sqrt{2}-1$', 'd': '$\\;\\;\\frac{1}{\\sqrt{2}} \\mathrm{tan}^{-1} \\left( \\frac{2}{\\sqrt{3}} \\right)$'} 2024 2024-05-18 shift_1 mathematics   76 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: $\;\;\text{let } i=\int\limits_{1}^{2} \;\frac{x^4-1}{x^6-1} dx$ $\;=\int\limits_{1}^{2} \;\frac{(x^2-1)(x^2+1)}{(x^2-1)(x^4+x^2+1)} dx$ $\;=\int\limits_{1}^{2} \;\frac{x^2+1}{x^4+x^2+1} dx=\int\limits_{1}^{2} \left( \frac{1+\frac{1}{x^2}}{x^2+\frac{1}{x^2}+1} \right) dx$ $\;=\int\limits_{1}^{2} \left( \frac{1+\frac{1}{x^2}}{x^2+\frac{1}{x^2}-2+3} \right) dx$ $\;=\int\limits_{1}^{2} \;\frac{1+\frac{1}{x^2}}{\left(x-\frac{1}{x}\right)^2+3} dx$ let $x-\frac{1}{x}=t \rightarrow \left(1+\frac{1}{x^2}\right) dx = dt$ when $x \rightarrow 1$ , then $t \rightarrow 0$ when $x \rightarrow 2$ , then $t \rightarrow \frac{3}{2}$ $i\;=\int\limits_{0}^{3/2} \;\frac{1}{t^2+3} dt$ $\;=\;\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}} \left[ \tan^{-1} \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}} \right]_{0}^{3/2}$ $\;=\;\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}} \tan^{-1} \frac{3}{2\sqrt{3}}$ $\;=\;\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}} \tan^{-1} \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$ © examsnet.com

question: The differential equation representing the family of circles having their centres on $Y$ -axis is $(y_1=\;\frac{d y}{d x}.$ and $y_2=\;\frac{d^2 y}{d x^2})$ [AP EAPCET 18 May 2024 Shift 1]
search_text: the differential equation representing the family of circles having their centres on $y$ -axis is $(y_1=\;\frac{d y}{d x}.$ and $y_2=\;\frac{d^2 y}{d x^2})$ [ap eapcet 18 may 2024 shift 1] {'a': '$\\;y_2=y (y_1^2+1)$', 'b': '$\\;y_2=x y (y_1^2+1)$', 'c': '$\\;x y_2=y_1 (y_1^2+1)$', 'd': '$\\;x y_2=y (y_1^2+1)$'} 2024 2024-05-18 shift_1 mathematics   78 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: let the circle have centre $(0,k)$ and radius $r$ , where $k$ and $r$ are arbitrary constants: $x^2+(y-k)^2=r^2$ since there are two arbitrary constants, the required differential equation is of second order. differentiating with respect to $x$ : $2x+2(y-k)y_1=0$ $x+(y-k)y_1=0$ $y-k=-\frac{x}{y_1}$ (1) differentiating once more with respect to $x$ : $1+y_1^2+(y-k)y_2=0$ substituting $y-k=-\frac{x}{y_1}$ from (1): $1+y_1^2-\frac{x\,y_2}{y_1}=0$ $1+y_1^2=\frac{x\,y_2}{y_1}$ $x\,y_2=y_1\,(y_1^2+1)$ hence the required differential equation is $x\,y_2=y_1\,(y_1^2+1)$ , which is option c. check: for the circle $x^2+y^2=1$ (centre on the $y$ -axis), $y_1=-\frac{x}{y}$ and $y_2=-\frac{1}{y^3}$ , so $x\,y_2=-\frac{x}{y^3}=y_1\,(y_1^2+1)$ , confirming the result. options involving $y\,(y_1^2+1)$ or $y_2$ alone do not reproduce this family. © examsnet.com

question: The general solution of the differential equation $(\sin y \cos^2 y - x \sec^2 y) dy = (\tan y) dx$ is [AP EAPCET 18 May 2024 Shift 1]
search_text: the general solution of the differential equation $(\sin y \cos^2 y - x \sec^2 y) dy = (\tan y) dx$ is [ap eapcet 18 may 2024 shift 1] {'a': '$\\tan y = 3 x \\cos^3 y + c$', 'b': '$x(\\sec y + \\tan y) = \\cos^2 y + c$', 'c': '$y \\sin y = x^2 \\cos^2 y + c$', 'd': '$3 x \\tan y + \\cos^3 y = c$'} 2024 2024-05-18 shift_1 mathematics   79 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: rewrite the differential equation with $x$ as the dependent variable and $y$ as the independent variable: $(\sin y \cos^2 y - x \sec^2 y)\,dy = (\tan y)\,dx.$ dividing by $\tan y\,dy$ gives $\frac{dx}{dy}=\frac{\sin y \cos^2 y - x \sec^2 y}{\tan y}.$ thus $\frac{dx}{dy}+\frac{\sec^2 y}{\tan y}x=\cos^3 y.$ since $\frac{\sec^2 y}{\tan y}=\frac{1}{\sin y\cos y}$ , this becomes $\frac{dx}{dy}+\frac{x}{\sin y\cos y}=\cos^3 y.$ the integrating factor is $\mu(y)=e^{\int \frac{1}{\sin y\cos y}\,dy}.$ now $\int \frac{1}{\sin y\cos y}\,dy=\ln|\tan y|,$ because $\frac{d}{dy}\left(\ln|\tan y|\right)=\frac{\sec^2 y}{\tan y}=\frac{1}{\sin y\cos y}.$ hence $\mu(y)=\tan y.$ multiplying the linear differential equation by $\tan y$ gives $\tan y\frac{dx}{dy}+x\sec^2 y=\sin y\cos^2 y.$ the left side is $\frac{d}{dy}(x\tan y).$ so $\frac{d}{dy}(x\tan y)=\sin y\cos^2 y.$ integrating, $x\tan y=\int \sin y\cos^2 y\,dy.$ let $u=\cos y$ , so $du=-\sin y\,dy$ : $x\tan y=-\frac{\cos^3 y}{3}+c.$ therefore, $3x\tan y+\cos^3 y=c.$ this matches option $3$ . © examsnet.com

question: The general solution of the differential equation $(x-y-1) dy=(x+y+1) dx$ is [AP EAPCET 18 May 2024 Shift 1]
search_text: the general solution of the differential equation $(x-y-1) dy=(x+y+1) dx$ is [ap eapcet 18 may 2024 shift 1] {'a': '$\\tan^{-1} \\left( \\frac{y+1}{x} \\right) - \\frac{1}{2} \\log (x^2+y^2+2y+1) = c$', 'b': '$(x-y)+\\log(x+y)=c$', 'c': '$y^2-x^2+xy-3y-x=c$', 'd': '$(x-y-1)^2(x+y+1)^3=c$'} 2024 2024-05-18 shift_1 mathematics   80 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: rewrite the equation in the standard form: $\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{x+y+1}{x-y-1}$ group the linear terms by putting $z=y+1$ , so that $\frac{dz}{dx}=\frac{dy}{dx}$ , which gives: $\frac{dz}{dx}=\frac{x+z}{x-z}$ this is homogeneous, so use the substitution $z=vx$ , hence: $\frac{dz}{dx}=v+x\frac{dv}{dx}$ substituting back: $v+x\frac{dv}{dx}=\frac{1+v}{1-v}$ so: $x\frac{dv}{dx}=\frac{1+v}{1-v}-v=\frac{1+v-v+v^{2}}{1-v}=\frac{1+v^{2}}{1-v}$ separating the variables: $\frac{1-v}{1+v^{2}}\,dv=\frac{dx}{x}$ integrating both sides: $\int\left(\frac{1}{1+v^{2}}-\frac{v}{1+v^{2}}\right)dv=\int\frac{dx}{x}$ this yields: $\tan^{-1}v-\frac{1}{2}\log(1+v^{2})=\log|x|+c$ now $1+v^{2}=1+\frac{z^{2}}{x^{2}}=\frac{x^{2}+z^{2}}{x^{2}}$ , so: $\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{z}{x}\right)-\frac{1}{2}\log\frac{x^{2}+z^{2}}{x^{2}}=\log|x|+c$ that is: $\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{z}{x}\right)-\frac{1}{2}\log\left(x^{2}+z^{2}\right)+\log|x|=\log|x|+c$ the $\log|x|$ terms cancel, leaving: $\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{z}{x}\right)-\frac{1}{2}\log\left(x^{2}+z^{2}\right)=c$ finally, replacing $z=y+1$ : $\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{y+1}{x}\right)-\frac{1}{2}\log\left(x^{2}+y^{2}+2y+1\right)=c$ this matches option a, so it is the correct general solution. © examsnet.com

question: An object is projected such that it has to attain maximum range, another body is projected to reach maximum height. If both the objects reached the same maximum height, then the ratio initial velocities [AP EAPCET 18 May 2024 Shift 1]
search_text: an object is projected such that it has to attain maximum range, another body is projected to reach maximum height. if both the objects reached the same maximum height, then the ratio initial velocities [ap eapcet 18 may 2024 shift 1] {'a': '$2:1$', 'b': '$\\sqrt{2}:1$', 'c': '$1:\\sqrt{2}$', 'd': '$1:2$'} 2024 2024-05-18 shift_1 physics   82 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: let the first object be projected at $45^\circ$ to attain maximum range. the maximum height of the first object is $h_1=\frac{u_1^2\sin^2 45^\circ}{2g}=\frac{u_1^2}{4g}$ . let the second object be projected vertically at $90^\circ$ to attain maximum height. the maximum height of the second object is $h_2=\frac{u_2^2\sin^2 90^\circ}{2g}=\frac{u_2^2}{2g}$ . since both reach the same maximum height, $h_1=h_2$ $\frac{u_1^2}{4g}=\frac{u_2^2}{2g}$ $u_1^2=2u_2^2$ $u_1=\sqrt{2}\,u_2$ therefore, $\frac{u_1}{u_2}=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{1}$ hence, the ratio of initial velocities is $\sqrt{2}:1$ . © examsnet.com

search_text: a ball is projected at an angle of $45^{\circ}$ with the horizontal. it passes through a wall of height ' $h$ ' at a horizontal distance $d_1$ from the point of projection and strikes the ground at a distance $d_1+d_2$ from the point of projection, then ' $h$ ' is [ap eapcet 18 may 2024 shift 1] {'a': '$h=\\frac{2 d_1 d_2}{d_1+d_2}$', 'b': '$h=\\frac{d_1 d_2}{d_1+d_2}$', 'c': '$h=\\frac{\\sqrt{2} d_1 d_2}{d_1+d_2}$', 'd': '$h=\\frac{d_1 d_2}{2 (d_1+d_2)}$'} 2024 2024-05-18 shift_1 physics   83 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: angle of projection $=45^{\circ}$ height of wall $=h$ we know that. the equation of trajectory of a projectale, $y=x \tan \theta - \frac{g x^2}{2 u^2 \cos^2 \theta}$ $y=x \tan \theta \left(1-\frac{g x}{2 u^2 \cos^2 \theta \cdot \tan \theta}\right)$ $y=x \tan \theta \left(1-\frac{g x}{2 u^2 \cos^2 \theta \cdot \frac{\sin \theta}{\cos \theta}}\right)$ $y=x \tan \theta \left(1-\frac{x}{r}\right) \{\because r=\frac{u^2 \sin 2\theta}{g}\}$ here, $r=d_1+d_2, x=d_1$ and $y=h$ so, $h=d_1 \tan 45^{\circ} \left(1-\frac{d_1}{d_1+d_2}\right)$ $h=d_1 \left(\frac{d_2}{d_1+d_2}\right)$ $h=\frac{d_1 d_2}{d_1+d_2}$ © examsnet.com

(ii): $g\,(m_1-m_2)=a\,(m_1+m_2)$ $10\,(m_1-m_2)=\frac{2}{3}\,(m_1+m_2)$ multiplying both sides by $\frac{3}{2}$ : $15\,(m_1-m_2)=(m_1+m_2)$ $15m_1-15m_2=m_1+m_2$ $14m_1=16m_2$ $7m_1=8m_2$ $\frac{m_1}{m_2}=\frac{8}{7}$ hence the correct answer is $\frac{8}{7}$ . © examsnet.com

search_text: in an inelastic collision, after collision the kinetic energy [ap eapcet 18 may 2024 shift 1] {'a': 'increases by 2 times', 'b': 'is less than before collision', 'c': 'is more than before collision', 'd': 'remains same'} 2024 2024-05-18 shift_1 physics   87 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: in an inelastic collision, although the momentum is conserved, kinetic energy is not. some of the initial kinetic energy is converted into other forms of energy, such as heat, sound, or energy used in deforming the colliding bodies. this means that the kinetic energy after the collision is less than before the collision. so, the correct answer is: option b: is less than before collision to summarize: in an inelastic collision, momentum is conserved. kinetic energy decreases because some energy is lost to other forms (like heat or sound). therefore, the kinetic energy after collision is less than the kinetic energy before the collision. © examsnet.com

search_text: a spring of $5 \times 10^3 \mathrm{nm}^{-1}$ spring constant is stretched initially by $10 \mathrm{cm}$ from unstretched position. the work required to stretch it further by another $10 \mathrm{cm}$ is [ap eapcet 18 may 2024 shift 1] {'a': '$75 \\, \\mathrm{n-m}$', 'b': '$50 \\, \\mathrm{n-m}$', 'c': '$76 \\, \\mathrm{n-m}$', 'd': '$82 \\, \\mathrm{n-m}$'} 2024 2024-05-18 shift_1 physics   88 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: spring constant, $k = 5 \times 10^3 \mathrm{n/m}$ initially stretched position, $x_1 = 10 \mathrm{cm} = 0.1 \mathrm{m}$ further stretched position, $x_2 = 20 \mathrm{cm} = 0.2 \mathrm{m}$ work done: the work done to further stretch the spring from $x_1$ to $x_2$ is equal to the change in potential energy of the spring. this can be calculated using the formula: $\; \text{ work done } \; = \; \frac{1}{2} k \left[ (x_2)^2 - (x_1)^2 \right]$ substitute the given values: $\; = \; \frac{1}{2} \times 5 \times 10^3 \left[ (0.2)^2 - (0.1)^2 \right]$ $\; = \; \frac{1}{2} \times 5 \times 10^3 \times (0.04-0.01)$ $\; = \; \frac{1}{2} \times 5 \times 10^3 \times 0.03$ $\; = 2.5 \times 10^3 \times 0.03$ $\; = 75 \, \mathrm{n \cdot m}$ therefore, the work required to stretch the spring further by another 10 cm is $75 \, \mathrm{n \cdot m}$ . © examsnet.com

question: A wheel of angular speed $600\,\text{rev}/\text{min}$ is made to slow down at a rate of $2\,\text{rad}\,\text{s}^{-2}$ . The number of revolutions made by the wheel before coming to rest is [AP EAPCET 18 May 2024 Shift 1]
search_text: a wheel of angular speed $600\,\text{rev}/\text{min}$ is made to slow down at a rate of $2\,\text{rad}\,\text{s}^{-2}$ . the number of revolutions made by the wheel before coming to rest is [ap eapcet 18 may 2024 shift 1] {'a': '157', 'b': '314', 'c': '177', 'd': '117'} 2024 2024-05-18 shift_1 physics   90 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: we need to determine the number of revolutions a wheel makes before coming to a stop. here's the breakdown of the solution: initial angular velocity, $\omega_0=600\ \text{rev}/\text{min}$ to convert to radians per second: $\omega_0=600\times\frac{2\pi}{60}=20\pi\ \text{rad}/\text{s}$ angular deceleration, $\alpha=-2\ \text{rad}/\text{s}^2$ final angular velocity, $\omega=0\ \text{rad}/\text{s}$ find: number of revolutions, $n$ solution: using the angular kinematic equation: $\omega^2=\omega_0^2+2\alpha\theta$ plugging in the given values: $0=(20\pi)^2+2(-2)\theta$ simplify: $0=400\pi^2-4\theta$ rearrange to solve for $\theta$ : $4\theta=400\pi^2\theta=100\pi^2$ relate $\theta$ to revolutions: since $\theta=2\pi n$ , $2\pi n=100\pi^2$ solve for $n$ : $n=\frac{100\pi^2}{2\pi}n=50\pi$ assuming $\pi\approx3.14$ , $n=50\times3.14=157$ © examsnet.com

question: Time period of a simple pendulum in Air is $T$ . If the pendulum is in water and executes SHM, its time period is $t$ . The value of $\;\frac{T}{t}$ is [AP EAPCET 18 May 2024 Shift 1]
search_text: time period of a simple pendulum in air is $t$ . if the pendulum is in water and executes shm, its time period is $t$ . the value of $\;\frac{t}{t}$ is [ap eapcet 18 may 2024 shift 1] {'a': '$\\;\\frac{2}{5}$', 'b': '$\\sqrt{\\;\\frac{2}{5}}$', 'c': '$\\;\\frac{5}{2}$', 'd': '$\\sqrt{\\;\\frac{5}{2}}$'} 2024 2024-05-18 shift_1 physics   91 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: time period of a simple pendulum in air is $t=2\pi\sqrt{\frac{l}{g}}$ . in water, the upthrust of water reduces the effective weight of the bob, so the effective acceleration due to gravity becomes $g'=g\left(1-\frac{\sigma}{\rho}\right)$ , where $\sigma$ is the density of water and $\rho$ is the density of the bob. taking the density of the bob, $\rho=\frac{5000}{3}\ \mathrm{kg/m^3}$ , and the density of water, $\sigma=1000\ \mathrm{kg/m^3}$ . the time period in water is therefore $t=2\pi\sqrt{\frac{l}{g'}}=\frac{t}{\sqrt{1-\frac{\sigma}{\rho}}}$ . substitute the values: $1-\frac{\sigma}{\rho}=1-\frac{1000 \times 3}{5000}=1-0.6=0.4=\frac{2}{5}$ . hence $\frac{t}{t}=\sqrt{1-\frac{\sigma}{\rho}}=\sqrt{0.4}=\sqrt{\frac{2}{5}}$ . note that $\frac{t}{t}<1$ because buoyancy makes the pendulum slower in water, so $\sqrt{\frac{5}{2}}$ (the reciprocal) is incorrect. thus the value of $\;\frac{t}{t}$ is $\sqrt{\;\frac{2}{5}}$ . © examsnet.com

question: For a particle executing simple harmonic motion, match the following statements (conditions) from column I to statements (shapes of graph) in column II Column I Column II a) Velocity-displacement graph $(w=1)$ i) Straight line b) Acceleration-displacement graph ii) Sinusoidal c) Acceleration - time graph iii) Circle d) Acceleration - velocity $(w \neq 1)$ iv) Ellipse [AP EAPCET 18 May 2024 Shift 1]
search_text: for a particle executing simple harmonic motion, match the following statements (conditions) from column i to statements (shapes of graph) in column ii column i column ii a) velocity-displacement graph $(w=1)$ i) straight line b) acceleration-displacement graph ii) sinusoidal c) acceleration - time graph iii) circle d) acceleration - velocity $(w \neq 1)$ iv) ellipse [ap eapcet 18 may 2024 shift 1] {'a': 'a-iv, b-i, c-ii, d-iii', 'b': 'a-iii, b-i, c-ii, d-iv', 'c': 'a-iii, b-ii, c-i, d-iv', 'd': 'a-iv, b-ii, c-i, d-iii'} 2024 2024-05-18 shift_1 physics   92 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: for a body performing simple harmonic motion, the relation between velocity and displacement $v=\omega \sqrt{a^{2}-x^{2}}$ square both side $v^{2}=\omega^{2}(a^{2}-x^{2})$ for ( $\omega=1$ ) $v^{2}+x^{2}=a^{2}$ (a) so, the graph between velocity and displacement will be a circle. (b) we know that, $x=a\sin\;\omega t$ differentiate w.r.t. to $t$ $\frac{dx}{dt}=v=+\omega a\cos\omega t$ again differentiate w.r.t. to $t$ , $\frac{d^{2}x}{dt^{2}}=a=-\omega^{2}a\sin\;\omega t$ from eq. (i), $a=-\omega^{2}x$ comparing from eq. $y=mx+c$ it is a equation of straight line with slope, $m=-\omega^{2}$ . so, the graph between acceleration and displacement will be a straight line. (c) from eq. (iii), $\frac{d^{2}x}{dt^{2}}=a=-\omega^{2}a\sin\;\omega t$ the graph between acceleration and time will be a function of sine wave. (d) from eq. $(a)$ , $v=\omega\sqrt{a^{2}-\omega^{2}}$ $v^{2}=\omega^{2}(a^{2}-x^{2})$ $x^{2}= \left(-\frac{v^{2}}{\omega^{2}}+a^{2}\right)$ $x=\sqrt{a^{2}-\frac{v^{2}}{\omega^{2}}}$ putting this value in eq. (iv), $a=-\omega^{2}\sqrt{a^{2}-\frac{v^{2}}{\omega^{2}}}$ square both side $a^{2}=\omega^{4}\left(a^{2}-\frac{v^{2}}{\omega^{2}}\right)$ $a^{2}=\omega^{4}a^{2}-v^{2}\omega^{2}$ $\left(\frac{a}{\omega^{2}}\right)^{2}=a^{2}-\frac{v^{2}}{\omega^{2}}$ $\left(\frac{a}{\omega^{2}}\right)^{2}+\left(\frac{v}{\omega}\right)^{2}=a^{2}$ when $\omega \neq 1$ , the graph between acceleration $a$ as a function of velocity $v$ in shm is an ellipse. © examsnet.com

question: Two satellites of masses $m$ and $1.5 m$ are revolving around the earth with different speeds in two circular orbits of heights $R_E$ and $2 R_E$ respectively, where $R_E$ is the radius of the earth. The ratio of the minimum and maximum gravitational forces on the earth due to the two satellites is [AP EAPCET 18 May 2024 Shift 1]
search_text: two satellites of masses $m$ and $1.5 m$ are revolving around the earth with different speeds in two circular orbits of heights $r_e$ and $2 r_e$ respectively, where $r_e$ is the radius of the earth. the ratio of the minimum and maximum gravitational forces on the earth due to the two satellites is [ap eapcet 18 may 2024 shift 1] {'a': '$\\;2:5$', 'b': '$\\;2:3$', 'c': '$\\;1:2$', 'd': '$\\;1:5$'} 2024 2024-05-18 shift_1 physics   93 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: let the mass of the earth be $m$ . for the first satellite of mass $m$ at height $r_e$ , the distance from earth's center is $r_1=r_e+r_e=2r_e$ . the magnitude of its gravitational pull on the earth is $f_1=\frac{g m m}{(2r_e)^2}=\frac{g m m}{4r_e^2}$ . for the second satellite of mass $1.5m$ at height $2r_e$ , the distance from earth's center is $r_2=r_e+2r_e=3r_e$ . the magnitude of its gravitational pull on the earth is $f_2=\frac{g m(1.5m)}{(3r_e)^2}=\frac{1.5g m m}{9r_e^2}=\frac{g m m}{6r_e^2}$ . the net gravitational force on the earth due to the two satellites is maximum when the two pulls are in the same direction: $f_{\max}=f_1+f_2=\frac{g m m}{4r_e^2}+\frac{g m m}{6r_e^2}=\frac{5g m m}{12r_e^2}$ . the net gravitational force is minimum when the two pulls are opposite in direction: $f_{\min}=|f_1-f_2|=\left|\frac{g m m}{4r_e^2}-\frac{g m m}{6r_e^2}\right|=\frac{g m m}{12r_e^2}$ . therefore, the required ratio is: $\frac{f_{\min}}{f_{\max}}=\frac{\frac{g m m}{12r_e^2}}{\frac{5g m m}{12r_e^2}}=\frac{1}{5}$ . thus, $f_{\min}:f_{\max}=1:5$ , which matches option d. © examsnet.com

question: Two copper wires $A$ and $B$ of lengths in the ratio $1: 2$ and diameters in the ratio $3: 2$ are stretched by forces in the ratio $3: 1$ . The ratio of the elastic potential energies stored per unit volume in the wires $A$ and $B$ is [AP EAPCET 18 May 2024 Shift 1]
search_text: two copper wires $a$ and $b$ of lengths in the ratio $1: 2$ and diameters in the ratio $3: 2$ are stretched by forces in the ratio $3: 1$ . the ratio of the elastic potential energies stored per unit volume in the wires $a$ and $b$ is [ap eapcet 18 may 2024 shift 1] {'a': '$2: 1$', 'b': '$4: 9$', 'c': '$16: 9$', 'd': '$4: 3$'} 2024 2024-05-18 shift_1 physics   94 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: lengths: $\;\frac{l_a}{l_b}=\;\frac{1}{2}$ diameters: $\;\frac{d_a}{d_b}=\;\frac{3}{2}$ implies $\;\frac{r_a}{r_b}=\;\frac{3}{2}$ . thus, $\;\frac{r_a^2}{r_b^2}=\;\frac{9}{4}$ . forces: $\;\frac{f_a}{f_b}=\;\frac{3}{1}$ elastic potential energy per unit volume is $u=\frac12 \frac{f\delta l}{v}$ using $y=\frac{f l}{a\delta l}$ , we get $\delta l=\frac{f l}{a y}$ . since $v=a l$ , $u=\frac12 \frac{f\cdot f l}{a l\cdot a y}=\frac12\frac{f^2}{a^2y}$ . thus $u\propto \frac{f^2}{a^2}$ . here $a\propto d^2$ , so $\frac{u_a}{u_b}=\left(\frac{f_a}{f_b}\right)^2\left(\frac{d_b}{d_a}\right)^4$ . substitute the ratios: $\frac{u_a}{u_b}=\left(\frac31\right)^2\left(\frac23\right)^4$ . $\frac{u_a}{u_b}=9\cdot\frac{16}{81}=\frac{16}{9}$ . therefore, the ratio of elastic potential energies stored per unit volume in wires $a$ and $b$ is $16:9$ . © examsnet.com

question: 216 small identical liquid drops each of surface area $A$ coalesce to form a bigger drop. If the surface tension of the liquid is $T$ , the energy released in the process is [AP EAPCET 18 May 2024 Shift 1]
search_text: 216 small identical liquid drops each of surface area $a$ coalesce to form a bigger drop. if the surface tension of the liquid is $t$ , the energy released in the process is [ap eapcet 18 may 2024 shift 1] {'a': '$360 at$', 'b': '$180 at$', 'c': '$90 at$', 'd': '$120 at$'} 2024 2024-05-18 shift_1 physics   95 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: to determine the energy released when 216 small liquid drops coalesce into a larger drop, follow these steps: number of small drops $=216$ surface area of each small drop $=a=4 \pi r^2$ surface tension of the liquid $=t$ calculations: volumes: volume of one small drop: $\;\frac{4}{3} \pi r^3$ total volume for 216 small drops: $216 \times \;\frac{4}{3} \pi r^3$ volume of the large drop: since volume is conserved, the volume of the large drop is: $\;\frac{4}{3} \pi r^3 = 216 \times \;\frac{4}{3} \pi r^3$ $r^3 = 6 r^3 \;\; \rightarrow \;\; r = 6 r$ surface areas: total surface area of 216 small drops: $216 \times 4 \pi r^2 = 864 \pi r^2$ surface area of the large drop: $4 \pi (6 r)^2 = 144 \pi r^2$ decrease in surface area: $\delta a = 864 \pi r^2 - 144 \pi r^2 = 720 \pi r^2$ energy released: using the formula $e = t \cdot \delta a$ : $\;e = t \cdot 720 \pi r^2$ $\;e = 180 \cdot t \cdot 4 \pi r^2$ $\;e = 180 a t$ thus, the energy released during the coalescence process is $180 a t$ . © examsnet.com

The thermal conductivity of the metal in $\mathrm{Wm}^{-1}\ \mathrm{K}^{-1}$ is (Latent heat of fusion $=80\ \mathrm{cal} / \mathrm{gm}$ ) [AP EAPCET 18 May 2024 Shift 1]
search_text: the length of a metal bar is $20\ \mathrm{cm}$ and the area of cross section is $4 \times 10^{-4}\ \mathrm{m}^2$ . if one end of the rod is kept in ice at $0^{\circ}\ \mathrm{c}$ and the other end is kept in steam at $100^{\circ}\ \mathrm{c}$ , the mass of ice melted in one minute is $5\ \mathrm{g}$ . the thermal conductivity of the metal in $\mathrm{wm}^{-1}\ \mathrm{k}^{-1}$ is (latent heat of fusion $=80\ \mathrm{cal} / \mathrm{gm}$ ) [ap eapcet 18 may 2024 shift 1] {'a': '140', 'b': '120', 'c': '100', 'd': '160'} 2024 2024-05-18 shift_1 physics   96 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: length of the rod, $x=20\ \mathrm{cm}=0.2\ \mathrm{m}$ temperatures at the ends: $\;t_1=0^{\circ}\ \mathrm{c}=273\ \mathrm{k}$ $\;t_2=100^{\circ}\ \mathrm{c}=373\ \mathrm{k}$ cross-sectional area, $a=4 \times 10^{-4}\ \mathrm{m}^2$ mass of ice melted, $m=5\ \mathrm{g}$ time, $t=1\ \mathrm{min}=60\ \mathrm{s}$ latent heat of fusion, $l_{\;\text{ice}\;}=80\ \mathrm{cal} / \mathrm{g} =336\ \mathrm{j} / \mathrm{g}$ calculation: total heat required to melt the ice: $q=m \times l_{\;\text{ice}\;}=5 \times 336=1680\ \mathrm{j}$ rate of heat transfer: $\;\frac{q}{t}=\;\frac{1680}{60}=28\ \mathrm{j} / \mathrm{s}$ thermal conductivity ( $k$ ): $\;k=\;\frac{\delta q \cdot x}{a \cdot \delta t}=\;\frac{28 \times 0.2}{4 \times 10^{-4}(373-273)}$ $\;k=\;\frac{1.4 \times 10^4}{100}$ $\;k=1.4 \times 10^2$ $\;k=140\ \mathrm{w} / \mathrm{mk}$ © examsnet.com

question: The work done by an ideal gas of 2 moles in increasing its volume from $V$ to $2V$ at constant temperature $T$ is $W$ . The work done by an ideal gas of 4 moles in increasing its volume from $V$ to $8V$ at constant temperature $\;\frac{T}{2}$ is [AP EAPCET 18 May 2024 Shift 1]
search_text: the work done by an ideal gas of 2 moles in increasing its volume from $v$ to $2v$ at constant temperature $t$ is $w$ . the work done by an ideal gas of 4 moles in increasing its volume from $v$ to $8v$ at constant temperature $\;\frac{t}{2}$ is [ap eapcet 18 may 2024 shift 1] {'a': '$w$', 'b': '$2w$', 'c': '$3w$', 'd': '$4w$'} 2024 2024-05-18 shift_1 physics   97 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: given: initial work done by the gas, $w_1=w$ final volume for the first process, $v_{f_1}=2v$ initial volume for the first process, $v_{i_1}=v$ temperature for the first process, $t_1=t$ number of moles for the first process, $n=2$ the work done by an ideal gas during an isothermal expansion is given by the equation: $w=n \cdot r \cdot t \ln \left( \frac{v_f}{v_i} \right)$ substituting the given values for the first process: $w_1=2 \cdot r \cdot t \ln \left( \frac{2v}{v} \right) =2 \cdot r \cdot t \ln 2$ for the second process: final volume, $v_{f_2}=8v$ initial volume, $v_{i_2}=v$ temperature, $t_2=\;\frac{t}{2}$ number of moles, $n_2=4$ the work done for the second process is: $w_2=n_2 \cdot r \cdot t_2 \ln \left( \frac{v_{f_2}}{v_{i_2}} \right)$ substituting the values: $\;w_2=4 \cdot r \cdot \;\frac{t}{2} \ln \left( \frac{8v}{v} \right)$ $\;w_2=2 \cdot r \cdot t \ln (2^3)$ $\;w_2=3 \cdot 2 \cdot r \cdot t \ln 2$ this simplifies to: $w_2=3 \cdot w$ hence, the work done by the ideal gas in the second process is $3w$ . © examsnet.com

question: When 40 J of heat is absorbed by a monatomic gas, the increase in the intermal energy of the gas is [AP EAPCET 18 May 2024 Shift 1]
search_text: when 40 j of heat is absorbed by a monatomic gas, the increase in the intermal energy of the gas is [ap eapcet 18 may 2024 shift 1] {'a': '$12\\ \\mathrm{j}$', 'b': '$16\\ \\mathrm{j}$', 'c': '$24\\ \\mathrm{j}$', 'd': '$32\\ \\mathrm{j}$'} 2024 2024-05-18 shift_1 physics   98 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: to analyze the increase in internal energy when heat is absorbed by a monoatomic gas: first, we know that the heat absorbed, $q$ , is given as 40 j . for a monoatomic ideal gas, the specific heat capacities are: $\;c_p=\;\frac{5r}{2}$ $\;c_v=\;\frac{3r}{2}$ the relationship for heat transfer in terms of $c_p$ is: $q=n c_p \delta t$ substituting in known values: $40=n\cdot\;\frac{5r}{2}\cdot\delta t$ from this, we obtain: $nr\delta t=16\;\;(i)$ next, we determine the increase in internal energy, $\delta u$ , which is given by: $\;\delta u=n c_v \delta t$ $\;\delta u=n\cdot\;\frac{3}{2}r\delta t$ $\;\delta u=\;\frac{3}{2}\cdot nr\delta t$ using equation (i), we substitute for $nr\delta t$ : $\delta u=\;\frac{3}{2}\times 16$ this simplifies to: $\delta u=24\ \mathrm{j}$ thus, the increase in the internal energy of the gas is 24 j . © examsnet.com

question: In a Carnot engine, the absolute temperature of the source is $25\%$ more than the absolute temperature of the sink. The efficiency of the engine is [AP EAPCET 18 May 2024 Shift 1]
search_text: in a carnot engine, the absolute temperature of the source is $25\%$ more than the absolute temperature of the sink. the efficiency of the engine is [ap eapcet 18 may 2024 shift 1] {'a': '$10\\%$', 'b': '$50\\%$', 'c': '$25\\%$', 'd': '$20\\%$'} 2024 2024-05-18 shift_1 physics   99 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: the efficiency of a carnot engine is calculated using the formula: $\eta = 1 - \frac{t_{\text{sink}}}{t_{\text{source}}}$ given that the absolute temperature of the source ( $t_{\text{source}}$ ) is $25\%$ more than that of the sink ( $t_{\text{sink}}$ ), we can express this relationship as: $t_{\text{source}} = t_{\text{sink}} + \frac{25 \times t_{\text{sink}}}{100}$ simplifying, this becomes: $t_{\text{source}} = 1.25 \times t_{\text{sink}}$ substituting into the efficiency equation, we have: $\eta = \left(1 - \frac{t_{\text{sink}}}{1.25 \times t_{\text{sink}}}\right) \times 100\%$ this simplifies to: $\eta = \left(1 - \frac{1}{1.25}\right) \times 100\%$ $\eta = (1-0.8) \times 100\%$ $\eta = 0.2 \times 100\%$ thus, the efficiency of the carnot engine is: $\eta = 20\%$ © examsnet.com

question: The molar specific heat capacity of a diatomic gas at constant pressure is $C$ . The molar specific heat capacity of a monoatomic gas at constant volume is [AP EAPCET 18 May 2024 Shift 1]
search_text: the molar specific heat capacity of a diatomic gas at constant pressure is $c$ . the molar specific heat capacity of a monoatomic gas at constant volume is [ap eapcet 18 may 2024 shift 1] {'a': '$\\;\\frac{2c}{7}$', 'b': '$\\;\\frac{3c}{7}$', 'c': '$\\;\\frac{c}{7}$', 'd': '$\\;\\frac{4c}{7}$'} 2024 2024-05-18 shift_1 physics   100 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: molar heat capacity at constant pressure for a diatomic gas, $c_p=c$ we need to find the molar heat capacity at constant volume for a monoatomic gas, $c_v$ . calculations: for a diatomic gas: for a diatomic gas, the molar heat capacity at constant volume is: $c_v=\;\frac{5}{2} r$ therefore, the relation between $c_p$ and $c_v$ is: $c_p=c_v+r=\;\frac{5}{2} r+r=\;\frac{7}{2} r$ since $c_p=c$ , we have: $\;\frac{7}{2} r=c$ solving for $r$ , we get: $r=\;\frac{2c}{7}$ for a monoatomic gas: the molar heat capacity at constant volume for a monoatomic gas is: $c_v=\;\frac{3}{2} r$ substituting the value of $r$ from equation (i): $c_v=\;\frac{3}{2} \cdot \;\frac{2c}{7}=\;\frac{3c}{7}$ therefore, the molar specific heat capacity of a monoatomic gas at constant volume is $\;\frac{3c}{7}$ . © examsnet.com

search_text: two stretched strings $a$ and $b$ when vibrated together produce 4 beats per second. if the tension applied to the string $a$ increased, the number of beats produced per second is increased to 7 . if the frequency of string $b$ is $480\,\text{hz}$ initially, the frequency of string $a$ is [ap eapcet 18 may 2024 shift 1] {'a': '$473\\,\\text{hz}$', 'b': '$476\\,\\text{hz}$', 'c': '$484\\,\\text{hz}$', 'd': '$487\\,\\text{hz}$'} 2024 2024-05-18 shift_1 physics   101 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: to determine the frequency of string $a$ , we start with the following information: initial beat frequency is 4 beats per second. frequency of string $b,\ f_b=480\,\text{hz}$ . the relation for beat frequency: $\left| f_a-f_b \right|=4$ . given that the tension on string $a$ is increased, the frequency of $a$ will increase, leading to an increase in the beat frequency. the new beat frequency becomes 7 beats per second. the vibration frequency of a string is determined by the formula: $f=\frac{n}{2l}\cdot\sqrt{\frac{t}{\mu}}$ where: $n$ is the mode of vibration. $l$ is the length of the string. $t$ is the tension in the string. $\mu$ is the linear mass density. since the tension in string $a$ is increased, we know the frequency of $a$ increases. consequently, the following must be true for the beat frequency to increase: $f_a-f_b=4\ \text{or}\ f_b-f_a=4$ however, since the frequency of $a$ increases and the beat frequency becomes 7, it implies that: $f_a-f_b=7$ given: initially, $f_a-480=4$ , thus $f_a=484\,\text{hz}$ . therefore, as $f_a$ increases past 480 hz and still satisfies the condition where the beat frequency becomes 7 , this confirms that initially: $f_a=484\,\text{hz}$ © examsnet.com

(1) into the equation: $\beta'=\;\frac{1.5}{0.9}\times 3$ calculating the above expression: $\beta'=\;\frac{45}{9}=5\ \mathrm{mm}$ thus, the new fringe width is 5 mm . © examsnet.com

search_text: two point charges $+6 \mu \mathrm{c}$ and $+10 \mu \mathrm{c}$ kept at certain distance repel each other with a force of $30 \mathrm{n}$ . if each charge is given an additional charge of $-8 \mu \mathrm{c}$ , the two charges [ap eapcet 18 may 2024 shift 1] {'a': 'attract with a force of $2 \\mathrm{n}$', 'b': 'repel with a force of $2 \\mathrm{n}$', 'c': 'attract with a force of $15 \\mathrm{n}$', 'd': 'repel with a force of $15 \\mathrm{n}$'} 2024 2024-05-18 shift_1 physics   104 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: given: initial charges: $\;q_1=+6 \mu \mathrm{c}=6 \times 10^{-6} \mathrm{c}$ $\;q_2=+10 \mu \mathrm{c}=10 \times 10^{-6} \mathrm{c}$ force of repulsion: $f=30 \mathrm{n}$ using coulomb's law: $f=\frac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0} \cdot \frac{q_1 q_2}{r^2}$ solve for $r^2$ : $\;r^2=\frac{9 \times 10^9 \times 6 \times 10 \times 10^{-12}}{30}$ $\;r^2=18 \times 10^{-3}$ adding additional charges: each charge receives an additional $-8 \mu \mathrm{c}$ : $\;q_1^{'}=+6-8=-2 \mu \mathrm{c}$ $\;q_2^{'}=+10-8=+2 \mu \mathrm{c}$ recalculate the force using coulomb's law: $f^{'}=\frac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0} \cdot \frac{q_1^{'} \cdot q_2^{'}}{r^2}$ substitute $q_1^{'}$ and $q_2^{'}$ : $f^{'}=\frac{9 \times 10^9 \times 2 \times 2 \times 10^{-12}}{18 \times 10^{-3}}$ (from equation 1) $f^{'}=2 \mathrm{n}$ © examsnet.com

search_text: in a region, the electric field is $(30 \overline{i}+40 j) \mathrm{nc}^{-1}$ . if the electric potential at the origin is zero, the electric potential at the point $(1 \mathrm{m}, 2 \mathrm{m})$ is [ap eapcet 18 may 2024 shift 1] {'a': '$-60 \\mathrm{v}$', 'b': '$-75 \\mathrm{v}$', 'c': '$-55 \\mathrm{v}$', 'd': '$-110 \\mathrm{v}$'} 2024 2024-05-18 shift_1 physics   106 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: to find the electric potential at the point $(1 \mathrm{m}, 2 \mathrm{m})$ , we begin with the given electric field and displacement vector: $\;e = (30 \hat{i} + 40 \hat{j}) \mathrm{n/c}$ $\;d = (1 \hat{i} + 2 \hat{j}) \mathrm{m}$ the formula for electric potential $v$ with respect to a chosen reference point is given by: $v = -e \cdot r$ applying the formula, we compute the dot product: $v = -(30 \hat{i} + 40 \hat{j}) \cdot (1 \hat{i} + 2 \hat{j})$ break it down as follows: $v \;= -(30 \cdot 1 + 40 \cdot 2)$ $v \;= -(30+80)$ $v \;= -110 \mathrm{v}$ thus, the electric potential at the point $(1 \mathrm{m}, 2 \mathrm{m})$ is -110 v . © examsnet.com

question: In a potentiometer, the area of cross section of the wire is $4 \text{cm}^2$ , the current flowing in the circuit is $1 \text{A}$ and the potential gradient is $7.5 \text{Vm}^{-1}$ , then the resistivity of the potentiometer wire is [AP EAPCET 18 May 2024 Shift 1]
search_text: in a potentiometer, the area of cross section of the wire is $4 \text{cm}^2$ , the current flowing in the circuit is $1 \text{a}$ and the potential gradient is $7.5 \text{vm}^{-1}$ , then the resistivity of the potentiometer wire is [ap eapcet 18 may 2024 shift 1] {'a': '$\\; 3 \\times 10^{-3} \\omega \\text{m}$', 'b': '$\\; 2 \\times 10^{-6} \\omega \\text{m}$', 'c': '$\\; 4 \\times 10^{-2} \\omega \\text{m}$', 'd': '$\\; 5 \\times 10^{-4} \\omega \\text{m}$'} 2024 2024-05-18 shift_1 physics   107 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: to find the resistivity of the potentiometer wire, we are provided with the following information: area of cross-section (a): $4 \text{cm}^2 = 4 \times 10^{-4} \text{m}^2$ current (i): 1 a potential gradient $(\;\text{v/l}) : 7.5 \text{v/m}$ we need to calculate the resistivity ( $\rho$ ) of the wire. calculation: from ohm's law, we know the following relationship: $v = i \cdot r$ the resistance $r$ for a wire can be expressed in terms of its resistivity: $r = \rho \; \frac{l}{a}$ thus, substituting $r$ in the equation for $v$ : $v = i \cdot \; \frac{\rho l}{a}$ rearranging this equation to solve for resistivity ( $\rho$ ): $\rho = \; \frac{v}{l} \cdot \; \frac{a}{i}$ substitute the known values: $\rho = \left(7.5 \text{v/m}\right) \cdot \left(\; \frac{4 \times 10^{-4} \text{m}^2}{1 \text{a}}\right)$ calculate $\rho$ : $\rho = \; \frac{7.5 \times 4 \times 10^{-4}}{1}$ $\; \rho = 30 \times 10^{-4}$ $\; \rho = 3 \times 10^{-3} \omega\text{-m}$ therefore, the resistivity of the potentiometer wire is $3 \times 10^{-3} \omega\text{-m}$ . © examsnet.com

search_text: drift speed $(v)$ varies with the intensity of electric field $(e)$ as per the relation [ap eapcet 18 may 2024 shift 1] {'a': '$\\; v \\propto e$', 'b': '$\\; v \\propto \\; \\frac{1}{e}$', 'c': '$\\; v \\propto e^2$', 'd': '$\\; v \\propto e^{-2}$'} 2024 2024-05-18 shift_1 physics   108 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: drift velocity is the average velocity acquired by free electrons in a conductor under the influence of an applied electric field. drift velocity is related to the electric field $e$ through the mobility $\mu$ of the charge carriers as: $\mu = \frac{v}{e} \rightarrow v = \mu e$ for a given material at a given temperature, the mobility $\mu$ is a constant. hence the drift speed is directly proportional to the applied electric field: $v \propto e$ so the correct relation is $v \propto e$ , which corresponds to option a. © examsnet.com

question: A current carrying coil experiences a torque due to a magnetic field. The value of the torque is $80\%$ of the maximum possible torque. The angle between the magnetic field and the normal to the plane of the coil is [AP EAPCET 18 May 2024 Shift 1]
search_text: a current carrying coil experiences a torque due to a magnetic field. the value of the torque is $80\%$ of the maximum possible torque. the angle between the magnetic field and the normal to the plane of the coil is [ap eapcet 18 may 2024 shift 1] {'a': '$30^{\\circ}$', 'b': '$45^{\\circ}$', 'c': '$\\tan^{-1} \\left( \\frac{3}{4} \\right)$', 'd': '$\\tan^{-1} \\left( \\frac{4}{3} \\right)$'} 2024 2024-05-18 shift_1 physics   109 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: a coil carrying a current experiences a torque when placed in a magnetic field. this torque is quantified by the following relation: $\tau = n \cdot i \cdot a \cdot b \cdot \sin \theta$ where $n$ is the number of turns in the coil, $i$ is the current flowing through the coil, $a$ is the area of the coil, $b$ is the magnetic field strength, and $\theta$ is the angle between the magnetic field and the normal to the plane of the coil. the torque is at its maximum when $\sin \theta = 1$ , which occurs at $\theta = 90^{\circ}$ . thus, the maximum torque $\tau_{\max}$ can be expressed as: $\tau_{\max} = n \cdot i \cdot a \cdot b$ according to the problem, the experienced torque is $80\%$ of this maximum: $n \cdot i \cdot a \cdot b \cdot \sin \theta = 0.8 \cdot \tau_{\max}$ substituting $\tau_{\text{max}}$ from equation (i): $n \cdot i \cdot a \cdot b \cdot \sin \theta = \frac{80}{100} \cdot (n \cdot i \cdot a \cdot b)$ this simplifies to: $\sin \theta = \frac{4}{5}$ we know that: $\cos \theta = \sqrt{1 - \sin^2 \theta} = \frac{3}{5}$ thus, the tangent of the angle $\theta$ becomes: $\tan \theta = \frac{\sin \theta}{\cos \theta} = \frac{4/5}{3/5} = \frac{4}{3}$ therefore, the angle $\theta$ is: $\theta = \tan^{-1} \left( \frac{4}{3} \right)$ © examsnet.com
