question: An electron is moving with a velocity $(2 \hat{i}+3 \hat{j}) \text{m/s}$ in an electric field $(3 \hat{i}+6 \hat{j}+2 \hat{k}) \text{V/s}$ and a magnetic field of $(2 \hat{j}+3 \hat{k}) \text{T}$ . Then the magnitude and direction (with $x$ -axis) of the Lorentz force acting on the electron is [AP EAPCET 18 May 2024 Shift 1]
search_text: an electron is moving with a velocity $(2 \hat{i}+3 \hat{j}) \text{m/s}$ in an electric field $(3 \hat{i}+6 \hat{j}+2 \hat{k}) \text{v/s}$ and a magnetic field of $(2 \hat{j}+3 \hat{k}) \text{t}$ . then the magnitude and direction (with $x$ -axis) of the lorentz force acting on the electron is [ap eapcet 18 may 2024 shift 1] {'a': '$9.6 \\times 10^{-19} \\text{n}, \\quad \\theta = \\cos^{-1}\\left(\\frac{2}{\\sqrt{5}}\\right)$', 'b': '$9.6 \\times 10^{-19} \\text{n}, \\quad \\theta = \\cos^{-1}\\left(\\frac{5}{\\sqrt{2}}\\right)$', 'c': '$2.15 \\times 10^{-18} \\text{n}, \\quad \\theta = \\cos^{-1}\\left(\\frac{2}{\\sqrt{5}}\\right)$', 'd': '$2.15 \\times 10^{-18} \\text{n}, \\quad \\theta = \\cos^{-1}\\left(\\frac{5}{\\sqrt{2}}\\right)$'} 2024 2024-05-18 shift_1 physics   110 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: velocity of the electron: $v = (2 \hat{i}+3 \hat{j}) \text{m/s}$ electric field: $e = (3 \hat{i}+6 \hat{j}+2 \hat{k}) \text{v/m}$ magnetic field: $b = (2 \hat{j}+3 \hat{k}) \top$ the lorentz force is calculated using the formula: $f = q (e + v \times b)$ first, solve for $v \times b$ : $v \times b = \begin{vmatrix} \hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k} \\ 2 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 3 \end{vmatrix}$ $= (9 \hat{i} - 6 \hat{j} + 4 \hat{k})$ now, find the total force $f$ : $f = q[(3 \hat{i}+6 \hat{j}+2 \hat{k})+(9 \hat{i}-6 \hat{j}+4 \hat{k})]$ $= q[12 \hat{i}+6 \hat{k}]$ for an electron, $q = 1.6 \times 10^{-19} \text{c}$ : $f = 1.6 \times 10^{-19} \times [12 \hat{i}+6 \hat{k}]$ $|f| = 1.6 \times 10^{-19} \times \sqrt{12^2+6^2}$ $|f| = 1.6 \times 10^{-19} \times \sqrt{180}$ $|f| = 2.15 \times 10^{-18} \text{n}$ to determine the direction of $f$ with respect to the $x$ -axis: $\theta = \tan^{-1}\left(\frac{6}{12}\right) = \tan^{-1}\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)$ thus, we have: $\cos \theta = \frac{2}{\sqrt{5}} \quad \rightarrow \quad \theta = \cos^{-1}\left(\frac{2}{\sqrt{5}}\right)$ © examsnet.com

question: A magnet suspended in a uniform magnetic field is heated so as to reduce its magnetic moment by $19\%$ . By doing this, the time period of the magnet approximately [AP EAPCET 18 May 2024 Shift 1]
search_text: a magnet suspended in a uniform magnetic field is heated so as to reduce its magnetic moment by $19\%$ . by doing this, the time period of the magnet approximately [ap eapcet 18 may 2024 shift 1] {'a': 'increases by $19\\%$', 'b': 'decreases by $4\\%$', 'c': 'increases by $19 \\%$', 'd': 'decreases by $4 \\%$'} 2024 2024-05-18 shift_1 physics   111 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: we know that the time period for an oscillating magnet is given by: $t=2\pi\sqrt{\frac{i}{m b_h}}$ where: $m$ is the magnetic moment, $i$ is the moment of inertia, and $b_h$ is the horizontal component of the earth's magnetic field. given that the magnetic moment decreases by $19\%$ , we can express the initial magnetic moment as $m_1=m$ and the reduced magnetic moment as: $m_2=m-\frac{19\times m}{100}=0.81m$ from the equation for the time period, we derive: $\frac{t_1}{t_2}=\sqrt{\frac{m_2}{m_1}}$ substituting the values we have: $\frac{t_1}{t_2}=\sqrt{\frac{0.81m}{m}}=\sqrt{0.81}=\frac{9}{10}$ rearranging gives: $t_2=\frac{10}{9}t_1$ this implies: $t_2=1.11t_1$ so, the new time period $t_2$ is $t_1+0.11t_1$ , which indicates that: the time period increases by $11\%$ . © examsnet.com

question: If the current through an inductor increases from $2 A$ to $3 A$ , the magnetic energy stored in the inductor increases by [AP EAPCET 18 May 2024 Shift 1]
search_text: if the current through an inductor increases from $2 a$ to $3 a$ , the magnetic energy stored in the inductor increases by [ap eapcet 18 may 2024 shift 1] {'a': '$125\\%$', 'b': '$225\\%$', 'c': '$50\\%$', 'd': '$75\\%$'} 2024 2024-05-18 shift_1 physics   112 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: the magnetic energy stored in an inductor is given by the formula: $u = \frac{1}{2} l i^2$ where: $u$ is the energy stored, $l$ is the inductance, $i$ is the current through the inductor. in this case, the current increases from $i_1 = 2 a$ to $i_2 = 3 a$ . calculating the initial energy stored $u_1$ when the current is $i_1$ : $u_1 = \frac{1}{2} l i_1^2 = \frac{1}{2} \times l \times 4 = 2 l$ calculating the energy stored $u_2$ when the current is $i_2$ : $u_2 = \frac{1}{2} l i_2^2 = \frac{1}{2} \times l \times 9 = 4.5 l$ the increase in energy stored, $\delta u$ , is: $\delta u = u_2 - u_1 = 4.5 l - 2 l = 2.5 l$ to find the percentage increase in energy stored: percentage increase $= \frac{\delta u}{u_1} \times 100\% = \frac{2.5 l}{2 l} \times 100\% = 125\%$ © examsnet.com

question: The Solar Radiation is [AP EAPCET 18 May 2024 Shift 1]
search_text: the solar radiation is [ap eapcet 18 may 2024 shift 1] {'a': 'stationary wave', 'b': 'mechanical wave', 'c': 'transverse em wave', 'd': 'longitudinal em wave'} 2024 2024-05-18 shift_1 physics   114 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: correct answer: transverse em wave (option c). solar radiation is electromagnetic radiation emitted by the sun, consisting of visible light, ultraviolet, infrared, and other electromagnetic waves. electromagnetic waves are produced by oscillating electric and magnetic fields, denoted by $\vec{e}$ and $\vec{b}$ , which are mutually perpendicular and also perpendicular to the direction of propagation. therefore, electromagnetic waves are transverse in nature — they are transverse em waves . they are not mechanical waves, since mechanical waves (like sound) require a material medium, whereas solar radiation travels through the vacuum of space. they are not stationary waves, since a stationary (standing) wave is formed by the superposition of two identical waves travelling in opposite directions, which is not the case for radiation propagating from the sun. they are not longitudinal em waves, because a longitudinal wave has oscillations along the direction of propagation, which does not occur for electromagnetic radiation. hence, solar radiation is a transverse em wave , i.e. option c. © examsnet.com

question: Energy required to remove an electron from aluminum surface is $4.2\ \mathrm{eV}$ . If light of wavelength $2000\ \text{\AA}$ falls on the surface, the velocity of the fastest electron ejected from the surface will be [AP EAPCET 18 May 2024 Shift 1]
search_text: energy required to remove an electron from aluminum surface is $4.2\ \mathrm{ev}$ . if light of wavelength $2000\ \text{\aa}$ falls on the surface, the velocity of the fastest electron ejected from the surface will be [ap eapcet 18 may 2024 shift 1] {'a': '$8.4\\times 10^5\\ \\mathrm{ms}^{-1}$', 'b': '$7.4\\times 10^5\\ \\mathrm{ms}^{-1}$', 'c': '$6.4\\times 10^5\\ \\mathrm{ms}^{-1}$', 'd': '$8.4\\times 10^6\\ \\mathrm{ms}^{-1}$'} 2024 2024-05-18 shift_1 physics   115 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: the energy required to remove an electron from the aluminium surface is the work function $\phi_0=4.2\ \mathrm{ev}$ . the wavelength of the incident light is $\lambda=2000\ \text{\aa}=2000\times10^{-10}\ \mathrm{m}=2\times10^{-7}\ \mathrm{m}$ . energy of the incident photon: $e=\frac{hc}{\lambda}=\frac{6.6\times10^{-34}\times3\times10^{8}}{2\times10^{-7}}=9.9\times10^{-19}\ \mathrm{j}$ in electron-volts: $e=\frac{9.9\times10^{-19}}{1.6\times10^{-19}}\approx6.2\ \mathrm{ev}$ using einstein's photoelectric equation: $\frac{1}{2}mv_{\max}^{2}=e-\phi_0$ $\frac{1}{2}mv_{\max}^{2}=6.2-4.2=2.0\ \mathrm{ev}$ $\frac{1}{2}mv_{\max}^{2}=2.0\times1.6\times10^{-19}=3.2\times10^{-19}\ \mathrm{j}$ taking $m=9.1\times10^{-31}\ \mathrm{kg}$ for the electron: $v_{\max}=\sqrt{\frac{2\times3.2\times10^{-19}}{9.1\times10^{-31}}}=\sqrt{\frac{6.4}{9.1}\times10^{12}}$ $v_{\max}=\sqrt{7.03\times10^{11}}=8.4\times10^{5}\ \mathrm{ms}^{-1}$ hence the velocity of the fastest ejected electron is $8.4\times10^{5}\ \mathrm{ms}^{-1}$ , which is option (0). the option $8.4\times10^{6}\ \mathrm{ms}^{-1}$ is a distractor arising from a factor-of-ten error, so the currently marked answer is correct. © examsnet.com

question: If the bonding energy of the electron in a hydrogen atom is $13.6  \text{eV}$ , then energy required to remove electron from first excited state of $L i^{2+}$ is [AP EAPCET 18 May 2024 Shift 1]
search_text: if the bonding energy of the electron in a hydrogen atom is $13.6  \text{ev}$ , then energy required to remove electron from first excited state of $l i^{2+}$ is [ap eapcet 18 may 2024 shift 1] {'a': '$122.4  \\text{ev}$', 'b': '$3.4  \\text{ev}$', 'c': '$13.6  \\text{ev}$', 'd': '$30.6  \\text{ev}$'} 2024 2024-05-18 shift_1 physics   116 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: given: the binding energy of the electron in a hydrogen atom is $13.6 \text{ ev}$ . we know: the energy of an electron in the $n$ -th state of a hydrogen-like ion is given by: $e_n=-13.6 \frac{z^2}{n^2} \text{ ev}$ for $\mathrm{li}^{2+}$ , the atomic number is $z=3$ . the first excited state corresponds to $n=2$ . substitute $z=3$ and $n=2$ into the equation: $e_2=-13.6 \times \frac{3^2}{2^2}=-13.6 \times \frac{9}{4}$ $e_2=-30.6 \text{ ev}$ the energy required to remove the electron is the negative of the energy of the state, since $e_2 + e = 0$ : $-30.6 + e = 0$ $e=+30.6 \text{ ev}$ therefore, the energy required to remove the electron from the first excited state of $\mathrm{li}^{2+}$ is $30.6 \text{ ev}$ . hence, the correct option is $30.6 \text{ ev}$ (option d). © examsnet.com

question: A mixture consists of two radioactive materials $A_1$ and $A_2$ with half lives of $20\ \mathrm{s}$ and $10\ \mathrm{s}$ respectively. Initially the mixture has $40\ \mathrm{g}$ of $A_1$ and $160\ \mathrm{g}$ of $A_2$ . The amount of the two in the mixture will become equal after [AP EAPCET 18 May 2024 Shift 1]
search_text: a mixture consists of two radioactive materials $a_1$ and $a_2$ with half lives of $20\ \mathrm{s}$ and $10\ \mathrm{s}$ respectively. initially the mixture has $40\ \mathrm{g}$ of $a_1$ and $160\ \mathrm{g}$ of $a_2$ . the amount of the two in the mixture will become equal after [ap eapcet 18 may 2024 shift 1] {'a': '$\\;60\\ \\mathrm{s}$', 'b': '$\\;80\\ \\mathrm{s}$', 'c': '$\\;20\\ \\mathrm{s}$', 'd': '$\\;40\\ \\mathrm{s}$'} 2024 2024-05-18 shift_1 physics   117 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: given: initial amount of $a_1=40\ \mathrm{g}$ initial amount of $a_2=160\ \mathrm{g}$ half-life of $a_1,\ t_{a_1}=20\ \mathrm{s}$ half-life of $a_2,\ t_{a_2}=10\ \mathrm{s}$ to determine when the amounts of $a_1$ and $a_2$ will be equal, we use the decay formula: $n=n_0 \left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{t/t}$ for $a_1$ , the remaining amount is: $n_{a_1}=40 \left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{t/20}$ for $a_2$ , the remaining amount is: $n_{a_2}=160 \left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{t/10}$ to find the time when these amounts are equal, set $n_{a_1}=n_{a_2}$ : $40 \left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{t/20}\;=160 \left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{t/10}$ dividing both sides by $40$ and taking reciprocals gives: $2^{t/10}\;=4 \cdot 2^{t/20} \rightarrow 2^{\frac{t}{10}-\frac{t}{20}}=4$ $2^{t/20}\;=2^2 \rightarrow \frac{t}{20}=2$ $t\;=40\ \mathrm{s}$ verification: at $t=40\ \mathrm{s}$ , $n_{a_1}=40\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{2}=10\ \mathrm{g}$ and $n_{a_2}=160\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{4}=10\ \mathrm{g}$ , so the amounts are indeed equal. therefore, the amounts of $a_1$ and $a_2$ in the mixture will become equal after 40 seconds. © examsnet.com

question: If $n_e$ and $n_h$ are concentrations of electrons and holes in a semi-conductor, then the intrinsic carrier concentration $(n_j)$ in thermal equilibrium is [AP EAPCET 18 May 2024 Shift 1]
search_text: if $n_e$ and $n_h$ are concentrations of electrons and holes in a semi-conductor, then the intrinsic carrier concentration $(n_j)$ in thermal equilibrium is [ap eapcet 18 may 2024 shift 1] {'a': '$\\; n_i = \\sqrt{\\frac{n_e}{n_h}}$', 'b': '$\\; n_i = \\; \\frac{n_h}{n_e}$', 'c': '$\\; n_i = \\sqrt{n_e n_h}$', 'd': '$\\; n_i = n_e + n_h$'} 2024 2024-05-18 shift_1 physics   118 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: according to the law of mass action, for a semiconductor in thermal equilibrium the product of the electron concentration and hole concentration is a constant equal to the square of the intrinsic carrier concentration: $n_e\, n_h = n_i^{2}$ therefore, rearranging for the intrinsic carrier concentration, $n_i = \sqrt{n_e\, n_h}$ this relation holds in thermal equilibrium for both intrinsic and extrinsic (doped) semiconductors; for a pure intrinsic semiconductor it reduces to $n_i = n_e = n_h$ . hence the correct option is $n_i = \sqrt{n_e n_h}$ . © examsnet.com

search_text: in the given digital circuit if the inputs are $a=1, b=1$ and $c=1$ then the values of $y_1$ and $y_2$ are respectively [ap eapcet 18 may 2024 shift 1] {'a': '$\\;0,1$', 'b': '$\\;0,0$', 'c': '$\\;1,1$', 'd': '$\\;1,0$'} 2024 2024-05-18 shift_1 physics   119 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: given, input, $a=1$ $\;b=1$ $\;c=1$ here, $b$ and $c$ are inputs for nand gate. so, output $y_1\;=\overline{b \cdot c}$ $y_1\;=\overline{1 \cdot 1} \rightarrow y_1=0$ now, $\overline{a}$ and $y_1$ are inputs for nor gate. so, output, $y_2\;=\overline{\overline{a}+y_1}$ $y_2\;=\overline{0+0} \rightarrow y_2=1$ therefore, $y_1=0, y_2=1$ © examsnet.com

question: If the maximum and minimum voltages of an $A \cdot M$ wave are $V_{\max}$ and $V_{\min}$ respectively. Then the modulation factor ' $m$ ' is [AP EAPCET 18 May 2024 Shift 1]
search_text: if the maximum and minimum voltages of an $a \cdot m$ wave are $v_{\max}$ and $v_{\min}$ respectively. then the modulation factor ' $m$ ' is [ap eapcet 18 may 2024 shift 1] {'a': '$\\frac{v_{\\max}+v_{\\min}}{v_{\\max} \\cdot v_{\\min}}$', 'b': '$\\frac{v_{\\max} - v_{\\min}}{v_{\\max} + v_{\\min}}$', 'c': '$\\frac{2 v_{\\max} v_{\\min}}{v_{\\max} + v_{\\min}}$', 'd': '$\\frac{v_{\\max}+v_{\\min}}{v_{\\max}-v_{\\min}}$'} 2024 2024-05-18 shift_1 physics   120 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: maximum voltage of an am wave: $v_{\max}$ minimum voltage of an am wave: $v_{\;\text{min}\;}$ amplitude of the modulating signal is calculated as: $a_m = \frac{v_{\max} - v_{\min}}{2}$ amplitude of the carrier signal is calculated as: $a_c = \frac{v_{\max} + v_{\min}}{2}$ the modulation index or modulation factor $m$ is defined as the ratio of the amplitude of the modulating signal to the amplitude of the carrier signal: $m = \frac{a_m}{a_c}$ substituting the expressions for $a_m$ and $a_c$ , the modulation index becomes: $m = \frac{\frac{v_{\max} - v_{\min}}{2}}{\frac{v_{\max} + v_{\min}}{2}} \rightarrow m = \frac{v_{\max} - v_{\min}}{v_{\max} + v_{\min}}$ © examsnet.com

question: The de Broglie wavelength of a particle of mass $1\ \mathrm{mg}$ moving with a velocity of $10\ \mathrm{ms}^{-1}$ is $( h=6.63 \times 10^{-34}\ \mathrm{J}\ \mathrm{s})$ [AP EAPCET 18 May 2024 Shift 1]
search_text: the de broglie wavelength of a particle of mass $1\ \mathrm{mg}$ moving with a velocity of $10\ \mathrm{ms}^{-1}$ is $( h=6.63 \times 10^{-34}\ \mathrm{j}\ \mathrm{s})$ [ap eapcet 18 may 2024 shift 1] {'a': '$\\;6.63 \\times 10^{-29}\\ \\mathrm{m}$', 'b': '$\\;6.63 \\times 10^{-31}\\ \\mathrm{m}$', 'c': '$\\;6.63 \\times 10^{-34}\\ \\mathrm{m}$', 'd': '$\\;6.63 \\times 10^{-22}\\ \\mathrm{m}$'} 2024 2024-05-18 shift_1 chemistry   121 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: to calculate the de-broglie wavelength of a particle, we use the formula: $\lambda = \frac{h}{mv}$ where $\lambda$ is the wavelength, $h$ is planck's constant, $m$ is the mass of the particle, and $v$ is the velocity of the particle. given: mass $m=1\ \mathrm{mg} =1 \times 10^{-3}\ \mathrm{g}=1 \times 10^{-6}\ \mathrm{kg}$ velocity $v=10\ \mathrm{m/s}$ planck's constant $h=6.63 \times 10^{-34}\ \mathrm{js}$ substitute these values into the formula: $\lambda = \frac{6.63 \times 10^{-34}}{1 \times 10^{-6} \times 10} = \frac{6.63 \times 10^{-34}}{10^{-5}} = 6.63 \times 10^{-29}\ \mathrm{m}$ therefore, the de-broglie wavelength of the particle is $6.63 \times 10^{-29}\ \mathrm{m}$ . © examsnet.com

search_text: correct set of four quantum numbers for the valence electron of strontium $(z=38)$ is [ap eapcet 18 may 2024 shift 1] {'a': '$5,0,0,+\\;\\frac{1}{2}$', 'b': '$5,1,0,+\\;\\frac{1}{2}$', 'c': '$5,1,1,+\\;\\frac{1}{2}$', 'd': '$6,0,0,+\\;\\frac{1}{2}$'} 2024 2024-05-18 shift_1 chemistry   122 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: strontium has atomic number $z=38$ , so its electronic configuration is $1s^2\,2s^2\,2p^6\,3s^2\,3p^6\,4s^2\,3d^{10}\,4p^6\,5s^2$ or $[\mathrm{kr}]5s^2$ . the valence electrons are in the $5s$ orbital. for a $5s$ electron, the principal quantum number is $n=5$ . the azimuthal quantum number is $l=0$ because it is an $s$ -orbital. the magnetic quantum number is $m_l=0$ since $m_l$ ranges from $-l$ to $+l$ , and for $l=0$ the only value is $0$ . the spin quantum number can be $+\frac{1}{2}$ or $-\frac{1}{2}$ ; among the given options, $+\frac{1}{2}$ is listed. thus, the correct set of four quantum numbers for the valence electron is $\left(5,0,0,+\frac{1}{2}\right)$ . © examsnet.com

search_text: match the following list i element list ii electron gain enthalpy (in $\mathrm{kj\,mol}^{-1}$ ) a) f $i$ ) $-141$ b) cl $ii$ ) $-328$ c) o $iii$ ) $-200$ d) s $iv$ ) $-349$ the correct answer is [ap eapcet 18 may 2024 shift 1] {'a': 'a-ii, b-iv, c-i, d-iii', 'b': 'a-iv, b-ii, c-i, d-iii', 'c': 'a-iii, b-ii, c-iv, d-i', 'd': 'a-ii, b-iii, c-iv, d-i'} 2024 2024-05-18 shift_1 chemistry   123 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: the correct match is a-ii, b-iv, c-i, d-iii. electron gain enthalpy is the energy released when an electron is added to an isolated gaseous atom, so the values are negative. the accepted values are: $\; \mathrm{f} \longrightarrow -328\ \mathrm{kj\,mol}^{-1}$ $\; \mathrm{cl} \longrightarrow -349\ \mathrm{kj\,mol}^{-1}$ $\; \mathrm{o} \longrightarrow -141\ \mathrm{kj\,mol}^{-1}$ $\; \mathrm{s} \longrightarrow -200\ \mathrm{kj\,mol}^{-1}$ the magnitude becomes more negative on moving left to right across a period, since nuclear charge increases and atomic size decreases. hence $\mathrm{cl}$ has the most negative value and $\mathrm{o}$ has the least negative value among the four. however, $\mathrm{f}$ is unexpectedly less negative than $\mathrm{cl}$ because of the very small size of the $2p$ orbital, which causes strong inter-electronic repulsion and a high electron density in the compact shell. similarly, $\mathrm{s}$ is more negative than $\mathrm{o}$ because the larger $3p$ orbital of $\mathrm{s}$ accommodates the incoming electron with less repulsion. so the matching is $\mathrm{a-ii}$ , $\mathrm{b-iv}$ , $\mathrm{c-i}$ , $\mathrm{d-iii}$ , i.e. option a-ii, b-iv, c-i, d-iii. © examsnet.com

search_text: the correct formula used to determine the formal charge $(q_{f})$ on an atom in the given lewis structure of a molecule or ion is $(v=$ number of valence electrons in free atom, $u=$ number of unshared electrons on the atom, $b=$ number of bonds around the atom) [ap eapcet 18 may 2024 shift 1] {'a': '$q_f = v - \\left( \\frac{u}{b} \\right)$', 'b': '$q_f = v + (u - b)$', 'c': '$q_f = v - (u + b)$', 'd': '$q_f = v - \\left( \\frac{b}{u} \\right)$'} 2024 2024-05-18 shift_1 chemistry   125 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: a formal charge is the charge assigned to an atom in a molecule in the covalent view of bonding assuming that electrons in all chemical bonds are shared equally between atoms regardless of relative electronegativity. it is the difference between an atoms number of valence electrons in its neutral state and the number allocated to that atom in a lewis structure. $q_f=v-(v+b)$ where, $v$ is sumber of valence electron in free atom. $u=$ number of unshared electron in atom. $b=$ number of bond around the atom. © examsnet.com

What is the weight (in g) of oxygen consumed? $\text{(C=12 u: H=1 u)}$ [AP EAPCET 18 May 2024 Shift 1]
search_text: a hydrocarbon containing $\mathrm{c}$ and $\mathrm{h}$ has $92.3\% \mathrm{c}$ . when $39\,\mathrm{g}$ of hydrocarbon was completely burnt in $\mathrm{o}_2, x$ moles of water and $y$ moles of $\mathrm{co}_2$ were formed. $x$ moles of water is sufficient to liberate 0.75 moles of $\mathrm{h}_2$ with na metal. what is the weight (in g) of oxygen consumed? $\text{(c=12 u: h=1 u)}$ [ap eapcet 18 may 2024 shift 1] {'a': '120', 'b': '240', 'c': '360', 'd': '180'} 2024 2024-05-18 shift_1 chemistry   128 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: carbon $=\frac{92.3}{12}=7.7$ hydrogen $=\frac{7.7}{1}=7.7$ ratio $c:h=1:1$ so, emperical formula $= \mathrm{ch}$ 39 g of hydrocarbon is given, it means 3 moies of ch is needed. so, $3\mathrm{ch} + \;\frac{15}{4} \mathrm{o}_2 \underset{\mathrm{y}}{\underset{\downarrow}{\rightarrow 3}} \mathrm{co}_2 + \;\frac{3}{\underset{\mathrm{x}}{\underset{\downarrow}{2}}} \mathrm{h}_2\mathrm{o}$ also, $2\mathrm{na} + 2\mathrm{h}_2\mathrm{o} \rightarrow 2\mathrm{naoh} + \mathrm{h}_2$ $2\mathrm{h}_2\mathrm{o}$ gives $1\,\mathrm{mol}\,\mathrm{h}_2$ so, $\;\frac{3}{2}\,\mathrm{mol}$ of $\mathrm{h}_2\mathrm{o}$ gives $\;\frac{1}{2} \times 1.5\,\mathrm{mol}$ of $\mathrm{h}_2$ $=0.75\,\mathrm{mol}\,\mathrm{h}_2$ so, all $\mathrm{h}_2\mathrm{o}$ is consumed to liberate 0.75 mole of $\mathrm{h}_2$ . thus, weight of $\mathrm{o}_2$ consumed $=\;\frac{15}{4} \times 32=120\,\mathrm{g}$ © examsnet.com

search_text: at $300\ \text{k}$ , for the reaction $a \rightarrow p$ , the $\delta s_{\text{sys}}$ is $5\ \text{jk}^{-1}\ \text{mol}^{-1}$ . what is the heat absorbed (in $\text{kj}\ \text{mol}^{-1}$ ) by the system? [ap eapcet 18 may 2024 shift 1] {'a': '$1.5$', 'b': '$15$', 'c': '$1500$', 'd': '$0.6$'} 2024 2024-05-18 shift_1 chemistry   129 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: given for the reaction $a \rightarrow p$ : temperature $t=300\ \text{k}$ entropy change $\delta s_{\;\text{system }} = 5\ \text{j}/\text{k}/\text{mol}$ the heat absorbed by the system can be calculated using the formula: $\delta h_{\;\text{system }} = t \times \delta s_{\;\text{system }}$ substitute the given values: $\delta h_{\;\text{system }} = 300\ \text{k} \times 5\ \text{j}/\text{k}/\text{mol} = 1500\ \text{j}/\text{mol}$ since the answer is needed in kilojoules per mole, convert joules to kilojoules: $1500\ \text{j}/\text{mol} = 1.5\ \text{kj}/\text{mol}$ thus, the heat absorbed by the system is $1.5\ \text{kj}/\text{mol}$ . © examsnet.com

[ap eapcet 18 may 2024 shift 1] {'a': '$\\;1.86,0.0187$', 'b': '$\\;1.98,0.02$', 'c': '$\\;0.0187,1.86$', 'd': '$\\;0.02,1.98$'} 2024 2024-05-18 shift_1 chemistry   131 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: to analyze the equilibrium concentrations for the reaction $a_2(g) \rightleftharpoons b_2(g)$ , where the equilibrium constant $k_c$ at temperature $t(k)$ is 99.0, follow these steps: given: $k_c = 99.0$ initial moles of $a_2: 2$ moles volume of the flask: 1 l calculation: initial conditions and definition: since the reaction starts with 2 moles of $a_2(s)$ which sublimes to $a_2(g)$ , the initial concentration of $a_2$ is $2\ \text{mol/l}$ (as the flask is 1 l in volume). setting up the equilibrium expression: for the equilibrium constant expression: $k_c = \frac{[b_2]}{[a_2]}$ let the concentration of $b_2$ at equilibrium be $x\ \text{mol/l}$ . therefore, the concentration of $a_2$ becomes $(2-x)\ \text{mol/l}$ at equilibrium. solving the equilibrium equation: substitute the equilibrium values into the $k_c$ expression: $99 = \frac{x}{2-x}$ solving for $x$ : $\;99(2-x)=x$ $\;198-99x=x$ $\;198=100x$ $\;x=1.98$ thus, the concentration of $b_2$ is $[b_2] = 1.98\ \text{mol/l}$ . finding the concentration of $a_2$ : calculate $[a_2]$ using the expression $2-x$ : $[a_2] = 2-1.98=0.02\ \text{mol/l}$ conclusion: the concentrations at equilibrium are: $\; [a_2] = 0.02\ \text{mol/l}$ $\; [b_2] = 1.98\ \text{mol/l}$ © examsnet.com

search_text: at $27^{\circ}\:\mathrm{c}$ , the degree of dissociation of weak acid $(\mathrm{ha})$ in its $0.5\:\mathrm{m}$ aqueous solution is $1\%$ . its $k_a$ value is approximately [ap eapcet 18 may 2024 shift 1] {'a': '$\\;5 \\times 10^{-4}$', 'b': '$\\;5 \\times 10^{-5}$', 'c': '$\\;5 \\times 10^{-6}$', 'd': '$\\;5 \\times 10^{-8}$'} 2024 2024-05-18 shift_1 chemistry   132 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: let's work through the problem step by step. the dissociation of the weak acid is given by: $\mathrm{ha} \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{h}^{+}+\mathrm{a}^{-}.$ the initial concentration of ha is 0.5 m . with a degree of dissociation, $\alpha=0.01$ (or 1\%), the equilibrium concentrations are: $\; [\mathrm{ha}]=0.5(1-0.01)=0.5 \times 0.99=0.495\:\mathrm{m}$ $\; [\mathrm{h}^{+}] =0.5 \times 0.01=0.005\:\mathrm{m}$ $\; [\mathrm{a}^{-}] =0.005\:\mathrm{m}$ the acid dissociation constant, $k_a$ , is defined as: $k_a=\frac{[\mathrm{h}^{+}][\mathrm{a}^{-}]}{[\mathrm{ha}]}.$ substitute the equilibrium concentrations: $k_a=\frac{(0.005)(0.005)}{0.495}=\frac{0.000025}{0.495}.$ simplifying the expression: $k_a \approx 5 \times 10^{-5}.$ thus, the approximate value of $k_a$ (or $k_e$ , as referenced) is $5 \times 10^{-5}$ . the correct option is option b. © examsnet.com

question: The diffraction pattern of crystalline solid gave a peak at $2\theta = 60^{\circ}$ . What is the distance (in $\text{cm}$ ) between the layers which gave this peak? $(\lambda \,\text{of}\, X \,\text{-rays is}\, 1.54 \text{\AA}) (\sin 30^{\circ}=0.5, \sin 60^{\circ}=0.866 ; n=1)$ [AP EAPCET 18 May 2024 Shift 1]
search_text: the diffraction pattern of crystalline solid gave a peak at $2\theta = 60^{\circ}$ . what is the distance (in $\text{cm}$ ) between the layers which gave this peak? $(\lambda \,\text{of}\, x \,\text{-rays is}\, 1.54 \text{\aa}) (\sin 30^{\circ}=0.5, \sin 60^{\circ}=0.866 ; n=1)$ [ap eapcet 18 may 2024 shift 1] {'a': '$8.89 \\times 10^{-9}$', 'b': '$8.89 \\times 10^{-1}$', 'c': '$1.54 \\times 10^{-8}$', 'd': '$1.54$'} 2024 2024-05-18 shift_1 chemistry   140 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: to find the distance between the layers in a crystalline solid that produces a diffraction peak at $2\theta = 60^{\circ}$ , we first need to determine $\theta$ . given that $2\theta = 60^{\circ}$ , it follows that $\theta = 30^{\circ}$ . then, we use bragg's law for diffraction, which is: $n\lambda = 2d \sin\theta$ given: wavelength of x-rays, $\lambda = 1.54 \text{\aa} = 1.54 \times 10^{-10} \text{m}$ order of reflection, $n=1$ $\sin 30^{\circ} = 0.5$ rearranging bragg's law to solve for $d$ , we have: $d = \frac{n\lambda}{2\sin\theta}$ substituting the given values into the equation: $d = \frac{1 \times 1.54 \times 10^{-10}}{2 \times 0.5} = \frac{1.54 \times 10^{-10}}{1} = 1.54 \times 10^{-10} \text{m} = 1.54 \times 10^{-8} \text{cm}$ thus, the distance between the layers is $1.54 \times 10^{-8} \text{cm}$ . © examsnet.com

search_text: the concentration of $1\ \mathrm{l}$ of $\mathrm{caco}_3$ solution is 1000 ppm. what is its concentration in $\mathrm{mol}\ \mathrm{l}^{-1}$ ? $(\mathrm{ca}=40\ \mathrm{u},\ \mathrm{o}=16\ \mathrm{u},\ \mathrm{c}=12\ \mathrm{u})$ [ap eapcet 18 may 2024 shift 1] {'a': '$\\;10^{-3}$', 'b': '$\\;10^{-1}$', 'c': '$\\;10^{-4}$', 'd': '$\\;10^{-2}$'} 2024 2024-05-18 shift_1 chemistry   141 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: to determine the concentration of a $\mathrm{caco}_3$ solution in molarity ( $\mathrm{mol}/\mathrm{l}$ ), given its concentration is 1000 ppm , we proceed as follows: mass of $\mathrm{caco}_3$ in 1 liter: since 1000 ppm means 1000 mg of $\mathrm{caco}_3$ per liter, it converts to grams as: $\;\frac{1000 \times 1000\ \mathrm{mg}}{1000000}=1\ \mathrm{g}$ calculation of moles: the molar mass of $\mathrm{caco}_3$ is calculated using the atomic masses: $\mathrm{ca}=40\;\text{ u},\ \mathrm{c}=12\;\text{ u, }\ \mathrm{o}=16\;\text{ u. }$ therefore, the molar mass of $\mathrm{caco}_3=40+12+(16 \times 3)=100\ \mathrm{g}/\mathrm{mol}$ . now, calculate the number of moles ( $n$ ): $n=\frac{\;\text{ mass of }\;\; \mathrm{caco}_3}{\;\text{ molar mass }\;}=\frac{1}{100}=0.01\ \mathrm{mol}$ determine molarity: the molarity (concentration in $\mathrm{mol}/\mathrm{l}$ ) is given by: $\;\text{ molarity }\;=\frac{\;\text{ number of moles }\;}{\;\text{ volume of solution in }\; \mathrm{l}}=\frac{0.01}{1}=0.01\ \mathrm{mol}/\mathrm{l}=10^{-2}\ \mathrm{mol}/\mathrm{l}$ thus, the concentration of the $\mathrm{caco}_3$ solution is $10^{-2}\ \mathrm{mol}/\mathrm{l}$ . © examsnet.com

search_text: at $293\ \text{k}$ , methane gas was passed into $1\ \text{l}$ of water. the partial pressure of methane is 1 bar. the number of moles of methane dissolved in $1\ \text{l}$ water is $(k_{h}.$ of methane $=0.4\ \text{kbar})$ [ap eapcet 18 may 2024 shift 1] {'a': '$\\;1.38$', 'b': '$\\;1.38\\times 10^{-2}$', 'c': '$1.38\\times 10^{-3}$', 'd': '$1.38\\times 10^{-1}$'} 2024 2024-05-18 shift_1 chemistry   142 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: using henry's law in the form $p = k_h \chi_{\text{ch}_4}$ , where $\chi_{\text{ch}_4}$ is the mole fraction of methane in the solution. given $p = 1\ \text{bar}$ and $k_h = 0.4\ \text{kbar} = 0.4 \times 10^3\ \text{bar} = 400\ \text{bar}$ . so, $\chi_{\text{ch}_4} = \frac{p}{k_h} = \frac{1}{400} = 2.5 \times 10^{-3}$ . for $1\ \text{l}$ of water, mass $= 1000\ \text{g}$ , so $n_{\text{water}} = \frac{1000}{18} = 55.5\ \text{mol}$ . in dilute solution, $\chi_{\text{ch}_4} \approx \frac{n_{\text{ch}_4}}{n_{\text{water}}}$ . thus, $n_{\text{ch}_4} \approx \chi_{\text{ch}_4} n_{\text{water}} = (2.5 \times 10^{-3})(55.5)$ . $n_{\text{ch}_4} \approx 0.1388\ \text{mol} \approx 1.38 \times 10^{-1}\ \text{mol}$ . hence the correct option is $1.38 \times 10^{-1}$ . © examsnet.com

search_text: the $e^{\theta}$ of $\mathrm{m}_{\mathrm{m}}^{2+} \| \mathrm{cu}^{2+} \mid \mathrm{cu}$ is $0.3\ \mathrm{v}$ . at what concentration of $\mathrm{cu}^{2+} (.$ in $\mathrm{mol}\ \mathrm{l}^{-1})$ , the $e_{\;\text{cell }\;}$ value becomes zero? $\left(\frac{2.303\,rt}{f}=0.06\right)\;;\;$ (conc. of $\mathrm{m}^{2+}=0.1\ \mathrm{m}$ ) [ap eapcet 18 may 2024 shift 1] {'a': '$\\;10^{-9}$', 'b': '$\\;10^{-8}$', 'c': '$\\;10^{-11}$', 'd': '$\\;10^{-10}$'} 2024 2024-05-18 shift_1 chemistry   143 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: the given standard electrode potential is: $e_{\;\text{cell }\;}^{\circ}=0.3\ \mathrm{v}$ according to the nernst equation: $e_{\;\text{cell }\;} = e_{\;\text{cell }\;}^{\circ} - \frac{2.303\,r t}{n f} \log \left[ \frac{[\mathrm{cu}^{2+}]}{[\mathrm{m}^{2+}]} \right]$ in this context: $n=2$ (since it involves the transfer of 2 electrons) $e_{\;\text{cell }\;}=0\;\text{ (when the cell voltage is zero)}\;$ $\;[\mathrm{m}^{2+}] =0.1\ \mathrm{m}$ $\;\frac{2.303\,r t}{f}=0.06$ substituting these values into equation (1) gives: $0.3 = - \frac{0.06}{2} \log \left[ \frac{[\mathrm{cu}^{2+}]}{0.1} \right]$ solving for the log term: $-\frac{0.6}{0.06} = \log \left[ \frac{[\mathrm{cu}^{2+}]}{0.1} \right]$ taking the antilog: $10^{-10} = \frac{[\mathrm{cu}^{2+}]}{0.1}$ this implies: $[\mathrm{cu}^{2+}] = 10^{-10} \times 10^{-1} = 10^{-11} \text{mol/l}$ therefore, the concentration of $\mathrm{cu}^{2+}$ required to make the cell potential zero is $10^{-11} \text{mol/l}$ . © examsnet.com

search_text: if a real valued function $f:[a,\infty)\to[b,\infty)$ defined by $f(x)=2x^2-3x+5$ is a bijection, then $3a+2b=$ [ap eapcet 19 may 2024 shift 2] {'a': '20', 'b': '10', 'c': '12', 'd': '6'} 2024 2024-05-19 shift_2 mathematics   1 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: for $f(x)=2x^2-3x+5$ , the vertex is at $x=-\frac{-3}{2\cdot 2}=\frac{3}{4}$ . the minimum value is $f\left(\frac{3}{4}\right)=2\left(\frac{3}{4}\right)^2-3\left(\frac{3}{4}\right)+5=\frac{9}{8}-\frac{9}{4}+5=\frac{31}{8}$ . using the intended interpretation that the bijective restriction starts at the vertex, we get $a=\frac{3}{4}$ . the range then starts at the minimum value, so $b=\frac{31}{8}$ . now $3a+2b=3\left(\frac{3}{4}\right)+2\left(\frac{31}{8}\right)=\frac{9}{4}+\frac{31}{4}=\frac{40}{4}=10$ . hence the correct option is $10$ . © examsnet.com

question: The domain of the real valued function $f(x)=\;\frac{1}{\sqrt{\log_{0.5}(2x-3)}}+\sqrt{4-9x^2}$ is [AP EAPCET 19 May 2024 Shift 2]
search_text: the domain of the real valued function $f(x)=\;\frac{1}{\sqrt{\log_{0.5}(2x-3)}}+\sqrt{4-9x^2}$ is [ap eapcet 19 may 2024 shift 2] {'a': '$[\\frac{2}{3}, \\frac{3}{2})$', 'b': 'null set', 'c': '$[\\frac{2}{3}, 2)$', 'd': '$\\left[-\\frac{2}{3}, \\frac{2}{3}\\right]$'} 2024 2024-05-19 shift_2 mathematics   2 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: step 1: condition from the first term the function contains $\frac{1}{\sqrt{\log_{0.5}(2x-3)}}$ , so we need the quantity inside the square root to be positive and the logarithm to be defined. hence $\log_{0.5}(2x-3) > 0$ and $2x-3 > 0$ . since the base $0.5 < 1$ , the logarithm is a decreasing function, so $\log_{0.5}(2x-3) > 0 = \log_{0.5} 1$ implies $2x-3 < 1$ . combining with $2x-3 > 0$ gives $0 < 2x-3 < 1$ . therefore $\frac{3}{2} < x < 2$ . step 2: condition from the second term the function contains $\sqrt{4-9x^2}$ , so the expression under the square root must be non-negative. $4-9x^2 \ge 0 \;\rightarrow\; x^2 \le \frac{4}{9}$ . solving gives $-\frac{2}{3} \le x \le \frac{2}{3}$ . step 3: intersection of the two conditions the domain must satisfy both $\frac{3}{2} < x < 2$ and $-\frac{2}{3} \le x \le \frac{2}{3}$ simultaneously. these two intervals do not overlap at all, since $\frac{2}{3} < \frac{3}{2}$ . hence their intersection is the empty set, i.e. the domain is a null set. therefore the correct answer is the null set, option b. © examsnet.com

search_text: let $f(x)=3+2x$ and $g_n(x)=($ o $f$ of 0 ..... n times $)(x)$ . $\forall n \in n$ if all the lines $y = g_n(x)$ pass through a fixed point $(\alpha, \beta)$ , then $\alpha+\beta=$ [ap eapcet 20 may 2024 shift 1] {'a': '$-5$', 'b': '$-4$', 'c': '$-3$', 'd': '$-6$'} 2024 2024-05-20 shift_1 mathematics   1 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: given $f(x)=3+2x$ and $g_n(x)$ is the $n$ -fold composition of $f$ with itself. for an affine map $f(x)=2x+3$ , the $n$ -fold iterate is $g_n(x)=2^n x+3(2^n-1).$ so each line can be written as $y=2^n x+3(2^n-1)=2^n(x+3)-3.$ if all these lines pass through the fixed point $(\alpha,\beta)$ , then for every $n\in\mathbb{n}$ , $\beta=2^n(\alpha+3)-3.$ using $n=1$ and $n=2$ : $\beta=2(\alpha+3)-3=2\alpha+3,$ $\beta=4(\alpha+3)-3=4\alpha+9.$ equating these, $2\alpha+3=4\alpha+9 \implies -2\alpha=6 \implies \alpha=-3.$ then $\beta=2(-3)+3=-3.$ therefore, $\alpha+\beta=-3+(-3)=-6.$ hence the correct option is $-6$ . © examsnet.com

question: The paramagnetic complex ion which has no unpaired electrons in $t_{2g}$ orbitals is [AP EAPCET 20 May 2024 Shift 1]
search_text: the paramagnetic complex ion which has no unpaired electrons in $t_{2g}$ orbitals is [ap eapcet 20 may 2024 shift 1] {'a': '$[\\mathrm{fe}(\\mathrm{cn})_6]^{4-}$', 'b': '$[\\mathrm{fe}(\\mathrm{cn})_6]^{3-}$', 'c': '$[\\mathrm{zn}(\\mathrm{nh}_3)_6]^{2+}$', 'd': '$[\\mathrm{ni}(\\mathrm{nh}_3)_6]^{2+}$'} 2024 2024-05-20 shift_1 chemistry   150 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: in an octahedral complex, the $t_{2g}$ orbitals are lower in energy and the $e_g$ orbitals are higher in energy. for $[\mathrm{ni}(\mathrm{nh}_3)_6]^{2+}$ , ni is in the $+2$ oxidation state, so the ion is $d^8$ . $\mathrm{nh}_3$ is a weak-field ligand, so this is a high-spin octahedral complex. the $d^8$ configuration is $t_{2g}^{6}e_g^{2}$ . thus the two unpaired electrons occupy the $e_g$ orbitals, and there are no unpaired electrons in the $t_{2g}$ orbitals. the complex is paramagnetic, so the correct option is (3), $[\mathrm{ni}(\mathrm{nh}_3)_6]^{2+}$ . checking the other options: $[\mathrm{fe}(\mathrm{cn})_6]^{4-}$ is $\mathrm{fe}^{2+}$ $d^6$ low-spin with $t_{2g}^{6}e_g^{0}$ and is diamagnetic. $[\mathrm{fe}(\mathrm{cn})_6]^{3-}$ is $\mathrm{fe}^{3+}$ $d^5$ low-spin with $t_{2g}^{5}e_g^{0}$ ; it is paramagnetic but has unpaired electrons in $t_{2g}$ . $[\mathrm{zn}(\mathrm{nh}_3)_6]^{2+}$ is $\mathrm{zn}^{2+}$ $d^{10}$ and is diamagnetic. © examsnet.com

search_text: $\text{benzamide} \xrightarrow{\mathrm{br}_2/\mathrm{naoh}} x \xrightarrow[\text{alc.koh}]{\mathrm{chcl}_3} y$ the conversion of $x$ to $y$ is [ap eapcet 20 may 2024 shift 1] {'a': 'hoffmann reaction', 'b': 'etard reaction', 'c': 'stephen reaction', 'd': 'carbyl amine reaction'} 2024 2024-05-20 shift_1 chemistry   160 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: step 1: benzamide with $\mathrm{br_2/naoh}$ undergoes hofmann bromamide degradation. step 2: this converts the $-\mathrm{conh_2}$ group to $-\mathrm{nh_2}$ , so $x$ is aniline, $\mathrm{c_6h_5nh_2}$ . step 3: aniline reacts with $\mathrm{chcl_3}$ and alcoholic $\mathrm{koh}$ to form phenyl isocyanide, $\mathrm{c_6h_5nc}$ . $\mathrm{c_6h_5nh_2 + chcl_3 + 3koh(alc.) \rightarrow c_6h_5nc + 3kcl + 3h_2o}$ step 4: this reaction is called the carbylamine reaction or hofmann isocyanide test. conclusion: the conversion of $x$ to $y$ is a carbylamine reaction, so option d is correct; option a refers to the first step only. © examsnet.com

question: $f: \mathbb{R} \longrightarrow \mathbb{R}$ is defined by $f(x+y)=f(x)+12 y, \forall x, y \in \mathbb{R}$ . If $f(1)=6$ , then $\sum\limits_{r=1}^{n} f(r)=$ [AP EAPCET 20 May 2024 Shift 2]
search_text: $f: \mathbb{r} \longrightarrow \mathbb{r}$ is defined by $f(x+y)=f(x)+12 y, \forall x, y \in \mathbb{r}$ . if $f(1)=6$ , then $\sum\limits_{r=1}^{n} f(r)=$ [ap eapcet 20 may 2024 shift 2] {'a': '$n^2$', 'b': '$5 n^2$', 'c': '$6 n^2$', 'd': '$\\frac{3 n(n+1)}{2}$'} 2024 2024-05-20 shift_2 mathematics   1 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: given $f(x+y)=f(x)+12y$ for all $x,y\in\mathbb{r}$ . by swapping $x$ and $y$ , we also get $f(x+y)=f(y)+12x$ . hence $f(x)+12y=f(y)+12x$ for all $x,y$ . so $f(x)-12x=f(y)-12y$ , meaning $f(x)-12x$ is constant. let $f(x)=12x+c$ . using $f(1)=6$ , we get $12+c=6$ , so $c=-6$ . thus $f(x)=12x-6$ . therefore $\sum\limits_{r=1}^{n} f(r)=\sum\limits_{r=1}^{n}(12r-6)$ . $=12\cdot \frac{n(n+1)}{2}-6n$ . $=6n(n+1)-6n=6n^2$ . so the correct option is $6n^2$ . © examsnet.com

search_text: at $t(\mathrm{k})$ , the equilibrium constant for the reaction $\mathrm{h}_2(g) + \mathrm{br}_2(g) \rightleftharpoons 2\,\mathrm{hbr}(g)$ is $1.6 \times 10^5$ . if 10 bar of $\mathrm{hbr}$ is introduced into a sealed vessel at $t(\mathrm{k})$ , the equilibrium pressure of $\mathrm{hbr}$ (in bar) is approximately [ap eapcet 20 may 2024 shift 2] {'a': '$10.20$', 'b': '$10.95$', 'c': '$9.95$', 'd': '$11.95$'} 2024 2024-05-20 shift_2 chemistry   131 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: the equilibrium constant is for the formation reaction, so $k_p=\frac{(p_{\mathrm{hbr}})^2}{p_{\mathrm{h_2}}p_{\mathrm{br_2}}}=1.6\times10^5$ . let the equilibrium partial pressures of $\mathrm{h_2}$ and $\mathrm{br_2}$ formed be $x$ bar each. then the equilibrium pressure of $\mathrm{hbr}$ is $10-2x$ bar. substitute into $k_p$ : $k_p=\frac{(10-2x)^2}{x^2}=1.6\times10^5$ . taking the positive square root gives $\frac{10-2x}{x}=400$ . solving: $10-2x=400x$ , so $x=\frac{10}{402}\approx0.0249$ bar. thus $p_{\mathrm{hbr}}=10-2x\approx10-0.0498=9.9502$ bar. therefore, the equilibrium pressure of $\mathrm{hbr}$ is approximately $9.95$ bar. the correct option is $9.95$ . © examsnet.com

[ap eapcet 20 may 2024 shift 2] {'a': 'leucine', 'b': 'valine', 'c': 'serine', 'd': 'threonine'} 2024 2024-05-20 shift_2 chemistry   153 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: the correct answer is threonine . a chiral centre is a carbon atom bonded to four different groups. for the options given, we examine the structure of each amino acid: leucine: $\text{(ch}_3\text{)}_2\text{ch}-\text{ch}_2-\text{ch}(\text{nh}_2)-\text{cooh}$ . only the $\alpha$ -carbon is bonded to four different groups, so it has only one chiral centre. valine: $\text{(ch}_3\text{)}_2\text{ch}-\text{ch}(\text{nh}_2)-\text{cooh}$ . here again only the $\alpha$ -carbon is chiral, so it has only one chiral centre. serine: $\text{ho}-\text{ch}_2-\text{ch}(\text{nh}_2)-\text{cooh}$ . the $\beta$ -carbon bears two identical hydrogen atoms, so it is not chiral; serine has only one chiral centre. threonine: $\text{ch}_3-\text{ch}(\text{oh})-\text{ch}(\text{nh}_2)-\text{cooh}$ . both the $\alpha$ -carbon (bonded to $\text{nh}_2$ , $\text{cooh}$ , $\text{h}$ and the side chain) and the $\beta$ -carbon (bonded to $\text{oh}$ , $\text{h}$ , $\text{ch}_3$ and the rest of the molecule) are bonded to four different groups. therefore threonine possesses two chiral centres and hence exists as four stereoisomers ( $\text{l}$ -threonine, $\text{d}$ -threonine, $\text{l}$ -allothreonine and $\text{d}$ -allothreonine). among the given options, only threonine has two chiral centres. © examsnet.com

search_text: which of the following orders are correct regarding their covalent character? i. $\mathrm{kf} < \mathrm{ki}$ ii. $\mathrm{lif} < \mathrm{kf}$ iii. $\mathrm{sncl}_2 < \mathrm{sncl}_4$ iv. $\mathrm{nacl} < \mathrm{cucl}$ the correct option is [ap eapcet 21 may 2024 shift 1] {'a': 'i, ii, iii only', 'b': 'ii, iii, iv only', 'c': 'i, iii, iv only', 'd': 'i, ii, iv only'} 2024 2024-05-21 shift_1 chemistry   124 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: according to fajans' rules, covalent character increases with smaller cation size, higher cation charge, larger and more polarizable anion, and pseudo-noble gas configuration of the cation. (i) $\mathrm{kf} < \mathrm{ki}$ : both have $\mathrm{k^+}$ , but $\mathrm{i^-}$ is larger and more polarizable than $\mathrm{f^-}$ , so $\mathrm{ki}$ is more covalent than $\mathrm{kf}$ . thus, (i) is correct. (ii) $\mathrm{lif} < \mathrm{kf}$ : $\mathrm{li^+}$ is smaller than $\mathrm{k^+}$ , so $\mathrm{li^+}$ has greater polarizing power and $\mathrm{lif}$ is more covalent than $\mathrm{kf}$ . thus, $\mathrm{lif} < \mathrm{kf}$ is incorrect; the actual order is $\mathrm{lif} > \mathrm{kf}$ . (iii) $\mathrm{sncl}_2 < \mathrm{sncl}_4$ : sn is in $+2$ state in $\mathrm{sncl}_2$ and $+4$ state in $\mathrm{sncl}_4$ . the higher charge on $\mathrm{sn^{4+}}$ gives greater polarizing power, so $\mathrm{sncl}_4$ is more covalent than $\mathrm{sncl}_2$ . thus, (iii) is correct. (iv) $\mathrm{nacl} < \mathrm{cucl}$ : $\mathrm{cu^+}$ is smaller and has a pseudo-noble gas $3d^{10}$ configuration, so it polarizes $\mathrm{cl^-}$ more than $\mathrm{na^+}$ does. hence, $\mathrm{cucl}$ is more covalent than $\mathrm{nacl}$ . thus, (iv) is correct. the correct orders are (i), (iii), and (iv) only, which is option i, iii, iv only . © examsnet.com

search_text: identify the correct statements from the following i. $\delta_r g$ is zero for $a \rightleftharpoons b$ reaction ii. the entropy of pure crystalline solids approaches zero as the temperature approaches absolute zero iii. $\delta u$ of a reaction can be determined using bomb calorimeter [ap eapcet 21 may 2024 shift 1] {'a': 'i, ii only', 'b': 'i, iii only', 'c': 'ii, iii only', 'd': 'i, ii, iii'} 2024 2024-05-21 shift_1 chemistry   129 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: concept: this question tests three separate thermodynamic facts: gibbs energy at equilibrium, the third law of thermodynamics, and the use of a bomb calorimeter. formulas / statements: at equilibrium: $\delta_r g = 0$ third law: $s \to 0$ as $t \to 0\ \mathrm{k}$ for a pure crystalline solid bomb calorimeter (constant volume): $\delta u = q_v$ explanation: i. for $a \rightleftharpoons b$ , at equilibrium $\delta_r g = 0$ (since $\delta_r g = \delta_r g^{\circ} + rt\ln q$ and $q = k$ ), so statement i is correct. ii. the entropy of a pure crystalline solid approaches zero as temperature approaches absolute zero ( $0\ \mathrm{k}$ ) — this is the third law of thermodynamics, so statement ii is correct. iii. a bomb calorimeter works at constant volume, so the heat measured gives $\delta u$ directly, so statement iii is correct. answer: all three statements i, ii and iii are correct, hence option d. © examsnet.com

question: The range of the real valued function $f(x)= \sin^{-1}\left(\frac{1+x^2}{2x}\right) + \cos^{-1}\left(\frac{2x}{1+x^2}\right)$ is [AP EAPCET 21 May 2024 Shift 2]
search_text: the range of the real valued function $f(x)= \sin^{-1}\left(\frac{1+x^2}{2x}\right) + \cos^{-1}\left(\frac{2x}{1+x^2}\right)$ is [ap eapcet 21 may 2024 shift 2] {'a': '$\\left\\{\\frac{\\pi}{2}\\right\\}$', 'b': '$r$', 'c': '$q$', 'd': '$\\left\\{-\\frac{\\pi}{2}, \\frac{\\pi}{2}\\right\\}$'} 2024 2024-05-21 shift_2 mathematics   1 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: first determine the domain of $f$ . the argument of $\sin^{-1}$ must satisfy $\left|\frac{1+x^2}{2x}\right|\le 1$ . let $a=\frac{1+x^2}{2x}=\frac12\left(x+\frac1x\right)$ for $x\ne0$ . for $x>0$ , am-gm gives $x+\frac1x\ge2$ , so $a\ge1$ . for $x<0$ , $x+\frac1x\le-2$ , so $a\le-1$ . thus $|a|\le1$ can occur only when $|a|=1$ , so $x=1$ or $x=-1$ . at $x=1$ , $f(1)=\sin^{-1}(1)+\cos^{-1}(1)=\frac{\pi}{2}+0=\frac{\pi}{2}$ . at $x=-1$ , $f(-1)=\sin^{-1}(-1)+\cos^{-1}(-1)=-\frac{\pi}{2}+\pi=\frac{\pi}{2}$ . therefore the range is $\left\{\frac{\pi}{2}\right\}$ . hence option a is correct. © examsnet.com

question: The real valued function $f: R \to \left[\;\frac{5}{2}, \infty\right)$ defined by $f(x)=|2x+1|+|x-2|$ is [AP EAPCET 21 May 2024 Shift 2]
search_text: the real valued function $f: r \to \left[\;\frac{5}{2}, \infty\right)$ defined by $f(x)=|2x+1|+|x-2|$ is [ap eapcet 21 may 2024 shift 2] {'a': 'one-one function but not onto', 'b': 'onto function but not one-one', 'c': 'bijection', 'd': 'neither one-one function nor onto'} 2024 2024-05-21 shift_2 mathematics   2 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: for $x<-\frac{1}{2}$ , $f(x)=|2x+1|+|x-2|=-(2x+1)-(x-2)=-3x+1$ . for $-\frac{1}{2}\le x\le 2$ , $f(x)=(2x+1)+(2-x)=x+3$ . for $x>2$ , $f(x)=(2x+1)+(x-2)=3x-1$ . at $x=-\frac{1}{2}$ , $f(x)=\frac{5}{2}$ , which is the minimum value of the function. as $x\to -\infty$ or $x\to \infty$ , $f(x)\to \infty$ . hence the range is $\left[\frac{5}{2},\infty\right)$ , which equals the given codomain, so the function is onto. it is not one-one because $f\left(-\frac{4}{3}\right)=5$ and $f(2)=5$ , while $-\frac{4}{3}\ne 2$ . therefore, the function is onto but not one-one. © examsnet.com

search_text: if $n$ is an integer and $z=\cos \theta + i \sin \; \theta, \theta \neq (2n+1) \; \frac{\pi}{2'}$ , then $\; \frac{1+z^{2n}}{1-z^{2n}} =$ [ap eapcet 21 may 2024 shift 2] {'a': '$i \\tan n \\theta$', 'b': '$i \\cot n \\theta$', 'c': '$-i \\tan n \\theta$', 'd': '$-i \\cot n \\theta$'} 2024 2024-05-21 shift_2 mathematics   9 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: since $z=\cos\theta+i\sin\theta=e^{i\theta}$ , we have $z^{2n}=e^{i2n\theta}$ . using $1+e^{i\alpha}=2\cos\frac{\alpha}{2}e^{i\alpha/2}$ and $1-e^{i\alpha}=-2i\sin\frac{\alpha}{2}e^{i\alpha/2}$ with $\alpha=2n\theta$ gives: $1+z^{2n}=2\cos(n\theta)e^{in\theta}$ and $1-z^{2n}=-2i\sin(n\theta)e^{in\theta}$ . therefore, $\frac{1+z^{2n}}{1-z^{2n}}=\frac{2\cos(n\theta)e^{in\theta}}{-2i\sin(n\theta)e^{in\theta}}$ cancelling $e^{in\theta}$ and $2$ , we get: $\frac{1+z^{2n}}{1-z^{2n}}=\frac{\cos(n\theta)}{-i\sin(n\theta)}$ since $\frac{1}{-i}=i$ , this becomes: $\frac{1+z^{2n}}{1-z^{2n}}=i\cot(n\theta)$ hence the correct option is $i\cot n\theta$ . the currently marked answer is correct. © examsnet.com

search_text: if $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are two distinct negative roots of $x^5-5x^3+5x^2-1=0$ , then the equation of least degree with integer coefficients having $\sqrt{-\alpha}$ and $\sqrt{-\beta}$ as its roots is [ap eapcet 22 may 2024 shift 1] {'a': '$\\;x^2-3x+1=0$', 'b': '$\\;-x^4+5x^2-5x+1=0$', 'c': '$\\;-x^4-5x^2+5x+1=0$', 'd': '$\\;x^4-3x^2+1=0$'} 2024 2024-05-22 shift_1 mathematics   12 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: factor the given polynomial as $x^5-5x^3+5x^2-1=(x-1)^3(x^2+3x+1).$ the negative roots are the roots of $x^2+3x+1=0$ , so take $\alpha=\frac{-3+\sqrt5}{2},\qquad \beta=\frac{-3-\sqrt5}{2}.$ then $-\alpha=\frac{3-\sqrt5}{2}=\left(\frac{\sqrt5-1}{2}\right)^2,\qquad -\beta=\frac{3+\sqrt5}{2}=\left(\frac{\sqrt5+1}{2}\right)^2.$ hence the required roots are $\sqrt{-\alpha}=\frac{\sqrt5-1}{2},\qquad \sqrt{-\beta}=\frac{\sqrt5+1}{2}.$ let $u=\frac{\sqrt5+1}{2}$ . then $u^2-u-1=0$ , so the minimal polynomial of $u$ is $x^2-x-1$ . let $v=\frac{\sqrt5-1}{2}$ . then $v^2+v-1=0$ , so the minimal polynomial of $v$ is $x^2+x-1$ . both $u$ and $v$ must be roots. their sum is $\sqrt5$ , which is irrational, so no quadratic with integer coefficients can contain both. thus the least degree polynomial is the product $(x^2-x-1)(x^2+x-1)=x^4-3x^2+1.$ therefore the required equation is $x^4-3x^2+1=0.$ this matches option d. © examsnet.com

search_text: if $|x| < 1$ , then the number of terms in the expansion of $\left[\; \frac{1}{2} \left(1.2+2.3x+3.4x^2+\cdots \infty\right) \right]^{-25}$ is [ap eapcet 22 may 2024 shift 1] {'a': 'infinite', 'b': '101', 'c': '76', 'd': '51'} 2024 2024-05-22 shift_1 mathematics   18 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: interpreting $1.2$ , $2.3$ , $3.4$ as $1\cdot2$ , $2\cdot3$ , $3\cdot4$ respectively, the series is $\sum_{n=1}^{\infty} n(n+1)x^{n-1}$ . using standard sums, $\sum_{n=1}^{\infty} n x^{n-1}=\frac{1}{(1-x)^2}$ and $\sum_{n=1}^{\infty} n^2x^{n-1}=\frac{1+x}{(1-x)^3}$ . then $\sum_{n=1}^{\infty} n(n+1)x^{n-1} = \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} (n^2+n)x^{n-1} = \frac{1+x}{(1-x)^3}+\frac{1}{(1-x)^2} = \frac{2}{(1-x)^3}$ . so $\frac12(1\cdot2+2\cdot3x+3\cdot4x^2+\cdots\infty)=\frac{1}{(1-x)^3}$ . thus $\left[\frac{1}{(1-x)^3}\right]^{-25} = (1-x)^{75}$ . the binomial expansion of $(1-x)^{75}$ has $75+1=76$ terms. therefore, the correct answer is 76 . © examsnet.com

search_text: angle between the circles $x^2+y^2-4x-6y-3=0$ and $x^2+y^2+8x-4y+11=0$ is [ap eapcet 22 may 2024 shift 2] {'a': '$\\;\\frac{\\pi}{3}$', 'b': '$\\;\\frac{\\pi}{6}$', 'c': '$\\;\\frac{\\pi}{2}$', 'd': '$\\;\\frac{\\pi}{4}$'} 2024 2024-05-22 shift_2 mathematics   51 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: for a circle $x^2+y^2+2gx+2fy+c=0$ , the center is $(-g,-f)$ and the radius is $\sqrt{g^2+f^2-c}$ . for $x^2+y^2-4x-6y-3=0$ , we have $g=-2$ , $f=-3$ , $c=-3$ . thus its center is $o_1=(2,3)$ and its radius is $r_1=\sqrt{(-2)^2+(-3)^2-(-3)}=\sqrt{16}=4$ . for $x^2+y^2+8x-4y+11=0$ , we have $g=4$ , $f=-2$ , $c=11$ . thus its center is $o_2=(-4,2)$ and its radius is $r_2=\sqrt{4^2+(-2)^2-11}=\sqrt{9}=3$ . the distance between the centers is $d=o_1o_2=\sqrt{(2+4)^2+(3-2)^2}=\sqrt{37}$ . the acute angle $\theta$ between the circles satisfies $\cos\theta=\left|\frac{r_1^2+r_2^2-d^2}{2r_1r_2}\right|.$ substituting $r_1=4$ , $r_2=3$ , and $d^2=37$ , we get $\cos\theta=\left|\frac{16+9-37}{2\cdot4\cdot3}\right|=\left|\frac{-12}{24}\right|=\frac12.$ therefore $\theta=\frac{\pi}{3}$ . so the correct option is $0$ , namely $\frac{\pi}{3}$ . © examsnet.com

search_text: $\omega$ is a complex cube root of unity and if $z$ is a complex number satisfying $\left|z-1\right| \leq 2$ and $\left| \omega^2 z - 1 - \omega \right| = a$ , then the set of possible values of $a$ is [ap eapcet 23 may 2024 s1] {'a': '$\\;0 \\leq a \\leq 2$', 'b': '$\\;\\;\\frac{1}{2} \\leq a \\leq \\;\\frac{\\sqrt{3}}{2}$', 'c': '$\\;|\\omega| \\leq a \\leq \\;\\frac{\\sqrt{3}}{2}+2$', 'd': '$\\;0 \\leq a \\leq 4$'} 2024 2024-05-23 shift_1 mathematics   7 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: since $\omega$ is a primitive complex cube root of unity, $1+\omega+\omega^2=0$ and $|\omega|=1$ . thus $-1-\omega=\omega^2$ , so the given modulus becomes $|\omega^2 z-1-\omega|=|\omega^2 z+\omega^2|=|\omega^2|\,|z+1|=|z+1|.$ hence $a=|z+1|$ . the condition $|z-1|\le 2$ represents the closed disk centered at $1$ with radius $2$ . the point $z=-1$ lies in this disk because $|-1-1|=2$ . therefore the minimum possible value of $a=|z+1|$ is $0$ , attained at $z=-1$ . for the maximum, $|z+1|=|(z-1)+2|\le |z-1|+2\le 4$ . equality occurs when $z-1=2$ , i.e. $z=3$ , which is in the disk. thus the possible values are $0\le a\le 4$ . so the correct option is $0\le a\le 4$ (option d). © examsnet.com

search_text: among the 4 digit numbers formed using the digits $0,1,2,3,4$ when repetition of digits allowed. the number of numbers which are divisible by 4 is [ap eapcet 23 may 2024 s1] {'a': '140', 'b': '160', 'c': '180', 'd': '200'} 2024 2024-05-23 shift_1 mathematics   14 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: the divisibility by $4$ depends only on the last two digits. let the tens digit be $a$ and the units digit be $b$ , with $a,b \in \{0,1,2,3,4\}$ . the last two-digit number is $10a+b$ , so we need $10a+b \equiv 0 \pmod{4}$ . since $10 \equiv 2 \pmod{4}$ , this becomes $2a+b \equiv 0 \pmod{4}$ . checking $a=0,1,2,3,4$ gives: $a=0$ : $b=0,4$ , so $2$ choices. $a=1$ : $b=2$ , so $1$ choice. $a=2$ : $b=0,4$ , so $2$ choices. $a=3$ : $b=2$ , so $1$ choice. $a=4$ : $b=0,4$ , so $2$ choices. thus the number of possible last-two-digit pairs is $2+1+2+1+2=8$ . for the first two digits, the thousands digit can be any of $1,2,3,4$ but not $0$ , giving $4$ choices. the hundreds digit can be any of $0,1,2,3,4$ , giving $5$ choices. so the number of four-digit numbers is $4 \times 5 \times 8=160$ . therefore, the correct option is á (option b). © examsnet.com

search_text: $\tan^2\;\frac{\pi}{16}+\tan^2\;\frac{2\pi}{16}+\tan^2\;\frac{3\pi}{16}+\tan^2\;\frac{4\pi}{16}+\tan^2\;\frac{5\pi}{16}+\tan^2\;\frac{6\pi}{16}+\tan^2\;\frac{7\pi}{16}=$ [ap eapcet 23 may 2024 s1] {'a': '35', 'b': '41', 'c': '37', 'd': '33'} 2024 2024-05-23 shift_1 mathematics   20 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: let $x=\tan\theta$ for $\theta=\frac{k\pi}{16}$ . since $\sin(16\theta)=0$ at these angles, the finite roots of the following polynomial are $0$ and $\pm\tan\frac{k\pi}{16}$ for $k=1,2,\ldots,7$ . using the expansion of $\sin(16\theta)$ gives $p(x)=16x-\binom{16}{3}x^3+\binom{16}{5}x^5-\cdots+\binom{16}{13}x^{13}-16x^{15}.$ let $a_k=\tan\frac{k\pi}{16}$ and $s=\sum_{k=1}^{7}a_k^2$ . because the leading coefficient of $p(x)$ is $-16$ , its factored form is $p(x)=-16x\prod_{k=1}^{7}(x^2-a_k^2).$ from the expanded form, the coefficient of $x^{13}$ is $\binom{16}{13}=560$ . from the factored form, the coefficient of $x^{13}$ is $16s$ . thus $16s=560$ , so $s=35$ . therefore, the correct option is $35$ . © examsnet.com

search_text: the probability that a speaks truth is $75\%$ and the probability that b speaks truth is $80\%$ . the probability that they contradict each other when asked to speak on a fact is [ap eapcet 23 may 2024 s1] {'a': '$\\;\\frac{3}{20}$', 'b': '$\\;\\frac{4}{20}$', 'c': '$\\;\\frac{7}{20}$', 'd': '$\\;\\frac{5}{20}$'} 2024 2024-05-23 shift_1 mathematics   37 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: let $p(a_t)=\frac{3}{4}$ and $p(b_t)=\frac{4}{5}$ . then $p(a_l)=1-\frac{3}{4}=\frac{1}{4}$ and $p(b_l)=1-\frac{4}{5}=\frac{1}{5}$ . they contradict each other when exactly one of them speaks the truth. assuming their truth-telling events are independent, the required probability is $p(a_t\cap b_l)+p(a_l\cap b_t)$ . this equals $\frac{3}{4}\cdot\frac{1}{5}+\frac{1}{4}\cdot\frac{4}{5}$ . $=\frac{3}{20}+\frac{4}{20}=\frac{7}{20}$ . hence the correct option is $\frac{7}{20}$ (option c). © examsnet.com

search_text: path of projectile is given by the equation $y=p x-q x^2$ , match the following accordingly (acceleration due to gravity $=g$ ) a) range i) $\frac{p}{q}$ b) maximum height ii) p c) time of flight iii) $\;\frac{p^2}{4q}$ d) tangent of projection iv) $\left( \sqrt{\;\frac{2}{gq}} \right) p$ [ap eapcet 23 may 2024 s1] {'a': 'a-i, b-iii, c-iv, d-ii', 'b': 'a-i, b-iii, c-ii, d-iv', 'c': 'a-iii, b-i, c-iv, d-ii', 'd': 'a-iv, b-ii, c-iii, d-i'} 2024 2024-05-23 shift_1 physics   83 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: the standard projectile path is $y=x\tan\theta-\frac{gx^2}{2u^2\cos^2\theta}.$ comparing with $y=px-qx^2$ gives $\tan\theta=p$ and $q=\frac{g}{2u^2\cos^2\theta}$ . range is the nonzero root of $y=0$ : $x(p-qx)=0$ , so $r=\frac{p}{q}$ ; hence a matches i. maximum height occurs at $x=\frac{p}{2q}$ , so $h=y_{\max}=\frac{p^2}{4q}$ ; hence b matches iii. time of flight is $t=\frac{2u\sin\theta}{g}$ . using $\tan\theta=p$ and $q=\frac{g}{2u^2\cos^2\theta}$ , $t^2=\frac{4u^2\sin^2\theta}{g^2}=\frac{2p^2}{gq},$ so $t=p\sqrt{\frac{2}{gq}}$ ; hence c matches iv. tangent of projection is $\tan\theta=p$ ; hence d matches ii. therefore the correct matching is a-i, b-iii, c-iv, d-ii, which is option a. © examsnet.com

search_text: a particle of mass ' $m$ ' at rest on a rough horizontal surface with a coefficient of friction ' $\mu$ ' is given a velocity ' $u$ '. the average power imparted by friction before it stops [ap eapcet 23 may 2024 s1] {'a': 'zero', 'b': '$\\;\\frac{1}{2} \\mu \\text{mgu}$', 'c': '$\\mu \\text{mgu}$', 'd': '$2 \\mu \\text{mgu}$'} 2024 2024-05-23 shift_1 physics   87 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: friction is the only horizontal force acting on the particle, and it opposes the motion. friction force: $f = \mu mg$ retardation of the particle: $a = \frac{f}{m} = \mu g$ if $t$ is the time taken to stop, then using $v = u - at$ with $v = 0$ : $t = \frac{u}{\mu g}$ work done by friction equals the loss in kinetic energy of the particle: $w = \frac{1}{2}mu^2$ average power imparted by friction is the work done divided by the time taken: $p_{avg} = \frac{w}{t} = \frac{\frac{1}{2}mu^2}{\frac{u}{\mu g}} = \frac{1}{2}\mu mgu$ hence the average power imparted by friction before the particle stops is $\frac{1}{2}\mu \text{mgu}$ , which matches option (1). therefore, the marked answer option (1) is correct. © examsnet.com

question: If the position of the electron was measured with an accuracy of $+0.002 \text{nm}$ , the uncertainty in the momentum of it would be (in $\text{kg} \text{ms}^{-1}) ( h = 6.626 \times 10^{-34} \text{J} \text{s})$ [AP EAPCET 23 May 2024 S1]
search_text: if the position of the electron was measured with an accuracy of $+0.002 \text{nm}$ , the uncertainty in the momentum of it would be (in $\text{kg} \text{ms}^{-1}) ( h = 6.626 \times 10^{-34} \text{j} \text{s})$ [ap eapcet 23 may 2024 s1] {'a': '$\\; 2.637 \\times 10^{-23}$', 'b': '$\\; 2.637 \\times 10^{-24}$', 'c': '$\\; 8.283 \\times 10^{-23}$', 'd': '$\\; 8.283 \\times 10^{-24}$'} 2024 2024-05-23 shift_1 chemistry   122 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: for the uncertainty in position, take $\delta x = 0.002\ \text{nm}$ . convert to metres: $\delta x = 0.002 \times 10^{-9}\ \text{m} = 2 \times 10^{-12}\ \text{m}$ . using heisenberg's uncertainty principle: $\delta x \cdot \delta p \ge \frac{h}{4\pi}$ . so, $\delta p \ge \frac{h}{4\pi \delta x}$ . substitute the values: $\delta p = \frac{6.626 \times 10^{-34}}{4\pi(2 \times 10^{-12})}$ . $\delta p = \frac{6.626 \times 10^{-34}}{8\pi \times 10^{-12}}$ . $\delta p \approx 2.637 \times 10^{-23}\ \text{kg}\ \text{m}\ \text{s}^{-1}$ . thus, the uncertainty in momentum is $2.637 \times 10^{-23}\ \text{kg}\ \text{m}\ \text{s}^{-1}$ , which matches option a. © examsnet.com

question: $p$ -Methyl benzene nitrile can be prepared from which of the following? [AP EAPCET 23 May 2024 S1]
search_text: $p$ -methyl benzene nitrile can be prepared from which of the following? [ap eapcet 23 may 2024 s1] {'a': '', 'b': '', 'c': '', 'd': ''} 2024 2024-05-23 shift_1 chemistry   160 careerindia https://www.careerindia.com/exam/ap-eamcet-eapcet-question-papers-e21.html solution: the compound is $p$ -methylbenzonitrile, $p\text{-ch}_3\text{c}_6\text{h}_4\text{cn}$ , in which the $-\text{cn}$ group is attached directly to the aromatic ring. such aryl nitriles are best prepared by the sandmeyer reaction. in this route, $p$ -toluidine is first diazotized with $\text{nano}_2$ and $\text{hcl}$ at $273\text{–}278\ \text{k}$ to form $p$ -methylbenzenediazonium chloride. the diazonium salt is then treated with $\text{cucn}/\text{kcn}$ , which replaces the diazonium group by $-\text{cn}$ and gives $p$ -methylbenzonitrile. $p\text{-ch}_3\text{c}_6\text{h}_4\text{nh}_2 \xrightarrow{\text{nano}_2/\text{hcl}} p\text{-ch}_3\text{c}_6\text{h}_4\text{n}_2^+\text{cl}^- \xrightarrow{\text{cucn}/\text{kcn}} p\text{-ch}_3\text{c}_6\text{h}_4\text{cn} + \text{n}_2$ the other routes do not give the required aryl nitrile: $p$ -methylbenzyl chloride with $\text{kcn}$ gives $p$ -methylphenylacetonitrile, and aryl halides do not undergo simple nucleophilic substitution with ordinary $\text{kcn}$ . hence the correct option is the one showing diazotization of $p$ -toluidine followed by the sandmeyer reaction (option c). © examsnet.com

question: The domain and range of a real valued function $f(x)=\cos x-3$ are respectively. [AP EAPCET 21 May 2025 S1]

[ap eapcet 21 may 2025 s1] {'a': '$r \\setminus \\{0\\}$ and $[-1,1]$', 'b': 'r and $[-1,1]$', 'c': '$r \\setminus \\{0\\}$ and $[-4,-2]$', 'd': 'r and $[-4,-2]$'} 2025 2025-05-21 shift_1 mathematics   1 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: $\;\;\text{ we have }\; f(x)=\cos x-3$ $\;\;\text{ domain }\; =r$ $\;\;\text{ range }\; -1 \leq \cos x \leq 1$ $\; -1-3 \leq \cos x-3 \leq 1-3$ $\; -4 \leq f(x) \leq -2$ $\;\;\text{ range }\; =[-4,-2]$ © examsnet.com

question: If $f: R \longrightarrow R$ and $g: R \longrightarrow R$ are two functions defined by $f(x)=2x-3$ and $g(x)=5x^2-2$ , then the least value of the function $(g \circ f)(x)$ is [AP EAPCET 21 May 2025 S1]
search_text: if $f: r \longrightarrow r$ and $g: r \longrightarrow r$ are two functions defined by $f(x)=2x-3$ and $g(x)=5x^2-2$ , then the least value of the function $(g \circ f)(x)$ is [ap eapcet 21 may 2025 s1] {'a': '-2', 'b': '2', 'c': '-4', 'd': '4'} 2025 2025-05-21 shift_1 mathematics   2 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: given, $f(x)=2x-3$ and $g(x)=5x^2-2$ $g \circ f(x)=5[f(x)]^2-2=5(2x-3)^2-2$ $\because$ least value of $g \circ f(x)=-2$ © examsnet.com

question: For all $n \in N$ , if $1^3+2^3+3^3+\dots+n^3 > x$ , then a value of x among the following is [AP EAPCET 21 May 2025 S1]
search_text: for all $n \in n$ , if $1^3+2^3+3^3+\dots+n^3 > x$ , then a value of x among the following is [ap eapcet 21 may 2025 s1] {'a': '$\\frac{n^2}{4}$', 'b': '$n^2$', 'c': '$n^4$', 'd': '$\\frac{n^2 (n+1)^2}{4}$'} 2025 2025-05-21 shift_1 mathematics   3 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: we have, $1^3+2^3+3^3+\dots+n^3 > x$ $\because \sum n^3 = \left[\frac{n(n+1)}{2}\right]^2 = \frac{n^2}{4}(n+1)^2 > x$ $\because \frac{n^2}{4} < \frac{n^2}{4}(n+1)^2$ $\therefore x = \frac{n^2}{4}$ © examsnet.com

question: If $z_1$ and $z_2$ are two of the $n^{\text{th}}$ roots of unity such that the line segment joining them subtends a right angle at the origin then for a positive integer $k, n$ takes the form [AP EAPCET 21 May 2025 S1]
search_text: if $z_1$ and $z_2$ are two of the $n^{\text{th}}$ roots of unity such that the line segment joining them subtends a right angle at the origin then for a positive integer $k, n$ takes the form [ap eapcet 21 may 2025 s1] {'a': '$4k$', 'b': '$4k+1$', 'c': '$4k+2$', 'd': '$4k+3$'} 2025 2025-05-21 shift_1 mathematics   8 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: $z_1$ and $z_2$ are both $n$ th roots of unity. this means each one can be written in the form $e^{\frac{i 2\pi r}{n}}$ , where $r$ is an integer. let $z_1=e^{\frac{i 2\pi r_1}{n}}$ and $z_2=e^{\frac{i 2\pi r_2}{n}}$ for some integers $r_1$ and $r_2$ . if the line segment joining $z_1$ and $z_2$ makes a right angle at the origin, this means the points $z_1, z_2$ , and the origin form a right-angled triangle with the right angle at the origin. this can only happen if $\frac{z_1}{z_2}$ is a purely imaginary number. a complex number is purely imaginary when its argument (angle) is $\frac{\pi}{2}$ or $\frac{3\pi}{2}$ , or in general, $\frac{\pi}{2}+m\pi$ where $m$ is an integer. we find: $\frac{z_1}{z_2}=e^{\frac{i 2\pi}{n}(r_1-r_2)}$ for this to be purely imaginary, we need: $\frac{2\pi}{n}(r_1-r_2)=\frac{\pi}{2}+m\pi$ divide both sides by $\pi: \frac{2}{n}(r_1-r_2)=\frac{2m+1}{2}$ now solve for $n: n=\frac{4(r_1-r_2)}{2m+1}$ since $n$ must be a positive integer, $2m+1$ must divide evenly into $4(r_1-r_2)$ . the simplest way for this to always work for integer values is when $n$ is a multiple of 4 . therefore, $n=4k$ for some positive integer $k$ . © examsnet.com

question: $\left(\sqrt{\sqrt{2}+1}+i\sqrt{\sqrt{2}-1}\right)^8=$ [AP EAPCET 21 May 2025 S1]
search_text: $\left(\sqrt{\sqrt{2}+1}+i\sqrt{\sqrt{2}-1}\right)^8=$ [ap eapcet 21 may 2025 s1] {'a': '64', 'b': '64 i', 'c': '-64', 'd': '$-64i$'} 2025 2025-05-21 shift_1 mathematics   9 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: let, $z=\sqrt{\sqrt{2}+1}+i\sqrt{\sqrt{2}-1}$ $\; \rightarrow  \;\; |z|=\sqrt{\sqrt{2}+1+\sqrt{2}-1}=\sqrt{2\sqrt{2}}$ $\; \;\;  \cos \theta=\frac{\sqrt{\sqrt{2}+1}}{\sqrt{2\sqrt{2}}}, \sin \theta=\frac{\sqrt{\sqrt{2}-1}}{\sqrt{2\sqrt{2}}}$ $\; \therefore   \;\;  \cos^2 \theta=\frac{\sqrt{2}+1}{2\sqrt{2}}, \sin^2 \theta=\frac{\sqrt{2}-1}{2\sqrt{2}}$ $\; \rightarrow \;\frac{1+\cos 2\theta}{2}=\frac{\sqrt{2}+1}{2\sqrt{2}}$ $\; \rightarrow \cos 2\theta=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$ $\rightarrow 2\theta=\frac{\pi}{4}$ (since, real and imaginary part are positive.) now, $\; z^8=\left(\sqrt{2\sqrt{2}}\right)^8 \left(\cos\left(8 \times \; \frac{\pi}{8}\right)+i\sin\left(8 \times \; \frac{\pi}{8}\right)\right)$ $\; =\left(2\sqrt{2}\right)^4\left(\cos\pi+i\sin\pi\right)$ $\; = \left(2^{\frac{3}{2}} \times 4\right)(-1+0)$ $\; =2^6(-1)=-64$ © examsnet.com

search_text: all the values of k such that the quadratic expression $2 (kx)^2-(4k+1)x+2$ is negative for exactly three integral vaules of $x$ , lie in the interval [ap eapcet 21 may 2025 s1] {'a': '$\\left[\\frac{1}{12}, \\frac{1}{10}\\right)$', 'b': '$\\left(\\frac{1}{6}, \\frac{1}{5}\\right)$', 'c': '$[-1,2)$', 'd': '$[2,6)$'} 2025 2025-05-21 shift_1 mathematics   11 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: we have, $2 k x^2-(4 k+1) x+2 \; < 0$ $\because 2 k x^2-4 k x-x+2 \; < 0$ $2 k x(x-2)-1(x-2) \; < 0$ $(x-2)(2 k x-1) \; < 0$ $2 < x \; < \; \frac{1}{2k}$ expression is negative for exactly 3 integral values of $x$ which is $x=3,4,5$ $5 < x \le 6$ $\because \; \frac{1}{2k} \le 6 \rightarrow k \ge \frac{1}{12}$ $\therefore \; \frac{1}{2k} > 5 \rightarrow k < \frac{1}{10}$ $\therefore \; k \in \left[\frac{1}{12}, \frac{1}{10}\right)$ © examsnet.com

search_text: if $\alpha$ and $\beta(\alpha>\beta)$ are the multiple roots of the equation $4 x^{4}+4 x^{3}-23 x^{2}-12 x$ $+36=0$ , then $2 \alpha-\beta=$ [ap eapcet 21 may 2025 s1] {'a': '$-1$', 'b': '$3$', 'c': '$5$', 'd': '$-7$'} 2025 2025-05-21 shift_1 mathematics   12 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: we have, $f(x)=4 x^{4}+4 x^{3}-23 x^{2}-12 x+36=0$ using concept a polynomial $f(x)$ has a multiple root $r$ , then $f(r)=0$ and $f'(r)=0$ $f'(x)=16 x^{3}+12 x^{2}-46 x-12$ now, using hit and trial by taking $x=-2$ $f(-2)=4(-2)^{4}+4(-2)^{3}-23(-2)^{2}$ $-12(-2)+36$ $=64-32-92+24+36=0$ $\rightarrow f'(-2)=16(-2)^{3}+12(-2)^{2}$ $-46(-2)-12$ $=-128+48+92-12=0$ $\because x=-2$ is a multiple root. by dividing the equation by $(x+2)^{2}$ , we get another multiple root $x=\frac{3}{2}$ given, $\alpha>\beta$ $\therefore \alpha=\frac{3}{2} \text{ and } \beta=-2$ $\therefore 2\alpha-\beta=3+2=5$ © examsnet.com

search_text: if $\alpha, \beta$ and $\gamma$ are the roots of the equation $x^3-13 x^2+k x+189=0$ such that $\beta-\gamma=2$ , then $\beta+\gamma: k+\alpha=$ [ap eapcet 21 may 2025 s1] {'a': '$4: 3$', 'b': '$2: 1$', 'c': '$6: 5$', 'd': '$3: 4$'} 2025 2025-05-21 shift_1 mathematics   13 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: given, $x^3-13 x^2+k x+189=0$ $\alpha+\beta+\gamma=13, \alpha \beta+\beta \gamma+\gamma \alpha=k$ and $\alpha \beta \gamma=-189$ and $\beta-\gamma=2$ $\;\left[ \because \gamma=\beta-2 \right]$ $\;\alpha+\beta+\beta-2=13$ $\rightarrow (15-2 \beta) \beta(\beta-2)=-189$ $\rightarrow \beta (15 \beta-2 \beta^2-30+4 \beta) =-189$ $\rightarrow -2 \beta^3+19 \beta^2-30 \beta+189=0$ $\rightarrow 2 \beta^3-19 \beta^2+30 \beta-189=0$ $\rightarrow (\beta-9) (2 \beta^2-\beta+21)=0$ $\rightarrow \beta=9,2\beta^2-\beta+21 \neq 0 \forall \beta \in r$ $\therefore \;\beta=9, \gamma=7$ and $\;\;  \alpha=-3$ $k=\alpha \beta+\beta \gamma+\gamma \alpha=-27+63-21=15$ now, $\;\frac{\beta+\gamma}{k+\alpha}=\;\frac{9+7}{15-3}=\;\frac{16}{12}=\;\frac{4}{3}$ $\therefore   \;\;  \beta+\gamma: k+\alpha=4: 3$ © examsnet.com

search_text: let $h(x)=3 x^4+6 x^3-2 x^2+1$ and $g(x)$ be a linear polynomial. if $\; \frac{h(x)}{(x-1)(x+1)(x-2)} = f(x) + \; \frac{g(x)}{(x-1)(x+1)(x-2)}$ , then $h(-1)+2 h(2)-3 h(1)=$ [ap eapcet 21 may 2025 s1] {'a': '$f(-1)+2 f(2)-3 f(1)$', 'b': '$h(-1)+ f(2)+ g(3)$', 'c': '$g(-1)+2 g(2)-3 g(1)$', 'd': '$h(1)+2  f(2)- g(1)$'} 2025 2025-05-21 shift_1 mathematics   19 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: given, $h(x)=3 x^4+6 x^3-2 x^2+1$ given, $\; \frac{h(x)}{(x-1)(x-2)(x+1)}$ $\; = f(x) + \; \frac{g(x)}{(x-1)(x+1)(x-2} \; \text{ taking lcm }\;$ $\; h(x)=f(x)(x-1)(x+1)(x-2)+g(x)$ $\; h(-1)=g(-1)$ $\; h(2)=g(2)$ $\; h(1)=g(1)$ now, $h(-1)+2 h(2)-3 h(1)$ $=g(-1)+2 g(2-3 g(1)$ © examsnet.com

search_text: if $630^{\circ} < \theta < 810^{\circ}$ and $\tan \theta = -\frac{7}{24}$ , then $\cos \left( \frac{\theta}{4} \right) =$ [ap eapcet 21 may 2025 s1] {'a': '$-\\sqrt{ \\frac{7+5\\sqrt{2}}{10\\sqrt{2}} }$', 'b': '$\\sqrt{ \\frac{7+5\\sqrt{2}}{2\\sqrt{2}} }$', 'c': '$-\\sqrt{ \\frac{5\\sqrt{2}-7}{10\\sqrt{2}} }$', 'd': '$\\sqrt{ \\frac{5\\sqrt{2}-7}{2\\sqrt{2}} }$'} 2025 2025-05-21 shift_1 mathematics   20 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: given, $630^{\circ} < \theta < 810^{\circ}$ and $\tan \theta = \frac{-7}{24}$ $\therefore \theta$ lies iv quadrant $\therefore \; \; \cos \theta \;=\; \frac{24}{25} \; \; 315^{\circ} < \; \frac{\theta}{2} < 405^{\circ}$ $2 \cos^2 \frac{\theta}{2} - 1 \;=\; \frac{24}{25} \; \; 157 \; \frac{1}{2} < \; \frac{\theta}{4} < 2.02 \; \frac{1}{2}$ $2 \cos^2 \frac{\theta}{2} \;=\; \frac{49}{25} \; \; \frac{\theta}{4} \; \text{ lies iii quadrant } \;$ $\rightarrow \; \; \cos \frac{\theta}{2} \;=\; \frac{7}{5\sqrt{2}} \rightarrow 2 \cos^2 \frac{\theta}{4} - 1 = \frac{7}{5\sqrt{2}}$ $\rightarrow 2 \cos^2 \frac{\theta}{4} \;=1+ \frac{7}{5\sqrt{2}} = \frac{7+5\sqrt{2}}{5\sqrt{2}}$ $\rightarrow \; \; \cos \frac{\theta}{4} \;= -\sqrt{ \frac{7+5\sqrt{2}}{10\sqrt{2}} }$ © examsnet.com

question: For $\theta \in \left[-\;\frac{\pi}{2},\;\frac{\pi}{2}\right]$ if $2\cos\theta + \sin\theta = 1$ , and $7\cos\theta + 6\sin\theta = k$ , then the possible values of k are [AP EAPCET 21 May 2025 S1]
search_text: for $\theta \in \left[-\;\frac{\pi}{2},\;\frac{\pi}{2}\right]$ if $2\cos\theta + \sin\theta = 1$ , and $7\cos\theta + 6\sin\theta = k$ , then the possible values of k are [ap eapcet 21 may 2025 s1] {'a': '$8, -2$', 'b': '$6, 2$', 'c': '$12, 4$', 'd': '$7, 6$'} 2025 2025-05-21 shift_1 mathematics   21 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: we have, $2\cos\theta + \sin\theta = 1 \qquad \theta \in \left[-\;\frac{\pi}{2},\;\frac{\pi}{2}\right]$ squaring both sides, we get $\;\rightarrow\;\; (2\cos\theta)^2 = (1 - \sin\theta)^2$ $\;\rightarrow\;\; 4\cos^2\theta = 1 + \sin^2\theta - 2\sin\theta$ $\;\rightarrow\;\; 5\sin^2\theta - 2\sin\theta - 3 = 0$ $\;\rightarrow\;\; (\sin\theta - 1)(5\sin\theta + 3) = 0$ $\;\rightarrow\;\; \sin\theta = 1 \;\text{ and }\; -\frac{3}{5}$ $\;\rightarrow\;\; \cos\theta = 0 \;\text{ and }\; +\frac{4}{5}$ $\;\because\;\; 7\cos\theta + 6\sin\theta = k, \;\text{ when }\; \sin\theta = 1$ $\;\rightarrow\;\; 7(0) + 6(1) = k \rightarrow k = 6$ when, $\sin\theta = -\frac{3}{5}$ and $\cos\theta = \frac{4}{5}$ $k = 7\left(\frac{4}{5}\right) - 6\left(\frac{3}{5}\right) = \frac{28-18}{5} = \frac{10}{5} = 2$ © examsnet.com

question: $\sum\limits_{k=0}^{12} \frac{1}{\sin\left((k+1)\frac{\pi}{6}+\frac{\pi}{4}\right) \sin\left(\frac{k\pi}{6}+\frac{\pi}{4}\right)} =$ [AP EAPCET 21 May 2025 S1]
search_text: $\sum\limits_{k=0}^{12} \frac{1}{\sin\left((k+1)\frac{\pi}{6}+\frac{\pi}{4}\right) \sin\left(\frac{k\pi}{6}+\frac{\pi}{4}\right)} =$ [ap eapcet 21 may 2025 s1] {'a': '$2(\\sqrt{3}+1)$', 'b': '$2(3-\\sqrt{3})$', 'c': '$2(2-\\sqrt{3})$', 'd': '$2(\\sqrt{3}-1)$'} 2025 2025-05-21 shift_1 mathematics   22 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: $\sum\limits_{k=0}^{12} \frac{1}{\sin\left((k+1)\frac{\pi}{6}+\frac{\pi}{4}\right) \cdot \sin\left(\frac{k\pi}{6}+\frac{\pi}{4}\right)}$ multiplying $n^r$ and $d^r$ by $\sin\frac{\pi}{6}$ , $\frac{1}{\sin\frac{\pi}{6}} \sum\limits_{k=0}^{12} \frac{ \sin\left\{ \left((k+1)\frac{\pi}{6}+\frac{4}{\pi}\right) - \left(\frac{k\pi}{6}+\frac{\pi}{4}\right) \right\} }{ 2 \sum\limits_{k=0}^{12} \left( \left((k+1)\frac{\pi}{6}+\frac{\pi}{4}\right) \cdot \sin\left(\frac{k\pi}{6}+\frac{\pi}{4}\right) \right) }$ $=2\left[\cot\left(\frac{k\pi}{6}+\frac{\pi}{4}\right) - \cot\left((k+1)\frac{\pi}{6}+\frac{\pi}{4}\right)\right\}$ $\;\;\; + \left\{ \cot\left(\frac{\pi}{6}+\frac{\pi}{4}\right) - \cot\left(\frac{\pi}{6}+\frac{\pi}{4}\right) \right\}$ $\;\;\; + \dots + \left\{ \cot\left(\frac{12\pi}{6}+\frac{\pi}{4}\right) - \cot\left(\frac{13\pi}{6}+\frac{\pi}{4}\right) \right\}$ $=2\left[\cot\frac{\pi}{4} + \cot\left(\frac{\pi}{6}+\frac{\pi}{4}\right)\right]$ $=2\left[1 - \frac{\sqrt{3}-1}{\sqrt{3}+1}\right] =2\left(\frac{2}{\sqrt{3}+1}\right) =\frac{4(\sqrt{3}-1)}{2}$ $=2(\sqrt{3}-1)$ © examsnet.com

question: The number of solutions of the equation $2 \sin^2 \theta - 3 \cos^2 \theta = \sin \theta \cos \theta$ lying in the interval $(-\pi, \pi)$ is [AP EAPCET 21 May 2025 S1]
search_text: the number of solutions of the equation $2 \sin^2 \theta - 3 \cos^2 \theta = \sin \theta \cos \theta$ lying in the interval $(-\pi, \pi)$ is [ap eapcet 21 may 2025 s1] {'a': '2', 'b': '4', 'c': '3', 'd': '1'} 2025 2025-05-21 shift_1 mathematics   23 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: we have, $2 \sin^2 \theta - 3 \cos^2 \theta = \sin \theta \cos \theta$ dividing both sides by $\cos^2 \theta$ , we get $\cos \theta \neq 0$ $\;\rightarrow\;\; 2 \tan^2 \theta - 3 = \tan \theta$ $\;\rightarrow\;\; 2 \tan^2 \theta - \tan \theta - 3 = 0$ $\;\rightarrow\;\; (2 \tan \theta - 3)(\tan \theta + 1) = 0$ $\;\because\;\; \tan \theta = \frac{3}{2} \; \text{and} \; \tan \theta = -1$ clearly, in the interval $(-\pi, \pi) \tan \theta = \frac{3}{2}$ gives two solution and $\tan \theta = -1$ gives two solution $\therefore$ total number of solution $=4$ © examsnet.com

question: $\tan^{-1} \;\frac{\sqrt{8-2\sqrt{15}}}{\sqrt{15}+1}+\tan^{-1} \;\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}=$ [AP EAPCET 21 May 2025 S1]
search_text: $\tan^{-1} \;\frac{\sqrt{8-2\sqrt{15}}}{\sqrt{15}+1}+\tan^{-1} \;\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}=$ [ap eapcet 21 may 2025 s1] {'a': '$\\;\\frac{\\pi}{6}$', 'b': '$\\;\\frac{\\pi}{4}$', 'c': '$\\;\\frac{\\pi}{3}$', 'd': '$\\;\\frac{\\pi}{2}$'} 2025 2025-05-21 shift_1 mathematics   24 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: $\;\tan^{-1} \;\frac{\sqrt{8-2\sqrt{15}}}{\sqrt{15}+1}+\tan^{-1} \;\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}$ $\;=\tan^{-1} \left( \frac{\sqrt{5}-\sqrt{3}}{\sqrt{15}+1} \right) +\tan^{-1} \left( \frac{1}{\sqrt{5}} \right)$ $\;=\tan^{-1} \left( \frac{\sqrt{5}-\sqrt{3}}{\sqrt{15}+1} \times \frac{\sqrt{15}-1}{\sqrt{15}-1} \right) +\tan^{-1} \;\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}$ $\;=\tan^{-1} \left( \frac{5\sqrt{3} - 3\sqrt{5} - \sqrt{5} + \sqrt{3}}{14} \right) +\tan^{-1} \;\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}$ $\;=\tan^{-1} \left( \frac{6\sqrt{3} - 4\sqrt{5}}{14} \right) +\tan^{-1} \;\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}$ $\;=\tan^{-1} \left( \frac{3\sqrt{3} - 2\sqrt{5}}{7} \right) +\tan^{-1} \;\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}$ $\;=\tan^{-1} \left( \frac{ \frac{3\sqrt{3} - 2\sqrt{5}}{7} + \frac{1}{\sqrt{5}} }{ 1 - \frac{3\sqrt{3} - 2\sqrt{5}}{7} \times \frac{1}{\sqrt{5}} } \right)$ $\;=\tan^{-1} \left( \frac{3\sqrt{15} - 10 + 7}{7\sqrt{5} - 3\sqrt{3} + 2\sqrt{5}} \right)$ $\;=\tan^{-1} \left( \frac{3\sqrt{15} - 3}{9\sqrt{5} - 3\sqrt{3}} \right)$ $\;=\tan^{-1} \left( \frac{\sqrt{15} - 1}{3\sqrt{5} - \sqrt{3}} \times \frac{\sqrt{3}}{\sqrt{3}} \right)$ $\;=\tan^{-1} \left( \frac{3\sqrt{5} - \sqrt{3}}{3\sqrt{5} - \sqrt{3}} \times \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}} \right)$ $\;=\tan^{-1} \;\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}} = \frac{\pi}{6}$ © examsnet.com
