question: In $\triangle ABC$ , the sum of the lengths of two sides is x and the product of those lengths is $y$ . If $c$ is the length of its third side and $x^2-c^2=y$ , then the circumradius of that triangle is [AP EAPCET 21 May 2025 S1]
search_text: in $\triangle abc$ , the sum of the lengths of two sides is x and the product of those lengths is $y$ . if $c$ is the length of its third side and $x^2-c^2=y$ , then the circumradius of that triangle is [ap eapcet 21 may 2025 s1] {'a': '$\\;\\frac{c}{\\sqrt{3}}$', 'b': '$\\;\\frac{c}{3}$', 'c': '$\\;\\frac{y}{\\sqrt{3}}$', 'd': '$\\;\\frac{3y}{2}$'} 2025 2025-05-21 shift_1 mathematics   26 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: we have, $\;x=a+b$ $\;y=a b$ we have, $x^2-c^2=y$ $\rightarrow (a+b)^2-c^2=a b$ $\rightarrow a^2+b^2-c^2=-a b$ $\rightarrow \;\frac{a^2+b^2-c^2}{2ab}=-\;\frac{1}{2}$ $\;\cos c = -\;\frac{1}{2} \rightarrow c = \;\frac{2\pi}{3} \rightarrow \sin \;c = \;\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$ using circumradius formula, $\;c = 2r \sin \;c$ $\;r = \;\frac{c}{\frac{2\sqrt{3}}{2}} = \;\frac{c}{\sqrt{3}}$ © examsnet.com

search_text: if the area of a triangle abc is $4 \sqrt{5} \text{ sq}$ . units, length of the side ca is 6 units and $\tan \frac{b}{2} = \frac{\sqrt{5}}{4}$ , then its smallest side is of length [ap eapcet 21 may 2025 s1] {'a': '5 units<', 'b': '4 units', 'c': '3 units', 'd': '6 units'} 2025 2025-05-21 shift_1 mathematics   27 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: we have, $\tan \frac{b}{2} = \frac{\sqrt{5}}{4}$ and $b=6$ area of $\triangle abc = \triangle = 4 \sqrt{5}$ $\cos b = \frac{1 - \tan^2 \frac{b}{2}}{1 + \tan^2 \frac{b}{2}} = \frac{11}{21}$ $\rightarrow \sin b = \frac{\sqrt{320}}{21} = \frac{8 \sqrt{5}}{21}$ $\because \triangle = \frac{1}{2} a c \sin b = 4 \sqrt{5}$ $= \frac{1}{2} a c \frac{8 \sqrt{5}}{21} = 4 \sqrt{5}$ $\because a c = 21$ $\because b^2 = c^2 + a^2 - 2 a c \cos b$ $\rightarrow 36 = c^2 + a^2 - 2 \times 21 \times \frac{11}{21}$ $\rightarrow 36 = c^2 + a^2 - 22$ $\rightarrow c^2 + a^2 = 58$ $\because (c+a)^2 = c^2 + a^2 + 2 a c$ $= 58 + 42 = 100$ $c + a = 10$ $\rightarrow c = 7 \text{ and } a = 3$ $\because$ smallest sides is 3 units. © examsnet.com

search_text: if $\overline{a}, \overline{b}, \overline{c}$ are three unit vectors such that $\left|\overline{a}-\overline{b}\right|^2+\left|\overline{b}-\overline{c}\right|^2+\left|\overline{c}-\overline{a}\right|^2=15$ , then $\left|\overline{a}-\overline{b}-\overline{c}\right|^2-4(\overline{b} \cdot \overline{c})=$ [ap eapcet 21 may 2025 s1] {'a': '6', 'b': '15', 'c': '12', 'd': '10'} 2025 2025-05-21 shift_1 mathematics   31 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: given, $\;\left| a - b \right|^2+\left| b - c \right|^2+\left| c - a \right|^2=15$ $\rightarrow \left| a \right|^2+\left| b \right|^2-2 a \cdot b +\left| b \right|^2+\left| c \right|^2$ $\; -2 b \cdot c + \left| c \right|^2 + \left| a \right|^2 -2 c \cdot a =15$ $\rightarrow 6-2( a \cdot b + b \cdot c + c \cdot a )=15$ $\rightarrow a \cdot b + b \cdot c + c \cdot a =-\; \frac{9}{2}$ $\; \left| a - b - c \right|^2-4( b \cdot c )$ $\rightarrow \left| a \right|^2+\left| b \right|^2+\left| c \right|^2$ $\; +2(- a \cdot b + b \cdot c - c \cdot a )-4( b \cdot c )$ $\; =3-2( a \cdot b + b \cdot c + c \cdot a )$ $\; =3-2 \left(-\; \frac{9}{2}\right)$ $\; =3+9=12$ © examsnet.com

question: If $\overline{a} = \overline{i} + p \overline{j} - 3 \overline{k}, \overline{b} = p \overline{i} - 3 \overline{j} + \overline{k}, \overline{c} = -3 \overline{i} + \overline{j} + 2 \overline{k}$ are three vectors such that $\left| \overline{a} \times \overline{b} \right| = \left| \overline{a} \times \overline{c} \right|$ , then $p =$ [AP EAPCET 21 May 2025 S1]

search_text: if $\int \left(3 t^2 \sin \frac{1}{t} - t \cos \frac{1}{t}\right) dt = f(t) \sin \left(\frac{1}{t}\right) + c$ , then $f(2)=$ [ap eapcet 21 may 2025 s1] {'a': '$2$', 'b': '$-12$', 'c': '$8$', 'd': '$-16$'} 2025 2025-05-21 shift_1 mathematics   70 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: we have, $\int \left(3 t^2 \sin \frac{1}{t} - t \cos \frac{1}{t}\right) dt = f(t) \sin \frac{1}{t} + c$ $\int \sin \frac{1}{t} \cdot 3 t^2 dt - \int t \cos \frac{1}{t} dt = f(t) \sin \frac{1}{t} + c$ $\sin \frac{1}{t} \cdot t^3 - \int \cos \left(\frac{1}{t}\right) \left(-\frac{1}{t^2}\right) t^3 dt - \int t \cos \frac{1}{t} dt$ $\rightarrow t^3 \sin \frac{1}{t} + \int t \cos \frac{1}{t} dt - \int t \cos \frac{1}{t} dt = f(t) \sin \frac{1}{t} + c$ $\rightarrow t^3 \sin \frac{1}{t} = f(t) \sin \frac{1}{t} + c$ $\therefore f(t) = t^3$ $f(2)=2^3=8$ © examsnet.com

search_text: $\int \frac{\sin 2x}{\sin^2 x + 3\cos x - 3} dx$ [ap eapcet 21 may 2025 s1] {'a': '$2\\log\\left| \\frac{\\cos x-2}{\\cos x-1} \\right|+c$', 'b': '$\\log\\left( \\frac{(\\cos x-2)^2}{(\\cos x-1)^4} \\right)+c$', 'c': '$\\log\\left( \\frac{(\\cos x-2)^2}{\\left|\\cos x-1\\right|} \\right)+c$', 'd': '$\\log\\left(\\frac{(\\cos x-2)^4}{(\\cos x-1)^2}\\right)+c$'} 2025 2025-05-21 shift_1 mathematics   72 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: $\;\text{ let }\; i=\int \frac{\sin 2x}{\sin^2 x + 3\cos x - 3} dx$ $\;=-\int \frac{\sin 2x}{1-\cos^2 x+3\cos x-3} dx$ $\;=\int \frac{2 \sin x \cdot \cos x}{-\cos^2 x+3\cos x-2} dx$ $\;=\int \frac{2t(-dt)}{-t^2+3t-2} \qquad \text{put } \cos x=t$ $\; \sin x dx = -dt$ $\;=\int \frac{2t dt}{t^2-3t+2} = \int \frac{2t}{(t-2)(t-1)} dt$ $\;=2 \int \left( \frac{2}{t-2} - \frac{1}{t-1} \right) dt$ $\;=2[2\ln(t-2)-\ln(t-1)]$ $\;=2\ln\left( \frac{(t-2)^2}{t-1} \right) = \ln \frac{(t-2)^4}{(t-1)^2} + c$ $\;=\ln\left(\frac{(\cos x-2)^4}{(\cos x-1)^2}\right)+c$ © examsnet.com

search_text: if $\int \frac{dx}{\sin^3 x + \cos^3 x} = a \log \left| \frac{\sqrt{2}+t}{\sqrt{2}-t} \right| + b \tan^{-1}(t) + c$ , then $\left( \frac{b}{a}, t \right) =$ [ap eapcet 21 may 2025 s1] {'a': '$(3\\sqrt{2}, \\sin x - \\cos x)$', 'b': '$(2\\sqrt{2}, \\sin x - \\cos x)$', 'c': '$\\left( \\frac{\\sqrt{2}}{3}, \\sin x - \\cos x \\right)$', 'd': '$\\left( \\frac{3}{\\sqrt{2}}, \\sin x + \\cos x \\right)$'} 2025 2025-05-21 shift_1 mathematics   73 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: $\text{ let } i = \int \frac{1}{\sin^3 x + \cos^3 x} \, dx$ $= \int \frac{1}{(\sin x + \cos x)(\sin^2 x + \cos^2 x - \sin x \cos x)} \, dx$ $= \int \frac{\sin x + \cos x}{(\sin x + \cos x)^2 (1 - \sin x \cos x)} \, dx$ $= \int \frac{\sin x + \cos x}{(1 + 2 \sin x \cos x)(1 - \sin x \cos x)} \, dx$ $= \int \frac{dt}{(1+1-t^2)\left(1-\frac{1-t^2}{2}\right)}$ put $\sin x - \cos x = t$ $(\cos x + \sin x) \, dx = dt$ $1 - 2 \sin x \cos x = t^2$ $2 \sin x \cos x = 1 - t^2$ $= \int \frac{2 \, dt}{(2-t^2)(1+t^2)} = -2 \int \frac{dt}{(t^2+1)(t^2-2)}$ $= -\frac{2}{3} \int \left( \frac{1}{t^2-2} - \frac{1}{t^2+1} \right) dt$ $= -\frac{2}{3} \left[ \frac{1}{2\sqrt{2}} \ln \left( \frac{t-\sqrt{2}}{t+\sqrt{2}} \right) - \tan^{-1} t \right]$ $= -\frac{1}{3\sqrt{2}} \ln \left( \frac{\sin x - \cos x - \sqrt{2}}{\sin x - \cos x + \sqrt{2}} \right) + \frac{2}{3} \tan^{-1}(\sin x - \cos x) + c$ $= \frac{1}{3\sqrt{2}} \ln \left| \frac{\sin x - \cos + \sqrt{2}}{\sin x - \cos x - \sqrt{2}} \right| + \frac{2}{3} \tan^{-1}(\sin x - \cos x) + c$ $\because a = \frac{1}{3\sqrt{2}}, b = \frac{2}{3} \text{ and } t = \sin x - \cos x$ $\because \left( \frac{b}{a}, t \right) = (2\sqrt{2}, \sin x - \cos x)$ © examsnet.com

question: $\int\limits_{\pi/4}^{\pi/3} \frac{\cos x - \sin x}{\sin 2x}dx=$ [AP EAPCET 21 May 2025 S1]
search_text: $\int\limits_{\pi/4}^{\pi/3} \frac{\cos x - \sin x}{\sin 2x}dx=$ [ap eapcet 21 may 2025 s1] {'a': '$\\frac{1}{2} \\log \\left[ \\frac{(3+2\\sqrt{2})(2-\\sqrt{3})}{\\sqrt{3}} \\right]$', 'b': '$\\frac{1}{2} \\log \\left[ \\frac{(3-2\\sqrt{2})(2+\\sqrt{3})}{\\sqrt{3}} \\right]$', 'c': '$\\log \\left[ \\frac{(3-2\\sqrt{2})(2-\\sqrt{3})}{\\sqrt{3}} \\right]$', 'd': '$\\log \\left[ \\frac{(3+2\\sqrt{2})(2-\\sqrt{3})}{\\sqrt{3}} \\right]$'} 2025 2025-05-21 shift_1 mathematics   74 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: $i=\int_{\frac{\pi}{4}}^{\frac{\pi}{3}} \frac{\cos x - \sin x}{\sin 2x} dx$ $i=\int_{\sqrt{2}}^{\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}+\frac{1}{2}} \frac{dt}{t^2-1}$ put $\sin x + \cos x = t$ $(\cos x - \sin x) dx = dt$ $1 + \sin 2x = t^2$ $=\left[ \frac{1}{2} \ln \left( \frac{t-1}{t+1} \right) \right]_{\sqrt{2}}^{\frac{\sqrt{3}+1}{2}}$ $=\frac{1}{2} \left[ \ln \left( \frac{\frac{\sqrt{3}+1}{2}-1}{\frac{\sqrt{3}+1}{2}+1} \right) - \ln \left( \frac{\sqrt{2}-1}{\sqrt{2}+1} \right) \right]$ $=\frac{1}{2} \left[ \ln \frac{\sqrt{3}-1}{\sqrt{3}+3} - \ln \left( \frac{\sqrt{2}-1}{\sqrt{2}+1} \right) \right]$ $=\frac{1}{2} \left[ \ln \frac{2(2\sqrt{3}-3)}{6} - \ln (3-2\sqrt{2}) \right]$ $=\frac{1}{2} \left[ \ln \frac{2\sqrt{3}-3}{3} + \ln (3+2\sqrt{2}) \right]$ $=\frac{1}{2} \left[ \ln \left( \frac{2-\sqrt{3}}{\sqrt{3}} \right) + \ln (3+2\sqrt{2}) \right]$ $=\frac{1}{2} \ln \left[ \frac{(3+2\sqrt{2})(2-\sqrt{3})}{\sqrt{3}} \right]$ © examsnet.com

question: $\int\limits_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{2}} \;\frac{\sin x}{1+\cos x+\sin x} dx=$ [AP EAPCET 21 May 2025 S1]
search_text: $\int\limits_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{2}} \;\frac{\sin x}{1+\cos x+\sin x} dx=$ [ap eapcet 21 may 2025 s1] {'a': '$\\frac{\\pi}{2}+\\frac{1}{2}\\log 2$', 'b': '$\\frac{\\pi}{4}-\\frac{1}{2}\\log 2$', 'c': '$\\frac{\\pi}{4}$', 'd': '$\\frac{3\\pi}{4}+\\log 2$'} 2025 2025-05-21 shift_1 mathematics   75 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: $i\;=\int\limits_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{2}} \;\frac{\sin x}{1+\cos x+\sin x} dx$ $\;=\int\limits_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{2}} \;\frac{2\sin\frac{x}{2}\cos\frac{x}{2}}{2\cos^2\frac{x}{2}+2\sin\frac{x}{2}\cos\frac{x}{2}} dx$ $\;=\int\limits_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{2}} \;\frac{\sin\frac{x}{2}}{\cos\frac{x}{2}+\sin\frac{x}{2}} dx$ $\;=\frac{1}{2}\int\limits_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{2}} \;\frac{\sin\frac{x}{2}+\cos\frac{x}{2}+\sin\frac{x}{2}-\cos\frac{x}{2}}{\cos\frac{x}{2}+\sin\frac{x}{2}} dx$ $\;=\frac{1}{2}\int\limits_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{2}} \left(1+\frac{\sin\frac{x}{2}-\cos\frac{x}{2}}{\cos\frac{x}{2}+\sin\frac{x}{2}}\right) dx$ $\;=\frac{1}{2}\left[x+\left(-2\ln\left(\cos\frac{x}{2}+\sin\frac{x}{2}\right)\right)\right]_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{2}}$ $\;=\frac{1}{2}\left[x-2\ln\left(\cos\frac{x}{2}+\sin\frac{x}{2}\right)\right]_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{2}}$ $\;=\frac{1}{2}\left[\left(\frac{\pi}{2}-2\ln\sqrt{2}\right)-0\right]$ $\;=\frac{\pi}{4}-\ln\sqrt{2}=\frac{\pi}{4}-\frac{1}{2}\ln 2$ © examsnet.com

search_text: $\lim\limits_{n \to \infty}\left[\;\frac{n+1}{n^2+1^2}+\;\frac{n+2}{n^2+2^2}+\;\frac{n+3}{n^2+3^2}+\dots+\;\frac{n+2n}{n^2+4n^2}\right] =$ [ap eapcet 21 may 2025 s1] {'a': '$\\tan^{-1} 2+\\;\\frac{1}{2} \\log 3$', 'b': '$\\;\\frac{\\pi}{4}+\\;\\frac{1}{2} \\log 3$', 'c': '$\\tan^{-1} 2+\\;\\frac{1}{2} \\log 5$', 'd': '$\\;\\frac{\\pi}{4}+\\;\\frac{1}{2} \\log 5$'} 2025 2025-05-21 shift_1 mathematics   76 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: $\;\lim\limits_{n \to \infty}\sum\limits_{r=1}^{2n} \;\frac{n+r}{n^2+(r)^2}$ $\;\lim\limits_{n \to \infty}\;\frac{1}{n} \sum\limits_{r=1}^{2n} \;\frac{1+\frac{r}{n}}{1+\left(\;\frac{r}{n}\right)^2}$ $\;=\int\limits_{0}^{2} \;\frac{1+x}{1+(x)^2}\,dx$ $\;=\int\limits_{0}^{2} \;\frac{1}{1+x^2}\,dx+\int\limits_{0}^{2} \;\frac{x}{1+x^2}\,dx$ $\;=\left(\tan^{-1} x\right)_0^2+\left(\;\frac{1}{2} \ln (1+x^2)\right)_0^2$ $\;=\tan^{-1} 2+\;\frac{1}{2} \ln 5$ © examsnet.com

search_text: $\int\limits_{0}^{\pi} \;\frac{x \sin x}{1+\cos^2 x} dx=$ [ap eapcet 21 may 2025 s1] {'a': '$\\;\\frac{\\pi^2}{4}$', 'b': '$\\;\\frac{\\pi}{2}$', 'c': '$\\;\\frac{\\pi^2}{2}$', 'd': '$\\;\\frac{\\pi}{4}$'} 2025 2025-05-21 shift_1 mathematics   77 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: $i=\int\limits_{0}^{\pi} \;\frac{x \sin x}{1+\cos^2 x}$ apply property $\;\int\limits_{a}^{b} x f(x) dx=\;\frac{a+b}{2} \int f(x) dx$ $\;\; \text{ if } \; f(a+b-x)=f(x)$ $\;\;\;\;\; i=\;\frac{\pi}{2} \int\limits_{0}^{\pi} \;\frac{\sin x}{1+\cos^2 x} dx$ put $\cos x = t$ $\sin x dx\; = -dt$ $i\; = -\;\frac{\pi}{2} \int\limits_{+1}^{-1} \;\frac{dt}{1+t^2}$ $\; = \;\frac{\pi}{2} \int_{-1}^{1} \;\frac{dt}{1+t^2} = \;\frac{\pi}{2} \cdot 2 \int\limits_{0}^{1} \;\frac{dt}{1+t^2}$ $\; = \pi (\tan^{-1} t)_0^1$ $\; = \pi \tan^{-1} 1 = \pi \times \;\frac{\pi}{4} = \;\frac{\pi^2}{4}$ © examsnet.com

search_text: the differential equation corresponding to the family of parabolas whose axis is along $x=1$ is [ap eapcet 21 may 2025 s1] {'a': '$\\; \\frac{d^2 y}{dx^2}-(x-1) \\;\\frac{dy}{dx}=0$', 'b': '$(x-1) \\;\\frac{d^2 y}{d x^2}-\\;\\frac{d y}{d x}=0$', 'c': '$\\; \\frac{d^2 y}{dx^2}+(x-1) \\;\\frac{dy}{dx}- y=0$', 'd': '$(x-1) \\;\\frac{d^2 y}{d x^2}+\\;\\frac{d y}{d x}=0$'} 2025 2025-05-21 shift_1 mathematics   78 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: let the equation of parabola having axis $x=1$ be $(x-1)^2=4 a y$ now, differenting w.r.t. $x$ , we get $\;2(x-1)\;=4 a y^{'}$ $\rightarrow 2(x-1)\;=\;\frac{(x-1)^2}{y} \cdot y^{'}$ $\rightarrow 2 y\;=(x-1) y^{'}$ again, differentiating $\;2 y^{'}=(x-1) y^{''}+y^{'}$ $\; \because (x-1) \;\frac{d^2 y}{d x^2}-\;\frac{d y}{d x}=0$ © examsnet.com

search_text: the general solution of the equation $\frac{dy}{dx}+\frac{1}{x}y=\frac{1}{x}e^x$ is [ap eapcet 21 may 2025 s1] {'a': '$y=x e^x+c$', 'b': '$y=x e^x+c e^{-x}$', 'c': '$y=\\frac{e^x+c}{x}$', 'd': '$y=\\frac{e^{-x}+c x}{x}$'} 2025 2025-05-21 shift_1 mathematics   79 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: $\frac{dy}{dx}+\frac{y}{x}=\frac{e^x}{x}$ $if=e^{\int\frac{1}{x}dx}=e^{\ln x}=x$ solution of differential equations is $y\cdot x=\int e^x\cdot\frac{1}{x}\cdot x\,dx$ $\rightarrow xy=e^x+c$ $\therefore y=\frac{e^x+c}{x}$ © examsnet.com

search_text: the general solution of the differential equation $\left(x \sin \frac{y}{x}\right) dy = \left(y \sin \frac{y}{x} - x\right) dx$ is [ap eapcet 21 may 2025 s1] {'a': '$\\log x + \\tan \\frac{y}{x} = c$', 'b': '$\\log x + \\cos \\frac{y}{x} = c$', 'c': '$\\log x - \\sin \\frac{y}{x} = c$', 'd': '$\\log x - \\cos \\frac{y}{x} = c$'} 2025 2025-05-21 shift_1 mathematics   80 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: $\left(x \sin \frac{y}{x}\right) dy = \left(y \sin \frac{y}{x} - x\right) dx$ $\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{y \sin \frac{y}{x} - x}{x \sin \frac{y}{x}}$ put $y = v x$ $\frac{dy}{dx} = v + x \frac{dv}{dx}$ $\rightarrow v + x \frac{dv}{dx} = \frac{v \sin v - 1}{\sin v}$ $\rightarrow x \frac{dv}{dx} = \frac{v \sin v - 1 - v \sin v}{\sin v}$ $= -\frac{1}{\sin v}$ $\rightarrow \int \sin v \, dv + \int \frac{dx}{x} = 0$ $\rightarrow - \cos v + \ln x = c$ $\rightarrow \ln x - \cos \frac{y}{x} = c$ © examsnet.com

search_text: as shown in the figure, a force $f$ is applied on a block of mass $\sqrt{3} \ \mathrm{kg}$ placed on a rough horizontal surface. the maximum value of f for the block not to move is (coefficient of static friction between the block and the surface is $\; \frac{1}{2\sqrt{3}}$ and acceleration due to gravity $=10 \ \mathrm{m} \ \mathrm{s}^{-2}$ [ap eapcet 21 may 2025 s1] {'a': '$5 \\ \\mathrm{n}$', 'b': '$10 \\ \\mathrm{n}$', 'c': '$15 \\ \\mathrm{n}$', 'd': '$20 \\ \\mathrm{n}$'} 2025 2025-05-21 shift_1 physics   86 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: maximum static friction $(f_s)_{\max} = \mu_s n$ for the block not to move, $\; f \cos 60^{\circ} = (f_s)_{\max}$ $\; f \cos 60^{\circ} = \mu_s n$ $\; f \cos 60^{\circ} = \mu_s (m g + f \sin \; 60^{\circ})$ $\; \rightarrow f \times \; \frac{1}{2} = \; \frac{1}{2\sqrt{3}} \left(\sqrt{3} \times 10 + f \; \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)$ $\; \rightarrow \;\; f = \; \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}} \left(10 \sqrt{3} + \; \frac{f \sqrt{3}}{2}\right)$ $\; \rightarrow \;\; f = 10 + \; \frac{f}{2}$ $\; \rightarrow \;\; f - \; \frac{f}{2} = 10$ $\; f = 20 \ \mathrm{n}$ © examsnet.com

search_text: the linear momentum of a body of mass 8 kg is $24\,\mathrm{kg}\,\mathrm{m}\,\mathrm{s}^{-1}$ . if a constant force of 24 n acts on the body in the direction of motion of the body for a time of 3 s , then the increase in the kinetic energy of the body is [ap eapcet 21 may 2025 s1] {'a': '$480\\,\\mathrm{j}$', 'b': '$540\\,\\mathrm{j}$', 'c': '$270\\,\\mathrm{j}$', 'd': '$240\\,\\mathrm{j}$'} 2025 2025-05-21 shift_1 physics   87 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: $\;p=mv=24\,\mathrm{kg}\,\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}$ $\; \therefore u=\frac{24}{m}=\frac{24}{8}=3\,\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}$ $\;\;\text{ impulse, }\; j=f \cdot \delta t$ $\;\;\;\;\;\;\; =24 \times 3=72\,\mathrm{ns}$ $\therefore \;\; j=\delta p=72\,\mathrm{ns}$ $\therefore$ final momentum $p_f\;=p_i+\delta p=24+72$ $\;=96\,\mathrm{kg}\,\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}$ $\;\;\therefore\;\; v_f\;=\;\frac{p_f}{m}=\;\frac{96}{8}=12\,\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}$ thus, increase in kinetic energy, $\delta k\;=k_f-k_i$ $\;=\;\frac{1}{2} m v_f^2-\;\frac{1}{2} m u^2$ $\;=\;\frac{1}{2} m (v_f^2-u^2)$ $\;=\;\frac{1}{2} \times 8 (12^2-3^2)$ $\;=4(135)=540\,\mathrm{j}$ © examsnet.com

question: If the sum of heights of transmitting and receiving antennas in line of sight of communication is ' $h$ ', then the height of receiving antenna, to have the range maximum is [AP EAPCET 21 May 2025 S1]
search_text: if the sum of heights of transmitting and receiving antennas in line of sight of communication is ' $h$ ', then the height of receiving antenna, to have the range maximum is [ap eapcet 21 may 2025 s1] {'a': '$\\;\\frac{h}{2}$', 'b': '$\\;\\frac{h}{4}$', 'c': '$2 h$', 'd': '$\\;\\frac{2h}{3}$'} 2025 2025-05-21 shift_1 physics   120 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: the line-of-sight range for antenna heights $h_t$ and $h_r$ is $x=\sqrt{2rh_t}+\sqrt{2rh_r}$ given that the sum of the heights is fixed, $h_t+h_r=h$ let the transmitting antenna height be $h_t=h$ then the receiving antenna height is $h_r=h-h$ so the range becomes $x=\sqrt{2r}\left(\sqrt{h}+\sqrt{h-h}\right)$ for maximum range, set the derivative with respect to $h$ equal to zero: $\frac{dx}{dh}=\sqrt{2r}\left(\frac{1}{2\sqrt{h}}-\frac{1}{2\sqrt{h-h}}\right)=0$ this gives $\frac{1}{\sqrt{h}}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{h-h}}$ $h=h-h$ $h=\frac{h}{2}$ therefore, $h_r=h-h=h-\frac{h}{2}=\frac{h}{2}$ hence the receiving antenna height required for maximum range is $\frac{h}{2}$ . so the correct option is (0). © examsnet.com

question: Gold crystallises in fcc lattice. The edge length of the unit cell is $4\ \text{\AA}$ . What are $x$ and $y$ respectively? $(.$ Molar mass of gold $=197\ \text{g mol}^{-1} ;\ N=6 \times 10^{23}\ \text{mol}^{-1})$ [AP EAPCET 21 May 2025 S1]
search_text: gold crystallises in fcc lattice. the edge length of the unit cell is $4\ \text{\aa}$ . the closest distance between gold atoms is ' $x$ ' $\text{\aa}$ and density of gold is ' $y$ ' $\text{g cm}^{-3}$ . what are $x$ and $y$ respectively? $(.$ molar mass of gold $=197\ \text{g mol}^{-1} ;\ n=6 \times 10^{23}\ \text{mol}^{-1})$ [ap eapcet 21 may 2025 s1] {'a': '$\\sqrt{2}, 41.04$', 'b': '$2\\sqrt{2}, 20.52$', 'c': '$2\\sqrt{3}, 10.25$', 'd': '$\\sqrt{3}, 5.15$'} 2025 2025-05-21 shift_1 chemistry   140 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: the closest distance $r$ is given by $r =\; \frac{a}{\sqrt{2}} \rightarrow r =\; \frac{4}{\sqrt{2}} = 2\sqrt{2}\ \text{\aa} = x\ \text{\aa}$ the density ( $d$ ) is given by, $d =\; \frac{z m}{a^3 n_a}$ $z = 4,\ m = 197\ \text{g mol}^{-1}$ $a = 4 \times 10^{-8}\ \text{cm},\ n_a = 6 \times 10^{23}\ \text{mol}^{-1}$ $d =\; \frac{4 \times 197\ \text{g mol}^{-1}}{(4 \times 10^{-8}\ \text{cm})^3 \times 6 \times 10^{23}\ \text{mol}^{-1}}$ $\approx 20.52\ \text{g cm}^{-3}=y\ \text{g cm}^{-3}$ $\therefore\ x=2\sqrt{2}\ \text{and}\ y=20.52$ © examsnet.com

question: If $2.5+5.9+8.13+11.17+\dots$ to n terms $= an^{3}+bn^{2}+cn+d$ , then $a-b+c-d=$ [AP EAPCET 21 May 2025 S2]
search_text: if $2.5+5.9+8.13+11.17+\dots$ to n terms $= an^{3}+bn^{2}+cn+d$ , then $a-b+c-d=$ [ap eapcet 21 may 2025 s2] {'a': '7', 'b': '5', 'c': '-3', 'd': '-1'} 2025 2025-05-21 shift_2 mathematics   3 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: given, $2 \cdot 5+5 \cdot 9+8 \cdot 13+11 \cdot 17+\dots+$ upto $n$ terms $\;t_n=(3n-1)(4n+1)$ $\;t_n=12n^{2}-n-1$ $\;\therefore s_n=\sum t_n=\sum (12n^{2}-n-1)=12\sum n^{2}-\sum n-\sum 1$ $\;=12 \cdot \frac{n(n+1)(2n+1)}{6}-\frac{n(n+1)}{2}-n$ $\;=n\left[2(2n^{2}+3n+1)-\frac{n+1}{2}-1\right]=\frac{n}{2}\left[8n^{2}+12n+4-n-1-2\right]$ $\;=\frac{n}{2}[8n^{2}+11n+1]$ $\;=4n^{3}+\frac{11}{2}n^{2}+\frac{n}{2}=an^{3}+bn^{2}+cn+d$ $\;\rightarrow a=4, b=\frac{11}{2}, c=\frac{1}{2}\;\text{ and }\;d=0$ $\;\therefore a-b+c-d=4-\frac{11}{2}+\frac{1}{2}-0=4-5=-1$ © examsnet.com

search_text: if $a=\begin{pmatrix} 1 & 2 & -2 \\ 2 & -1 & 2 \\ -1 & 1 & -2 \end{pmatrix}$ , then $a+2a^{-1}=$ [ap eapcet 21 may 2025 s2] {'a': '$\\begin{pmatrix} 1 & 4 & 0 \\\\ 4 & -5 & -4 \\\\ 0 & -2 & -7 \\end{pmatrix}$', 'b': '$\\begin{pmatrix} 0 & 2 & 2 \\\\ 2 & -4 & -6 \\\\ 2 & -3 & -5 \\end{pmatrix}$', 'c': '$\\begin{pmatrix} 0 & 2 & 1 \\\\ 2 & -4 & -3 \\\\ 2 & -6 & -5 \\end{pmatrix}$', 'd': '$\\begin{pmatrix} 1 & 4 & -1 \\\\ 4 & -5 & -1 \\\\ 1 & -5 & -7 \\end{pmatrix}$'} 2025 2025-05-21 shift_2 mathematics   4 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: we have, $a=\begin{pmatrix} 1 & 2 & -2 \\ 2 & -1 & 2 \\ -1 & 1 & -2 \end{pmatrix}$ $|a|\;=|(2-2)-2(-4+2)-2(2-1)|=4-2=2$ $\operatorname{adj}(a)\;=\begin{pmatrix} 0 & 2 & 2 \\ 2 & -4 & -6 \\ 1 & -3 & -5 \end{pmatrix}$ $a^{-1}\;=\;\frac{\operatorname{adj}(a)}{|a|}=\;\frac{1}{2}\begin{pmatrix} 0 & 2 & 2 \\ 2 & -4 & -6 \\ 1 & -3 & -5 \end{pmatrix}$ then, $a+2a^{-1}=\begin{pmatrix} 1 & 4 & 0 \\ 4 & -5 & -4 \\ 0 & -2 & -7 \end{pmatrix}$ © examsnet.com

question: If $A=\begin{pmatrix} a & b & c \\ d & e & f \\ 1 & m & n \end{pmatrix}$ is a matrix such that $|A|>0$ and $\mathrm{Adj}\,A=\begin{pmatrix}0 & 4 & -6\\10 & 8 & 0\\2 & 4 & -4\end{pmatrix}$ , then $\frac{cd}{fb}+\frac{\ln}{em}=$ [AP EAPCET 21 May 2025 S2]
search_text: if $a=\begin{pmatrix} a & b & c \\ d & e & f \\ 1 & m & n \end{pmatrix}$ is a matrix such that $|a|>0$ and $\mathrm{adj}\,a=\begin{pmatrix}0 & 4 & -6\\10 & 8 & 0\\2 & 4 & -4\end{pmatrix}$ , then $\frac{cd}{fb}+\frac{\ln}{em}=$ [ap eapcet 21 may 2025 s2] {'a': '$2a$', 'b': '$a+m$', 'c': '$a+b$', 'd': 'a'} 2025 2025-05-21 shift_2 mathematics   5 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: we have, $a=\begin{pmatrix} a & b & c \\ d & e & f \\ l & m & n \end{pmatrix}$ and $\mathrm{adj}(a)=\begin{pmatrix}0 & 4 & -6\\10 & 8 & 0\\2 & 4 & -4\end{pmatrix}|\mathrm{adj}\,a|=|a|^2 \rightarrow |a|^2=16 \rightarrow |a|=4$ we know that $\mathrm{adj}(\mathrm{adj}\,a)=|a|^{n-2}a=|a|^{3-2}a=|a|a$ $\rightarrow a=\frac{1}{|a|}\mathrm{adj}(\mathrm{adj}\,a)$ $\text{here,}\;\mathrm{adj}(\mathrm{adj}\,a)=\begin{pmatrix}-32 & -8 & 48\\40 & 12 & -60\\24 & 8 & -40\end{pmatrix}$ $\therefore a=\frac{1}{4}\begin{pmatrix}-32 & -8 & 48\\40 & 12 & -60\\24 & 8 & -40\end{pmatrix}=\begin{pmatrix}-8 & -2 & 12\\10 & 3 & -15\\6 & 2 & -10\end{pmatrix}$ $\rightarrow a=-8,\;b=-2,\;c=12,\;d=10,\;e=3,\;f=-15,\;l=6,\;m=2,$ $n=-10$ $\therefore \frac{cd}{fb}+\frac{\ln}{em}=\frac{12\times10}{(-15)\times(-2)}+\frac{6\times(-10)}{3\times2}$ $=\frac{120}{30}-\frac{60}{6}=4-10=-6$ also, (a) $2a=-16$ (b) $a+m=-8+2=-6$ (c) $a+b=-8-2=-10$ (d) $a=-8$ © examsnet.com

question: In solving a system of linear equations $AX = B$ by Cramer's rule, in the usual notation, if $\Delta_1 = \begin{vmatrix} -11 & 1 & -7 \\ -4 & 1 & -2 \\ 5 & 1 & 1 \end{vmatrix}$ and $\Delta_3 = \begin{vmatrix} 4 & 1 & -11 \\ 1 & 1 & -4 \\ 4 & 1 & 5 \end{vmatrix}$ , then $X =$ [AP EAPCET 21 May 2025 S2]
search_text: in solving a system of linear equations $ax = b$ by cramer's rule, in the usual notation, if $\delta_1 = \begin{vmatrix} -11 & 1 & -7 \\ -4 & 1 & -2 \\ 5 & 1 & 1 \end{vmatrix}$ and $\delta_3 = \begin{vmatrix} 4 & 1 & -11 \\ 1 & 1 & -4 \\ 4 & 1 & 5 \end{vmatrix}$ , then $x =$ [ap eapcet 21 may 2025 s2] {'a': '$\\begin{bmatrix} -1 \\\\ 1 \\\\ 2 \\end{bmatrix}$', 'b': '$\\begin{bmatrix} 2 \\\\ 1 \\\\ -1 \\end{bmatrix}$', 'c': '$\\begin{bmatrix} 1 \\\\ -1 \\\\ 2 \\end{bmatrix}$', 'd': '$\\begin{bmatrix} 1 \\\\ 2 \\\\ -1 \\end{bmatrix}$'} 2025 2025-05-21 shift_2 mathematics   6 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: given, $\delta_1\; = \begin{vmatrix} -11 & 1 & -7 \\ -4 & 1 & -2 \\ 5 & 1 & 1 \end{vmatrix}$ $\because \delta \delta_1\; = -11(3)-1(6)-7(-9)=-33-6+63=24$ $\delta_3\; = \begin{vmatrix} 4 & 1 & -11 \\ 1 & 1 & -4 \\ 4 & 1 & 5 \end{vmatrix} = 4(9)-1(21)-11(-3)=48$ $\delta\; = \begin{vmatrix} 4 & 1 & -7 \\ 1 & 1 & -2 \\ 4 & 1 & 1 \end{vmatrix} = 4(3)-1(9)-7(-3)=24$ by inspection $\; \delta_2 = \begin{vmatrix} 4 & -11 & -7 \\ 1 & -4 & -2 \\ 4 & 5 & 1 \end{vmatrix} = 4(6)+11(9)-7(21)=-24$ $\; x = \; \frac{\delta_1}{\delta} = \; \frac{24}{24} = 1, y = \; \frac{\delta_2}{\delta} = \; \frac{-24}{24} = -1 \; \text{ and } \; z = \; \frac{\delta_3}{\delta} = \; \frac{48}{24} = 2$ $\; x = \begin{bmatrix} x \\ y \\ z \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ -1 \\ 2 \end{bmatrix}$ © examsnet.com

question: If $a=\operatorname{Im}\left(\frac{1+z^2}{2 i z}\right)$ and $z$ is any non zero complex number such that $|z|=1$ , then $a=$ [AP EAPCET 21 May 2025 S2]
search_text: if $a=\operatorname{im}\left(\frac{1+z^2}{2 i z}\right)$ and $z$ is any non zero complex number such that $|z|=1$ , then $a=$ [ap eapcet 21 may 2025 s2] {'a': 're(z)', 'b': 're(z) im(z)', 'c': '- re(z)', 'd': 're(z) + im(z)'} 2025 2025-05-21 shift_2 mathematics   7 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: we have, $|z|=1$ $\because$ let $z=\cos\theta+i\sin\theta=e^{i\theta}$ $1+z^2=1+\cos 2\theta+i\sin 2\theta$ $=2\cos^2\theta+2i\sin\theta\cos\theta$ $=2\cos\theta(\cos\theta+i\sin\theta)=2\cos\theta\cdot e^{i\theta}$ now, $\frac{1+z^2}{2 i z}=\frac{2\cos\theta\cdot e^{i\theta}}{2 i e^{i\theta}}=\frac{\cos\theta}{i}=-i\cos\theta$ now, $\operatorname{lm}\left(\frac{1+z^2}{2 i z}\right)=-\cos\theta=-\operatorname{re}(z)$ © examsnet.com

search_text: if $\left(\frac{\cos\theta + i\sin\theta}{\sin\theta + i\cos\theta}\right)^{2024} + \left(\frac{1+\cos\theta + i\sin\theta}{1-\cos\theta + i\sin\theta}\right)^{2025} = x+iy$ , then the value of $x+y$ at $\theta = \frac{\pi}{2}$ is [ap eapcet 21 may 2025 s2] {'a': '1', 'b': '-1', 'c': '2', 'd': '2024'} 2025 2025-05-21 shift_2 mathematics   9 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: we have, $\left(\frac{\cos\theta + i\sin\theta}{\sin\theta + i\cos\theta}\right)^{2024} + \left(\frac{1+\cos\theta + i\sin\theta}{1-\cos\theta + i\sin\theta}\right)^{2025}$ $= \left\{ \frac{\cos\theta + i\sin\theta}{i(\cos\theta - i\sin\theta)} \right\}^{2024} + \left( \frac{2\cos^2\frac{\theta}{2} + 2i\sin\frac{\theta}{2}\cos\frac{\theta}{2}}{2\sin^2\frac{\theta}{2} + 2i\sin\frac{\theta}{2}\cos\frac{\theta}{2}} \right)^{2025}$ $= \left( \frac{e^{i\theta}}{e^{-i\theta}} \right)^{2024} + \frac{ \left(2\cos\frac{\theta}{2}\right)^{2025} \left(\cos\frac{\theta}{2}+i\sin\frac{\theta}{2}\right)^{2025} }{ \left(2\sin\frac{\theta}{2}\right)^{2025} \left(\sin\frac{\theta}{2}+i\cos\frac{\theta}{2}\right)^{2025} }$ $= (e^{2i\theta})^{2024} + \left(\cot\frac{\theta}{2}\right)^{2025} \frac{ (e^{i\theta/2})^{2025} }{ i^{2025} (e^{-i\theta/2})^{2025} }$ $= (e^{2i\theta})^{2024} + \left(\cot\frac{\theta}{2}\right)^{2025} \frac{1}{i} (e^{i\theta})^{2025}$ $= (\cos 2\theta + i\sin 2\theta)^{2024} - \left(\cot\frac{\theta}{2}\right)^{2025} i(\cos\theta + i\sin\theta)^{2025}$ now, put $\theta = \frac{\pi}{2}$ $= (-1)^{2024} - i(i)^{2025} = 1 - i^2 = 1 + 1 = 2$ © examsnet.com

search_text: if $ax^2 + bx + c < 0 \forall x \in \mathbb{r}$ and the expressions $cx^2 + ax + b$ and $ax^2 + bx + c$ have their extreme values at the same point $x$ , then for the expression $cx^2 + ax + b$ [ap eapcet 21 may 2025 s2] {'a': 'minimum value $= \\frac{4b}{3}$', 'b': 'maximum value $= \\frac{4a}{3}$', 'c': 'minimum value $= \\frac{3a}{4}$', 'd': 'maximum value $= \\frac{3b}{4}$'} 2025 2025-05-21 shift_2 mathematics   11 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: we have, $a x^2 + b x + c < 0$ if $a < 0$ , then $\delta < 0$ $a < 0$ and $b^2 - 4ac < 0$ $\therefore b^2 < 4ac$ and $c x^2 + a x + b$ and $a x^2 + b x + c$ have same extreme value $\because \;\; -\frac{a}{2c} = -\frac{b}{2a} \rightarrow a^2 = bc$ now, the minimum value of $c x^2 + a x + b$ is $-\frac{\delta}{4a} = -\frac{a^2 - 4bc}{4c} = -\frac{bc - 4bc}{4c} = -\left( -\frac{3bc}{4c} \right) = \frac{3b}{4}$ because $b^2 =$ positive and $a < 0 \rightarrow c < 0$ $\therefore \frac{3b}{4}$ is the maximum value of $c x^2 + a x + b$ © examsnet.com

question: If all the letters of the word COMBINATION are arranged in all possible ways to form 11 letter words (with or without meaning), then the number of words among them in which C and N occupy the end positions and no vowel appears exactly in the middle position is [AP EAPCET 21 May 2025 S2]
search_text: if all the letters of the word combination are arranged in all possible ways to form 11 letter words (with or without meaning), then the number of words among them in which c and n occupy the end positions and no vowel appears exactly in the middle position is [ap eapcet 21 may 2025 s2] {'a': '$\\frac{5}{2}(8!)$', 'b': '$4(8!)$', 'c': '$2(8!)$', 'd': '$36(7!)$'} 2025 2025-05-21 shift_2 mathematics   14 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: letters of combination: $c,o,m,b,i,n,a,t,i,o,n$ . vowels: $o,o,i,i,a$ (5 vowels). consonants: $c,m,b,n,n,t$ (6 consonants). the end positions must be occupied by $c$ and $n$ . these can be arranged as $c$ at first and $n$ at last, or $n$ at first and $c$ at last: $2$ ways. the middle position is the $6^{\text{th}}$ position. no vowel should appear exactly in the middle, so the middle must be a consonant. after using $c$ and one $n$ at the ends, the remaining consonants available for the middle are $m,b,n,t$ . so the middle can be filled in $4$ ways. the remaining $8$ positions are filled by the remaining letters: $o,o,i,i,a$ and the other three consonants. the number of arrangements of these remaining letters is $\frac{8!}{2!2!}$ . thus the total number of words is $2 \times 4 \times \frac{8!}{2!2!}$ . $=8 \times \frac{8!}{4}=2(8!)$ . hence the correct option is $2(8!)$ . © examsnet.com

search_text: the coefficient of $x^3$ in the expansion of $\;\frac{x^4+1}{(x^2+1)(x-1)}$ when it is expressed in terms of positive integral powers of $x$ , is [ap eapcet 21 may 2025 s2] {'a': '0', 'b': '1', 'c': '16', 'd': '24'} 2025 2025-05-21 shift_2 mathematics   19 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: given, $\;\frac{x^4+1}{(x^2+1)(x-1)}$ $\;=\;\frac{x^4\left(1+\frac{1}{x^4}\right)}{x^3\left(1+\frac{1}{x^2}\right)\left(1-\frac{1}{x}\right)}$ $\;=x\left(1+\frac{1}{x^4}\right)\left(1+\frac{1}{x^2}\right)^{-1}\left(1-\frac{1}{x}\right)^{-1}$ $\;=x\left(1+\frac{1}{x^4}\right)\left(1-\frac{1}{x^2}\right)\left(1+\frac{1}{x}+\frac{1}{x^2}+\dots\right)$ clearly, there is no terms containing $x^3$ coefficient of $x^3=0$ © examsnet.com

search_text: $\; \frac{1}{\sin 1^{\circ} \sin 2^{\circ}} + \; \frac{1}{\sin 2^{\circ} \sin 3^{\circ}} + \; \frac{1}{\sin 3^{\circ} \sin 4^{\circ}} + \cdots + \; \frac{1}{\sin 89^{\circ} \sin 90^{\circ}} =$ [ap eapcet 21 may 2025 s2] {'a': '$\\; \\frac{\\sin 1^{\\circ}}{\\tan 1^{\\circ}}$', 'b': '$\\; \\frac{1}{\\sin^2 1^{\\circ}}$', 'c': '$\\; \\frac{\\cot 1^{\\circ}}{\\sin 1^{\\circ}}$', 'd': '$\\; \\frac{\\tan 1^{\\circ}}{\\cos 1^{\\circ}}$'} 2025 2025-05-21 shift_2 mathematics   20 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: $\;\; \text{ we have, } \; \sum\limits_{r=1}^{89} \; \frac{1}{\sin r^{\circ} \cdot \sin (r+1)^{\circ}}$ $\; \rightarrow \; \frac{1}{\sin 1^{\circ}} \sum\limits_{r=1}^{89} \; \frac{\sin( (r^{\circ}+1^{\circ}) - r^{\circ} )}{\sin r^{\circ} \cdot \sin (r^{\circ}+1^{\circ})}$ $\; \rightarrow \; \frac{1}{\sin 1^{\circ}} \sum\limits_{r=1}^{89} \; \frac{ \sin (r+1)^{\circ} \cos r^{\circ} }{ \sin r^{\circ} \cdot \sin (r+1)^{\circ} }$ $\; \rightarrow \; \frac{1}{\sin 1^{\circ}} \sum_{r=1^{\circ}}^{89} \cot r^{\circ} - \cot (r+1)^{\circ}$ $\; \rightarrow \; \frac{1}{\sin 1^{\circ}} [ \cot 1^{\circ} - \cot 90^{\circ} ] = \; \frac{\cot 1^{\circ}}{\sin 1^{\circ}}$ © examsnet.com

question: Number of solutions of the equation $\cos\theta + \cos 2\theta - \sqrt{3}(\sin\theta + \sin 2\theta) + 1 = 0$ lying in the interval $(0,2\pi)$ is [AP EAPCET 21 May 2025 S2]
search_text: number of solutions of the equation $\cos\theta + \cos 2\theta - \sqrt{3}(\sin\theta + \sin 2\theta) + 1 = 0$ lying in the interval $(0,2\pi)$ is [ap eapcet 21 may 2025 s2] {'a': '3', 'b': '6', 'c': '5', 'd': '4'} 2025 2025-05-21 shift_2 mathematics   23 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: we have, $\cos\theta + \cos 2\theta - \sqrt{3}(\sin\theta + \sin 2\theta) + 1 = 0$ $\rightarrow \cos\theta + 2\cos^2\theta - \sqrt{3}\sin\theta - 2\sqrt{3}\sin\theta\cos\theta = 0$ $\rightarrow (\cos\theta - \sqrt{3}\sin\theta) + (2\cos^2\theta - 2\sqrt{3}\sin\theta\cos\theta) = 0$ $\rightarrow 1(\cos\theta - \sqrt{3}\sin\theta) + 2\cos\theta(\cos\theta - \sqrt{3}\sin\theta) = 0$ $\rightarrow (\cos\theta - \sqrt{3}\sin\theta)(2\cos\theta + 1) = 0$ $\rightarrow \cos\theta - \sqrt{3}\sin\theta = 0 \text{ or } 2\cos\theta = -1$ $\tan\theta = \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}} \text{ or } \cos\theta = -\frac{1}{2} = \cos\frac{2\pi}{3}$ $\theta = n\pi + \frac{\pi}{6} \text{ or } \theta = 2n\pi + \frac{2\pi}{3}$ $\theta = \frac{\pi}{6}, \frac{7\pi}{6} \text{ or } \theta = \frac{2\pi}{3}, \frac{4\pi}{3}$ $\because$ total number of solution in the interval $(0,2\pi)$ is 4 . © examsnet.com

search_text: if $x$ is a real number, then the number of solutions of $\tan^{-1}(\sqrt{x(x+1)})+\sin^{-1}(\sqrt{x^{2}+x+1}) = \frac{\pi}{2}$ is [ap eapcet 21 may 2025 s2] {'a': '1', 'b': '2', 'c': '3', 'd': '4'} 2025 2025-05-21 shift_2 mathematics   24 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: $\tan^{-1}\sqrt{x(x+1)} + \sin^{-1}(\sqrt{x^{2}+x+1}) = \frac{\pi}{2}$ $\rightarrow \tan^{-1}\sqrt{x(x+1)} = \cos^{-1}(\sqrt{x^{2}+x+1})$ $\rightarrow \tan^{-1}\sqrt{x(x+1)} = \tan^{-1}\sqrt{\frac{-x^{2}-x}{x^{2}+x+1}}$ $\rightarrow \sqrt{x(x+1)} = \sqrt{\frac{-x^{2}-x}{x^{2}+x+1}}$ $\rightarrow x(x+1) = \frac{-x(x+1)}{x^{2}+x+1}$ so, $x(x+1)=0$ or $x^{2}+x+2=0$ (rejected) $\rightarrow x(x+1)=0 \rightarrow x=0,-1$ $\because$ only two real solution. © examsnet.com

search_text: if $y = (ax + b) \cos x$ , then $y_2 + y_1 \sin 2x + y (1 + \sin^2 x) =$ [ap eapcet 21 may 2025 s2] {'a': '$y_2 \\cos^2 x$', 'b': '$y_2 \\sin^2 x$', 'c': '$y_1 \\sin^2 x$', 'd': '$y \\sin^2 x$'} 2025 2025-05-21 shift_2 mathematics   64 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: we have, $y=(a x+b) \cos x$ $\;y \sec x=a x+b$ $\;y \sec x \tan x+\sec x y_1=a$ again, differentiating w.r.t. $x$ , we get $\;\rightarrow y \sec x \sec^2 x+\sec x \tan x \cdot y_1+y \tan x \sec x \tan x+\sec x y_2+y_1 \sec x \tan x=0$ $\;\rightarrow y \sec^3 x+y_1 \sec x \tan x+y \sec x \tan^2 x+y_1 \sec x \tan x+\sec x \cdot y_2=0$ $\;\rightarrow y_2 \sec x+2 y_1 \sec x \tan x+y (\sec^2 x+\tan^2 x) \sec x=0$ on dividing both sides by $\sec^3 x$ , we get $y_2 \cos^2 x+2 y_1 \sin x \cdot \cos x+y (1+\sin^2 x)=0$ $\;y_2 - y_1 \sin^2 x + y_1 \sin 2x + y (1 + \sin^2 x) = 0$ $\therefore y_2 + y_1 \sin 2x + y(1+\sin^2 x) = y_2 \sin^2 x$ © examsnet.com

search_text: if the normal drawn at the point $p$ on the curve $y=x \log x$ is parallel to the line $2 x-2 y=3$ , then $p=$ [ap eapcet 21 may 2025 s2] {'a': '$(e, e)$', 'b': '$\\left( \\frac{1}{e}, \\frac{-1}{e} \\right)$', 'c': '$\\left( \\frac{1}{e^{2}}, \\frac{-2}{e^{2}} \\right)$', 'd': '$(e^3, 3 e^3)$'} 2025 2025-05-21 shift_2 mathematics   65 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: let $p(h, k)$ $\;y=x \log x$ $\rightarrow \;\; \frac{dy}{dx}=1+\log x$ $\therefore \; \text{slope of normal} \; = -\frac{1}{1+\log h}$ and slope of the given line $2 x-2 y=3$ is 1 $\rightarrow \; -\frac{1}{1+\log h}=1$ $\rightarrow \; 1+\ln h=-1$ $\rightarrow \ln h=-2$ $h=e^{-2}$ $k=h \ln h$ $k=e^{-2} \ln e^{-2}=e^{-2}(-2)=-\frac{2}{e^{2}}$ $\therefore \; \text{the point} \; p \; \text{is} \; \left( \frac{1}{e^{2}}, -\frac{2}{e^{2}} \right)$ © examsnet.com

question: If the function $y = \sin x (1+\cos x)$ is defined in the interval $[-\pi, \pi]$ , then $y$ is strictly increasing in the interval [AP EAPCET 21 May 2025 S2]
search_text: if the function $y = \sin x (1+\cos x)$ is defined in the interval $[-\pi, \pi]$ , then $y$ is strictly increasing in the interval [ap eapcet 21 may 2025 s2] {'a': '$\\left(-\\pi, -\\frac{\\pi}{3}\\right) \\cup \\left(\\frac{\\pi}{3}, \\pi\\right)$', 'b': '$\\left(\\frac{\\pi}{6}, \\frac{\\pi}{2}\\right)$', 'c': '$\\left(-\\frac{\\pi}{3}, \\frac{\\pi}{3}\\right)$', 'd': '$\\left(-\\pi, -\\frac{\\pi}{6}\\right) \\cup \\left(\\frac{\\pi}{6}, \\pi\\right)$'} 2025 2025-05-21 shift_2 mathematics   67 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: we have, $y = \sin x (1+\cos x)$ $\frac{dy}{dx} = \sin x (-\sin x) + (1+\cos x) \cos x$ $= -\sin^2 x + \cos x + \cos^2 x$ $= -1 + \cos^2 x + \cos x + \cos^2 x$ $= 2\cos^2 x + \cos x - 1$ $\rightarrow \frac{dy}{dx} = (\cos x+1)(2\cos x-1)$ given $y$ is strictly increasing $\therefore \frac{dy}{dx} = (\cos x+1)(2\cos x-1) > 0$ $\rightarrow \cos x < -1 \text{ or } \cos x > \frac{1}{2}$ $\rightarrow x \in \left(-\frac{\pi}{3}, \frac{\pi}{3}\right) \text{ in the interval } (-\pi, \pi)$ $\therefore x \in \left(-\frac{\pi}{3}, \frac{\pi}{3}\right)$ © examsnet.com

question: If the velocity of a particle moving on a straight line is proportional to the cube root of its displacement, then its acceleration is [AP EAPCET 21 May 2025 S2]
search_text: if the velocity of a particle moving on a straight line is proportional to the cube root of its displacement, then its acceleration is [ap eapcet 21 may 2025 s2] {'a': 'constant', 'b': 'inversely proportional to its velocity', 'c': 'proportional to its velocity', 'd': 'proportional to its displacement'} 2025 2025-05-21 shift_2 mathematics   68 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: given: velocity $v$ is proportional to the cube root of the displacement $x$ . $v \propto x^{1/3}$ this means we can write: $v = k x^{1/3}$ where $k$ is a constant of proportionality. we are asked to find how acceleration $a$ depends on other quantities. we know that: $a = \frac{dv}{dt} = \frac{dv}{dx} \cdot \frac{dx}{dt} = v \; \frac{dv}{dx}$ step 1: find $\frac{dv}{dx}$ from $v = k x^{1/3}$ , $\frac{dv}{dx} = k \cdot \frac{1}{3} x^{-2/3} = \frac{k}{3} x^{-2/3}$ step 2: substitute in acceleration formula: $a = v \frac{dv}{dx} = (k x^{1/3}) \cdot \left( \frac{k}{3} x^{-2/3} \right)$ simplify: $a = \frac{k^2}{3} x^{1/3-2/3} = \frac{k^2}{3} x^{-1/3}$ step 3: express in terms of velocity if desired since $v = k x^{1/3} \rightarrow x^{1/3} = \frac{v}{k}$ , $x^{-1/3} = \frac{k}{v}$ so: $a = \frac{k^2}{3} \cdot \frac{k}{v} = \frac{k^3}{3v}$ therefore: $a \propto \frac{1}{v}$ final answer: option b: inversely proportional to its velocity © examsnet.com

search_text: if $\int e^{\sin x}(1+\sec x\tan x) dx=e^{\sin x} f(x)+c$ , then in $0 \le x \le 2 \pi$ , the number of solutions of $f(x)=1$ is [ap eapcet 21 may 2025 s2] {'a': '4', 'b': '0', 'c': '2', 'd': '3'} 2025 2025-05-21 shift_2 mathematics   69 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: $\, \text{ given }\, \int e^{\sin x}(1+\sec x\tan x) dx$ $= e^{\sin x} f(x)+c$ $\int e^{\sin x} \left(\, \frac{1}{\cos x}+\, \frac{\sin x}{\cos^3 x}\,\right) \cos x dx$ put $\sin x = t$ $\, \cos x \, dx = dt$ $\, \cos x = \sqrt{1-t^2}$ $\, \int e^t \left[ \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-t^2}} + \frac{t}{(1-t^2)^{3/2}} \right] \, dt$ [using result $\int e^x \left[ f(x) + f'(x) \right] \, dx$ $= e^x f(x)+c]$ $\int e^t \left[ \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-t^2}} + \left( \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-t^2}} \right)^1 \right] \, dt = e^t \cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-t^2}}$ $= e^{\sin x} \cdot \frac{1}{\cos x} = e^{\sin x} \cdot \sec x + c$ comparing with $e^{\sin x} f(x)+c$ $\therefore \, \, f(x) \, = \, \sec x = 1$ $x \, = 0, 2 \pi$ $\therefore$ number of solution is 2 . © examsnet.com

search_text: if $\int\; \frac{dx}{(x-1)^{\frac{3}{2}}(x-3)^{\frac{1}{2}}} = \sqrt{f(x)} + c$ then $f(-1)-f(0)=$ [ap eapcet 21 may 2025 s2] {'a': '-3', 'b': '-4', 'c': '-2', 'd': '-1'} 2025 2025-05-21 shift_2 mathematics   70 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: $\; \int\; \frac{dx}{(x-1)^{\frac{3}{2}}(x-3)^{\frac{1}{2}}}$ $\text{ let }\; i=\int \frac{dx}{(x-1)^2 \left(\frac{x-3}{x-1}\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}}$ $\text{ put }\; \frac{x-3}{x-1}=t^2$ $\; \frac{x-1-x+3}{(x-1)^2} dx = 2 t dt$ $\; \frac{1}{(x-1)^2} dx = t dt$ $i = \int \frac{t dt}{t} = \int dt = t = \sqrt{\frac{x-3}{x-1}} + c$ $\; \because f(x) = \frac{x-3}{x-1}$ $\; f(-1)-f(0) = \frac{-4}{-2} - 3 = 2-3 = -1$ © examsnet.com

search_text: $\int \frac{x}{(1-x^2)\sqrt{2-x^2}} \, dx =$ [ap eapcet 21 may 2025 s2] {'a': '$\\log \\left| \\frac{\\sqrt{2-x^2}+1}{\\sqrt{2-x^2}-1} \\right| + c$', 'b': '$\\frac{1}{2} \\log \\left| \\frac{\\sqrt{2-x^2}}{1-x^2} \\right| + c$', 'c': '$\\frac{1}{2} \\log \\left| \\frac{1+\\sqrt{2-x^2}}{1-\\sqrt{2-x^2}} \\right| + c$', 'd': '$\\log \\left| \\frac{1 - x^2}{\\sqrt{2 - x^2}} \\right| + c$'} 2025 2025-05-21 shift_2 mathematics   71 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: $\text{ let } i = \int \frac{x}{(1-x^2)\sqrt{2-x^2}} \, dx$ put $2 - x^2 = t^2$ $\therefore \; -x \, dx = t \, dt \; \text{ and } \; x^2 = 2 - t^2$ $\rightarrow i = \int \frac{-t \, dt}{(t^2-1) t}$ $\rightarrow i = \int \frac{dt}{1-t^2} = \frac{1}{2} \ln \left( \frac{1+t}{1-t} \right)$ $= \frac{1}{2} \ln \left( \frac{1+\sqrt{2-x^2}}{1-\sqrt{2-x^2}} \right) + c$ © examsnet.com

question: If $\int x^2 \cos^2 x dx = \;\frac{1}{6} f(x) + g(x) \sin 2x + h(x) \cos 2x + c$ , then $f(1) + g(2) + h\left( \;\frac{1}{2} \right) =$ [AP EAPCET 21 May 2025 S2]
search_text: if $\int x^2 \cos^2 x dx = \;\frac{1}{6} f(x) + g(x) \sin 2x + h(x) \cos 2x + c$ , then $f(1) + g(2) + h\left( \;\frac{1}{2} \right) =$ [ap eapcet 21 may 2025 s2] {'a': '0', 'b': '2', 'c': '1', 'd': '-1'} 2025 2025-05-21 shift_2 mathematics   73 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: given, $\int x^2 \cos^2 x dx = \;\frac{1}{6} f(x) + g(x) \sin 2x + h(x) \cos 2x + c$ lhs $i\; = \int x^2 \cos^2 x dx = \int x^2 \left( \frac{1+\cos 2x}{2} \right) dx$ $i\; = \;\frac{1}{2} \int (x^2 + x^2 \cos 2x) dx$ $\; = \;\frac{1}{2} \int x^2 dx + \;\frac{1}{2} \int x^2 \cos 2x dx$ $\; = \;\frac{1}{2} \cdot \;\frac{x^3}{3} + \;\frac{1}{2} i_1$ where $i_1 = \int x^2 \cos^2 x dx$ $\;i_1 = \;\frac{x^2}{2} \sin 2x + \;\frac{1}{2} x \cos 2x - \;\frac{1}{4} \sin 2x + c$ $\; \rightarrow i = \;\frac{x^3}{6} + \;\frac{1}{2} \left\{ \sin 2x \left( \;\frac{x^2}{2} - \;\frac{1}{4} \right) + \;\frac{x}{2} \cos 2x \right\}$ $\; = \;\frac{x^3}{6} + \left( \;\frac{x^2}{4} - \;\frac{1}{8} \right) \sin 2x + \;\frac{x}{4} \cos 2x$ $\; = \;\frac{1}{6} f(x) + g(x) \sin 2x + h(x) \cos 2x + c$ $\; \because f(x)=x^3, g(x)=\;\frac{x^2}{4} - \;\frac{1}{8} \; \text{ and } \; h(x)=\;\frac{x}{4}$ $\; \rightarrow f(1)=1, g(2)=\;\frac{7}{8} h\left( \;\frac{1}{2} \right) = \;\frac{1}{8}$ $\; \therefore f(1)+g(2)+h\left( \;\frac{1}{2} \right) = 1+\;\frac{7}{8}+\;\frac{1}{8}=2$ © examsnet.com

search_text: $\int\limits_{0}^{\pi / 2} \log \left| \tan x+\cot x \right| dx =$ [ap eapcet 21 may 2025 s2] {'a': '$\\pi \\log 2$', 'b': '$-\\pi \\log 2$', 'c': '$\\frac{\\pi}{2} \\log 2$', 'd': '$2 \\pi \\log 2$'} 2025 2025-05-21 shift_2 mathematics   74 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: $\;\int\limits_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{2}} \ln (\tan x+\cot x) dx = \int\limits_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{2}} \ln \left( \frac{1}{\sin x \cos x} \right) dx$ $\;=\int\limits_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{2}} (\ln 2 - \ln \sin 2x) dx$ $\;=\ln 2 \int\limits_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{2}} dx - \int\limits_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{2}} \ln \sin 2x dx$ $\;\; \text{ put } 2x=t, dx = \frac{dt}{2}$ $\;=\frac{\pi}{2} \ln 2 - \frac{1}{2} \int\limits_{0}^{\pi} \ln \sin t dt$ $\;=\frac{\pi}{2} \ln 2 - \int\limits_{0}^{\pi / 2} \ln \sin t dt$ $\;=\frac{\pi}{2} \ln 2 - \left( -\frac{\pi}{2} \ln 2 \right)$ $\; \left[ \because \int\limits_{0}^{\pi / 2} \ln \sin x = -\frac{\pi}{2} \ln 2 \right]$ $\;= \pi \ln 2$ © examsnet.com

search_text: $\int\limits_{1/2}^{1/\sqrt{2}} \;\frac{1}{(x+\sqrt{1-x^2})(1-x^2)} dx=$ [ap eapcet 21 may 2025 s2] {'a': '$\\log (\\sqrt{3}+1)$', 'b': '$\\log (\\sqrt{3}-1)$', 'c': '$\\log (3+\\sqrt{3})$', 'd': '$\\log (3-\\sqrt{3})$'} 2025 2025-05-21 shift_2 mathematics   76 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: $\;i=\int\limits_{1/2}^{1/\sqrt{2}} \;\frac{1}{(x+\sqrt{1-x^2})(1-x^2)} dx$ $\;i=\int\limits_{\pi/6}^{\pi/4} \frac{\cos\theta\,d\theta}{(\sin\theta+\cos\theta)\cos^2\theta}$ put $x=\sin\theta \rightarrow dx=\cos\theta\,d\theta$ $=\int\limits_{\pi/6}^{\pi/4} \frac{d\theta}{\sin\theta\cos\theta+\cos^2\theta}$ dividing $n^t$ and $d^r$ by $\cos^2\theta$ , we get $=\int\limits_{\pi/6}^{\pi/4} \frac{\sec^2\theta}{\tan\theta+1} d\theta$ put $\tan\theta+1=t,\ \sec^2\theta\,d\theta=dt$ $\;=\int_{1/\sqrt{3}+1}^{2} \frac{dt}{t}=[\ln t]_{1+1/\sqrt{3}}^{2}$ $\;=\ln 2-\ln (1+1/\sqrt{3})$ $\;=\ln 2-\ln \left(\frac{\sqrt{3}+1}{\sqrt{3}}\right)=\ln \left(\frac{2\sqrt{3}}{\sqrt{3}+1}\right)$ $\;=\ln \left(\frac{2\sqrt{3}(\sqrt{3}-1)}{3-1}\right)=\ln (3-\sqrt{3})$ © examsnet.com

If the collision is elastic and after the collision the first sphere continues to move in its initial direction with a velocity of $\frac{7}{9}$ times its initial velocity, then the radius of the second sphere is [AP EAPCET 21 May 2025 S2]
search_text: a steel sphere of radius 1.2 cm collides a second steel sphere at rest. if the collision is elastic and after the collision the first sphere continues to move in its initial direction with a velocity of $\frac{7}{9}$ times its initial velocity, then the radius of the second sphere is [ap eapcet 21 may 2025 s2] {'a': '1.8 cm', 'b': '2.4 cm', 'c': '1.2 cm', 'd': '0.6 cm'} 2025 2025-05-21 shift_2 physics   88 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: given: the final velocity of the first sphere, $v_1 = \frac{7}{9} u_1$ $u_2 = 0$ (the second sphere is at rest) the mass of a sphere is proportional to the cube of its radius: $m \propto r^3$ let $m_1$ and $m_2$ be the masses, and $r_1$ and $r_2$ be the radii of the first and second spheres. step 1: use the formula for an elastic collision after the collision, the velocity of the first sphere is: $v_1 = \frac{(m_1 - m_2) u_1 + 2 m_2 u_2}{m_1 + m_2}$ step 2: substitute $u_2 = 0$ $v_1 = \frac{(m_1 - m_2) u_1}{m_1 + m_2}$ we know $v_1 = \frac{7}{9} u_1$ : $\frac{7}{9} u_1 = \frac{(m_1 - m_2) u_1}{m_1 + m_2}$ divide both sides by $u_1$ (since $u_1 \neq 0$ ): $\frac{7}{9} = \frac{m_1 - m_2}{m_1 + m_2}$ step 3: solve for $m_1$ in terms of $m_2$ multiply both sides by ( $m_1 + m_2$ ): $7 (m_1 + m_2) = 9 (m_1 - m_2)$ $7 m_1 + 7 m_2 = 9 m_1 - 9 m_2$ $7 m_2 + 9 m_2 = 9 m_1 - 7 m_1$ $16 m_2 = 2 m_1$ $m_1 = 8 m_2$ step 4: relate masses to radii since mass of a sphere, $m \propto r^3$ : $\frac{m_1}{m_2} = \left( \frac{r_1}{r_2} \right)^3$ $8 = \left( \frac{r_1}{r_2} \right)^3$ step 5: solve for $r_2$ take the cube root of both sides: $\frac{r_1}{r_2} = 2$ $r_1 = 2 r_2$ $r_2 = \frac{r_1}{2}$ plug in $r_1 = 1.2 \text{ cm}$ : $r_2 = \frac{1.2}{2} = 0.6 \text{ cm}$ © examsnet.com

search_text: if the angular velocity of a planet about its axis is halved, the distance of the stationary satellite of this planet from the centre of the planet becomes $2^{n}$ times the initial distance. then the value of ' $n$ ' is [ap eapcet 21 may 2025 s2] {'a': '$\\frac{2}{3}$', 'b': '$\\frac{3}{2}$', 'c': '$\\frac{1}{3}$', 'd': '$\\frac{4}{3}$'} 2025 2025-05-21 shift_2 physics   93 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: $\;t^2 \propto r^3$ $\; \rightarrow \;\; \left(\frac{2\pi}{\omega}\right)^2 \propto r^3$ $\; \rightarrow \;\; \frac{\omega^2}{4\pi^2} \propto \frac{1}{r^3}$ $\; \rightarrow \;\; \omega^2 \propto \frac{1}{r^3}$ $\; \rightarrow \;\; \left(\frac{\omega_2}{\omega_1}\right)^2 = \left(\frac{r_1}{r_2}\right)^3$ $\; \rightarrow \;\; \left(\frac{\omega_{1/2}}{\omega_1}\right)^2 = \left(\frac{r_1}{2^n r_1}\right)^3$ $\; \rightarrow \;\; \left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^2 = \left(\frac{1}{2^n}\right)^3$ $\; \rightarrow \;\; \frac{1}{2^2} = \frac{1}{2^{3n}}$ $\; \rightarrow \;\; 2^2 = 2^{3n} \rightarrow 2 = 3n$ $\;n = \frac{2}{3}$ © examsnet.com

search_text: when a wire of length 'l' clamped at one end is pulled by a force 'f' from the other end, its length increases by ' $l$ '. if the radius of the wire and the applied force were halved, then the increase in its length is [ap eapcet 21 may 2025 s2] {'a': '3l', 'b': '4l', 'c': '1.5l', 'd': '2l'} 2025 2025-05-21 shift_2 physics   94 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: we know that, $\; \;\;\;\;  y=\;\frac{f l}{\pi r^2 \delta l}$ $\;\rightarrow \delta l=\;\frac{f l}{\pi r^2 y}$ $\;\rightarrow \delta l \propto \;\frac{f l}{r^2}$ $\;\rightarrow \;\; \;\frac{\delta l_2}{\delta l_1} = \frac{f_2}{f_1} \times \frac{l_2}{l_1} \times \left(\;\frac{r_1}{r_2}\right)^2$ $\;= \left(\;\frac{f_{1/2}}{f_1}\right) \times \left(\;\frac{l_1}{l}\right) \left(\;\frac{r_1}{r_{1/2}}\right)^2$ $\;\rightarrow \;\; \frac{\delta l_2}{\delta l_1}\;= \frac{1}{2} \times 1 \times 2^2$ $\delta l_2\;=2\delta l_1$ $\;=2l \;\; [ \because \delta l_1 = l ]$ © examsnet.com

question: A liquid drop of diameter D splits into 3375 small identical drops. If S is the surface tension of the liquid, then the change in the surface energy in the process is [AP EAPCET 21 May 2025 S2]
search_text: a liquid drop of diameter d splits into 3375 small identical drops. if s is the surface tension of the liquid, then the change in the surface energy in the process is [ap eapcet 21 may 2025 s2] {'a': '$44 d^2 s$', 'b': '$44 \\pi d^2 s$', 'c': '$56 d^2 s$', 'd': '$56 \\pi d^2 s$'} 2025 2025-05-21 shift_2 physics   95 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: let $d$ be the diameter of each of the 3375 small identical droplets. since the volume of the liquid is conserved, $\frac{4}{3}\pi\left(\frac{d}{2}\right)^3 = 3375 \times \frac{4}{3}\pi\left(\frac{d}{2}\right)^3$ $d^3 = 3375\,d^3 = (15d)^3$ $\therefore d = 15d$ initial surface area of the big drop $= 4\pi\left(\frac{d}{2}\right)^2 = \pi d^2$ total surface area of all small drops $= 3375 \times 4\pi\left(\frac{d}{2}\right)^2 = 3375\,\pi d^2$ $= 3375\,\pi\left(\frac{d}{15}\right)^2 = \frac{3375}{225}\,\pi d^2 = 15\pi d^2$ increase in surface area $= \delta a = 15\pi d^2 - \pi d^2 = 14\pi d^2$ change in surface energy $= \delta w = s \times \delta a = 14\pi d^2 s$ taking $\pi = \frac{22}{7}$ , $\delta w = 14 \times \frac{22}{7}d^2 s = 44\,d^2 s$ since the surface area increases, the surface energy increases by $44\,d^2 s$ . hence the correct option is $44\,d^2 s$ . © examsnet.com

search_text: when a sphere is taken to the bottom of a sea of depth 1 km , it contracts in volume by $0.01\%$ , then the bulk modulus of the material of the sphere is (acceleration due to gravity $=10 \text{ m} \text{ s}^{-2}$ ) [ap eapcet 21 may 2025 s2] {'a': '$10 \\times 10^6 \\text{ n m}^{-2}$', 'b': '$1.2 \\times 10^{10} \\text{ n m}^{-2}$', 'c': '$10 \\times 10^{10} \\text{ n m}^{-2}$', 'd': '$10 \\times 10^{11} \\text{ n m}^{-2}$'} 2025 2025-05-21 shift_2 physics   96 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: depth of sea, $h=1 \text{ km}=1000 \text{ m}$ relative decrease in volume, $\; \frac{\delta v}{v}=0.01\%=0.0001=10^{-4}$ acceleration due to gravity, $g=10 \text{ m/s}^2$ density of sea water, $\rho \approx 10^3 \text{ kg/m}^3$ step 1. calculate the pressure at that depth $p = \rho g h = 1000 \times 10 \times 1000 = 10^7 \text{ n/m}^2$ step 2. use the definition of bulk modulus $k$ $k = -\; \frac{\delta p}{\frac{\delta v}{v}}$ here, $\delta p = p = 10^7 \text{ n/m}^2$ , and $\; \frac{\delta v}{v} = -10^{-4}$ $k = \; \frac{10^7}{10^{-4}} = 10^{11} \text{ n/m}^2$ final answer: $k = 10^{11} \text{ n/m}^2$ correct option: d) $10 \times 10^{10} \text{ n/m}^2$ © examsnet.com

search_text: if a gas of volume 400 cc at an initial pressure $p$ is suddenly compressed to 100 cc , then its final pressure is (the ratio of the specific heat capacities of the gas at constant pressure and constant volume is 1.5 ) [ap eapcet 21 may 2025 s2] {'a': '$\\; \\frac{p}{32}$', 'b': '8 p', 'c': '32p', 'd': '16p'} 2025 2025-05-21 shift_2 physics   97 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: given: initial volume $v_1=400\ \text{cc}$ final volume $v_2=100\ \text{cc}$ initial pressure $p_1=p$ the process is sudden (adiabatic) thus, for an adiabatic process: $p_1 v_1^\gamma = p_2 v_2^\gamma$ given: $\gamma = 1.5$ step 1: write the equation for $p_2$ $p_2 = p_1 \left( \frac{v_1}{v_2} \right)^\gamma$ step 2: substitute the values $p_2 = p \left( \frac{400}{100} \right)^{1.5} = p(4)^{1.5}$ step 3: simplify $(4)^{1.5} = 4^1 \times 4^{0.5} = 4 \times 2 = 8$ $p_2 = 8p$ final answer: $p_2 = 8p$ correct option: (b) $8p$ © examsnet.com

question: A Carnot engine having efficiency $60\%$ receives heat from a source at a temperature 600 K . For the same sink temperature, to increase its efficiency to $80\%$ , the temperature of the source is [AP EAPCET 21 May 2025 S2]
search_text: a carnot engine having efficiency $60\%$ receives heat from a source at a temperature 600 k . for the same sink temperature, to increase its efficiency to $80\%$ , the temperature of the source is [ap eapcet 21 may 2025 s2] {'a': '$300\\,\\mathrm{k}$', 'b': '$900\\,\\mathrm{k}$', 'c': '$1200\\,\\mathrm{k}$', 'd': '$720\\,\\mathrm{k}$'} 2025 2025-05-21 shift_2 physics   98 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: efficiency of carnot's engine is $\eta_1\;=1-\;\frac{t_2}{t_1}$ $0.6\;=1-\;\frac{t_2}{600}$ $\rightarrow \;\; t_2\;=240\,\mathrm{k}$ again, $\eta_2=80\%=0.8$ $\; \therefore \;\; \eta_2=1-\;\frac{t_2^{'}}{t_1^{'}}$ $\; \;\; 0.8=1-\;\frac{240}{t_1^{'}} \;\; [\because t_2^{'}=t_2=240\,\mathrm{k}]$ $\;\rightarrow t_1^{'}=1200\,\mathrm{k}$ © examsnet.com

search_text: the average translational kinetic energy of the oxygen molecules at a temperature of $127^{\circ} \mathrm{c}$ is $(.$ boltzmann constant $=1.38 \times 10^{-23} \mathrm{j} \mathrm{k}^{-1})$ [ap eapcet 21 may 2025 s2] {'a': '$4.07 \\times 10^{-21} \\mathrm{j}$', 'b': '$2.07 \\times 10^{-21} \\mathrm{j}$', 'c': '$8.28 \\times 10^{-21} \\mathrm{j}$', 'd': '$8.00 \\times 10^{-21} \\mathrm{j}$'} 2025 2025-05-21 shift_2 physics   100 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: given: temperature $t=127^{\circ} \mathrm{c}$ boltzmann constant $k=1.38 \times 10^{-23} \text{j/k}$ we know that: average translational kinetic energy per molecule $=\;\frac{3}{2} k t$ step 1: convert temperature to kelvins $t=127+273=400 \mathrm{k}$ step 2: substitute the values $e=\;\frac{3}{2} k t=\;\frac{3}{2} (1.38 \times 10^{-23}) (400)$ step 3: simplify $\;e=1.5 \times 1.38 \times 400 \times 10^{-23}$ $\;e=2.07 \times 400 \times 10^{-23}$ $\;e=8.28 \times 10^{-21} \mathrm{j}$ final answer: $8.28 \times 10^{-21} \mathrm{j}$ © examsnet.com

question: The speed of a stationary wave represented by the equation $y=0.7\;\sin\left(\;\frac{7\pi}{4} x\right)\,\cos(350\pi t)$ is (In the given equation $x$ and $y$ are in metre and $t$ is in second) [AP EAPCET 21 May 2025 S2]
search_text: the speed of a stationary wave represented by the equation $y=0.7\;\sin\left(\;\frac{7\pi}{4} x\right)\,\cos(350\pi t)$ is (in the given equation $x$ and $y$ are in metre and $t$ is in second) [ap eapcet 21 may 2025 s2] {'a': '$100\\ \\text{m}\\ \\text{s}^{-1}$', 'b': '$150\\ \\text{m}\\ \\text{s}^{-1}$', 'c': '$160\\ \\text{m}\\ \\text{s}^{-1}$', 'd': '$200\\ \\text{m}\\ \\text{s}^{-1}$'} 2025 2025-05-21 shift_2 physics   101 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: $y=0.7\;\sin\left(\;\frac{7\pi}{4} x\right)\,\cos(350\pi t)$ comparing with equation of stationary wave, $y=2a\;\sin(k x)\cos\omega t$ we get, $k=\frac{7\pi}{4},\ \omega=350\pi$ $\therefore$ speed of stationary wave, $v=\frac{\omega}{k}=\frac{350\pi}{\frac{7\pi}{4}}=200\ \text{m/s}$ © examsnet.com

question: Two thin convex lenses are kept in contact coaxially. If the focal length of the combination of the lenses is 4 cm and sum of the focal lengths of the two lenses is 18 cm , then the focal length of the lens of low power is [AP EAPCET 21 May 2025 S2]
search_text: two thin convex lenses are kept in contact coaxially. if the focal length of the combination of the lenses is 4 cm and sum of the focal lengths of the two lenses is 18 cm , then the focal length of the lens of low power is [ap eapcet 21 may 2025 s2] {'a': '$8\\text{ cm}$', 'b': '$10\\text{ cm}$', 'c': '$6\\text{ cm}$', 'd': '$12\\text{ cm}$'} 2025 2025-05-21 shift_2 physics   102 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: $f_1+f_2=18\text{ cm}$ $f=4\text{ cm}$ $\therefore \frac{1}{f} = \frac{1}{f_1} + \frac{1}{f_2}$ $\rightarrow \frac{1}{4} = \frac{f_2+f_1}{f_1 f_2}$ $\rightarrow \frac{1}{4} = \frac{18}{f_1 f_2}$ $\rightarrow f_1 f_2 = 72$ $\rightarrow f_1 (18-f_1) = 72$ $\rightarrow 18 f_1 - f_1^2 = 72$ $\rightarrow f_1^2 - 18 f_1 + 72 = 0$ $\rightarrow f_1^2 - 12 f_1 - 6 f' + 72 = 0$ $\rightarrow (f_1-12)(f_1-6) = 0$ $\therefore f_1=6\text{ cm},\ 12\text{ cm}$ when, $f_1=6\text{ cm}$ , then, $f_2=18-6=12\text{ cm}$ when $f_1=12\text{ cm}$ , then $f_2=18-12=6\text{ cm}$ since, $p \propto \frac{1}{f}$ $\therefore$ focal length of low power $=12\text{ cm}$ © examsnet.com

search_text: for an observer on the earth, if a spectral line of wavelength $6600\text{å}$ emitted by a star is found to be red shifted by $22\text{å}$ , then the star is [ap eapcet 21 may 2025 s2] {'a': 'receding away from earth with a speed of $9 \\times 10^5 \\text{m}\\,\\text{s}^{-1}$', 'b': 'receding away from earth with a speed of $10 \\times 10^5 \\text{m}\\,\\text{s}^{-1}$', 'c': 'moving towards earth with a speed of $9 \\times 10^5 \\text{m}\\,\\text{s}^{-1}$', 'd': 'moving towards earth with a speed of $10 \\times 10^5 \\text{m}\\,\\text{s}^{-1}$'} 2025 2025-05-21 shift_2 physics   103 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: given data wavelength emitted by the star (rest wavelength): $\lambda_0=6600\text{å}$ observed redshift (increase in wavelength): $\delta \lambda=22\text{å}$ the redshift implies that the star is moving away from the earth. formula (for non-relativistic doppler shift) for light at non-relativistic speeds: $\;\frac{\delta \lambda}{\lambda_0}=\;\frac{v}{c}$ where $v=$ radial speed of the source relative to the observer, $c=3 \times 10^8 \text{m s}^{-1}.$ substituting values $\;\frac{22}{6600}=\;\frac{v}{3 \times 10^8}$ $\;v=3 \times 10^8 \times \;\frac{22}{6600}$ $\;v=3 \times 10^8 \times 3.33 \times 10^{-3}$ $\;v=1.0 \times 10^6 \text{m s}^{-1}$ $\;v=10^6 \text{m s}^{-1}=10 \times 10^5 \text{m s}^{-1}$ direction since the wavelength is red shifted, the star is receding from earth. answer: option b receding away from earth with a speed of $10 \times 10^5 \text{m/s}$ © examsnet.com

question: A particle of mass $8\,\mathrm{\mu g}$ in motion collides with another stationary particle of mass $4\,\mathrm{\mu g}$ . If the collision is perfectly elastic and one dimensional, the ratio of their de Broglie wavelengths after collision is [AP EAPCET 21 May 2025 S2]
search_text: a particle of mass $8\,\mathrm{\mu g}$ in motion collides with another stationary particle of mass $4\,\mathrm{\mu g}$ . if the collision is perfectly elastic and one dimensional, the ratio of their de broglie wavelengths after collision is [ap eapcet 21 may 2025 s2] {'a': '$4: 1$', 'b': '$3: 1$', 'c': '$1: 1$', 'd': '$2: 1$'} 2025 2025-05-21 shift_2 physics   115 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: step 1: find the final velocities after the collision the first particle has mass $8\,\mathrm{\mu g}$ and moves with speed $u_1$ . the second particle has mass $4\,\mathrm{\mu g}$ and is at rest, so $u_2=0$ . the formula for the final speed of the first particle after an elastic, one-dimensional collision is: $v_1=\frac{(m_1-m_2) u_1+2 m_2 u_2}{m_1+m_2}$ plug in the numbers: $v_1=\frac{(8-4) u_1+2 \times 4 \times 0}{8+4}=\frac{4 u_1}{12}=\frac{u_1}{3}$ the formula for the final speed of the second particle is: $v_2=\frac{2 m_1 u_1+(m_2-m_1) u_2}{m_1+m_2}$ plug in the numbers: $v_2=\frac{2 \times 8 u_1+(4-8) \times 0}{8+4}=\frac{16 u_1}{12}=\frac{4}{3} u_1$ step 2: find the de-broglie wavelength for each particle the de-broglie wavelength formula is: $\lambda=\frac{h}{m v}$ where $h$ is planck's constant, $m$ is mass, and $v$ is velocity. to compare their wavelengths, find the ratio: $\frac{\lambda_2}{\lambda_1}=\frac{m_1 v_1}{m_2 v_2}$ plug in the values found earlier: $\frac{\lambda_2}{\lambda_1}=\frac{8 \times \frac{u_1}{3}}{4 \times \frac{4}{3} u_1}$ simplify the expression: $=\frac{8 \times \frac{u_1}{3}}{4 \times \frac{4 u_1}{3}}=\frac{\frac{8 u_1}{3}}{\frac{16 u_1}{3}}=\frac{8 u_1}{16 u_1}=\frac{1}{2}$ so, $\frac{\lambda_1}{\lambda_2}=2$ which means the ratio of their wavelengths after the collision is $2: 1$ © examsnet.com

search_text: the difference between the frequencies of the first and second lyman lines of hydrogen atom is ( r - rydberg constant and c - speed of light in vacuum) [ap eapcet 21 may 2025 s2] {'a': '$\\;\\frac{9 rc}{28}$', 'b': '$\\;\\frac{7 rc}{12}$', 'c': '$\\;\\frac{3 rc}{8}$', 'd': '$\\;\\frac{5 rc}{36}$'} 2025 2025-05-21 shift_2 physics   116 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: frequency of spectral line of hydrogen atom $v=r c \;\left(\frac{1}{n_1^2}-\frac{1}{n_2^2}\right)$ for the first line of lyman series $\;n_1=1 \;\text{ and }\; n_2=2$ $\;\therefore v_1=r c \left(\frac{1}{1^2}-\frac{1}{2^2}\right) =\frac{3 r c}{4}$ for the second line of lyman series, $\;n_1=1 \;\text{ and }\; n_2=3$ $\;v_2=r c \left(\frac{1}{1^2}-\frac{1}{3^2}\right) =\frac{8}{9} r c$ thus, $v_2-v_1=\frac{8}{9} r c-\frac{3}{4} r c=\frac{5}{36} r c$ © examsnet.com

search_text: 209 g of an element reacts with chlorine to form 315.5 g of its chloride. what is the weight (in g ) of oxygen that reacts with 418 g of same element ? $(c\ \ell=35.5\ \mathrm{u};\ o=16\ \mathrm{u})$ [ap eapcet 21 may 2025 s2] {'a': '24', 'b': '48', 'c': '96', 'd': '36'} 2025 2025-05-21 shift_2 chemistry   128 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: mass of chlorine is the difference between the mass of the chloride and mass of the elements. $315.5-209=106.59$ equivalent weight of element $=\frac{\text{mass of element}}{\text{mass of chlorine}} \times \text{atomic weight}$ $\text{ of chlorine }$ $=\frac{209\ \mathrm{g}}{106.5\ \mathrm{g}} \times 35.5\ \mathrm{u} \approx 69.66\ \mathrm{u}$ $\therefore$ mass of oxygen $=\frac{\text{mass of element}}{\text{equivalent weight}} \times \text{atomic weight} \\ \text{ of oxygen }$ of element $=\frac{418\ \mathrm{g}}{69.66\ \mathrm{u}} \times 16\ \mathrm{u}=6 \times 16\ \mathrm{g}=96\ \mathrm{g}$ © examsnet.com

question: Consider the following Statement-I : During isothermal expansion of an ideal gas its enthalpy decreases. Statement-II : When 2.0 L of an ideal gas expands isothermally into vaccum, $\Delta U=0$ . The correct answer is [AP EAPCET 21 May 2025 S2]
search_text: consider the following statement-i : during isothermal expansion of an ideal gas its enthalpy decreases. statement-ii : when 2.0 l of an ideal gas expands isothermally into vaccum, $\delta u=0$ . the correct answer is [ap eapcet 21 may 2025 s2] {'a': 'both statement-i and statement-ii are correct', 'b': 'both statement-i and statement-ii are not correct', 'c': 'statement-i is correct, but statement-ii is not correct', 'd': 'statement-i is not correct, but statement-ii is  correct'} 2025 2025-05-21 shift_2 chemistry   129 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: statement i during isothermal expansion of an ideal gas its enthalpy decreases. for an ideal gas, enthalpy $h=u+pv$ . for an ideal gas: $u=nc_vt$ and since internal energy $u$ depends only on temperature for an ideal gas, $du=0 \;\;$ if temperature is constant (isothermal process). also, $pv=nrt$ . therefore, $h=u+pv=nc_vt+nrt=n(c_v+r)t=nc_pt$ since $t$ is constant (isothermal), enthalpy $h$ is also constant. hence, enthalpy does not decrease, it remains the same. statement i is incorrect. statement ii when 2.0 l of an ideal gas expands isothermally into vacuum, $\delta u=0$ . for free expansion into vacuum: external pressure $=0$ so $w=0$ no heat exchange ( $q=0$ ) because the system is isolated (expanding into vacuum) thus, $\delta u=q+w=0+0=0$ also, for an ideal gas, $\delta u$ depends only on temperature, and since it is isothermal, $\delta u=0$ . statement ii is correct. final answer statement i is not correct but statement ii is correct. correct option: d © examsnet.com

search_text: at $25^{\circ}  \mathrm{c}$ , the percentage of ionization of $x  \mathrm{m}$ acetic acid is 4.242 . what is the ph of the acetic acid solution? $(\log 4.242=0.6275) ;(\log 0.04242=-1.372) \;\; (k_a=1.8 \times 10^{-5})$ [ap eapcet 21 may 2025 s2] {'a': '$3.37$', 'b': '$1.70$', 'c': '$1.37$', 'd': '$2.37$'} 2025 2025-05-21 shift_2 chemistry   131 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: (a) percentage ionisation $\;=\;\frac{[h^+]}{\;\text{initial concentration of acid}\;} \times 100\%$ $\;4.242=\;\frac{[h^+]}{x} \times 100$ $\; [h^+] = \frac{4.242 \times x}{100} = 0.04242 x$ $\; [\mathrm{ch}_3\mathrm{coo}^-] = 0.04242 x$ [ $\because$ \% ionisation is small] $[\mathrm{ch}_3\mathrm{cooh}] \;= x - 0.04242 x$ $\;= 0.95758 x$ for equilibrium reaction, $\mathrm{ch}_3\mathrm{cooh} \;\rightleftharpoons \mathrm{ch}_3\mathrm{coo}^- + h^+$ $k_a = \frac{ [\mathrm{ch}_3\mathrm{coo}^-] [h^+] }{ [\mathrm{ch}_3\mathrm{cooh}] }$ $1.8 \times 10^{-5} = \frac{0.04242 x \times 0.04242 x}{0.95758 x}$ $x \;= 0.009579$ $[h^+] = 0.04242 \times 0.009579$ $\;= 0.00040693$ $ph \;= -\log [h^+]$ $\;= -\log [0.00040693] = 3.37$ © examsnet.com

search_text: at 298 k , the value of $k_c$ for the following reaction is $x\ \mathrm{mol}\ \mathrm{l}^{-1}$ . what is the approximate $k_p$ value for this reaction? $(r=0.082\ \mathrm{l}\ \mathrm{atm}\ \mathrm{mol}^{-1}\ \mathrm{k}^{-1}) .$ $\mathrm{a}_2\mathrm{o}_4(g) \rightleftharpoons 2\mathrm{ao}_2(g)$ [ap eapcet 21 may 2025 s2] {'a': '$24.4 x$', 'b': '$12.2 x$', 'c': '$\\;\\frac{x}{24.4}$', 'd': '$\\;\\frac{24.4}{x}$'} 2025 2025-05-21 shift_2 chemistry   132 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: given reaction: $\mathrm{a_2o_4}(g) \rightleftharpoons 2\mathrm{ao_2}(g)$ at 298 k , the equilibrium constant in concentration units is $k_c = x\ \mathrm{mol}\ \mathrm{l}^{-1}$ . we need to find the approximate value of $k_p$ . relation between $k_p$ and $k_c$ for a gaseous reaction: $k_p = k_c (rt)^{\delta n}$ where $\delta n = \text{(moles of gaseous products)} - \text{(moles of gaseous reactants)}$ step 1: determine $\delta n$ moles of gaseous products $=2$ moles of gaseous reactants $=1$ $\rightarrow \delta n = 2-1 = +1$ step 2: substitute into the relation $k_p = k_c (rt)^1 = k_c (rt)$ step 3: plug in the given values at $t = 298\ \mathrm{k}$ , $r = 0.082\ \mathrm{l}\ \mathrm{atm}\ \mathrm{mol}^{-1}\ \mathrm{k}^{-1}$ $rt = 0.082 \times 298 = 24.4\ \mathrm{l}\ \mathrm{atm}\ \mathrm{mol}^{-1}$ step 4: therefore, $\;k_p = k_c \times 24.4$ $\;k_p = 24.4 x$ final answer: option a - $24.4 x$ © examsnet.com

question: Which of the following sets are correctly matched ? Metal Refining process I) Hg distillation II) Cu poling III) B zone refining IV) Ti liquation [AP EAPCET 21 May 2025 S2]
search_text: which of the following sets are correctly matched ? metal refining process i) hg distillation ii) cu poling iii) b zone refining iv) ti liquation [ap eapcet 21 may 2025 s2] {'a': 'i, iii & iv only', 'b': 'i, ii & iii only', 'c': 'ii, iii & iv only', 'd': 'i, ii, iii & iv'} 2025 2025-05-21 shift_2 chemistry   147 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: i. hg (mercury) - distillation distillation is a refining process used for volatile metals with low boiling points. mercury is a liquid metal at room temperature and has a relatively low boiling point ( $356.7^{\circ}\mathrm{c}$ ), making it suitable for purification by distillation to separate it from nonvolatile impurities. this match is correct. ii. cu (copper) - poling poling is a pyrometallurgical refining process used to remove small amounts of oxygen from molten copper (blister copper). in this process, green wood logs are stirred into the molten copper. the hydrocarbons in the wood act as reducing agents, converting cuprous oxide ( $\mathrm{cu}_2\mathrm{o}$ ) to metallic copper. this match is correct. iii. b (boron) - zone refining zone refining is a purification technique used for producing extremely pure metals and metalloids, especially for semiconductor applications. it works on the principle that impurities are more soluble in the molten state than in the solid state. boron is a metalloid, and ultra-pure boron is vital for certain applications. zone refining is indeed a method used for the purification of boron, as well as silicon and germanium. this match is correct. iv. ti (titanium) - liquation liquation is a refining process suitable for metals with low melting points that can be separated from higher melting point impurities (e.g., tin, lead). titanium, however, has a very high melting point ( $1668^{\circ}\mathrm{c}$ ). its refining typically involves methods like the kroll process (to produce titanium sponge) followed by electron beam melting or vacuum arc remelting for further purification. liquation is not appropriate for titanium. this match is incorrect. based on the evaluation, pairs i, ii, and iii are correctly matched. © examsnet.com

Statement-II : The order of basic strength of amines in aqueous phase follows the order $(\mathrm{C}_2\mathrm{H}_5)_3\mathrm{N}>(\mathrm{C}_2\mathrm{H}_5)_2\mathrm{NH}>\mathrm{C}_2\mathrm{H}_5\mathrm{NH}_2$ The correct answer is [AP EAPCET 21 May 2025 S2]
search_text: consider the following statement-i : $\mathrm{ch}_3\ \mathrm{nh}_2$ is more basic than $\mathrm{nh}_3$ but $\mathrm{c}_6\ \mathrm{h}_5\ \mathrm{nh}_2$ is less basic than $\mathrm{nh}_3$ . statement-ii : the order of basic strength of amines in aqueous phase follows the order $(\mathrm{c}_2\mathrm{h}_5)_3\mathrm{n}>(\mathrm{c}_2\mathrm{h}_5)_2\mathrm{nh}>\mathrm{c}_2\mathrm{h}_5\mathrm{nh}_2$ the correct answer is [ap eapcet 21 may 2025 s2] {'a': 'both statement-i and statement-ii are correct', 'b': 'both statement-i and statement-ii are not correct', 'c': 'statement-i is correct, but statement-ii is not correct', 'd': 'statement-i is not correct, but statement-ii is correct'} 2025 2025-05-21 shift_2 chemistry   160 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: statement-i: $\mathrm{ch}_3\mathrm{nh}_2$ is more basic than $\mathrm{nh}_3$ but $\mathrm{c}_6\mathrm{h}_5\mathrm{nh}_2$ is less basic than $\mathrm{nh}_3$ . explanation: in methylamine $(\mathrm{ch}_3\mathrm{nh}_2)$ , the $-\mathrm{ch}_3$ group is electron donating ( $+\mathrm{i}$ effect), which increases the electron density on the nitrogen atom and makes it more basic than ammonia. in aniline $(\mathrm{c}_6\mathrm{h}_5\mathrm{nh}_2)$ , the lone pair on nitrogen is delocalised into the benzene ring through resonance, so it is much less available to accept a proton, making aniline less basic than ammonia. hence, statement-i is correct. statement-ii: the order $(\mathrm{c}_2\mathrm{h}_5)_3\mathrm{n}>(\mathrm{c}_2\mathrm{h}_5)_2\mathrm{nh}>\mathrm{c}_2\mathrm{h}_5\mathrm{nh}_2$ is the order of basic strength in the gas phase, i.e. the order expected from the $+\mathrm{i}$ effect alone. in the aqueous phase, the basicity is governed by two opposing factors: (i) $+\mathrm{i}$ effect of alkyl groups, which increases as tertiary $>$ secondary $>$ primary, and (ii) solvation (hydration) of the conjugate ammonium ion, which is strongest for the primary amine (maximum number of $\mathrm{n}-\mathrm{h}$ bonds available for hydrogen bonding) and decreases as primary $>$ secondary $>$ tertiary. because of this competing solvation effect, the observed order in water is not the gas-phase order. the actual order in aqueous solution, from the $\mathrm{p}k_b$ values, is: $(\mathrm{c}_2\mathrm{h}_5)_2\mathrm{nh}\ (\mathrm{p}k_b=3.00)>(\mathrm{c}_2\mathrm{h}_5)_3\mathrm{n}\ (\mathrm{p}k_b=3.25)>\mathrm{c}_2\mathrm{h}_5\mathrm{nh}_2\ search_text: if the extreme value of the function $f(x)=\frac{4}{\sin x}+\frac{1}{1-\sin x}$ in $\left[0,\frac{\pi}{2}\right]$ is $m$ and it exists at $x=k$ , then $\cos k=$ [ap eapcet 22 may 2025 s1] {'a': '$\\frac{\\sqrt{m}}{4}$', 'b': '$\\frac{\\sqrt{m+1}}{\\sqrt{2}}$', 'c': '$\\frac{\\sqrt{5}}{\\sqrt{m}}$', 'd': '$\\frac{1}{m}$'} 2025 2025-05-22 shift_1 mathematics   67 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: $f(x)=\frac{4}{\sin x}+\frac{1}{1-\sin x}$ $\rightarrow f'(x)=\frac{-4\cos x}{\sin^2 x}+\frac{\cos x}{(1-\sin x)^2}$ $f'(x)=0$ $\rightarrow \cos x \left[\frac{1}{(1-\sin x)^2}-\frac{4}{\sin^2 x}\right]=0$ $\rightarrow \cos x \left[\frac{\sin^2 x-4(1-\sin x)^2}{\sin^2 x (1-\sin x)^2}\right]=0$ $\rightarrow \cos x[(\sin x+2-2\sin x)(\sin x-2+2\sin x)]$ $=0$ $\rightarrow x=\frac{\pi}{2}, \sin x=2 \sin x=\frac{2}{3}$ $f(0)=\text{not possible}$ $f\left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right)=\text{not possible}$ $\sin x \neq 2 \; (\because \sin x \in [-1,1])$ $\therefore \sin x=\frac{2}{3}$ $f(x)_{\max}=6+3=9=m$ $\rightarrow \cos k=\sqrt{1-\frac{4}{9}}=\sqrt{\frac{5}{9}}=\sqrt{\frac{5}{m}}$ © examsnet.com

search_text: $\int \frac{1}{9 \cos^2 x - 24 \sin x \cos x + 16 \sin^2 x} \, dx =$ [ap eapcet 22 may 2025 s1] {'a': '$\\frac{\\cos x}{4(3 \\cos x - 4 \\sin x)} + c$', 'b': '$\\frac{\\sin x}{4(3 \\cos x - 4 \\sin x)} + c$', 'c': '$\\frac{\\cos x}{3 \\cos x - 4 \\sin x} + c$', 'd': '$\\frac{\\sin x}{3 \\cos x - 4 \\sin x} + c$'} 2025 2025-05-22 shift_1 mathematics   69 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: $i = \int \frac{1}{9 \cos^2 x - 24 \sin x \cos x + 16 \sin^2 x} \, dx =$ $\rightarrow i = \int \frac{1}{(3 \cos x - 4 \sin x)^2} \, dx$ $\rightarrow i = \int \frac{\sec^2 x}{(3 - 4 \tan x)^2} \, dx$ $3 - 4 \tan x = t$ $-4 \sec^2 x \, dx = dt$ $\rightarrow i = \frac{1}{-4} \int t^{-2} \, dt$ $= \frac{1}{4} \cdot \frac{1}{t} + c = \frac{\cos x}{4(3 \cos x - 4 \sin x)} + c$ © examsnet.com

search_text: if $\int \frac{1}{\cot \frac{x}{2} \cot \frac{x}{3} \cot \frac{x}{6}} \, dx = a \log \left| \cos \frac{x}{2} \right| + b \log \left| \cos \frac{x}{3} \right| + c \log \left| \cos \frac{x}{6} \right| + k$ then $a + b + c =$ [ap eapcet 22 may 2025 s1] {'a': '$7$', 'b': '$11$', 'c': '$-7$', 'd': '$1$'} 2025 2025-05-22 shift_1 mathematics   70 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: $\int \frac{1}{\cot \frac{x}{2} \cot \frac{x}{3} \cot \frac{x}{6}} \, dx$ $= \int \tan \frac{x}{2} \tan \frac{x}{3} \tan \frac{x}{6} \, dx$ $\because \frac{x}{6} = \frac{x}{2} - \frac{x}{3}$ $\rightarrow \tan \frac{x}{6} = \frac{ \tan \frac{x}{2} - \tan \frac{x}{3} }{ 1 + \tan \frac{x}{2} \tan \frac{x}{3} }$ $\int \left( \tan \frac{x}{2} - \tan \frac{x}{3} - \tan \frac{x}{6} \right) \, dx$ $= -2 \log \left| \cos \frac{x}{2} \right| + 3 \log \left| \cos \frac{x}{3} \right|$ $+ 6 \log \left| \sec \frac{x}{6} \right| + k$ $\therefore a = -2, b = 3, c = 6$ $\rightarrow a + b + c = 7 .$ © examsnet.com

search_text: $\int \frac{\sin x + \cos x}{\sin x - \cos x} \, dx =$ [ap eapcet 22 may 2025 s1] {'a': '$-x + \\log |\\cos x - \\sin x| + c$', 'b': '$x - \\log |\\cos x - \\sin x| + c$', 'c': '$-\\log |\\cos x - \\sin x| + c$', 'd': '$\\log |\\cos x - \\sin x| + c$'} 2025 2025-05-22 shift_1 mathematics   71 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: $\; i = \int \frac{\sin x + \cos x}{\sin x - \cos x} \, dx \; \text{ put } \; \sin x - \cos x = t$ $\; \rightarrow \; -(\cos x + \sin x) dx = dt$ $i = -\int \frac{1}{t} dt$ $\; = -\log |\sin x - \cos x| + c$ $\; = -\log |\cos x - \sin x| + c$ © examsnet.com

search_text: $\int\; \frac{x^4-1}{x^2 \sqrt{x^4+x^2+1}} dx=$ [ap eapcet 22 may 2025 s1] {'a': '$\\; \\frac{2\\sqrt{x^4+x^2+1}}{x} + c$', 'b': '$\\; \\frac{\\sqrt{x^4+x^2+1}}{x} + c$', 'c': '$\\; \\frac{\\sqrt{x^4+x^2+1}}{2x} + c$', 'd': '$\\; \\frac{4\\sqrt{x^4+x^2+1}}{x} + c$'} 2025 2025-05-22 shift_1 mathematics   72 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: $\; i = \int\; \frac{x^4-1}{x^2 \sqrt{x^4+x^2+1}} dx$ $\; \rightarrow \;\; i = \int\; \frac{x^2 - \frac{1}{x^2}}{\sqrt{x^4+x^2+1}} dx$ $= \int\; \frac{x - \frac{1}{x^3}}{\sqrt{x^2 + \; \frac{1}{x^2} + 1}} dx$ $\;\; \text{ put } \;\; x^2 + \frac{1}{x^2} + 1 = t^2$ $\; \rightarrow \;\; 2x - \frac{2}{x^3} dx = 2t dt$ $\; i = \int dt = t + c = \frac{\sqrt{x^4+x^2+1}}{x} + c$ © examsnet.com
