search_text: $\int\limits_{-\pi/4}^{\pi/3} \left| \tan\left( x - \frac{\pi}{6} \right) \right| \, dx =$ [ap eapcet 22 may 2025 s1] {'a': '$\\log \\frac{\\sqrt{3}-1}{\\sqrt{6}}$', 'b': '$\\log\\left( 2\\sqrt{2} (\\sqrt{3}+1) \\right)$', 'c': '$\\log \\frac{\\sqrt{3}+1}{\\sqrt{6}}$', 'd': '$\\log\\left( 2\\sqrt{2} (\\sqrt{3}-1) \\right)$'} 2025 2025-05-22 shift_1 mathematics   74 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: $i = \int\limits_{\frac{-\pi}{4}}^{\frac{\pi}{3}} \left| \tan\left( x - \frac{\pi}{6} \right) \right| \, dx$ put $\tan\left( x - \frac{\pi}{6} \right) = 0 \rightarrow x - \frac{\pi}{6} = 0$ $i = \int\limits_{\frac{-\pi}{4}}^{\frac{\pi}{6}} -\tan\left( x - \frac{\pi}{6} \right) \, dx + \int\limits_{\frac{\pi}{6}}^{\frac{\pi}{3}} \tan\left( x - \frac{\pi}{6} \right) \, dx$ $= - \left[ \log\left( \sec\left( x - \frac{\pi}{6} \right) \right) \right]_{-\pi}^{\frac{\pi}{6}} + \left[ \log\left( \sec\left( x - \frac{\pi}{6} \right) \right) \right]_{\frac{\pi}{6}}^{\frac{\pi}{3}}.$ $\rightarrow \log\left( \sec\left( \frac{5\pi}{12} \right) \right) + \log\left( \sec\left( \frac{\pi}{6} \right) \right)$ $= \log\left( \sec\left( \frac{5\pi}{12} \right) \sec\left( \frac{\pi}{6} \right) \right)$ $= \log\left( 2\sqrt{2} \, \frac{\sqrt{3}+1}{\sqrt{3}} \right)$ © examsnet.com

search_text: $\int\limits_{0}^{\pi} \;\frac{x \sin x}{\sin ^{2} x+2 \cos ^{2} x} dx =$ [ap eapcet 22 may 2025 s1] {'a': '$\\frac{\\pi}{2}$', 'b': '$\\frac{\\pi^{2}}{2}$', 'c': '$\\frac{\\pi^{2}}{4}$', 'd': '$\\frac{\\pi}{4}$'} 2025 2025-05-22 shift_1 mathematics   75 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: $\;i=\int\limits_{0}^{\pi} \;\frac{x \sin x}{\sin ^{2} x+2 \cos ^{2} x} dx$ $\rightarrow i=\int\limits_{0}^{\pi} \;\frac{(\pi-x) \sin x}{\sin ^{2} x+2 \cos ^{2} x} dx$ $\; \left[ \because \int\limits_{0}^{a} f(x) dx = \int\limits_{0}^{a} f(a-x) dx \right]$ $\rightarrow 2i = \int\limits_{0}^{\pi} \;\frac{\pi \sin x}{1+\cos ^{2} x} dx$ put $\cos x = t \rightarrow -\sin x dx = dt$ $\rightarrow 2i = -\pi \left[ \tan^{-1} t \right]_{1}^{-1}$ $\rightarrow 2i = -\pi \left[ \frac{-\pi}{4} - \frac{\pi}{4} \right] \rightarrow i = \frac{\pi^{2}}{4}$ © examsnet.com

search_text: the area of the region lying between the curves $y=\sqrt{4-x^{2}}, y^{2}=3x$ and the y-axis is [ap eapcet 22 may 2025 s1] {'a': '$\\frac{\\pi}{3} - \\frac{1}{2\\sqrt{3}}$', 'b': '$\\frac{\\pi}{6} + \\frac{1}{2\\sqrt{3}}$', 'c': '$\\frac{\\pi}{3} + \\frac{1}{2\\sqrt{3}}$', 'd': '$\\frac{\\pi}{6} - \\frac{1}{2\\sqrt{3}}$'} 2025 2025-05-22 shift_1 mathematics   76 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: $y=\sqrt{4-x^{2}}$ and $y^{2}=3x$ $\rightarrow 3x=4-x^{2}$ $\rightarrow x^{2}+3x-4=0$ $\rightarrow (x+4)(x-1)=0$ $\;x=1,-4 \rightarrow y=\sqrt{3}$ $\therefore$ required area, $\;=\;\frac{1}{3} \int\limits_{0}^{\sqrt{3}} y^{2} d y + \int_{\sqrt{3}}^{2} \sqrt{4-y^{2}} d y$ $\;=\;\frac{1}{3} \left[\; \frac{y^{3}}{3} \right]_{0}^{\sqrt{3}} + \left[\; \frac{y}{2} \sqrt{4-y^{2}} + \;\frac{4}{2} \sin^{-1} \frac{y}{2} \right]_{\sqrt{3}}^{2}$ $\;=\;\frac{1}{9}(3\sqrt{3}) + 2 \frac{\pi}{2} - \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} - 2 \left( \frac{\pi}{3} \right)$ $\;=\;\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3} - \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} + \frac{\pi}{3} = \frac{\pi}{3} - \frac{1}{2\sqrt{3}}$ © examsnet.com

search_text: $\lim\limits_{n \to \infty}\left( \frac{1}{1^2+n^2}+\frac{2}{2^2+n^2}+\frac{3}{3^2+n^2}+\cdots+\frac{n}{n^2+n^2} \right) =$ [ap eapcet 22 may 2025 s1] {'a': '1', 'b': '$\\frac{1}{2} \\log 2$', 'c': '$2 \\log 2$', 'd': '0'} 2025 2025-05-22 shift_1 mathematics   77 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: $\;\lim\limits_{n \to \infty}\left[ \frac{1}{1^2+n^2}+\frac{2}{2^2+n^2}+\frac{3}{3^2+n^2}+\frac{n}{n^2+n^2} \right]$ $\;\lim\limits_{n \to \infty}\sum\limits_{r=1}^{n} \frac{r}{r^2+n^2}=\lim\limits_{n \to \infty}\sum \frac{ \frac{r}{n} }{1+ \left( \frac{r}{n} \right)^2 } \cdot \frac{1}{n}$ $\;\rightarrow \int\limits_{0}^{1} \frac{x}{1+x^2}\, dx$ $\;\;\text{put}\; 1+x^2=t \rightarrow 2x\,dx=dt$ $\;\rightarrow \frac{1}{2} \int\limits_{1}^{2} \frac{1}{t}\, dt \rightarrow \frac{1}{2}[\log t]_1^2=\frac{1}{2} \log 2$ © examsnet.com

question: The general solution of the differential equation $\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{2x^2 - xy - y^2}{x^2 - y^2}$ is [AP EAPCET 22 May 2025 S1]
search_text: the general solution of the differential equation $\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{2x^2 - xy - y^2}{x^2 - y^2}$ is [ap eapcet 22 may 2025 s1] {'a': '$\\log \\left| \\frac{y^2 - 2x^2}{x^2} \\right| + \\sqrt{2} \\log \\left| \\frac{y - \\sqrt{2}x}{y + \\sqrt{2}x} \\right| + 2\\sqrt{2} \\log |x| = c$', 'b': '$\\sqrt{2} \\log \\left| \\frac{y^2 - 2x^2}{x^2} \\right| + \\log \\left| \\frac{y - \\sqrt{2}x}{y + \\sqrt{2}x} \\right| + 2\\sqrt{2} \\log |x| = c$', 'c': '$\\sqrt{2} \\log \\left| \\frac{y^2 + 2x^2}{x^2} \\right| + \\log \\left| \\frac{y + \\sqrt{2}x}{y - \\sqrt{2}x} \\right| + 2\\sqrt{2} \\log |x| = c$', 'd': '$\\log \\left| \\frac{2x^2 - y^2}{x^2} \\right| + \\sqrt{2} \\log \\left| \\frac{y + \\sqrt{2}x}{y - \\sqrt{2}x} \\right| + \\log |x| = c$'} 2025 2025-05-22 shift_1 mathematics   78 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: $\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{2x^2 - xy - y^2}{x^2 - y^2}$ $\text{put} y = vx$ $\frac{dy}{dx} = v + x \frac{dv}{dx}$ $\rightarrow v + x \frac{dv}{dx} = \frac{2x^2 - v x^2 - v^2 x^2}{x^2 - v^2 x^2}$ $\rightarrow x \frac{dv}{dx} = \frac{2 - v - v^2}{1 - v^2} - v$ $\rightarrow x \frac{dv}{dx} = \frac{2 - 2v - v^2 + v^3}{1 - v^2}$ $\rightarrow \frac{1 - v^2}{v^3 - v^2 - 2v + 2} dv = \frac{1}{x} dx$ $\rightarrow \int \frac{1 - v^2}{(v^2 - 2)(v - 1)} dv = \int \frac{1}{x} dx$ $\rightarrow \int \left( \frac{-v}{v^2 - 2} - \frac{1}{v^2 - 2} \right) dv = \frac{1}{x} dx$ $\rightarrow \frac{1}{2} \log (v^2 - 2) - \frac{1}{2\sqrt{2}} \log \frac{v - \sqrt{2}}{v + \sqrt{2}} - \log x + c$ put $v = \frac{y}{x}$ $\rightarrow \sqrt{2} \log \left| \frac{y^2 - 2x^2}{x^2} \right| + \log \left| \frac{y - \sqrt{2}x}{y + \sqrt{2}x} \right| + 2\sqrt{2} \log |x| = c$ © examsnet.com

search_text: if the degree of the differential equation corresponding to the family of curves $y = ax + \frac{1}{a}$ (where $a \neq 0$ is an arbitary constant) is r and it's order is m , then the solution of $\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{y}{2x}, y(1)=\sqrt{r+m}$ is [ap eapcet 22 may 2025 s1] {'a': '$y = 3^x$', 'b': '$y^2 = 3x$', 'c': '$x^2 = 3y$', 'd': '$y = 3 \\log x$'} 2025 2025-05-22 shift_1 mathematics   79 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: $y = ax + \frac{1}{a}$ $\rightarrow \frac{dy}{dx}=a \rightarrow \frac{d^2 y}{dx^2}=0$ $\rightarrow x \frac{dy}{dx} + \frac{dx}{dy} = y = 0$ $\rightarrow x \left( \frac{dy}{dx} \right)^2 + 1 - y \frac{dy}{dx} = 0$ $r=2, m=1$ $\text{now, } \frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{y}{2x}, y(1)=\sqrt{3}$ $\rightarrow \int \frac{1}{y} \, dy = \int \frac{1}{2x} \, dx$ $\rightarrow \log y = \frac{1}{2} \log(x) + \log c$ $\rightarrow \log \sqrt{3} = \log c \rightarrow c = \sqrt{3}$ $\rightarrow \log y = \log \sqrt{x} + \log \sqrt{3}$ $\rightarrow y = \sqrt{3x}$ $\therefore y^2 = 3x$ © examsnet.com

search_text: the general solution of the differential equation $y+\cos x \left(\frac{dy}{dx}\right)-\cos^2 x=0$ is [ap eapcet 22 may 2025 s1] {'a': '$(\\sec x+\\tan x) y=x+\\cos x+c$', 'b': '$(1+\\cos x) y=(x+c)\\cos x-\\cos^2 x$', 'c': '$(1+\\sin x) y=(x+c)\\cos x-\\cos^2 x$', 'd': '$(\\sec x+\\tan x) y=x-\\sin x+c$'} 2025 2025-05-22 shift_1 mathematics   80 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: $y+\cos x \left(\frac{dy}{dx}\right)-\cos^2 x=0$ $\rightarrow \frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{\cos^2 x-y}{\cos x}$ $\rightarrow \frac{dy}{dx}+y \sec x=\cos x$ $\rightarrow \text{ if } = e^{\int \sec x \, dx} = \sec x+\tan x$ $\rightarrow y(\sec x+\tan x)=\int (1+\sin x) \, dx$ $\rightarrow \frac{y(1+\sin x)}{\cos x}=x-\cos x+c$ $\rightarrow (1+\sin x) y=(x+c)\cos x-\cos^2 x$ © examsnet.com

question: During adiabatic expansion, if the temperature of 3 moles of a diatomic gas decreases by $50^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ , then the work done by the gas is (R - Universal gas constant) [AP EAPCET 22 May 2025 S1]
search_text: during adiabatic expansion, if the temperature of 3 moles of a diatomic gas decreases by $50^{\circ} \mathrm{c}$ , then the work done by the gas is (r - universal gas constant) [ap eapcet 22 may 2025 s1] {'a': '$375 r$', 'b': '$750 r$', 'c': '$1500 r$', 'd': '$825 r$'} 2025 2025-05-22 shift_1 physics   98 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: we know that in adiabatic expansion, there is no heat exchange. so, $\delta q = 0$ . from the first law of thermodynamics: $\delta q = \delta u + w$ since $\delta q = 0$ , this means: $0 = \delta u + w$ so, $w = -\delta u$ the change in internal energy for $n$ moles of a diatomic gas is: $\delta u = n c_v \delta t$ where $c_v$ for a diatomic gas is $\frac{5}{2} r$ . here, $n = 3$ moles and the temperature change $\delta t = -50^{\circ} \mathrm{c}$ (or -50 in kelvin, since the size of the degree is the same). so, $w = -\delta u = -n c_v \delta t = -3 \times \frac{5}{2} r \times (-50)$ multiplying out: $-3 \times \frac{5}{2} r \times (-50) = 7.5 r \times 50 = 375 r$ the work done by the gas is $375 r$ . © examsnet.com

search_text: if the time taken for a radioactive substance to decay $8\%$ to $77\%$ is 12 minutes, then the half life of the substance in minutes is [ap eapcet 22 may 2025 s1] {'a': '24', 'b': '18', 'c': '12', 'd': '6'} 2025 2025-05-22 shift_1 physics   117 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: when $8\%$ of nuclei decays, then remaining nuclei are $92\%$ from as, $n=n_0 e^{-\lambda t}$ here, $n=0.92 n_0$ so, $0.92 n_0=n_0 e^{-\lambda t_1}$ when, $77\%$ nuclei decay remaining number of nuclei are $23\%$ . so, $\;\; n=0.23 n_0$ $0.23 n_0=n_0 e^{-\lambda t_2}$ by dividing in equation (i) by equation (ii) $\; \frac{0.92}{0.23} = \; \frac{e^{-\lambda t_1}}{e^{-\lambda t_2}} = e^{\lambda (t_2-t_1)}$ so, $e^{\lambda (t_2-t_1)} = 4$ by taking natural log of both sides $\lambda (t_2-t_1) \; = \ln 4$ $\; \text{ and } \; t_2-t_1 \; =12 \; \text{ minutes } \;$ $12 \lambda \; = 2 \ln 2$ $\lambda \; = \; \frac{\ln 2}{6}$ and relation between half life and decay constant is $\lambda = \; \frac{\ln 2}{t_{1/2}}$ so, $\; \frac{\ln 2}{6} = \; \frac{\ln 2}{t_{1/2}}$ and $t_{1/2}=6$ minutes © examsnet.com

search_text: for which of the following processes entropy change $(\delta s)$ is negative ? i) sublimation of dry ice ii) freezing of water iii) crystallisation of the dissolved substance iv) burning of rocket fuel [ap eapcet 22 may 2025 s1] {'a': 'i & ii only', 'b': 'ii & iii only', 'c': 'iii & iv only', 'd': 'i & iv only'} 2025 2025-05-22 shift_1 chemistry   130 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: let's analyze each process in terms of entropy change ( $\delta s$ ): i. sublimation of dry ice (solid $c o _{ 2 } ⟶$ gas $c o _{ 2 }$ ) a solid goes directly to a gas. the disorder (randomness) increases significantly. entropy increases $\rightarrow \delta s > 0$ ii. freezing of water (liquid $⟶$ solid) a liquid becomes a more ordered solid structure. disorder decreases. entropy decreases $\rightarrow \delta s < 0$ iii. crystallisation of the dissolved substance dissolved ions/molecules (disordered) form a regular crystal lattice (ordered). disorder decreases. entropy decreases $\rightarrow \delta s < 0$ iv. burning of rocket fuel (combustion) chemical reaction produces gases and increases randomness overall. entropy increases $\longrightarrow \delta s>0$ processes with negative entropy change: ii. freezing of water iii. crystallisation of the dissolved substance correct answer: option b - ii and iii only © examsnet.com

search_text: at $t(k), k_c$ value for $\mathrm{ao}_2(\mathrm{g})+\mathrm{bo}_2(\mathrm{g}) \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{ao}_3(\mathrm{g})+\mathrm{bo}(\mathrm{g})$ is 16. in a closed 1 l flask, one mole each of $\mathrm{ao}_2, \mathrm{bo}_2, \mathrm{ao}_3$ and bo are taken and heated to $t(k)$ . what is the concentration (in $\text{mol l}^{-1}$ ) of $\mathrm{ao}_3$ at equilibrium? [ap eapcet 22 may 2025 s1] {'a': '$0.4$', 'b': '$0.6$', 'c': '$1.6$', 'd': '$1.4$'} 2025 2025-05-22 shift_1 chemistry   132 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: we are given these starting amounts: $[ \mathrm{ao}_2 ] = 1 \text{ mol/l} \quad [ \mathrm{bo}_2 ] = 1 \text{ mol/l} \quad [ \mathrm{ao}_3 ] = 1 \text{ mol/l} \quad [ \mathrm{bo} ] = 1 \text{ mol/l} \quad k_c = 16$ we need to find the equilibrium concentration of $a\,o_3$ . step 1: write the reaction equation. $\mathrm{ao}_2(\mathrm{g})+\mathrm{bo}_2(\mathrm{g}) \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{ao}_3(\mathrm{g})+\mathrm{bo}(\mathrm{g})$ step 2: set up an ice (initial, change, equilibrium) table. at the start (initial): $[ \mathrm{ao}_2 ] = 1, [ \mathrm{bo}_2 ] = 1, [ \mathrm{ao}_3 ] = 1, [ \mathrm{bo} ] = 1$ let $x$ be the amount that reacts. $\;\text{ change in concentrations: }\; \begin{array}{cccc} \mathrm{ao}_2 & \mathrm{bo}_2 & \mathrm{ao}_3 & \mathrm{bo} \\ -x & -x & +x & +x \end{array}$ at equilibrium: $\; [ \mathrm{ao}_2 ] = 1 - x$ $\; [ \mathrm{bo}_2 ] = 1 - x$ $\; [ \mathrm{ao}_3 ] = 1 + x$ $\; [ \mathrm{bo} ] = 1 + x$ step 3: write the equilibrium expression and solve for $x$ . $k_c = \frac{ [ \mathrm{ao}_3 ] [ \mathrm{bo} ] }{ [ \mathrm{ao}_2 ] [ \mathrm{bo}_2 ] } = \frac{ (1+x)(1+x) }{ (1-x)(1-x) } = 16$ take the square root of both sides: $\frac{1+x}{1-x} = 4$ solve for $x$ : $1 + x = 4(1 - x)$ $1 + x = 4 - 4x$ $1 + x + 4x = 4$ $1 + 5x = 4$ $5x = 3$ $x = 0.6$ step 4: find the equilibrium concentration of $\mathrm{ao}_3$ . $[ \mathrm{ao}_3 ] = 1 + x = 1 + 0.6 = 1.6 \text{ mol/l}$ © examsnet.com

question: The mole fractions of glucose and water in aqueous glucose solution are 0.0244 and 0.9756 respectively. What is the weight percentage (w/w) of glucose in this solution? [AP EAPCET 22 May 2025 S1]
search_text: the mole fractions of glucose and water in aqueous glucose solution are 0.0244 and 0.9756 respectively. what is the weight percentage (w/w) of glucose in this solution? [ap eapcet 22 may 2025 s1] {'a': '$40$', 'b': '$25$', 'c': '$20$', 'd': '$10$'} 2025 2025-05-22 shift_1 chemistry   141 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: let's assume we have 1 mole of the total solution. mole fraction of glucose is 0.0244 . this means there are 0.0244 moles of glucose in the solution. the mass of glucose is calculated by multiplying the number of moles by the molar mass of glucose ( $\mathrm{180.16\,g/mol}$ ): $0.0244 \times 180.16 = 4.3959\,\mathrm{g}$ the mole fraction of water is 0.9756 . this means there are 0.9756 moles of water in the solution. the mass of water is found by multiplying the number of moles by the molar mass of water ( $\mathrm{18.01\,g/mol}$ ): $0.9756 \times 18.01 = 17.570\,\mathrm{g}$ the total mass of the solution is just the mass of glucose plus the mass of water: $4.3959 + 17.570 = 21.9659\,\mathrm{g}$ to find the weight percent $\text{(w/w)}$ of glucose, divide the mass of glucose by the total mass and multiply by 100 : $\;\frac{4.3959}{21.9659} \times 100 = 20\%$ © examsnet.com

question: At $T(\mathrm{K})$ , the vapour pressure of an aqueous solution of a non-volatile solute, whose mole fraction is 0.02 is found to be 34.65 mm Hg . What is the vapour pressure (in mm Hg ) of pure water at the same temperature ? [AP EAPCET 22 May 2025 S1]
search_text: at $t(\mathrm{k})$ , the vapour pressure of an aqueous solution of a non-volatile solute, whose mole fraction is 0.02 is found to be 34.65 mm hg . what is the vapour pressure (in mm hg ) of pure water at the same temperature ? [ap eapcet 22 may 2025 s1] {'a': '$35.70$', 'b': '$35.36$', 'c': '$35.00$', 'd': '$34.30$'} 2025 2025-05-22 shift_1 chemistry   142 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: step 1: find the mole fraction of water. the solution has a mole fraction of solute $=0.02$ . mole fraction of water $=1$ minus mole fraction of solute. so, $\chi_{\text{water}} = 1-0.02 = 0.98$ step 2: use raoult's law to relate vapour pressures. raoult's law says: vapour pressure of solution $=$ vapour pressure of pure water $\times$ mole fraction of water. $p_{\text{solution}} = p_{\text{water}} \times \chi_{\text{water}}$ we know $p_{\text{solution}} = 34.65 \text{ mm hg}$ and $\chi_{\text{water}} = 0.98$ . so, $34.65 = p_{\text{water}} \times 0.98$ step 3: solve for the vapour pressure of pure water. divide both sides by 0.98 : $p_{\text{water}} = \frac{34.65}{0.98} = 35.36 \text{ mm hg}$ © examsnet.com

question: The set of all real values of $x$ for which $f(x)=\sqrt{\;\frac{|x|-2}{|x|-3}}$ is a well defined function is [AP EAPCET 22 May 2025 S2]
search_text: the set of all real values of $x$ for which $f(x)=\sqrt{\;\frac{|x|-2}{|x|-3}}$ is a well defined function is [ap eapcet 22 may 2025 s2] {'a': '$\\mathbb{r}-[-3,-2)\\cup(2,3]$', 'b': '$\\mathbb{r}-[-3,3]$', 'c': '$(-3,3)$', 'd': '$(-3,3)$'} 2025 2025-05-22 shift_2 mathematics   1 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: to define $f(x)=\sqrt{\frac{|x|-2}{|x|-3}}$ , the radicand must be non-negative and the denominator must be non-zero. let $t=|x|\ge 0$ . then we need $\frac{t-2}{t-3}\ge 0$ with $t\ne 3$ . the critical values are $t=2$ and $t=3$ . a sign analysis gives $t\in[0,2]\cup(3,\infty)$ . since $t=|x|$ , $0\le |x|\le 2$ gives $-2\le x\le 2$ . also $|x|>3$ gives $x<-3$ or $x>3$ . thus the domain is $(-\infty,-3)\cup[-2,2]\cup(3,\infty)$ . this is the same as $\mathbb{r}-[-3,-2)\cup(2,3]$ . hence the correct option is a. © examsnet.com

search_text: the coefficient of $x^3$ in the power series expansion of $\;\frac{1+4x-3x^2}{(1+3x)^3}$ is [ap eapcet 22 may 2025 s2] {'a': '$-27$', 'b': '$27$', 'c': '$153$', 'd': '$-153$'} 2025 2025-05-22 shift_2 mathematics   18 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: $\;\;\frac{1+4x-3x^2}{(1+3x)^3}= (1+4x-3x^2)(1+3x)^{-3}$ $\;\rightarrow (1+3x)^{-3}=1-3(3x)+\frac{(-3)(-4)(3x)^2}{2!}$ $\;\;\;+\;\frac{(-3)(-4)(-5)(3x)^3}{3!}+\ldots$ $\;\rightarrow (1+3x)^{-3}=1-9x+54x^2-270x^3+\ldots$ $\; (1+4x-3x^2)(1-9x+54x^2-270x^3+\ldots)$ $\;\;\;=1(-270x^3)+4x(5x^2)-3x^2(-9x)$ $\;\;\;=-270x^3+216x^3+27x^3$ $\;\;\;=-270+216+27=-27$ ⇒ the coefficient of $x^3=-27$ © examsnet.com

search_text: if $\alpha, \beta$ are the acute angles such that $\frac{\sin \alpha}{\sin \beta} = \frac{6}{5}$ and $\frac{\cos \alpha}{\cos \beta} = \frac{9}{5 \sqrt{5}}$ then $\sin \alpha =$ [ap eapcet 22 may 2025 s2] {'a': '$\\frac{4}{5}$', 'b': '$\\frac{3}{5}$', 'c': '$\\frac{3}{4}$', 'd': '$\\frac{2}{3}$'} 2025 2025-05-22 shift_2 mathematics   20 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: $\sin \beta = \frac{5}{6} \sin \alpha$ $\rightarrow \cos \beta = \frac{5 \sqrt{5}}{9} \cos \alpha$ $\rightarrow \sin^2 \beta + \cos^2 \beta = 1$ $\rightarrow \left( \frac{5}{6} \sin \alpha \right)^2 + \left( \frac{5 \sqrt{5}}{9} \cos \alpha \right)^2 = 1$ $\rightarrow \frac{25}{36} \sin^2 \alpha + \frac{125}{81} \cos^2 \alpha = 1$ $\rightarrow \frac{25}{36} \sin^2 \alpha + \frac{125}{81} - \frac{125}{81} \sin^2 \alpha = 1$ $\rightarrow \left( \frac{225-500}{324} \right) \sin^2 \alpha = \frac{81-125}{81}$ $\rightarrow \sin^2 \alpha = \frac{-44}{81} \times \frac{324}{-275}$ $\rightarrow \sin^2 \alpha = \frac{4}{9} \times \frac{11}{9} \times \frac{4}{25} \times \frac{81}{11}$ $\rightarrow \sin^2 \alpha = \frac{16}{25} \rightarrow \sin \alpha = \frac{4}{5}$ © examsnet.com

question: If $2 \sin x - \cos 2x = 1$ , then $(3 - 2 \sin^2 x) =$ [AP EAPCET 22 May 2025 S2]
search_text: if $2 \sin x - \cos 2x = 1$ , then $(3 - 2 \sin^2 x) =$ [ap eapcet 22 may 2025 s2] {'a': '$\\sqrt{3}$', 'b': '$-\\sqrt{3}$', 'c': '$\\sqrt{5}$', 'd': '$-\\sqrt{5}$'} 2025 2025-05-22 shift_2 mathematics   21 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: $2 \sin x - \cos 2x = 1$ $\rightarrow 2 \sin x - (1 - 2 \sin^2 x) = 1$ $\rightarrow 2 \sin x - 1 + 2 \sin^2 x = 1$ $\rightarrow 2 \sin^2 x + 2 \sin x - 2 = 0$ $\rightarrow \sin^2 x + \sin x - 1 = 0$ $\rightarrow \sin x = \frac{-1 \pm \sqrt{1+4}}{2 \times 1}$ $\rightarrow \sin x = \frac{-1 \pm \sqrt{5}}{2}$ $\rightarrow \sin x = \frac{\sqrt{5} - 1}{2}$ $\rightarrow 3 - 2 \sin^2 x = 3 - 2 \frac{(\sqrt{5} - 1)^2}{4}$ $= \frac{12 - 2(5 + 1 - 2\sqrt{5})}{4}$ $= \frac{12 - 12 + 4\sqrt{5}}{4} = \sqrt{5}$ © examsnet.com

question: If $\left(\frac{\sin 3\theta}{\sin \theta}\right)^2 - \left(\frac{\cos 3\theta}{\cos \theta}\right)^2 = a \cos b \theta$ , then $a: b =$ [AP EAPCET 22 May 2025 S2]
search_text: if $\left(\frac{\sin 3\theta}{\sin \theta}\right)^2 - \left(\frac{\cos 3\theta}{\cos \theta}\right)^2 = a \cos b \theta$ , then $a: b =$ [ap eapcet 22 may 2025 s2] {'a': '$4: 1$', 'b': '$8: 1$', 'c': '$3: 2$', 'd': '$2: 1$'} 2025 2025-05-22 shift_2 mathematics   22 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: $\left(\frac{\sin 3\theta}{\sin \theta}\right)^2 - \left(\frac{\cos 3\theta}{\cos \theta}\right)^2 = a \cos b \theta$ $\rightarrow \left(\frac{3\sin\theta - 4\sin^3\theta}{\sin\theta}\right) - \left(\frac{4\cos^3\theta - 3\cos\theta}{\cos\theta}\right) = a \cos b \theta$ $\rightarrow (3 - 4\sin^2\theta)^2 - (4\cos^2\theta - 3)^2 = a \cos b \theta$ $\rightarrow 9 + 16\sin^4\theta - 24\sin^2\theta - 16\cos^4\theta - 9 + 24\cos^2\theta = a \cos b \theta$ $\rightarrow 24(\cos^2\theta - \sin^2\theta) - 16(\cos^4\theta - \sin^4\theta) = a \cos^b \theta$ $\rightarrow 8(\cos^2\theta - \sin^2\theta)(3 - 2(\cos^2\theta + \sin^2\theta)) = a \cos b \theta,$ $\rightarrow 8 \cos 2\theta (3 - 2) = a \cos b \theta$ $\rightarrow 8 \cos 2\theta = a \cos b \theta \rightarrow a = 8, b = 2$ $\therefore a: b = 8: 2 = 4: 1$ © examsnet.com

search_text: if $\frac{1}{2} \sin^{-1} \left( \frac{3 \sin 2\theta}{5+4\cos 2\theta} \right) = \tan^{-1} x$ then $x=$ [ap eapcet 22 may 2025 s2] {'a': '$\\tan \\frac{\\theta}{3}$', 'b': '$\\frac{1}{3} \\tan \\theta$', 'c': '$\\tan 3\\theta$', 'd': '$\\frac{1}{3} \\tan 3\\theta$'} 2025 2025-05-22 shift_2 mathematics   24 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: $\frac{1}{2} \sin^{-1} \left( \frac{3 \sin 2\theta}{5+4\cos 2\theta} \right) = \tan^{-1} x$ $\rightarrow \frac{1}{2} \sin^{-1} \left( \frac{3 \cdot \frac{2 \tan \theta}{1+\tan^2 \theta}}{5+4 \left( \frac{1-\tan^2 \theta}{1+\tan^2 \theta} \right)} \right) = \tan^{-1} x$ $\rightarrow \sin^{-1} \left( \frac{6 \tan \theta}{9+\tan 2\theta} \right) = 2 \tan^{-1} x$ $\rightarrow \sin^{-1} \left( \frac{2 \cdot \left( \frac{1}{3} \tan \theta \right)}{1+ \left( \frac{\tan \theta}{3} \right)^2} \right) = \sin^{-1} \left( \frac{2x}{1+x^2} \right)$ $\rightarrow x = \frac{1}{3} \tan \theta$ © examsnet.com

question: If $\operatorname{sech}^{-1} x = \log 2$ and $\operatorname{cosech}^{-1} y = -\log 3$ , then $(x+y)=$ [AP EAPCET 22 May 2025 S2]
search_text: if $\operatorname{sech}^{-1} x = \log 2$ and $\operatorname{cosech}^{-1} y = -\log 3$ , then $(x+y)=$ [ap eapcet 22 may 2025 s2] {'a': '$\\; \\frac{1}{6}$', 'b': '$\\; \\frac{1}{20}$', 'c': '$6$', 'd': '$20$'} 2025 2025-05-22 shift_2 mathematics   25 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: $\; \operatorname{sech}^{-1} x = \log 2$ $\; {\; \text{ and } \; \operatorname{cosech}^{-1} y = -\log 3}^{\operatorname{sech}^{-1} x = \log 2}$ $\; \rightarrow \;\; \log \left( \frac{1+\sqrt{1-x^2}}{x} \right) = \log 2$ $\; \rightarrow \;\; \frac{1+\sqrt{1-x^2}}{x}=2$ $\; \rightarrow \;\; 1+\sqrt{1-x^2}=2x$ $\; \sqrt{1-x^2}=2x-1$ squaring both sides, we get $\; \rightarrow \;\; 1-x^2=4x^2+1-4x$ $\; \rightarrow \;\; 5x^2-4x=0$ $\; \rightarrow \;\; x(5x-4)=0$ $\; \;\; x=\; \frac{4}{5}$ $\; \because \operatorname{cosech}^{-1} y = -\log 3$ $\; \rightarrow \;\; \log \left( \frac{1+\sqrt{1+y^2}}{y} \right) = \log \; \frac{1}{3}$ $\; \rightarrow \;\; \frac{1+\sqrt{1+y^2}}{y} = \; \frac{1}{3}$ $\; \rightarrow \;\; 1+\sqrt{1+y^2} = \frac{y}{3}$ $\; \rightarrow \;\; \sqrt{1+y^2} = \frac{y}{3} - 1$ squaring both sides, we get $\; \rightarrow \;\; 1+y^2 = \frac{y^2}{9} + 1 - \frac{2}{3} y$ $\; \rightarrow \;\; \frac{8y^2}{9} + \frac{2}{3} y = 0$ $\; \rightarrow \;\; \frac{2}{3} y \left( \frac{4y}{3} + 1 \right) = 0$ $\; \rightarrow \;\; y = \frac{-3}{4}$ $\; \rightarrow \;\; x+y = \frac{4}{5} - \frac{3}{4} = \frac{16-15}{20}$ $\; \rightarrow \;\; x+y = \frac{1}{20}$ © examsnet.com

search_text: if the sides $a, b, c$ of the triangle $a b c$ are in harmonic progression, then $\csc^2 \frac{a}{2}, \csc^2 \frac{b}{2}, \csc^2 \frac{c}{2}$ are in [ap eapcet 22 may 2025 s2] {'a': 'arithmetico-geometric progression', 'b': 'arithmetic progression', 'c': 'geometric progression', 'd': 'harmonic progression'} 2025 2025-05-22 shift_2 mathematics   26 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: $a, b, c$ are in hp. $\rightarrow b=\frac{2ac}{a+c}$ let $\csc^2 \frac{a}{2}, \csc^2 \frac{b}{2}, \csc^2 \frac{c}{2}$ are in ap . $\rightarrow \frac{1}{\sin^2 \frac{a}{2}}, \frac{1}{\sin^2 \frac{b}{2}}, \frac{1}{\sin^2 \frac{c}{2}} \text{ are in ap.}$ $\rightarrow \frac{bc}{(s-b)(s-c)}, \frac{ac}{(s-a)(s-c)}$ $\frac{ab}{(s-a)(s-b)}$ are in ap. $\rightarrow \frac{bc}{s(s-b)(s-c)}, \frac{ac}{s(s-a)(s-c)}$ $\frac{ab}{s(s-a)(s-b)}$ are in ap. $\rightarrow \frac{bc(s-a)}{s(s-a)(s-b)(s-c)}, \frac{ac(s-b)}{s(s-a)(s-b)(s-c)^{\prime}}, \frac{ab(s-c)}{s(s-a)(s-b)(s-c)}$ are in ap. $\rightarrow b c s - a b c, a c s - a b c, a b s - a b c$ are in ap. $\rightarrow b c s, a c s, a b s$ are in ap. $\rightarrow b c, a c, a b$ are in ap. $\rightarrow \frac{1}{a}, \frac{1}{b}, \frac{1}{c}$ are in ap. $\rightarrow a, b, c$ are in hp. which is true. © examsnet.com

search_text: an aeroplane is flying at a constant speed, parallel to the horizontal ground at a height of 5 kms . a person on the ground observed that the angle of elevation of the plane is changed from $15^{\circ}$ to $30^{\circ}$ in the duration of 50 seconds, then the speed of the plane (in kmph) is [ap eapcet 22 may 2025 s2] {'a': '$100$', 'b': '$720$', 'c': '$360$', 'd': '$540$'} 2025 2025-05-22 shift_2 mathematics   28 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: let $x_1$ be the initial horizontal distance $\tan 15^{\circ} = \frac{5}{x_1} \rightarrow x_1 = \frac{5}{\tan 15^{\circ}}$ let $x_2$ be the final horizontal distance $\tan 30^{\circ} = \frac{5}{x_2}$ $\rightarrow x_2 = \frac{5}{\tan 30^{\circ}}$ the distance travelled is $d=x_1-x_2$ $\;d = \frac{5}{\tan 15^{\circ}} - \frac{5}{\tan 30^{\circ}}$ $\;d \approx 5(3.732-1.732)$ $\;d \approx 5 \times 2$ $\;d = 10 \text{ km}$ $\; \text{ speed } \; = \; \frac{d}{t} = \; \frac{10}{50} = 0.2 \text{ km / s} \; = 3600 \times 0.2 \text{ km / h} = 720 \text{ km / h}$ ⇒ the speed of the plane is $720 \text{ km / h}$ © examsnet.com

search_text: if the vector $\overline{i}-7\overline{j}+2\overline{k}$ is along the internal bisector of the angle between the vectors $\overline{a}$ and $-2\overline{i}-\overline{j}+2\overline{k}$ and the unit vector along $\overline{a}$ is $x\overline{i}+y\overline{j}+z\overline{k}$ then $x=$ [ap eapcet 22 may 2025 s2] {'a': '0', 'b': '$\\frac{7}{9}$', 'c': '$-\\frac{1}{9}$', 'd': '$\\frac{5}{3}$'} 2025 2025-05-22 shift_2 mathematics   29 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: magnitude of the vector $-2\hat{i}-\hat{j}+2\hat{k}$ $\rightarrow |b|=\sqrt{4+1+4}=\sqrt{9}=3$ $\rightarrow \text{unit vector} \hat{b} = \frac{-2\hat{i}}{3} - \frac{1}{3}\hat{j} + \frac{2}{3}\hat{k}$ now, let $c = \hat{i} - 7\hat{j} + 2\hat{k}$ $|c| = \sqrt{54} = 3\sqrt{6}$ $\hat{c} = \frac{1}{3\sqrt{6}}\hat{i} - \frac{7}{3\sqrt{6}}\hat{j} + \frac{2}{3\sqrt{6}}\hat{k}$ $\rightarrow c = a + b \rightarrow a = c - b$ $= \frac{(1+2\sqrt{6})\hat{i}}{3\sqrt{6}} + \frac{(-7+\sqrt{6})\hat{j}}{3\sqrt{6}} + \frac{(2-2\sqrt{6})\hat{k}}{3\sqrt{6}}$ compaire with $a = x\hat{i} + y\hat{j} + z\hat{k}$ $\rightarrow x = \frac{1+2\sqrt{6}}{3\sqrt{6}} = \frac{\sqrt{6}+12}{18} \cong \frac{7}{9}$ $\rightarrow x = \frac{7}{9}$ © examsnet.com

search_text: if $\overline{a}=2\overline{i}-\overline{j}+6\overline{k} ; \overline{b}=\overline{i}-\overline{j}+\overline{k}$ and $\overline{c}=3\overline{j}-\overline{k}$ , then $\overline{a} \times \overline{b}+\overline{b} \times \overline{c}+\overline{c} \times \overline{a}=$ [ap eapcet 22 may 2025 s2] {'a': '$20 \\overline{i}+3 \\overline{j}-4 \\overline{k}$', 'b': '$20 \\overline{i}-3 \\overline{j}+4 \\overline{k}$', 'c': '$3 \\overline{i}+20 \\overline{j}-4 \\overline{k}$', 'd': '$4 \\overline{i}+20 \\overline{j}-3 \\overline{k}$'} 2025 2025-05-22 shift_2 mathematics   30 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: $\;a =2 \hat{i}-\hat{j}+6 \hat{k}, b =\hat{i}-\hat{j}+\hat{k},$ $\;c =3 \hat{j}-\hat{k}$ $\;a \times b =\hat{ \begin{vmatrix} \hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k} \\ 2 & -1 & 6 \\ 1 & -1 & 1 \end{vmatrix} }$ $\;=\hat{i}(-1+6)-\hat{j}(2-6)+\hat{k}(-2+1)$ $\;=5 \hat{i}+4 \hat{j}-\hat{k}$ $\;b \times c =\hat{ \begin{vmatrix} i & \hat{j} & \hat{k} \\ 1 & -1 & 1 \\ 0 & 3 & -1 \end{vmatrix} }$ $\;=\hat{i}(1-3)-\hat{j}(-1-0)+\hat{k}(3-0)$ $\;=-2 \hat{i}+\hat{j}+3 \hat{k}$ $\;c \times a =\hat{ \begin{vmatrix} i & \hat{j} \\ 0 & 3 \\ k & -1 \\ 2 & -1 \\ 6 & \end{vmatrix} }$ $\;=\hat{i}(18-1)-\hat{j}(+2)+\hat{k}(-6)$ $\;=17 \hat{i}-2 \hat{j}-6 \hat{k}$ $\;a \times b + b \times c + c \times a$ $\;=5 \hat{i}+4 \hat{j}-\hat{k}+(-2 \hat{i}+\hat{j}+3 \hat{k})+17 \hat{i}-2 \hat{j}-6 \hat{k}$ $\;=20 \hat{i}+3 \hat{j}-4 \hat{k}$ © examsnet.com

question: Let $\overline{a}=2\overline{i}+\overline{j}-2\overline{k}$ and $\overline{b}=\overline{i}+\overline{j}$ be two vectors. If $\overline{c}$ is a vector such that $\overline{a} \cdot \overline{c}=|\overline{c}|,|\overline{c}-\overline{a}|=2\sqrt{2}$ and the angle between $\overline{a} \times \overline{b}$ and $\overline{c}$ is $30^{\circ}$ , then $|(\overline{a} \times \overline{b}) \times \overline{c}|=$ [AP EAPCET 22 May 2025 S2]

search_text: if the probability distribution of a discrete random variable x is given by $p(x=k)=\frac{2^{-k}(3k+1)}{2^{c}}, k=0,1,2,\dots\infty \text{ then } p(x\le c)=$ [ap eapcet 22 may 2025 s2] {'a': '$\\frac{c}{5}$', 'b': '$\\frac{c}{4}$', 'c': '$\\frac{c+2}{5}$', 'd': '$\\frac{c-2}{7}$'} 2025 2025-05-22 shift_2 mathematics   39 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: $\sum\limits_{k=0}^{\infty} p(x=k)=1$ $\rightarrow \sum\limits_{k=0}^{\infty} \frac{2^{-k}(3k+1)}{2^{c}}=1$ $\rightarrow \frac{1}{2^{c}} \left(3 \sum\limits_{k=0}^{\infty} k \cdot 2^{-k} + \sum\limits_{k=0}^{\infty} 2^{-k}\right)=1$ $\rightarrow \frac{1}{2^{c}} \left(3 \cdot \frac{2^{-1}}{(1-2^{-1})^{2}} + \frac{1}{1-2^{-1}}\right)=1$ $\rightarrow \frac{1}{2^{c}} \left( \frac{\frac{3}{2}}{\frac{1}{4}} + \frac{1}{\frac{1}{2}} \right)=1$ $\rightarrow \frac{1}{2^{c}}(6+2)=1 \rightarrow \frac{8}{2^{c}}=1$ $\rightarrow 2^{c}=8 \rightarrow 2^{c}=2^{3}$ $\rightarrow c=3$ $p(x\le c)=p(x\le 3)=p(x=0)+p(x=1)+p(x=2)+p(x=3)$ $=\frac{1}{2^{3}}+\frac{2^{-1} \times 4}{2^{3}}+\frac{2^{-2} \times 7}{2^{3}}+\frac{2^{-3} \times 10}{2^{3}}$ $=\frac{1}{2^{3}}+\frac{4}{2^{4}}+\frac{7}{2^{5}}+\frac{10}{2^{6}}$ $=\frac{2^{3}+16+14+10}{2^{6}}$ $=\frac{8+16+14+10}{2^{6}}=\frac{48}{64}=\frac{3}{4}$ $p(x\le c)=\frac{3}{4}=\frac{c}{4}$ © examsnet.com

search_text: in a binomial distribution, if $n=4$ and $p(x=0)=\;\frac{16}{81}$ , then $p(x=4)=$ [ap eapcet 22 may 2025 s2] {'a': '$\\;\\frac{1}{8}$', 'b': '$\\;\\frac{1}{27}$', 'c': '$\\;\\frac{1}{16}$', 'd': '$\\;\\frac{1}{81}$'} 2025 2025-05-22 shift_2 mathematics   40 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: we know that $n=4$ (there are 4 trials) and $p(x=0)=\;\frac{16}{81}$ (the chance of getting zero successes is $\;\frac{16}{81}$ ). in a binomial distribution, $p$ is the chance of success each time, and $q$ is the chance of failure. $q=1-p$ . the formula to find the probability of getting $k$ successes is: $p(x=k)={}^n c_k p^k q^{n-k}$ . step 1: find $q$ $p(x=0)={}^4 c_0 p^0 q^4$ ${}^4 c_0=1$ and $p^0=1$ , so: $p(x=0)=1 \cdot 1 \cdot q^4=q^4$ we know $q^4=\frac{16}{81}$ . to find $q$ , take the fourth root of both sides: $q=\;\frac{2}{3}$ because $(\;\frac{2}{3})^4=\;\frac{16}{81}$ . step 2: find $p$ since $q=\;\frac{2}{3}$ , $p=1-\frac{2}{3}=\frac{1}{3}$ . step 3: find $p(x=4)$ $p(x=4)$ is the probability of getting 4 successes out of 4 tries. $p(x=4)={}^4 c_4 p^4 q^0$ ${}^4 c_4=1$ and $q^0=1$ , so: $p(x=4)=1 \cdot \left(\;\frac{1}{3}\right)^4 \cdot 1= \left(\;\frac{1}{3}\right)^4$ calculate $\left(\;\frac{1}{3}\right)^4=\;\frac{1}{81}$ . © examsnet.com

question: The transformed equation of $3 x^2 - 4 x y = r^2$ when the coordinate axes are rotated about the origin through an angle of $\tan^{-1}(2)$ in positive direction is [AP EAPCET 22 May 2025 S2]
search_text: the transformed equation of $3 x^2 - 4 x y = r^2$ when the coordinate axes are rotated about the origin through an angle of $\tan^{-1}(2)$ in positive direction is [ap eapcet 22 may 2025 s2] {'a': '$x^2 - 4 y^2 = r^2$', 'b': '$2 x y + r^2 = 0$', 'c': '$4 y^2 - x^2 = r^2$', 'd': '$x y = r^2$'} 2025 2025-05-22 shift_2 mathematics   42 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: $\tan \theta = 2$ $\sin \theta = \frac{2}{\sqrt{5}}$ $\cos \theta = \frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}$ $x = x' \cos \theta - y' \sin \theta = \frac{x'}{\sqrt{5}} - \frac{2 y'}{\sqrt{5}}$ $y = x' \sin \theta + y' \cos \theta = \frac{2 x'}{\sqrt{5}} + \frac{y'}{\sqrt{5}}$ $\rightarrow 3 \left( \frac{x'}{\sqrt{5}} - \frac{2 y'}{\sqrt{5}} \right)^2 - 4 \left( \frac{x'}{\sqrt{5}} - \frac{2 y'}{\sqrt{5}} \right) \left( \frac{2 x'}{\sqrt{5}} + \frac{y'}{\sqrt{5}} \right) = r^2$ $\rightarrow \frac{3 x'^2 - 12 x' y' + 12 y'^2}{5} - \frac{8 x'^2 - 12 x' y' - 8 y'^2}{5} = r^2$ $\rightarrow -x'^2 + 4 y'^2 = r^2$ ⇒ the transformed equation is $4 y'^2 - x^2 = r^2$ $\rightarrow 4 y^2 - x^2 = r^2$ © examsnet.com

question: A line $L_1$ passing through the point of intersection of the lines $x-2y+3=0$ and $2x - y = 0$ is parallel to the Line $L_2$ . question: If $\int\; \frac{\cos^3 x}{\sin^2 x + \sin^4 x} dx = c - \csc x - f(x)$ , then $f \left( \frac{\pi}{2} \right) =$ [AP EAPCET 22 May 2025 S2]
search_text: if $\int\; \frac{\cos^3 x}{\sin^2 x + \sin^4 x} dx = c - \csc x - f(x)$ , then $f \left( \frac{\pi}{2} \right) =$ [ap eapcet 22 may 2025 s2] {'a': '$1$', 'b': '$0$', 'c': '$\\frac{\\pi}{2}$', 'd': '$\\pi$'} 2025 2025-05-22 shift_2 mathematics   71 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: $\;\int\; \frac{\cos^3 x}{\sin^2 x + \sin^4 x} dx$ $= \;\int\; \frac{\cos x (1 - \sin^2 x)}{\sin^2 x (1 + \sin^2 x)} dx$ put $u = \sin x$ $du = \cos x dx = \int\; \frac{1-u^2}{u^2 (1+u^2)} du$ $= \int \left( \frac{1}{u^2} - \frac{2}{1+u^2} \right) du$ $= -\frac{1}{u} - 2 \tan^{-1}(u) + c$ $= -\frac{1}{\sin x} - 2 \tan^{-1}(\sin x) + c$ $\rightarrow f(x) = 2 \tan^{-1}(\sin x)$ $\rightarrow f \left( \frac{\pi}{2} \right) = 2 \tan^{-1}(1) = 2 \times \frac{\pi}{4} = \frac{\pi}{2}$ © examsnet.com

search_text: $\int \sqrt{x^2+x+1}\,dx$ [ap eapcet 22 may 2025 s2] {'a': '$\\;\\frac{2x+1}{4}\\sqrt{x^2+x+1}+\\frac{3}{8}\\sinh^{-1}\\left(\\frac{2x+1}{\\sqrt{3}}\\right)+c$', 'b': '$\\;\\frac{x+1}{4}\\sqrt{x^2+x+1}+\\frac{3}{8}\\sinh^{-1}\\left(\\frac{2x+1}{\\sqrt{3}}\\right)+c$', 'c': '$\\;\\frac{x+1}{4}\\sqrt{x^2+x+1}-\\frac{3}{8}\\sinh^{-1}\\left(\\frac{2x+1}{\\sqrt{3}}\\right)+c$', 'd': '$\\;\\frac{2x+1}{4}\\sqrt{x^2+x+1}-\\frac{3}{8}\\sinh^{-1}\\left(\\frac{2x+1}{\\sqrt{3}}\\right)+c$'} 2025 2025-05-22 shift_2 mathematics   73 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: $\;\int \sqrt{x^2+x+1}\,dx$ $\;=\int\sqrt{x^2+x+\frac{1}{4}-\frac{1}{4}+1}\,dx$ $\;=\int\sqrt{\left(x+\frac{1}{2}\right)^2+\frac{3}{4}}\,dx$ $\;=\int\sqrt{\left(x+\frac{1}{2}\right)^2+\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)^2}\,dx$ $\;=\;\frac{x+\frac{1}{2}}{2}\sqrt{x^2+x+1}+\frac{3}{8}\ln\left|x+\frac{1}{2}+\sqrt{x^2+x+1}\right|+c$ $\;=\;\frac{2x+1}{4}\sqrt{x^2+x+1}+\frac{3}{8}\sin^{-1}\left(\frac{2x+1}{\sqrt{3}}\right)+c$ © examsnet.com

search_text: if $k \in n$ then $\lim\limits_{n \to \infty} \left[ \;\frac{1}{n+1} + \;\frac{1}{n+2} + \;\frac{1}{n+3} + \dots + \;\frac{1}{kn} \right] =$ [ap eapcet 22 may 2025 s2] {'a': '$\\log (k + 1)$', 'b': '$\\log k$', 'c': '$\\log (k + 5)$', 'd': '$\\log (k + 1) - \\log 6$'} 2025 2025-05-22 shift_2 mathematics   74 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: $\;\lim\limits_{n \to \infty} \left[ \;\frac{1}{n+1} + \;\frac{1}{n+2} + \;\frac{1}{n+3} + \dots + \;\frac{1}{k n} \right]$ $\;\sum\limits_{i=1}^{(k-1) n} \;\frac{1}{n+i}$ $\; \rightarrow \; \frac{1}{n} \sum\limits_{i=1}^{(k-1) n} \;\frac{1}{1+\;\frac{i}{n}} = \lim\limits_{n \to \infty} \;\frac{1}{n} \sum\limits_{i=1}^{(k-1) n} \;\frac{1}{1+\;\frac{i}{n}}$ $\; = \int\limits_{0}^{k-1} \;\frac{1}{1+x} \, dx = [\ln (1+x)]_0^{k-1}$ $\; = \ln k$ © examsnet.com

question: $\int\limits_{-1}^{4} \sqrt{\frac{4-x}{x+1}} dx =$ [AP EAPCET 22 May 2025 S2]
search_text: $\int\limits_{-1}^{4} \sqrt{\frac{4-x}{x+1}} dx =$ [ap eapcet 22 may 2025 s2] {'a': '$0$', 'b': '$\\frac{\\pi}{2}$', 'c': '$\\frac{3\\pi}{2}$', 'd': '$\\frac{5\\pi}{2}$'} 2025 2025-05-22 shift_2 mathematics   75 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: $\; \int\limits_{-1}^{4} \sqrt{\;\frac{4-x}{x+1}} dx$ $\; \; \text{ let } \; x = \frac{5}{2} \sin \;\theta + \frac{3}{2}$ $\; \rightarrow dx = \frac{5}{2} \cos \;\theta d \theta$ $\; \rightarrow 4 - x = 4 - \left( \frac{5}{2} \sin \;\theta + \frac{3}{2} \right)$ $\; = \frac{5}{2} (1 - \sin \;\theta)$ $\; \rightarrow x + 1 = \frac{5}{2} \sin \;\theta + \frac{3}{2} + 1 = \frac{5}{2} (1 + \sin \;\theta)$ $\; \rightarrow \; \; \frac{4-x}{x+1} = \frac{1 - \sin \;\theta}{1 + \sin \;\theta}$ $\; \rightarrow \; \; \sqrt{\;\frac{4-x}{x+1}} = \sqrt{\;\frac{1 - \sin \;\theta}{1 + \sin \;\theta}} = \frac{1 - \sin \;\theta}{\cos \theta}$ $\; \int \sqrt{\;\frac{4-x}{x+1}} dx = \int \frac{1 - \sin \;\theta}{\cos \theta} \;\frac{5}{2} \cos \theta d \theta$ $\; = \frac{5}{2} \int (1 - \sin \;\theta) d \theta$ $\; = \frac{5}{2} (\theta + \cos \theta) + c$ $\; x = \frac{5}{2} \sin \;\theta + \frac{3}{2} \rightarrow \sin \;\theta = \frac{2x - 3}{5}$ $\; \rightarrow \cos \theta = \sqrt{1 - \sin^2 \theta} = \frac{2}{5} \sqrt{4 + 3x - x^2}$ $\; \int\limits_{-1}^{4} \sqrt{\;\frac{4-x}{x+1}} dx = \left[ \frac{5}{2} \sin^{-1} \left( \frac{2x - 3}{5} \right) + \sqrt{4 + 3x - x^2} \right]_{-1}^{4}$ $\; \; = \frac{5}{2} \cdot \frac{\pi}{2} - \frac{5}{2} \left( \frac{-\pi}{2} \right)$ $\; \; = \frac{5\pi}{4} + \frac{5\pi}{4} = \frac{5\pi}{2}$ © examsnet.com

search_text: $\int\limits_{0}^{\pi/4} \;\frac{\cos^2 x}{\cos^2 x+4\sin^2 x} dx=$ [ap eapcet 22 may 2025 s2] {'a': '$\\frac{\\pi}{2}-\\;\\frac{1}{3} \\mathrm{tan}^{-1} 2$', 'b': '$-\\;\\frac{\\pi}{4}-\\;\\frac{4}{3} \\mathrm{tan}^{-1} 2$', 'c': '$\\;\\frac{\\pi}{6}+\\;\\frac{2}{3} \\mathrm{tan}^{-1} 2$', 'd': '$-\\;\\frac{\\pi}{12}+\\;\\frac{2}{3} \\mathrm{tan}^{-1} 2$'} 2025 2025-05-22 shift_2 mathematics   76 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: $\;\int\limits_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{4}} \;\frac{\cos^2 x\,dx}{\cos^2 x+4\sin^2 x}$ $\;\;\; =\int\limits_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{4}} \;\frac{1}{1+4\tan^2 x} dx$ put $u=2 \tan x$ $du\;=2 \sec^2 x dx$ $dx\;=\;\frac{du}{2(1+\tan^2 x)}=\;\frac{2 du}{4+u^2}$ $x\;=0, u=0$ $x\;=\;\frac{\pi}{4}, u=2$ $\;=\int\limits_{0}^{2} \;\frac{1}{1+u^2} \cdot \;\frac{2 du}{4+u^2}$ $\;=\int\limits_{0}^{2} \left(\;\frac{2}{3} \;\frac{1}{1+u^2}-\;\frac{2}{3} \;\frac{1}{4+u^2}\right) du$ $\;=\;\frac{2}{3} \left[\tan^{-1} u\right]_0^2-\;\frac{2}{3} \cdot \;\frac{1}{2} \left[\tan^{-1} \frac{u}{2}\right]_0^2$ $\;=\;\frac{2}{3} \tan^{-1}(2)-\;\frac{\pi}{12}$ © examsnet.com

question: $\int\limits_{5\pi}^{25\pi} \left| \sin 2x + \cos 2x \right| \, dx =$ [AP EAPCET 22 May 2025 S2]
search_text: $\int\limits_{5\pi}^{25\pi} \left| \sin 2x + \cos 2x \right| \, dx =$ [ap eapcet 22 may 2025 s2] {'a': '$20\\sqrt{2}$', 'b': '$10\\sqrt{2}$', 'c': '$40\\sqrt{2}$', 'd': '$80\\sqrt{2}$'} 2025 2025-05-22 shift_2 mathematics   77 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: $\int\limits_{5\pi}^{25\pi} \sin 2x + \cos 2x \, \vert \, dx$ $\rightarrow \left| \sin 2x + \cos 2x \right| = \sqrt{2} \left| \sin\left(2x + \frac{\pi}{4}\right) \right|$ $\rightarrow \int\limits_{5\pi}^{25\pi} \sin 2x + \cos 2x \, \vert \, dx$ $= \int\limits_{5\pi}^{25\pi} \sqrt{2} \left| \sin\left(2x + \frac{\pi}{4}\right) \right| \, dx$ let $u = 2x + \frac{\pi}{4}$ $du = 2 \, dx$ $dx = \frac{1}{2} \, du$ $x = 5\pi, \quad u = 10\pi + \frac{\pi}{4}$ $x = 25\pi, \quad u = 50\pi + \frac{\pi}{4}$ $= \sqrt{2} \int_{10\pi + \frac{\pi}{4}}^{50\pi + \frac{\pi}{4}} \left| \sin u \right| \cdot \frac{1}{2} \, du$ $= \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} \int_{10\pi + \frac{\pi}{4}}^{50\pi + \frac{\pi}{4}} \left| \sin u \right| \, du$ the period of $\left| \sin u \right|$ is $\pi$ . the length of the interval of integration is $= \left(50\pi + \frac{\pi}{4}\right) - \left(10\pi + \frac{\pi}{4}\right) = 40\pi$ $= \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} \cdot 40 \int\limits_{0}^{\pi} \left| \sin u \right| \, du$ $= \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} \times 40 \times 2$ $= 40\sqrt{2}$ © examsnet.com

search_text: the differential equation of the family of circles passing through the origin and having centre on $x$ -axis is [ap eapcet 22 may 2025 s2] {'a': '$(y^2+x^2) dx-2 y d y=0$', 'b': '$(y^2-x^2) dx-2 x y d y=0$', 'c': '$(y^2-x^2) dx+2 y d y=0$', 'd': '$(y^2+x^2) dx+2 y d y=0$'} 2025 2025-05-22 shift_2 mathematics   78 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: general equation of circle passing through the origin and having centres on the $x$ -axis. $\;x^2+y^2+2 g x=0$ $\rightarrow 2 x+2 y \;\frac{d y}{d x}+2 g=0$ $\rightarrow g=-x-y \;\frac{d y}{d x}$ $\rightarrow x^2+y^2+2 x \left(-x-y \;\frac{d y}{d x}\right) =0$ $\rightarrow x^2+y^2-2 x^2-2 x y \;\frac{d y}{d x}=0$ $\rightarrow -x^2+y^2-2 x y \;\frac{d y}{d x}=0$ $\rightarrow y^2-x^2=2 x y \;\frac{d y}{d x}$ $\rightarrow (y^2-x^2) dx-2 x y d y=0$ © examsnet.com

question: The general solution of the differential equation $\; \frac{dy}{dx} = \; \frac{x+y}{x-y}$ is [AP EAPCET 22 May 2025 S2]
search_text: the general solution of the differential equation $\; \frac{dy}{dx} = \; \frac{x+y}{x-y}$ is [ap eapcet 22 may 2025 s2] {'a': '$y-x=c x^2$', 'b': '$\\tan^{-1} \\left( \\frac{y}{x} \\right) = \\log \\left( c x \\sqrt{x^2+y^2} \\right)$', 'c': '$x+y=c x^2$', 'd': '$\\tan^{-1} \\left( \\frac{y}{x} \\right) = \\log \\left( c \\sqrt{x^2+y^2} \\right)$'} 2025 2025-05-22 shift_2 mathematics   79 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: $\;\; \frac{dy}{dx} = \; \frac{x+y}{x-y}$ $\rightarrow y=v x \rightarrow v=\; \frac{y}{x}$ $\rightarrow \;\; \frac{dy}{dx} = v + x \; \frac{dv}{dx}$ $\rightarrow v + x \; \frac{dv}{dx} = \; \frac{x+v x}{x-v x}$ $\rightarrow v + x \; \frac{dv}{dx} = \; \frac{1+v}{1-v}$ $\rightarrow x \; \frac{dv}{dx} = \; \frac{1+v}{1-v} - v$ $\rightarrow = \; \frac{1+v-v+v^2}{1-v}$ $\rightarrow x \; \frac{dv}{dx} = \; \frac{1+v^2}{1-v}$ $\rightarrow \; \frac{1-v}{1+v^2} dv = \; \frac{1}{x} dx$ integrating both sides, we get $\;\rightarrow \;\; \int \frac{1-v}{1+v^2} dv = \int \frac{1}{x} dx$ $\;\rightarrow \;\; \log x = \int \frac{1}{1+v^2} dv - \int \frac{v}{1+v^2} dv$ $\;\rightarrow \;\; \log x = \tan^{-1} v - \frac{1}{2} \int \frac{1}{t} dt$ where, $1+v^2=t$ $2 v dv = dt$ $\; v dv = \; \frac{1}{2} dt$ $\;\rightarrow \log x = \tan^{-1} v - \frac{1}{2} \log |1+v^2| + c$ $\;\rightarrow \log x = \tan^{-1} \frac{y}{x} - \frac{1}{2} \log \left| 1+\frac{y^2}{x^2} \right| + c$ $\;\rightarrow \log x = \tan^{-1} \frac{y}{x} - \frac{1}{2} \log \left| \frac{y^2+x^2}{x^2} \right| + c$ $\;\rightarrow \tan^{-1} \left( \frac{y}{x} \right) = \log \left( c \sqrt{x^2+y^2} \right)$ © examsnet.com

search_text: the general solution of the differential equation $\;\frac{dy}{dx}+\;\frac{\sec x}{\cos x+\sin x} y=\;\frac{\cos x}{1+\tan x}$ is [ap eapcet 22 may 2025 s2] {'a': '$(\\cos x+\\sin x) y = \\sin x + c$', 'b': '$(\\cos x+\\sin x) y = \\cos x + c$', 'c': '$(1+\\tan x) y = \\cos x + c$', 'd': '$\\sec x (\\cos x+\\sin x) y = \\sin x + c$'} 2025 2025-05-22 shift_2 mathematics   80 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: $\;\;\frac{dy}{dx}+\;\frac{\sec x}{\cos x+\sin x} y=\;\frac{\cos x}{1+\tan x}$ $\;\text{if} = e^{\int\;\frac{\sec x}{\cos x+\sin x}dx} = e^{\int\;\frac{\sec^2 x}{1+\tan x}dx}$ $\;= e^{\log(1+\tan x)} = 1+\tan x$ $\; \rightarrow y \cdot (1+\tan x)$ $\;= \int (1+\tan x) \cdot \;\frac{\cos x}{1+\tan x} dx$ $\;= \int \cos x dx$ $\;= \sin x + c$ $\; \rightarrow \sec x (\cos x+\sin x) y = \sin x + c$ © examsnet.com

question: The number of significant figures in the simplification of $\;\frac{0.501}{0.05}(0.312-0.03)$ is [AP EAPCET 22 May 2025 S2]
search_text: the number of significant figures in the simplification of $\;\frac{0.501}{0.05}(0.312-0.03)$ is [ap eapcet 22 may 2025 s2] {'a': '1', 'b': '3', 'c': '2', 'd': '5'} 2025 2025-05-22 shift_2 physics   81 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: evaluate the subtraction: $0.312-0.03=0.282$ . in addition/subtraction, the result is limited by the least number of decimal places. here $0.03$ has $2$ decimal places, so the result is rounded to $0.28$ , which has $2$ significant figures. for the division: $\frac{0.501}{0.05}=10.02$ . in multiplication/division, the result is limited by the least number of significant figures. the number $0.05$ has only $1$ significant figure, so the division result must be limited to $1$ significant figure. now the overall expression becomes $\frac{0.501}{0.05}(0.312-0.03)=10.02\times0.282=2.82564$ . the least number of significant figures among the given quantities is $1$ (from $0.05$ ). rounding $2.82564$ to $1$ significant figure gives $3$ . thus the simplified value has $1$ significant figure. hence the correct option is $1$ . © examsnet.com

search_text: if the magnitude of a vector $\vec{p}$ is 25 units and its y -component is 7 units, then its x -component is [ap eapcet 22 may 2025 s2] {'a': '24 units', 'b': '18 units', 'c': '32 units', 'd': '16 units'} 2025 2025-05-22 shift_2 physics   83 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: $p = |p| = 25 \text{ units}$ $p_y = 7$ $\text{ since, } \sqrt{p_x^2 + p_y^2} = p$ $\rightarrow p_x^2 + p_y^2 = p^2$ $\rightarrow p_x^2 + 7^2 = 25^2$ $\rightarrow p_x = \sqrt{25^2 - 7^2}$ $= \sqrt{625 - 49}$ $= \sqrt{576} = 24 \text{ units}$ © examsnet.com

search_text: the height of ceiling in an auditorium is 30 m . a ball is thrown with a speed of $30  \mathrm{m}  \mathrm{s}^{-1}$ from the entrance such that it just moves very near to the ceiling without touching it and then it reaches the ground at the end of the auditorium. then the length of auditorium is [acceleration due to gravity $=10  \mathrm{m}  \mathrm{s}^{-2}$ ] [ap eapcet 22 may 2025 s2] {'a': '$60 \\sqrt{2} \\mathrm{m}$', 'b': '$30 \\sqrt{2} \\mathrm{m}$', 'c': '$70 \\sqrt{2} \\mathrm{m}$', 'd': '$100 \\sqrt{2} \\mathrm{m}$'} 2025 2025-05-22 shift_2 physics   84 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: height of auditorium is 30 m and ball just reaches to this height so this is the maximum height of projectile. let angle of projection is $\theta$ . $\;\;\text{ so, }\; h_{max}=30=\;\frac{u^2 \sin^2\theta}{2g}$ $\;\;\;\;\;   30\;=\;\frac{(30)^2 \sin^2\theta}{2 \times 10}$ $\sin^2\theta\;=\;\frac{600}{900}=\;\frac{2}{3}$ $\;\rightarrow  \sin\theta=\sqrt{\;\frac{2}{3}}$ $\;\;\text{ and }\; \cos\theta=\;\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$ now, length of auditorium will be equal to range of projectile. $\;\text{ so, }\;\;r=\frac{u^2 \sin 2\theta}{g}$ $\;=\;\frac{u^2 (2 \sin\theta \cos\theta)}{g}$ $r\;=\;\frac{(30)^2 \times 2 \times \sqrt{\frac{2}{3}} \times \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}}{0.10}$ $r\;=\;\frac{1800 \sqrt{2}}{30}$ $\;=60 \sqrt{2} \mathrm{m}$ © examsnet.com

search_text: a balloon with mass ' $m$ ' is descending vertically with an acceleration ' $a$ ' (where $a < g$ ). the mass to be removed from the balloon, so that it starts moving vertically up with an acceleration 'a' is [ap eapcet 22 may 2025 s2] {'a': '$\\frac{ma}{g+a}$', 'b': '$\\frac{ma}{g-a}$', 'c': '$\\frac{2ma}{g+a}$', 'd': '$\\frac{2ma}{g-a}$'} 2025 2025-05-22 shift_2 physics   85 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: when the balloon is descending, the net force acting on it is given by $f_{\text{net}} = mg - b = ma$ , where $b$ is the buoyant force. thus, $b = mg - ma$ for the balloon to move upwards with the same acceleration $a$ , a mass $\delta m$ must be removed. the new net force equation becomes $b - (m-\delta m)g = (m-\delta m)a$ $mg - ma - (m-\delta m)g = (m-\delta m)a \quad [\text{from eq. (i)}]$ $\rightarrow \quad \delta m = \frac{2ma}{g+a}$ © examsnet.com

search_text: a conveyor belt is moving horizontally with a velocity of $2 \mathrm{m}\,\mathrm{s}^{-1}$ . if a body of mass 10 kg is kept on it, then the distance travelled by the body before coming to rest is (the coefficient of kinetic friction between the belt and the body is 0.2 and acceleration due to gravity is $10 \mathrm{m}\,\mathrm{s}^{-2}$ ) [ap eapcet 22 may 2025 s2] {'a': '$4 \\mathrm{m}$', 'b': '$0 \\mathrm{m}$', 'c': '$1 \\mathrm{m}$', 'd': '$2 \\mathrm{m}$'} 2025 2025-05-22 shift_2 physics   86 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: frictional force $f_s\; = \mu m g = 0.2 \times 10 \times 10$ $\rightarrow \;\; f_s\; = 20 \mathrm{n}$ ∴ deceleration, $a = \frac{f_s}{m}$ $= \frac{20}{10} = 2 \mathrm{m/s^2}$ using, $v^2 = u^2 + 2 a s$ $\rightarrow \;\; s = \frac{v^2-u^2}{2a}$ $= \frac{0^2-2^2}{2 \times (-2)} = 1 \mathrm{m}$ © examsnet.com

question: Two bodies A and B of masses 20 kg and 5 kg respectively are at rest. Due to the action of a force of 40 N separately, if the two bodies acquire equal kinetic energies in times $t_A$ and $t_B$ respectively, then $t_A: t_B=$ [AP EAPCET 22 May 2025 S2]
search_text: two bodies a and b of masses 20 kg and 5 kg respectively are at rest. due to the action of a force of 40 n separately, if the two bodies acquire equal kinetic energies in times $t_a$ and $t_b$ respectively, then $t_a: t_b=$ [ap eapcet 22 may 2025 s2] {'a': '$1: 2$', 'b': '$2: 1$', 'c': '$2: 5$', 'd': '$5: 6$'} 2025 2025-05-22 shift_2 physics   87 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: let's use the work-energy theorem, which says: $k\;=w$ $\rightarrow \;\; k\;=f \times s \;\; \ldots (i)$ here, $k$ is kinetic energy, $f$ is force, and $s$ is distance. when a force acts and the body starts from rest, the distance $s$ covered in time $t$ is: $s = \frac{1}{2} a t^2$ since acceleration $a = \frac{f}{m}$ (where $m$ is mass), we get: $s = \frac{1}{2} \times \frac{f}{m} \times t^2$ now, substitute $s$ from (ii) into our equation (i): $k = f \times \frac{1}{2} \times \frac{f}{m} \times t^2$ so, $k = \frac{f^2}{2 m} t^2$ we are told both bodies $a$ and $b$ get the same kinetic energy ( $k_a = k_b$ ) using the same force $f = 40\,\mathrm{n}$ , but their masses and times are different. set up the equation for both bodies and compare: $\frac{f^2}{2 m_a} t_a^2 = \frac{f^2}{2 m_b} t_b^2$ you can cancel out $f^2$ and $\frac{1}{2}$ because they are the same: $\frac{t_a^2}{m_a} = \frac{t_b^2}{m_b}$ rearrange to solve for time ratio: $\frac{t_a^2}{t_b^2} = \frac{m_a}{m_b}$ take the square root for the ratio $t_a: t_b$ : $\frac{t_a}{t_b} = \sqrt{\frac{m_a}{m_b}}$ plug in $m_a = 20\,\mathrm{kg}$ and $m_b = 5\,\mathrm{kg}$ : $\frac{t_a}{t_b} = \sqrt{\frac{20}{5}} = \sqrt{4} = 2$ so, the ratio $t_a: t_b = 2: 1$ . © examsnet.com

search_text: two satellites $a$ and $b$ are revolving around the earth in orbits of heights $1.25 r_e$ and $19.25 r_e$ from the surface of earth respectively, where $r_e$ is the radius of the earth. the ratio of the orbital speeds of the satellites $a$ and $b$ is [ap eapcet 22 may 2025 s2] {'a': '$5: 1$', 'b': '$4: 1$', 'c': '$9: 1$', 'd': '$3: 1$'} 2025 2025-05-22 shift_2 physics   93 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: height of satellite $a$ above earth's surface: $h_a=1.25 r_e$ height of satellite $b$ above earth's surface: $h_b=19.25 r_e$ hence, the orbital radii (distance from earth's center): $\; r_a=r_e+h_a=r_e+1.25 r_e=2.25 r_e$ $\; r_b=r_e+h_b=r_e+19.25 r_e=20.25 r_e$ formula for orbital speed for a satellite in a circular orbit around earth: $v=\sqrt{\frac{g m_e}{r}}$ where $g$ is the gravitational constant and $m_e$ is earth's mass. thus, for two satellites $a$ and $b$ : $\frac{v_a}{v_b}=\sqrt{\frac{r_b}{r_a}}$ substitute $r_a$ and $r_b$ $\frac{v_a}{v_b}=\sqrt{\frac{20.25 r_e}{2.25 r_e}}=\sqrt{\frac{20.25}{2.25}}=\sqrt{9}=3$ therefore, $v_a : v_b = 3 : 1$ © examsnet.com

question: When a stretched wire of fundamental frequency fis divided into three segments, the fundamental frequencies of these three segments are $f_1, f_2$ and $f_3$ respectively. Then the relation among $f_1, f_2, f_3$ and f is (Assume tension is constant) [AP EAPCET 22 May 2025 S2]
search_text: when a stretched wire of fundamental frequency fis divided into three segments, the fundamental frequencies of these three segments are $f_1, f_2$ and $f_3$ respectively. then the relation among $f_1, f_2, f_3$ and f is (assume tension is constant) [ap eapcet 22 may 2025 s2] {'a': '$\\sqrt{f} = \\sqrt{f_1} + \\sqrt{f_2} + \\sqrt{f_3}$', 'b': '$f = f_1 + f_2 + f_3$', 'c': '$\\frac{1}{f} = \\frac{1}{f_1} + \\frac{1}{f_2} + \\frac{1}{f_3}$', 'd': '$\\frac{1}{\\sqrt{f}} = \\frac{1}{\\sqrt{f_1}} + \\frac{1}{\\sqrt{f_2}} + \\frac{1}{\\sqrt{f_3}}$'} 2025 2025-05-22 shift_2 physics   101 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: a stretched wire has a fundamental frequency $f$ . when it is divided into $3$ segments, their fundamental frequencies are $f_1, f_2$ , and $f_3$ . tension $t$ is constant. we need to find the relation among $f, f_1, f_2, f_3$ . step 1: formula for fundamental frequency of a stretched string for a string under tension $t$ , length $l$ , and linear density $\mu$ : $f = \frac{1}{2l} \sqrt{\frac{t}{\mu}}$ step 2: frequencies of the three parts suppose the original length is divided into three parts of lengths $l_1, l_2, l_3$ , so that $l = l_1 + l_2 + l_3$ then their fundamental frequencies are $f_1 = \frac{1}{2l_1} \sqrt{\frac{t}{\mu}}, \quad f_2 = \frac{1}{2l_2} \sqrt{\frac{t}{\mu}}, \quad f_3 = \frac{1}{2l_3} \sqrt{\frac{t}{\mu}}$ step 3: express $l_i$ in terms of $f_i$ from the above, $l_i = \frac{1}{2 f_i} \sqrt{\frac{t}{\mu}}$ and $l = \frac{1}{2 f} \sqrt{\frac{t}{\mu}}$ step 4: use $l = l_1 + l_2 + l_3$ $\frac{1}{2f} \sqrt{\frac{t}{\mu}} = \frac{1}{2} \sqrt{\frac{t}{\mu}} \left( \frac{1}{f_1} + \frac{1}{f_2} + \frac{1}{f_3} \right)$ cancel the common factor $\frac{1}{2} \sqrt{\frac{t}{\mu}}$ : $\frac{1}{f} = \frac{1}{f_1} + \frac{1}{f_2} + \frac{1}{f_3}$ © examsnet.com

search_text: images of same size are formed by a convex lens when an object is placed either at 20 cm or 10 cm distance from the lens. the focal length of the lens is [ap eapcet 22 may 2025 s2] {'a': '12 cm', 'b': '40 cm', 'c': '18 cm', 'd': '15 cm'} 2025 2025-05-22 shift_2 physics   102 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: magnification of a lens is given as $m=\;\frac{v}{u}$ from lens formula $\;\frac{1}{v}\;-\;\frac{1}{u}=\;\frac{1}{f}$ $\;\frac{1}{v}\;=\;\frac{f+u}{f u}$ $\rightarrow \;\; \;\frac{u}{v}\;=\;\frac{f+u}{f}$ and $m=\;\frac{v}{u}=\;\frac{f}{f+u}$ now, magnification in both case is equal. so, $m_1=-m_2$ $\;\frac{f}{f-20}\;=\;\frac{-f}{f-10}$ $f-20\;=-f+10$ $2 f\;=30 \rightarrow f=15\ \text{cm}$ © examsnet.com

search_text: the length and area of cross-section of a copper wire are respectively 30 m and $6 \times 10^{-7} \text{m}^2$ . if the resistivity of copper is $1.7 \times 10^{-8} \omega \text{m}$ , then the resistance of the wire is [ap eapcet 22 may 2025 s2] {'a': '$0.51 \\omega$', 'b': '$0.68 \\omega$', 'c': '$0.85 \\omega$', 'd': '$0.75 \\omega$'} 2025 2025-05-22 shift_2 physics   107 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: length $l=30 \text{m}$ area of cross-section $a=6 \times 10^{-7} \text{m}^2$ resistivity $\rho=1.7 \times 10^{-8} \omega \text{m}$ formula: $r=\rho \frac{l}{a}$ substitution: $r=(1.7 \times 10^{-8}) \times \frac{30}{6 \times 10^{-7}}$ simplify: $\frac{30}{6 \times 10^{-7}}=5 \times 10^7$ so, $r=1.7 \times 10^{-8} \times 5 \times 10^7$ $r=(1.7 \times 5) \times 10^{-1}$ $r=8.5 \times 10^{-1}=0.85 \omega$ © examsnet.com

question: If current of 80 A is passing through a straight conductor of length 10 m , then the total momentum of electrons in the conductor is (mass of electron $=9.1 \times 10^{-31}  \text{kg}$ and charge of electron $=1.6 \times 10^{-19}  \text{C}$ ) [AP EAPCET 22 May 2025 S2]
search_text: if current of 80 a is passing through a straight conductor of length 10 m , then the total momentum of electrons in the conductor is (mass of electron $=9.1 \times 10^{-31}  \text{kg}$ and charge of electron $=1.6 \times 10^{-19}  \text{c}$ ) [ap eapcet 22 may 2025 s2] {'a': '$910 \\times 10^{-9}  \\text{ns}$', 'b': '$910 \\times 10^{-11}  \\text{ns}$', 'c': '$455 \\times 10^{-9}  \\text{ns}$', 'd': '$455 \\times 10^{-11}  \\text{ns}$'} 2025 2025-05-22 shift_2 physics   108 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: the current $i=80 \text{a}$ , and the length of the conductor $l=10 \text{m}$ . expression for current: current can be written as $i=n e a v_d$ , where $n$ is the number of electrons per unit volume, $e$ is the charge of an electron, $a$ is the cross-sectional area, and $v_d$ is the drift velocity of electrons. total number of electrons: let $n$ be the total number of free electrons in the length $l$ of the conductor. $n=n a l$ . total momentum: the total momentum of all free electrons is $p_{\text{total}} = n (m_e v_d)$ , where $m_e$ is the mass of an electron. substitute $n$ : so, $p_{\text{total}} = (n a l) (m_e v_d)$ . rewrite with current expression: since $i=n e a v_d$ , we can replace $n a v_d$ with $\frac{i}{e}$ . therefore, $p_{\text{total}} = \frac{i}{e} l m_e$ . simplified formula: so, $p_{\text{total}} = i \frac{l m_e}{e}$ . plug in the values: $p_{\text{total}} = 80 \times \frac{10 \times 9.1 \times 10^{-31}}{1.6 \times 10^{-19}}$ first, multiply $80 \times 10 = 800$ . now $800 \times 9.1 = 7280$ . so, numerator is $7280 \times 10^{-31}$ and denominator is $1.6 \times 10^{-19}$ . divide 7280 by 1.6 to get 4550 . power of ten: $\frac{10^{-31}}{10^{-19}} = 10^{-12}$ final answer: $p_{\text{total}} = 4550 \times 10^{-12} \text{n-s} = 4.55 \times 10^{-9} \text{n-s} = 455 \times 10^{-11} \text{n-s}$ © examsnet.com

question: The magnetic field at the centre of a current carrying circular coil of radius $R$ is $B_c$ and the magnetic field at a point on its axis at a distance $R$ from its centre is $B_a$ . The value of $\;\frac{B_c}{B_a}$ is [AP EAPCET 22 May 2025 S2]
search_text: the magnetic field at the centre of a current carrying circular coil of radius $r$ is $b_c$ and the magnetic field at a point on its axis at a distance $r$ from its centre is $b_a$ . the value of $\;\frac{b_c}{b_a}$ is [ap eapcet 22 may 2025 s2] {'a': '$\\sqrt{2}$', 'b': '$\\;\\frac{1}{2 \\sqrt{2}}$', 'c': '$2 \\sqrt{2}$', 'd': '$\\;\\frac{1}{\\sqrt{2}}$'} 2025 2025-05-22 shift_2 physics   110 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: $b_a=\;\frac{\mu_0 i r^2}{2 (r^2+a^2)^{\frac{3}{2}}}$ here, $a=r$ $\; \therefore   \;\;  b_a=\;\frac{\mu_0 i r^2}{2 (r^2+r^2)^{\frac{3}{2}}}=\;\frac{\mu_0 i}{4 \sqrt{2} r}$ $\;=\;\frac{\mu_0 i}{2 r} \cdot \;\frac{1}{2 \sqrt{2}}$ $\;\rightarrow b_a=\;\frac{b_c}{2 \sqrt{2}} \left[ \because  b_c=\;\frac{\mu_0 i}{2 r}\right]$ $\;\rightarrow \;\frac{b_c}{b_a}=2 \sqrt{2}$ © examsnet.com

question: A short bar magnet of magnetic moment $10^4 \mathrm{J} \mathrm{T}^{-1}$ is free to rotate in a horizontal plane. The work done in rotating the magnet slowly from the direction parallel to a horizontal magnetic field of $4 \times 10^{-5} \mathrm{T}$ to a direction $60^{\circ}$ to the direction of the field is [AP EAPCET 22 May 2025 S2]
search_text: a short bar magnet of magnetic moment $10^4 \mathrm{j} \mathrm{t}^{-1}$ is free to rotate in a horizontal plane. the work done in rotating the magnet slowly from the direction parallel to a horizontal magnetic field of $4 \times 10^{-5} \mathrm{t}$ to a direction $60^{\circ}$ to the direction of the field is [ap eapcet 22 may 2025 s2] {'a': '$0.2 \\mathrm{j}$', 'b': '$2.6 \\mathrm{j}$', 'c': '$0.4 \\mathrm{j}$', 'd': '$6.2 \\mathrm{j}$'} 2025 2025-05-22 shift_2 physics   111 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: magnetic moment of the bar magnet: $m = 10^4 j t^{-1}$ magnetic field: $b = 4 \times 10^{-5} t$ initial orientation: $\theta_1 = 0^{\circ}$ (parallel to $b$ ) final orientation: $\theta_2 = 60^{\circ}$ relevant concept the potential energy of a magnetic dipole in a magnetic field is $u = -m b \cos \theta$ when the magnet is rotated slowly (quasi-statically), the work done by an external agent equals the change in potential energy of the system: $w = u_2 - u_1 = \left[ -m b \cos \theta_2 \right] - \left[ -m b \cos \theta_1 \right]$ $w = m b (\cos \theta_1 - \cos \theta_2)$ substitute the values $w = (10^4) (4 \times 10^{-5}) (\cos 0^{\circ} - \cos 60^{\circ})$ compute step by step: $\cos 0^{\circ} = 1, \quad \cos 60^{\circ} = \frac{1}{2}$ so, $w = (10^4) (4 \times 10^{-5}) (1-0.5)$ $w = (10^4) (4 \times 10^{-5}) (0.5)$ $w = (10^4 \times 4 \times 10^{-5} \times 0.5)$ $w = (4 \times 10^{-1} \times 0.5) = 0.2 \mathrm{j}$ © examsnet.com

search_text: a resistor of $450\ \omega$ and an inductor are connected in series to an ac source of frequency $\;\frac{75}{\pi}\ \mathrm{hz}$ . if the power factor of the circuit is 0.6 , then the inductance connected in the circuit is [ap eapcet 22 may 2025 s2] {'a': '$6\\ \\mathrm{mh}$', 'b': '$4\\ \\mathrm{h}$', 'c': '$4\\ \\mathrm{mh}$', 'd': '$6\\ \\mathrm{h}$'} 2025 2025-05-22 shift_2 physics   113 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: power factor $\cos \phi\;=\;\frac{r}{z}$ $0.6\;=\;\frac{r}{\sqrt{r^2+x_l^2}}$ $\rightarrow\;\;0.36\;=\;\frac{r^2}{r^2+(2\pi f l)^2}$ $\rightarrow\;\;0.36\;=\;\frac{(450)^2}{(450)^2+\left(2\pi\times\frac{75}{\pi}l\right)^2}$ $\rightarrow\;\;0.36\;=\;\frac{(450)^2}{450^2+(150l)^2}$ solving, we get $l=4\ \mathrm{h}$ © examsnet.com

search_text: if the threshold wavelength of light for photoelectric emission to take place from a metal surface is $6250 \text{\aa}$ , then the work function of the metal is (planck's constant $=6.6 \times 10^{-34} \text{j s}$ ) [ap eapcet 22 may 2025 s2] {'a': '$3.98 \\text{ev}$', 'b': '$1.98 \\text{ev}$', 'c': '$2.98 \\text{ev}$', 'd': '$4.98 \\text{ev}$'} 2025 2025-05-22 shift_2 physics   115 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: threshold wavelength, $\lambda_0=6250 \text{\aa}=6250 \times 10^{-10} \text{m}=6.25 \times 10^{-7} \text{m}$ planck's constant, $h=6.6 \times 10^{-34} \text{j} \cdot \text{s}$ speed of light, $c=3 \times 10^8 \text{m/s}$ formula: work function $\phi = \frac{h c}{\lambda_0}$ calculation: $\; \phi = \frac{6.6 \times 10^{-34} \times 3 \times 10^8}{6.25 \times 10^{-7}}$ $\; \phi = \frac{19.8 \times 10^{-26}}{6.25 \times 10^{-7}} = 3.168 \times 10^{-19} \text{j}$ converting to ev: $\; 1 \text{ev} = 1.6 \times 10^{-19} \text{j}$ $\; \phi = \frac{3.168 \times 10^{-19}}{1.6 \times 10^{-19}} = 1.98 \text{ev}$ © examsnet.com

question: The ratio of the wavelengths of the first Lyman line and the second Balmer line of hydrogen atom is [AP EAPCET 22 May 2025 S2]
search_text: the ratio of the wavelengths of the first lyman line and the second balmer line of hydrogen atom is [ap eapcet 22 may 2025 s2] {'a': '$3 : 4$', 'b': '$1 : 4$', 'c': '$2 : 3$', 'd': '$1 : 3$'} 2025 2025-05-22 shift_2 physics   116 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: the formula for wavelength is: $\frac{1}{\lambda} = r \left( \frac{1}{n_1^2} - \frac{1}{n_2^2} \right)$ first line of lyman series: for lyman series, $n_1 = 1$ . the first line means $n_2 = 2$ . $\frac{1}{\lambda_l} = r \left( \frac{1}{1^2} - \frac{1}{2^2} \right) = r \left( 1 - \frac{1}{4} \right) = r \left( \frac{3}{4} \right) = \frac{3r}{4}$ so, $\lambda_l = \frac{4}{3r}$ second line of balmer series: for balmer series, $n_1 = 2$ . the second line means $n_2 = 4$ . $\frac{1}{\lambda_b} = r \left( \frac{1}{2^2} - \frac{1}{4^2} \right) = r \left( \frac{1}{4} - \frac{1}{16} \right) = r \left( \frac{3}{16} \right) = \frac{3r}{16}$ so, $\lambda_b = \frac{16}{3r}$ find the ratio: now, find $\frac{\lambda_l}{\lambda_b}$ : $\frac{\lambda_l}{\lambda_b} = \frac{\frac{4}{3r}}{\frac{16}{3r}} = \frac{4}{16} = \frac{1}{4}$ this means $\lambda_l : \lambda_b = 1 : 4$ © examsnet.com

search_text: each nuclear fission of ${}^{235}\mathrm{u}$ releases 200 mev of energy. if a reactor generates 1 mw power, then the rate of fission in the reactor is [ap eapcet 22 may 2025 s2] {'a': '$3.125 \\times 10^6$', 'b': '$3.125 \\times 10^8$', 'c': '$3.125 \\times 10^{10}$', 'd': '$3.125 \\times 10^{16}$'} 2025 2025-05-22 shift_2 physics   117 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: $\;\; \text{ energy per fission }\; = 200 \mathrm{mev}$ $\;\; =200 \times 1.6 \times 10^{-13} \;\text{ joule }\;$ $\;e=3.2 \times 10^{11} \mathrm{j}$ power of reactor $p=1 \mathrm{mw}$ so, number of fissions in time $t$ $n=\;\frac{p t}{e}$ so, number of fissions per second $\;\frac{n}{t}\;=\;\frac{p}{e}=\;\frac{10^6}{3.2 \times 10^{11}}$ $\;\simeq 3.125 \times 10^{16}$ rate of fission $=3.125 \times 10^6$ per second © examsnet.com

search_text: for transmitting a signal of frequency 1000 khz , the minimum length of the antenna is [ap eapcet 22 may 2025 s2] {'a': '$30\\,\\text{m}$', 'b': '$50\\,\\text{m}$', 'c': '$75\\,\\text{m}$', 'd': '$1500\\,\\text{m}$'} 2025 2025-05-22 shift_2 physics   120 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: $f=1000\,\text{khz}=1\times10^6\,\text{hz}$ speed of electromagnetic wave in free space, $c=3\times10^8\,\text{m/s}$ step 2: find the wavelength $\lambda=\frac{c}{f}=\frac{3\times10^8}{1\times10^6}=300\,\text{m}$ step 3: relation between antenna length and wavelength for efficient radiation, the minimum antenna length (usually a quarter-wave antenna) is: $l=\frac{\lambda}{4}$ step 4: calculate $l$ $l=\frac{300}{4}=75\,\text{m}$ © examsnet.com

search_text: the difference between the radii of $3^{\text{rd}}$ and $2^{\text{nd}}$ orbit of h-atom is $x \pm$ . the difference between the radii of $4^{\text{th}}$ and $3^{\text{rd}}$ orbit of $\mathrm{li}^{2+}$ ion is $y \pm y: x$ is equal to [ap eapcet 22 may 2025 s2] {'a': '$15:7$', 'b': '$7:15$', 'c': '$3:1$', 'd': '$1:3$'} 2025 2025-05-22 shift_2 chemistry   121 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: the radii of $n$ th orbit of hydrogen atom, $r_n = \frac{a_0 n^2}{z}$ for hydrogen atom the radii of 3 rd and 2 nd obit respectively can be calculated as $r_3 = \frac{a_0 3^2}{1} = 9 a_0 \quad (z=1)$ $r_2 = \frac{a_0 2^2}{1} = 4 a_0$ $x = r_3 - r_2 = 9 a_0 - 4 a_0 = 5 a_0$ for $\mathrm{li}^{2+}$ ion, the radii of 3rd and 4th orbit respectively can be calculated as $r_4 = a_0 \frac{4^2}{3} = \frac{16 a_0}{3} \quad (z=3)$ $r_3 = a_0 \frac{3^2}{3} = 3 a_0$ $y = r_4 - r_3 = \frac{7 a_0}{3}$ $y: x = \frac{7 a_0}{3} \times \frac{1}{5 a_0} = 7:15$ © examsnet.com

search_text: the de broglie wavelength of an electron in the third bohr orbit of h -atom is [ap eapcet 22 may 2025 s2] {'a': '$3 \\pi \\times 5.29 \\pm$', 'b': '$4 \\pi \\times 52.9 \\pm$', 'c': '$6 \\pi \\times 52.9 \\pm$', 'd': '$2 \\pi \\times 5.29 \\pm$'} 2025 2025-05-22 shift_2 chemistry   122 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: radius of $n$ th orbit of h-atom. $\; r_n = r_0 \times n^2$ $\; r_3 = 3^2 \times 52.9 \text{ pm}$ using bohr's postulate of angular momentum $m v r = \frac{n h}{2 \pi} \rightarrow m v = \frac{3 h}{2 \pi r}$ according to de-broglie $\lambda = \frac{h}{m v} = \frac{h}{\frac{3h}{2\pi r}} = \frac{2\pi r}{3}$ $\rightarrow \lambda = \frac{2 \pi \times 3^2 \times 52.9}{3}$ $\rightarrow \lambda = 6 \pi \times 52.9 \text{ pm}$ © examsnet.com

search_text: the pair of molecules / ions with the same bond order value is [ap eapcet 22 may 2025 s2] {'a': '$\\mathrm{b}_2, \\mathrm{c}_2$', 'b': '$\\mathrm{o}_2, \\mathrm{c}_2$', 'c': '$\\mathrm{o}_2^{+}, \\mathrm{o}_2^{-}$', 'd': '$\\mathrm{h}_2^{+}, \\mathrm{li}_2$'} 2025 2025-05-22 shift_2 chemistry   125 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: the pair of molecules that have the same bond order are $\mathrm{o}_2$ and $\mathrm{c}_2$ . bond order shows how many chemical bonds are between two atoms. to find bond order, use this formula: $\text{ bond order } = \frac{\text{ number of bonding electrons } - \text{ number of antibonding electrons }}{2}$ for $\mathrm{o}_2$ : number of bonding electrons $=10$ , number of antibonding electrons $=6$ bond order $=\frac{10-6}{2}=2$ for $\mathrm{c}_2$ : number of bonding electrons $=8$ , number of antibonding electrons = 4 bond order $=\frac{8-4}{2}=2$ so, both $\mathrm{o}_2$ and $\mathrm{c}_2$ have a bond order of 2 . © examsnet.com

question: At what temperature (in K ) the rms velocity of $\mathrm{SO}_2$ molecules is equal to rms velocity of $\mathrm{O}_2$ molecules at $27^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ . [AP EAPCET 22 May 2025 S2]
search_text: at what temperature (in k ) the rms velocity of $\mathrm{so}_2$ molecules is equal to rms velocity of $\mathrm{o}_2$ molecules at $27^{\circ}\mathrm{c}$ . [ap eapcet 22 may 2025 s2] {'a': '$300$', 'b': '$1200$', 'c': '$600$', 'd': '$900$'} 2025 2025-05-22 shift_2 chemistry   126 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: we want to find the temperature where the rms (root mean square) speed of $\mathrm{so}_2$ molecules is equal to the rms speed of $\mathrm{o}_2$ molecules at $27^{\circ}\mathrm{c}$ . the formula for rms velocity is: $v_{\text{rms}}=\sqrt{\frac{3 r t}{m}}$ where $r$ is the gas constant, $t$ is temperature in kelvin, and $m$ is molar mass. we set the rms speeds equal: $v_{\text{rms}(\mathrm{so}_2)} = v_{\text{rms}(\mathrm{o}_2)} \text{ so }, \sqrt{\frac{3 r t_{\mathrm{so}_2}}{m_{\mathrm{so}_2}}} = \sqrt{\frac{3 r t_{\mathrm{o}_2}}{m_{\mathrm{o}_2}}}$ squaring both sides removes the square root: $\frac{t_{\mathrm{so}_2}}{m_{\mathrm{so}_2}}=\frac{t_{\mathrm{o}_2}}{m_{\mathrm{o}_2}}$ rearrange for $t_{\mathrm{so}_2}: t_{\mathrm{so}_2}=t_{\mathrm{o}_2} \times \frac{m_{\mathrm{so}_2}}{m_{\mathrm{o}_2}}$ the temperature given for $\mathrm{o}_2$ is $27^{\circ}\mathrm{c}$ . convert this to kelvin: $27+273=300\,	ext{k}$ the molar mass of $\mathrm{so}_2$ is 64 , and of $\mathrm{o}_2$ is 32 . plug in the values: $t_{\mathrm{so}_2}=300 \times \frac{64}{32}=300 \times 2=600\,\text{k}$ © examsnet.com

question: For one mole of an ideal gas an isochore is obtained. The slope of the isochore is $0.082\,\text{atm}\,\text{K}^{-1}$ . What will be its pressure (in atm) when the temperature is $12.2 \text{K} ? ( R = 0.082 \text{L} \text{atm} \text{mol}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1} )$ . [AP EAPCET 22 May 2025 S2]
search_text: for one mole of an ideal gas an isochore is obtained. the slope of the isochore is $0.082\,\text{atm}\,\text{k}^{-1}$ . what will be its pressure (in atm) when the temperature is $12.2 \text{k} ? ( r = 0.082 \text{l} \text{atm} \text{mol}^{-1} \text{k}^{-1} )$ . [ap eapcet 22 may 2025 s2] {'a': '$10.0$', 'b': '$0.1$', 'c': '$1.0$', 'd': '$0.5$'} 2025 2025-05-22 shift_2 chemistry   127 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: the slope of an isochore (a line where volume does not change) for an ideal gas is given by $\frac{dp}{dt} = \frac{nr}{v}$ , where: $n =$ number of moles, $r =$ gas constant, $v =$ volume. here, the slope is $0.082 \text{atm} \text{k}^{-1}, n=1$ , and $r=0.082 \text{l} \text{atm} \text{mol}^{-1} \text{k}^{-1}$ . substitute the known values into the formula: $0.082 = \;\frac{1 \times 0.082}{v}$ solve for $v$ : $v = 1 \text{l}$ now, use the ideal gas equation: $p v = n r t$ . substitute the values: $p \times 1 = 1 \times 0.082 \times 12.2$ calculate the multiplication: $0.082 \times 12.2 = 1.0004$ so, $p = 1.0004 \text{atm}$ . round to nearest whole number: $p = 1 \text{atm}$ © examsnet.com

question: At $T(K)$ , the following gaseous equilibrium is established. $W+X\rightleftharpoons Y+Z$ The initial concentration of $W$ is two times to the initial concentration of $X$ . The system is heated to $T(K)$ to establish the equilibrium. At equilibrium the concentration of Y is four times to the concentration of X . What is the value of $K_{c}$ ? [AP EAPCET 22 May 2025 S2]
search_text: at $t(k)$ , the following gaseous equilibrium is established. $w+x\rightleftharpoons y+z$ the initial concentration of $w$ is two times to the initial concentration of $x$ . the system is heated to $t(k)$ to establish the equilibrium. at equilibrium the concentration of y is four times to the concentration of x . what is the value of $k_{c}$ ? [ap eapcet 22 may 2025 s2] {'a': '$0.375$', 'b': '$1.333$', 'c': '$2.666$', 'd': '$5.333$'} 2025 2025-05-22 shift_2 chemistry   132 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: $w+x\rightleftharpoons y+z$ initial concentrations: w starts at $2 x, x$ starts at $x$ , and both y and z start at 0 . at equilibrium: let the amount of y and z formed be $y$ . so, at equilibrium: $\;w=2 x-y$ $\;x=x-y$ $\;y=y$ $\;z=y$ relationship between y and x at equilibrium: at equilibrium, the amount of y is four times the amount of x . this gives us: $[y]_{e q}=4[x]_{e q}$ so, $y=4(x-y)$ solve for $y$ : $y=4 x-4 y$ $y+4 y=4 x$ $5 y=4 x$ $y=\;\frac{4}{5}x$ write $k_c$ expression and substitute values: the equilibrium constant is: $k_c=\;\frac{[y][z]}{[w][x]}$ plug in the equilibrium values: $k_c=\;\frac{\left(\frac{4}{5}x\right)\left(\frac{4}{5}x\right)}{\left(2x-\;\frac{4}{5}x\right)\left(x-\;\frac{4}{5}x\right)}$ simplify: numerator: $\left(\;\frac{4}{5}x\right)^2=\;\frac{16}{25}x^2$ denominator: $\;2 x-\;\frac{4}{5}x=\;\frac{10 x-4 x}{5}=\;\frac{6 x}{5}$ $\;x-\;\frac{4}{5}x=\;\frac{5 x-4 x}{5}=\;\frac{x}{5}$ so denominator: $\;\frac{6 x}{5} \cdot \;\frac{x}{5}=\;\frac{6 x^2}{25}$ therefore, $k_c=\;\frac{\frac{16x^2}{25}}{\frac{6x^2}{25}}=\;\frac{16}{6}=2.666$ © examsnet.com

question: Consider the following Statement-I : $\;\;\mathrm{Al}_2\mathrm{O}_3$ is amphoteric in nature. Statement-II : $\;\;\mathrm{Tl}_2\mathrm{O}_3$ is more basic than $\mathrm{Ga}_2\mathrm{O}_3$ [AP EAPCET 22 May 2025 S2]
search_text: consider the following statement-i : $\;\;\mathrm{al}_2\mathrm{o}_3$ is amphoteric in nature. statement-ii : $\;\;\mathrm{tl}_2\mathrm{o}_3$ is more basic than $\mathrm{ga}_2\mathrm{o}_3$ [ap eapcet 22 may 2025 s2] {'a': 'both statement-i and statement-ii are correct', 'b': 'both statement-i and statement-ii are not correct', 'c': 'statement-i is correct, but statement-ii is not correct', 'd': 'statement-i is not correct, but statement-ii is correct'} 2025 2025-05-22 shift_2 chemistry   135 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: statement i: $\mathrm{al}_2\mathrm{o}_3$ is amphoteric in nature. explanation: aluminum oxide reacts both with acids and with bases, forming salts in each case. $\;\mathrm{al}_2\mathrm{o}_3 + 6\mathrm{hcl} \longrightarrow 2\mathrm{alcl}_3 + 3\mathrm{h}_2\mathrm{o}$ $\;\mathrm{al}_2\mathrm{o}_3 + 2\mathrm{naoh} + 3\mathrm{h}_2\mathrm{o} \longrightarrow 2\mathrm{na}[\mathrm{al}(\mathrm{oh})_4]$ hence, aluminum oxide is amphoteric. so, statement i is correct. statement ii: $\mathrm{tl}_2\mathrm{o}_3$ is more basic than $\mathrm{ga}_2\mathrm{o}_3$ . we are comparing group 13 element oxides: $\mathrm{b}_2\mathrm{o}_3 < \mathrm{al}_2\mathrm{o}_3 < \mathrm{ga}_2\mathrm{o}_3 < \mathrm{in}_2\mathrm{o}_3 < \mathrm{tl}_2\mathrm{o}_3$ → trend: from b to ti, metallic character increases, so basic character of oxides increases (acidic → amphoteric → basic). thus, $\mathrm{tl}_2\mathrm{o}_3$ (thallium(iii) oxide) is more basic than $\mathrm{ga}_2\mathrm{o}_3$ (gallium oxide). so, statement ii is also correct. final answer: option a: both statement i and statement ii are correct. © examsnet.com

question: At $298\ \text{K}, 0.714$ moles of liquid A is dissolved in 5.555 moles of liquid B . The vapour pressure of the resultant solution is 475 torr. search_text: at $298\ \text{k}, 0.714$ moles of liquid a is dissolved in 5.555 moles of liquid b . the vapour pressure of the resultant solution is 475 torr. the vapour pressure of pure liquid $a$ at the same temperature is 280.7 torr. what is the vapour pressure of pure liquid b in torr ?
