question: The number of solutions of $\tan^{-1} 1 + \frac{1}{2} \cos^{-1} x^2 - \tan^{-1} \left( \frac{\sqrt{1+x^2} + \sqrt{1-x^2}}{\sqrt{1+x^2} - \sqrt{1-x^2}} \right) = 0$ is [AP EAPCET 23 May 2025 S2]
search_text: the number of solutions of $\tan^{-1} 1 + \frac{1}{2} \cos^{-1} x^2 - \tan^{-1} \left( \frac{\sqrt{1+x^2} + \sqrt{1-x^2}}{\sqrt{1+x^2} - \sqrt{1-x^2}} \right) = 0$ is [ap eapcet 23 may 2025 s2] {'a': '3', 'b': '0', 'c': '1', 'd': 'infinitely many'} 2025 2025-05-23 shift_2 mathematics   24 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: $\tan^{-1}(1) + \frac{1}{2} \cos^{-1}(x^2)$ $- \tan^{-1} \left( \frac{\sqrt{1+x^2} + \sqrt{1-x^2}}{\sqrt{1+x^2} - \sqrt{1-x^2}} \right) = 0$ $\because \tan^{-1}(1) = \frac{\pi}{4} \text{ and let } \theta = \cos^{-1}(x^2)$ $\rightarrow x^2 = \cos \theta$ $\text{ and } 1+x^2 = 1+\cos x, 1-x^2 = 1-\cos x$ $\frac{\pi}{4} + \frac{\theta}{2} - \tan^{-1} \left( \frac{\sqrt{1+\cos\theta} + \sqrt{1-\cos\theta}}{\sqrt{1+\cos\theta} - \sqrt{1-\cos\theta}} \right)$ $\frac{\pi}{4} + \frac{\theta}{2} - \tan^{-1} \left( \frac{ \sqrt{2} \frac{\cos\theta}{2} + \sqrt{2} \frac{\sin\theta}{2} }{ \sqrt{2} \frac{\cos\theta}{2} - \sqrt{2} \frac{\sin\theta}{2} } \right)$ $\frac{\pi}{4} + \frac{\theta}{2} - \tan^{-1} \left( \frac{ \frac{\cos\theta}{2} + \frac{\sin\theta}{2} }{ \frac{\cos\theta}{2} - \frac{\sin\theta}{2} } \right)$ $\because \frac{\cos x + \sin x}{\cos x - \sin x} = \tan\left( \frac{\pi}{4} + x \right)$ $\frac{\pi}{4} + \frac{\theta}{2} - \tan^{-1} \left( \tan \left( \frac{\pi}{4} + \frac{\theta}{2} \right) \right)$ $\frac{\pi}{4} + \frac{\theta}{2} - \frac{\pi}{4} - \frac{\theta}{2} = 0$ hence, the identify is true for all $x$ infinite many solutions. © examsnet.com

question: $\tanh^{-1}(\sin \theta)=$ [AP EAPCET 23 May 2025 S2]
search_text: $\tanh^{-1}(\sin \theta)=$ [ap eapcet 23 may 2025 s2] {'a': '$\\sinh^{-1}(\\csc \\theta)$', 'b': '$\\sinh^{-1}(\\sec \\theta)$', 'c': '$\\cosh^{-1}(\\csc \\theta)$', 'd': '$\\cosh^{-1}(\\sec \\theta)$'} 2025 2025-05-23 shift_2 mathematics   25 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: $\because \tanh^{-1}(x)=\frac{1}{2}\ln\left(\frac{1+x}{1-x}\right) \;(\text{ for }|x|<1)$ $\;\;\;\;\; \text{so, } \tanh^{-1}(\sin \theta)=\frac{1}{2}\ln\left(\frac{1+\sin \theta}{1-\sin \theta}\right)$ $\frac{1+\sin \theta}{1-\sin \theta}=\frac{(1+\sin \theta)^2}{1-\sin^2 \theta}=\left(\frac{1+\sin \theta}{\cos \theta}\right)^2$ $=\frac{1}{2}\ln\left(\frac{1+\sin \theta}{\cos \theta}\right)^2$ $=\ln\left(\frac{1+\sin \theta}{\cos \theta}\right) \;\;\;\cdot\cdot\cdot\cdot\cdot\cdot\cdot(i)$ $\text{ and } \cosh^{-1}(x)=\ln\left(x+\sqrt{x^2-1}\right)$ $\therefore \cosh^{-1}(\sec \theta)=\ln\left(\frac{1}{\cos \theta}+\sqrt{\frac{1-\cos^2 \theta}{\cos^2 \theta}}\right)$ $=\ln\left(\frac{1+\sin \theta}{\cos \theta}\right) \;\;\;\cdot\cdot\cdot\cdot\cdot\cdot\cdot(ii)$ by comparing eqs. (i) and (ii), we get $\tanh^{-1}(\sin \theta)=\cosh^{-1}(\sec \theta)$ © examsnet.com

search_text: in $\triangle abc$ , if $a=8, b=10, c=12$ , then $\;\frac{r}{r}=$ [ap eapcet 23 may 2025 s2] {'a': '$\\;\\;\\frac{8}{15}$', 'b': '$\\;\\;\\frac{7}{16}$', 'c': '$\\;\\;\\frac{3}{5}$', 'd': '$\\;\\;\\frac{5}{8}$'} 2025 2025-05-23 shift_2 mathematics   26 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: $\; \because a=8, b=10 \; \text{ and } \; c=12$ $\;\; \text{ and } \; r=\frac{\delta}{s}, r=\frac{abc}{4\delta}$ $\;\; \text{ so, } \; \frac{r}{r} = \frac{4 \delta^2}{s \cdot abc}$ $\; \because \; s=\frac{a+b+c}{2}=15$ $\;\; \text{ also, } \; \delta=\sqrt{15(15-8)(15-10)(15-12)}$ $\; =\sqrt{15 \times 7 \times 5 \times 3}=15\sqrt{7}$ $\;\; \text{ thus, } \; \frac{r}{r} = \frac{4 \times 225 \times 7}{15 \times 8 \times 10 \times 12} = \frac{7}{16}$ © examsnet.com

question: In triangle ABC , if $a=13, b=8, c=7$ , then $\cos(B+C)=$ [AP EAPCET 23 May 2025 S2]
search_text: in triangle abc , if $a=13, b=8, c=7$ , then $\cos(b+c)=$ [ap eapcet 23 may 2025 s2] {'a': '$\\;\\frac{11}{13}$', 'b': '$\\;\\frac{23}{26}$', 'c': '$\\;\\frac{3}{4}$', 'd': '$\\;\\frac{1}{2}$'} 2025 2025-05-23 shift_2 mathematics   27 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: $\;\text{ in }\;\triangle abc, \angle a+\angle b+\angle c=180^{\circ}$ so, $\angle b+\angle c=180^{\circ}-\angle a$ $\rightarrow \cos(b+c)\;=\cos(180^{\circ}-a)$ $\;=-\cos a$ now, $\cos a\;=\;\frac{b^2+c^2-a^2}{2bc}=\;\frac{8^2+7^2-13^2}{2 \times 8 \times 7}$ $\;=\;\frac{64+49-169}{112}=-\;\frac{56}{112}$ $\;=-\;\frac{1}{2}$ hence, $\cos(b+c)=-\left(-\;\frac{1}{2}\right)=\;\frac{1}{2}$ © examsnet.com

question: In a triangle $A B C$ , if $(r_1-r_3)  (r_1-r_2) -2 r_2 r_3=0$ , then $a^2-b^2=$ [AP EAPCET 23 May 2025 S2]
search_text: in a triangle $a b c$ , if $(r_1-r_3)  (r_1-r_2) -2 r_2 r_3=0$ , then $a^2-b^2=$ [ap eapcet 23 may 2025 s2] {'a': '$c^2+\\;\\frac{b^2}{4}$', 'b': '$c^2$', 'c': 'abc', 'd': '$\\;\\frac{b+a}{c}$'} 2025 2025-05-23 shift_2 mathematics   28 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: $\because  (r_1-r_3)  (r_1-r_2) -2 r_2 r_3=0$ and we know that $r_1=\;\frac{\delta}{s-a}, r_2=\;\frac{\delta}{s-b}, r_3=\;\frac{\delta}{s-c}$ substitute these values $\rightarrow \delta^2 \left(\;\frac{1}{s-a}-\;\frac{1}{s-c}\right) \left(\;\frac{1}{s-a}-\;\frac{1}{s-b}\right) -2 \delta^2 \left(\;\frac{1}{(s-b)(s-c)}\right) =0$ $\;\rightarrow  \;\;  \left(\;\frac{s-c-s+a}{(s-a)(s-c)}\right)  \left(\;\frac{s-b-s+a}{(s-a)(s-b)}\right) - \left(\;\frac{2}{(s-b)(s-c)}\right) =0$ $\rightarrow \;\frac{1}{(s-b)(s-c)} \left[\;\frac{(a-c)(a-b)}{(s-a)^2}-2\right] =0$ $\rightarrow (a-c)(a-b)-2(s-a)^2=0$ $\rightarrow (a-c)(a-b)-2 \left(\;\frac{a+b+c}{2}-a\right)^2=0$ $\rightarrow 2(a-c)(a-b)-(b+c-a)^2=0$ $\rightarrow 2 (a^2-a b-a c+b c) - (b^2+c^2+a^2) -2(b c-c a-a b)=0$ $\rightarrow a^2-b^2-c^2-2 a b-2 a c+2 b c-2 b c+2 a c+2 a b=0$ $\rightarrow a^2-b^2=c^2$ © examsnet.com

search_text: if $\overline{a}=2\hat{i}-3\hat{j}+5\hat{k}$ and $\overline{b}=-\hat{i}+3\hat{j}+3\hat{k}$ are two vectors, then the vector of magnitude 28 units in the direction of the vector $\overline{a}-\overline{b}$ is [ap eapcet 23 may 2025 s2] {'a': '$\\;3\\overline{i}+6\\overline{j}-2\\overline{k}$', 'b': '$\\;12\\overline{i}-24\\overline{j}+8\\overline{k}$', 'c': '$\\;3\\overline{i}-6\\overline{j}-2\\overline{k}$', 'd': '$12\\overline{i}+24\\overline{j}-8\\overline{k}$'} 2025 2025-05-23 shift_2 mathematics   30 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: $a=2\hat{i}-3\hat{j}+5\hat{k}, b=-\hat{i}+3j+3\hat{k}$ so, $a - b =2\hat{i}-3\hat{j}+5\hat{k}+\hat{i}-3\hat{j}-3\hat{k}$ $=3\hat{i}-6\hat{j}+2\hat{k}$ and $|a-b|=\sqrt{3^2+(-6)^2+2^2}=7$ unit vector in $(a-b)$ $=\;\frac{1}{7}(3\hat{i}-6\hat{j}+2\hat{k})$ thus, the vector of magnitude 28 units $\;=28\left(\;\frac{1}{7}(3\hat{i}-6\hat{j}+2\hat{k})=4(3\hat{i}-6\hat{j}+2\hat{k})\right)$ $\;=12\hat{i}-24\hat{j}+8\hat{k}$ © examsnet.com

question: If $\overline{a}$ is a unit vector, then $\left|\overline{a} \times \overline{i}\right|^2+\left|\overline{a} \times \overline{j}\right|^2+\left|\overline{a} \times \overline{k}\right|^2=$ [AP EAPCET 23 May 2025 S2]
search_text: if $\overline{a}$ is a unit vector, then $\left|\overline{a} \times \overline{i}\right|^2+\left|\overline{a} \times \overline{j}\right|^2+\left|\overline{a} \times \overline{k}\right|^2=$ [ap eapcet 23 may 2025 s2] {'a': '4', 'b': '1', 'c': '0', 'd': '2'} 2025 2025-05-23 shift_2 mathematics   31 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: let, $a = x \hat{i} + y \hat{j} + z \hat{k}$ then, $a \times i = \widehat{\begin{vmatrix} i & \hat{j} & \hat{k} \\ x & y & z \\ 1 & 0 & 0 \end{vmatrix}}$ $= \hat{i}(0-0) - \hat{j}(0-z) + \hat{k}(0-y)$ $= z \hat{j} - y \hat{k}$ so, $\left| a \times i \right|^2 = z^2 + y^2$ similarly, $\left| a \times \hat{j} \right|^2 = x^2 + z^2$ and $\left| a \times \hat{k} \right|^2 = x^2 + y^2$ thus, $\left| a \times \hat{i} \right|^2+\left| a \times \hat{j} \right|^2+\left| a \times \hat{k} \right|^2$ $= 2 (x^2 + y^2 + z^2)$ $\because a$ is unit vector so, $x^2+y^2+z^2=1$ hence, $\left| a \times \hat{i} \right|^2+\left| a \times \hat{j} \right|^2+\left| a \times \hat{k} \right|^2$ $= 2 \times 1 = 2$ © examsnet.com

search_text: if $\overline{a}=\overline{i}-2\overline{j}-3\overline{k}, \overline{b}=-2\overline{i}+3\overline{j}+4\overline{k}, \overline{c}=5\overline{i}-4\overline{j}+3\overline{k}$ and $\overline{d}=3\overline{i}+\overline{j}+5\overline{k}$ are four vectors then $(\overline{a} \times \overline{b}) \times (\overline{c} \times \overline{d})=$ [ap eapcet 23 may 2025 s2] {'a': '$\\;18\\overline{i}+6\\overline{j}+30\\overline{k}$', 'b': '$\\;8\\overline{i}-3\\overline{j}+8\\overline{k}$', 'c': '$\\;19\\overline{i}-5\\overline{j}+21\\overline{k}$', 'd': '$\\;27\\overline{i}-8\\overline{j}+29\\overline{k}$'} 2025 2025-05-23 shift_2 mathematics   32 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: $\; \; \; ( a \times b ) = \begin{vmatrix} \hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k} \\ 1 & -2 & -3 \\ -2 & 3 & 4 \end{vmatrix}$ $\; \; \; =\hat{i}(-8+9)-\hat{j}(4-6)+\hat{k}(3-4)$ $\; \; \; =\hat{i}+2\hat{j}-\hat{k}$ $\; \; \text{ and } ( c \times d ) = \begin{vmatrix} \hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k} \\ 5 & -4 & 3 \\ 3 & 1 & 5 \end{vmatrix}$ $\; =\hat{i}(-20-3)-\hat{j}(25-9)+\hat{k}(5+12)$ $\; =-23\hat{i}-16\hat{j}+17\hat{k}$ $\; \; \text{ thus, } ( a \times b ) \times ( c \times d ) = \begin{vmatrix} \hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k} \\ 1 & 2 & -1 \\ -23 & -16 & 7 \end{vmatrix}$ $\; =\hat{i}(34-16)-\hat{j}(17-23)+\hat{k}(-16+4)$ $\; =18\hat{i}+6\hat{j}+30\hat{k}$ © examsnet.com

search_text: $3 \overline{i}+\overline{j}+\overline{k}, 2 \overline{i}+\overline{k}, \overline{i}+5 \overline{j}$ are the position vectors of three non collinear points $a, b, c$ respectively. if the perpendicular drawn from c onto $\overline{ab}$ meets $\overline{ab}$ at the point $a \overline{i}+b \overline{j}+c \overline{k}$ , then $a+b+c=$ [ap eapcet 23 may 2025 s2] {'a': '5', 'b': '3', 'c': '7', 'd': '9'} 2025 2025-05-23 shift_2 mathematics   33 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: $ab = ob - oa = (2-3)\hat{i}+(0-1)\hat{j}+(1-1)\hat{k} = -\hat{i}-\hat{j}$ so, the direction vector of $\text{lin} e a b$ is $d = -\hat{i} - \hat{j}$ $\text{let} p = a + \lambda d$ $= (3\hat{i}+\hat{j}+\hat{k}) + \lambda(-\hat{i}-\hat{j})$ $= (3-\lambda)\hat{i} + (1-\lambda)\hat{j} + \hat{k}$ and $pc = c - p = (\hat{i} + 5\hat{j})$ $-[(3-\lambda)\hat{i} + (1-\lambda)\hat{j} + \hat{k})$ $= (\lambda-2)\hat{i} + (4+\lambda)\hat{j} - \hat{k}$ as, given in the question $\because pc \perp ab$ $\rightarrow pc \cdot ab = 0$ $\rightarrow (\lambda-2)(-1) + (4+\lambda)(-1) + (-1)(0) = 0$ $\rightarrow -\lambda+2-4-\lambda = 0$ $\rightarrow \lambda = -1$ $\therefore p = (3-\lambda)\hat{i} + (1-\lambda)\hat{j} + \hat{k}$ $= (3+1)\hat{i} + (1+1)\hat{j} + \hat{k}$ $= 4\hat{i} + 2\hat{j} + \hat{k}$ therefore, $a=4, b=2$ and $c=1$ hence, $a+b+c=4+2+1=7$ © examsnet.com

question: Let $x_1, x_2, \dots, x_{11}$ be the observations satisfying $\sum\limits_{i=1}^{11} (x_i-4)=22$ and $\sum\limits_{i=1}^{11} (x_i-4)^2=154$ . If the mean and variance of the observations are $\alpha$ and $\beta$ , then the quadratic equation having the roots $\;\frac{\alpha}{\beta}$ and $\;\frac{\beta}{\alpha}$ is [AP EAPCET 23 May 2025 S2]
search_text: let $x_1, x_2, \dots, x_{11}$ be the observations satisfying $\sum\limits_{i=1}^{11} (x_i-4)=22$ and $\sum\limits_{i=1}^{11} (x_i-4)^2=154$ . if the mean and variance of the observations are $\alpha$ and $\beta$ , then the quadratic equation having the roots $\;\frac{\alpha}{\beta}$ and $\;\frac{\beta}{\alpha}$ is [ap eapcet 23 may 2025 s2] {'a': '$\\;15x^2 - 16x + 15 = 0$', 'b': '$\\;15x^2 - 34x + 15 = 0$', 'c': '$\\;x^2 - 16x + 60 = 0$', 'd': '$\\;12x^2 - 25x + 20 = 0$'} 2025 2025-05-23 shift_2 mathematics   34 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: $\;\sum\limits_{i=1}^{11} (x_i-4)=22$ $\;\rightarrow \;\; \sum\limits_{i=1}^{11} x_i - 4 \times 11 = 22$ $\;\rightarrow \;\; \sum\limits_{i=1}^{11} x_i = 66$ so, mean $(\overline{x}) = \frac{66}{11} = 6$ and $\sum\limits_{i=1}^{11} (x_i-4)^2 = 154$ $\because \;\; x_i - \overline{x} = x_i - 6$ $= (x_i-4) - 2$ $\therefore \;\; [x_i - \overline{x}]^2 = [ (x_i-4) - 2 ]^2$ $= (x_i-4)^2 - 4(x_i-4) + 4$ so, $\sum\limits_{i=1}^{11} (x_i-\overline{x})^2 = \sum\limits_{i=1}^{11} (x-4)^2$ $-4 \sum\limits_{i=1}^{11} (x_i-4) + 11 \times 4$ $= 154 - 4 \times 22 + 44 = 110$ $\;\text{variance}\; (\sigma) = \frac{1}{n} \sum (x_i-\overline{x})^2 \\ = \frac{1}{11} \times 110 = 10$ thus, $\alpha = 6, \beta = 10$ therefore, $\;\frac{\alpha}{\beta} + \;\frac{\beta}{\alpha} = \;\frac{6}{10} + \;\frac{10}{6} = \;\frac{3}{5} + \;\frac{5}{3}$ $= \frac{9+25}{15} = \frac{34}{15} = \;\text{sum of roots}\;$ and $\;\frac{\alpha}{\beta} \cdot \;\frac{\beta}{\alpha} = 1 =$ product of roots hence, the quadratic is $\;x^2 - \left(\;\frac{34}{15}\right) x + 1 = 0$ $\rightarrow 15x^2 - 34x + 15 = 0$ © examsnet.com

search_text: there are 8 boys and 7 girls in a class room. if the names of all those children are written on paper slips and 3 slips are drawn at random from them, then the probability of getting the names of one boy and two girls or one girl and two boys is [ap eapcet 23 may 2025 s2] {'a': '$\\;\\frac{1}{5}$', 'b': '$\\;\\frac{3}{4}$', 'c': '$\\;\\frac{4}{5}$', 'd': '$\\;\\frac{1}{4}$'} 2025 2025-05-23 shift_2 mathematics   35 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: total childrens $=15(8 b+7 g)$ total ways of choosing 3 childrens out of 15 is $={}^{15} c_3=\;\frac{15 \times 14 \times 13}{3 \times 2 \times 1}=455$ case i choosing 1 boy and 2 girls $={}^8 c_1 \cdot {}^7 c_2=\;\frac{8 \times 7 \times 6}{2}=168$ case ii choosing 2 boys and 1 girl $={}^8 c_2 \cdot {}^7 c_1=\;\frac{8 \times 7}{2} \times 7=196$ thus, required probability $=\;\frac{168+196}{455}=\;\frac{364}{455}=\;\frac{4}{5}$ © examsnet.com

search_text: a four member committee is to be formed from a group containing 9 men and 5 women. if a committee is formed randomly, then the probability that it contains atleast one woman is [ap eapcet 23 may 2025 s2] {'a': '$\\;\\;\\frac{125}{143}$', 'b': '$\\;\\;\\frac{18}{143}$', 'c': '$\\;\\;\\frac{60}{143}$', 'd': '$\\;\\;\\frac{65}{143}$'} 2025 2025-05-23 shift_2 mathematics   36 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: total people $=14(9 m +5 w)$ total ways to choose 4 peoples from 14 is ${}^{14}c_4$ total ways to choose all men is $={}^{9}c_4$ so, total ways to choose atleast one women $\;={}^{14}c_4-{}^{9}c_4=\;\frac{14 \times 13 \times 12 \times 11}{4 \times 3 \times 2 \times 1}-\;\frac{9 \times 8 \times 7 \times 6}{4 \times 3 \times 2 \times 1}$ $\;=1001-126=875$ hence, required probability $=\;\frac{875}{1001}=\;\frac{125}{143}$ © examsnet.com

question: A die is thrown twice. Let A be the event of getting a prime number when the die is thrown first time and $B$ be the event of getting an even number when the die is thrown second time. Then $P(A / \overline{B})$ [AP EAPCET 23 May 2025 S2]
search_text: a die is thrown twice. let a be the event of getting a prime number when the die is thrown first time and $b$ be the event of getting an even number when the die is thrown second time. then $p(a / \overline{b})$ [ap eapcet 23 may 2025 s2] {'a': '$\\frac{1}{2}$', 'b': '$\\frac{2}{3}$', 'c': '$\\frac{1}{5}$', 'd': '$\\frac{3}{5}$'} 2025 2025-05-23 shift_2 mathematics   37 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: total outcomes $=\{1,2,3,4,5,6\}=6$ prime number $=\{2,3,5\}=3$ so, $p(a)=\frac{3}{6}=\frac{1}{2}$ and even numbers $=\{2,4,6\}=3$ $\therefore p(b)=\frac{3}{6}=\frac{1}{2}$ thus, $p(\overline{b})=1-p(b)=1-\frac{1}{2}=\frac{1}{2}$ total sample for 2 throws $=6 \times 6=36$ then, $p(a / \overline{b})=\frac{p(a \cap \overline{b})}{p(\overline{b})}$ first throw is prime $=\{2,3,5\}$ second throw is not even $=\{1,3,5\}$ pairs where first is in $\{2,3,5\}$ and second is in $\{1,3,5\}=3 \times 3=9$ outcomes so, $p(a \cap \overline{b})=\frac{9}{36}=\frac{1}{4}$ therefore, $p(a / \overline{b})=\frac{\frac{1}{4}}{\frac{1}{2}}=\frac{1}{2}$ © examsnet.com

question: A bag contains 5 balls of unknown colours. There are equal chances that out of these five balls, there may be 0 or 1 or 2 or 3 or 4 or 5 red balls. A ball is taken out from the bag at random and is found to be red. The probability that it is the only red ball in the bag is [AP EAPCET 23 May 2025 S2]
search_text: a bag contains 5 balls of unknown colours. there are equal chances that out of these five balls, there may be 0 or 1 or 2 or 3 or 4 or 5 red balls. a ball is taken out from the bag at random and is found to be red. the probability that it is the only red ball in the bag is [ap eapcet 23 may 2025 s2] {'a': '$\\frac{1}{5}$', 'b': '$\\frac{1}{6}$', 'c': '$\\frac{1}{15}$', 'd': '$\\frac{1}{30}$'} 2025 2025-05-23 shift_2 mathematics   38 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: let $r_k$ be the event that are exactly $k$ red balls is in bag, where $k=1,2,3,4,5$ so, $p(r_k) = \frac{1}{5}$ for $k=1,2,3,4,5$ let $a$ be the event that a red ball is drawn. $p(r_1 / a) = \frac{p(r_1 \cap a)}{p(a)}$ $\because\ p(a / r_1) = \frac{1}{5}$ $\text{ and }\ p(r_1 \cap a) = p(r_1) \cdot p(a / r_1)$ $= \frac{1}{5} \cdot \frac{1}{5} = \frac{1}{25}$ $\text{ and }\ p(a) = \sum\limits_{k=0}^{5} p(r_k) \cdot p(a / r_k)$ $= \frac{1}{5} \sum\limits_{k=0}^{5} \frac{k}{5} = \frac{1}{25}(1+2+3+4+5)$ $= \frac{1}{25} \times 15 = \frac{15}{25}$ hence, $p(r_1 / a) = \frac{p(r_1 \cap a)}{p(a)} = \frac{\frac{1}{25}}{\frac{15}{25}} = \frac{1}{15}$ © examsnet.com

question: If $X \sim B(9, p)$ is a binomial variate satisfying the equation $P(x=3)=P(x=6)$ , then $P(x<3)=$ [AP EAPCET 23 May 2025 S2]
search_text: if $x \sim b(9, p)$ is a binomial variate satisfying the equation $p(x=3)=p(x=6)$ , then $p(x<3)=$ [ap eapcet 23 may 2025 s2] {'a': '$\\;\\;\\frac{23}{256}$', 'b': '$\\;\\;\\frac{65}{256}$', 'c': '$\\;\\;\\frac{5}{256}$', 'd': '$\\;\\;\\frac{45}{512}$'} 2025 2025-05-23 shift_2 mathematics   39 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: $\; \because p(x=r)={}^{n}c_{r} p^{r}(1-p)^{n-r}$ $\;\; \text{ and }\; \;\; p(x=3)=p(x=6)$ $\;\rightarrow \;\; {}^{9}c_{3} p^{3}(1-p)^{6}={}^{9}c_{6} p^{6}(1-p)^{3}$ $\;\rightarrow \;\; (1-p)^{3}=p^{3}$ $\;\rightarrow \;\; \frac{1-p}{p}=1$ $\;\rightarrow \;\; p=\frac{1}{2}$ $\;\; \text{ so, }\; p(x<3)=p(x=0)+p(x=1)+p(x=2)$ $\;={}^{9}c_{0} \left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{9}+{}^{9}c_{1} \left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{9}+{}^{9}c_{2} \left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{9}$ $\;=\frac{1}{512}+\frac{9}{512}+\frac{36}{512}=\frac{46}{512}=\frac{23}{256}$ © examsnet.com

question: The mean and variance of a binomial distribution are x and 5 respectively. If x is an integer, then the possible values for x are [AP EAPCET 23 May 2025 S2]
search_text: the mean and variance of a binomial distribution are x and 5 respectively. if x is an integer, then the possible values for x are [ap eapcet 23 may 2025 s2] {'a': '$6,10,30$', 'b': '$8,12,28$', 'c': '$10,15,25$', 'd': '$9, 18, 24$'} 2025 2025-05-23 shift_2 mathematics   40 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: the mean of a binomial distribution is $x$ , and the variance is 5 . we know that the mean, $\mu = n p = x$ . this means $n$ times $p$ is $x$ . the formula for variance is $\sigma^2 = n p (1-p) = 5$ . this means $n$ times $p$ times $(1-p)$ is 5 . from the mean formula, $p = \frac{x}{n}$ . substitute $p = \frac{x}{n}$ into the variance formula: $x \left(1 - \frac{x}{n}\right) = 5$ if we open the bracket, we get: $x - \frac{x^2}{n} = 5$ take $\frac{x^2}{n}$ to the other side: $\frac{x^2}{n} = x - 5$ now, solve for $n$ : $n = \frac{x^2}{x-5}$ to get a whole number for $n, x-5$ must divide $x^2$ exactly. let's check different $x$ values: if $x=6: n = \frac{36}{1} = 3636$ is an integer. if $x=10: n = \frac{100}{5} = 2020$ is an integer. if $x=30: n = \frac{900}{25} = 3636$ is an integer. so, the possible values for $x$ are: $6,10,30$ . © examsnet.com

question: After the coordinate axes are rotated through an angle $\;\frac{\pi}{4}$ in the anti clockwise direction without shifting the origin, if the equation $x^2+y^2-2x-4y-20=0$ transforms to $ax^2+2hxy+by^2+2gx+2fy+c=0$ in the new coordinate system, then $\begin{vmatrix} a & h & g \\ h & b & f \\ g & f & c \end{vmatrix}=$ [AP EAPCET 23 May 2025 S2]
search_text: after the coordinate axes are rotated through an angle $\;\frac{\pi}{4}$ in the anti clockwise direction without shifting the origin, if the equation $x^2+y^2-2x-4y-20=0$ transforms to $ax^2+2hxy+by^2+2gx+2fy+c=0$ in the new coordinate system, then $\begin{vmatrix} a & h & g \\ h & b & f \\ g & f & c \end{vmatrix}=$ [ap eapcet 23 may 2025 s2] {'a': '$\\; -20$', 'b': '$\\; -25$', 'c': '$\\; -30$', 'd': '$\\; -35$'} 2025 2025-05-23 shift_2 mathematics   42 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: $\because x^2+y^2-2x-4y-20=0$ after rotation of axes through $\theta=\frac{\pi}{4}$ , it transforms to $ax^2+2hxy+by^2+2gx+2fy+c=0$ in the given equation $a=1, h=0, b=1, g=-1, f=-2, c=-20$ after rotation of $\theta=\frac{\pi}{4}$ $a' = a\cos^2\theta + b\sin^2\theta + 2h\cos\theta\sin\theta$ $\;\;\; = 1\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right)^2 + 1\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right)^2 + 0 = 1$ $b' = a\sin^2\theta + b\cos^2\theta - 2h\sin\theta\cos\theta$ $\; = 1\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right)^2 + 1\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right)^2 - 0 = 1$ also, $h' = (b-a)\sin\theta\cos\theta + h(\cos^2\theta - \sin^2\theta)$ $\; = 0+0 = 0$ similarly, $x' = x\cos\theta - y\sin\theta = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}(x-y)$ and $y' = x\sin\theta + y\sin\theta = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}(x+y)$ then ${-2x'-4y'} = \frac{-2x+2y-4x-4y}{\sqrt{2}}$ $\; = \frac{-6x-2y}{\sqrt{2}}$ $\; = -3\sqrt{2}x - \sqrt{2}y = 2gx + 2fy$ then $g = -\frac{3}{\sqrt{2}}, f = -\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}, c = -20$ so, $\;\begin{vmatrix} a & h & g \\ h & b & f \\ g & f & c \end{vmatrix} = \begin{vmatrix} 1 & 0 & -\frac{3}{\sqrt{2}} \\ 0 & 1 & -\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \\ -\frac{3}{\sqrt{2}} & -\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} & -20 \end{vmatrix}$ $\;\;\; = 1\left(-20-\frac{1}{2}\right) - \frac{3}{\sqrt{2}}\left(+\frac{3}{\sqrt{2}}\right)$ $\;\;\; = -\frac{41}{2} - \frac{9}{2} = -25$ © examsnet.com

(i) $2 x^2+x y-y^2=0$ assume $y=m x$ , and substitute $2 x^2+x(m x)-(m x)^2=0$ coefficient of $x^2$ should be zero $\rightarrow \;\; 2+m-m^2=0 \rightarrow m=2,-1$ $m_1=2 \;\text{ and }\; m_2=-1$ ∵ both lines are perpendicular their slopes must be $-\;\frac{1}{m_1}=-\;\frac{1}{2} \;\text{ and }\; \frac{-1}{m_2}=1$ so, the perpendicular lines has their slopes $-\frac{1}{2}$ and 1 and passing through $(1,1)$ ∴ pair of lines are $\; (y-y_1-m_1 (x-x_1) )$ $\; (y-y_1-m_2 (x-x_2) )=0$ $\rightarrow \left(y-1+\frac{1}{9}(x-1)\right) (y-1-(x-1))=0$ $\rightarrow \left(\frac{x}{2}+y-\frac{3}{2}\right) (y-x)=0$ $\rightarrow \frac{1}{2} x y-\frac{1}{2} x^2+y^2-x y-\frac{3}{2} y+\frac{3}{2} x=0$ $\rightarrow -x^2-x y+2 y^2-3 y+3 x=0$ compare with $\;\;\; a x^2+2 h x y+b y^2+2 g x+3 y=0$ $\; \therefore \;\; a=-1, h=+\frac{1}{2}, b=2 g=-\frac{3}{2}$ $\;\;\text{ so, }\; \frac{b}{a}=\frac{2}{-1}=-2$ $\;\;\text{ and }\; 2(g+h)=2 \left(-\frac{3}{2}+\frac{1}{2}\right) =-2$ hence, $\frac{b}{a}=2(g+h)$ © examsnet.com

question: If the combined equation of the lines joining the origin to the points of intersection of the curve $x^2+y^2-2x-4y+2=0$ and the line $x+y-2=0$ is $(l_1x+m_1y)(l_2x+m_2y)=0$ , then $l_1+l_2+m_1+m_2=$ [AP EAPCET 23 May 2025 S2]
search_text: if the combined equation of the lines joining the origin to the points of intersection of the curve $x^2+y^2-2x-4y+2=0$ and the line $x+y-2=0$ is $(l_1x+m_1y)(l_2x+m_2y)=0$ , then $l_1+l_2+m_1+m_2=$ [ap eapcet 23 may 2025 s2] {'a': '$16$', 'b': '$-6$', 'c': '$-2$', 'd': '$10$'} 2025 2025-05-23 shift_2 mathematics   46 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: put $x=2-y$ in the given conic $\rightarrow (2-y)^2+y^2-2(2-y)-4y+2=0$ $\rightarrow y^2-4y+4+y^2-4+2y-4y+2=0$ $\rightarrow 2y^2-6y+2=0 \rightarrow y^2-3y+1$ $\therefore y=\frac{3\pm\sqrt{5}}{2}$ $\rightarrow y_1=\frac{3+\sqrt{5}}{2}, y_2=\frac{3-\sqrt{5}}{2}$ thus, $x_1=2-\left(\frac{3+\sqrt{5}}{2}\right)=\frac{1-\sqrt{5}}{2}$ and $x_2=2-\left(\frac{3-\sqrt{5}}{2}\right)=\frac{1+\sqrt{5}}{2}$ then, $p_1 \equiv \left(\frac{1-\sqrt{5}}{2}, \frac{3+\sqrt{5}}{2}\right)$ and $p_2 \equiv \left(\frac{1+\sqrt{5}}{2}, \frac{3-\sqrt{5}}{2}\right)$ the lines $op_1$ and $op_2$ will have equation of the form $y=mx$ $\rightarrow lx+my=0$ $\because m_1=\frac{y_1}{x_1}=\frac{3+\sqrt{5}}{1-\sqrt{5}}$ $=\frac{3+\sqrt{5}}{1-\sqrt{5}} \times \frac{1+\sqrt{5}}{1+\sqrt{5}} = -2-\sqrt{5}$ $\text{ and } m_2=\frac{y_2}{x_2}=\frac{3-\sqrt{5}}{1+\sqrt{5}}$ $=\frac{3-\sqrt{5}}{1+\sqrt{5}} \times \frac{1-\sqrt{5}}{1-\sqrt{5}} = -2+\sqrt{5}$ ∴ combined equation of lines are $(m_1x-y_1)(m_2x-y)=0$ will form $\rightarrow (l_1x+m_1y)(l_2x+m_2y)=0$ lets expands and compare $m_1m_2x^2-(m_1+m_2)xy+y^2=l_1l_2x^2$ $+(l_1m_2+l_2m_1)xy+m_1m_2y^2$ $\therefore l_1l_2=m_1m_2, \quad l_1m_2+l_2m_1=-(m_1+m_2),$ $m_1m_2=1$ $m_1=-2-\sqrt{5}, \quad m_2=-2+\sqrt{5}$ $\text{ and } m_1+m_2=-4$ $\because l_1l_2=m_1m_2=1$ $\rightarrow l_1=\frac{1}{l_2}$ $\therefore l_1m_2+\frac{m_1}{l_1}=4$ $\rightarrow (\sqrt{5}-2)l_1^2+(-\sqrt{5}-2)=4l_1.$ $\rightarrow l_1=1 \text{ and } l_2=1$ hence, $l_1+l_2+m_1+m_2=1+1-4=-2$ © examsnet.com

search_text: the equation of the normal drawn at the point $(\sqrt{2}+1,-1)$ to the ellipse $x^2+2 y^2-2 x+8 y+5=0$ is [ap eapcet 23 may 2025 s2] {'a': '$\\; x+y=\\sqrt{2}$', 'b': '$\\; x-2 y=3+\\sqrt{2}$', 'c': '$\\; \\sqrt{2} x-y=3+\\sqrt{2}$', 'd': '$2 x+y=2 \\sqrt{2}+1$'} 2025 2025-05-23 shift_2 mathematics   53 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: $s(x, y) \equiv x^2+2 y^2-2 x+8 y+5$ thus, $\; \frac{\partial s}{\partial x}=2 x-2 \; \frac{\partial s}{\partial y}=4 y+8$ at $p \equiv (\sqrt{2}+1,-1)$ $2 x-2=2(\sqrt{2}+1)-2=2 \sqrt{2}$ and $4 y+8=-4+8=4$ so, $n = \langle 2 \sqrt{2}, 4 \rangle$ so, slope $= \; \frac{4}{2 \sqrt{2}} = \sqrt{2}$ then, equation of normal (at $\sqrt{2}+1,-1$ ) $\; y-(-1)=\sqrt{2}(x-(\sqrt{2}+1))$ $\rightarrow y+1=\sqrt{2} x-2-\sqrt{2}$ $\rightarrow y-\sqrt{2} x+\sqrt{2}+3=0$ $\rightarrow \sqrt{2} x-y-3-\sqrt{2}=0$ $\rightarrow \sqrt{2} x-y=3+\sqrt{2}$ © examsnet.com

question: If $3x+2\sqrt{2}y+k=0$ is a normal to the hyperbola $4x^2-9y^2-36=0$ making positive intercepts on both the axes, then $k=$ [AP EAPCET 23 May 2025 S2]
search_text: if $3x+2\sqrt{2}y+k=0$ is a normal to the hyperbola $4x^2-9y^2-36=0$ making positive intercepts on both the axes, then $k=$ [ap eapcet 23 may 2025 s2] {'a': '$13\\sqrt{2}$', 'b': '$-5\\sqrt{2}$', 'c': '$-2\\sqrt{2}$', 'd': '$-13\\sqrt{2}$'} 2025 2025-05-23 shift_2 mathematics   54 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: $4x^2-9y^2=36 \rightarrow \frac{x^2}{9}-\frac{y^2}{4}=0$ so, $a^2=9, b^2=4$ thus, equation of normal $\frac{9x}{x_1}+\frac{4y}{y_1}=(9+4)=13 \;\;\;\cdot\cdot\cdot\cdot\cdot\cdot\cdot(i)$ and the given equation is $3x+2\sqrt{2}y+k=0$ $\rightarrow \;\; 3x+2\sqrt{2}y=-k \;\;\;\cdot\cdot\cdot\cdot\cdot\cdot\cdot(ii)$ ∵ both equation are proportional thus, $\frac{\frac{9}{x_1}}{3}=\frac{\frac{4}{y_1}}{2\sqrt{2}}=\frac{13}{-k}$ $\rightarrow \;\; \frac{3}{x_1}=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{y_1} \rightarrow x_1=\frac{3}{\sqrt{2}} y_1$ put in equation of hyperbola $\frac{\left(\frac{3}{\sqrt{2}} y_1\right)^2}{9}-\frac{y^2}{4}=1 \rightarrow y_1^2=4 \rightarrow y_1= \pm 2$ at $y_1=2 \rightarrow x_1=3\sqrt{2}$ and at $y_1=-2$ $\rightarrow x_1=-3\sqrt{2}$ also, $\frac{3}{x_1}=-\frac{13}{k} \rightarrow -k=\frac{13}{3} \times 3\sqrt{2}=13\sqrt{2}$ hence, $k=-13\sqrt{2}$ © examsnet.com

search_text: if a hyperbola has asymptotes $3x-4y-1=0$ and $4x-3y-6=0$ , then the transverse and conjugate axes of that hyperbola are [ap eapcet 23 may 2025 s2] {'a': '$\\;x+y-5=0, x-y-1=0$', 'b': '$\\;4x-3y=0, 3x+4y=0$', 'c': '$\\;3x-4y=0, 4x+3y=0$', 'd': '$\\;x+2y-1=0, 2x-y+1=0$'} 2025 2025-05-23 shift_2 mathematics   55 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: asymptotes are $\;3x-4y-1=0 \;\;\;\cdot\cdot\cdot\cdot\cdot\cdot\cdot (i)$ $\;4x-3y-6=0 \;\;\;\cdot\cdot\cdot\cdot\cdot\cdot\cdot (ii)$ by eqs. (i) and (ii), we get $x=3, y=2$ now, the direction vectors of asymptotes for $3x-4y=1 \rightarrow d_1=\langle 4,3 \rangle$ and for $4x-3y=6 \rightarrow d_2=\langle 3,4 \rangle$ thus, transverse and conjugate axis directions. $\;\;\frac{l_1}{\sqrt{a_1^2+b_1^2}} = \pm \;\frac{l_2}{\sqrt{a_2^2+b_2^2}}$ $\rightarrow \;\frac{3x-4y-1}{\sqrt{3^2+(-4)^2}} = \pm \;\frac{4x-3y-6}{\sqrt{4^2+(-3)^2}}$ $\rightarrow 3x-4y-1 = \pm 4x-3y-6$ $\;\text{ so, }\;\;3x-4y-1=4x-3y-6$ $\;\text{ or }\;\;3x-4y-1=-4x+3y+6$ $\rightarrow x+y-5=0$ $\;\text{ or }\;\;7x-7y-7=0$ $\rightarrow x+y-5=0 \;\text{ or }\; x-y-1=$ hence, transverse and conjugate axis are $x+y=5, x-y=1$ © examsnet.com

search_text: if the direction cosines of two lines satisfy the equations $l-2m+n=0$ , $lm+10mn-2nl=0$ and $\theta$ is the angle between the lines, then $\cos \theta =$ [ap eapcet 23 may 2025 s2] {'a': '$\\;\\;\\frac{\\pi}{6}$', 'b': '$\\;\\;\\frac{8}{\\sqrt{70}}$', 'c': '$\\;\\;\\frac{\\pi}{3}$', 'd': '$\\;\\;\\frac{20}{3\\sqrt{70}}$'} 2025 2025-05-23 shift_2 mathematics   57 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: $\because l-2m+n=0 \rightarrow l=2m-n$ substitute in $lm+10mn-2nl=0$ $\;\rightarrow (2m-n)m+100mn-2n(2m-n)=0$ $\;\rightarrow 2m^2+5mn+2n^2=0$ $\;\rightarrow m = \frac{-5n \pm 3n}{4} = \frac{-n}{2}, -2n$ if $m = \frac{-n}{2}, l = -2n$ then, direction ratios of are $1 : m : n = -2n : \frac{n}{2} : n = -4 : -1 : 2$ and direction cosine are $(-4k)^2+(-k)^2+(2k)^2=1 \rightarrow k = \frac{1}{\sqrt{21}}$ $= \left( \frac{-4}{\sqrt{21}}, \frac{-1}{\sqrt{21}}, \frac{2}{\sqrt{21}} \right)$ if $m = -2n$ , then $l = -5n$ and dr's are $l : m : n = -5 : -2 : 1$ and dc's are $(-5k)^2+(-2k)^2+k^2=1$ $\rightarrow \;\; k = \frac{1}{\sqrt{30}} = \left( \frac{-5}{\sqrt{30}}, \frac{-2}{\sqrt{30}}, \frac{1}{\sqrt{30}} \right)$ therefore angle between given lines are $\;\cos \theta = \left| l_1 l_2 + m_1 m_2 + n_1 n_2 \right|$ $\; = \left| \frac{-4}{\sqrt{21}} \times \left( \frac{-5}{\sqrt{30}} \right) + \left( \frac{-1}{\sqrt{21}} \right) \right|$ $\left( \frac{-2}{\sqrt{30}} \right) + \left( \frac{2}{\sqrt{21}} \right) \left( \frac{1}{\sqrt{30}} \right) .$ $\; = \frac{24}{\sqrt{630}} = \frac{24}{3\sqrt{70}}$ $\; = \frac{8}{\sqrt{70}}$ © examsnet.com

search_text: if $(2,-1,3)$ is the foot of the perpendicular drawn from the origin $(0,0,0)$ to a plane then the equation of that plane is [ap eapcet 23 may 2025 s2] {'a': '$2 x + y - 3 z + 6 = 0$', 'b': '$2 x - y + 3 z - 14 = 0$', 'c': '$2 x - y + 3 z - 13 = 0$', 'd': '$2 x + y + 3 z - 10 = 0$'} 2025 2025-05-23 shift_2 mathematics   58 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: as given, the vector from the origin to the point $(2,-1,3)$ is normal to plane. $\therefore \;\; n = \langle 2,-1,3 \rangle$ then, general equation of plane $2 x - y + 3 z = d$ $\because \;\; (2,-1,3)$ lies on the plane. $\therefore \;\; 2(2)-(-1)+3 \times 3 = d \rightarrow d=14$ hence, equation of the plane $2 x - y + 3 z - 14 = 0$ © examsnet.com

search_text: $\lim\limits_{x\to 0}\;\frac{x^2 \sin^2(3x) + \sin^4(6x)}{(1-\cos 3x)^2}=$ [ap eapcet 23 may 2025 s2] {'a': '$\\;\\frac{580}{9}$', 'b': '$\\;\\frac{145}{3}$', 'c': '$\\;\\frac{580}{3}$', 'd': '$\\;\\frac{145}{9}$'} 2025 2025-05-23 shift_2 mathematics   59 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: $\;\lim\limits_{x\to 0}\;\frac{x^2 \sin^2(3x) + \sin^4(6x)}{(1-\cos 3x)^2}$ $\;=\lim\limits_{x\to 0}\;\frac{x^2 \sin^2(3x) + \sin^4(6x)}{\left(2 \sin^2\left(\frac{3x}{2}\right)\right)^2}$ for small-angles $\{\because x\to 0\}$ $\;\sin kx \to kx$ $\;=\lim\limits_{x\to 0}\;\frac{x^2 (3x)^2 + (6x)^4}{\left(2 \left(\frac{3x}{2}\right)^2\right)^2}$ $\;=\lim\limits_{x\to 0}\;\frac{x^4[9+1296]}{x^4 \left[\frac{9}{2}\right]^2}=\lim\limits_{x\to 0}\;\frac{1305}{81}\times 4$ $\;=\frac{435}{27}\times 4=\frac{580}{9}$ © examsnet.com

question: If a real valued function $f(x)=\begin{cases} (1+\sin x)^{\csc x} & -\frac{\pi}{2} < x < 0 \\ a & x=0 \\ \frac{e^{\frac{2}{x}}+e^{\frac{3}{x}}}{a e^{\frac{2}{x}}+b e^{\frac{3}{x}}} & 0 < x < \frac{\pi}{2} \end{cases}$ , is continuous at $x=0$ , then $ab=$ [AP EAPCET 23 May 2025 S2]
search_text: if a real valued function $f(x)=\begin{cases} (1+\sin x)^{\csc x} & -\frac{\pi}{2} < x < 0 \\ a & x=0 \\ \frac{e^{\frac{2}{x}}+e^{\frac{3}{x}}}{a e^{\frac{2}{x}}+b e^{\frac{3}{x}}} & 0 < x < \frac{\pi}{2} \end{cases}$ , is continuous at $x=0$ , then $ab=$ [ap eapcet 23 may 2025 s2] {'a': '$e$', 'b': '$e^2$', 'c': '1', 'd': '$-1$'} 2025 2025-05-23 shift_2 mathematics   60 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: $f(x)=\begin{cases} (1+\sin x)^{\cos x} & -\frac{\pi}{2} < x < 0 \\ a & x=0 \\ \frac{e^{\frac{2}{x}}+e^{\frac{3}{x}}}{a e^{\frac{2}{x}}+b e^{\frac{3}{2}}} & 0 < x < \frac{\pi}{2} \end{cases}$ so, $\lim\limits_{x \to 0^{-}} f(x) = \lim\limits_{x \to 0^{-}} (1+\sin x)^{\cos x}$ let $y = (1+\sin x)^{\cos x}$ $\rightarrow \ln y = \cos x \ln (1+\sin x)$ $= \frac{\ln (1+\sin x)}{\sin x} = 1$ $\rightarrow y = e$ $\therefore \lim\limits_{x \to 0^{-}} (1+\sin x)^{\cos x} = e = a = f(0)$ $\text{ and } \lim\limits_{x \to 0^{+}} f(x) = \lim\limits_{x \to 0^{+}} \frac{e^{\frac{2}{x}}+e^{\frac{3}{x}}}{a e^{\frac{2}{x}}+b e^{\frac{3}{2}}}$ $= \lim\limits_{x \to 0^{+}} \frac{e^{\frac{3}{x}} \left(e^{-\frac{1}{x}}+1\right)}{e^{\frac{3}{x}} \left(e \cdot e^{-\frac{1}{x}}+b\right)} = \frac{1}{b}$ so, $e = \frac{1}{b} \rightarrow b = \frac{1}{e}$ hence, $a b = e \cdot \frac{1}{e} = 1$ © examsnet.com

question: $\lim\limits_{x\to 0}\;\frac{(\csc x-\cot x)(e^{x}-e^{-x})}{\sqrt{3}-\sqrt{2+\cos x}}=$ [AP EAPCET 23 May 2025 S2]
search_text: $\lim\limits_{x\to 0}\;\frac{(\csc x-\cot x)(e^{x}-e^{-x})}{\sqrt{3}-\sqrt{2+\cos x}}=$ [ap eapcet 23 may 2025 s2] {'a': '$\\;3\\sqrt{2}$', 'b': '$\\;2\\sqrt{3}$', 'c': '$\\;3\\sqrt{3}$', 'd': '$4\\sqrt{3}$'} 2025 2025-05-23 shift_2 mathematics   61 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: $\lim\limits_{x\to 0}\;\frac{(\csc x-\cot x)(e^{x}-e^{-x})}{\sqrt{3}-\sqrt{2+\cos x}}$ convert, $\csc x$ and $\cot x$ into $\sin x$ and $e^{x}-e^{-x}=2\sinh x$ $\;=\lim\limits_{x\to 0}\;\frac{ \left( \frac{2\sin^{2}\frac{x}{2}}{2\sin\frac{x}{2}\cos\frac{x}{2}} \cdot 2\sinh x \right) }{\sqrt{3}-\sqrt{2+\cos x}}$ $\;=\lim\limits_{x\to 0}\;\frac{2\tan\frac{x}{2}\cdot\sinh x}{\sqrt{3}-\sqrt{2+\cos x}} \times \frac{\sqrt{3}+\sqrt{2+\cos x}}{\sqrt{3}+\sqrt{2+\cos x}}$ $\;=\lim\limits_{x\to 0}\;\frac{2\tan\frac{x}{2}\cdot\sinh x(\sqrt{3}+\sqrt{2+\cos x})}{1-\cos x}$ $\;=\lim\limits_{x\to 0}\;\frac{2\tan\frac{x}{2}\cdot\sinh x(\sqrt{3}+\sqrt{2+\cos x})}{1-\cos x}$ $\;=\lim\limits_{x\to 0}\;\frac{ \frac{2\sin\frac{x}{2}}{\cos\frac{x}{2}} \cdot \sinh x(\sqrt{3}+\sqrt{2+\cos x}) }{2\sin^{2}\frac{x}{2}}$ $\;=\lim\limits_{x\to 0}\;\frac{ \sinh x(\sqrt{3}+\sqrt{2+\cos x}) }{\cos\frac{x}{2} \cdot \sin\frac{x}{2}}$ $\; \because x \to 0 \rightarrow \cos\frac{x}{2} \to 1 \;\text{ and }\; \sin\frac{x}{2} \to \frac{x}{2}$ $\; \sinh x \to x$ $\;=\;\frac{x(\sqrt{3}+\sqrt{2+1})}{\frac{x}{2}} = 2(\sqrt{3}+\sqrt{3})$ $=2(2\sqrt{3}) = 4\sqrt{3}$ © examsnet.com

search_text: if $y = \sqrt{\cosh x + \sqrt{\cosh x}}$ , then $\; \frac{dy}{dx} =$ [ap eapcet 23 may 2025 s2] {'a': '$\\; \\frac{\\sinh x (2 y^2+2 \\cosh x+1)}{4 y (y^2+\\cosh x)}$', 'b': '$\\; \\frac{\\sinh x (2 y^2-2 \\cosh x-1)}{4 y (y^2-\\cosh x)}$', 'c': '$\\; \\frac{\\sinh x (1-2 \\sqrt{\\cosh x})}{4 y \\sqrt{\\cosh x}}$', 'd': '$\\; \\frac{\\sinh x (1+2 \\sqrt{\\cosh x})}{4 y \\sqrt{\\cosh x}}$'} 2025 2025-05-23 shift_2 mathematics   62 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: $y = \sqrt{\cosh x + \sqrt{\cosh x}}$ let $\sqrt{\cosh x} = u \rightarrow y = \sqrt{u^2 + u}$ now, $\; \frac{dy}{dx} = \; \frac{1}{2 \sqrt{u^2+u}} \cdot (2u+1) = \; \frac{2u+1}{2 \sqrt{u^2+u}}$ $\; \frac{dy}{du} = \; \frac{2u+1}{2y}$ now, $\; \frac{du}{dx} = \; \frac{d}{dx}(\sqrt{\cosh x}) = \; \frac{1}{2 \sqrt{\cosh x}} (\sinh x)$ $= \; \frac{\sinh x}{2u}$ thus, $\; \frac{dy}{dx} = \; \frac{dy}{du} \cdot \; \frac{du}{dx} = \; \frac{2u+1}{2y} \cdot \; \frac{\sinh x}{2u}$ $= \; \frac{(2u+1) \sinh x}{4 y u}$ put $u = \sqrt{\cosh x}$ therefore, $\; \frac{dy}{dx} = \; \frac{\sinh x (1+2 \sqrt{\cosh x})}{4 y \sqrt{\cosh x}}$ © examsnet.com

search_text: if $y = \tan^{-1} \sqrt{x^2-1} + \sinh^{-1} \sqrt{x^2-1}, x>1$ , then $\; \frac{dy}{dx} =$ [ap eapcet 23 may 2025 s2] {'a': '$\\;\\; \\frac{1}{x \\sqrt{x^2-1}}$', 'b': '$\\;\\; \\frac{x+1}{x \\sqrt{x^2-1}}$', 'c': '$\\;\\; \\frac{x+1}{x^2 \\sqrt{x^2-1}}$', 'd': '$\\; \\frac{x}{\\sqrt{x^2-1}}$'} 2025 2025-05-23 shift_2 mathematics   63 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: $\; y = \tan^{-1} \sqrt{x^2-1} + \sinh^{-1} \sqrt{x^2-1}$ $\; \therefore \; \frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{d}{dx} (\tan^{-1} \sqrt{x^2-1}) + \frac{d}{dx} (\sinh^{-1} \sqrt{x^2-1})$ $\; = \frac{1}{1+ (\sqrt{x^2-1})^2} \left( \frac{2x}{2 \sqrt{x^2-1}} \right) + \frac{1}{\sqrt{1+ (\sqrt{x^2-1})^2}} \left( \frac{2x}{2 \sqrt{x^2-1}} \right)$ $\; = \frac{2x}{x^2 (2 \sqrt{x^2-1})} + \frac{1}{x} \left( \frac{2x}{2 \sqrt{x^2-1}} \right)$ $\; \;\; = \; \frac{1+x}{x \sqrt{x^2-1}}$ © examsnet.com

question: If $y=(\log x)^{\frac{1}{x}}+x^{\log x}$ , at $x=e, \; \frac{dy}{dx}=$ [AP EAPCET 23 May 2025 S2]
search_text: if $y=(\log x)^{\frac{1}{x}}+x^{\log x}$ , at $x=e, \; \frac{dy}{dx}=$ [ap eapcet 23 may 2025 s2] {'a': '$2 + \\frac{1}{e}$', 'b': '$e^2 + \\frac{1}{2}$', 'c': '$\\frac{1}{e^2} + 2$', 'd': '$e + \\frac{1}{e}$'} 2025 2025-05-23 shift_2 mathematics   64 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: $y = (\log x)^{\frac{1}{x}} + \underset{v}{\;x}_{v}^{\log x}$ $\;\; \text{ so, } \; \ln(u) = \frac{1}{x} \log(\log x)$ $\frac{1}{u} \cdot \frac{du}{dx} = \frac{1}{x} \cdot \frac{1}{x \log x} + \log(\log x) \cdot \left(-\frac{1}{x^2}\right)$ $\frac{1}{x^2 \log x} - \frac{\log(\log x)}{x^2}$ $\rightarrow \left. \frac{du}{dx} \right|_{x=e} = (\log e)^{\frac{1}{e}} \left[ \frac{1}{e^2 \log e} - \frac{\log(\log e)}{e^2} \right]$ $= 1 \left[ \frac{1}{e^2} - 0 \right] = \frac{1}{e^2}$ and $\ln(y) = \log x \cdot \log(x) = (\log x)^2$ $\rightarrow \frac{1}{v} \frac{dv}{dx} = 2 \log(x) \cdot \frac{1}{x}$ $\rightarrow \frac{dv}{dx} = \eta \left[ \frac{2 \log x}{x} \right]$ at $x=e$ $= e^{\log x} \left[ \frac{2 \log x}{e} \right]$ $= e \cdot \frac{2}{e} = 2$ hence, $\left. \frac{dy}{dx} \right|_{x=e} = \frac{1}{e^2} + 2$ © examsnet.com

search_text: the interval in which the function $f(x)=\tan^{-1}(\sin x+\cos x)$ is an increasing function, is [ap eapcet 23 may 2025 s2] {'a': '$\\left(0,\\frac{\\pi}{2}\\right)$', 'b': '$\\left(-\\frac{\\pi}{2},\\frac{\\pi}{2}\\right)$', 'c': '$\\left(-\\frac{3\\pi}{4},\\frac{\\pi}{4}\\right)$', 'd': '$\\left(\\frac{\\pi}{4},\\frac{\\pi}{2}\\right)$'} 2025 2025-05-23 shift_2 mathematics   65 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: $\because \sin x+\cos x = \sqrt{2}\sin\left(x+\frac{\pi}{4}\right)$ $\therefore f(x)=\tan^{-1}\left(\sqrt{2}\sin\left(x+\frac{\pi}{4}\right)\right)$ $\text{ now, } f'(x)=\frac{1}{1+\left(\sqrt{2}\sin\left(x+\frac{\pi}{4}\right)\right)^2}$ $\left(\sqrt{2}\cos\left(x+\frac{\pi}{4}\right)\right)$ $=\frac{\sqrt{2}\cos\left(x+\frac{\pi}{4}\right)}{1+2\sin^2\left(x+\frac{\pi}{4}\right)}\longrightarrow\text{ always }>0$ for increasing $\sqrt{2}\cos\left(x+\frac{\pi}{4}\right)>0$ $\rightarrow \cos\left(x+\frac{\pi}{4}\right)>0$ so, $-\frac{\pi}{2}+2k\pi < x+\frac{\pi}{4} < \frac{\pi}{2}+2k\pi$ $\rightarrow -\frac{3\pi}{4}+2k\pi < x < \frac{\pi}{4}+2k\pi$ for the principal interval, let $k=0$ thus, the interval is $x\in\left(-\frac{3\pi}{4},\frac{\pi}{4}\right)$ © examsnet.com

question: If $\int\frac{dx}{2\cos x+3\sin x+4}=\frac{2}{\sqrt{3}}f(x)+c$ , then $f\left(\frac{2\pi}{3}\right)=$ [AP EAPCET 23 May 2025 S2]
search_text: if $\int\frac{dx}{2\cos x+3\sin x+4}=\frac{2}{\sqrt{3}}f(x)+c$ , then $f\left(\frac{2\pi}{3}\right)=$ [ap eapcet 23 may 2025 s2] {'a': '$\\frac{\\pi}{12}$', 'b': '$\\frac{\\pi}{8}$', 'c': '$\\frac{5\\pi}{12}$', 'd': '$\\frac{5\\pi}{8}$'} 2025 2025-05-23 shift_2 mathematics   72 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: $\int\frac{dx}{2\cos x+3\sin x+4}$ $\text{ let } t=\tan\frac{x}{2} \rightarrow \sin x=\frac{2t}{1+t^2}$ $\cos x=\frac{1-t^2}{1+t^2}$ $\text{ and } dx=\frac{2dt}{1+t^2}$ $=\int\frac{2dt}{(1+t^2)\left[\frac{2(1-t^2)}{1+t^2}+\frac{6t}{1+t^2}+4\right]}$ $=\int\frac{2dt}{2-2t^2+6t+4+4t^2} dt$ $=\int\frac{dt}{t^2+3t+3}=\int\frac{dt}{\left(t+\frac{3}{2}\right)^2+\frac{3}{4}}$ $\text{ put } u=t+\frac{3}{2} \rightarrow du=dt$ $=\int\frac{1}{u^2+\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)^2} du$ $=\frac{1}{\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}}\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{u}{\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}}\right)+c$ $=\frac{2}{\sqrt{3}}\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{2u}{\sqrt{3}}\right)+c$ $=\frac{2}{\sqrt{3}}\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{2t+3}{\sqrt{3}}\right)+c$ $=\frac{2}{\sqrt{3}}\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{2\tan\frac{x}{2}+3}{\sqrt{3}}\right)+c$ $\text{ thus, } f(x)=\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{2\tan\left(\frac{x}{2}\right)+3}{\sqrt{3}}\right)$ $\therefore f\left(\frac{2\pi}{3}\right)=\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{2\tan\left(\frac{\pi}{3}\right)+3}{\sqrt{3}}\right)$ $=\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{2\sqrt{3}+3}{\sqrt{3}}\right)$ $=\tan^{-1}(2+\sqrt{3})=\frac{5\pi}{12}$ © examsnet.com

search_text: if $\int \frac{1}{((x+4)^3(x+1)^5)^{1/4}} dx = a \cdot \left(\frac{x+4}{x+1}\right)^n + c$ , then [ap eapcet 23 may 2025 s2] {'a': '$n \\cdot a = 3$', 'b': '$n + \\frac{1}{a} = -\\frac{1}{2}$', 'c': '$a + n = 1$', 'd': '$a = n$'} 2025 2025-05-23 shift_2 mathematics   73 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: $\because \int \frac{1}{((x+4)^3(x+1)^5)^{\frac{1}{4}}} dx$ $= a \cdot \left(\frac{x+4}{x+1}\right)^n + c$ $= \int \frac{1}{(x+1)^2 \left(\frac{x+4}{x+1}\right)^{\frac{3}{2}}} dx$ $\text{ let } t = \frac{x+4}{x+1}$ $\rightarrow dt = \frac{-3}{(x+1)^2} dx = -\int \frac{1}{3} t^{-3/4} dt$ $= - \frac{1}{3} \left[ \frac{-\frac{3}{4}+1}{-\frac{3}{4}+1} \right] + c$ $= - \frac{1}{3} \left[ 4 t^{1/4} \right] + c$ $= - \frac{4}{3} \left(\frac{x+4}{x+1}\right)^{1/4} + c$ comparing with $a = \frac{(x+4)^n}{x+1} + c$ $a = -\frac{4}{3}, n = \frac{1}{4}$ therefore, $n + \frac{1}{a} = \frac{1}{4} + \frac{1}{ \left( -\frac{4}{3} \right) }$ $= \frac{1}{4} - \frac{3}{4}$ $= \frac{-2}{4} = \frac{-1}{2}$ © examsnet.com

search_text: $\int\limits_{0}^{400\pi} \sqrt{1-\cos 2x}\,dx=$ [ap eapcet 23 may 2025 s2] {'a': '$100\\sqrt{2}$', 'b': '$200\\sqrt{2}$', 'c': '$400\\sqrt{2}$', 'd': '$800\\sqrt{2}$'} 2025 2025-05-23 shift_2 mathematics   76 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: $i\;=\int\limits_{0}^{400\pi} \sqrt{1-\cos 2x}\,dx$ $\;=\int\limits_{0}^{400\pi} \sqrt{2\sin^2 x}\,dx$ $\;=\sqrt{2}\int\limits_{0}^{400\pi} \sin x\,dx$ $\;=400\sqrt{2}\int\limits_{0}^{\pi} \sin x\,dx$ $\;=2\times 400\sqrt{2}\int\limits_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{2}} \sin x\,dx$ $\;=800\sqrt{2}[-\cos x]_{0}^{\frac{\pi}{2}}$ $\;=800\sqrt{2}\left[-\cos\frac{\pi}{2}+\cos 0\right]$ $\;=800\sqrt{2}$ © examsnet.com

search_text: if the order and degree of the differential equation $x \;\frac{d^2 y}{d x^2}= \left(1+ \left(\;\frac{d^2 y}{d x^2}\right)^2\right)^{\frac{-1}{2}}$ are k and $l$ respectively, then $k, l$ are the roots of [ap eapcet 23 may 2025 s2] {'a': '$\\;x^2-5x+6=0$', 'b': '$\\;x^2-3x+2=0$', 'c': '$\\;x^2-7x+12=0$', 'd': '$x^2-6x+8=0$'} 2025 2025-05-23 shift_2 mathematics   78 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: $\;x \;\frac{d^2 y}{d x^2}= \left(1+ \left(\;\frac{d^2 y}{d x^2}\right)^2\right)^{\frac{-1}{2}}$ $\;\rightarrow \;\; \left[x \;\frac{d^2 y}{d x^2}\right]^2 = \left[ \left(1+ \left(\;\frac{d^2 y}{d x^2}\right)^2\right)^{\frac{-1}{2}} \right]^{-2}$ $\;\rightarrow \;\; \frac{1}{x^2 \left(\;\frac{d^2 y}{d x^2}\right)^2}=1+ \left(\;\frac{d^2 y}{d x^2}\right)^2$ $\;\rightarrow \;\; 1=x^2 \left(\;\frac{d^2 y}{d x^2}\right)^2+x^2 \left(\;\frac{d^2 y}{d x^2}\right)^4$ $\;\rightarrow \;\; x^2 \left(\;\frac{d^2 y}{d x^2}\right)^4+x^2 \left(\;\frac{d^2 y}{d x^2}\right)^2-1=0$ $\;\;\text{ so, order }\;=k=2$ $\;\;\text{ and degree }\;=l=4$ thus, quadratic equation, $\;(x-2)(x-4)=0$ $\rightarrow \;\; x^2-6x+8=0$ © examsnet.com

search_text: the equation of the curve passing through the point $(0, \pi)$ and satisfying the differential equation $y dx = (x + y^3 \cos y) dy$ is [ap eapcet 23 may 2025 s2] {'a': '$x = y^2 \\sin y + y \\cos^2 y$', 'b': '$x = y^2 \\sin y + 2 y \\cos^2 \\frac{y}{2}$', 'c': '$x = y^2 \\sin y + y \\cos^2 \\frac{y}{2}$', 'd': '$x = y^2 \\sin y - y \\cos^2 y$'} 2025 2025-05-23 shift_2 mathematics   79 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: $y dx = (x + y^3 \cos y) dy$ $\rightarrow \frac{dx}{dy} - \frac{x}{y} = y^2 \cos y$ $\therefore if = e^{\int -\frac{1}{y} dy}$ $= e^{\ln (y)^{-1}} = -\frac{1}{y}$ $\therefore \frac{1}{y} \left( \frac{dy}{dy} \right) - \frac{x}{y^2} = y \cdot \cos y$ $\rightarrow \int \frac{d}{dy} \left( \frac{x}{y} \right) dy = \int y \cdot \cos y \, dy$ $\rightarrow \frac{x}{y} = y \sin y - \int \sin y \, dy$ $x = y \sin y + \cos y + c$ $x = y^2 \sin y + y \cos y + c y$ put point ( $0, \pi$ ) into it $\rightarrow 0 = 0 - \pi + c \pi \rightarrow c = 1$ $\therefore x = y^2 \sin y + y \cos y + y$ $\rightarrow x = y^2 \sin y + y (1 + \cos y)$ $\rightarrow x = y^2 \sin y + 2 y \cos^2 \left( \frac{y}{2} \right)$ © examsnet.com

search_text: the general solution of the differential equation $(x-(x+y) \log (x+y)) dx+x d y=0$ is [ap eapcet 23 may 2025 s2] {'a': '$\\;y \\log (x+y)=c x$', 'b': '$\\;x \\log (x+y)=c y$', 'c': '$\\;\\log (x+y)=c y$', 'd': '$\\;\\log (x+y)=c x$'} 2025 2025-05-23 shift_2 mathematics   80 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: $\;(x-(x+y) \log (x+y)) dx+x d y=0$ $\;\rightarrow \;\frac{d y}{d x}=\;\frac{(x+y) \log (x+y)-x}{x}$ $\;=\;\frac{x+y}{x} \log (x+y)-1$ $\;\;\text{put.}\;\;\;\;u=x+y \rightarrow \;\frac{d u}{d x}=\;\frac{d y}{d x}+1$ $\;\rightarrow\;\;\;\frac{d y}{d x}=\;\frac{d u}{d x}-1$ $\;\rightarrow\;\;\;\frac{d u}{d x}-1=\;\frac{u}{x} \log (u)-1$ $\;\rightarrow\;\;\;\int\;\frac{d u}{u \log u}=\int\;\frac{1}{x} dx$ $\;\rightarrow\;\;\;\log (\log u)=\log x+\log (c)$ $\;\rightarrow\;\;\;\log (\log u)=\log (c x)$ $\;\rightarrow\;\;\;\log u=c x$ $\;\rightarrow\;\;\;\log (x+y)=c x \;\; ( \because u=x+y)$ © examsnet.com

search_text: if the equation for the velocity of a particle at time ' $t$ ' is $v = a t + \frac{b}{t+c}$ , then the dimensions of $a, b, c$ are respectively [ap eapcet 23 may 2025 s2] {'a': '$l t^{-2}, l, t$', 'b': '$l^2, l, t$', 'c': '$l t^{-2}, l t, l$', 'd': '$l, l t, l^2$'} 2025 2025-05-23 shift_2 physics   81 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: let's restate the given problem carefully: the velocity of a particle is given by $v = a t + \frac{b}{t+c}$ we need to find the dimensions of $a, b$ , and $c$ . step 1. dimensional formula of velocity $[v] = [l t^{-1}]$ step 2. dimensional analysis of first term at in the expression $v = a t + \frac{b}{t+c}$ , both terms on the right-hand side must have the same dimensions as velocity. the first term: $a t$ $[a][t] = [v] = [l t^{-1}]$ $[a] = \frac{[l t^{-1}]}{[t]} = [l t^{-2}]$ so, $[a] = [l t^{-2}]$ step 3. the second term $\frac{b}{t+c}$ this term must also have the dimensions of velocity: $\left[\frac{b}{t+c}\right] = [l t^{-1}]$ now, $t+c$ is a sum - you can only add quantities with the same dimensions, so: $[c] = [t] = [t]$ then, $[b] = [l t^{-1}] \cdot [t+c] = [l t^{-1}] \cdot [t] = [l]$ so, $[b] = [l]$ final dimensions: $[a] = [l t^{-2}], \quad [b] = [l], \quad [c] = [t]$ © examsnet.com

search_text: two blocks a and b of masses 2 kg and 4 kg respectively are kept on a rough horizontal surface. if same force of 20 n is applied on each block, then the ratio of the accelerations of the blocks $a$ and $b$ is (coefficient of kinetic friction between the surface and the blocks is 0.3 and acceleration due to gravity $=10\,\text{m}\,\text{s}^{-2}$ ) [ap eapcet 23 may 2025 s2] {'a': '$1: 1$', 'b': '$7: 2$', 'c': '$1: 2$', 'd': '$4: 3$'} 2025 2025-05-23 shift_2 physics   86 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: step 1: find the friction force for each block the friction force is given by: $f_{\;\text{friction}\;}=\mu_k \times m \times g$ for block $a$ (mass $=2\,\text{kg}$ ): $f_{k\,a}=0.3 \times 2 \times 10=6\,\text{n}$ for block $b$ (mass $=4\,\text{kg}$ ): $f_{k\,b}=0.3 \times 4 \times 10=12\,\text{n}$ step 2: find the net force on each block the net force is the applied force minus friction: for block $a$ : $f_a=20-6=14\,\text{n}$ for block $b$ : $f_b=20-12=8\,\text{n}$ step 3: find the acceleration of each block use $a=\;\frac{f_{n\,e\,t}}{m}$ for each block. for block $a$ : $a_a=\;\frac{14}{2}=7\,\text{m/s}^2$ for block $b$ : $a_b=\;\frac{8}{4}=2\,\text{m/s}^2$ step 4: find the ratio of accelerations $\;\frac{a_a}{a_b}=\;\frac{7}{2}$ so, the ratio is $7: 2$ . © examsnet.com

search_text: a circular well of diameter 2 m has water upto the ground level. if the bottom of the well is at a depth of 14 m , the time taken in seconds to empty the well using a 1.4 kw motor is (acceleration due to gravity $=10 \text{m} \text{s}^{-2}$ ) [ap eapcet 23 may 2025 s2] {'a': '$1860$', 'b': '$2200$', 'c': '$2660$', 'd': '$3300$'} 2025 2025-05-23 shift_2 physics   88 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: step 1: find the volume of water in the well the well is a cylinder. its diameter is 2 m , so its radius $r=1 \text{m}$ . its depth (height) $h=14 \text{m}$ . the volume formula for a cylinder is $v=\pi r^2 h$ . so, the volume of water is $v=\pi \times 1^2 \times 14 = 14 \pi$ cubic meters. step 2: find the mass of the water the density $(\rho)$ of water is $1000 \text{kg/m}^3$ . so, mass $(m)=$ volume × density $=14 \pi \times 1000 \text{kg}$ . step 3: calculate work needed to lift all the water the work to lift water from the bottom to the ground level is $w=m g h$ , where $g=10 \text{m/s}^2$ and $h$ is the height ( 14 m ). so, $w=(1000 \times 14 \pi) \times 10 \times 7$ step 4: substitute values and calculate $w=1000 \times \;\frac{22}{7} \times 1^2 \times 14 \times 10 \times 7 = 3.08 \times 10^6 \text{j}$ step 5: use the power of the motor to find time power $(p)$ is 1.4 kw , which is $1.4 \times 10^3 \text{w}$ . time $(t)=\;\frac{w}{p}=\;\frac{3.08 \times 10^6}{1.4 \times 10^3}$ . $t=22 \times 10^2 \text{s} = 2200 \text{s}$ © examsnet.com

search_text: a spring is stretched by 0.2 m when a mass of 0.5 kg is suspended to it. the time period of the spring when 0.5 kg mass is replaced with a mass of 0.25 kg is suspended to it is (acceleration due to gravity $=10\ \mathrm{m}\ \mathrm{s}^{-2}$ ) [ap eapcet 23 may 2025 s2] {'a': '$\\;0.628\\ \\mathrm{s}$', 'b': '$\\;6.28\\ \\mathrm{s}$', 'c': '$\\;62.8\\ \\mathrm{s}$', 'd': '$\\;0.0628\\ \\mathrm{s}$'} 2025 2025-05-23 shift_2 physics   92 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: step 1: find spring constant $(k)$ the spring stretches by 0.2 m when a 0.5 kg mass hangs from it. this means the force from the weight $(m_1 g)$ equals the force from the spring $(k x)$ : $k x=m_1 g$ so, $k=\;\frac{m_1 g}{x}=\;\frac{0.5 \times 10}{0.2}=25\ \mathrm{n/m}$ step 2: use the new mass the new hanging mass is $m_2=0.25\ \mathrm{kg}$ . step 3: find the new time period ( $t$ ) the time period of a mass-spring system is: $t=2\pi \sqrt{\frac{m_2}{k}}$ substitute the values: $t=2\pi \sqrt{\frac{0.25}{25}}$ $t=2\pi \sqrt{0.01}$ $t=2\pi \times 0.1=0.2\pi\ \mathrm{s}$ step 4: calculate the value using $\pi \approx 3.14$ : $t=0.2 \times 3.14=0.628\ \mathrm{s}$ © examsnet.com

question: If the longitudinal strain of a stretched wire is $0.2\%$ and the Poisson's ratio of the material of the wire is 0.3 , then the volume strain of the wire is [AP EAPCET 23 May 2025 S2]
search_text: if the longitudinal strain of a stretched wire is $0.2\%$ and the poisson's ratio of the material of the wire is 0.3 , then the volume strain of the wire is [ap eapcet 23 may 2025 s2] {'a': '$\\;0.12\\%$', 'b': '$\\;0.08\\%$', 'c': '$0.14\\%$', 'd': '$0.26\\%$'} 2025 2025-05-23 shift_2 physics   94 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: longitudinal strain, $ε_l=0.2\%=0.002$ poisson's ratio, $\mu=0.3$ we are asked to find the volume strain $(ε_v)$ . step 1: recall the formula for volume strain for small deformations, volume strain $= \varepsilon_v = \varepsilon_l (1-2\mu)$ however, to be more precise, the change in volume $\frac{\delta v}{v}=ε_l+2ε_t$ , where $\varepsilon_t = -\mu \varepsilon_l$ (lateral strain is negative if the material stretches longitudinally). so, $\;\frac{\delta v}{v}=\varepsilon_l+2(-\mu \varepsilon_l)$ $\;\rightarrow ε_v=ε_l(1-2\mu)$ step 2: substitute the values $\;ε_v=0.002(1-2\times 0.3)$ $\;ε_v=0.002(1-0.6)$ $\;ε_v=0.002\times 0.4=0.0008$ step 3: convert to percentage $ε_v=0.0008\times 100=0.08\%$ final answer: $0.08\%$ © examsnet.com

question: If two soap bubbles $A$ and $B$ of radii $r_1$ and $r_2$ respectively are kept in vaccum at constant temperature, then the ratio of masses of air inside the bubbles $A$ and $B$ is [AP EAPCET 23 May 2025 S2]
search_text: if two soap bubbles $a$ and $b$ of radii $r_1$ and $r_2$ respectively are kept in vaccum at constant temperature, then the ratio of masses of air inside the bubbles $a$ and $b$ is [ap eapcet 23 may 2025 s2] {'a': '$\\; r_2^2 : r_1^2$', 'b': '$\\; r_1^2 : r_2^2$', 'c': '$\\; r_1 : r_2$', 'd': '$r_2 : r_1$'} 2025 2025-05-23 shift_2 physics   95 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: step 1: find extra pressure inside a bubble the extra (excess) pressure inside a soap bubble is $p = \; \frac{4 t}{r}$ , where $t$ is surface tension and $r$ is the radius. so for bubble $a$ : $p_a = \; \frac{4 t}{r_1}$ and for bubble $b$ : $p_b = \; \frac{4 t}{r_2}$ step 2: use the gas law for bubbles the usual gas equation is $p v = n r t$ . here, $p$ is pressure, $v$ is volume, $n$ is the number of moles, $r$ is the gas constant, and $t$ is temperature. since the temperature is constant, $p v \propto n$ . the number of moles $n$ is related to the mass $m$ of the gas. so, $p v \propto m$ . step 3: work out the mass for each bubble for bubble $a$ : the volume of a sphere is $v_a = \; \frac{4}{3} \pi r_1^3$ . so $p_a v_a \propto m_a$ becomes: $\; \frac{4 t}{r_1} \times \; \frac{4}{3} \pi r_1^3 \propto m_a$ this simplifies to $m_a \propto r_1^2$ . for bubble $b$ : similarly, $v_b = \; \frac{4}{3} \pi r_2^3$ . so $\; \frac{4 t}{r_2} \times \; \frac{4}{3} \pi r_2^3 \propto m_b$ this gives us $m_b \propto r_2^2$ . step 4: find the ratio of the masses the ratio is $\; \frac{m_a}{m_b} = \; \frac{r_1^2}{r_2^2}$ . © examsnet.com

search_text: a small quantity of water of mass ' m ' at temperature $\theta^{\circ} \mathrm{c}$ is mixed with a large mass ' m ' of ice which is at its melting point. if ' s ' is specific heat capacity of water and ' $l$ ' is the latent heat of fusion of ice, then the mass of ice melted is [ap eapcet 23 may 2025 s2] {'a': '$\\;\\frac{ml}{m s \\theta}$', 'b': '$\\;\\frac{m s \\theta}{ml}$', 'c': '$\\;\\frac{m s \\theta}{l}$', 'd': '$\\;\\frac{m s \\theta}{l}$'} 2025 2025-05-23 shift_2 physics   96 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: when water (at temperature $\theta$ ) is mixed with ice (at $0^{\circ}$ ), heat will flow from the warmer water to the ice. the water cools down from $\theta$ to $0^{\circ} \mathrm{c}$ . the ice melts, using that heat. no heat is lost to surroundings. step 1: heat lost by water cooling to $0^{\circ} \mathrm{c}$ $q_{\;\text{lost }\;}=m s \theta$ step 2: heat gained by ice (for melting) if $x$ is the mass of ice melted, then: $q_{\;\text{gained }\;}=x l$ step 3: equating heat lost and gained $m s \theta = x l$ step 4: solve for $x$ $x = \;\frac{m s \theta}{l}$ step 5: check if $m$ (the large mass of ice) matters since $m$ is very large, its temperature doesn't rise; it only partly melts. hence $m$ appears only to indicate that the ice remains at $0^{\circ} \mathrm{c}$ . final answer: $x = \;\frac{m s \theta}{l}$ © examsnet.com

question: In a Carnot engine, if the absolute temperature of the source is $25\%$ more than the absolute temperature of the sink, then the efficiency of the engine is [AP EAPCET 23 May 2025 S2]
search_text: in a carnot engine, if the absolute temperature of the source is $25\%$ more than the absolute temperature of the sink, then the efficiency of the engine is [ap eapcet 23 may 2025 s2] {'a': '$25\\%$', 'b': '$50\\%$', 'c': '$20\\%$', 'd': '$40\\%$'} 2025 2025-05-23 shift_2 physics   97 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: the efficiency formula for a carnot engine is: $\eta = 1 - \frac{t_2}{t_1}$ here, $t_1$ is the absolute temperature of the source, and $t_2$ is the absolute temperature of the sink. the problem says the source is $25\%$ hotter than the sink. that means: $t_1 = t_2 + 0.25 \times t_2 = 1.25 t_2$ now, plug $t_1 = 1.25 t_2$ into the efficiency formula: $\eta = 1 - \frac{t_2}{1.25 t_2}$ $\eta = 1 - \frac{1}{1.25}$ $\frac{1}{1.25} = \frac{4}{5}$ so, $\eta = 1 - \frac{4}{5}$ $\eta = \frac{1}{5}$ to change this to a percentage, multiply by $100\%$ : $\eta = \frac{1}{5} \times 100\% = 20\%$ so, the engine's efficiency is $20\%$ . © examsnet.com

question: One of the two identical capacitors having the same capacitance $C$ , is charged to a potential $V_1$ and the other is charged to a potential $V_2$ . If they are connected with their like plates together, then the decrease in the electrostatic potential energy of the combined system is [AP EAPCET 23 May 2025 S2]
search_text: one of the two identical capacitors having the same capacitance $c$ , is charged to a potential $v_1$ and the other is charged to a potential $v_2$ . if they are connected with their like plates together, then the decrease in the electrostatic potential energy of the combined system is [ap eapcet 23 may 2025 s2] {'a': '$\\; \\frac{c}{4} (v_1^2-v_2^2)$', 'b': '$\\; \\frac{c}{4} (v_1^2+v_2^2)$', 'c': '$\\; \\frac{c}{4} (v_1-v_2)^2$', 'd': '$\\; \\frac{c}{4} (v_1+v_2)^2$'} 2025 2025-05-23 shift_2 physics   105 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: $u_i\;=\;\frac{1}{2} c v_1^2+\;\frac{1}{2} c v_2^2$ $\;=\;\frac{1}{2} c (v_1^2+v_2^2)$ common potential, $v\;=\;\frac{q_1+q_2}{c_1+c_2}=\;\frac{c v_1+c v_2}{c+c}$ $\;=\;\frac{v_1+v_2}{2}$ $\rightarrow \; v\;=\;\frac{v_1+v_2}{2}$ $\therefore \; u_f\;=\;\frac{1}{2} c^1 v^2$ $\;=\;\frac{1}{2}(2 c) \left(\frac{v_1+v_2}{2}\right)^2 = c \left(\frac{v_1+v_2}{2}\right)^2$ $\therefore \; \delta u = u_i - u_f$ $= \;\; \frac{1}{2} c (v_1^2+v_2^2) - c \left(\frac{v_1+v_2}{2}\right)^2$ $= \;\; \frac{c}{2} (v_1^2+v_2^2) - \; \frac{c}{4} (v_1^2+v_2^2+2 v_1 v_2)$ $= \;\; \frac{c}{4} \left[ 2 v_1^2+2 v_2^2-v_1^2-v_2^2-2 v_1 v_2 \right]$ $= \;\; \frac{c}{4} \left[ v_1^2+v_2^2-2 v_1 v_2 \right] = \; \frac{c}{4} (v_1-v_2)^2$ © examsnet.com

question: If the energy stored in a spherical conductor having a charge of $12 \mu \mathrm{C}$ is 6 J , then the radius of the spherical conductor is [AP EAPCET 23 May 2025 S2]
search_text: if the energy stored in a spherical conductor having a charge of $12 \mu \mathrm{c}$ is 6 j , then the radius of the spherical conductor is [ap eapcet 23 may 2025 s2] {'a': '$10.8 \\mathrm{cm}$', 'b': '$0.108 \\mathrm{cm}$', 'c': '$1.08 \\mathrm{cm}$', 'd': '$108 \\mathrm{cm}$'} 2025 2025-05-23 shift_2 physics   106 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: the energy stored in a capacitor is given by the formula: $u=\frac{q^2}{2c}$ where $u$ is energy, $q$ is charge, and $c$ is capacitance. step 2: rearranging to find capacitance we can solve for $c$ as follows: $c=\frac{q^2}{2u}$ here, $q=12 \times 10^{-6} \mathrm{c}$ and $u=6 \mathrm{j}$ . substitute these values into the formula: $c=\frac{(12 \times 10^{-6})^2}{2 \times 6}$ step 3: calculate capacitance simplify the above equation: $c=12 \times 10^{-12} \mathrm{f}$ step 4: capacitance of a spherical conductor the capacitance of a spherical conductor is given by: $c=4 \pi \varepsilon_0 r$ step 5: find the radius rearrange to find the radius $r: r=\frac{c}{4 \pi \varepsilon_0}$ we can also use $\frac{1}{4 \pi \varepsilon_0}=9 \times 10^9 \mathrm{n m^2 / c^2}$ so: $r=9 \times 10^9 \times 12 \times 10^{-12}$ step 6: solve for the radius multiply the values: $r=108 \times 10^{-3}=0.108 \mathrm{m}=10.8 \mathrm{cm}$ © examsnet.com

search_text: a dc supply of 160 v is used to charge a battery of emf 10 v and internal resistance $1\ \omega$ by connecting a series resistance of $24\ \omega$ . the terminal voltage of the battery during charging is [ap eapcet 23 may 2025 s2] {'a': '$\\;8\\ \\mathrm{v}$', 'b': '$\\;12\\ \\mathrm{v}$', 'c': '$\\;16\\ \\mathrm{v}$', 'd': '$\\;4\\ \\mathrm{v}$'} 2025 2025-05-23 shift_2 physics   108 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: terminal voltage of the battery during charging, $v=e+i r$ here, $e=10$ volt net emf in the circuit $e^{'}\;=v_{\;\text{supply }\;}-e=160-10$ $\;=150\ \mathrm{v}$ $\therefore \;\; i\;=\;\frac{e^{'}}{r+r}\;=\;\frac{150}{24+1}\;=\;\frac{150}{25}=6\ \mathrm{a}$ ∴ from eqn (i) $v\;=e+i r$ $\;=10+6\times 1$ $\;=16\ \mathrm{v}$ © examsnet.com

search_text: the work done in rotating a bar magnet which is initially in the direction of a uniform magnetic field through $45^{\circ}$ is w . the additional work to be done to rotate the magnet further through $15^{\circ}$ is [ap eapcet 23 may 2025 s2] {'a': '$\\;\\;\\frac{w}{\\sqrt{2}}$', 'b': '$\\;\\;\\frac{w}{2}$', 'c': '$\\;w \\sqrt{2}$', 'd': '$\\;2 w$'} 2025 2025-05-23 shift_2 physics   111 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: $w=m b (\cos \theta_1 - \cos \theta_2)$ initially, $\theta_1=0^{\circ}, \theta_2=45^{\circ}$ $\therefore w_1\;=m b (\cos 0 - \cos 45^{\circ})$ $\;=m b \left(1-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right)$ $\;= \left(\frac{\sqrt{2}-1}{\sqrt{2}}\right) m b$ again, $\theta_2=45^{\circ}+15^{\circ}=60^{\circ}$ $\therefore w_2\;=m b (\cos 45^{\circ} - \cos 60^{\circ})$ $\;=m b \left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}-\frac{1}{2}\right)$ $\;=m b \left(\frac{\sqrt{2}-1}{2}\right)$ $\therefore \frac{w_2}{w_1}\;=\;\frac{m b \left(\frac{\sqrt{2}-1}{2}\right)}{m b \left(\frac{\sqrt{2}-1}{\sqrt{2}}\right)} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$ $\rightarrow w_2\;=\;\frac{w_1}{\sqrt{2}} = \frac{w}{\sqrt{2}}$ © examsnet.com

question: When a current of 4 mA passes through an inductor, if the flux linked with it is $32 \times 10^{-6} \mathrm{T} \mathrm{m}^2$ , then the energy stored in the inductor is [AP EAPCET 23 May 2025 S2]
search_text: when a current of 4 ma passes through an inductor, if the flux linked with it is $32 \times 10^{-6} \mathrm{t} \mathrm{m}^2$ , then the energy stored in the inductor is [ap eapcet 23 may 2025 s2] {'a': '$64 \\times 10^{-9} \\mathrm{j}$', 'b': '$32 \\times 10^{-9} \\mathrm{j}$', 'c': '$128 \\times 10^{-9} \\mathrm{j}$', 'd': '$96 \\times 10^{-9} \\mathrm{j}$'} 2025 2025-05-23 shift_2 physics   112 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: we are given: current $i=4 \mathrm{ma}=4 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{a}$ and flux $\phi = 32 \times 10^{-6} \mathrm{t} \mathrm{m}^2$ . step 1: find the inductance ( $l$ ). the relationship between flux, inductance, and current is $\phi = l i$ . so, $l = \frac{\phi}{i} = \frac{32 \times 10^{-6}}{4 \times 10^{-3}} = 8 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{h}$ . step 2: find the energy stored in the inductor. the formula for energy stored is $e = \frac{1}{2} l i^2$ . plug in the values: $e = \frac{1}{2} \times 8 \times 10^{-3} \times (4 \times 10^{-3})^2$ . calculate the value: $e = 64 \times 10^{-9} \mathrm{j}$ . © examsnet.com

search_text: in a series resonant lcr circuit, for the power dissipated to become half of the maximum power dissipated, the current amplitude is [ap eapcet 23 may 2025 s2] {'a': '$\\; \\frac{1}{\\sqrt{2}}$ times its maximum value.', 'b': '$\\; \\frac{1}{2}$ times its maximum value.', 'c': 'twice its maximum value.', 'd': '$\\sqrt{2}$ times its maximum value.'} 2025 2025-05-23 shift_2 physics   113 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: we need to find: for the power dissipated to become half of its maximum value, what is the current amplitude? step 1: relation between power and current the average power dissipated in an ac circuit is given by: $p = i_{\text{rms}}^2 r$ at resonance, the impedance is purely resistive ( $z = r$ ), and the current is maximum ( $i = i_{\text{ max }}$ ). so maximum power is: $p_{\text{max}} = i_{\text{rms, max}}^2 \;\; r = \left( \frac{i_{\text{max}}}{\sqrt{2}} \right)^2 r = \frac{i_{\text{max}}^2 \;\; r}{2}$ but we only need relative power, so we can use $p \propto i^2$ . step 2: condition for half power we are told $p = \frac{1}{2} p_{\text{ max }}$ so: $i^2 r = \frac{1}{2} i_{\text{max}}^2 r$ simplify: $i = \frac{i_{\text{max}}}{\sqrt{2}}$ so the current amplitude becomes $\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$ times its maximum value when the power is half of the maximum. © examsnet.com

question: If the de Broglie wavelength of an electron is 2 nm , then its kinetic energy is nearly (Planck's constant $=6.6 \times 10^{-34} \text{ J}$ s and mass of electron $=9 \times 10^{-31} \text{ kg}$ ) [AP EAPCET 23 May 2025 S2]
search_text: if the de broglie wavelength of an electron is 2 nm , then its kinetic energy is nearly (planck's constant $=6.6 \times 10^{-34} \text{ j}$ s and mass of electron $=9 \times 10^{-31} \text{ kg}$ ) [ap eapcet 23 may 2025 s2] {'a': '$0.48 \\text{ ev}$', 'b': '$0.68 \\text{ ev}$', 'c': '$0.38 \\text{ ev}$', 'd': '$0.25 \\text{ ev}$'} 2025 2025-05-23 shift_2 physics   115 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: the de-broglie wavelength is given by: $\lambda = \frac{h}{\sqrt{2 m k}}$ step 2: rearranging to find kinetic energy we can rearrange the formula to find kinetic energy $k: \lambda^2 = \frac{h^2}{2 m k}$ so, $k = \frac{h^2}{2 m \lambda^2}$ step 3: substitute the values here, planck's constant, $h = 6.6 \times 10^{-34} \text{ js}$ mass of electron, $m = 9 \times 10^{-31} \text{ kg}$ wavelength, $\lambda = 2 \text{ nm} = 2 \times 10^{-9} \text{ m}$ now substitute these into the formula: $k = \frac{(6.6 \times 10^{-34})^2}{2 \times 9 \times 10^{-31} \times (2 \times 10^{-9})^2}$ step 4: calculation calculate the value: $k = \frac{(6.6 \times 10^{-34})^2}{2 \times 9 \times 10^{-31} \times (2 \times 10^{-9})^2}$ this gives: $k = 0.608 \times 10^{-19} \text{ j}$ step 5: convert joules to electron volts 1 electron volt $( \text{ev} ) = 1.6 \times 10^{-19} \text{ j}$ . so, $k = \frac{0.608 \times 10^{-19}}{1.6 \times 10^{-19}} \text{ ev} = 0.38 \text{ ev}$ the kinetic energy of the electron is about 0.38 ev . © examsnet.com

question: The ratio of the wavelengths of the spectral lines emitted due to transitions $3 \rightarrow 2$ and $2 \rightarrow 1$ orbits in the hydrogen atom is [AP EAPCET 23 May 2025 S2]
search_text: the ratio of the wavelengths of the spectral lines emitted due to transitions $3 \rightarrow 2$ and $2 \rightarrow 1$ orbits in the hydrogen atom is [ap eapcet 23 may 2025 s2] {'a': '$3: 1$', 'b': '$9: 17$', 'c': '$27: 5$', 'd': '$25: 9$'} 2025 2025-05-23 shift_2 physics   116 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: $\frac{1}{\lambda}=r\left(\frac{1}{n_1^2}-\frac{1}{n_2^2}\right)$ $\frac{1}{\lambda_{3 \rightarrow 2}}=r\left(\frac{1}{2^2}-\frac{1}{3^2}\right)$ $\frac{1}{\lambda_{3 \rightarrow 2}}=\frac{5r}{36} \rightarrow \lambda_{3 \rightarrow 2}=\frac{36}{5r}$ $\text{ and } \frac{1}{\lambda_{2 \rightarrow 1}}=r\left(\frac{1}{1^2}-\frac{1}{2^2}\right)=\frac{3r}{4}$ $\rightarrow \lambda_{2 \rightarrow 1}=\frac{4}{3r}$ $\therefore \frac{\lambda_{3 \rightarrow 2}}{\lambda_{2 \rightarrow 1}} = \frac{\frac{36}{5r}}{\frac{4}{3r}}$ $=\frac{36 \times 3r}{5r \times 4}=\frac{27}{5}$ © examsnet.com

question: The density (in $\mathrm{kg}\,\mathrm{m}^{-3}$ ) of nuclear matter is of the order of [AP EAPCET 23 May 2025 S2]
search_text: the density (in $\mathrm{kg}\,\mathrm{m}^{-3}$ ) of nuclear matter is of the order of [ap eapcet 23 may 2025 s2] {'a': '$10^{21}$', 'b': '$10^{17}$', 'c': '$10^{12}$', 'd': '$10^8$'} 2025 2025-05-23 shift_2 physics   117 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: a nucleus has: radius $r=r_0 a^{\frac{1}{3}}$ , where $r_0 \approx 1.2 \times 10^{-15} \,\mathrm{m}$ each nucleon (proton or neutron) has a mass $m_n \approx 1.67 \times 10^{-27} \,\mathrm{kg}$ step 2: estimate the number of nucleons per unit volume for nuclear matter, the volume per nucleon is roughly the volume of a sphere of radius $r_0$ : $v_{\;\text{per nucleon}\;} \;\; \approx \;\frac{4}{3} \pi r_0^3$ $v_{\;\text{per nucleon}\;} \;\; \approx \;\frac{4}{3} \pi (1.2 \times 10^{-15})^3 \approx 7.2 \times 10^{-45} \,\mathrm{m}^3$ hence, number density of nucleons: $n=\;\frac{1}{v_{\;\text{per nucleon}\;}} \approx \;\frac{1}{7.2 \times 10^{-45}} \approx 1.4 \times 10^{44} \,\mathrm{m}^{-3}$ step 3: compute the mass density $\rho = n \times m_n = (1.4 \times 10^{44}) (1.67 \times 10^{-27}) \approx 2.3 \times 10^{17} \,\mathrm{kg}\,\mathrm{m}^{-3}$ density of nuclear matter $\sim 10^{17} \,\mathrm{kg}\,\mathrm{m}^{-3}$ © examsnet.com

question: In common emitter amplifier of a transistor, if the ratio of the voltage gain and current amplification factor is 4 , then the ratio of the collector and base resistances is [AP EAPCET 23 May 2025 S2]
search_text: in common emitter amplifier of a transistor, if the ratio of the voltage gain and current amplification factor is 4 , then the ratio of the collector and base resistances is [ap eapcet 23 may 2025 s2] {'a': '$16: 1$', 'b': '$1: 16$', 'c': '$1: 4$', 'd': '$4: 1$'} 2025 2025-05-23 shift_2 physics   118 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: the question tells us that the voltage gain divided by the current amplification factor ( $\beta$ ) equals 4. we know that the formula for voltage gain in a common emitter amplifier is $a_v = \; \frac{\beta \times r_c}{r_b}$ , where $r_c$ is collector resistance and $r_b$ is base resistance. so if we divide $a_v$ by $\beta$ , we get: $\frac{a_v}{\beta} = \frac{ \; \frac{\beta \times r_c}{r_b} }{\beta}$ this simplifies to: $\frac{r_c}{r_b}$ the question gives $\frac{a_v}{\beta}=4$ , so: $\frac{r_c}{r_b}=4$ this means the ratio of collector resistance to base resistance is $4: 1$ . © examsnet.com

search_text: the uncertainty in the velocities of two particles a and b are 0.03 and 0.01 $\mathrm{m}\,\mathrm{s}^{-1}$ respectively. the mass of $b$ is four times to the mass of $a$ . the ratio of uncertainties in their positions is [ap eapcet 23 may 2025 s2] {'a': '$\\frac{3}{4}$', 'b': '$\\frac{16}{9}$', 'c': '$\\frac{9}{16}$', 'd': '$\\;{9}/{16}$'} 2025 2025-05-23 shift_2 chemistry   121 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: uncertainty principle for particle $\delta x_a (m_a \cdot \delta v_a) = \frac{h}{4\pi} \; \cdot \cdot \cdot \cdot \cdot \cdot \cdot (i)$ ; $b$ for particle $\delta x_b (m_b \cdot \delta v_b) = \frac{h}{4\pi} \; \cdot \cdot \cdot \cdot \cdot \cdot \cdot (ii)$ , $\frac{\delta x_a}{\delta x_b} = \frac{m_b \cdot \delta v_b}{m_a \cdot \delta v_a}$ divide eq. (i) by eq. (ii) $m_b = 4 m_a, \delta v_a = 0.03$ now substitute the given value $\delta v_b = 0.01$ $\frac{\delta x_a}{\delta x_b} = \frac{0.04}{0.03} = \frac{4}{3}$ $\frac{4}{3}$ © examsnet.com

[ap eapcet 23 may 2025 s2] {'a': '$0.4$', 'b': '$0.8$', 'c': '$0.5$', 'd': '$0.6$'} 2025 2025-05-23 shift_2 chemistry   127 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: total moles of gas, $n_{\;\text{total }\;}\;\;=\;\frac{\;\text{ volume }\;}{\;\text{ molar volume at stp }\;}$ $\;\;=\;\frac{28}{224}=1.25\text{ moles}$ $\;\mathrm{c}_2\mathrm{h}_6+\frac{7}{2}\mathrm{o}_2\rightarrow 2\mathrm{co}_2+3\mathrm{h}_2\mathrm{o}$ $\;\mathrm{c}_2\mathrm{h}_4+3\mathrm{o}_2\rightarrow 2\mathrm{co}_2+2\mathrm{h}_2\mathrm{o}$ moles of $\mathrm{o}_2=\frac{128}{32}=4\text{ mol}$ let $x$ be the moles of $\mathrm{c}_2\mathrm{h}_6$ and $y$ be moles of $\mathrm{c}_2\mathrm{h}_4$ $\;x+y=1.25$ $\;\;\frac{7}{2}x+3y=4$ solve for $y, y=0.75\text{ mol}$ mole fraction of $\mathrm{c}_2\mathrm{h}_4=\frac{0.75}{1.25}=0.6$ © examsnet.com

[ap eapcet 23 may 2025 s2] {'a': '$4.25$', 'b': '$2.5$', 'c': '$1.75$', 'd': '$8.50$'} 2025 2025-05-23 shift_2 chemistry   128 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: the balanced equation for complete reaction is, $2\mathrm{c}_2\mathrm{h}_6+7\mathrm{o}_2\rightarrow4\mathrm{co}_2+6\mathrm{h}_2\mathrm{o}$ moles of $\mathrm{c}_2\mathrm{h}_6=\frac{15\ \mathrm{g}}{30.07}=0.499\ \mathrm{mol}$ moles of $\mathrm{o}_2=\frac{112}{32}=3.50\ \mathrm{mol}$ moles of $\mathrm{o}_2$ required for 0.499 mol of $\mathrm{c}_2\mathrm{h}_6$ $0.499\times\frac{7}{2}=1.747\ \mathrm{mol}\ \mathrm{o}_2$ since, $3.50\ \mathrm{mol},\ \mathrm{o}_2$ is available and only 1.747 mol . $\mathrm{o}_2$ is needed, $\mathrm{c}_2\mathrm{h}_6$ is limiting reactant. mol of $\mathrm{co}_2$ produced $0.499\times\frac{4}{2}=0.998\ \mathrm{mol}\ \mathrm{co}_2$ mol of $\mathrm{h}_2\mathrm{o}$ produced $0.499\times\frac{6}{2}=1.497\ \mathrm{mol}\ \mathrm{h}_2\mathrm{o}$ moles of excess $\mathrm{o}_2=3.50-1.747$ $=1.753\ \mathrm{mol}$ total mol of gaseous substance, $0.998+1.497+1.753=4.25\ \mathrm{mol}$ © examsnet.com

search_text: enthalpy of formation of $\mathrm{co}_2(g), \mathrm{h}_2\mathrm{o}(l)$ and $\mathrm{c}_6\mathrm{h}_{12}\mathrm{o}_6(s)$ are $-393,-286$ and $-1170\ \mathrm{kj}\ \mathrm{mol}^{-1}$ respectively. the quantity of heat liberated when 18 g of $\mathrm{c}_6\mathrm{h}_{12}\mathrm{o}_6(s)$ is burnt completely in oxygen is [ap eapcet 23 may 2025 s2] {'a': '$520\\ \\mathrm{kj}$', 'b': '$145\\ \\mathrm{kj}$', 'c': '$290\\ \\mathrm{kj}$', 'd': '$420\\ \\mathrm{kj}$'} 2025 2025-05-23 shift_2 chemistry   130 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: the complete combustion reaction is $\; \mathrm{c_6h_{12}o_6}(s)+6\,\mathrm{o_2}(g) \rightarrow 6\,\mathrm{co_2}(g)+6\,\mathrm{h_2 0}(n)$ $\; \delta h^{\circ}_{\text{comb}} = \sum \delta h^{\circ}_{\text{froduct}} - \sum \delta h^{\circ}_{\text{frectant}}$ $\; = [6 \times (-393) + 6 \times (-286)] - [1 \times (-1170) + 6 \times 0]$ $\; = -2904\ \mathrm{kj}$ $\; \text{ moles of glucose } \;\; = \frac{\; \text{ mass } \;}{\; \text{ molar mass } \;} = \frac{18\ \mathrm{g}}{180}$ $\; = 0.1\ \mathrm{mol}$ $\; \text{ heat liberated } \;\; = \text{ moles } \times \delta h^{\circ}_{\text{combustion}}$ $\; = 0.1 \times (-2904)$ $\;\; \approx -290\ \mathrm{kj}$ © examsnet.com

question: The percentage of ionization of 1 L of $x \mathrm{M}$ acetic acid is 4.242 and is called solution "A". The percentage of ionization of 1 L of $y \mathrm{M}$ acetic acid is 3 and is called solution "B". Solution "A" is mixed with solution "B". What is the concentration of acetic acid in the resultant solution? $( K_{a}.$ of acetic acid $=1.8 \times 10^{-5})$ [AP EAPCET 23 May 2025 S2]
search_text: the percentage of ionization of 1 l of $x \mathrm{m}$ acetic acid is 4.242 and is called solution "a". the percentage of ionization of 1 l of $y \mathrm{m}$ acetic acid is 3 and is called solution "b". solution "a" is mixed with solution "b". what is the concentration of acetic acid in the resultant solution? $( k_{a}.$ of acetic acid $=1.8 \times 10^{-5})$ [ap eapcet 23 may 2025 s2] {'a': '$\\;0.05 \\mathrm{m}$', 'b': '$\\;0.015 \\mathrm{m}$', 'c': '$\\;0.02 \\mathrm{m}$', 'd': '$\\;0.15 \\mathrm{m}$'} 2025 2025-05-23 shift_2 chemistry   131 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: convert the percentage ionisation to decimal $\alpha_a \; = \; \frac{4.242}{100} = 0.04242$ $\alpha \; = \sqrt{ \frac{k_\alpha}{c} }$ $\rightarrow \; \; c_a \; = \; \frac{k_\alpha}{\alpha_a^2}$ $c_a \; = \; \frac{1.8 \times 10^{-5}}{(0.04242^2.}, c_a = 0.01 \mathrm{m}$ $\alpha_b \; = \; \frac{3}{100} = 0.03$ $c_b \; = \; \frac{k_\alpha}{\alpha_b^2} = \; \frac{1.8 \times 10^{-5}}{(0.03)^2} = 0.02 \mathrm{m}$ moles from solution $a$ , $n_a = c_a \times v_a = 0.01 \mathrm{m} \times 1 \mathrm{l} = 0.01 \mathrm{mol}$ $n_b = c_b \times v_b = 0.02 \mathrm{m} \times 1 \mathrm{l} = 0.02 \mathrm{mol}$ $n_{\text{total}} = n_a + n_b = 0.03 \mathrm{mol}$ $v_{\text{total}} = v_a + v_b = 1 + 1 = 2 \mathrm{l}$ $c_{\text{final}} = \frac{n_{\text{total}}}{v_{\text{total}}} = \frac{0.03}{2 \mathrm{l}} = 0.015 \mathrm{m}$ © examsnet.com
