question: If the range of a body projected with a velocity of $60\ \mathrm{m}\ \mathrm{s}^{-1}$ is $180\sqrt{3}\ \mathrm{m}$ , then the angle of projection of the body is (Acceleration due to gravity $=10\ \mathrm{m}\ \mathrm{s}^{-2}$ ) [AP EAPCET 24 May 2025 S1]
search_text: if the range of a body projected with a velocity of $60\ \mathrm{m}\ \mathrm{s}^{-1}$ is $180\sqrt{3}\ \mathrm{m}$ , then the angle of projection of the body is (acceleration due to gravity $=10\ \mathrm{m}\ \mathrm{s}^{-2}$ ) [ap eapcet 24 may 2025 s1] {'a': '$30^{\\circ}$ or $60^{\\circ}$', 'b': '$37^{\\circ}$ or $53^{\\circ}$', 'c': '$20^{\\circ}$ or $70^{\\circ}$', 'd': '$15^{\\circ}$ or $75^{\\circ}$'} 2025 2025-05-24 shift_1 physics   83 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: step 1: write the formula for range the formula to find the range $r$ when a body is projected is: $r = \frac{u^2 \sin 2\theta}{g}$ step 2: put in the given values here, $r = 180\sqrt{3}\ \mathrm{m},\ u = 60\ \mathrm{m/s}$ , and $g = 10\ \mathrm{m/s^2}$ . step 3: arrange the formula to find $\sin 2\theta$ $\sin 2\theta = \frac{r g}{u^2}$ step 4: substitute the values $\sin 2\theta = \frac{180\sqrt{3} \times 10}{60 \times 60}$ $\sin 2\theta = \frac{1800\sqrt{3}}{3600} = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$ step 5: identify the angle for $\sin 2\theta$ we know that $\sin 60^{\circ} = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$ . so, $2\theta = 60^{\circ}$ $\theta = 30^{\circ}$ step 6: check for other possible angles the range at angle $\theta$ is the same as at $90^{\circ} - \theta$ . so, the angle of projection can be $30^{\circ}$ or $60^{\circ}$ . © examsnet.com

search_text: if the height of a projectile at a time of 2 s from the beginning of motion is 60 m , then the time of flight of the projectile is (acceleration due to gravity $=10\,\text{m}\,\text{s}^{-2}$ ) [ap eapcet 24 may 2025 s1] {'a': '$12\\,\\text{s}$', 'b': '$4\\,\\text{s}$', 'c': '$6\\,\\text{s}$', 'd': '$8\\,\\text{s}$'} 2025 2025-05-24 shift_1 physics   84 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: considering vertical motion, $u_y=u \sin \theta,\, s_y=60\,\text{m}$ $a_y=-10\,\mathrm{m}\,\mathrm{s}^{-2},\, t=2\,\text{s}$ using $s_y=u_y t+\frac{1}{2} a_y t^2$ we get, $60=u \sin \theta \times 2-\frac{1}{2} \times 10 \times 2^2$ $\rightarrow u \sin \theta =40$ now, time of flight is $t=\frac{2 n \sin \theta}{g}=\frac{2 \times 40}{10}=8\,\text{s}$ © examsnet.com

If the bullets rebound with the same speed, then the speed of each bullet is (Acceleration due to gravity $=10\ \mathrm{ms}^{-2}$ ) [AP EAPCET 24 May 2025 S1]
search_text: a disc of mass 0.2 kg is kept floating in air without falling by vertically firing bullets each of mass 0.05 kg on the disc at the rate of 10 bullets per every second. if the bullets rebound with the same speed, then the speed of each bullet is (acceleration due to gravity $=10\ \mathrm{ms}^{-2}$ ) [ap eapcet 24 may 2025 s1] {'a': '$\\;2\\ \\mathrm{m\\,s^{-1}}$', 'b': '$\\;10\\ \\mathrm{m\\,s^{-1}}$', 'c': '$\\;20\\ \\mathrm{m\\,s^{-1}}$', 'd': '$1\\ \\mathrm{m\\,s^{-1}}$'} 2025 2025-05-24 shift_1 physics   85 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: as disc is floating in air without falling, force by bullets balances gravitational force. $\rightarrow \; \left( \frac{n \delta p}{\delta t} \right) = m_d g$ here, $n=$ number of bullets fired $\; \frac{\delta p}{\delta t} =$ rate of change of one bullet $m_d=$ mass of disc hence, bullets rebound with same speed, momentum change for each bullet $=m(v-(-v))=2 m v$ $\therefore \; \frac{n}{t} \cdot 2 m_b v = m_d g$ substituting given values, $10 \times 2 \times 0.05 \times v = 0.2 \times 10$ $\therefore \; v = \frac{0.2 \times 10}{10 \times 2 \times 0.05} = 2\ \text{m/s}$ © examsnet.com

search_text: a body moving along a straight line collides another body of same mass moving in the same direction with half of the velocity of the first body. if the coefficient of restitution between the two bodies is 0.5 , then the ratio of the velocities of the two bodies after collision is (treat the collision as one dimensional) [ap eapcet 24 may 2025 s1] {'a': '$2:5$', 'b': '$2:3$', 'c': '$5:7$', 'd': '$3:7$'} 2025 2025-05-24 shift_1 physics   88 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: let initial velocities are $u$ and $\; \frac{u}{2}$ and final velocities are $v_a$ and $v_b$ . then, momentum is conserved, $m u + \frac{m u}{2} = m v_a + m v_b$ or $v_a + v_b = \frac{3 u}{2}$ coefficient of restitution is 0.5 , $\rightarrow e = \frac{v_b - v_a}{u_a - u_b} = \frac{v_b - v_a}{u - \left(\frac{u}{2}\right)}$ $\rightarrow v_b - v_a = \frac{u}{4} \ldots (ii)$ from (i) and (ii) $v_b = \frac{7}{8} \cdot u$ and from (i) and (iii) $v_a = \frac{5}{8} u$ hence, ratio $\frac{v_a}{v_b} = \frac{\frac{5}{8}}{\frac{7}{8}} = \frac{5}{7}$ © examsnet.com

question: The time period of a simple pendulum on the surface of the earth is T . If the pendulum is taken to a height equal to half of the radius of the earth, then its time period is [AP EAPCET 24 May 2025 S1]
search_text: the time period of a simple pendulum on the surface of the earth is t . if the pendulum is taken to a height equal to half of the radius of the earth, then its time period is [ap eapcet 24 may 2025 s1] {'a': '$\\frac{t}{2}$', 'b': '$\\frac{3t}{2}$', 'c': '$2t$', 'd': '$3t$'} 2025 2025-05-24 shift_1 physics   91 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: time period of a simple pendulum on the surface of the earth is $t = 2\pi \sqrt{\frac{l}{g}}$ at a height $h = \frac{r}{2}$ above the earth's surface, the acceleration due to gravity is $g_h = g \left( \frac{r}{r+h} \right)^2 = g \left( \frac{r}{r + \frac{r}{2}} \right)^2 = g \left( \frac{2}{3} \right)^2 = \frac{4}{9} g$ so the time period at that height becomes $t' = 2\pi \sqrt{\frac{l}{g_h}} = 2\pi \sqrt{\frac{l}{\frac{4}{9} g}} = \frac{3}{2} \left( 2\pi \sqrt{\frac{l}{g}} \right)$ $\therefore t' = \frac{3}{2} t$ hence the correct option is $\frac{3t}{2}$ . © examsnet.com

question: A particle is executing simple harmonic motion starting from its mean position. If the time period of the particle is 1.5 s , then the minimum time at which the ratio of the kinetic and total energies of the particle becomes $3 : 4$ is [AP EAPCET 24 May 2025 S1]
search_text: a particle is executing simple harmonic motion starting from its mean position. if the time period of the particle is 1.5 s , then the minimum time at which the ratio of the kinetic and total energies of the particle becomes $3 : 4$ is [ap eapcet 24 may 2025 s1] {'a': '$\\frac{1}{4}\\ \\mathrm{s}$', 'b': '$\\frac{1}{12}\\ \\mathrm{s}$', 'c': '$\\frac{1}{8}\\ \\mathrm{s}$', 'd': '$\\frac{1}{6}\\ \\mathrm{s}$'} 2025 2025-05-24 shift_1 physics   92 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: for particle in shm, $t = 1.5\ \mathrm{sso}$ $\omega = \frac{2\pi}{t} = \frac{4\pi}{3}\ \mathrm{rad/s}$ let oscillations starts from $t = 0$ and $x = a \sin \omega t$ is displacement equation then, ke at time $t$ is, $k = \frac{1}{2} m v^{2} = \frac{1}{2} m \left(\frac{dx}{dt}\right)^{2}$ $= \frac{1}{2} m \cdot a^{2} \omega^{2} \cos^{2} \omega t \cdots (i)$ and total energy of particle is, $e = \frac{1}{2} k a^{2}$ here, $k = m \omega^{2}$ $= \frac{1}{2} m a^{2} \omega^{2} \cdots (ii)$ given, ratio, $\frac{k}{e} = \frac{3}{4}$ $\rightarrow \frac{ \frac{1}{2} m a^{2} \omega^{2} \cos^{2} \omega t }{ \frac{1}{2} m a^{2} \omega^{2} } = \frac{3}{4}$ $\rightarrow \cos^{2} \omega t = \frac{3}{4}$ $\rightarrow \cos \omega t = \sqrt{ \frac{3}{2} }$ $\rightarrow \omega t = \frac{\pi}{6}$ $\rightarrow t = \frac{\pi}{6\omega} = \frac{\pi \times 3}{6 \times 4\pi} = \frac{1}{8}\ \mathrm{s}$ © examsnet.com

question: If the escape velocity of a body from the surface of the earth is $11.2\,\mathrm{km}\,\mathrm{s}^{-1}$ , then the orbital velocity of a satellite in an orbit which is at a height equal to the radius of the earth is [AP EAPCET 24 May 2025 S1]
search_text: if the escape velocity of a body from the surface of the earth is $11.2\,\mathrm{km}\,\mathrm{s}^{-1}$ , then the orbital velocity of a satellite in an orbit which is at a height equal to the radius of the earth is [ap eapcet 24 may 2025 s1] {'a': '$11.2\\,\\mathrm{km}\\,\\mathrm{s}^{-1}$', 'b': '$2.8\\,\\mathrm{km}\\,\\mathrm{s}^{-1}$', 'c': '$22.4\\,\\mathrm{km}\\,\\mathrm{s}^{-1}$', 'd': '$5.6\\,\\mathrm{km}\\,\\mathrm{s}^{-1}$'} 2025 2025-05-24 shift_1 physics   93 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: step 1: escape velocity from the earth's surface $v_{\text{escape}} = \sqrt{\frac{2gm}{r}} = 11.2\,\mathrm{km}\,\mathrm{s}^{-1}$ here $g$ is the gravitational constant, $m$ is the mass of the earth and $r$ is the radius of the earth. step 2: orbital velocity of a satellite at height $h = r$ the orbital velocity at a distance $r$ from the centre of the earth is $v_{\text{orbit}} = \sqrt{\frac{gm}{r}}$ . for a height $h = r$ , the orbital radius is $r = r + r = 2r$ . so $v_{\text{orbit}} = \sqrt{\frac{gm}{2r}}$ . step 3: compare the two velocities $\frac{v_{\text{orbit}}}{v_{\text{escape}}} = \frac{\sqrt{\frac{gm}{2r}}}{\sqrt{\frac{2gm}{r}}} = \sqrt{\frac{gm}{2r}\cdot\frac{r}{2gm}} = \sqrt{\frac{1}{4}} = \frac{1}{2}$ hence the orbital velocity is half the escape velocity. step 4: substitute the given value $v_{\text{orbit}} = \frac{v_{\text{escape}}}{2} = \frac{11.2}{2} = 5.6\,\mathrm{km}\,\mathrm{s}^{-1}$ therefore the correct option is $5.6\,\mathrm{km}\,\mathrm{s}^{-1}$ . © examsnet.com

question: A wire is stretched 1 mm by a force F . If a second wire of same material, same length and 4 times the diameter of the first wire is stretched by the same force $F$ , then the elongation of the second wire is [AP EAPCET 24 May 2025 S1]
search_text: a wire is stretched 1 mm by a force f . if a second wire of same material, same length and 4 times the diameter of the first wire is stretched by the same force $f$ , then the elongation of the second wire is [ap eapcet 24 may 2025 s1] {'a': '$\\;\\;\\frac{1}{8} \\text{mm}$', 'b': '$\\;8 \\text{mm}$', 'c': '$\\;16 \\text{mm}$', 'd': '$\\;\\;\\frac{1}{16} \\text{mm}$'} 2025 2025-05-24 shift_1 physics   94 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: step 1: formula for elongation the amount a wire stretches depends on young's modulus formula: $y=\;\frac{f l}{\delta l a}=\;\frac{4 f l}{\delta l \pi d^2}$ step 2: what stays the same? both wires are made of the same material, have the same length, and the same stretching force. this means their young's modulus $(y)$ , original length $(l)$ , and force $(f)$ are the same. step 3: setting up the equation for both wires since young's modulus is the same for both wires, we set the formulas equal for each wire: $y_1=y_2$ $\;\frac{4 f l}{\delta l_1 \pi d_1^2}=\;\frac{4 f l}{\delta l_2 \pi d_2^2}$ step 4: rearranging to compare elongations we can simplify to find how the elongation ( $\delta l$ ) relates to diameter ( $d$ ): $\delta l_1 \cdot d_1^2 = \delta l_2 \cdot d_2^2$ so, $\delta l_2 = \delta l_1 \cdot \left( \;\frac{d_1}{d_2} \right)^2$ step 5: substitute values we are told $\delta l_1 = 1\,\text{mm}$ (the first wire stretches 1 mm ) and $d_2 = 4 d_1$ (the second wire's diameter is 4 times bigger). $\delta l_2 = 1 \cdot \left( \;\frac{d_1}{4 d_1} \right)^2 = 1 \cdot \left( \;\frac{1}{4} \right)^2 = \;\frac{1}{16} \text{mm}$ final answer the second, thicker wire stretches only $\;\frac{1}{16} \text{mm}$ when the same force is applied. © examsnet.com

search_text: in a water tank, an air bubble rises from the bottom to the top surface of the water. if the depth of the water in the tank is 7.28 m and atmospheric pressure is 10 m of water, then the ratio of the radii of the bubble at the bottom of the tank and at the top surface of the water is (temperature of the water in the tank is constant) [ap eapcet 24 may 2025 s1] {'a': '$\\;2: 3$', 'b': '$\\;5: 6$', 'c': '$\\;3: 4$', 'd': '$\\;4: 5$'} 2025 2025-05-24 shift_1 physics   95 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: as temperature is constant, for air in bubble, $p_1 v_1=p_2 v_2$ given, $\;p_1=10 \times \rho_w \times g$ $\;p_2=(10+7.28) \rho_w \times g$ $\;v_1=\;\frac{4}{3} \pi r_1^3 \;\text{ and }\; v_2=\;\frac{4}{3} \pi r_2^3$ now by $p_1 v_1=p_2 v_2$ $\rightarrow  \;\;  \;\frac{v_2}{v_1}\;= \left(\;\frac{r_2}{r_1}\right) ^3=\;\frac{p_1}{p_2}$ $\rightarrow  \;\;  \;\frac{r_2}{r_1}\;= \left(\;\frac{p_1}{p_2}\right) ^{\;\frac{1}{3}}= \left(\;\frac{10}{17.28}\right) ^{\;\frac{1}{3}}$ $\;= \left(\;\frac{1000}{1728}\right) ^{\;\frac{1}{3}}= \left(\;\frac{125}{216}\right) ^{\;\frac{1}{3}}=\;\frac{5}{6}$ © examsnet.com

search_text: a wire of length 0.5 m and area of cross-section $4 \times 10^{-6} \mathrm{m}^2$ at a temperature of $100^{\circ} \mathrm{c}$ is suspended vertically by fixing its upper end to the ceiling. the wire is then cooled to $0^{\circ} \mathrm{c}$ , but is prevented from contracting, by attaching a mass at the lower end. if the mass of the wire is negligible, then the value of the mass attached to the wire is [young's modulus of material of the wire $=10^{11} \mathrm{n} \, \mathrm{m}^{-2}$ ; coefficient of linear expansion of the material of the wire $=10^{-5} \mathrm{k}^{-1}$ and acceleration due to gravity $=10 \mathrm{m} \, \mathrm{s}^{-2}$ ] [ap eapcet 24 may 2025 s1] {'a': '10 kg', 'b': '20 kg', 'c': '30 kg', 'd': '40 kg'} 2025 2025-05-24 shift_1 physics   96 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: as contraction in wire is prevented by extending it with a load, thermal contraction $=$ extension due to load $\;\rightarrow\;\; \alpha l \delta t = \;\frac{f l}{y a} \rightarrow \alpha l \delta t = \;\frac{m g l}{y a}$ $\;\rightarrow\;\; m = \;\frac{\alpha \delta t \cdot y a}{g} = \;\frac{\alpha \delta t y a}{g}$ substituting given values, $m \; = \; \frac{10^{-5} \times 100 \times 10^{11} \times 4 \times 10^{-6}}{10}$ $\; = 4 \times 10 = 40 \mathrm{kg}$ © examsnet.com

search_text: the temperature of water of mass 100 g is raised from $24^{\circ}\,\mathrm{c}$ to $90^{\circ}\,\mathrm{c}$ by adding steam to it. the mass of the steam added is (latent heat of steam $=540\,\mathrm{cal}\,\mathrm{g}^{-1}$ and specific heat capacity of water $=1\,\mathrm{cal}\,\mathrm{g}^{-1}\,{}^{\circ}\mathrm{c}^{-1}$ ) [ap eapcet 24 may 2025 s1] {'a': '$\\;10\\,\\mathrm{g}$', 'b': '$\\;12\\,\\mathrm{g}$', 'c': '$\\;8\\,\\mathrm{g}$', 'd': '$\\;16\\,\\mathrm{g}$'} 2025 2025-05-24 shift_1 physics   97 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: let $m=$ mass of steam condensed. then, $m$ grams of steam forms $m$ grams of water at $100^{\circ}\,\mathrm{c}$ which further losses heat and comes at $90^{\circ}\,\mathrm{c}$ . final mixture is water at $90^{\circ}\,\mathrm{c}$ now using heat lost = heat gained, we gel heat lost by steam in condensation + heat lost by water formed at $100^{\circ}\,\mathrm{c}$ $=$ heat gained by water at $24^{\circ}\,\mathrm{c}$ $\; \rightarrow m l + m c(100-90) = 100(c)(90-24)$ $\; \rightarrow m(540 + 1 \times 10) = 100 \times 1 \times 66$ $\; \rightarrow m = \; \frac{100 \times 66}{550} = \; \frac{10 \times 6}{5} = 12\,\mathrm{g}$ © examsnet.com

question: A refrigerator of coefficient of performance 5 that extracts heat from the cooling compartment at the rate of 250 J per cycle is placed in a room. The heat released per cycle to the room by the refrigerator is [AP EAPCET 24 May 2025 S1]
search_text: a refrigerator of coefficient of performance 5 that extracts heat from the cooling compartment at the rate of 250 j per cycle is placed in a room. the heat released per cycle to the room by the refrigerator is [ap eapcet 24 may 2025 s1] {'a': '$250 \\, \\text{j}$', 'b': '$50 \\, \\text{j}$', 'c': '$200 \\, \\text{j}$', 'd': '$300 \\, \\text{j}$'} 2025 2025-05-24 shift_1 physics   99 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: step 1: for a refrigerator, the coefficient of performance is defined as the heat extracted from the cold compartment divided by the work input per cycle: $cop = \frac{q_c}{w}$ step 2: here $cop = 5$ and $q_c = 250 \, \text{j}$ , so the work done per cycle is: $w = \frac{q_c}{cop} = \frac{250}{5} = 50 \, \text{j}$ step 3: by conservation of energy (first law) for one cycle, the heat rejected to the room equals the heat absorbed from the cooling compartment plus the work input: $q_h = q_c + w$ step 4: substitute the values: $q_h = 250 \, \text{j} + 50 \, \text{j} = 300 \, \text{j}$ step 5: hence the heat released per cycle to the room is $300 \, \text{j}$ , which matches the option $300 \, \text{j}$ . © examsnet.com

question: The potential difference across a conducting wire of length 20 cm is 30 V . If the electron mobility is $2 \times 10^{-6} \, \mathrm{m}^2 \, \mathrm{V}^{-1} \, \mathrm{s}^{-1}$ , then the drift velocity of the electrons is [AP EAPCET 24 May 2025 S1]
search_text: the potential difference across a conducting wire of length 20 cm is 30 v . if the electron mobility is $2 \times 10^{-6} \, \mathrm{m}^2 \, \mathrm{v}^{-1} \, \mathrm{s}^{-1}$ , then the drift velocity of the electrons is [ap eapcet 24 may 2025 s1] {'a': '$3 \\times 10^{-3} \\, \\mathrm{m}\\,\\mathrm{s}^{-1}$', 'b': '$1.5 \\times 10^{-3} \\, \\mathrm{m}\\,\\mathrm{s}^{-1}$', 'c': '$1.5 \\times 10^{-4} \\, \\mathrm{m}\\,\\mathrm{s}^{-1}$', 'd': '$3 \\times 10^{-4} \\, \\mathrm{m}\\,\\mathrm{s}^{-1}$'} 2025 2025-05-24 shift_1 physics   108 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: we know the electron mobility $(\mu)$ and want to find the drift velocity $(v_d)$ . the formula is: $\mu = \frac{v_d}{e}$ here, $e$ stands for the electric field. for a wire, $e = \frac{v}{l}$ , where $v$ is the voltage and $l$ is the length of the wire. so, the drift velocity can be found as: $v_d = e \mu = \frac{v}{l} \cdot \mu$ plug in the values: $v = 30\,\mathrm{v},\ l = 20\,\mathrm{cm} = 20 \times 10^{-2}\,\mathrm{m}$ , and $\mu = 2 \times 10^{-6} \, \mathrm{m}^2 \, \mathrm{v}^{-1} \, \mathrm{s}^{-1}$ . $v_d = \frac{30 \times 2 \times 10^{-6}}{20 \times 10^{-2}}$ do the calculation step by step: $30 \times 2 = 60,\ 20 \times 10^{-2} = 0.2$ . $v_d = \frac{60 \times 10^{-6}}{0.2} = 300 \times 10^{-6} = 3 \times 10^{-4} \, \mathrm{m}\,\mathrm{s}^{-1}$ © examsnet.com

question: A maximum current of 0.5 mA can pass through a galvanometer of resistance $15 \Omega$ . The resistance to be connected in series to the galvanometer to convert it into a voltmeter of range $0-10\ \mathrm{V}$ is [AP EAPCET 24 May 2025 S1]
search_text: a maximum current of 0.5 ma can pass through a galvanometer of resistance $15 \omega$ . the resistance to be connected in series to the galvanometer to convert it into a voltmeter of range $0-10\ \mathrm{v}$ is [ap eapcet 24 may 2025 s1] {'a': '$\\;9985\\ \\omega$', 'b': '$\\;20015\\ \\omega$', 'c': '$\\;20000\\ \\omega$', 'd': '$\\;19985\\ \\omega$'} 2025 2025-05-24 shift_1 physics   109 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: here, $i_g=0.5 \times 10^{-3}\ \mathrm{a}$ $g=15\ \omega$ and the required voltmeter range is $v_{ab}=10\ \mathrm{v}$ for a voltmeter, a resistance $r_s$ is connected in series with the galvanometer, so $v_{ab}=i_g\,(g+r_s)$ $\rightarrow\;10=0.5 \times 10^{-3}\,(15+r_s)$ $\rightarrow\;15+r_s=\frac{10}{0.5 \times 10^{-3}}=20000$ $\rightarrow\;r_s=20000-15=19985\ \omega$ hence, the correct option is $19985\ \omega$ . © examsnet.com

question: Two charged particles of specific charges in the ratio $2: 1$ and masses in the ratio $1: 4$ moving with same kinetic energy enter a uniform magnetic field at right angles to the direction of the field. The ratio of the radii of the circular paths in which the particles move under the influence of the magnetic field is [AP EAPCET 24 May 2025 S1]
search_text: two charged particles of specific charges in the ratio $2: 1$ and masses in the ratio $1: 4$ moving with same kinetic energy enter a uniform magnetic field at right angles to the direction of the field. the ratio of the radii of the circular paths in which the particles move under the influence of the magnetic field is [ap eapcet 24 may 2025 s1] {'a': '$2: 1$', 'b': '$1: 1$', 'c': '$4: 1$', 'd': '$8: 1$'} 2025 2025-05-24 shift_1 physics   110 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: for a charged particle moving perpendicular to a uniform magnetic field, the radius of the circular path is $r=\frac{mv}{bq}$ since kinetic energy is $k=\frac{1}{2}mv^2$ , we have $mv=\sqrt{2mk}$ , so $r=\frac{\sqrt{2mk}}{bq}$ writing charge in terms of the specific charge $s=\frac{q}{m}$ (so $q=ms$ ), $r=\frac{\sqrt{2mk}}{b\,m\,s}=\frac{\sqrt{2k}}{b\,s\sqrt{m}}$ thus $r\propto \frac{1}{s\sqrt{m}}$ for the same $k$ and $b$ . given $s_1:s_2=2:1$ and $m_1:m_2=1:4$ , $\frac{r_1}{r_2}=\frac{s_2}{s_1}\sqrt{\frac{m_2}{m_1}}=\sqrt{\left(\frac{s_2}{s_1}\right)^2\left(\frac{m_2}{m_1}\right)}$ $\frac{r_1}{r_2}=\sqrt{\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^2\left(\frac{4}{1}\right)}=\sqrt{1}=1$ hence $r_1:r_2=1:1$ . correct option: $1:1$ © examsnet.com

search_text: a sample of paramagnetic salt contains $2 \times 10^{24}$ atomic dipoles each of dipole moment $1.5 \times 10^{-23} \text{jt}^{-1}$ . the sample is placed under homogeneous magnetic field of 0.6 t and cooled to a temperature 4.2 k . the degree of magnetic saturation achived is $20\%$ . then total dipole moment of the sample for a magnetic field of 0.9 t and a temperature of 2.8 k is material changes with temperature and magnetic field. according to curie's law, the magnetisation $(m)$ is directly proportional to the magnetic field $(b_0)$ and inversely proportional to the temperature $(t)$ : $m \propto \frac{b_0}{t}$ or, $m = c \cdot \frac{b_0}{t}$ where $c$ (curie's constant) stays the same for the same substance. curie's constant can be written as: $c = \frac{m t}{b_0}$ where: $t =$ temperature in kelvin $b_0 =$ external magnetic field $m =$ magnetisation (total dipole moment) since $c$ (curie's constant) is the same for all measurements of the same sample, we can relate two cases as: $\frac{m_1 t_1}{b_{0_1}} = \frac{m_2 t_2}{b_{0_2}}$ so, $m_2 = m_1 \cdot \frac{t_1}{t_2} \cdot \frac{b_{0_2}}{b_{0_1}}$ now, let's fill in the given values: number of dipoles $= 2 \times 10^{24}$ dipole moment per dipole $= 15 \times 10^{-23} \text{jt}^{-1}$ step 1: find initial total dipole moment total dipole moment possible (if $100\%$ aligned): $2 \times 10^{24} \times 15 \times 10^{-23} = 3 \times 10^2 \text{jt}^{-1}$ but, at first, only $20\%$ saturation is achieved: $m_1 = 0.2 \times 3 \times 10^2 = 60 \text{jt}^{-1}$ step 2: use curie's law for new conditions magnetic field changes from $b_{0_1} = 0.6 \text{t}$ to $b_{0_2} = 0.9 \text{t}$ and temperature from $t_1 = 4.2 \text{k}$ to $t_2 = 2.8 \text{k}$ . now, use the formula: $m_2 = m_1 \times \frac{t_1}{t_2} \times \frac{b_{0_2}}{b_{0_1}}$ substitute the numbers in: $m_2 = 60 \times \frac{4.2}{2.8} \times \frac{0.9}{0.6}$ calculate step by step: $\frac{4.2}{2.8} = 1.5$ $\frac{0.9}{0.6} = 1.5$ so, $m_2 = 60 \times 1.5 \times 1.5 = 135 \text{jt}^{-1}$ © examsnet.com

question: A coil of resistance $200 \Omega$ is placed in a magnetic field. If the magnetic flux $\phi$ (in weber) linked with the coil varies with time ' $t$ ' (in second) as per the equation $\phi=50 t^2+4$ , then the current induced in the coil at a time $t=2\,\mathrm{s}$ is [AP EAPCET 24 May 2025 S1]
search_text: a coil of resistance $200 \omega$ is placed in a magnetic field. if the magnetic flux $\phi$ (in weber) linked with the coil varies with time ' $t$ ' (in second) as per the equation $\phi=50 t^2+4$ , then the current induced in the coil at a time $t=2\,\mathrm{s}$ is [ap eapcet 24 may 2025 s1] {'a': '$\\;2\\ \\mathrm{a}$', 'b': '$\\;1\\ \\mathrm{a}$', 'c': '$\\;0.5\\ \\mathrm{a}$', 'd': '$\\;0.1\\ \\mathrm{a}$'} 2025 2025-05-24 shift_1 physics   112 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: we need to find the current in the coil at $t=2$ seconds. step 1: find the induced emf. the magnetic flux is given by $\phi=50 t^2+4$ . to find the emf ( $e$ ), we take the derivative of $\phi$ with respect to $t$ : $e=\;\frac{d\phi}{dt}$ now, differentiate $\phi$ : $\;\frac{d}{dt} (50 t^2+4) =100 t$ (because the derivative of $t^2$ is $2t$ , and 50 times $2t$ is $100t$ ; the derivative of a constant is 0 ). step 2: calculate emf at $t=2$ seconds. plug in $t=2$ : $e=100 \times 2=200\;\text{ volts }\;$ step 3: find the current using ohm's law. ohm's law: $i=\;\frac{e}{r}$ here, $e=200$ volts and $r=200 \omega$ . $i=\;\frac{200}{200}=1\ \mathrm{a}$ so, the current induced in the coil at $t=2$ seconds is 1 ampere. © examsnet.com

question: A laser produces a beam of light of frequency $5 \times 10^{14} \text{ Hz}$ with an output power of 33 mW . The average number of photons emitted by the laser per second is $($ Planck's constant $= 6.6 \times 10^{-34} \text{ J} \text{ s})$ [AP EAPCET 24 May 2025 S1]
search_text: a laser produces a beam of light of frequency $5 \times 10^{14} \text{ hz}$ with an output power of 33 mw . the average number of photons emitted by the laser per second is $($ planck's constant $= 6.6 \times 10^{-34} \text{ j} \text{ s})$ [ap eapcet 24 may 2025 s1] {'a': '$40 \\times 10^{16}$', 'b': '$10 \\times 10^{16}$', 'c': '$30 \\times 10^{16}$', 'd': '$20 \\times 10^{16}$'} 2025 2025-05-24 shift_1 physics   115 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: step 1: understanding power power is how much energy is used or given out each second. so: power $= \frac{\text{ energy }}{\text{ time }}$ step 2: energy of one photon the energy in one photon of light is found using: $e = h f$ where $h$ is planck's constant and $f$ is the frequency. step 3: total energy from many photons if $n$ photons come out in time $t$ , the total energy is $n \times h f$ . step 4: linking power and number of photons so, power $= \frac{\text{ total energy }}{\text{ time }} = \frac{n \times h f}{t}$ step 5: average number of photons per second the number of photons per second is $n = \frac{n}{t} = \frac{p}{h f}$ plug in the numbers: $n = \frac{33 \times 10^{-3}}{6.6 \times 10^{-34} \times 5 \times 10^{14}}$ step 6: final calculation this works out to: $n = 10 \times 10^{16}$ so, the laser gives off $10 \times 10^{16}$ photons every second. © examsnet.com

search_text: if the ratio of the maximum and minimum amplitudes of an amplitude modulated wave is $7: 3$ , then the modulation index is [ap eapcet 24 may 2025 s1] {'a': '$\\;0.6$', 'b': '$\\;0.7$', 'c': '$\\;0.4$', 'd': '$\\;0.3$'} 2025 2025-05-24 shift_1 physics   120 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: modulation index is given by $\mu \;=\; \frac{a_{\max} - a_{\min}}{a_{\max} + a_{\min}}$ $\;=\; \frac{ \;\frac{a_{\max}}{a_{\min}} - 1 }{ \frac{a_{\max}}{a_{\min}} + 1 }$ $\;=\; \frac{ \;\frac{7}{3} - 1 }{ \frac{7}{3} + 1 } = \frac{ \;\frac{4}{3} }{ \frac{10}{3} } = 0.4$ © examsnet.com

question: Which of the following represents the wavelength of spectral line of Balmer series of $\mathrm{He}^{+}$ ion? $( R = \text{Rydberg constant,}\ n > 2)$ [AP EAPCET 24 May 2025 S1]
search_text: which of the following represents the wavelength of spectral line of balmer series of $\mathrm{he}^{+}$ ion? $( r = \text{rydberg constant,}\ n > 2)$ [ap eapcet 24 may 2025 s1] {'a': '$\\;\\;\\frac{n^2}{r(n-2)(n+2)}$', 'b': '$\\;\\;\\frac{r(n-2)(n+2)}{n^2}$', 'c': '$\\;\\;\\frac{n^2}{4 r(n-2)(n+2)}$', 'd': '$\\;\\;\\frac{4 r(n-2)(n+2)}{n^2}$'} 2025 2025-05-24 shift_1 chemistry   121 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: using the rydberg formula $\frac{1}{\lambda}=r z^2 \left[ \frac{1}{n_f^2} - \frac{1}{n_i^2} \right]$ for $\mathrm{he}^{+}$ , $z=2$ , and for the balmer series, $n_f=2$ . the initial level is $n_i=n$ where $n>2$ . $\frac{1}{\lambda}=r(2)^2 \left[ \frac{1}{2^2} - \frac{1}{n^2} \right]$ $\rightarrow \frac{1}{\lambda}=4r \left( \frac{1}{4} - \frac{1}{n^2} \right)$ $\rightarrow \frac{1}{\lambda}=r \left( 1 - \frac{4}{n^2} \right)= \frac{r(n^2-4)}{n^2}$ taking the reciprocal, $\lambda=\frac{n^2}{r(n^2-4)}$ $\rightarrow \lambda=\frac{n^2}{r(n-2)(n+2)}$ this matches option (0), so the marked answer is correct. © examsnet.com

search_text: observe the following substances. ethanol, acetic acid, ethylamine, trimethylamine, salicylic acid, ethanal. in the above list, the number of substances with h -bonding is [ap eapcet 24 may 2025 s1] {'a': '4', 'b': '3', 'c': '5', 'd': '2'} 2025 2025-05-24 shift_1 chemistry   125 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: hydrogen bonding occurs when a molecule has a hydrogen atom bonded to a highly electronegative atom like $n$ , $o$ , or $f$ - and there is a lone pair on another $n , o$ , or $f$ atom that can participate in bonding. 1. ethanol $( ch _3 ch _2 oh )$ has an - oh group can form hydrogen bonds ( $o - h ⋯ o$ ) 2. acetic acid $( ch _3 c o o h )$ has both $c = o$ and - oh groups forms strong hydrogen bonds (dimers, intramolecular and intermolecular h-bonding possible) 3. ethylamine $( c h _{ 3 } c h _{ 2 } n h _{ 2 })$ has an $- nh _2$ group can form hydrogen bonds ( $n - h ⋯ n$ or $n - h ⋯ o$ with other molecules) 4. trimethylamine $( ( ch _3) _3 n)$ has nitrogen with a lone pair but no $n - h$ bond cannot form h-bonds as donor, though it can accept them - but "having h-bonding" typically means being capable of intermolecular h -bonding as both donor and acceptor. since it cannot donate an h , we generally do not count it as hydrogen-bonding on its own. 5. salicylic acid (o-hydroxybenzoic acid) has both - oh and - cooh groups; strong intramolecular hydrogen bond and intermolecular as well. h-bonding present 6. ethanal ( $c h _{ 3 } c h o$ ) has a $c = o$ group only, no - oh or $- nh -$ cannot form hydrogen bonds with itself (can accept h bonds but not donate). substances with h-bonding: ethanol acetic acid ethylamine salicylic acid total $= 4$ © examsnet.com

question: Consider the following Statement-I : If thermal energy is stronger than intermolecular forces, the substance prefers to be in gaseous state. Statement-II : At constant temperature, the density of an ideal gas is proportional to its pressure. [AP EAPCET 24 May 2025 S1]
search_text: consider the following statement-i : if thermal energy is stronger than intermolecular forces, the substance prefers to be in gaseous state. statement-ii : at constant temperature, the density of an ideal gas is proportional to its pressure. [ap eapcet 24 may 2025 s1] {'a': 'statement-i is correct, but statement-ii is not correct', 'b': 'statement-i is not correct, but statement-ii is correct', 'c': 'both statement-i and statement-ii are correct', 'd': 'both statement-i and statement-ii are not correct'} 2025 2025-05-24 shift_1 chemistry   126 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: statement i if thermal energy is stronger than intermolecular forces, the substance prefers to be in gaseous state. when thermal (kinetic) energy of molecules exceeds the intermolecular attractive forces, the molecules move freely, far apart - this is the gaseous state. statement i is correct. statement ii at constant temperature, the density of an ideal gas is proportional to its pressure. from the ideal gas law: $p v=n r t$ or $p=\;\frac{n}{v} r t$ now, $\;\frac{n}{v} = \;\frac{\rho}{m}$ , where $\rho$ is density and $m$ is molar mass. thus, $p=\;\frac{\rho}{m} r t \rightarrow \rho=\;\frac{p m}{r t}$ at constant $t$ and $m$ : $\rho \propto p$ statement ii is also correct. © examsnet.com

question: At $27^{\circ} \mathrm{C}, 1 \mathrm{L}$ of $\mathrm{H}_2$ with a pressure of 1 bar is mixed with 2 L of $\mathrm{O}_2$ with a pressure of 2 bar in a 10 L flask. What is the pressure exerted by gaseous mixture in bar? (Assume $\mathrm{H}_2$ and $\mathrm{O}_2$ as ideal gases) [AP EAPCET 24 May 2025 S1]
search_text: at $27^{\circ} \mathrm{c}, 1 \mathrm{l}$ of $\mathrm{h}_2$ with a pressure of 1 bar is mixed with 2 l of $\mathrm{o}_2$ with a pressure of 2 bar in a 10 l flask. what is the pressure exerted by gaseous mixture in bar? (assume $\mathrm{h}_2$ and $\mathrm{o}_2$ as ideal gases) [ap eapcet 24 may 2025 s1] {'a': '$4$', 'b': '$0.05$', 'c': '$1$', 'd': '$0.5$'} 2025 2025-05-24 shift_1 chemistry   127 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: calculating the partial pressure of $\mathrm{h}_2$ in 10 l flask $\; p_{\mathrm{h}_2 \; \text{ initial }} \; \; v_{\mathrm{h}_2 \; \text{ initial }} = p_{\mathrm{h}_2 \; \text{ final }} \; \; v_{\text{ total }}$ $\; p_{\mathrm{h}_2 \; \text{ final }} = \; \frac{1 \times 1}{10} = 0.1 \text{ bar}$ using boyle's law for partial pressure of $\mathrm{o}_2$ $p_{\mathrm{o}_2 \; \text{ final }} \; = \; \frac{p_{\mathrm{o}_2 \; \text{ initial }} \times v_{\mathrm{o}_2 \; \text{ initial }}}{v_{\text{ total }}}$ $\; = \; \frac{2 \times 2}{10} = 0.4 \text{ bar}$ use dalton's law of partial pressure. $p_{\text{ total }} \; = p_{\mathrm{h}_2 \; \text{ final }} \; \; + p_{\mathrm{o}_2 \; \text{ final }}$ $\; = 0.1+0.4=0.5 \text{ bar}$ since $\mathrm{h}_2$ and $\mathrm{o}_2$ do not react at $27^{\circ} \mathrm{c}$ in the absence of a spark or catalyst, the total pressure is simply the sum of the partial pressures of the two gases. hence the pressure exerted by the gaseous mixture is $0.5 \text{ bar}$ , i.e. option (3). © examsnet.com

question: Two acids A and B are titrated separately. 25 mL of $0.5\ \mathrm{M}\ \mathrm{Na}_2\mathrm{CO}_3$ solution requires 10 mL of A and 40 mL of B for complete neutralisation. search_text: two acids a and b are titrated separately. 25 ml of $0.5\ \mathrm{m}\ \mathrm{na}_2\mathrm{co}_3$ solution requires 10 ml of a and 40 ml of b for complete neutralisation. the volume (in $l)$ of a and b required to produce 1 l of 1 n acid solution respectively are [ap eapcet 24 may 2025 s1] {'a': '$0.2,0.8$', 'b': '$0.8,0.2$', 'c': '$0.3,0.7$', 'd': '$0.7,0.3$'} 2025 2025-05-24 shift_1 chemistry   128 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: normality of $\mathrm{na}_2\mathrm{co}_3=$ molarity $\times n$ -factor $=0.5\ \mathrm{m}\times 2=1\ \mathrm{n}$ normality of acid $a$ , $\;n_{\;\text{acid }\;} a \times v_{\;\text{acid }\;a}=n_{\mathrm{na}_2\mathrm{co}_3} \times v_{\mathrm{na}_2\mathrm{co}_3}$ $\;n_{\;\text{acid }\;} a=\;\frac{1\times 25}{10}=2.5\ \mathrm{n}$ similarly normality of acid $b$ $n_{\;\text{acid }\;b}=0.625\ \mathrm{n}$ volume of acid $a$ needed for 1 l of 1 n solution $\;n_{\;\text{acid }\;a} \times v_{a\;\text{final }\;}=n_{\;\text{final }\;} \times v_{\;\text{final }\;}$ $\;v_{a\;\text{final }\;}=\;\frac{1\times 1}{2.5}=0.4\ \mathrm{l}\;\;\;\cdot\cdot\cdot\cdot\cdot\cdot\cdot(i)$ volume of acid $b$ needed for 1 l of 1 n solution, $v_{b\;\text{final }\;}=\;\frac{1\times 1}{0.625}=1.6\ \mathrm{l}\;\;\;\cdot\cdot\cdot\cdot\cdot\cdot\cdot(ii)$ © examsnet.com

question: The $C_{p}$ of $\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}(l)$ is $75.3\ \mathrm{J\,mol^{-1}\,K^{-1}}$ . What is the energy (in J ) required to raise 180 g of liquid water from $10^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ to $15^{\circ}\mathrm{C} ? (\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}=18\ \mathrm{u})$ [AP EAPCET 24 May 2025 S1]
search_text: the $c_{p}$ of $\mathrm{h}_2\mathrm{o}(l)$ is $75.3\ \mathrm{j\,mol^{-1}\,k^{-1}}$ . what is the energy (in j ) required to raise 180 g of liquid water from $10^{\circ}\mathrm{c}$ to $15^{\circ}\mathrm{c} ? (\mathrm{h}_2\mathrm{o}=18\ \mathrm{u})$ [ap eapcet 24 may 2025 s1] {'a': '$3.765$', 'b': '$3765$', 'c': '$753$', 'd': '$376.5$'} 2025 2025-05-24 shift_1 chemistry   130 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: first, we need to find out how many moles of water we have. $n\;=\;\frac{m}{m}\;=\;\frac{180}{18}$ $\;=10\ \mathrm{mol}$ $\delta t\;=t_2-t_1=15-10=5\ \mathrm{k}$ the energy needed to heat the water is given by the formula: $q=n c_p \delta t$ here, $n$ is number of moles (10), $c_p$ is the specific heat $(75.3\ \mathrm{j\,mol^{-1}\,k^{-1}})$ , and $\delta t$ is the temperature change (5 k). so, $q=10 \times 75.3 \times 5=3765\ \mathrm{j}$ © examsnet.com

(assume all gases as ideal) [ap eapcet 24 may 2025 s1] {'a': '$0.2$', 'b': '$0.6$', 'c': '$0.4$', 'd': '$0.8$'} 2025 2025-05-24 shift_1 chemistry   131 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: the given reaction is, $\mathrm{n}_2\mathrm{o}_5 \rightarrow 2\mathrm{no}_2 + \frac{1}{2}\mathrm{o}_2$ let $p_0=$ initial pressure of $\mathrm{n}_2\mathrm{o}_5 x =$ pressure of $\mathrm{n}_2\mathrm{o}_5$ decomposed. initial state $= \mathrm{n}_2\mathrm{o}_5$ has pressure $p_0$ equilibrium state $= \mathrm{n}_2\mathrm{o}_5$ has pressure $=p_0 - x$ $\mathrm{no}_2 = 2x$ pressure, $\mathrm{o}_2 = \frac{1}{2} x$ pressure $p_{\text{equilibrium}} = (p_0 - x) + 2x + \frac{1}{2}x$ $480 = p_0 + \frac{3}{2} x$ $\rightarrow p_0 = 300\text{ mmhg}$ $180 = \frac{3}{2} x, x = 120\text{ mmhg}$ fraction decomposed $= \frac{\text{ pressure of }\mathrm{n}_2\mathrm{o}_5\text{ decomposed }}{\text{ initial pressure of }\mathrm{n}_2\mathrm{o}_5}$ $= \frac{x}{p_0} = \frac{120}{300} = \frac{2}{5} = 0.4$ © examsnet.com

question: Consider the following Statement-I $\; :$ Both $\mathrm{BeSO}_4$ and $\mathrm{MgSO}_4$ are readily soluble in water. Statement-II : Among the nitrates of alkaline earth metals, only $\mathrm{Be}(\mathrm{NO}_3)_2$ on strong heating gives its oxide, $\mathrm{NO}_2$ and $\mathrm{O}_2$ . The correct answer is [AP EAPCET 24 May 2025 S1]
search_text: consider the following statement-i $\; :$ both $\mathrm{beso}_4$ and $\mathrm{mgso}_4$ are readily soluble in water. statement-ii : among the nitrates of alkaline earth metals, only $\mathrm{be}(\mathrm{no}_3)_2$ on strong heating gives its oxide, $\mathrm{no}_2$ and $\mathrm{o}_2$ . the correct answer is [ap eapcet 24 may 2025 s1] {'a': 'both statement-i and statement-ii are correct', 'b': 'statement-i is correct, but statement-ii is not correct', 'c': 'statement-i is not correct, but statement-ii is correct', 'd': 'both statement-i and statement-ii are not correct'} 2025 2025-05-24 shift_1 chemistry   134 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: analysis of statement-i: both $\mathrm{beso}_4$ and $\mathrm{mgso}_4$ are readily soluble in water. the solubility of sulfates of alkaline earth metals generally decreases down the group. $\mathrm{beso}_4$ (beryllium sulfate) is readily soluble in water. this is due to the very small size of the $\mathrm{be}^{2+}$ ion, which leads to very high hydration energy. this high hydration energy more than compensates for the relatively high lattice energy, making it highly soluble. $\mathrm{mgso}_4$ (magnesium sulfate, commonly known as epsom salt) is also readily soluble in water. similar to beryllium, the $\mathrm{mg}^{2+}$ ion is relatively small, leading to significant hydration energy. in contrast, $\mathrm{caso}_4$ (calcium sulfate) is sparingly soluble, and $\mathrm{srso}_4$ (strontium sulfate) and $\mathrm{baso}_4$ (barium sulfate) are practically insoluble. therefore, statement - i is correct. analysis of statement - ii: among the nitrates of alkaline earth metals, only $\mathrm{be}(\mathrm{no}_3)_2$ on strong heating gives its oxide, $\mathrm{no}_2$ and $\mathrm{o}_2$ . alkaline earth metal nitrates decompose on strong heating to give the metal oxide, nitrogen dioxide ( $\mathrm{no}_2$ ), and oxygen $(\mathrm{o}_2)$ . the general reaction is: $2 \mathrm{m}(\mathrm{no}_3)_2(s) \xrightarrow{\; \text{heat} \;} 2 \mathrm{mo}(s) + 4 \mathrm{no}_2(g) + \mathrm{o}_2(g)$ this decomposition pattern is observed for all alkaline earth metal nitrates. $\; \mathrm{be}(\mathrm{no}_3)_2 \xrightarrow{\; \text{heat} \;} \mathrm{beo} + 2 \mathrm{no}_2 + \frac{1}{2} \mathrm{o}_2$ $\; \mathrm{mg}(\mathrm{no}_3)_2 \xrightarrow{\; \text{heat} \;} \mathrm{mgo} + 2 \mathrm{no}_2 + \frac{1}{2} \mathrm{o}_2$ $\; \mathrm{ca}(\mathrm{no}_3)_2 \xrightarrow{\; \text{heat} \;} \mathrm{cao} + 2 \mathrm{no}_2 + \frac{1}{2} \mathrm{o}_2$ and similarly for $\mathrm{sr}(\mathrm{no}_3)_2$ and $\mathrm{ba}(\mathrm{no}_3)_2$ . the thermal stability of these nitrates generally increases down the group $(\mathrm{be}(\mathrm{no}_3)_2.$ is the least stable, and $\mathrm{ba}(\mathrm{no}_3)_2$ is the most stable), meaning they decompose at different temperatures, but the decomposition products are the same for all of them. the statement claims that "only $\mathrm{be}(\mathrm{no}_3)_2$ " decomposes in this manner, which is incorrect as all alkaline earth metal nitrates follow this decomposition pathway. therefore, statement - ii is not correct. conclusion: statement - i is correct. statement - ii is not correct. this matches option b. © examsnet.com

question: Which one of the following statements related to photochemical smog is not correct? [AP EAPCET 24 May 2025 S1]
search_text: which one of the following statements related to photochemical smog is not correct? [ap eapcet 24 may 2025 s1] {'a': 'it is controlled by the use of catalytic converters in automobiles', 'b': 'it causes corrosion of metals', 'c': 'it is a mixture of $\\mathrm{so}_2$ , smoke and fog', 'd': 'it causes extensive damage to plant life'} 2025 2025-05-24 shift_1 chemistry   137 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: photochemical smog: formed when sunlight acts on nitrogen oxides (nox) and hydrocarbons (unburnt fuel), producing secondary pollutants like ozone $(\mathrm{o}_3)$ , peroxyacetyl nitrate (pan), formaldehyde, etc. it is also called los angeles smog or summer smog. it mainly occurs in warm, dry, and sunny climates. option a: it is controlled by the use of catalytic converters in automobiles. correct. catalytic converters reduce emissions of nox and hydrocarbons, which are precursors of photochemical smog. option b: it causes corrosion of metals. correct. ozone and other oxidants in photochemical smog can corrode metals. option c: it is a mixture of $\mathrm{so}_2$ , smoke, and fog. not correct. this describes classical smog (also called london smog or reducing smog), which occurs in cool, humid conditions and is a mixture of $\mathrm{so}_2$ and particulates with fog. photochemical smog, on the other hand, contains nox, hydrocarbons, and oxidants such as ozone-not so2-based smoke and fog. option d: it causes extensive damage to plant life. correct. ozone and pan damage leaves and affect photosynthesis. © examsnet.com

question: An element occurs in the body centred cubic structure with edge length of 288 pm . The density of the element is $7.2\ \mathrm{g}\ \mathrm{cm}^{-3}$ . The number of atoms present in 208 g of the element is nearly [AP EAPCET 24 May 2025 S1]
search_text: an element occurs in the body centred cubic structure with edge length of 288 pm . the density of the element is $7.2\ \mathrm{g}\ \mathrm{cm}^{-3}$ . the number of atoms present in 208 g of the element is nearly [ap eapcet 24 may 2025 s1] {'a': '$24.2 \\times 10^{23}$', 'b': '$12.1 \\times 10^{23}$', 'c': '$24.2 \\times 10^{24}$', 'd': '$36.3 \\times 10^{23}$'} 2025 2025-05-24 shift_1 chemistry   140 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: given values: the edge length $a=288\ \mathrm{pm}$ . the density $(\rho)$ is $7.2\ \mathrm{g}/\mathrm{cm}^3$ . the mass given is 208 g . step 1: find volume of one unit cell the edge length must be changed to centimeters: $1\ \mathrm{pm}=10^{-10}\ \mathrm{cm}$ . so: $a=288 \times 10^{-10}\ \mathrm{cm}$ . the volume of one unit cell is: $v=a^3= (288 \times 10^{-10})^3\ \mathrm{cm}^3=2.389 \times 10^{-23}\ \mathrm{cm}^3$ step 2: find total volume that 208 g will occupy $v_{\text{total}} = \frac{m}{\rho} = \frac{208}{7.2} = 28.89\ \mathrm{cm}^3$ step 3: find the number of unit cells in $208\ \mathrm{g}$ $\text{number of unit cells} = \frac{v_{\text{total}}}{v_{\text{unit cell}}} = \frac{28.89}{2.389 \times 10^{-23}} = 1.209 \times 10^{24}$ step 4: find the total number of atoms a body centered cubic (bcc) unit cell has 2 atoms per unit cell. so, total atoms $=$ number of unit cells $\times 2=1.209 \times 10^{24} \times 2=2.42 \times 10^{24}$ which is the same as $24.2 \times 10^{23}$ . © examsnet.com

question: An aqueous solution containing 0.2 g of a non volatile solute ' A ' in 21.5 g of water freezes at 272.814 K . If the freezing point of water is 273.16 K , the molar mass (in $\mathrm{g} \mathrm{mol}^{-1}$ ) of solute $A$ is $[ K_f (\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}) = 1.86 \mathrm{K} \mathrm{kg} \mathrm{mol}^{-1} ]$ [AP EAPCET 24 May 2025 S1]
search_text: an aqueous solution containing 0.2 g of a non volatile solute ' a ' in 21.5 g of water freezes at 272.814 k . if the freezing point of water is 273.16 k , the molar mass (in $\mathrm{g} \mathrm{mol}^{-1}$ ) of solute $a$ is $[ k_f (\mathrm{h}_2\mathrm{o}) = 1.86 \mathrm{k} \mathrm{kg} \mathrm{mol}^{-1} ]$ [ap eapcet 24 may 2025 s1] {'a': '80', 'b': '75', 'c': '100', 'd': '50'} 2025 2025-05-24 shift_1 chemistry   141 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: step 1: find the decrease in freezing point the difference between the normal freezing point of water and the solution's freezing point is called the depression in freezing point. the calculation is: $\; \delta t_f = t_f^0 - t_f = 273.16 - 272.814$ $\; \delta t_f = 0.346 \mathrm{k}$ step 2: use the freezing point depression formula the formula is: $\delta t_f = k_f \cdot m$ where $m$ is molality. $m = \; \frac{\delta t_f}{k_f} = \; \frac{0.346}{1.86} = 0.186 \mathrm{mol/kg}$ step 3: calculate the moles of solute molality tells us moles of solute in 1 kg of solvent (water). here, amount of water is $21.5 \mathrm{g} = 0.0215 \mathrm{kg}$ . moles of solute $= 0.186 \times 0.0215 = 0.00400 \mathrm{mol}$ step 4: calculate the molar mass molar mass $= \frac{\text{mass of solute}}{\text{moles of solute}}$ molar mass $= \frac{0.2}{0.00400} = 50 \mathrm{g/mol}$ © examsnet.com

question: At $T(K)$ , the vapour pressure of $x$ molal aqueous solution containing a non-volatile solute is 12.078 kPa . The vapour pressure of pure water at $T(K)$ is 12.3 kPa . What is the value of $x$ ? [AP EAPCET 24 May 2025 S1]
search_text: at $t(k)$ , the vapour pressure of $x$ molal aqueous solution containing a non-volatile solute is 12.078 kpa . the vapour pressure of pure water at $t(k)$ is 12.3 kpa . what is the value of $x$ ? [ap eapcet 24 may 2025 s1] {'a': '$\\; 10$', 'b': '$\\; 1.018$', 'c': '$\\; 0.1018$', 'd': '$\\; 0.018$'} 2025 2025-05-24 shift_1 chemistry   142 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: mole fraction of solvent $\chi_{\;\text{solute }\;} \; = \; \frac{p_0-p_s}{p_0}$ $\rightarrow \;\; \chi_{\;\text{solute }\;} \; = \; \frac{12.3-12.078}{12.3} = 0.01805$ moles of water in 1000 g of water $= \; \frac{1000}{18} = 55.56 \text{ mol}$ for dilute solution, $\chi_{\;\text{solute }\;} = \frac{n_{\;\text{solute }\;}}{n_{\;\text{solute }\;}+n_{\;\text{water }\;}} \approx \frac{n_{\;\text{solute }\;}}{n_{\;\text{water }\;}}$ since molality $x$ is moles of solute per 1 kg of solvent $\; x = n_{\;\text{solute }\;} \rightarrow \;\; x_{\;\text{solute }\;} = \frac{x}{55.56}$ $\; x = 0.01805 \times 55.56 \approx 1.018$ © examsnet.com

The equilibrium constant for the reaction is $10^x$ . search_text: consider the following cell reaction $2\,\mathrm{fe}^{3+}(\mathrm{aq}) + 2\,\mathrm{i}^{-}(\mathrm{aq}) \rightleftharpoons 2\,\mathrm{fe}^{2+}(\mathrm{aq}) + \mathrm{i}_2(\mathrm{s})$ at 298 k , the cell emf is 0.237 v . the equilibrium constant for the reaction is $10^x$ . the value of $x$ is $(f = 96500\,\mathrm{c}\,\mathrm{mol}^{-1}; r = 8.3\,\mathrm{j}\,\mathrm{k}^{-1}\,\mathrm{mol}^{-1})$ [ap eapcet 24 may 2025 s1] {'a': '8', 'b': '7', 'c': '6', 'd': '9'} 2025 2025-05-24 shift_1 chemistry   143 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: the reaction is, $\;2\,\mathrm{fe}^{3+}(\mathrm{aq}) + 2\,\mathrm{i}^{-}(\mathrm{aq}) \rightarrow 2\,\mathrm{fe}^{2+}(\mathrm{aq}) + \mathrm{i}_2(\mathrm{s})$ $n=2$ at equilibrium, $e_{\text{cell}} = 0\,\mathrm{v}, q=k$ using nernst equation $e_{\text{cell}} = e_{\text{cell}}^{\circ} - \frac{r t}{n f} \ln k$ $\ln k = \frac{n f e_{\text{eall}}^{\circ}}{r t}$ , substituting values, $\ln$ $k = 18.493$ $\log_{10} k = \frac{18.493}{2.303} \approx 8 \rightarrow 10^8$ so, the value of $x$ is 8 . © examsnet.com

question: What is the indicator used in Argentometric titrations? [AP EAPCET 24 May 2025 S1]
search_text: what is the indicator used in argentometric titrations? [ap eapcet 24 may 2025 s1] {'a': 'starch solution', 'b': 'eosin dye', 'c': '$\\mathrm{kmno}_4$ solution', 'd': 'phenolphthalein'} 2025 2025-05-24 shift_1 chemistry   145 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: argentometric titrations are titrations involving silver nitrate $(\mathrm{agno}_3)$ as the titrant, typically used for the determination of halide ions such as $\mathrm{cl}^{-}, \mathrm{br}^{-}$ , and $\mathrm{i}^{-}$ . one common method is the fajans method, where an adsorption indicator, such as fluorescein or eosin, is used. before the equivalence point, halide ions are present in excess, and the precipitate surface $(\mathrm{agx})$ is negatively charged. after the equivalence point, excess $\mathrm{ag}^{+}$ ions make the surface positively charged, allowing the negatively charged dye ions (like eosin) to adsorb on the surface and cause a visible color change - signaling the end point. hence, eosin dye (an adsorption indicator) is used in argentometric titrations by fajans' method. © examsnet.com

search_text: match the following list-i (process) list-ii (metal) a) hall-heroult process i) ti b) mond process ii) in c) van-arkel process iii) $\mathrm{al}$ d) zone refining process iv) ni [ap eapcet 24 may 2025 s1] {'a': 'a-iv, b-iii, c-i, d-ii', 'b': 'a-ii, b-iii, c-iv, d-i', 'c': 'a-iii, b-i, c-iv, d-ii', 'd': 'a-iii, b-iv, c-i, d-ii'} 2025 2025-05-24 shift_1 chemistry   147 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: let's match each process with the metal it is primarily associated with: hall-heroult process: this is a major industrial process for the primary production of aluminum (ai). it involves the electrolytic reduction of alumina $(\mathrm{al}_2\mathrm{o}_3)$ dissolved in molten cryolite. so, (a) hall-heroult process matches with (iii) ai. mond process: this process is used for the purification of nickel (ni). impure nickel is reacted with carbon monoxide to form volatile nickel tetracarbonyl $[\mathrm{ni}(\mathrm{co})_4]$ , which is then decomposed at a higher temperature to yield pure nickel. so, (b) mond process matches with (iv) ni. van-arkel process: this process is used for the ultra-purification of metals like titanium (ti), zirconium (zr), and hafnium ( hf ). the metal is converted into a volatile compound (e.g., iodide) and then decomposed to yield a very pure metal. so, (c) van-arkel process matches with (i) ti. zone refining process: this method is used for obtaining highly pure metals, especially for semiconductors, by exploiting the difference in solubility of impurities in the molten and solid states of the metal. metals like germanium (ge), silicon (si), gallium (ga), and indium (in) are purified by this method. so, (d) zone refining process matches with (ii) in. © examsnet.com

question: The co-ordination number of chromium in $\mathrm{K} [ \mathrm{Cr} ( \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O} )_2 ( \mathrm{C}_2 \mathrm{O}_4 )_2 ]$ is [AP EAPCET 24 May 2025 S1]
search_text: the co-ordination number of chromium in $\mathrm{k} [ \mathrm{cr} ( \mathrm{h}_2 \mathrm{o} )_2 ( \mathrm{c}_2 \mathrm{o}_4 )_2 ]$ is [ap eapcet 24 may 2025 s1] {'a': '5', 'b': '4', 'c': '6', 'd': '3'} 2025 2025-05-24 shift_1 chemistry   150 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: to determine the coordination number of chromium $( \mathrm{cr} )$ in the complex $\mathrm{k} [ \mathrm{cr} ( \mathrm{h}_2 \mathrm{o} )_2 ( \mathrm{c}_2 \mathrm{o}_4 )_2 ]$ , we need to identify the ligands and their denticity. identify the central metal atom: the central metal atom is chromium (cr). identify the ligands: $\mathrm{h}_2 \mathrm{o}$ (aqua) $\mathrm{c}_2 \mathrm{o}_4$ (oxalato, derived from oxalic acid, $\mathrm{c}_2 \mathrm{o}_4^{2-}$ ) determine the denticity of each ligand: $\mathrm{h}_2 \mathrm{o}$ (water): this is a monodentate ligand, meaning each water molecule forms one coordinate bond with the central metal atom. $\mathrm{c}_2 \mathrm{o}_4^{2-}$ (oxalate): this is a bidentate ligand, meaning each oxalate ion forms two coordinate bonds with the central metal atom, typically through its two oxygen atoms. calculate the total number of coordinate bonds: there are two $\mathrm{h}_2 \mathrm{o}$ ligands. since each is monodentate, they contribute $2 \times 1 = 2$ coordinate bonds. there are two $\mathrm{c}_2 \mathrm{o}_4^{2-}$ ligands. since each is bidentate, they contribute $2 \times 2 = 4$ coordinate bonds. sum the coordinate bonds to find the coordination number: coordination number $= (.$ bonds from $\mathrm{h}_2 \mathrm{o} ) + (.$ bonds from $\mathrm{c}_2 \mathrm{o}_4^{2-})$ coordination number $=2+4=6$ therefore, the coordination number of chromium in the given complex is 6 . the final answer is 6 . © examsnet.com

search_text: match the following list-i (glycosidic linkage) list-ii (polysaccharide) a) $\alpha-1,4$ i) amylose b) $\beta-1,4$ ii) amylopectin c) $\alpha-1,4, \alpha-1,6$ iii) cellulose [ap eapcet 24 may 2025 s1] {'a': 'a-ii, b-i, c-iii', 'b': 'a-iii, b-i, c-ii', 'c': 'a-i, b-ii, c-iii', 'd': 'a-i, b-iii, c-ii'} 2025 2025-05-24 shift_1 chemistry   152 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: amylose: amylose is a linear polymer made up of d-glucose units. the glucose units are linked together by $\alpha - 1 , 4$ -glycosidic bonds. amylopectin: amylopectin is a branched polymer of d-glucose units. the linear chains are formed by $\alpha - 1 , 4$ -glycosidic bonds. branching occurs due to $\alpha - 1 , 6$ -glycosidic bonds at intervals. cellulose: cellulose is a linear polymer of d-glucose units. the glucose units are linked by $\beta$ -1,4-glycosidic bonds. this type of linkage gives cellulose its rigid, structural properties. now, let's match list-i (glycosidic linkage) with list-ii (polysaccharide): (a) $\alpha - 1 , 4$ : this linkage is characteristic of the linear chains in both amylose and amylopectin. since amylose only has $\alpha-1,4$ linkages for its main structure, it's the most direct match here. so, a - (i) amylose. (b) $\beta$ -1,4: this linkage is unique to (iii) cellulose among the given options. so, b - (iii) cellulose. (c) $\alpha - 1 , 4 , \alpha - 1 , 6$ : the presence of both $\alpha -1,4$ and $\alpha -1,6$ linkages indicates a branched polysaccharide with alpha linkages, which is characteristic of (ii) amylopectin. so, c - (ii) amylopectin. © examsnet.com

question: An alcohol $X(\mathrm{C}_5\mathrm{H}_{12}\mathrm{O})$ on dehydration gives Y (major product). Reaction of Y with HBr gave $Z(\mathrm{C}_5\mathrm{H}_{11}\mathrm{Br}.)$ , major product). Z undergoes nucleophilic substitution in two steps. What are X and Y ? [AP EAPCET 26 May 2025 S1]
search_text: an alcohol $x(\mathrm{c}_5\mathrm{h}_{12}\mathrm{o})$ on dehydration gives y (major product). reaction of y with hbr gave $z(\mathrm{c}_5\mathrm{h}_{11}\mathrm{br}.)$ , major product). z undergoes nucleophilic substitution in two steps. what are x and y ? [ap eapcet 26 may 2025 s1] {'a': '', 'b': '', 'c': '', 'd': ''} 2025 2025-05-26 shift_1 chemistry   157 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: identify z: since z undergoes nucleophilic substitution in two steps, it follows an $\mathrm{s_n1}$ mechanism, so z must be a tertiary alkyl bromide. for the formula $\mathrm{c}_5\mathrm{h}_{11}\mathrm{br}$ , the tertiary bromide is 2-bromo-2-methylbutane, $\mathrm{(ch_3)_2c(br)ch_2ch_3}$ . identify y: hbr addition to y gives this tertiary bromide by markovnikov addition, so y is 2-methylbut-2-ene, $\mathrm{(ch_3)_2c=chch_3}$ . identify x: dehydration of x must give 2-methylbut-2-ene as the major product. the alcohol that directly gives this more substituted alkene is 2-methylbutan-2-ol, $\mathrm{(ch_3)_2c(oh)ch_2ch_3}$ . mechanism check: z ionizes slowly to a tertiary carbocation and $\mathrm{br^-}$ , then the nucleophile attacks in a fast second step, confirming two-step $\mathrm{s_n1}$ substitution. thus x is 2-methylbutan-2-ol and y is 2-methylbut-2-ene, which corresponds to option option b. © examsnet.com

search_text: if $a x^3+b x y=4$ (a and b are arbitrary constants) is the general solution of the differential equation $f(x) \;\frac{d^2 y}{d x^2}+g(x) \;\frac{d y}{d x}-2 y=0$ , then $f(1)+g(1)=$ [ap eapcet 27 may 2025 s1] {'a': '1', 'b': '0', 'c': '4', 'd': '9'} 2025 2025-05-27 shift_1 mathematics   80 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet25/eapcet/eapcet_exampapersfinal.aspx solution: solve the implicit general solution for $y$ . assuming $b\ne 0$ , from $a x^3+bxy=4$ we get $y=\frac{4-ax^3}{bx}=\frac{4}{b}\frac{1}{x}-\frac{a}{b}x^2.$ set $c_1=\frac{4}{b}$ and $c_2=-\frac{a}{b}$ , so the general solution is $y=\frac{c_1}{x}+c_2x^2.$ differentiate twice: $y'=-\frac{c_1}{x^2}+2c_2x,\qquad y''=\frac{2c_1}{x^3}+2c_2.$ substitute these into $f(x)y''+g(x)y'-2y=0$ : $f(x)\left(\frac{2c_1}{x^3}+2c_2\right)+g(x)\left(-\frac{c_1}{x^2}+2c_2x\right)-2\left(\frac{c_1}{x}+c_2x^2\right)=0.$ since $c_1$ and $c_2$ are arbitrary, their coefficients must separately vanish. for $c_1$ : $\frac{2f(x)}{x^3}-\frac{g(x)}{x^2}-\frac{2}{x}=0.$ multiplying by $x^3$ gives $2f(x)-xg(x)-2x^2=0.$ for $c_2$ : $2f(x)+2xg(x)-2x^2=0,$ or $f(x)+xg(x)-x^2=0.$ adding the two simplified equations gives $3f(x)-3x^2=0$ , so $f(x)=x^2$ . then $f(x)+xg(x)-x^2=0$ gives $xg(x)=0$ , so $g(x)=0$ . therefore $f(1)+g(1)=1^2+0=1.$ thus the correct option is option a. © examsnet.com

assertion (a): $1+(2+3)+(4+5+6)+\cdots n$ terms $=\sum_{r=1}^n \frac{r\left(r^2+1\right)}{2}, n \in \mathbb{n}$ reason (r): $n^{\text {th }}$ term of sequence $1+2+4+7+\cdots$ is $\frac{n^2-n+2}{2}, n \in \mathbb{n}$ and sum to $n$ terms of an arithmetic progression $\left\{t_n: a+(n-1) d\right\}$ is $\frac{n}{2}[2 a+(n-1) d]$ {'a': '(a) is true, (r) is true and (r) is the correct explanation to (a)', 'b': '(a) is true, (r) is true but (r) is not the correct explanation to (a)', 'c': '(a) is true , (r) is false', 'd': '(a) is false, (r) is true'} 2026 2026-05-12 shift_1 mathematics sequences and series grouped arithmetic series 3 apsche (official) https://cets.apsche.ap.gov.in/eapcet/eapcet/eapcet_exampapers.aspx 1. given: groups contain 1, 2, 3, … consecutive positive integers.

3. the first integer in group r is 1+r(r−1)/2=(r²−r+2)/2. the last is r(r+1)/2.
